ते विद्वांसः अनृता प्रतिचक्ष्य आविशं यतः ऊं आयन् पुनः तत् उत् ईयुः (te vidvāṃsaḥ anṛtā praticakṣya āviśaṃ yataḥ ūṃ āyan punaḥ tat ut īyuḥ)—अभिज्ञास्त्येऽर्जसोऽनृतान्यसुरैः कृता मायाः दृष्ट्वा प्रवेष्टुं यत एव स्थानादागच्छन् तत् स्थानं पुनः उत्कर्षण प्राप्ताः (abhijñāstye 'rjaso 'nṛtānyasuraiḥ kṛtā māyāḥ dṛṣṭvā praveṣṭuṃ yata eva sthānādāgacchan tat sthānaṃ punaḥ utkarṣaṇa prāptāḥ) (as supplied; the bhāṣya printed above has अभिज्ञास्तेऽंगिरसोऽनृता अनृतान्यसुरैः (abhijñāste 'ṃgiraso 'nṛtā anṛtānyasuraiḥ) and उत्कर्षेण (utkarṣeṇa) here). Because they knew everything, those Aṅgirā sages came again to the place which they had already come and learned beforehand — how to enter the secret place where the Paṇis, by tricks and devices, had hidden the cows so that no one knew. The sense is: the Aṅgirā sages knew by their discernment the cave in which the Paṇis had hidden the cows; even so, they had already looked at that cave and examined it beforehand and learned where and how it should be entered. Accordingly they came again to a place convenient for entering that cave first.

p. 28

Running head: [28 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied).

Besides this meaning, another, different meaning can be given to this Ṛk. It also appears to suggest that the Aṅgirā sages, who know everything, by the power of their sacrificial rites made rain fall, when the clouds (अभिनक्षंतः (abhinakṣaṃtaḥ)) moving in the atmosphere were holding back, without pouring it down on the earth as rain, the water stored in them as treasure.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ऋ॒तावा॑नः प्रति॒चक्ष्यान्वि॑ता॒ पुन॒रात॒ आ त॑स्थुः क॒वयो॑ म॒हस्प॒थः । ते बा॒हुभ्यां॑ धमि॒तम॒ग्निमश्म॑नि॒ नकिः॒ षो अ॒स्त्यर॑णो ज॒हुर्हि तं॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ऋतवानः । प्रतिचक्ष्य । अनृता । पुनः । आ । अतः । आ ; तस्तुः । कवयः । महः । पथः । ते । बाहुभ्यां । धमितं । अग्निं । अश्मनि । नकिः । सः । अस्ति । अरणः । जहुः । हि । तं ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ऋतावानः । ऋतमिति सत्यनामधेयं । तद्वंतः कवयः क्रांतदर्शिनः सर्वज्ञा अंगीरसोऽनृता अनृतानि प्रतिचक्ष्य पूर्वोक्तप्रकारेण दृष्ट्वा अतोऽस्मात्स्थानात् पुनराजिगमषवो महस्पथो महतो मार्गान् प्रति आतस्थुः । अवतस्थिरे । अवतिष्ठमानाश्च ते बाहुभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां धमितं मंथनोत्पादितं प्रज्वालितमग्निम- श्मनि पणीनां निवासभूते शिलोच्चये जहुर्हि। दग्दुं त्यक्तवंतः खलु । अरणोऽर मयिता दाहेन दुःखकारी सोऽग्निः पूर्वं तत्र नकिरस्ति । न विद्यते । अविद्यमान- मग्निं स्वसामर्थ्यादुत्पाद्य तत्र प्रचिक्षिपुरित्यर्थः ॥

ṛtāvānaḥ | ṛtamiti satyanāmadheyaṃ | tadvaṃtaḥ kavayaḥ krāṃtadarśinaḥ sarvajñā aṃgīraso 'nṛtā anṛtāni praticakṣya pūrvoktaprakāreṇa dṛṣṭvā ato 'smātsthānāt punarājigamaṣavo mahaspatho mahato mārgān prati ātasthuḥ | avatasthire | avatiṣṭhamānāśca te bāhubhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ dhamitaṃ maṃthanotpāditaṃ prajvālitamagnima- śmani paṇīnāṃ nivāsabhūte śiloccaye jahurhi| dagduṃ tyaktavaṃtaḥ khalu | araṇo 'ra mayitā dāhena duḥkhakārī so 'gniḥ pūrvaṃ tatra nakirasti | na vidyate | avidyamāna- magniṃ svasāmarthyādutpādya tatra pracikṣipurityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: the truthful, all-seeing Aṅgirases, having seen the Asuras' illusions, turned back to the great paths and cast fire, kindled by churning with their arms, on the Paṇis' rocky dwelling, where no such fire had been before.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

ऋतावानः (ṛtāvānaḥ)—endowed with truth; कवयः (kavayaḥ)—far-seeing (all-knowing) Aṅgirases; अनृता (anṛtā)—the false (illusions of the Asuras); प्रतिचक्ष्य (praticakṣya)—having seen; अतः (ataḥ)—from that place; पुनः (punaḥ)—wishing to return; महस्पथः (mahaspathaḥ)—to the great road; आ तस्थुः (ā tasthuḥ)—

p. 29

Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 2] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 29 (as supplied).

(continued from p. 28) ... came and stood; ते (te)—they; बाहुभ्यां (bāhubhyāṃ)—with their arms; धमितं (dhamitaṃ)—churned and kindled; तं अग्निं (taṃ agniṃ)—that fire; आत्मनी (ātmanī) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā and Pada have अश्मनि (aśmani))—on the rocks of the mountain (the dwelling of the Paṇis); जहुर्हि (jahurhi)—they placed; अरणः (araṇaḥ)—[the gloss is printed वहिसतक्क (vahisatakka), "bearing"; the Bhāvārtha has "burning"] [?]; सः (saḥ)—that fire; नकिः अस्ति (nakiḥ asti)—(before) was not there at all.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Aṅgirases, endowed with truth and all-knowing, having seen the illusions of the Asuras, which were untrue, and wishing to return from that place, came and stood on the great road. They placed the fire, churned with their arms and blazing, on the rocks of the mountain, the dwelling of the Paṇis. The burning fire had not been there before.

Printed English

Those sages, eminent for truth, having seen through the false (illusions of the Asura), again pursued the main road thither, and with their hands cast against the rock the destructive fire, which, till then, was not there.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ऋतावानः कवयः अनृता प्रतिचक्ष्य अतः पुनः महस्पथः आ तस्थुः (ṛtāvānaḥ kavayaḥ anṛtā praticakṣya ataḥ punaḥ mahaspathaḥ ā tasthuḥ)—Those Āṅgirā sages, truthful and far-seeing, that is, all-knowing, having seen the magical snares of the Asuras, found no way to enter inside the cave where the cows were hidden, and came and stood on the great road by which they had come. But they did not wish to go away without doing the task for which they had come. Therefore,

ते बाहुभ्यां धमितं तं अग्निं अश्मनि जहुर्हि (te bāhubhyāṃ dhamitaṃ taṃ agniṃ aśmani jahurhi)—आतिष्ठमानाश्च ते हस्ताभ्यां मंथनोत्पादितं प्रज्वालितमग्निं पणीनां निवासभूतेशिलोच्चये दग्धुं त्यक्तवंतः खलु (ātiṣṭhamānāśca te hastābhyāṃ maṃthanotpāditaṃ prajvālitamagniṃ paṇīnāṃ nivāsabhūteśiloccaye dagdhuṃ tyaktavaṃtaḥ khalu). They strongly churned with their hands and produced fire, and while it blazed they set it alight in the dwellings on the mountain where the Paṇis lived, and made it burn. In general, when enemies are to be defeated in war and the like, it is even now the custom to set fire to their dwellings and cause them immense loss. Thereby the enemies are terrified and defeated. Following this method, the Aṅgirā sages churned out fire, and as soon as it was well kindled and began to blaze, they set fire to the town of the enemy Paṇis, or to their huts: this is the sense.

p. 30

Running head: [30 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied; the word "bhāṣya" is misprinted सायणभाव्यसहिता (sāyaṇabhāvyasahitā) in the supplied text). The supplied text has no separate page head for p. 30; its contents were found inside p. 29 and are taken as p. 30.

अरणः सः नकिः अस्ति (araṇaḥ saḥ nakiḥ asti)—अरणो अरमयिता । दाहेन दुःखकारी सः अग्निः पूर्वं तत्र न विद्यते (araṇo aramayitā | dāhena duḥkhakārī saḥ agniḥ pūrvaṃ tatra na vidyate). In many places रण (raṇa) is explained as "delightful". अरणः (araṇaḥ) therefore means "not delightful". Here, because the heat of fire causes suffering in the form of burning and the like, fire is described as अरणः (araṇaḥ). Since fire has the nature of burning, it causes people suffering; that is, when dwellings are burning with fire, it is natural for people to feel great sorrow. Such a distress-causing [?] fire was not there before.

(The supplied text has here an ornamental picture, described by the text-reading software as containing no text; it is not reproduced.)

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ऋ॒तज्ये॑न क्षि॒प्रेण॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पति॒र्यत्र॒ वष्टि॒ प्र तद॑श्नोति॒ धन्व॑ना । तस्य॑ सा॒ध्वरिष॑वो॒ याभि॒रस्य॑ति नृ॒चक्ष॑सो दृ॒शये॒ कर्ण॑योनयः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ऋतज्येन । क्षिप्रेण । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः । यत्र । वष्टि । प्र । तत् । अश्नोति । धन्वना । तस्य । साध्वीः । इषवः । याभिः । अस्यति । नृचक्षसः । दृशये । कर्णयोनयः ॥ ८ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ऋतं सत्यमेव ज्या यस्य तेन क्षिप्रेणेषूणां क्षेपकेण धन्वना धरणभूतेन धनुषा ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणो मंत्रस्य पालयिता देवो यत्र यस्मिन्विषये वष्टि कामयते, तत्पाश्नोति । प्रकर्षेण व्याप्प्नोति ॥ अश्नोतेर्व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ तस्य धनुषः साध्वीः साधिकास्ता इषवो भवंति याभिरिषुभिर्ब्रह्मणस्पतिरस्यति । राक्षसा- दीन् क्षिपति । कीदृश्यस्ताः । नृचक्षसो नृन् पश्यतः । उपलक्षणमेतत् । सर्वज्ञस्य ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्द्र्यशये दर्शनाय ज्ञानाय जाताः कर्णयोनयः श्रोत्रेंद्रियेण ग्राह्या मंत्रभूता आकर्णकृष्णा वा बाणाः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मंत्रैरेव सर्वं साधय- तीति भावः ॥

ṛtaṃ satyameva jyā yasya tena kṣipreṇeṣūṇāṃ kṣepakeṇa dhanvanā dharaṇabhūtena dhanuṣā brahmaṇaspatirbrahmaṇo maṃtrasya pālayitā devo yatra yasminviṣaye vaṣṭi kāmayate, tatpāśnoti | prakarṣeṇa vyāppnoti ‖ aśnotervyatyayena parasmaipadaṃ ‖ tasya dhanuṣaḥ sādhvīḥ sādhikāstā iṣavo bhavaṃti yābhiriṣubhirbrahmaṇaspatirasyati | rākṣasā- dīn kṣipati | kīdṛśyastāḥ | nṛcakṣaso nṛn paśyataḥ | upalakṣaṇametat | sarvajñasya brahmaṇaspaterdryaśaye darśanāya jñānāya jātāḥ karṇayonayaḥ śrotreṃdriyeṇa grāhyā maṃtrabhūtā ākarṇakṛṣṇā vā bāṇāḥ | brahmaṇaspatirmaṃtraireva sarvaṃ sādhaya- tīti bhāvaḥ ‖

Gist: Brahmaṇaspati, with a quick-shooting bow whose string is truth, attains whatever he desires; his arrows, perceived through the ear (the mantras), accomplish everything.

p. 31

Running head: [A. 2 A. 7 V. 2.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 31 (as supplied). The window begins inside Ṛk 8, at the Pratipadārtha.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

ऋतज्येन (ऋतज्येन (ṛtajyena))—with the one whose bowstring is truth; क्षिप्रेण (क्षिप्रेण (kṣipreṇa))—that shoots arrows swiftly; धन्वना (धन्वना (dhanvanā))—with the bow; ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (brahmaṇaspatiḥ))—Brahmaṇaspati; यत्र (यत्र (yatra))—at whatever target; वष्टि (वष्टि (vaṣṭi))—takes aim and desires; तत् (तत् (tat))—that; प्र अश्नोति (प्र अश्नोति (pra aśnoti))—he attains fully; याभिः (याभिः (yābhiḥ))—with which arrows; अस्यति (अस्यति (asyati))—Bṛhaspati [sic: so in the Kannada] overthrows the Rākṣasas and the like, such (arrows); नृचक्षसः (नृचक्षसः (nṛcakṣasaḥ))—of the all-knowing Brahmaṇaspati; दृशये (दृशये (dṛśaye))—produced for the sake of knowledge; कर्णयोनयः (कर्णयोनयः (karṇayonayaḥ))—perceptible by the organ of hearing, and of the nature of mantras; तस्य (तस्य (tasya))—of that bow; इषवः (इषवः (iṣavaḥ))—the arrows; साध्वीः (साध्वीः (sādhvīḥ))—accomplish their work.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

With the bow whose string is truth and which shoots arrows swiftly, Brahmaṇaspati fully attains whatever target he takes aim at and desires. The arrows of that bow, with which Bṛhaspati [so in the Kannada] overthrows the Rākṣasas and the like, which are produced for the knowledge of the all-knowing Brahmaṇaspati, and which are perceived by the organ of hearing and are of the nature of mantras, accomplish their work.

Printed English

Whatever Brahmanaspathi aims at with the truthrst-rung [sic] quick-darting bow, that (mark) he surely attains: holy are its arrows with which he shoots, (intended) for the eyes of men, and having their abode in the ear.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ऋतज्येन क्षिप्रेण धन्वना यत्र वष्टि तत् प्र अश्नोति (brahmaṇaspatiḥ ṛtajyena kṣipreṇa dhanvanā yatra vaṣṭi tat pra aśnoti)—सत्यमेव ज्या यस्य तेन इषूणां क्षेपकेण धनुषा ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्ब्रह्मणो मंत्रस्य पालयिता देवः यस्मिन् विषये कामयते तत्पकर्षेण प्राप्नोति (satyameva jyā yasya tena iṣūṇāṃ kṣepakeṇa dhanuṣā brahmaṇaspatirbrahmaṇo maṃtrasya pālayitā devaḥ yasmin viṣaye kāmayate tatpakarṣeṇa prāpnoti). Brahmaṇaspati is the god who protects the mantras; that is, with mantras he can accomplish any undertaking. The bowstring (ज्या (jyā)) of his bow is of the nature of truth; that is, truth itself is the string (cord) of his bow. Fitting such a string called truth to his bow, with arrows shot in quick succession (that is, with mantras), whatever matter Brahmaṇaspati aims at he accomplishes without fail. He does not miss the mark he has set; that is, he does not leave unaccomplished an undertaking he has resolved to carry out. Here the arrows are mantras, or the oblation offered to the gods. As the English translator Wilson says, "The arrows are oblations and mantras": the arrows are the oblation offered by him and the mantras uttered.

p. 32

Running head: [32 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied; "bhāṣya" misspelt in the supplied text).

There is nothing that cannot be accomplished by these. Therefore they carry the qualifying expression साद्वी8 (sādvī8) [?] (so in the supplied text; evidently साध्वीः (sādhvīḥ)), साधिकाः (sādhikāḥ), that is, "accomplishing the intended work".

नृचक्षसः कर्णयोनयः—नृन्‌पश्यतः, सर्वज्ञस्य बृहस्पतेः, श्रोत्रेंद्रियेण ग्राह्याः मंत्रभूता आकर्णकृष्टा वा बाणाः । ब्रह्मणस्पतिः मंत्रैरेव सर्वं साधयतीति भावः (nṛcakṣasaḥ karṇayonayaḥ—nṛnpaśyataḥ, sarvajñasya bṛhaspateḥ, śrotreṃdriyeṇa grāhyāḥ maṃtrabhūtā ākarṇakṛṣṭā vā bāṇāḥ | brahmaṇaspatiḥ maṃtraireva sarvaṃ sādhayatīti bhāvaḥ). Sāyaṇa understands नृचक्षसः (nṛcakṣasaḥ) as "seeing men", that is, "all-knowing", and कर्णयोनयः (karṇayonayaḥ) as "perceptible by the organ of hearing, of the nature of mantras, or arrows drawn back to the ear". Here he has applied नृचक्षसः (nṛcakṣasaḥ) to Brahmaṇaspati and stated his omniscience. But if we take the view of the English scholars cited above, the arrows are of two forms, oblation and mantra. Of these the oblations are नृचक्षसः (nṛcakṣasaḥ), visible to men, and the mantras are कर्णयोनयः (karṇayonayaḥ), to be heard by the ears of men [the Kannada reads किविगैकेळसतक्कवु (kivigaikeḷasatakkavu), apparently a misreading of "to be heard by the ear"]. Thus the mantras employed by Brahmaṇaspati and the oblations given are capable of doing the intended work. This Sāyaṇācārya has explained by the sentence ब्रह्मणस्पतिः मंत्रेणैव सर्वं साधयति (brahmaṇaspatiḥ maṃtreṇaiva sarvaṃ sādhayati) ("Brahmaṇaspati accomplishes everything by mantra alone"). The text ends with a numeral-like mark (as supplied: "-௨௰௪-", i.e. apparently the Sūkta number 24; not read further).

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स सं॑न॒यः स वि॑न॒यः पु॒रोहि॑तः॒ स सुष्टु॑तः॒ स यु॒धि ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ । चा॒क्ष्मो यद्वाजं॒ भर॑ते म॒ती धनादित्सूर्य॑स्तपति तप्य॒तुर्वृथा॑ ॥

Running head: [A. 2. A. 7. V. 2.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 33 (as supplied).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पुरोहितो देवैः पुरतोऽत्र स्थापितः स ब्रह्मणस्पतिः संनयः विश्लिष्टानां मंत्रैः संगमयिता भवति । विनयः संगतानां विविधं नेता पृथक्कर्तापि स एव । तथा सुष्टुतः शोभनं स्तोतृभिः स्तुतश्च भवति । तथा युधि संग्रामे स स्तोतृणा- मनुग्रहाय प्रादुर्भवतीति शेषः । यद्यदा चाक्ष्मः ॥ चष्टेः क्षमतीर्वा ॥ सर्वस्य द्रष्टा सर्वसहो ना ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वाजमन्नं मती मननीयं प्रशस्तं धना धनं च स्तोतृणामर्थाय भरते । बिभर्ति । वृष्टिद्वारा पोषयति । आदित् अनंतरमेव तप्यतुस्तापकः सूर्यो वृथा । अनायासवचनमेतत् । अनायासेन तपति । दीप्यते। ब्रह्मणस्पतिना दत्तैरन्नॆर्धनैश्च यज्ञस्य सिद्धत्वात् स्वयं केवलं हवींषि भुंजान एव वर्तत इत्यर्थः ॥

purohito devaiḥ purato 'tra sthāpitaḥ sa brahmaṇaspatiḥ saṃnayaḥ viśliṣṭānāṃ maṃtraiḥ saṃgamayitā bhavati | vinayaḥ saṃgatānāṃ vividhaṃ netā pṛthakkartāpi sa eva | tathā suṣṭutaḥ śobhanaṃ stotṛbhiḥ stutaśca bhavati | tathā yudhi saṃgrāme sa stotṛṇā- manugrahāya prādurbhavatīti śeṣaḥ | yadyadā cākṣmaḥ ‖ caṣṭeḥ kṣamatīrvā ‖ sarvasya draṣṭā sarvasaho nā brahmaṇaspatirvājamannaṃ matī mananīyaṃ praśastaṃ dhanā dhanaṃ ca stotṛṇāmarthāya bharate | bibharti | vṛṣṭidvārā poṣayati | ādit anaṃtarameva tapyatustāpakaḥ sūryo vṛthā | anāyāsavacanametat | anāyāsena tapati | dīpyate| brahmaṇaspatinā dattairannèrdhanaiśca yajñasya siddhatvāt svayaṃ kevalaṃ havīṃṣi bhuṃjāna eva vartata ityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: Brahmaṇaspati, set in front by the gods as priest, joins and separates things by mantras, is well praised and comes to aid his praisers in battle; he brings food and wealth, and the sun shines effortlessly.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

पुरोहितः (पुरोहितः (purohitaḥ))—established at the head (of the gods); सः ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (सः ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (saḥ brahmaṇaspatiḥ))—that Brahmaṇaspati; संनयः (संनयः (saṃnayaḥ))—he who brings together, by the power of his mantras, things that are separate; विनयः (विनयः (vinayaḥ))—he who separates what is joined together; सः (सः (saḥ))—he; सुष्टुतः (स सुष्टुतः (sa suṣṭutaḥ))—is excellently praised; युधि (युधि (yudhi))—in battle; सः (सः (saḥ))—he is the helper of the praisers; यत् (यत् (yat))—when; चाक्ष्मी (चाक्ष्मी (cākṣmī)) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has चाक्ष्मो (cākṣmo) and the Pada चाक्ष्मः (cākṣmaḥ))—the all-knowing Brahmaṇaspati; वाजं (वाजं (vājaṃ))—food; मती (मती (matī))—excellent; धना (धना (dhanā))—wealth; भरते (भरते (bharate))—he bears (for the praisers); आदित् (आदित् (ādit))—immediately thereupon; तप्यतुः (तप्यतुः (tapyatuḥ))—the burning; सूर्यः (सूर्यः (sūryaḥ))—the sun; वृथा (वृथा (vṛthā))—effortlessly; तपति (तपति (tapati))—shines.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That same Brahmaṇaspati, established as priest of the gods, is the one who by the power of his mantras brings together things that are separate and separates what is joined. He is also excellently praised. In battle he is the helper. When Brahmaṇaspati bears food and excellent wealth for his praisers, immediately thereupon the burning sun shines effortlessly.

Printed English

He Brahmanaspathi, is the aggregator and subjugator (of objects); the family priest (of the gods); and the renowed [sic] in battle; the beholder (of all), who bestows food and desired treasures, whence the radiant sun shines without exertion.

p. 34

Running head: [34 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पुरोहितः ब्रह्मणस्पतिः संनयः (purohitaḥ brahmaṇaspatiḥ saṃnayaḥ)—"he brings together, by mantras, those who have been separated." Yāska explains the word purohita as "they place him in front" (Ni. 2-12). Sāyaṇa says "set in front by the gods": the gods keep Brahmaṇaspati before them. He describes this Brahmaṇaspati as one who, by the power of his mantras, brings together in one place those who are separated from one another. Further, विनयः (vinayaḥ) (the text has संगशानां (saṃgaśānāṃ) [?], evidently for the bhāṣya's संगतानां (saṃgatānāṃ)): "he too is the one who separates those who are joined" — he explains that, by reciting mantras, he can make those who are together, through affection or other causes, live apart.

सुष्टुतः युधि सः (suṣṭutaḥ yudhi saḥ) (the text has स्तोत्यणामनुग्रहाय प्रादुर्भवति (stotyaṇāmanugrahāya prādurbhavati)): being praised, he appears in person, to show his favour, when battle comes upon them.

For the word चाक्षृः (cākṣṛḥ) (so in the supplied text; the Saṃhitā and Pada have चाक्ष्मो (cākṣmo) / चाक्ष्मः (cākṣmaḥ)) the explanation is सर्वस्य द्रष्टा सर्वसहो ना (sarvasya draṣṭā sarvasaho nā): Brahmaṇaspati sees everything directly and endures all kinds of sorrows and calamities. Then वाजं मती धना भरते (vājaṃ matī dhanā bharate) is explained: for those who praise him he makes food and excellent wealth increase, bringing rain-waters, and so he nourishes them.

From this: since the sacrifice is accomplished by the foods and wealth given by Brahmaṇaspati, the burning sun is left merely enjoying the oblations himself (केवलं हवींषि भुंजान एव वर्तते (kevalaṃ havīṃṣi bhuṃjāna eva vartate)). That is, because Brahmaṇaspati carries out the sacrifices of the sacrificers with foods and wealth, the sun, who illumines and protects everything, merely receives his shares of the oblations and stays idle; this states the extent of Brahmaṇaspati's nourishing of those who depend on him.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वि॒भु प्र॒भु प्र॑थ॒मं मे॒हना॑वतो॒ बृह॒स्पतेः॑ सुवि॒दत्रा॑णि॒ राध्या॑ । इ॒मा सा॒तानि॑ वे॒न्यस्य॑ वा॒जिनो॒ येन॒ जना॑ उ॒भये॑ भुंज॒ते विशः॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

विभु। प्रभु। प्रथमं । मेहनावतः । बृहस्पतेः । सुविदत्राणि । राध्या । इमा । सातानि । वेन्यस्य । वाजिनः । येन । जनाः । उभये । भुंजते । विशः ॥ १० ॥

vibhu| prabhu| prathamaṃ | mehanāvataḥ | bṛhaspateḥ | suvidatrāṇi | rādhyā | imā | sātāni | venyasya | vājinaḥ | yena | janāḥ | ubhaye | bhuṃjate | viśaḥ ‖ 10 ‖

p. 35

Running head: [A. 2, A. 7, V. 2.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 35 (as supplied).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

विभु विभूनि व्याप्तानि प्रभु प्रभूणि प्रौढानि प्रथमं प्रथमानि मुख्यानि । एवंभूतानि मेहनावतो वर्षणवतो वृष्टिप्रदस्य बृहस्पतेर्बृहतो मंत्रस्य पालयितुः संबंधीनि सुविदत्राणि ॥ विदल्ग लाभे । सुविदेः कत्रन् । उ. ३ १०८. ॥ सुष्टु लब्बव्यानि ॥ सुविदत्रं धनं भवतीति यास्कः ॥ राध्या राध्यानि सम्यक् साधनीयानि । प्राप्तव्यानीति यावत् । इमा सातानीमानि धनानि वेन्यस्य कमनीयस्य वाजिनोऽन्नवतो ब्रह्मणस्पतेः ॥ तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी ॥ ब्रह्मणस्पतिना दत्तानि । येन धनेनोभय उभयविधा जनाः स्तोतारो यजमानाश्च देवा मनुष्याश्च वा विशो निविष्टाः संतो भुंजते । भोगान् लभंते । तत्सर्वं ब्रह्मणस्पतिना दत्तमित्यर्थः ॥

vibhu vibhūni vyāptāni prabhu prabhūṇi prauḍhāni prathamaṃ prathamāni mukhyāni | evaṃbhūtāni mehanāvato varṣaṇavato vṛṣṭipradasya bṛhaspaterbṛhato maṃtrasya pālayituḥ saṃbaṃdhīni suvidatrāṇi ‖ vidalga lābhe | suvideḥ katran | u. 3 108. ‖ suṣṭu labbavyāni ‖ suvidatraṃ dhanaṃ bhavatīti yāskaḥ ‖ rādhyā rādhyāni samyak sādhanīyāni | prāptavyānīti yāvat | imā sātānīmāni dhanāni venyasya kamanīyasya vājino 'nnavato brahmaṇaspateḥ ‖ tṛtīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī ‖ brahmaṇaspatinā dattāni | yena dhanenobhaya ubhayavidhā janāḥ stotāro yajamānāśca devā manuṣyāśca vā viśo niviṣṭāḥ saṃto bhuṃjate | bhogān labhaṃte | tatsarvaṃ brahmaṇaspatinā dattamityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: These bountiful riches of the rain-giving Bṛhaspati are pervasive, mighty and chief; all who partake of them, praisers and sacrificers (or gods and men), enjoy what he has given.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मेहनावतः (mehanāvataḥ)—of the rain-giver; बृहस्पतेः (bṛhaspateḥ)—of Bṛhaspati; सुविदत्राणि (suvidatrāṇi)—the riches; विभु (vibhu)—pervading everywhere; प्रभु (prabhu)—mighty; प्रथमं (prathamaṃ)—very excellent, they are; येन (yena)—by which wealth; उभये (ubhaye)—both kinds, men and gods; जनाः (janāḥ)—people; विशः (viśaḥ)—gathering together; भुंजते (bhuṃjate)—enjoy pleasures, such (riches too); राध्या (rādhyā)—worthy of worship; इमा सातानि (imā sātāni)—these riches; वेन्यस्य (venyasya)—of the beloved one; वाजिनः (vājinaḥ)—and possessor of food, namely Bṛhaspati — are given by him.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The riches of the rain-giving Bṛhaspati are pervasive everywhere, mighty and very excellent. Such riches, by which men and gods together enjoy pleasures, and which are worthy of worship, are given by Bṛhaspati, the beloved one, the possessor of food.

Printed English

Expansive, vast, and excellent riches, are the attainable (bounties) of Brihaspathi, the sender of the rain : these {are the gifts of the adorable giver of food, whereby both (descriptions of worshippers) entering here enjoy (abundance).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

मेहनावतः बृहस्पतेः सुविदत्राणि (mehanāvataḥ bṛhaspateḥ suvidatrāṇi) - वृष्टिप्रदस्य बृहतो मंत्रस्य पालयितुः सुष्टुलब्धव्यानि (vṛṣṭipradasya bṛhato maṃtrasya pālayituḥ suṣṭulabdhavyāni) (the bhāṣya, as supplied, has सुष्टु लब्बव्यानि (suṣṭu labbavyāni)). He is the one who pours rain-waters and protects all the abundant mantras

p. 36

Running head: [36 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied).

(Special Topics continued.) — thus explaining the greatness of Bṛhaspati or Brahmaṇaspati. Sāyaṇa explains the word सुविदत्र (suvidatra) as "that which is to be obtained in abundance" and gives its meaning as wealth.

Yāska gives the meaning सुविदत्रः कल्याणविद्यः (suvidatraḥ kalyāṇavidyaḥ) (Ni. 6-14), and explains सुविदत्रं धनं भवति (suvidatraṃ dhanaṃ bhavati) (Ni. 7-9), and quotes usages for both senses.

The wealth to be obtained from this Bṛhaspati — विभु, प्रभु, प्रथमं राध्या (vibhu, prabhu, prathamaṃ rādhyā) — is pervasive, mighty (abundant), chief, and something that must certainly be attained: thus the greatness of wealth is stated. And वाजिनः येन उभये जनाः भुंजते (vājinaḥ yena ubhaye janāḥ bhuṃjate): it is described that both kinds of people — the praising priests and the sacrificers, or men and gods — obtain the wealth bestowed by Bṛhaspati, the possessor of food, and live happily enjoying pleasures.

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

योऽव॑रे वृ॒जने॑ वि॒श्वथा॑ वि॒भुर्म॒हामु॑ र॒ण्वः शव॑सा व॒वक्षि॑थ । स दे॒वो दे॒वान्प्रति॑ पप्रथे पृ॒थु विश्वेदु॒ ता प॑रि॒भूर्ब्रह्म॑ण॒-॑ स्पतिः ॥ ११ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । अवरे । पृजने । विश्वथा । विभुः । महां । ऊं इति । रण्वः । शवसा । ववक्षिथ । सः । देवः । देवान् । प्रति । पप्रथे । पृथु । विश्वा । इत् । ऊं इति । ता । परिभूः । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ ११ ॥

yaḥ | avare | pṛjane | viśvathā | vibhuḥ | mahāṃ | ūṃ iti | raṇvaḥ | śavasā | vavakṣitha | saḥ | devaḥ | devān | prati | paprathe | pṛthu | viśvā | it | ūṃ iti | tā | paribhūḥ | brahmaṇaḥ | patiḥ ‖ 11 ‖

p. 37

Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 3] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 37 (as supplied).

(Ṛk 11 continues.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

विश्वथा सर्वप्रकारेण विभुर्व्याप्तो रणो रमयिता स्तोतव्यो वा यो ब्रह्मणस्पतिरवरे निकृष्टे वृजने वर्जनहेतुभूते बले वर्तमानं । दुर्बलमिति यावत् । महामु महांतं च ॥ छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥ उभयविधं स्तोतारं शवसात्मीयेन बलेन ववक्षिथ । वोढुमिच्छति । सर्वदा वहतीति यावत् ॥ वहते? सनंतस्य लिट्येतद्रूपं । पुरुषव्यत्ययः ॥ स देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तो देवान् प्रति सर्वेषां देवानां । प्रतिनिधिः सन् पृथु पप्रथे । अत्यंतं प्रथते । यशसा विस्तीर्णो भवतीति यावत् । यस्मादेवं तस्माद्विश्वेदु सर्वाण्येव ता तानि सर्वाणि भूतजातानि परिभूः परिभवन् अभिभवन् वर्तत इति शेषः ॥

viśvathā sarvaprakāreṇa vibhurvyāpto raṇo ramayitā stotavyo vā yo brahmaṇaspatiravare nikṛṣṭe vṛjane varjanahetubhūte bale vartamānaṃ | durbalamiti yāvat | mahāmu mahāṃtaṃ ca ‖ chāṃdaso varṇalopaḥ ‖ ubhayavidhaṃ stotāraṃ śavasātmīyena balena vavakṣitha | voḍhumicchati | sarvadā vahatīti yāvat ‖ vahate? sanaṃtasya liṭyetadrūpaṃ | puruṣavyatyayaḥ ‖ sa devo dānādiguṇayukto devān prati sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ | pratinidhiḥ san pṛthu paprathe | atyaṃtaṃ prathate | yaśasā vistīrṇo bhavatīti yāvat | yasmādevaṃ tasmādviśvedu sarvāṇyeva tā tāni sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni paribhūḥ paribhavan abhibhavan vartata iti śeṣaḥ ‖

Gist: Brahmaṇaspati, pervasive and delightful, wishes to bear by his own strength both the lowly and the eminent worshipper; being the foremost representative of the gods he is widely renowned and surpasses all beings.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

विश्वथा (viśvathā)—in every way; विभुः (vibhuḥ)—all-pervading; रण्वः (raṇvaḥ)—delightful; यः ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (yaḥ brahmaṇaspatiḥ)—which Brahmaṇaspati; अवरे (avare)—low; वृजने (vṛjane)—the worshipper who is in a miserable state; महामु (mahāmu)—the worshipper who is in an excellent state; शवसा (śavasā)—with his strength; ववक्षिथ (vavakṣitha)—wishes to bear; सः देवः (saḥ devaḥ)—he, the divine one; देवान् प्रति (devān prati)—in the eyes of the gods; पृथु (pṛthu)—exceedingly; पप्रथे (paprathe)—has become widely spread (by his fame he is renowned beyond all of them); विश्वेदु (viśvedu)—all; ता (tā)—beings; परिभूः (paribhūḥ)—surpassing, he is superior to all.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Brahmaṇaspati, who is all-pervading and delightful, wishes to bear with his strength both the worshipper in a low, wretched state and the worshipper in an excellent state. The same Brahmaṇaspati, being of divine nature, is more famed than all the gods. Surpassing all beings, he is superior to everything.

Printed English

He, who is all-pervading and delighting, is willing to sustain by his strength the noble worshipper, as well as one who is in low distress: greatly is that Brahmanaspathi renowned amongst the gods, and therefore is he verily supreme above all (beings).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Brahmaṇaspati is pervasive in many ways; this god, who is a giver of happiness or worthy of praise, is, according to Sāyaṇa, वृजने—वर्जनहेतुभूते बले वर्तमानं दुर्बलं (vṛjane—varjanahetubhūte bale vartamānaṃ durbalaṃ)

p. 38

Running head: [38 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied).

(Special Topics continued.) — one who is weak, abandoned by all, and महांतं च (mahāṃtaṃ ca), one who is filled with greatness: it is described that he wishes to protect, by his own power, the worshippers of these two kinds; and that this god, who is endowed with qualities such as generosity, shines alone as the representative of all the gods (देवान् पप्रथे (devān paprathe)), and therefore his fame is widespread. विश्वेदु ता परिभूः - सर्वाणि भूतजातानि अभिभवन् वर्तते (viśvedu tā paribhūḥ - sarvāṇi bhūtajātāni abhibhavan vartate): it is concluded that this god shines, overcoming all creatures by his fame and by his power.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

विश्वं॑ स॒त्यं म॑घवाना यु॒वोरिदाप॑श्च॒न प्रमि॑नंति व्र॒तं वां॑ । अच्छें॑द्राब्रह्मणस्पती ह॒विर्नोऽन्नं॒ युजी॑व वा॒जिना॑ जिगातं ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

विश्वं । सत्यं । मघवाना । युवोः । इत् । आपः । चन । प्र । मिनंति । व्रतं । नां [?] ! अच्छ । इंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती इति । हविः । नः । अन्नं । युजाइव । वाजिना । जिगातं ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

(No Ṛk number is printed after the Saṃhitā in the supplied text. The bhāṣya runs on to p. 39.)

हे मघवाना । मघमिति धननाम । तद्वंताविंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती युवोरित् युवयोरेव विश्वं सर्वं स्तोत्रं सत्यं यथार्थं । स्तुत्या यद्यद्गुणजातं प्रतिपाद्यते तत्सर्वं युवयोर्विद्यमानमेव न त्वारोपितमित्यर्थः । तथा चनेत्येतत्पदद्वयसमुदायः । ऐकपद्यं त्वध्यापकसांप्रदायिकं यद्येव शब्दस्य पूर्वपदे न । अपश्च आपोऽपि । उपलक्षणमेतत् । एतदुपलक्षितानि सर्वाण्यपि भूतानि वां युवयोर्व्रतं कर्म न प्रमिनंति । न हिंसंति ॥ मीज् हिंसायां क्रैयादिकः । मीनार्तेनिगम इति ह्रस्वत्वं ॥ हे इंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती नोऽस्माकं हविरच्छाभिमुख्येन जिगातं । गच्छतं । आगच्छतमिति यावत् ॥ जिगातिर्गतिकर्मा । जौहोत्यादिकः ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । युजीव वाजिना । युजा रथे नियुक्तौ वाजिनौ

he maghavānā | maghamiti dhananāma | tadvaṃtāviṃdrābrahmaṇaspatī yuvorit yuvayoreva viśvaṃ sarvaṃ stotraṃ satyaṃ yathārthaṃ | stutyā yadyadguṇajātaṃ pratipādyate tatsarvaṃ yuvayorvidyamānameva na tvāropitamityarthaḥ | tathā canetyetatpadadvayasamudāyaḥ | aikapadyaṃ tvadhyāpakasāṃpradāyikaṃ yadyeva śabdasya pūrvapade na | apaśca āpo 'pi | upalakṣaṇametat | etadupalakṣitāni sarvāṇyapi bhūtāni vāṃ yuvayorvrataṃ karma na praminaṃti | na hiṃsaṃti ‖ mīj hiṃsāyāṃ kraiyādikaḥ | mīnārtenigama iti hrasvatvaṃ ‖ he iṃdrābrahmaṇaspatī no 'smākaṃ haviracchābhimukhyena jigātaṃ | gacchataṃ | āgacchatamiti yāvat ‖ jigātirgatikarmā | jauhotyādikaḥ ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | yujīva vājinā | yujā rathe niyuktau vājinau

p. 39

Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 3] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 39 (as supplied).

(Bhāṣya of Ṛk 12 continues, mid-word.)

वेजनवंतावश्वावन्नं घासं प्रति यथा स्वयमेव शीघ्रं गच्छतस्तद्वत् शीघ्रमाग- च्छतमित्यर्थः ॥ युजेवेत्यत्र सुपां सुलुगिति प्रथमाद्वि वचनस्याकारः । तृतियायां हि सावेकाच इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥

vejanavaṃtāvaśvāvannaṃ ghāsaṃ prati yathā svayameva śīghraṃ gacchatastadvat śīghramāga- cchatamityarthaḥ ‖ yujevetyatra supāṃ sulugiti prathamādvi vacanasyākāraḥ | tṛtiyāyāṃ hi sāvekāca iti vibhakterudāttatvaṃ ‖

Gist: "All praise is true of you both, Indra and Brahmaṇaspati; creatures (waters) do not violate your rite; come swiftly to our oblation like two harnessed horses to their fodder." The grammatical tail (the ending of the dual, accent of the instrumental) is not explained.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मघवाना (maghavānā)—lords of wealth [as supplied, a stray "1" follows this word]; इंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती (iṃdrābrahmaṇaspatī)—O gods, Indra and Brahmaṇaspati; विश्वं (viśvaṃ)—all praise; सत्यं (satyaṃ)—in truth; युवोरित् (yuvorit)—is yours alone; आपश्च (āpaśca)—and all beings that rest on water; वां (vāṃ)—of you two; व्रतं (vrataṃ)—the rite; न प्र मिनंति (na pra minaṃti)—do not harm (do not transgress); युजा (yujā)—yoked to a chariot; वाजिना (vājinā)—horses; अन्नं इव (annaṃ iva)—as they go eagerly towards grass; नः (naḥ)—our; हविः (haviḥ)—to the oblation; अच्छ (accha)—facing; जिगातं (jigātaṃ)—come.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra and Brahmaṇaspati, lords of wealth, all praise is truly yours. All beings that rest on water do not [?] your rite. As horses harnessed to a पथ (patha)-[?] (the supplied text has पथक्कॆ (pathakkè) "to the path", probably for रथक्कॆ (rathakkè) "to the chariot") go eagerly towards grass, so come to our oblation.

(Doubt: the supplied text has मारुवुदिल्ल (māruvudilla) "will not sell" where the Pratipadārtha has "do not harm (transgress)"; probably मीरुवुदिल्ल (mīruvudilla) "do not transgress".)

Printed English

All truth, lords of wealth, (Indra and Brahmanaspathi), is inherent in you both : the waters injure not your rites: come to our presence (to receive) our oblations, like a pair of steeds (to receive) their provender.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this sūkta both Indra and Brahmaṇaspati are praised. मघवाना—तद्वंत् इंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती (maghavānā—tadvaṃt iṃdrābrahmaṇaspatī). The word मघ (magha) is stated by Yāska among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9). By this word Indra and Brahmaṇaspati are addressed as possessors of wealth. युवयोरित् विश्वं सत्यं—युवयोरेव सर्वं स्तोत्रं यथार्थं । स्तुत्या यद्यद्गुणजातं प्रतिपाद्यते तत्सर्वं युवयोः विद्यमानमेव न त्वारोपितं (yuvayorit viśvaṃ satyaṃ—yuvayoreva sarvaṃ stotraṃ yathārthaṃ | stutyā yadyadguṇajātaṃ pratipādyate tatsarvaṃ yuvayoḥ vidyamānameva na tvāropitaṃ). Here the word विइल्लिश्व (viilliśva) [?] (as supplied, evidently विश्व (viśva) with a stray word run in) is given the meaning "all kinds (of every sort) of praises".

p. 40

Running head: [Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied; the page number is garbled to "4)").

(Special Topics of Ṛk 12 continued.) All the qualities stated in the Ṛks of Indra and Brahmaṇaspati are really present in them; they are not merely attributed, as poets say in their poems. In this way the abundant excellence of their qualities is described.

आपश्च वां व्रतं न प्रमिनंति—अपोऽपि । (āpaśca vāṃ vrataṃ na praminaṃti—apo 'pi |) Although the word आपः (āpaḥ) here names the waters, it is explained that all creatures pervaded by the five elements beginning with water (as supplied "ಉಪಕ", evidently for water) cannot destroy (cannot transgress) the obligatory duties performed by Indra and पृथ्विस्थितिगळु (pṛthvisthitigaḷu) (as supplied). The quoted Sanskrit has "ಏತದುಲಪಕ್ಷಿತಾನಿ" (as supplied).

नः हविः युजीव वाजिना अच्छ- (naḥ haviḥ yujīva vājinā accha-) ... "Just as swift horses yoked to a chariot go quickly towards their fodder, so may you come quickly." Just as the swift horses yoked to a chariot come with speed for their food, so may Indra and Brahmaṇaspati come quickly to receive the oblations and the like in our sacrifice; thus the prayer of the sacrificer is stated.

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उताःष्ठा [?] आम [?] शृण्वंति वह्नयः सभेयो विप्रो भरते मतिः धना । वी॒ळु॒द्वेषा॒ अनु॒ वश॑ ऋ॒णमा॑द॒दिः स ह॑ वा॒जी स॑मि॒थे ब्रह्म॑ण॒-॑ स्पतिः ॥ १३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत । आशिष्ठाः । अनु । शृण्वंति । वह्नयः । सभेयः । विप्रः । धरते [?] । मती । धना वीळुद्वेषाः । अनु । वशा । ऋणं । आददिः । सति [?] . ह । वाजी । संइथे । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ १३ ॥

uta | āśiṣṭhāḥ | anu | śṛṇvaṃti | vahnayaḥ | sabheyaḥ | vipraḥ | dharate [?] | matī | dhanā vīḷudveṣāḥ | anu | vaśā | ṛṇaṃ | ādadiḥ | sati [?] . ha | vājī | saṃithe | brahmaṇaḥ | patiḥ ‖ 13 ‖

p. 41

Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 3] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 41 (as supplied).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उत अपि च आशिष्ठा आशुतराः शीघ्रगामिनो वह्नयः !! आश्वनामृतत् ॥ वोढारो ब्रह्मणस्पतेरश्वा अनु शृण्वंति । अस्माभिः कृतं स्तोत्रमनुक्रमेण शृण्वंति । यद्वा ब्रह्मणस्पतिना कृतमनुशासनं शृण्वंति । आतस्ते तमस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रापयंत्विति शेषः । सभेयः सभायां साधुः ॥ ढश्चंदसीति ढः ॥ विप्रो मेधावी अध्वर्युर्होता वा मती मत्या मननीयेन स्तोत्रेण ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्व- सवर्णदीर्घः ॥ धना हविर्लक्षणानि धनानि तस्मै ब्रह्मणस्पतये भरते । बिभर्ति । संपादयतीति यावत् । यद्वा स्तोत्रेण धनानि भरते । बिभर्ति पोषयति । आतो वीळुद्देषाः । वीळून् दृढान् प्रबलान् राक्षसादीन् द्वेष्टीति तादृशो ब्रह्मणस्पति- र्वशा वशाया गोः ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति षष्ठ्या लुक् ! ऋत्यक इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥ ऋणमस्माभिर्यज्जभिः प्रदेयमवदानात्मकमनुक्रमेणाददिरादाता भवत्विति शेषः । अवदानस्य ऋणत्वं च तैत्तिरीये त्रिभिर्यणवा जायते ब्रह्मचर्येण ऋषिभ्यः । ६. ३. १०. ५. । इत्यादिना स्पष्टमाम्मातं । यद्वा अनुरानुगुण्ये । वशा वशस्य काम- स्याभिलाषस्यानुगुणमादाता भवत्विति योज्यं । हशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । स खलु ब्रह्मणस्पतिः समिथे । संयंति संगच्छंतेऽस्मिन्नाहुतिभिर्देवा इति समिथो यज्ञः । तस्मिन्वाजी अन्नवान् । तस्माद्भव विष आदाता भवत्वित्यर्थः ॥

uta api ca āśiṣṭhā āśutarāḥ śīghragāmino vahnayaḥ !! āśvanāmṛtat ‖ voḍhāro brahmaṇaspateraśvā anu śṛṇvaṃti | asmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ stotramanukrameṇa śṛṇvaṃti | yadvā brahmaṇaspatinā kṛtamanuśāsanaṃ śṛṇvaṃti | ātaste tamasmadīyaṃ yajñaṃ prāpayaṃtviti śeṣaḥ | sabheyaḥ sabhāyāṃ sādhuḥ ‖ ḍhaścaṃdasīti ḍhaḥ ‖ vipro medhāvī adhvaryurhotā vā matī matyā mananīyena stotreṇa ‖ supāṃ sulugiti pūrva- savarṇadīrghaḥ ‖ dhanā havirlakṣaṇāni dhanāni tasmai brahmaṇaspataye bharate | bibharti | saṃpādayatīti yāvat | yadvā stotreṇa dhanāni bharate | bibharti poṣayati | āto vīḷuddeṣāḥ | vīḷūn dṛḍhān prabalān rākṣasādīn dveṣṭīti tādṛśo brahmaṇaspati- rvaśā vaśāyā goḥ ‖ supāṃ sulugiti ṣaṣṭhyā luk ! ṛtyaka iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ ‖ ṛṇamasmābhiryajjabhiḥ pradeyamavadānātmakamanukrameṇādadirādātā bhavatviti śeṣaḥ | avadānasya ṛṇatvaṃ ca taittirīye tribhiryaṇavā jāyate brahmacaryeṇa ṛṣibhyaḥ | 6. 3. 10. 5. | ityādinā spaṣṭamāmmātaṃ | yadvā anurānuguṇye | vaśā vaśasya kāma- syābhilāṣasyānuguṇamādātā bhavatviti yojyaṃ | haśabdaḥ prasiddhau | sa khalu brahmaṇaspatiḥ samithe | saṃyaṃti saṃgacchaṃte 'sminnāhutibhirdevā iti samitho yajñaḥ | tasminvājī annavān | tasmādbhava viṣa ādātā bhavatvityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: The swift horses of Brahmaṇaspati hear our praise (or his command); the wise priest brings wealth with praise; may Brahmaṇaspati, destroyer of strong demons, accept our debt-like oblation, being rich in food at the sacrifice.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

उत (uta)—and; आशिष्ठाः (āśiṣṭhāḥ)—swift-going; वह्नयः (vahnayaḥ)—horses; अनु शृण्वंति (anu śṛṇvaṃti)—may they listen to our praises; सभेयः (sabheyaḥ)—excellent in the assembly; विप्रः (vipraḥ)—and wise, the Adhvaryu; मती (matī)—with a hymn worthy of thought; धना (dhanā)—the wealth in the form of oblations; भरते (bharate)—offers; वीळुद्देषाः (vīḷuddeṣāḥ)—Brahmaṇaspati, who hates the mighty demons; वशा (vaśā)—produced from the cow; ऋणं (ṛṇaṃ)—and offered by the sacrificers, the avadāna (offering); अनु आददिः (anu ādadiḥ)—may he accept (for the reason that); स ह ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (sa ha brahmaṇaspatiḥ)—that Brahmaṇaspati indeed; समिथे (samithe)—in this sacrifice; वाजी (vājī)—is possessed of food.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the swift horses of Brahmaṇaspati listen to our praises. The Adhvaryu, excellent in the assembly and wise, offers with a hymn worthy of thought the wealth in the form of oblations. May Brahmaṇaspati, who hates the mighty demons, accept the avadāna (the oblation), which is produced from the cow and offered by the sacrificers. For that Brahmaṇaspati is indeed possessed of food at this sacrifice.

p. 42

Running head: [42 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24] (as supplied).

Printed English

The very swift horses (of Brahmanaspathi) listen to (our invocation); the priest of the assembly offers with praise the (sacrificial) wealth: may Brahmanaspathi, the hater of the oppressor, accept (the payment of) the debt, agreeably to his pleasure : may he be the accepter of the (sacificial) [sic] food presented at this coremony [sic].

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आशिष्ठा वयः अनु शृण्वंति— (āśiṣṭhā vayaḥ anu śṛṇvaṃti—) शीघ्रगामिनः ब्रह्मणस्पतेरश्वाः अस्माभिः कृतं (śīghragāminaḥ brahmaṇaspateraśvāḥ asmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ) स्तोत्रं अनुक्रमेण शृण्वंति । (stotraṃ anukrameṇa śṛṇvaṃti |) यद्वा ब्रह्मणस्पतिना कृतमनुशासनं शृण्वंति । (yadvā brahmaṇaspatinā kṛtamanuśāsanaṃ śṛṇvaṃti |) The horses of Brahmaṇaspati, moving with speed, listen to the praises of Brahmaṇaspati recited by the sacrificers or by the priests; or they listen to the command of Brahmaṇaspati. Therefore, the prayer of the sacrificers is stated: may those horses quickly bring Brahmaṇaspati to our sacrifice.

विप्रः मती धना भरते—मेधावी अध्वर्युः होता वा मननीयेन स्तोत्रेण (vipraḥ matī dhanā bharate—medhāvī adhvaryuḥ hotā vā mananīyena stotreṇa) हनिर्लक्षणानि धनानि पोषयति । (hanirlakṣaṇāni dhanāni poṣayati |) The word विप्र (vipra) is stated by Yāska (Ni. 3-19) among the names of the wise. Sāyaṇa gives two kinds of sense: that the wise Adhvaryu, or the priest called Hotṛ, recites excellent praises and gathers this abundant wealth for the sacrifice of Brahmaṇaspati; or that by praiseworthy hymns he wins the favour of Brahmaṇaspati (by his grace) and increases the wealth so acquired.

वीळुद्वेषाः वशा ऋणमाददिः— (vīḷudveṣāḥ vaśā ṛṇamādadiḥ—) Here the word वीळु (vīḷu) is read by Yāska among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9). By it the meaning is given that Brahmaṇaspati दृढान् राक्षसार्दी द्वेष्टि (dṛḍhān rākṣasārdī dveṣṭi) (as supplied), that is, subdues the demons and the like, who have abundant power. Thus Brahmaṇaspati, possessed of such greatness, अस्माभिः यज्ज्वभिः प्रदेयं अवदानात्मकं (हविः) (asmābhiḥ yajjvabhiḥ pradeyaṃ avadānātmakaṃ (haviḥ)) अनुक्रमेण आदाता भवतु (anukrameṇa ādātā bhavatu): the oblations that the officiating priests who perform the homa offer for him in the sacrifices (the materials given as a debt) are prayed to be accepted, as if a debt due were accepted without fail.

Here it may be said that the oblation-portion offered for Brahmaṇaspati is of the nature of a debt, and, since it must necessarily be offered, it is like a debt. Having explained the meaning thus, Sāyaṇa quotes: अवदानस्य ऋणत्वं च—जायमानो वै ब्राह्मणस्त्रिभिर्यणवा (avadānasya ṛṇatvaṃ ca—jāyamāno vai brāhmaṇastribhiryaṇavā) (the passage continues on the next page; the window ends here).

p. 43

जायते ब्रह्मचर्यण ऋषिभ्यो यज्ञेन देवेभ्यः प्रजया पितृभ्य एष वा अनृणो यः पुत्री यज्वा ब्रह्मचारिवासी (jāyate brahmacaryaṇa ṛṣibhyo yajñena devebhyaḥ prajayā pitṛbhya eṣa vā anṛṇo yaḥ putrī yajvā brahmacārivāsī) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-3-10-5). A twice-born man is born already bound by three kinds of debts: the debt to the sages, to the gods and to the fathers. The debt to the sages is discharged by studying the Veda in brahmacarya, the debt to the gods by performing sacrifice, and the debt to the fathers by begetting a son. Since this is said, Sāyaṇa explains that the oblation-portion (हविरवदान (haviravadāna)) is here spoken of by the word ऋण (ṛṇa) (debt), and he cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā passage. And a second meaning is also given: यद्वा वशस्य कामस्य अभिलाषस्य अनुगुणवादाता भवतु (yadvā vaśasya kāmasya abhilāṣasya anuguṇavādātā bhavatu), that is, may Brahmaṇaspati accept the oblations offered by the priests according to the wish of each priest, in order to fulfil that priest's desire. In this sense the word वश (vaśa) is given the meaning "wish" (desire).

The word समिथे (samithe) is read by Yāska among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Sāyaṇa explains the word thus: संयंति संगच्छंते अस्मिन्नाहुतिभिः देवाः इति समिथो यज्ञः (saṃyaṃti saṃgacchaṃte asminnāhutibhiḥ devāḥ iti samitho yajñaḥ), that is, the rite in which the gods assemble, each with his own oblation-portion, is the sacrifice. तस्मात् हविष आदाता भवतु (tasmāt haviṣa ādātā bhavatu): therefore the prayer is explained to be that Brahmaṇaspati (together with all the gods) may be the receiver of the oblations in the sacrifices where all the gods gather together.

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पते॑रभवद्यथाव॒शं स॒त्यो म॒न्युर्महि॒ कर्मा॑ करिष्य॒तः । योगा उ॒दाज॒त्स दि॒वे वि चा॑भजन्म॒हीव॑ री॒तिः शव॑सासर॒त्पृथ॑क् ॥१४॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ब्रह्मणः । पतेः । अभवत् । यथावशं । सत्यः । मन्युः । महि । कर्म । करिष्यतः । यः । गाः । उत्आजत् । सः । दिवे । वि । च । अभजत् । महीs इव । रीतिः । शवसा । असरत् । पृथक् ॥ १४ ॥

brahmaṇaḥ | pateḥ | abhavat | yathāvaśaṃ | satyaḥ | manyuḥ | mahi | karma | kariṣyataḥ | yaḥ | gāḥ | utājat | saḥ | dive | vi | ca | abhajat | mahīs iva | rītiḥ | śavasā | asarat | pṛthak ‖ 14 ‖

p. 44

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

महि महत्कर्म करिष्यतो ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्मन्युर्मननसाधनो मंत्रः क्रोधो वा यथावशं यथाकामं सत्योऽवितथोऽभवत् । स यथा कामयते तथा करो- तीत्यर्थः । यो ब्रह्मणस्पतिः पणिभिरपहृता गा उदाजत् । उदगमयत् गुहाया निरगमयदित्यर्थः । स ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्दिवे द्युलोकाय तत्रत्येभ्यो देवेभ्य इत्यर्थः । व्यभजच्च । ता गा विभक्ताश्चाकरोत् । स च गोसमूहो महीव रीतिः । महती स्तुतिरितिव ॥ रीज् स्रवणे ॥ यथा गंगादीनां स्रोतो विभक्तं सत् निम्म दे- शाभिमुखं प्रसरति तथा शवसात्मीयेन बलेन तत्तद्देवगृहं पृथक् विभिन्नोऽसरत् । अगच्छत ॥

mahi mahatkarma kariṣyato brahmaṇaspatermanyurmananasādhano maṃtraḥ krodho vā yathāvaśaṃ yathākāmaṃ satyo 'vitatho 'bhavat | sa yathā kāmayate tathā karo- tītyarthaḥ | yo brahmaṇaspatiḥ paṇibhirapahṛtā gā udājat | udagamayat guhāyā niragamayadityarthaḥ | sa brahmaṇaspatirdive dyulokāya tatratyebhyo devebhya ityarthaḥ | vyabhajacca | tā gā vibhaktāścākarot | sa ca gosamūho mahīva rītiḥ | mahatī stutiritiva ‖ rīj sravaṇe ‖ yathā gaṃgādīnāṃ sroto vibhaktaṃ sat nimma de- śābhimukhaṃ prasarati tathā śavasātmīyena balena tattaddevagṛhaṃ pṛthak vibhinno 'sarat | agacchata ‖

Gist: Brahmaṇaspati's mantra (or wrath), meant to do a great deed, proved true by his will; he drove out the cows and divided them among the gods, and they flowed apart like rivers.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

mahi—great. karma—the work. kariṣyataḥ—of him who will accomplish. brahmaṇaspateḥ—of Brahmaṇaspati. manyuḥ—the mantra, an instrument of meditation (or his wrath). yathāvaśam—according to his wish. satyaḥ—true in effect (not in vain). anubhavat [?]—became. yaḥ—the Brahmaṇaspati who. gāḥ—the cows (carried off by the Paṇis). udājat—released and brought out from the cave. saḥ—that same Brahmaṇaspati. dive—to the gods of the world of the gods. vi abhajat ca—divided and distributed (then that herd of cows). mahīva rītiḥ—like the currents of rivers such as the Gaṅgā, splitting into branches and flowing apart. śavasā—by their own strength. pṛthak—(to the houses of the gods) separately. āsarat—went.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The mantra, an instrument of meditation, of Brahmaṇaspati who accomplishes great works, became fruitful in truth according to his wish. The same Brahmaṇaspati who released from the cave the cows carried off by the Paṇis divided them among the gods in the world of the gods. Then that herd of cows, like the currents of rivers such as the Gaṅgā breaking into branches and flowing apart, went by their own strength separately to the houses of the gods.

Printed English translation

The purpose of Brahmaspathi, engaging in a great work, has been successful, according to his wish ; for he it was who recovered (the stolen) cattle for (the dwellers in) heaven ; and distributed them ; so that of their own power they took different directions, like (the branches of) a mighty river.

p. 45

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ब्रह्मणस्पतेः मन्युः सत्यः (brahmaṇaspateḥ manyuḥ satyaḥ): here the word मन्यु (manyu) is explained in two ways, as मननसाधनो मंत्रः क्रोधो वा (mananasādhano maṃtraḥ krodho vā), a mantra or (क्रोध (krodha)) anger; since Brahmaṇaspati is one who performs great works, the mantra of this god, or his anger as well, is true. And सः यथा कामयते तथा करोति (saḥ yathā kāmayate tathā karoti): this god acts as he wishes, that is, he performs his actions (duties) with complete independence; so it is explained.

यः गाः उदजत्, सः दिवे विभजच्च (yaḥ gāḥ udajat, saḥ dive vibhajacca): this Brahmaṇaspati, पणिभिरपहृताः गाः उदगमयत् (paṇibhirapahṛtāḥ gāḥ udagamayat), brought back the cows seized by the demons, bringing them out of the cave and protecting them; द्युलोकाय तत्रत्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः विभक्ताश्च अकरोत् (dyulokāya tatratyebhyo devebhyaḥ vibhaktāśca akarot): he divided them and gave them to the gods dwelling in heaven. This narrative has been told earlier.

महीव रीतिः शवसा पृथक् असरत् यथा गंगादीनां स्रोतः विभक्तं सत् निम्म देशाभिमुखं प्रसरति तथा विभिन्नः तत्तद्देवगृहं आत्मीयेन बलेन अगच्छत (mahīva rītiḥ śavasā pṛthak asarat yathā gaṃgādīnāṃ srotaḥ vibhaktaṃ sat nimma deśābhimukhaṃ prasarati tathā vibhinnaḥ tattaddevagṛhaṃ ātmīyena balena agacchata): as the current of the Gaṅgā flows towards low-lying regions and branches, so this herd of cows, in separate droves, reached the houses of the respective gods; thus the comparison with the Gaṅgā's current is stated.

The word शवः (śavaḥ) is read by Yāska among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9).

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ब्रह्म॑णस्पते सु॒यम॑स्य वि॒श्वहा॑ रा॒यः स्या॑म र॒थ्यो॒३॒॑३वय॑स्वतः । वी॒रेषु॑ वी॒रा उप॑ पृंगि न॒स्त्वं यदीशा॑नो॒ ब्रह्म॑णा॒ वेशि॑ मे॒॑ हवं ॥ १५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ब्रह्मणः । पते । सुयमस्य । विश्वहा । रायः । स्याम । रथ्यः । वयस्वतः । वीरेषु । वीरान् । उप । पृंगि । नः । त्वं । यत् । ईशानः । ब्रह्मणा । वेषि । मे हवं ॥ १५ ॥

brahmaṇaḥ | pate | suyamasya | viśvahā | rāyaḥ | syāma | rathyaḥ | vayasvataḥ | vīreṣu | vīrān | upa | pṛṃgi | naḥ | tvaṃ | yat | īśānaḥ | brahmaṇā | veṣi | me havaṃ ‖ 15 ‖

p. 46

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे ब्रह्मणस्पते मंत्राधिपते सुयमस्य सुष्टु नियंतव्यस्य वयस्सतोऽन्न- युक्तस्य रायो धनस्य विश्वहा विश्लेषु सर्वॆष्टहःसु रथ्योऽधिपतयः स्याम । भूयास्म । रथा एषां संतीति रथ्यः ॥ छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्त्वर्थीय ईकारः ॥ अपि च नोऽस्माकं वीरेषु वीर्याज्जातेष्वस्मदीयेषु पुत्रेषु वीरान् पुत्रान् त्वमुप पृज्ञि । संपृक्तान् कुरु । उत्पादय ॥ पृची संपर्के । रौधादिकं ॥ वयं पौत्रानपि लभेमहीति यावत् । ईशानः सर्वस्येश्वरस्त्वं ब्रह्मणा ॥ अन्ननामैतत् ॥ हविर्लक्ष- णेनान्नेन सह मे हवं मदीयं स्तुतिलक्षणमाह्वानं वेषि । कामयसे ॥ वी गति- प्रजननकांत्यसनखादनेषु ॥ अतो मयोक्तं कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

he brahmaṇaspate maṃtrādhipate suyamasya suṣṭu niyaṃtavyasya vayassato 'nna- yuktasya rāyo dhanasya viśvahā viśleṣu sarvèṣṭahaḥsu rathyo 'dhipatayaḥ syāma | bhūyāsma | rathā eṣāṃ saṃtīti rathyaḥ ‖ chaṃdasīvanipāviti mattvarthīya īkāraḥ ‖ api ca no 'smākaṃ vīreṣu vīryājjāteṣvasmadīyeṣu putreṣu vīrān putrān tvamupa pṛjñi | saṃpṛktān kuru | utpādaya ‖ pṛcī saṃparke | raudhādikaṃ ‖ vayaṃ pautrānapi labhemahīti yāvat | īśānaḥ sarvasyeśvarastvaṃ brahmaṇā ‖ annanāmaitat ‖ havirlakṣa- ṇenānnena saha me havaṃ madīyaṃ stutilakṣaṇamāhvānaṃ veṣi | kāmayase ‖ vī gati- prajananakāṃtyasanakhādaneṣu ‖ ato mayoktaṃ kurvityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: May we be lords of well-regulated, food-bearing wealth every day; since you accept my invocation with oblation, grant heroic sons among our sons.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

brahmaṇaspate—O Brahmaṇaspati. suyamasya—of that which is excellently regulated. vayasvataḥ—and endowed with food. rāyaḥ—of wealth. viśvahā—on all days. rathyaḥ—as lords. syāma—may we be (grant it). yat—because. īśānaḥ—you, the lord of all. brahmaṇā—together with food in the form of the oblation. me—my. havam—invocation. veṣi—you desire (therefore). naḥ—our. vīreṣu—among the heroic sons. vīrān—heroic sons. upa pṛṅgi—cause them to be born.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Brahmaṇaspati, grant that we may be, on all days, lords of wealth that is excellently [निर्मितवादुदू (nirmitavādudū) "constructed", as supplied] ordered and endowed with food. Because you, lord of all, desire my invocation made with the food of the oblation, cause heroic sons to be born among our heroic sons.

Printed English translation

May we, Brahmanaspathi, be daily in the possession of well-regulated and food-supplying wealth: add for us posterity to posterity, since you, who are the ruler (of all), accept my invocation with (offered sacrificial) food.

p. 47

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 3, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 47.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this ṛk the word ब्रह्मणस्पते (brahmaṇaspate) is explained as मंत्राधिपते (maṃtrādhipate): Brahmaṇaspati is the lord (master) of all mantras; thus the address is explained.

The sacrificers: रायः विश्वहा रथ्यः स्याम (rāyaḥ viśvahā rathyaḥ syāma) — the wish is prayed for that they be lords, at all times, of riches that are certainly worth protecting and that come with food. For the word रथ्यः (rathyaḥ) the meaning is given as रथाः एषां संति (rathāḥ eṣāṃ saṃti), "those who possess chariots", lords.

नः वीरेषु वीर्रा उपपृच्छि (naḥ vīreṣu vīrrā upapṛcchi) (as supplied; the Ṛk reads vīrān upa pṛṅgi) — the word वीरेषु (vīreṣu) is explained as "those born of virility", i.e. sons; the prayer is that Brahmaṇaspati grant us, the sacrificers, grandsons as well.

ईशानः (īśānaḥ) — it is explained that Bṛhaspati is the lord of everything, and since this god desires ब्रह्मणा मे हवं वेषि (brahmaṇā me havaṃ veṣi), the invocation in the form of praise made by the sacrificer who comes with food in the form of the oblation, the wish is also expressed that he fulfil the sacrificers' desire.

Yāska has read the word ब्रह्म (brahma) among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) and also among the names of food. Here it is used in the sense of food.

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ब्रह्म॑णस्पते॒ त्वम॒स्य यं॒ता सू॒क्तस्य॑ बोधि॒ तन॑यं च जिन्व । विश्वं॒ तद्भ॒द्रं यदवं॑ति दे॒वा बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ १६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ब्रह्मणः । पते । त्वं । अस्य । यंता । सुउक्तस्य । बोधि । तनयं । च । जिन्व । विश्वं । तत् । भद्रं । यत् । अवंति । देवाः । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुवीराः ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे ब्रह्मणस्पते यंता सर्वस्य जगतो नियंता त्वमस्य सूक्तस्येदं सूक्तं॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्च तुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी॥ बोधि। बुध्यस्व ।

he brahmaṇaspate yaṃtā sarvasya jagato niyaṃtā tvamasya sūktasyedaṃ sūktaṃ‖ kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvācca turthyarthe ṣaṣṭhī‖ bodhi| budhyasva |

p. 48

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 24, p. 48.

बुद्धा तनयं पुत्रं चास्मभ्यं जिन्व । प्रेरय ॥ जिविः प्रीणनार्थः । अत्र प्रेरणे वर्तते धातूनामनेकार्थत्वात् ॥ यद्भद्रं कल्याणं देवाः सर्वॆSवंति रक्षंति विश्वं सर्वं तद्भद्रं च जिन्वेति शेषः । वयं च सुवीराः शोभनैर्विरैः पुत्रपौत्रा- दिभिरुपेताः संतो बृहत् प्रौढं स्तोत्रं विदथे । विदंति यष्टव्यतयास्मिन्देवान् जानंतीति विदथो यज्ञः । तस्मिन् वदेम । ब्रूयाम ॥ ३ ॥

buddhā tanayaṃ putraṃ cāsmabhyaṃ jinva | preraya ‖ jiviḥ prīṇanārthaḥ | atra preraṇe vartate dhātūnāmanekārthatvāt ‖ yadbhadraṃ kalyāṇaṃ devāḥ sarvèSvaṃti rakṣaṃti viśvaṃ sarvaṃ tadbhadraṃ ca jinveti śeṣaḥ | vayaṃ ca suvīrāḥ śobhanairviraiḥ putrapautrā- dibhirupetāḥ saṃto bṛhat prauḍhaṃ stotraṃ vidathe | vidaṃti yaṣṭavyatayāsmindevān jānaṃtīti vidatho yajñaḥ | tasmin vadema | brūyāma ‖ 3 ‖

Gist: O Brahmaṇaspati, controller of the world, hear this hymn and send us a son; send us all the good that the gods protect; blessed with fine sons may we recite exalted praise at the sacrifice (vidatha = sacrifice).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

brahmaṇaspate—O Brahmaṇaspati. yantā—controller of the whole world. tvaṃ—you. asya sūktasya—(recited by us) this hymn. bodhi—understand. yat—by which greatness. bhadraṃ—all good. devāḥ—the gods. avanti—protect. viśvaṃ—the whole. tat—that good. jinva—cause to come to us; (therefore) tanayaṃ ca—a son also (jinva—cause to be born to us). suvīrāḥ—we, accompanied by sons and others endowed with virility. bṛhat—exalted praise. vidathe—in this sacrifice. vadema—we shall recite.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Brahmaṇaspati, you, controller of the whole world, understand (hear) this hymn [पतितवाद (patitavāda) (patitavāda), "fallen", as supplied; presumably paṭhita, "recited" — [?]] by us. By the same greatness by which the gods protect all good, cause all good to come to us also. Therefore bring about the gain of a son. We, accompanied by sons and others endowed with virility, shall recite exalted praise at this sacrifice.

Printed English translation

Brahmanaspathi, you are the regulator of this (world), understand (the purport of) our hymn, and grant us posterity; for all is prosperous that the gods protect : (and therefore) may we, blessed with excellent descendants, glorify you at this sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Brahmaṇaspati, it is explained that this god is सर्वस्य जगतो नियंता (sarvasya jagato niyaṃtā), the controller of the whole world, and that अस्य सूक्तस्य बोधि (asya sūktasya bodhi) means he should listen to this hymn that we recite (the text prints पडिसुव (paḍisuva), "that we cause", for the expected पठिसुव (paṭhisuva) — as supplied).

तनयं च जिन्व—पुत्रं च प्रेरय । जिविः प्रीणनार्थोSत्र प्रेरणे वर्तते । (tanayaṃ ca jinva—putraṃ ca preraya | jiviḥ prīṇanārthoStra preraṇe vartate |) The root जिवि (jivi) is used in the sense "to gladden", but here it is used in the sense "to impel"

p. 49

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 4, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 49.

(Special Topics continued.) — thus Sāyaṇa explains; and the prayer is that Brahmaṇaspati hear this hymn of ours and impel our sons also to recite this hymn; and सर्वॆ देवाः सर्वं अवंति तत् भद्रं च जिन्व (sarvè devāḥ sarvaṃ avaṃti tat bhadraṃ ca jinva): that all the gods impel the good that protects the whole world to come to us.

सुवीराः—शोभनैः वीरैः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिरुपेताः (suvīrāḥ—śobhanaiḥ vīraiḥ putrapautrādibhirupetāḥ) — the word सुवीर (suvīra) is explained as children and grandchildren endowed with all kinds of good qualities; it is described that, accompanied by them, we recite exalted praises at sacrifices.

विदथे—यष्टव्यतया अस्मिन् देवान् जानाति इति विदथो यज्ञः । (vidathe—yaṣṭavyatayā asmin devān jānāti iti vidatho yajñaḥ |) The meaning of the word vidatha is explained: the rite in which oblations are offered with the gods in view is called a sacrifice.

Sūkta 25 (Maṇḍala 2)

The twenty-fifth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

इंधान इति पंचर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं जागतं ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इंधानः पंच जागतं त्विति । लैंगिको विनियोगः ॥

Gist: indhānaḥ is the third sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of five ṛks, by Gṛtsamada, in jagatī metre, with Brahmaṇaspati as deity; the application is by indication (liṅga).

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta indhāno agniṃ is the third sūkta of the third anuvāka. It has five ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada; the deity is Brahmaṇaspati; the metre is jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इंधानः पंच जागतं तु (iṃdhānaḥ paṃca jāgataṃ tu). The application (viniyoga) is laiṅgika.

Sūkta—25

Maṇḍala 2 ‖ Anuvāka 3 ‖ Sūkta 25 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 7 ‖ Varga 4 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 5 · Ṛṣi: Gṛtsamada · Devatā: as supplied बृह्णस्पतिः (bṛhṇaspatiḥ) (the Anuvāda gives Brahmaṇaspati) · Chandas: jagatī.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

इंधा॑नो अ॒ग्निं व॑नवद्वनुष्य॒तः कृ॒तब्र॑ह्मा शूशुवद्रा॒तह॑व्य॒ इत् । जा॒तेन॑ जा॒तमति॒ स प्र स॑र्सृते॒ यंयं॒ युजं॑ कृणु॒ते ब्रह्म॑ण॒- स्पतिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

iṃdhāno agniṃ vanavadvanuṣyataḥ kṛtabrahmā śūśuvadrātahavya it | jātena jātamati sa pra sarsṛte yaṃyaṃ yujaṃ kṛṇute brahmaṇa- spatiḥ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 50

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 25, p. 50.

Ṛk 1 (continued)

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इंधानः । अग्निं । वनवत् । वनुष्यतः । कृतब्रह्मा । शूशुवत् । रातहव्यः । इत् । जातेन । जातं । अति । सः । प्र । सर्सृते । यंयं । युजं । कृणुते । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अग्निमिंधानो ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्यागार्थमग्निं प्रज्वलयन्यजमानो वनु- ष्यतो हिंसिष्यतो हिंसां कुर्वतो वा शत्रून्वनवत् । वनुयात् हिंस्यात् ॥ वनुष्यतिर्हंतिकर्मति यास्कः । इदिति जार्थे ॥ कृतब्रह्मा ! ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं कृतं येन स तथोक्तः । रातहव्यः । रातं दत्तं हव्यं हविर्येन । एवंभूतः सन् शूशुवत् । वर्धते॥ टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योः। अस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुजु रूपं॥ तथा यजमानो जातेन पुत्रेण जातं जनितमुत्पादितं स्वस्य पौत्रमिति प्रसस्पृते : अतीत्य भृशं प्रसरति । पौत्रमपि पश्यन् चिरकालं जीवेदित्यर्थः ॥ सर्तेर्यज् लुगंताद्वत्य- येनात्मनेपदं ॥ यंयं यजमानं ब्रह्मणस्पतिः स्तोत्रहविषोः स्वीकरणेन युजं सखायं कृणुते । कुरुते । स समान एव भवतीत्यर्थः ॥

Gist: the sacrificer who kindles the fire for Brahmaṇaspati destroys hostile enemies, prospers through hymn and oblation, and lives long enough to see his grandson; the grammatical remarks (roots vanu, śuṣ/śū, sṛ) are noted but not explained.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(For the sacrifice addressed to Brahmaṇaspati) agnim—the fire; indhānaḥ—the sacrificer who makes it blaze; vanuṣyataḥ—the enemies who cause obstruction to the sacrifice; vanavat—he strikes and drives far away; it—and; kṛtabrahmā—composing hymns; rātahavyaḥ—offering oblations; śūśuvat—he gains increase; yaṃyam—whichever sacrificer; brahmaṇaspatiḥ—Brahmaṇaspati; yujam—as a friend; kṛṇute—makes (him his own); saḥ—that sacrificer; jātena—(beyond) the son; jātam—the grandson born; ati pra sarsṛte—passes beyond and lives long (he lives long enough to see grandsons and others also).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who makes the fire blaze for the sacrifice addressed to Brahmaṇaspati strikes down and drives far away the enemies who obstruct the sacrifice; and, composing hymns and offering oblations, he gains increase. The sacrificer whom Brahmaṇaspati makes his friend lives long, so that he sees all his sons and grandsons and rejoices.

p. 51

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 4, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 51.

Printed English translation

Kindling the fire, may (the worshipper) overcome the malevolent (disturbers of the rite); may he, repeating prayers, and laden with oblations, prosper; he whom Brahmanaspathi makes his associate, lives to behold the son of his son.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अग्निं इंधानः (agniṃ iṃdhānaḥ)—ब्रहणस्पतेर्यागार्थमग्निं प्रज्वलर्य यजमानः (brahaṇaspateryāgārthamagniṃ prajvalarya yajamānaḥ). Here the word indhānaḥ is given the sense "the sacrificer who kindles the fire"; the meaning is explained thus: in the sacrifice performed for Brahmaṇaspati, the sacrificer drives far away, by the greatness of the fire, all the enemies who harm him. Yāska reads वनुष्यतिर्हिंसा कर्मा (vanuṣyatirhiṃsā karmā) (Ni. 5-2) ["vanuṣyati means the act of harming"], and cites it, explaining वनुयाम (vanuyāma), वनुष्यतः (vanuṣyataḥ).

कृतब्रह्मा (kṛtabrahmā)—The word brahma is read by Yāska (Ni. 3-9) in the senses of food and wealth; Sāyaṇa here explains brahma as "hymn" with कृतं ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं येन (kṛtaṃ brahma stotraṃ yena).

जातेन जातं (jātena jātaṃ)—यजमानः पुत्रेण जनितं स्वस्य पौत्रं अतीत्य भृशं प्रसरति । पौत्रमपि पश्यन् चिरकालं जीवेत् (yajamānaḥ putreṇa janitaṃ svasya pautraṃ atītya bhṛśaṃ prasarati | pautramapi paśyan cirakālaṃ jīvet). Here jātena means "by the son", i.e. by the sacrificer's son; jātam means the grandson born of such a son. So the words jātena jātam mean the son of the sacrificer's son, i.e. the grandson. The prayer made here to Brahmaṇaspati is that he grant us sacrificers life to last until the time of such a grandson, so that we may go on living [the source's word जीनिसिरुवंतॆ (jīnisiruvaṃtè) is printed thus, as supplied].

ब्रह्मणस्पतिः यंयं युजं कृणुते सः (brahmaṇaspatiḥ yaṃyaṃ yujaṃ kṛṇute saḥ)—The explanation of the word brahmaṇaspati has been given earlier. Some hold that he is Bṛhaspati, others that he is a deity different from Bṛhaspati. It is explained that this god regards as his friend the sacrificer who has satisfied him with oblations and the like offered in his name, and makes him one of greatness equal to his own.

p. 52

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 25, p. 52.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वी॒रेभि॑र्वि॒रान्व॑नद्वनुष्य॒तो गोभी॑ र॒यिं प॑प्रथ॒द्योध॑ति॒ त्मना॑ । तो॒कं च॒ तस्य॒ तन॑यं च वर्धते॒ यंयं॒ युजं॑ कृणु॒ते ब्रह्म॑ण॒-॑ स्पतिः ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

वीरेभिः । वीरान् । वनवत् । वनुष्यतः । गोभिः । रयिं । पप्रथत् । बोधति । त्मना । तोकं । च । तस्य । तनयं । च । वर्धते । यंऽयं । युजं । कृणुते । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स यजमानो वीरेभिर्वीरैरात्मीयैः पुत्रैर्वनुष्यतो हिंसतो वीरान् शत्रुपुत्रान् वनवत् । वनुयात् हिंस्यात् । अपि च गोभिः सहितं धनं पप्रथत् । प्रथयति विस्तारयति ॥ प्रथयतेर्लुजि चज्येतद्रूपं ॥ तथा त्मना आत्मनैव बोधति । सर्वं जानाति । अनन्याधीनज्ञानो भवतीत्यर्थः । किंच तस्य यजमानस्य तोकं पुत्रस्तनयं ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ तनयस्तत्पुत्रश्च वर्धते । प्रवृद्दो भवति । यद्वा तोकं तनयं पुत्रं पौत्रं च ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्वर्धयति ॥ वृधिरंतर्भावितण्यर्थो द्रष्टव्यः । अन्यद्धतं ॥

Gist: that sacrificer, with his own sons, destroys the enemies' sons, increases wealth with cattle, knows everything by himself; his son and grandson prosper (or Brahmaṇaspati makes them prosper).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yaṃyam—whichever sacrificer; brahmaṇaspatiḥ—Brahmaṇaspati; yujam—as a friend; kṛṇute—makes (that sacrificer); vīrebhiḥ—together with his heroic sons; vanuṣyataḥ—the harming; vīrān—enemy sons; vanavat—he will strike down; (and) gobhiḥ—with cattle; rayim—wealth; paprathat—he extends and increases; tmanā—by his own power; bodhati—he knows everything; tasya—of that sacrificer; tokam ca—the son; tanayam ca—and the grandson; vardhate—gain increase.

p. 53

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 4, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 53.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer whom Brahmaṇaspati makes his friend, together with his heroic sons, strikes down the harming sons of his enemies; and he expands and increases his wealth together with cattle. By his own power he knows everything. The son and grandson of such a sacrificer attain increase.

Printed English translation

(Surrounded) by his descendants, may he surpass the malevolent descendants (of his adversaries), for hc [sic] is famed for great wealth of cattle, and understands (all things) of himself: his sons and grandsons prosper whom Brahmanaspathi makes his associate.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वीरेभिः वीरान् वनवत् (vīrebhiḥ vīrān vanavat)—Yāska explains वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान् वेतेर्वा स्याद्गतिकर्मणो वीरयतेर्वा (vīro vīrayatyamitrān vetervā syādgatikarmaṇo vīrayatervā) (Ni. 1-7, printed "ಸಿ." [sic]). From this the word vīra means one who destroys others by his own power (a hero). Here Sāyaṇa explains वीरेभिः (vīrebhiḥ) as आत्मीयैः पुत्रैः (ātmīyaiḥ putraiḥ), the sons (children) of the sacrificer, and वीरान् (vīrān) as the sons of enemies. The sense is: by the favour of Brahmaṇaspati may the sacrificer subdue the enemy heroes by the heroes on his own side.

गोभिः पप्रथत् (gobhiḥ paprathat)—गोभिस्सहितं धनं विस्तारयति (gobhissahitaṃ dhanaṃ vistārayati). For the word गौः (gauḥ) Yāska gives the meanings earth, animal, hide, phlegm, bowstring, the sun, the suṣumnā channel, rays (Ni. 2-5,6,7.8). Here the meaning "wealth in cows, consisting of cattle, horses, goats and other animals" (paśu) is given, and it is described that the sacrificer expands wealth of this kind by the favour of Brahmaṇaspati (the printed "ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಸ್ಪಣತಿ" is a slip of the supplied text).

त्मना बोधति (tmanā bodhati)—आत्मनैव सर्वं जानाति अनन्याधीनज्ञानो भवति (ātmanaiva sarvaṃ jānāti ananyādhīnajñāno bhavati). त्मना (tmanā) is explained as "by his own nature"; the sense that the sacrificer does so by the favour of Brahmaṇaspati is thereby made explicit.

तोकं तनयं वर्धते (tokaṃ tanayaṃ vardhate)—तोकं तनयस्तत्पुत्रः च प्रवृद्धो भवति (tokaṃ tanayastatputraḥ ca pravṛddho bhavati); or तोकं तनयं पुत्रं पौत्रं च वर्धयति ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (tokaṃ tanayaṃ putraṃ pautraṃ ca vardhayati brahmaṇaspatiḥ). Both senses are stated: Brahmaṇaspati makes the sacrificer's sons and grandsons increase, or by Brahmaṇaspati's favour they themselves increase.

p. 54

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 25, p. 54.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सिंधु॒र्न क्षोदः॒ शिमी॑वा ऋघाय॒तो वृषे॑व॒ वध्रे॑र॒भि व॒ष्टो-॑ जसा । अ॒ग्नेरि॑व॒ प्रसि॑ति॒र्नाह॒ वर्त॑वे॒ यंयं॒ युजं॑ कृणु॒ते ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सिंधुः । न । क्षोदः । शिमीवान् । ऋघायतः । वृषाइव । वध्रीन् । अभि । वष्टि । ओजसा । अग्नेः इव । प्रसितिः । न । अह । वर्तवे । यंयं । युजं । कृणुते । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सिंधुः स्यंदनशीला नदी क्षोदो न क्षुद्यमानं कूलं यथा भिनत्ति तथा शिमीवान् । शिमाति कर्मनाम । ब्रह्मणस्पतेः परिचरणात्मना कर्मणा युक्तो यजमान ऋघायतो हिंसतः शत्रून् ओजसा बलेनाभिवष्टि । हंतुमभितः कामयते ॥ वश कांतौ ॥ इदमपरं निदर्शनं । वृषेव वध्रीन् । वध्रयो निष्पिष्टमुष्का निर्वीर्या बलीवर्दाः । तान् यथा वृषा सेचनसमर्थः सवीर्यो वृषभोऽभिभवति तद्वच्छत्रूनभिभवतीत्यर्थः । अपि चासावग्नेरिव प्रसितिः । प्रसीयते बध्यतेnनयेति प्रसितिर्ज्वाला ॥ षिञ् बंधने । करणे क्तिन् ॥ यथाग्ने- र्ज्वालाप्रतिहतप्रसरा एवमपि न वर्तवे । वारयितुं निवर्तयितुं ना नैव शक्यते ॥ अहशब्दोऽवधारणे । वृणोतेरंतर्भावितण्यर्थात् वर्ततेर्वा तुमर्थे तवेन्प्रत्ययः । अन्यद्धतं ॥

Gist: the sacrificer, engaged in service of Brahmaṇaspati, overcomes the harming enemies by strength as a river breaks its bank and a bull throws down weak old oxen; like fire's flame he cannot be checked.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

sindhuḥ—the flowing river; kṣodaḥ na—as it cuts and splits its bank; vadhrīn—the impotent old oxen; vṛṣeva—as a strong bull throws them down; śimāvān [sic, as supplied]—the sacrificer engaged in the rite that serves Brahmaṇaspati; yaghāyataḥ [sic, as supplied]—the enemies who harm him; ojasā—by his strength; abhi vaṣṭi—surrounding them,

p. 55

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 4, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 55.

he wishes to destroy them; yaṃyam—whichever sacrificer; brahmaṇaspatiḥ—Brahmaṇaspati; yujam—as a friend; kṛṇute—makes (that sacrificer); agneḥ iva prasitiḥ—as fire spreads its flame and advances unobstructed; na vartave aha—(by anyone) he gains unstoppable increase.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a flowing river cuts and splits its bank, and as a strong bull throws down impotent old oxen, the sacrificer who is engaged in the service of Brahmaṇaspati wishes to surround with his strength and destroy the enemies who harm him. The sacrificer whom Brahmaṇaspati makes his friend gains an increase that no one can stop, as fire spreads its flame and advances unobstructed.

Printed English translation

As a river (washes away) its banks, so the devout worshipper, of Brahmanaspathi), [sic] overpowers his enemies by his strength, as a bull (overcomes) an ox : like the spreading flame of fire, it is impossible to stop him, whom Brahmanaspathi makes his associate.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

शिमीर्वा ऋघायतः ओजसा अभि वष्टि (śimīrvā ṛghāyataḥ ojasā abhi vaṣṭi)—The word शिमी (śimī) is read by Yāska among the names of action (Ni. 3-2), and it is also said शिमीति कर्मनाम, शमयतेर्वा शक्नोतेर्वा (śimīti karmanāma, śamayatervā śaknotervā) (Ni. 5-12). Sāyaṇa explains this passage as ब्रह्मणस्पतेः परिचरणात्मना कर्मणा युक्तो यजमानः हिंसतः शत्रुन् बलेन हंतुमभितः कामयते (brahmaṇaspateḥ paricaraṇātmanā karmaṇā yukto yajamānaḥ hiṃsataḥ śatrun balena haṃtumabhitaḥ kāmayate): the sacrificer who serves and worships Brahmaṇaspati desires to destroy with his strength those who harm him. Three similes are stated here. First, सिंधुः क्षोदः न (siṃdhuḥ kṣodaḥ na)—स्यंदनशीला नदी क्षुद्यमानं कूलं यथा भिनत्ति (syaṃdanaśīlā nadī kṣudyamānaṃ kūlaṃ yathā bhinatti): as a flowing river breaks and splits its bank. Second, वृषेव वध्रीन् (vṛṣeva vadhrīn)—वध्रयो निष्पिष्टमुष्का निर्वीर्या बलीवर्दाः र्तान् यथा सेचनसमर्थः सवीयः वृषभो अभिभवति (vadhrayo niṣpiṣṭamuṣkā nirvīryā balīvardāḥ rtān yathā secanasamarthaḥ savīyaḥ vṛṣabho abhibhavati) [the supplied text prints र्तान् (rtān) and सवीयः (savīyaḥ) thus]: as bulls of abundant strength gore and throw down feeble old oxen whose seed is crushed. Third, अग्नेरिव प्रसितिः (agneriva prasitiḥ)—यथा अग्निर्ज्वालाप्रतिहतप्रसरा वारयितुं निवर्तयितुं वा नैव शक्यते (yathā agnirjvālāpratihataprasarā vārayituṃ nivartayituṃ vā naiva śakyate): as the flame of a forest fire can neither be checked nor turned back;

p. 56

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 25, p. 56 (printed "ಸಾಯಣಭಾವ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ" in the supplied text).

thus it is described. By this it is described that the power of the sacrificer who has won Brahmaṇaspati's favour is most wonderful in overcoming his enemies.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तस्मा॑ अर्षंति दि॒व्या अ॑स॒श्चतः॒ स सत्व॑भिः प्रथ॒मो गोषु॑ गच्छति । अनि॑भृष्टतविषिर्हं॒त्योज॑सा॒ यंयं॒ युजं॑ कृणु॒ते ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तस्मै । अर्षंति । दिव्याः । असश्चतः । सः । सत्त्वभिः । प्रथमः । गोषु । गच्छति । अनिभृष्टतविषिः । हंति । ओजसा । यंयं । युजं । कृणुते । ब्रह्मणः पतिः ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

तस्यॆ यजमानाय दिव्या दिवि भवा वृष्टिलक्षणा आपोऽसश्चतोऽसज्यमाना अनिरुद्धाः सत्योऽर्षंति । गच्छंति प्राप्नुवंति ॥ आर्तेर्लॆटि रूपं ॥ तथा स यजमानः सत्वभिः । सत्वानः साधकाः परिचारकाः । तैः सहितः प्रथमोऽन्येभ्यो यजमानेभ्यः पूर्वभावी सन् गोषु गच्छति । गवादिधनं प्राप्नोतीत्यर्थः । किंच अनिभृष्टतविषिः । तविषीति बलनाम । अनिभृष्टा परैरबाधिता तविषी बलं यस्य तादृशः सन् ओजसा बलेन हंति शत्रून् ॥

Gist: for that sacrificer the rains of heaven pour unobstructed; with his attendants he is first to obtain cattle and wealth, and with unconquered strength he kills enemies.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yaṃyam—whichever sacrificer; brahmaṇaspatiḥ—Brahmaṇaspati; yujam—as a friend; kṛṇute—makes; tasmai—for that sacrificer; divyāḥ—the rains born of the heavenly world; asaścataḥ—without hindrance; arṣanti—pour; haḥ [sic, as supplied; for saḥ?]—he; satvabhiḥ—with his attendants; prathamaḥ—before other sacrificers; goṣu—wealth in the form of cattle; gacchati—obtains; anibhṛṣṭatavisiḥ—possessing strength that cannot be defeated by others; ojasā—by his vigour; hanti—he destroys (the enemies).

p. 57

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6 [sic, as supplied], Varga 4, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 57.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer whom Brahmaṇaspati makes his friend: for him the rains born of the heavenly world pour down without hindrance. Together with his attendants he obtains wealth in the form of cattle before other sacrificers. Possessing a strength that others cannot defeat, he destroys his enemies by his valour.

Printed English translation

For him, the unobstructed rains of heaven descend : first among the devout, he acquires (wealth) in cattle: of irresistible vigour, he destroys his enemies by his strength, whom Brahmanaspati makes his associate.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

For the sacrificers who please Brahmaṇaspati with oblations and the like, दिव्याः असश्चतः अर्षंति (divyāḥ asaścataḥ arṣaṃti): the waters produced from the excellent rain stored in the atmosphere will [?] (the word as supplied is मॊरकुवुवु (mòrakuvuvu)) as they wish. And सत्वभिः प्रथमः:—परिचारकैः सहितः अन्येभ्यः यजमानेभ्यः पूर्वभावी गोषु गच्चति (satvabhiḥ prathamaḥ:—paricārakaiḥ sahitaḥ anyebhyaḥ yajamānebhyaḥ pūrvabhāvī goṣu gaccati) [sic, गच्चति (gaccati) as supplied]: the sacrificer, accompanied by attendants, obtains wealth such as cattle. Further, अनिभृष्टतविषिः ओजसा बलेन हंति परैरबादिता तविषी यस्य तादृशः बलेन शत्रुहंति (anibhṛṣṭataviṣiḥ ojasā balena haṃti parairabāditā taviṣī yasya tādṛśaḥ balena śatruhaṃti): it is explained that the sacrificer who has earned Brahmaṇaspati's favour, possessing abundant strength that others cannot assail ("ಮತು" as supplied) and that suffices to subdue enemies, becomes able to subdue his enemies by it.

The word दिव्य (divya) is interpreted by Yāska as "born in heaven" दिविज (divija) (Ni. 7-18). The word तविषी (taviṣī) is stated among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9).

The word ओजः (ojaḥ) is stated both among the names of strength (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of water (Ni. 2-24), and is explained ओज ओजतेर्वा उज्जतेर्वा (oja ojatervā ujjatervā) (Ni. 6-8).

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तस्मा॒ इद्विश्वे॑ धुनयंत॒ सिंध॒वोऽच्छि॑द्रा॒ शर्म॑ दधिरे पु॒रूणि॑ । दे॒वानां॑ सु॒म्मे सु॒भगः॒ स ए॑धते॒ यंयं॒ युजं॑ कृणु॒ते ब्रह्म॑ण॒॑ स्पतिः ॥ ५ ॥

tasmā idviśve dhunayaṃta siṃdhavo 'cchidrā śarma dadhire purūṇi | devānāṃ summe subhagaḥ sa edhate yaṃyaṃ yujaṃ kṛṇute brahmaṇa spatiḥ ‖ 5 ‖

p. 58

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 25, p. 58.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तस्मै । इत् । विश्वे । धुनयंत । सिंधवः । अच्छिद्रा । शर्म । दधिरे । पुरूणि । देवानां । सुम्मे । सुभगः । सः । विधते । यंयं । युजं । कृणुते । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

तस्मा इत् तस्मा एव यजमानाय विश्वे सिंधवः सर्वाः स्यंदनशीला नद्यो धुनयंत । चलयंति । एतदभीष्टफलसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रवहंतीत्यर्थः । तथा अच्छिद्रा अच्छिद्राणि छिद्ररहितानि संततानि पुरूणि बहूनि शर्म शर्माणि सुखानि दधिरे । तस्मा एव धार्यंते । यद्वा शर्मेति गृहनाम । छिद्ररहितानि बहूनि सदनानि धार्यंते । सुभगः शोभनधनो देवानां सुम्मे देवैः प्रत्ये सुखे वर्तमानः सन् विधते । वर्धते । शिष्यं स्पष्टं ॥

Gist: for that sacrificer all the flowing rivers stream; many unbroken comforts (or houses) are held for him; rich in wealth and in the gods' favour he prospers.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yaṃyam—whichever sacrificer; brahmaṇaspatiḥ—Brahmaṇaspati; yujam—as a friend; kṛṇute—makes; tasmā it—for him alone; viśve sindhavaḥ—all the rivers; dhunayanta—flow; acchidrā—without break, everlasting; purūṇi—and abundant; śarma—comforts (or houses); dadhire—are held (for him); saḥ—that sacrificer; subhagaḥ—possessing excellent wealth; devānām—given by the gods; summe—while living in happiness; vidhate—enjoys increase.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer whom Brahmaṇaspati makes his friend: for his sake all the rivers flow. Comforts (houses) that are unbroken, everlasting and abundant are held for him alone. That sacrificer, possessing excellent wealth and living in the happiness given by the gods, enjoys increase. (The supplied text has "ಅವನಿಗೋ, / ಸ್ಕರವೇ" at the line break, for अवनिगोस्करवे (avanigoskarave) "for his sake".)

Printed English translation

Verily, for him all rivers flow : him do uninterrupted and numerous pleasures await : blessed with the felicity of the Gods he ever prospers, whom Brahmanaspati makes his associate.

p. 59

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 5, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 59.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

विश्वे सिंधवः तस्मा इत् धुनयंत (viśve siṃdhavaḥ tasmā it dhunayaṃta)—सर्वाः स्यंदनशीला नद्यः एतदभीष्टफलसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रवहंति (sarvāḥ syaṃdanaśīlā nadyaḥ etadabhīṣṭaphalasiddhyarthaṃ pravahaṃti): it is stated, as an extraordinary glory of Brahmaṇaspati, that all the rivers full of currents flow for the sacrificers who have pleased him, only so as to grant the desired objects.

अच्छिद्राणि पुरूणि शर्म दधिरे (acchidrāṇi purūṇi śarma dadhire)—अच्छिद्राणि (acchidrāṇi) means "without a break" (continuous, strung together without interruption). The word शर्म (śarma) is stated to mean both "house" and "comfort" (Ni. 3-13, as supplied, "ಸಿ."). It is described that the sacrificers obtain abundant comfort not mixed with sorrow and the like in the middle period, and छिद्ररहितानि बहूनि सदनानि (chidrarahitāni bahūni sadanāni), many firm houses.

Further, the sacrificer who has earned Brahmaṇaspati's favour—सुभगः देवानां सुम्मे विधते (subhagaḥ devānāṃ summe vidhate)—शोभनधनः देवैः प्रत्तॆ सुखे वर्तमानः वर्धते (śobhanadhanaḥ devaiḥ prattè sukhe vartamānaḥ vardhate) [sic, प्रत्तॆ (prattè) as supplied]: having excellent wealth and living in the excellent happiness granted by the gods, he grows; so it is described. The word सुम्म (summa) is read among the names of happiness (Ni. 3-13, as supplied, "ಸಿ.").

Sūkta 26 (Maṇḍala 2)

The twenty-sixth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

ऋजुरिति चतुर्यचं चतुर्थं सूक्तं गृत्समदस्यार्षं जागतं ब्राह्मणस्पत्यं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । ऋजुश्चतुष्कमिति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

Gist: ṛjuḥ is the fourth sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of four ṛks, by Gṛtsamada, in jagatī metre, with Brahmaṇaspati as deity; the application was stated before.

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta ṛjur is the fourth sūkta of the third anuvāka. It has four ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada; the deity is Brahmaṇaspati; the metre is jagatī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: ऋजुश्चतुष्कमिति (ṛjuścatuṣkamiti). The application (viniyoga) has been stated before, that is, it is as in the preceding sūkta.

Sūkta—26

p. 60

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 26, p. 60 (printed "ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ" in the supplied text).

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ऋ॒जुरिच्छंसो॑ वनवद्वनुष्य॒तो दे॑व॒यन्नि ददे॑वयंतम॒भ्य॑सत् । सु॒प्रा॒वीरिद्व॑नवत्पृ॒त्सु दु॒ष्टरं॒ यज्वेदय॑ज्यो॒र्वि भ॑जाति॒ भो-॑ जनं ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ऋजुः । इत् । शंसः । वनवत् । वनुष्यतः । देवयन् । इत् । अदेवयंतं । अभि । असत् । सुप्रअवीः । इत् । वनवत् । पृत्सु । दुस्तरं । यज्वा । इत् । अयज्योः । वि । भजाति । भोजनं ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ऋजुरित् आर्जवयुक्त एव । यद्वा मुंजतिः प्रसाधनकर्मा । स्तोत्राणां प्रसाधक एव तंसो ब्रह्मणस्पतेः स्तोता वनुष्यतो हिंसतः शत्रून् वनवत् । वनुयात् हिंस्यात् ॥ वनोतेर्हंतिकर्मण एतद्रूपं ॥ तथा देवयन्नित् देवं दानादिगुणयुक्तं ब्रह्मणस्पतिमात्मन इच्छन्नेव आदेवयंतं तद्वीपरीतं पुरुष मभ्यसत् । अभिभवेत् ॥ अस्तेर्लेट्येतद्रूपं ॥ तथा सुप्रावीरित् ॥ अवतेस्यप्यर्था- दौणादिक ईकारप्रत्ययः ॥ सुष्टु प्रकर्षेण ब्रह्मणस्पतेस्तरयितैव पृतु पृतनासु संग्रामेषु दुस्तरं तुरीतुमशक्यं वनवत् । हिंस्यात् । तथा यज्येत् ब्रह्मणस्पतिं हविषेष्टवानेव आयज्योरयज्जनो भोजनं भोगसाधनु विभजाति । विशेषेण भजेतेत्यर्थः ॥

Gist: the upright praiser of Brahmaṇaspati may slay hostile enemies; wishing for the god he overcomes the godless man; he overcomes foes hard to overcome in battles; the sacrificer enjoys the enjoyment of the non-sacrificer.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

ṛjur it—the very one of upright mind; śaṃsaḥ—the praiser (of Brahmaṇaspati); vanuṣyataḥ—the harming enemies; vanavat—may he destroy; devayan nit—wishing the favour of the god Brahmaṇaspati; adevayantam—the man without devotion to the gods; abhyasat—may he overcome; suprāvīr it—satisfying (Brahmaṇaspati) with worship; pṛtsu—in battles (the supplied text breaks off here, at संग्राम (saṃgrāma))

p. 61

Running head: Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 5, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 61.
