(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 1 continued from p. 60.) gaḷalli—in the (battles); dustaram—(printed दुस्तरं (dustaraṃ)) enemies who cannot be defeated by others; vanavat—may he destroy; yajyet—(as printed; the Saṃhitā has yajvā it) worshipping (Brahmaṇaspati) with oblation; ayajyoḥ—of the man without sacrifice; bhojanam—the wealth that is a means of enjoyment; vi bhajāti—may he obtain fully.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the one who praises Brahmaṇaspati with an upright mind destroy the harming enemies. Wishing the favour of Brahmaṇaspati, the divine one, may he overcome men who have no devotion to the gods. Satisfying Brahmaṇaspati with worship, may he destroy in battles the enemy who cannot be overcome by others. Worshipping Brahmaṇaspati with oblation, may he obtain fully the wealth, the means of enjoyment, of the man without sacrifice.

Printed English translation

May the sincere praiser (of Brahmanaspati) verily overcome (his) enemies; may the worshipper of the gods overcome him assuredly who does not reverence them: may the propitiator (of Brahmanaspati) overcome him who is difficult to be overcome in battles: may he who offers sacrifice appropriate the food of him who does not sacrifice

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this ṛk the word it is read in the words ṛjur it, devayan nit, suprāvīr it and yajvet [sic, as printed यज्वेत् (yajvet)]. For this word it, Yāska has cited, as "cid it is of many senses" (चिदित्येषोऽनेककर्मा (cidityeṣo 'nekakarmā), Ni. 1-4), the use of (cit) in many kinds of meanings. Here it is explained that the word is used in the sense of emphasis (avadhāraṇa) in all four places.

For the first word, ṛjur it, the explanation is आर्जुवयुक्त एव । यद्वा यंजति प्रसाधनकर्मा । स्तोत्राणां प्रसाधक एव (ārjuvayukta eva | yadvā yaṃjati prasādhanakarmā | stotrāṇāṃ prasādhaka eva) [the supplied text has ಯಂಜತಿ where Sāyaṇa's text of p. 60 has the root muñj; not changed]: the sacrificer who worships Brahmaṇaspati is one who is endowed with a straight path, or one who wins (him) over with praises; so the meaning is described.

देवयन्नित्-दानादिगुणयुक्तं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं आत्मन इच्छन्नेन (devayannit-dānādiguṇayuktaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ ātmana icchannena) [as supplied; apparently icchanneva]: the sacrificer is one who desires as his lord Brahmaṇaspati, who possesses the qualities of granting desired ends to those who worship him with praises and so on; so the meaning is explained.

p. 62

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 26, p. 62.

सुप्रावीत्—सुष्टु प्रकर्षेण ब्रह्मणस्पतेस्तर्पयित्यैव (suprāvīt—suṣṭu prakarṣeṇa brahmaṇaspatestarpayityaiva) [as supplied]: the sacrificer's quality is described as one who satisfies Brahmaṇaspati exceedingly.

यजेत्—ब्रह्मणस्पतिं हविषा इष्टवानेव (yajet—brahmaṇaspatiṃ haviṣā iṣṭavāneva): the sacrificer is one who delights Brahmaṇaspati in sacrifices with oblations. The qualities of the sacrificer having been described with these four words, it is further explained that the sacrificer rejects अदेवयंतं (adevayaṃtaṃ), those who do not worship Brahmaṇaspati, and the harming enemies, who lack these qualities; and that अयज्जनः भोगसाधनं विशेषेण भजते (ayajjanaḥ bhogasādhanaṃ viśeṣeṇa bhajate) [as supplied], he obtains the means of comfort of one who does not perform sacrifice.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यज॑स्व वीर॒ प्र वि॑हि मनाय॒तो भ॒द्रं मनः॑ कृणुष्व वृत्र॒तूर्ये॑ । ह॒विष्कृ॑णुष्व सु॒भगो॒ यथास॑सि॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पते॒रव॒ आ वृ॑णीमहे ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यजस्व । वीर । प्र । विहि । मनायतः । भद्रं । मनः । कृणुष्ट । वृत्रतूर्ये । हः । कृणष्ट्व । सुभगः । यथा । अससि । ब्रह्मणः । पतेः । आवः । आ । वृणीमहे ॥ २

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ऋषिरात्मीयं पुरुषं शास्ति । हे वीर विशेषेण स्तुतीनां प्रेरक सखे यजस्व । ब्रह्मणस्पतिं स्तुत्या पूजय । मनायतो मन एव शीघ्रं प्रवर्तमानान् हिंसकान् यद्वा अभिमन्यमानान् शत्रुन्प्रति प्रविहि । प्रकर्षेण युद्धार्थं गच्छ ॥ वी गत्यादिषु । छांदसो ह्रस्वः ॥ वृत्रतूर्ये वृत्राणामावारकाणां शत्रुणां हिंसाहेतुभूते संग्रामे भद्रं कल्याणं धार्ष्ट्योपेतं मनः कृणुष्ट । कुरुष्ट । ब्रह्मणस्पतेरनुग्रहात्तवैव जयो भविष्यति । तथा ब्रह्मणस्पतये हविश्वरपुरोडाशा- दिकं कृणुष्ट । कुरु । यथा त्वं सुभगः शोभनधनोऽससि । भवेः ॥ अस्तेर्लेट्य। डागमः ॥ ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्यागेन त्वं शोभनधनो भविष्यसीति यावत् । अपि च वयं ब्रह्मणस्पतेरवो रक्षणमाभिमुख्येन वृणीमहे । प्रार्थयामहे ॥

Gist: the seer instructs his own man: O hero, worship Brahmaṇaspati with praise, go forth against the swift hostile enemies, make a brave mind, prepare oblations so that you prosper; we also solicit his protection.

Note on the text as supplied: the Pada line has कृणुष्ट (kṛṇuṣṭa) and कृणष्ट्व (kṛṇaṣṭva) for the Saṃhitā's कृणुष्व (kṛṇuṣva), and हः (haḥ) where हविः (haviḥ) would be expected; the bhāṣya has कृणुष्ट (kṛṇuṣṭa), हविश्वर (haviśvara) and अससि (asasi). Left as supplied.

p. 63

Running head: Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Varga 5, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 63.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

vīra—O friend, who in a special way urge on the praise; yajasva—offer worship (to Brahmaṇaspati); manāyataḥ—(to defeat) the enemies who advance swiftly; pra vihi—set out facing the battle; vṛtratūrye—in the battle that destroys Vṛtra and the others; bhadram—firmly established and bringing welfare; manaḥ—the mind; kṛṇuṣṭva (printed कृणुष्ट्व (kṛṇuṣṭva))—make; yathā—in what manner; subhagaḥ—possessing excellent wealth; asasi—you become (in that way); haviḥ—cooked offerings, purodāśa and the like; kṛṇuṣṭva—(for Brahmaṇaspati) prepare; (vayaṃ—we also); brahmaṇaspateḥ—of Brahmaṇaspati; avaḥ—the protection; ā—facing it; vṛṇīmahe—we solicit.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificer, who in a special way urge on the praise, offer worship to Brahmaṇaspati. Set out facing the battle to defeat the enemies who advance swiftly, wishing only harm to you in their minds. In the battle that destroys Vṛtra and the others, make a mind that is firmly established and brings welfare. In the manner by which you become possessed of excellent wealth, prepare for Brahmaṇaspati the cooked offerings, purodāśa and the like. We also, facing it, solicit the protection of Brahmaṇaspati. (The supplied text has "ಪ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ", "I solicit", in the singular; and "ಮನ್ನುಗ್ಗಿ" for ಮುನ್ನುಗ್ಗಿ.)

Printed English translation

Offer worship, O man, (to Brahmanaspati): proceed resolutely against those who are meditating (hostility): keep your mind firm in contending against foes: offer oblations whereby you may be prosperous: we also solicit the protection of Brahmanaspathi.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

The manner in which the seer, the seer of the mantra, instructs his own men, those dear to him, is stated in this mantra.

vīra yajasva—here the word vīra is explained as स्तुतीनां प्रेरक सखे (stutīnāṃ preraka sakhe), "friend who urges on the praises" (the supplied Kannada has "ಪರಿಸುವ", apparently for prerisuva, "urging"); and the injunction is expressed that Brahmaṇaspati must be worshipped with praise.

मनायतः विहि—मन इव शीघ्रं प्रवर्तमानान्, हिंसका. अभिमन्यमानान् शत्रु प्रति युद्धार्थं गच्छ (manāyataḥ vihi—mana iva śīghraṃ pravartamānān, hiṃsakā. abhimanyamānān śatru prati yuddhārthaṃ gaccha) [as supplied]: with a swiftness abundant like the speed of the mind, rush forward... (the supplied text breaks off here, at ಮುನ್ನುಗ್ಗಿ).

p. 64

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 7, Sūkta 26, p. 64 (printed "ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ" in the supplied text).

(Special Topics of Ṛk 2 continued from p. 63.) ...forward, coming and doing violence, or against enemies who are full of arrogance: so it is said.

vṛtratūrye bhadraṃ manaḥ kṛṇuṣṭa—Sāyaṇa explains the word vṛtra in this sentence as used in the sense of enemies who envelop and do harm. Yāska has explained the various meanings of the word vṛtra (Ni. 2-16), and the word vṛtratūrya he has read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). Here it is stated, as the view of the seer of the mantra, that a mind endowed with courage should be employed against the enemies who practise violence, and that "by the favour of Brahmaṇaspati victory will be yours alone" (ब्रह्मणस्पतेरनुग्रहात्तवैव जयो भविष्यति (brahmaṇaspateranugrahāttavaiva jayo bhaviṣyati)).

यथा त्वं सुभगः आससि—ब्रह्मणस्पतेर्यागेन त्वं शोभनधनो भविष्यसि (yathā tvaṃ subhagaḥ āsasi—brahmaṇaspateryāgena tvaṃ śobhanadhano bhaviṣyasi): it is said that by performing sacrifice with Brahmaṇaspati as the object, the attainment of excellent wealth will come about. And वयं ब्रह्मणस्पतेः अवः आवृणीमहे (vayaṃ brahmaṇaspateḥ avaḥ āvṛṇīmahe), "we greatly desire protection from Brahmaṇaspati": this wish is also expressed.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स इज्जने॑न॒ स वि॒शा स जन्म॑ना॒ स पु॒त्रैर्वाजं॑ भरते॒ धना॒ नृभिः॑ । दे॒वानां॒ यः पि॒तर॑मा॒विवा॑सति श्र॒द्धाम॑ना ह॒विषा॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिं॑ ॥ ३ "

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सः । इत् । जनेन । सः । विशा । सः । जन्मना । सः । पुत्रैः । वाजं । भरते । धना । नृभिः । देवानां । यः । पितरं । आविवासति । श्रद्धामनाः । हविषा । ब्रह्मणः । पतिं ॥ ३ ॥

saḥ | it | janena | saḥ | viśā | saḥ | janmanā | saḥ | putraiḥ | vājaṃ | bharate | dhanā | nṛbhiḥ | devānāṃ | yaḥ | pitaraṃ | āvivāsati | śraddhāmanāḥ | haviṣā | brahmaṇaḥ | patiṃ ‖ 3 ‖

p. 65

Running head: Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 7 [sic, as supplied], Varga 5, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 65. (The running head was merged into the Pada block in the supplied text; placed here by hand.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यो यजमानः श्रद्धामनाः श्रद्धा मनसि यस्य शादृशः सन् देवानां पितरं पालयितारं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं हविषा चरुपुरोडाशादिनाविवासति । परिचरति ॥ विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा ॥ स इत् स एव यजमानो जनेन जातेन सर्वेण लोकेन वाजमन्नं भरते बिभर्ति संभरति वा । स एव विशा प्रजया जन्मनात्मीयेन बंधु- जनेन वाजं भरते । स एव पुत्रैरात्मीयैरपत्यैर्वाजं भरते । तथा नृभिर्नतृभि- रन्यैः परिचारकैर्धना धनानि भरते । बिभर्ति संपादयति वा । ब्रह्मणस्पतिमिष्टवतो यजमानस्य सर्वतो जना अन्नधनयोः साधका भवंतीति यावत् ॥

Gist: the sacrificer who serves Brahmaṇaspati, father of the gods, with oblations obtains food and wealth through all people, his kin, sons and attendants.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यः (yaḥ)—the sacrificer who; श्रद्धामनाः (śraddhāmanāḥ)—having a mind full of faith; देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods; पितरं (pitaraṃ)—the protector; ब्रह्मणस्पतिं (brahmaṇaspatiṃ)—Brahmaṇaspati; हविषा (haviṣā)—with cooked offerings, caru, purodāśa and the like; आ विवासति (ā vivāsati)—serves and worships; स इत् (sa it)—that sacrificer alone; (as his own kin) जन्मना जनेन (janmanā janena)—with all the people who have come into being; वाजं (vājaṃ)—food; भरते (bharate)—obtains; सः (saḥ)—he alone; विशा (viśā)—with his subjects (obtains food); सः (saḥ)—he alone; पुत्रैः (putraiḥ)—with his sons (obtains food); नृभिः (nṛbhiḥ)—with men who are his attendants; धना (dhanā)—(obtains) riches.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who, with a mind full of faith, attends and worships Brahmaṇaspati, the protector of the gods, with caru, purodāśa and the like, that sacrificer alone obtains food together with all those who have come into being as his kin, together with his subjects and with his sons. That sacrificer alone obtains riches together with the men who are his attendants. (The supplied text has "ಚರುಪುರೋಡಾರಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ" for ಚರುಪುರೋಡಾಶಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ, and "ನರದೊಡನೆ", apparently for ನರರೊಡನೆ; left as supplied.)

Printed English translation

He who with a believing mind worships Brahmanaspati, the father of the gods, with oblations. he verily receives food, together with his sons, his kindred. his descendants. his people, and (obtains) riches together with (all) men.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ब्रह्मणस्पतिमिष्टवतो यजमानस्य जनाः सर्वतो अन्नधनयोः साधकाः भवंति (brahmaṇaspatimiṣṭavato yajamānasya janāḥ sarvato annadhanayoḥ sādhakāḥ bhavaṃti): all people, in many ways, give food and wealth and help the sacrificer who performs a sacrifice directed to the god Brahmaṇaspati. This meaning is explained in this Ṛk by four sentences

p. 66

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 26, p. 66.

(continued) ...four sentences.

श्रद्धामनाः हविषा आ विवासति स इत् वाजं भरते (śraddhāmanāḥ haviṣā ā vivāsati sa it vājaṃ bharate): here the word विवासति (vivāsati) Yāska (Ni. 3-13-11-23, as printed) has read among the words meaning service. It is stated that the sacrificer who, full of devotion, has satisfied Brahmaṇaspati with oblations obtains food and nourishes all others.

In the same way, आत्मीयेन बंधुजनेन, आत्मीयैरपत्यैः नेतृभिरन्यैः परिचारकैः वाजं भरते संपादयति वा (ātmīyena baṃdhujanena, ātmīyairapatyaiḥ netṛbhiranyaiḥ paricārakaiḥ vājaṃ bharate saṃpādayati vā): it is explained that for a sacrificer of this kind his kinsfolk, his sons, and the servants who attend him also obtain food and wealth and are nourished by him. (The supplied text has "ಅವನು ಪುತ್ರರೂ" and "ವಿವರಿಸಿದೆ" preceded by "ಎಂದ"; left as supplied.)

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यो अ॑स्मै ह॒वैर्घृ॒तव॑द्भि॒रवि॑ध॒त्प्र, तं प्रा॒चा न॑यति॒ ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पतिः॑ । उ॒रु॒ष्यती॒मंह॑सो॒ रक्ष॑शी रि॒षो३ं॒३॒॑होश्चि॑दस्मा उरु॒चक्रि॒रद्भु॑तः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । अस्मै । हव्यैः । धृतवत्भिः । अविधत् । प्र । तं । प्राचा । नयति । ब्रह्मणः । पतिः । उरुष्यति । ईं । आंहसः । रक्षति । रिषः । आंहोः । चित् । अस्मै । उरुचक्रिः । अद्भुतः ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यो यजमानोऽस्मै ब्रह्मणस्पतये ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थी ॥ इमं ब्रह्मणस्पतिं धृतवद्भिरुपस्तरणाभिघारणात्मकेनाज्ये- नोपेतैर्हवैर्हविर्भिरविधत् । परिचरति ॥ विध विधाने तौदादिकः । आयं परिचरण-

yo yajamāno 'smai brahmaṇaspataye ‖ kriyāgrahaṇaṃ kartavyamiti karmaṇaḥ saṃpradānatvāccaturthī ‖ imaṃ brahmaṇaspatiṃ dhṛtavadbhirupastaraṇābhighāraṇātmakenājye- nopetairhavairhavirbhiravidhat | paricarati ‖ vidha vidhāne taudādikaḥ | āyaṃ paricaraṇa-

p. 67

Running head: Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 5, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 67.

कर्मसु पठितः ॥ तं यजमानं ब्रह्मणस्पतिः प्राचा प्राचीनेन ऋजुना मार्गेण प्रणयति । प्रकृष्टफलं प्रापयति । अपि च ईमेनमंहसः पापादुरुष्यति । रक्षति ॥ उरुष्यती रक्षाकर्मेति यास्कः ॥ तथा रिषो हिंसकादेनं रक्षति । अंहोश्चित् । अवृत्तेर्दारिद्रात् । यद्वा अगत्य हंतुरपि रक्षति । अपि चास्मै यजमानायाद्भुतः । महन्नामैतत् । आश्चर्यभूतो महान् ब्रह्मणस्पतिरुरुचक्रिरुरोविस्तीर्णस्योप- कारस्य कर्ता भवति ॥

Gist: Brahmaṇaspati leads the worshipper by a straight path to his reward, protects him from sin, the harmful foe and poverty, and as a great and wonderful one does him many favours.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यः (yaḥ)—the sacrificer who; अस्मै (asmai)—with this Brahmaṇaspati as the object; धृतवद्भिः (dhṛtavadbhiḥ)—endowed with ghee; हव्यैः (havyaiḥ)—with oblations; अविधत् (avidhat)—worships; तं (taṃ)—that sacrificer; ब्रह्मणस्पतिः (brahmaṇaspatiḥ)—Brahmaṇaspati; प्राचा (prācā)—by a most straight path; प्र नयति (pra nayati)—leads towards the fruit; (and) ईं (īṃ)—this sacrificer; अंहसः (aṃhasaḥ)—from sin; उरुष्यति (uruṣyati)—protects; रिषः (riṣaḥ)—from the harmful enemy; रक्षति (rakṣati)—protects; अंहोश्चित् (aṃhościt)—from the sin in the form of poverty also (protects); अस्मै (asmai)—to this same sacrificer; अद्भुतः (adbhutaḥ)—the great-souled Brahmaṇaspati; उरुचक्रिः (urucakriḥ)—becomes also abundantly a benefactor.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who worships Brahmaṇaspati with oblations endowed with ghee, that sacrificer Brahmaṇaspati leads along a most straight path towards the fruit. And he protects this sacrificer from sin, from the harmful enemy and from poverty. To this same sacrificer the great-souled Brahmaṇaspati becomes abundantly a benefactor.

Printed English translation

Brahmanaspathi leads by a straight path (to his reward), the worshipper who propitiates him with oblations of butter : he guards him against sin; he protects him from foes and from distresss [sic] ; and wonderful (in might), confers upon him many (favours)-

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

तं प्राचा प्रनयति—ब्रह्मणस्पतिः ऋजुना मार्गेण प्रकृष्टं फलं प्रापयति (taṃ prācā pranayati—brahmaṇaspatiḥ ṛjunā mārgeṇa prakṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prāpayati): Brahmaṇaspati, pleased by the offerings of oblations and the like, accompanied by the substances beginning with ghee (printed धृतादि (dhṛtādi)) which have been prepared (the supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the page, after "ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಪತಿಯು").

p. 68

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 27, p. 68.

leads the sacrificer along the right path and makes him a sharer of excellent fruit. Here the word प्राचा (prācā) is explained as प्राचीनेन (prācīnena): it is made clear that the meaning is a straight path followed by the forefathers.

ईं अंहसः उरुष्यति—एनं पापात् रक्षति (īṃ aṃhasaḥ uruṣyati—enaṃ pāpāt rakṣati): for the particle ईं (īṃ) the meaning "this sacrificer" is given here. Yāska has explained पादपूरणास्ते अनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति (pādapūraṇāste anarthakāḥ kamīmidviti) (Ni. 1-9): the particles कं, ईं, इत्, उ (kaṃ, īṃ, it, u) are employed only to fill out a sentence and convey no meaning of their own. Having commented उरुष्यती रक्षाकर्मा इति यास्कः (uruṣyatī rakṣākarmā iti yāskaḥ), it is described that Brahmaṇaspati protects the sacrificer from sins.

For the word अंहोश्चित् (aṃhościt), two meanings are given: अवृत्तेर्दारिद्र्यात् यद्वा अगत्य हंतुरपि (avṛtterdāridryāt yadvā agatya haṃturapi), that is, from poverty (want of livelihood), or from one who comes near and kills; it is stated that Brahmaṇaspati protects from these.

अस्मै अद्भुतः—आचार्यभूतः महान् (asmai adbhutaḥ—ācāryabhūtaḥ mahān): the word अद्भुत (adbhuta) is stated among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13). It is described that Brahmaṇaspati, being a teacher and a revered one to the sacrificer, performs abundant service for him.

Sūkta 27 (Maṇḍala 2)

The twenty-seventh sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

इमा गिर इति सप्तदशर्चं पंचमं सूक्तं गृत्समदपुत्रस्य कूर्मस्यार्षं गृत्समदस्यैव वा त्रैष्टुभमादित्यदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । इमा गिरस्त्रूना कूर्मो गार्त्समदो हि वादित्यमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । आदित्यदेवताके पशौ पुरोडाशस्यॆमा गिर इत्येषानुवाक्या । अग्नीषोमाविति खंडे सूत्रितं । इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतसूस्त आदित्यास उरवो गभीराः । आ-३-८ । इति ॥

Gist: imā giraḥ is the fifth sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of seventeen ṛks, by Kūrma son of Gṛtsamada (or Gṛtsamada himself), in triṣṭubh metre, with the Ādityas as deity; its application is by indication (laiṅgika), the first ṛk being the anuvākyā for the oblation cake in an animal sacrifice to the Ādityas.

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta imā giraḥ is the fifth sūkta of the third anuvāka. It has seventeen ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kūrma, son of Gṛtsamada, or it is said that Gṛtsamada himself is the seer. The Ādityas are the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: इमा गिरस्त्रूना कूर्मो गार्त्समदो हि वादित्यमिति (imā girastrūnā kūrmo gārtsamado hi vādityamiti) [as supplied]. The application of the sūkta is laiṅgika (by indication). In an animal sacrifice related to the Ādityas, the first ṛk of this sūkta, imā giraḥ, is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra while the oblation cake is offered; this is set out by the sūtra imā gira ādityebhyo ghṛtasūsta ādityāsa uravo gabhīrāḥ in the section Agnīṣomau of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 3-8).

p. 69

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 6, p. 69.

Sūkta—27

Maṇḍala 2 ‖ Anuvāka 3 ‖ Sūkta 27 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 7 ‖ Varga 6, 7, 8 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 17 · Ṛṣi: as supplied "ಕರ್ಮೋ ಗಾತ್ಸರ್ಮವೋ ಗೃತ್ಸಮದೋ ವಾ" (Kūrma Gārtsamada, or Gṛtsamada; the supplied reading is garbled, left as supplied) · Devatā: the Ādityas · Chandas: triṣṭubh (the supplied text has "ಭಂದುಃ" for the label).

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

इ॒मा गिर॑ आदि॒त्येभ्यो॑ घृ॒तस्नूः॑ स॒नाद्राज॑भ्यो जु॒ह्वा॑ जुहोमि । शृ॒णोतु॑ मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा भगो॑ नस्तुविजा॒तो वरु॑णो॒ दक्षो॒॑ अंशः ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इमाः । गिरः । आदित्येभ्यः । धृतस्नूः । सनात् । राजभ्यः । जुह्वा । जुहोमि । शृणोतु । मित्रः । अर्यमा । भगः । नः । तुविजातः । वरुणः । दक्षः । अंशः ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

आदित्येभ्योऽदितेः पुत्रेभ्यो राजभ्यो राजमानेभ्य ईश्वरेभ्यो वा मित्रादिभ्यो धृतस्नूर्घृतप्रस्राविणीर्घृतं क्षरंतीरिमा गिरः स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचः सनात्सर्वदा जुह्वा । वाज्ञामैतत् । वागिंद्रियेण जुहोमि । प्रयच्छामि । करो- मिति यावत् ! यद्वा जुहूस्थानीयेन धृतं क्षरंति वाग्रूपाणि हवींषि जुहोमि। आदित्यानुद्दिश्य त्यजामि । मंत्राणां पयोघृतादिक्षणहेतुत्वं च य ऋचोऽधीते पयसः कूल्या अस्येत्यादिना तैत्तिरीयके स्पष्टमाम्मातं । तै. आ. २. १०. ७. । नोऽस्मदीयस्ता गिरो मित्रादयः प्रत्येकं शृणोतु । ते च तैत्तिरीयेऽष्टौ पुत्रासो आदितेरित्युपक्रम्य स्पष्टमनुक्रांताः । मित्रश्च वरुणश्च धाता चार्यमा

ādityebhyo 'diteḥ putrebhyo rājabhyo rājamānebhya īśvarebhyo vā mitrādibhyo dhṛtasnūrghṛtaprasrāviṇīrghṛtaṃ kṣaraṃtīrimā giraḥ stutilakṣaṇā vācaḥ sanātsarvadā juhvā | vājñāmaitat | vāgiṃdriyeṇa juhomi | prayacchāmi | karo- miti yāvat ! yadvā juhūsthānīyena dhṛtaṃ kṣaraṃti vāgrūpāṇi havīṃṣi juhomi| ādityānuddiśya tyajāmi | maṃtrāṇāṃ payoghṛtādikṣaṇahetutvaṃ ca ya ṛco 'dhīte payasaḥ kūlyā asyetyādinā taittirīyake spaṣṭamāmmātaṃ | tai. ā. 2. 10. 7. | no 'smadīyastā giro mitrādayaḥ pratyekaṃ śṛṇotu | te ca taittirīye 'ṣṭau putrāso āditerityupakramya spaṣṭamanukrāṃtāḥ | mitraśca varuṇaśca dhātā cāryamā

p. 70

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 27, p. 70.

च अंशुश्च भगश्च इंद्रश्च विवस्वांश्चेत्येत इति । मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायकः । यद्वा सर्वेषां स्निग्धः । अरीन् यच्छति नियच्छतीत्यर्यमा ! भगो भजनीयो देवः । तुवीति बहुनाम । बहुषु देशेष्वनुग्रहार्थं प्रादुर्भूतः । वरुणविशेषणमेतत् । पापस्य निवारणाद्वरुणः । दक्षः समर्थः । एतच्चांशस्य विशेषणं । एते प्रत्येकं शृण्वंतु ॥

Gist: To the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, I offer these ghee-flowing praises with the ladle of speech; may Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa and Aṃśa each hear them.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

आदित्येभ्यः (ādityebhyaḥ)—to the sons of Aditi; राजभ्यः (rājabhyaḥ)—to the shining ones, the deities Mitra and the rest, addressing them; धृतस्नूः (dhṛtasnūḥ)—that cause ghee to flow; इमा गिरः (imā giraḥ)—these words in the form of praise; सनात् (sanāt)—always; जुह्वा (juhvā)—by means of the ladle (juhū) that is the organ of speech; जुहोमि (juhomi)—I offer [the supplied text has "ಆರ್ಪಿಸುತ್ತೇನೆ"]; नः (naḥ)—these praise-words of ours; मित्रः (mitraḥ)—Mitra; अर्यमा (aryamā)—Aryaman; भगः (bhagaḥ)—Bhaga; तुविजातः (tuvijātaḥ)—(for the good of the world) born in many places; वरुणः (varuṇaḥ)—Varuṇa; दक्षः (dakṣaḥ)—Dakṣa; अंशः (aṃśaḥ)—Aṃśa; शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—let hear.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To the sons of Aditi, the shining Mitra and the other deities, I offer always these praise-words, which cause ghee to flow, by means of the ladle that is the organ of speech. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa who is born in many places for the good of the world, Dakṣa and Aṃśa hear these praise-words of ours.

Printed English translation

I present cotinually [sic], with the ladle (of speech), these oblation-droping [sic] hymns to the royal Adityas: May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, the multipresent Varuna, the powerful Ansha, hear us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आदित्येभ्यः राजभ्यः धृतस्नूः गिरः जुह्वा जुहोमि—आदितिपुत्रेभ्यः राजमानेभ्य ईश्वरेभ्यो वा मित्रादिभ्यः धृतं क्षरंतीः स्तुतिलक्षणाः वाचः वागिंद्रियेण करोमि (ādityebhyaḥ rājabhyaḥ dhṛtasnūḥ giraḥ juhvā juhomi—āditiputrebhyaḥ rājamānebhya īśvarebhyo vā mitrādibhyaḥ dhṛtaṃ kṣaraṃtīḥ stutilakṣaṇāḥ vācaḥ vāgiṃdriyeṇa karomi): one kind of meaning has been described thus: to the sons of Goddess Aditi, who shine with brilliance or are lords of all, Mitra and the rest, I offer, with the organ of speech, praises that pour nectar (ghee), as one makes an oblation with the ladle, the instrument of sacrifice.

Secondly: यद्वा जुहूस्थानीयेन धृतं क्षरंति वाग्रूपाणि हवींषि आदित्यानुद्दिश्य त्यजामि (yadvā juhūsthānīyena dhṛtaṃ kṣaraṃti vāgrūpāṇi havīṃṣi ādityānuddiśya tyajāmi): addressing the Ādityas, with the [supplied text breaks off here, at the end of the page, in the words "ಜೂಹೂ ಎಂಬ ಹೋಮ"] ladle called juhū, the sacrificial instrument of oblation

p. 71

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 6, p. 71.

(Special Topics of Ṛk 1, continued) …the ladle, I offer oblations in the form of speech that pour ghee, through the organ of speech, which is like a vessel for making the oblation. This is how it is explained. The point that the mantras offer ghee and other substances abundantly is supported by the sentence of the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa, यदृचोऽधीते पयसः कुल्या अस्य (yadṛco 'dhīte payasaḥ kulyā asya) (Tai. Brā. 2-10).

जुह्वा (juhvā)—वागिंद्रियेण (vāgiṃdriyeṇa)—वाज्ञामैतत् (vājñāmaitat) [sic, as supplied]: such is also Sāyaṇa's explanation. Yāska has read the word जिह्वा (jihvā) among the names of speech (Si. 2-23).

नः शृणोतु (naḥ śṛṇotu)—for this sentence Sāyaṇa explains अस्मदीयाः ताः गिरः मित्रादयः प्रत्येकं शृणोतु (asmadīyāḥ tāḥ giraḥ mitrādayaḥ pratyekaṃ śṛṇotu): may Mitra and the other Ādityas, each separately, all hear these our words of praise that we, the praisers, offer. He then quotes the sentence of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, "अष्टौ पुत्रासो अदितेः (aṣṭau putrāso aditeḥ) … मित्रश्च वरुणश्च धाताचार्यमाच अंशुश्च भगश्च इंद्रश्च विवस्वांश्चेत्येते (mitraśca varuṇaśca dhātācāryamāca aṃśuśca bhagaśca iṃdraśca vivasvāṃścetyete)" (Tai. Ā. 1-13-3), which says that the goddess Aditi has eight sons: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryamā, Aṃśu, Bhaga, Indra and Vivasvān.

मित्रः (mitraḥ)—प्रमितेस्त्रायकः यद्वा सर्वेषां स्निग्धः (pramitestrāyakaḥ yadvā sarveṣāṃ snigdhaḥ): Sāyaṇa explains the word Mitra as one who protects living beings from dangers so that they do not die, or as one who is friendly towards living beings. Yāska explains the word Mitra as मित्रः प्रमितेस्त्रायते सम्मिन्वाने द्रवतीति वा वेदयतेर्वा (mitraḥ pramitestrāyate samminvāne dravatīti vā vedayatervā) (Si. 10-2).

अरी गच्छति नियच्छतीति आर्यमा (arī gacchati niyacchatīti āryamā)—Sāyaṇa states the explanation of the word Aryamā as one who restrains enemies. Yāska explains: अर्यमादित्यो अरीन्नियच्छति (aryamādityo arīnniyacchati) (Si. 11-23).

भगः भजनीयो देवः (bhagaḥ bhajanīyo devaḥ): Sāyaṇa's explanation is "the god who is worthy to be served". Yāska comments on the word Bhaga as भगो भजतेः (bhago bhajateḥ) (Ni. 1-7); he also read it among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) and explained the meaning as भगस्य भागधेयस्य धर्मस्य (bhagasya bhāgadheyasya dharmasya) (Ni. 9-31).

वरुणः तुविजातः (varuṇaḥ tuvijātaḥ)—अनुग्रहार्थं बहुषु देशेषु प्रादुर्भूतः पापनिवारणात् वरुणः (anugrahārthaṃ bahuṣu deśeṣu prādurbhūtaḥ pāpanivāraṇāt varuṇaḥ): Sāyaṇa explains that, since he has become manifest in many regions in order to protect living beings out of compassion and to remove their sins, he is called Varuṇa. Yāska explains it as वृणोतिति सतः (vṛṇotiti sataḥ) [sic, as supplied] (Ni. 10-5).

दक्षः अंशः (dakṣaḥ aṃśaḥ)—समर्थः (samarthaḥ): the word Dakṣa is given the meaning "able, possessed of power". It is explained as an epithet of the Āditya famed by the name Aṃśa. Thus these Mitra, Aryamā

p. 72

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 26 [as printed], p. 72.

Varuṇa and Aṃśa are invoked to hear separately the hymns recited by us, the priests, and to show favour.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

इ॒मं स्तोमं॒ सक्र॑तवो मे अ॒द्य मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मा वरु॑णो जुषन्त । आ॒दि॒त्यासः॒ शुच॑यो॒ धार॑पूता॒ अवृ॑जिना अनव॒द्या अरि॑स्वाः ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इमं । स्तोमं । सक्रतवः । मे । अद्य । मित्रः । अर्यमा । वरुणः । जुषन्त । आदित्यासः । शुचयः । धार्पूताः । अवृजिनाः । अनवद्याः । अरिस्वाः ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पूर्वोक्त एव पशाविमं स्तोममित्येषा वपाया याज्या । सूत्रितं च । इमं स्तोमं सक्रतवो मे अद्य तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन् त्रीरुत द्यून् । आ. ३ ८. । इति ॥ इमं मेऽस्मदीयं स्तोमं स्तोत्रं सक्रतवः समानकर्माणः समानप्रजा वा मित्रादयोऽद्येदानीं जुषंत । जुषंतां सेवंतां । कीदृशास्ते । आदित्या- सोऽदितेः पुत्राः शुचयो दीप्यमानाः । धारपूता उदकधाराभिरिव पूताः । निर्मला इत्यर्थः । अवृजिनाः । वृजी वर्जने । अवर्जितारः । सर्वानुग्राहका इत्यर्थः। अनवद्याः। अवद्येन गर्ह्येण पापेन रहिताः । अरिष्टाः केनाप्यहिंसिताः ॥

Gist: This Ṛk is the yājyā for the vapā (omentum) offering in the animal sacrifice mentioned above; may Mitra and the other Ādityas, pure and blameless, enjoy my praise today.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

आदित्यासः—the sons of Aditi; शुचयः—the shining ones; धारपूता—pure like a stream of water; अवृजिना—those who forsake (none of their devotees) but favour all; अनवद्या—free from sin; अरिष्टाः [sic: the Saṃhitā has अरिस्वाः]—not harmed by anyone; सक्रतवः—possessed of equal (rites or) wisdom; मित्रः—Mitra; अर्यमा—Aryaman; वरुणः—Varuṇa

p. 73

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 6, p. 73.

also; मे—recited by me; इमं स्तोमं—this praise; अद्य—at this time of sacrifice; जुषंत—let them enjoy.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the deities Mitra, Aryaman and Varuṇa—sons of Aditi, shining, pure like a stream of water, not forsaking any devotee but favouring all, free from sin, harmed by none, and possessed of equal rites and wisdom—enjoy at this time of sacrifice this praise recited by me. (May they hear it and be pleased.)

Printed English translation

May those of equal exploits, Mitra, Aryaman, Varuna, be pleased to-day by this my praise; they who are Adityas, luminous, purified by showers, who abandon none (that worship them), who are irreproachable, unassailable.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the animal sacrifice spoken of earlier, this Ṛk, इमं स्तोमं (imaṃ stomaṃ), is to be recited as the yājyā mantra while the vapā oblation is made; this is supported by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the sūtra इमं स्तोमं सक्रतवो मे अद्य तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन् त्रीरुत द्यून् (imaṃ stomaṃ sakratavo me adya tisro bhūmīrdhārayan trīruta dyūn) (Ā. 3-8).

सक्रतवः (sakratavaḥ)—समानकर्माणः समानप्रज्ञा वा मित्रादयः (samānakarmāṇaḥ samānaprajñā vā mitrādayaḥ): those having work of one kind, and possessed of knowledge of one manner—Mitra and the others—are described as hearing the praises of us, the priests, and being pleased.

These Ādityas are described as दीप्यमानाः (dīpyamānāḥ), brilliant; उदकधाराभिरिव पूताः (udakadhārābhiriva pūtāḥ), holy like streams of water; अवर्जितारः (avarjitāraḥ), bestowing favour on all; गर्ह्येन पापेन रहिताः (garhyena pāpena rahitāḥ), free from censured sins; and केनाप्यहिंसिताः (kenāpyahiṃsitāḥ), such that no one else can harm them. Thus their greatness has been made clear.

(A garbled line of the supplied text, "-~௨௪௬௧-", was removed.)

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त आ॑दि॒त्यास॑ उ॒रवो॑ गभी॒रा अद॑ब्धास्तो॒ दिप्स॑नो भूर्य॒क्षाः । अ॒न्तः प॑श्यंति वृजि॒नोत सा॒धु सर्वं॒ राज॑भ्यः पर॒मा चि॒दन्ति॑ ॥ ३ ॥

ta ādityāsa uravo gabhīrā adabdhāsto dipsano bhūryakṣāḥ | antaḥ paśyaṃti vṛjinota sādhu sarvaṃ rājabhyaḥ paramā cidanti ‖ 3 ‖

p. 74

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ते । आदित्यासः । उरवः । गभीराः । अदब्धासः । दिप्सन्तः । भूरि अक्षाः । अन्तरिति । पश्यंति । वृजिना । उत । साधु । सर्वं । राजभ्यः । परमा । चित् । अन्ति ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

तस्मिन्नेव पशौ त आदित्यास इति हविषोऽनुवाक्या । सूत्रं तु पूर्वमेवो- दाहृतं ॥ त आदित्यासोऽदितेः पुत्रा उरवो महांतो गभीरा गांभिर्योपेता अदब्बासः शत्रुभिरहिंसिताः संतो दिप्संतः शत्रुन्दंभितुं हिंसितुमिच्छंतः ॥ दंभु दंभे । अस्मादिच्छासनि सनीवंतर्धेतीडभावपक्षे दंभ इच्चेतीकारः । दंभेर्हल्- ग्रहणस्य जातिवाचकत्वासिद्धमिति सनः कित्वेऽनुनासिकलोपः ॥ तथा भूर्यक्षाः । भूरीणि बहून्य क्षीणि चक्षूंषि येषां ते तथोक्ताः । बहुतेजसो ना ॥ बहुव्रीहौ सक्ष्यक्षोरिति षच् समासांतः ॥ एवंभूता आदित्या अंतर्मध्यॆ प्राणिनां हृदि प्रेरकतया वर्तमानाः संतो वृजिना वृजिनानि पापानि उत अपि च साधु साधूनि पुण्यानि च प्राणिभिः कृतानि पश्यंति । जानंति । परमा चित् परमाणि दूरदेशावस्थिता- न्यपि सर्वं सर्वाणि दृश्यमानानि राजभ्यो राज्ञामीश्वराणामादित्यानामंत्यंतिके समीपे वर्तत इति शेषः ॥ कादिलोपो बहुलमित्यंतिकशब्दस्य कादिलोपः ॥

tasminneva paśau ta ādityāsa iti haviṣo 'nuvākyā | sūtraṃ tu pūrvamevo- dāhṛtaṃ ‖ ta ādityāso 'diteḥ putrā uravo mahāṃto gabhīrā gāṃbhiryopetā adabbāsaḥ śatrubhirahiṃsitāḥ saṃto dipsaṃtaḥ śatrundaṃbhituṃ hiṃsitumicchaṃtaḥ ‖ daṃbhu daṃbhe | asmādicchāsani sanīvaṃtardhetīḍabhāvapakṣe daṃbha iccetīkāraḥ | daṃbherhal- grahaṇasya jātivācakatvāsiddhamiti sanaḥ kitve 'nunāsikalopaḥ ‖ tathā bhūryakṣāḥ | bhūrīṇi bahūnya kṣīṇi cakṣūṃṣi yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | bahutejaso nā ‖ bahuvrīhau sakṣyakṣoriti ṣac samāsāṃtaḥ ‖ evaṃbhūtā ādityā aṃtarmadhyè prāṇināṃ hṛdi prerakatayā vartamānāḥ saṃto vṛjinā vṛjināni pāpāni uta api ca sādhu sādhūni puṇyāni ca prāṇibhiḥ kṛtāni paśyaṃti | jānaṃti | paramā cit paramāṇi dūradeśāvasthitā- nyapi sarvaṃ sarvāṇi dṛśyamānāni rājabhyo rājñāmīśvarāṇāmādityānāmaṃtyaṃtike samīpe vartata iti śeṣaḥ ‖ kādilopo bahulamityaṃtikaśabdasya kādilopaḥ ‖

Gist: the Ādityas, dwelling within beings as inspirers, see their sins and merits; even far-off things are near to these lords.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

आदित्यासः (ādityāsaḥ): sons of Aditi; उरवः (uravaḥ): of great form; गभीराः (gabhīrāḥ): endowed with profundity; अदब्बासः (adabbāsaḥ) [as supplied]: not harmed by enemies; दिप्पंतः (dippaṃtaḥ) [as supplied]: wishing the destruction of enemies; भूर्रक्षाः (bhūrrakṣāḥ) [as supplied]: having many eyes or abundant radiance; ते (te): those Ādityas; अंतः (aṃtaḥ): dwelling within the heart (of beings); वृजिना (vṛjinā): (men's) sins; उत (uta): and; साधु (sādhu): meritorious acts; पश्यंति (paśyaṃti): know; परमा चित् (paramā cit): even when extremely far off; सर्वं (sarvaṃ): all things; राजभ्यः (rājabhyaḥ): to the lords, the Ādityas; अंति (aṃti): are as if very near.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those Ādityas, sons of Aditi, of great form, profound, unharmed by enemies, wishing the destruction of enemies, possessed of abundant radiance, dwelling within the hearts of beings, know the sins of men and also their meritorious acts. Even all things that are extremely far off remain as if very near to those Ādityas, the lords.

p. 75

Printed English translation

Those Adityas, mighty, profound, unsubdued, subduing, many eyed behold the innermost (thoughts of men), whether wicked or virtuous, whether far from or nigh to those royal (deities).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the same animal sacrifice spoken of earlier, this Ṛk "ta ādityāsa" is to be used as the anuvākyā mantra when the oblation is offered; this is indicated in the sūtra cited earlier.

भूर्यक्षाः (bhūryakṣāḥ): बहूनि चक्षूंषि येषां ते बहुतेजसो वा (bahūni cakṣūṃṣi yeṣāṃ te bahutejaso vā). The Ādityas are described as seeing everything in many ways, as having many eyes, or as having abundant radiance.

अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—मध्यॆ प्राणिनां हृदि प्रेरकतया वर्तमानाः (madhyè prāṇināṃ hṛdi prerakatayā vartamānāḥ): dwelling in the hearts of beings in accordance with the acts they perform, and inspiring them; thus the Ādityas' quality of being inner controllers (antaryāmin) is described.

साधु पश्यंति (sādhu paśyaṃti)—प्राणिभिः कृतानि च पुण्यानि जानंति (prāṇibhiḥ kṛtāni ca puṇyāni jānaṃti): it is explained that they know all the merit that accords with the acts performed by the several beings.

परमा चित् सर्वं राजभ्यः अंति (paramā cit sarvaṃ rājabhyaḥ aṃti)—दूरदेशस्थितान्यपि सर्वाणि दृश्यमानानि ईश्वराणां आदित्यानां समीपे वर्तते (dūradeśasthitānyapi sarvāṇi dṛśyamānāni īśvarāṇāṃ ādityānāṃ samīpe vartate): all things situated in a distant place appear to the Ādityas, the lords of all, as if near; thus the keenness of their sight and the excellence of their knowledge are described.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

धा॒रय॑न्त आदि॒त्यासो॒ जग॒त्साथ दे॒वा विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य गो॒पाः । दी॒र्घाधि॑यो॒ रक्ष॑माणा असु॒र्य॑मृ॒ता॑न॒ाश्चर्य॑माना ऋ॒णानि॑ ॥

dhārayanta ādityāso jagatsātha devā viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ | dīrghādhiyo rakṣamāṇā asuryamṛtānāścaryamānā ṛṇāni ‖

p. 76

॥ पदपाठः ॥

धारयन्तः । आदित्यासः । जगत् । स्थाः । देवाः । विश्वस्य । भुवनस्य । गोपाः । दीर्घधियः । रक्षमाणाः । असुर्यं । ऋतवानः । चयमानाः । ऋणानि ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

साग्निचित्ये क्रत् दीक्षणीयायामादित्ययागस्य धारयंत इत्यादिके द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये । अत एव भुवद्वद्भुवनपतिविशेषणविशिष्टादित्ययागेऽपि । तथा च दीक्षणीयायामिति खंडे सूत्रितं । धारयंत आदित्यासो जगत्स्था इति द्वे एते एव भुवद्वद्भो भुवनपतिभ्यो ना । आ. ४. २. । इति ॥ जगज्जंगमं स्थाः स्थावरं च ॥ तिष्ठतेः कर्तर्यसुन् ॥ एतदुभयविधं भूतजातं धारयंतोऽवस्थापयंतो देवा दानादिगुणयुक्ता विश्वस्य भुवनस्य सर्वस्य लोकस्य गोपा गोपयितारो रक्षका दीर्घाधियो दीर्घाणि धियः कर्माणि ज्ञानानि ना येषां तादृशाः ॥ अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति पूर्वपदस्य दीर्घः ॥ असुर्य० । असवः प्राणाः । तेन च तद्देतुभूता आपो लक्ष्यंते । अपां तद्देतुत्वं च छांदोग्ये स्पष्टमाम्नातं । आपोमयः प्राणः । छां. उ. ६-५-४ । इति । असुमुदकं ददातीत्यसुरो मेघः । तत्र भवं मेघांतर्वर्तमानमुदकं रक्षमाणाः । तत्तत्काले वृष्टुत्पादनाय रक्षंतः ॥ असुरशब्दाद्भवे छंदसीति यत् ॥ ऋतावानः सत्यवंतो यज्ञवंतो वा ॥ छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्वर्थीयो वनिप् । पूर्ववद्धीर्घः ॥ ऋणानि स्तोतृभिरन्येभ्यः प्रदेयानि चयमाना अपगमयंतः ॥ चय गतौ । भौवादिकोऽनुदात्तेत् ॥ एवंगुणविशिष्टानुग्रहा वा अस्मदधीना भवंत्विति शेषः ॥

sāgnicitye krat dīkṣaṇīyāyāmādityayāgasya dhārayaṃta ityādike dve yājyānuvākye | ata eva bhuvadvadbhuvanapativiśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭādityayāge 'pi | tathā ca dīkṣaṇīyāyāmiti khaṃḍe sūtritaṃ | dhārayaṃta ādityāso jagatsthā iti dve ete eva bhuvadvadbho bhuvanapatibhyo nā | ā. 4. 2. | iti ‖ jagajjaṃgamaṃ sthāḥ sthāvaraṃ ca ‖ tiṣṭhateḥ kartaryasun ‖ etadubhayavidhaṃ bhūtajātaṃ dhārayaṃto 'vasthāpayaṃto devā dānādiguṇayuktā viśvasya bhuvanasya sarvasya lokasya gopā gopayitāro rakṣakā dīrghādhiyo dīrghāṇi dhiyaḥ karmāṇi jñānāni nā yeṣāṃ tādṛśāḥ ‖ anyeṣāmapi dṛśyata iti pūrvapadasya dīrghaḥ ‖ asurya0 | asavaḥ prāṇāḥ | tena ca taddetubhūtā āpo lakṣyaṃte | apāṃ taddetutvaṃ ca chāṃdogye spaṣṭamāmnātaṃ | āpomayaḥ prāṇaḥ | chāṃ. u. 6-5-4 | iti | asumudakaṃ dadātītyasuro meghaḥ | tatra bhavaṃ meghāṃtarvartamānamudakaṃ rakṣamāṇāḥ | tattatkāle vṛṣṭutpādanāya rakṣaṃtaḥ ‖ asuraśabdādbhave chaṃdasīti yat ‖ ṛtāvānaḥ satyavaṃto yajñavaṃto vā ‖ chaṃdasīvanipāviti matvarthīyo vanip | pūrvavaddhīrghaḥ ‖ ṛṇāni stotṛbhiranyebhyaḥ pradeyāni cayamānā apagamayaṃtaḥ ‖ caya gatau | bhauvādiko 'nudāttet ‖ evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭānugrahā vā asmadadhīnā bhavaṃtviti śeṣaḥ ‖

Gist: in the Agnicayana dīkṣaṇīyā, "dhārayanta" etc. are two yājyā-anuvākyā verses of the Āditya offering; the Ādityas sustain the moving and the fixed, guard the world, and keep the waters of the cloud.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

जगत् (jagat): moving beings; स्थाः (sthāḥ): fixed things; धारयंतः (dhārayaṃtaḥ): establishing and upholding; देवाः (devāḥ): possessed of the qualities of generosity etc.; विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (viśvasya bhuvanasya): of the whole world; गोपाः (gopāḥ): protectors; दीर्घधियः (dīrghadhiyaḥ): of far-reaching understanding; असुरं (asuraṃ) [as supplied]: the water residing in the clouds; रक्षमाणाः (rakṣamāṇāḥ): collecting and guarding it in due season; ऋतावानः (ṛtāvānaḥ): truthful; ऋणानि (ṛṇāni): the debts (which the praisers owe to others); चयमानाः (cayamānāḥ): discharging; आदित्यासः (ādityāsaḥ): the Ādityas (may favour us).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Ādityas, who establish and uphold the moving beings and the fixed things, who are possessed of generosity and other qualities, protectors of the whole world, of far-reaching understanding, guarding the water residing in the clouds [text of the page ends here; the sentence continues in the next window]

p. 77

(Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 4, continued) …who collect it and guard it at the proper time, truthful, and discharging the debts that the praisers owe to others — may such Ādityas favour us.

Printed English translation

The divine Adityas are the upholders (of all things). moveable or immoveble [sic]; the protectors of the universe: the provident in acts; the collectors of rain; the possessors of veracity; the acquitters of our debts.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the dīkṣaṇīyā rite when the Agnicayana is performed, in the Āditya offering, the Ṛk "dhārayanta ādityāsaḥ" धारयंत आदित्यासः (dhārayaṃta ādityāsaḥ) and the Ṛk following it are to be used as the yājyā and puro'nuvākyā mantras; and these Ṛks are also applied to the Āditya deities qualified as "bhuvadvat" and "bhuvanapati". This is concluded from the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, in the section beginning "tathā ca dīkṣaṇīyāyām", by the sūtra "dhārayanta ādityāso jagatsthā iti dve ete eva bhuvadvadbhyo bhuvanapatibhyo vā" धारयंत आदित्यासो जगत्सा इति द्वे एते एव भुवद्वद्भ्यो भुवनपतिभ्यो वा (dhārayaṃta ādityāso jagatsā iti dve ete eva bhuvadvadbhyo bhuvanapatibhyo vā) (Āś. 4-2 as printed).

जगत् स्थाःधारयंत— स्थावरं जंगमं च उभयविधं भूतजातं अवस्थापयंतः (jagat sthāḥdhārayaṃta— sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ ca ubhayavidhaṃ bhūtajātaṃ avasthāpayaṃtaḥ): it is described that the Ādityas have placed the two kinds of beings — the fixed, in the form of trees, creepers and so on, and the moving, in the form of animals, beasts, birds, men and the rest — each in accordance with its fitness; and the Ādityas are explained as देवाः—दानादिगुणयुक्ताः (devāḥ—dānādiguṇayuktāḥ), those endowed with qualities such as generosity.

दीर्घाधियः—धीर्घाणि धियः कर्माणि ज्ञानानि ना येषां (dīrghādhiyaḥ—dhīrghāṇi dhiyaḥ karmāṇi jñānāni nā yeṣāṃ): the Ādityas are described as those who perform abundant acts and are possessed of powerful knowledge.

असुरं रक्षमाणाः— असवः प्राणाः । तेन च तद्धेतुभूताः आपः लक्ष्यंते । असुमुदकं ददातीत्यसुरो मेघः । तत्र भवं मेघांतर्वतिनमुदकं तत्तत्काले वृष्ट्यत्पादनाय रक्षंतः (asuraṃ rakṣamāṇāḥ— asavaḥ prāṇāḥ | tena ca taddhetubhūtāḥ āpaḥ lakṣyaṃte | asumudakaṃ dadātītyasuro meghaḥ | tatra bhavaṃ meghāṃtarvatinamudakaṃ tattatkāle vṛṣṭyatpādanāya rakṣaṃtaḥ): here the meaning of the word asu is given as breath (life); from this the waters, which are the cause of breath, are meant. Because clouds give water to the earth, they are denoted by the word asura. It is described that the Ādityas guard, in the proper seasons, the water in the clouds so as to give it to the earth in the form of rain. And, अपां तद्देतुत्वं च आपोमयः प्राणः (apāṃ taddetutvaṃ ca āpomayaḥ prāṇaḥ) (Chāṃ. U. 6-5-4): explaining that the waters are the cause of breath, a sentence of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad is also cited.

ऋतावानः—सत्यवंतो यज्ञवंतो वा (ṛtāvānaḥ—satyavaṃto yajñavaṃto vā): the Ādityas are those who act by truth alone, or who perform sacrifice; ऋणानि चायमानाः—स्तोतृभिः अन्येभ्यः (ṛṇāni cāyamānāḥ—stotṛbhiḥ anyebhyaḥ) [the text of the page ends here; the sentence continues on p. 78]

p. 78

(Special Topics of Ṛk 4, continued) प्रदेयानि अपगमयंतः (pradeyāni apagamayaṃtaḥ) — it is described that the priests who praise them will have the debts they owe to others discharged.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वि॒द्यामा॑दित्या॒ अव॑सो वो अ॒स्य यद॑र्यमन्भ॒य आ चि॑न्मयो॒भु । यु॒ष्माकं॑ मित्रावरुणा॒ प्रणी॑तौ॒ परि॒ श्वभ्रे॑व दुरि॒तानि॑ वृज्यां ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

विद्यां । आदित्याः । अवसः । वः । अस्य । यत् । अर्यमन् । भये । आ । चित् । मयःभु । युष्माकं । मित्रावरुणा । प्रनीत् । परि । श्वभ्रा इव । दुःइतानि । वृज्यां ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे आदित्याः अदितेः पुत्रा वो युष्माकमस्यावसः ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ इदं रक्षणं विद्यां । लभेय । भये राक्षसादिभ्य अगते सति यद्युष्मदीयं रक्षणं । चिच्छब्दश्चार्थे । मयोभु मयसः सुखस्य भावयित्रु च तदितं लभेयेत्यन्वयः । हे अर्यमन् हे मित्रावरुणा युष्माकं प्रणीतावस्मद्विषये प्रकृष्टे नयने सति श्वभ्रेव श्वभ्राणीव स्थातुमयोग्यानि गर्तवंति स्थलानीव दुरितानि पापानि परिवृज्यां । परित्यजेयं ॥ वृजी वर्जने । बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ ६ ॥

he ādityāḥ aditeḥ putrā vo yuṣmākamasyāvasaḥ ‖ karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī ‖ idaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ vidyāṃ | labheya | bhaye rākṣasādibhya agate sati yadyuṣmadīyaṃ rakṣaṇaṃ | cicchabdaścārthe | mayobhu mayasaḥ sukhasya bhāvayitru ca taditaṃ labheyetyanvayaḥ | he aryaman he mitrāvaruṇā yuṣmākaṃ praṇītāvasmadviṣaye prakṛṣṭe nayane sati śvabhreva śvabhrāṇīva sthātumayogyāni gartavaṃti sthalānīva duritāni pāpāni parivṛjyāṃ | parityajeyaṃ ‖ vṛjī varjane | bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti vikaraṇasya luk ‖ 6 ‖

Gist: the Ādityas, sons of Aditi, are asked for the protection that brings happiness in time of fear from Rākṣasas etc.; under Aryaman's and Mitra-Varuṇa's guidance may I avoid sins as one avoids pits.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Ādityas: O Ādityas. Which protection of yours, when fear has come (from Rākṣasas etc.), removes that fear and produces happiness, that protection of yours — may I obtain it. Aryaman: O Aryaman. Mitra-Varuṇa: O Mitra and Varuṇa. When your excellent guidance exists, may I cross over sins [दुरिशानि (duriśāni) [?], as supplied] as one crosses a dangerous pit.

p. 79

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, may we obtain that protection of yours which, even when fear has come from Rākṣasas and others, removes that fear and brings happiness. O Aryaman [अरम (arama) [?], as supplied] and Mitra-Varuṇa, under your excellent guidance may I cross over sins as one crosses a dangerous pit.

Printed English translation

May I be conscious, Adityas, of this your protection, the cause of happiness (and security) in danger; Aryaman. Mitra, and Varuna, May I, through your guidance, escape the sins which are like pitfalls (in my path).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the sacrificer prays for two kinds of protection performed by the Ādityas. First, वः अस्य अवसः विद्यां लभेय (vaḥ asya avasaḥ vidyāṃ labheya): may the protection given by the Ādityas be knowledge-giving. And भये मयोभु—भये राक्षसादिभ्य आगते सति सुखस्य च भावयितृ (bhaye mayobhu—bhaye rākṣasādibhya āgate sati sukhasya ca bhāvayitṛ): when fear caused by Rākṣasas and the like has come upon the sacrificer, may the protection given by the Ādityas produce happiness. This is the second wish described.

Addressing Aryaman and Mitra-Varuṇa: युष्माकं प्रणीतौ श्वभ्रे दुरिशानि [?] परिवृज्यां—युष्माकं प्रकृष्णनयने सति स्थातुमयोग्यानि गर्तवंति स्कूलानीव पापानि परित्यजेयं (yuṣmākaṃ praṇītau śvabhre duriśāni [?] parivṛjyāṃ—yuṣmākaṃ prakṛṣṇanayane sati sthātumayogyāni gartavaṃti skūlānīva pāpāni parityajeyaṃ): the wish is expressed that, while these two protect the sacrificer, he may reach the state of getting rid of the abundant sins which bring misfortune, as one falls into big pits and has no chance to stand firm. A comparison of sins with deep pits is stated, and it is explained that protection from them is of the nature of release.

The word मयोभु (mayobhu) is used in the sense "producer of happiness" (सुखस्य भावयितृ (sukhasya bhāvayitṛ)), since Yāska has stated मयः (mayaḥ) among the words for happiness (Ni. 3-13).

p. 80

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सु॒गो हि वो॑ अर्यमन्मित्र॒ पन्था॑ अनृक्ष॒रो व॑रुण सा॒धुरस्ति॑ । तेना॑दित्या॒ अधि॑ वोचता नो॒ यच्छ॑ता नो दुष्परि॒हन्नु॒ शर्म॑ ॥६॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सुगः । हि । वः । अर्यमन् । मित्र । पन्थाः । अन्वृक्षरः । वरुण । साधुः । अस्ति । तेन । आदित्याः । अधि । वोचत । नः । यच्छत । नः । दुःपरिहन्नु । शर्म ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे आर्यवान् मित्र वरुण वो युष्माकॆं सुगः सुखेन गंतव्योऽनृक्षरः । ऋक्षरः कंटक ऋच्छतेरिति । तद्रहितः साधुः साधकः शोभनो वा । एवंगुणविशिष्टः पंथा मार्गोऽस्ति । विद्यते खलु । आतस्तेन पथास्मान् शोभनं नयतेति शेषः । हे आदित्या नोऽस्माकमधिवोचत । अधिवचनं पक्षपातेन वचनं कुरुत । अपि च नोऽस्मभ्यं दुष्परिहंतु परिहंतुं विनाशयितुमशक्यं शर्म सुखं यच्छत । दत्त ॥ दाण् दाने ! शपि प्राघ्रेत्यादिना यच्छादेशः ॥

he āryavān mitra varuṇa vo yuṣmākèṃ sugaḥ sukhena gaṃtavyo 'nṛkṣaraḥ | ṛkṣaraḥ kaṃṭaka ṛcchateriti | tadrahitaḥ sādhuḥ sādhakaḥ śobhano vā | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ paṃthā mārgo 'sti | vidyate khalu | ātastena pathāsmān śobhanaṃ nayateti śeṣaḥ | he ādityā no 'smākamadhivocata | adhivacanaṃ pakṣapātena vacanaṃ kuruta | api ca no 'smabhyaṃ duṣparihaṃtu parihaṃtuṃ vināśayitumaśakyaṃ śarma sukhaṃ yacchata | datta ‖ dāṇ dāne ! śapi prāghretyādinā yacchādeśaḥ ‖

Gist: the path of Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa is easy and free of thorns; the Ādityas are asked to lead us by it, to speak kindly to us and to grant undisturbed happiness.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Aryaman: O Aryaman. Mitra: O god Mitra. Varuṇa: O Varuṇa. Your path: easy to travel (सुगः), free of thorns (अनृक्षरः), and auspicious (साधुः). Pantha: as the path. Asti hi: it is well known to exist. Tena: by that same path (lead us). Ādityāḥ: O Ādityas. Naḥ: with us. Adhi vocata: speak lovingly. Naḥ: to us. Duṣparihantu: that which cannot be destroyed. Śamaṃ [?]: happiness. Yacchata: give.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, it is well known that your path is easy to travel, free of thorns and auspicious. Lead us by that same path. O Ādityas, speak lovingly with us. Give us happiness that enemies cannot destroy.

p. 81

Printed English translation

Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna, easy is the path (you show us), and free from thorns, and pleasant: therefore, Adityas, (lead us) by (it): speak to us favouably [sic], and grant us happiness difficult to be disturbed.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa, the wish is described that the sacrificer may enter upon a straight, thornless, pleasant path. अनृक्षरः साधुः पंथाः तेन (anṛkṣaraḥ sādhuḥ paṃthāḥ tena) — कंटकरहितः साधकः शोभनः मार्गः तेन शोभनं नयत (kaṃṭakarahitaḥ sādhakaḥ śobhanaḥ mārgaḥ tena śobhanaṃ nayata). The word अनृक्षरः is explained as ऋक्षरः कंटकः ऋच्छतेः (ṛkṣaraḥ kaṃṭakaḥ ṛcchateḥ) (Ni. 9-38); for this word the meaning is given as a path free from both thorns and fear.

आदित्याः नः अधिवोचत—अस्माकं पक्षपातेन वचनं कुरुत (ādityāḥ naḥ adhivocata—asmākaṃ pakṣapātena vacanaṃ kuruta): addressing the Ādityas, the wish is expressed that they speak to the sacrificers with confidence (affection). And दुष्परिहंतु शर्म यच्छत (duṣparihaṃtu śarma yacchata): the sacrificer's prayer is explained thus, that the Ādityas should bestow happiness that is always without break and does not meet destruction.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

पिप॑र्तु नो॒ अदि॑ती॒ राज॑पु॒त्राति॒ द्वेषां॑स्यर्य॒मा सु॒गेभिः॑ । बृ॒हन्मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ शर्मोप॑ स्याम पुरु॒वीरा॒ अरि॑ष्टाः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

पिपर्तु । नः । अदितिः । राजपुत्रा । अति । द्वेषांसि । आर्यमा । सुगेभिः । बृहत् । मित्रस्य । वरुणस्य । शर्म । उप । स्याम । पुरुवीराः । अरिष्टाः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

राजपुत्रा राजानो राजमाना मित्रादयः पुत्रा यस्यास्तादृश्यदितिरदीना अखंडनीया वा देवी नोऽस्मान् द्वेषांसि द्वेष्टणि रक्षांस्यति पिपर्तु । अति

rājaputrā rājāno rājamānā mitrādayaḥ putrā yasyāstādṛśyaditiradīnā akhaṃḍanīyā vā devī no 'smān dveṣāṃsi dveṣṭaṇi rakṣāṃsyati pipartu | ati

p. 82

पारयतु । अतिक्रम्य तद्रहितं देशं प्रापयत्वित्यर्थः । आर्यमा च सुगेभिः सुष्टु गंतवैर्मार्गैरस्मान्सारयतु । अपि च वयिं पुरुवीरा बहुभिर्वीरैः पुत्रादिभिरु . पेता अरिष्टाः केनाप्यहिंसिताश्च संतो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च बृहत्परिवृढं शर्म सुखमुपस्याम । उपगता भवेम ॥

pārayatu | atikramya tadrahitaṃ deśaṃ prāpayatvityarthaḥ | āryamā ca sugebhiḥ suṣṭu gaṃtavairmārgairasmānsārayatu | api ca vayiṃ puruvīrā bahubhirvīraiḥ putrādibhiru . petā ariṣṭāḥ kenāpyahiṃsitāśca saṃto mitrasya varuṇasya ca bṛhatparivṛḍhaṃ śarma sukhamupasyāma | upagatā bhavema ‖

Gist: Aditi, whose sons are the shining Mitra and others, is asked to carry us across enemies' hatred; Aryaman to lead us by good paths; and we to attain the great happiness of Mitra and Varuṇa.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Rājaputrā: she whose sons are the shining Mitra and others. Aditi: the indivisible divine mother. Naḥ: us. Dveṣāṃsi: from the hatred of enemies. Ati pipartu: carry across (to a place free of hatred). Aryamā: Aryaman also. Sugebhiḥ: by excellent, easily travelled paths (lead us). (Vayam: we also.) Puruvīrāḥ: accompanied by many heroic sons. Ariṣṭāḥ: unharmed by anyone. Mitrasya: belonging to Mitra. Varuṇasya: belonging to Varuṇa. Bṛhat: very great. Śarma: happiness. Upa syāma: may we attain.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the divine mother, whose sons are the shining Mitra and other gods and who is indivisible, carry us across the hatred of enemies to a place free of such hatred. May Aryaman [अरमन (aramana) [?], as supplied] also lead us by excellent, easily travelled paths. May we too, accompanied by many heroic sons and unharmed by anyone, attain the great happiness belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa.

Printed English translation

May Aditi, the mother of royal sons, place us beyond the malice (of our enemies): may Aryaman lead us by easy paths, and may we, blessed with many descendants, and safe from harm, attain the great happiness of Mitra and Varuna.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

राजपुत्रा अदितिः—राजमानाः मित्रादयः पुत्राः यस्याः अखंडनीया या देवी (rājaputrā aditiḥ—rājamānāḥ mitrādayaḥ putrāḥ yasyāḥ akhaṃḍanīyā yā devī). The abundant power of Aditi is described: the goddess Aditi has sons who shine with radiance. The word Aditi is stated by Yāska among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), of speech (Ni. 2-23), of cows (Ni. 3-9), and of heaven-and-earth (Ni. 3-22). And

p. 83

Aditi is explained as अदितिः देवमाता अदीना (aditiḥ devamātā adīnā) ("Aditi, the divine mother, the undiminished") (Ni. 4-23); and, citing the Ṛk आदितिर्दौरदितिरंतरिक्षं (āditirdauraditiraṃtarikṣaṃ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-89-10), it is described that Aditi's power is unbroken. The prayer is stated that this goddess may carry us, the sacrificers, beyond the demons (द्वेषांसि अति पिपर्तु (dveṣāṃsi ati pipartu)) and bring us to a country free of them, that is, make us dwell in regions where there is no affliction from rākṣasas.

By आर्यमा सुगेभिः (āryamā sugebhiḥ) the sacrificers pray for travel on a pleasant road, and for protection, from Aryaman. And by मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च बृहत् शर्म (mitrasya varuṇasya ca bṛhat śarma) it is wished that abundant happiness may come from Mitra and Varuṇa.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ति॒स्रो भूमी॑र्धारय॒न् त्रीरु॒त द्यून्त्रिणि॑ व्र॒ता वि॒दथे॑ अ॒न्तरे॑षां । ऋ॒तेना॑दित्या॒ महि॑ वो महि॒त्वं तद॑र्यमन्वरुण मित्र॒ चारु॑ ॥ ८ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तिस्रः । भूमिाः । धारयन् । त्रीन् । उत । द्यून् । त्रीणि । व्रता । विदथे । अंतः । एषां । यतेन । आदित्याः । महि । वः । महित्वं । तत् । अर्यमन् । वरुण । मित्र । चारु ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पूर्वोक्ते पशौ तिस्रो भूमीरिति पुरोडाशस्य याज्या । सूत्रं पूर्वमे- वोदाहृतं ॥ तिस्रो भूमिाः । अत्र भूमिाशब्दो लोकत्रये वर्तते । यो द्वितीयस्यां तृतीयस्यां पृथिव्यामित्यत्र यथा पृथिवीशब्दः । भूम्यंतरिक्षस्वर्गांस्त्रीन् लोकान् आदित्या धारयन् । वृष्टिप्रदानादिना धारयंति । उत आपि च द्यून् दीप्तान् तत उपरितनान् महरादिकानपि त्रीन् लोकान् धारयंति । यद्वा दीप्तान् अग्निं वायुं सूर्यं च धारयंति । अपि चैषामादित्यानां विदथे यज्ञे०तर्मध्यॆ श्रीणि व्रता सवनत्रयनिष्पाद्यानि श्रीणि कर्माणि संति । यद्वा एषां लोकानामंत- र्मध्यॆ विदथे यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति एषामादित्यानां त्रीणि कर्माणि रसादानधा-

pūrvokte paśau tisro bhūmīriti puroḍāśasya yājyā | sūtraṃ pūrvame- vodāhṛtaṃ ‖ tisro bhūmiāḥ | atra bhūmiāśabdo lokatraye vartate | yo dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāmityatra yathā pṛthivīśabdaḥ | bhūmyaṃtarikṣasvargāṃstrīn lokān ādityā dhārayan | vṛṣṭipradānādinā dhārayaṃti | uta āpi ca dyūn dīptān tata uparitanān maharādikānapi trīn lokān dhārayaṃti | yadvā dīptān agniṃ vāyuṃ sūryaṃ ca dhārayaṃti | api caiṣāmādityānāṃ vidathe yajñe0tarmadhyè śrīṇi vratā savanatrayaniṣpādyāni śrīṇi karmāṇi saṃti | yadvā eṣāṃ lokānāmaṃta- rmadhyè vidathe yajñe nimittabhūte sati eṣāmādityānāṃ trīṇi karmāṇi rasādānadhā-

p. 84

रणविसर्जनलक्षणानि संति । उत्तरोर्धर्चः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे आदित्या ऋतेन सत्येन यॆज्ञेन वा महि महत् प्रभूतं वो युष्माकं महित्वं महत्त्वं यन्महाभाग्यं हे अर्यमन् वरुण मित्र तन्महाभाग्यं चारु । शोभनं सर्वोत्कृष्टमित्यर्थः ॥

raṇavisarjanalakṣaṇāni saṃti | uttarordharcaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ | he ādityā ṛtena satyena yèjñena vā mahi mahat prabhūtaṃ vo yuṣmākaṃ mahitvaṃ mahattvaṃ yanmahābhāgyaṃ he aryaman varuṇa mitra tanmahābhāgyaṃ cāru | śobhanaṃ sarvotkṛṣṭamityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: the three worlds are the earth, atmosphere and heaven (or, alternatively, the three higher worlds, or Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya); the Ādityas sustain them, have three rites in the sacrifice, and their great might through truth or sacrifice is most excellent.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

तिस्रः भूमिाः (tisraḥ bhūmiāḥ): the three worlds beginning with the earth. धारयन् (dhārayan): (the Ādityas) have upheld. उत (uta): and. द्यून् (dyūn): the shining. त्रीन् (trīn): they have upheld also the three worlds beginning with Mahar. एषां (eṣāṃ): of these Ādityas. विदथे (vidathe): in the sacrifice, or, in the middle of the three worlds, occasioned by sacrifice. अंतः (aṃtaḥ): in the middle. त्रीणि व्रता (trīṇi vratā): three kinds of rites (accomplished through the three savanas) are well known (or: three kinds of rites, namely drinking up the water, holding it, and releasing it in the form of rain, are well known). आदित्याः (ādityāḥ): O Ādityas! वः (vaḥ): your. महित्वं (mahitvaṃ): greatness. ऋतेन (ṛtena): through truth or through sacrifice. महि (mahi): has grown in great form. अर्यमन् (aryaman): O Aryaman. वरुण (varuṇa): Varuṇa. मित्र (mitra): O Mitra. तत् (tat): that greatness of yours. चारु (cāru): is beautiful and the most excellent of all.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Ādityas have upheld the three worlds beginning with the earth, and the three upper worlds beginning with Mahar. In the middle of the three worlds that belong to these Ādityas, three rites occasioned by sacrifice, that is, drinking up the water, holding it, and releasing it as rain, are well known. O Ādityas, your greatness [माहात्म (māhātma), as supplied] has grown great through truth. O Aryaman [अय्यमने (ayyamane), as supplied], Varuṇa, that greatness of yours is beautiful and the most excellent of all.

Printed English translation

They uphold the three worlds, the three heavens; and in their sacrifices three ceremonies (are comprised): by truth, Adityas, has your great might (been produced), such as is most excellent; Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the matter stated before, it is explained in the Stotra already cited that this Ṛk तिस्रो भूमिाः (tisro bhūmiāḥ) is to be used as the yājyā mantra when the purodāśa oblation is offered. तिस्रो भूमिाः धारयन् (tisro bhūmiāḥ dhārayan): the meaning is explained thus: as in the mantra यो द्वितीयस्यां तृतीयस्यां पृथिव्यां (yo dvitīyasyāṃ tṛtīyasyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ) the word pṛthivī is said to mean the three worlds, so here too the word bhūmi is used in the sense of the three worlds.

p. 85

From this, भूम्यंतरिक्षस्वर्गस्थान् त्रीन् लोकान् आदित्याः वृष्टिप्रदानादिना धारयंति (bhūmyaṃtarikṣasvargasthān trīn lokān ādityāḥ vṛṣṭipradānādinā dhārayaṃti): the Ādityas uphold, that is, protect, the three worlds earth, atmosphere and heaven, and those who live in the three worlds, by granting rain, water and the like; this is how the meaning is described. And for the words द्यून् त्री९ (dyūn trī9) [as supplied] the meaning given with तत उपरितनान् महारादिर्का अपि (tata uparitanān mahārādirkā api) is: the three worlds beginning with Mahar, which lie above these three worlds; and one sense is described, that the Ādityas have upheld these. Then, with यद्वा दीर्प्ता अग्निं वायुं सूर्यं च धारयंति (yadvā dīrptā agniṃ vāyuṃ sūryaṃ ca dhārayaṃti), it is described that the Ādityas uphold also the shining Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya.

एषां विदथे अंतः व्रता त्रीणि संति (eṣāṃ vidathe aṃtaḥ vratā trīṇi saṃti), आदित्यानां एषां यज्ञ मध्यॆ सवनत्रय निष्पाद्यानि कर्माणि संति (ādityānāṃ eṣāṃ yajña madhyè savanatraya niṣpādyāni karmāṇi saṃti): the first meaning is explained thus: in the middle of the sacrifices performed in honour of these Ādityas, the duties (to be performed) in the rites of the morning, midday and evening savanas are also carried out. Secondly, यद्वा एषां लोकानां अंतर्मध्यॆ यज्ञे निमित्तभूते सति एषामादित्यानां रसादानधारण-विसर्जनलक्षणानि त्रीणि कर्माणि संति (yadvā eṣāṃ lokānāṃ aṃtarmadhyè yajñe nimittabhūte sati eṣāmādityānāṃ rasādānadhāraṇa-visarjanalakṣaṇāni trīṇi karmāṇi saṃti): the meaning is explained that, in the middle of the three worlds heaven, earth and atmosphere, at the time when sacrifice is performed, these Ādityas carry out three kinds of rites, receiving the waters, holding the waters received, and pouring them on the earth in the form of rain, and thereby protect sacrifices and other rites.

Addressing the Ādityas as हॆ अदित्याः आर्यमन्, मित्र, वरुण (hè adityāḥ āryaman, mitra, varuṇa) [as supplied], ऋतेन यज्ञेन सत्येन पा युष्माकं प्रभूतं महाभाग्यं चारु (ṛtena yajñena satyena pā yuṣmākaṃ prabhūtaṃ mahābhāgyaṃ cāru): it is described that their abundant glory, full of greatness, surpasses everything because it protects the sacrifice and truth. The meanings of the words Āryamā, Mitra and Varuṇa have been explained before. For the word ṛta the meanings truth and sacrifice are given by Yāska: सत्यं वा यज्ञं वा (satyaṃ vā yajñaṃ vā) (Ni. 4-19).

p. 86

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

श्री रो॑च॒ना दि॒व्या धा॑रयन्त हिर॒ण्ययाः॒ शुच॑यो॒ धार॑पूताः । अस्व॑प्नजो अनिमि॒षा अद॑ब्धा उरु॒शंसा॑ ऋ॒जवे॒ मर्त्या॑य ॥ ९ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

श्री । रोचना । दिव्या । धारयन्त । हिरण्ययाः । शुचयः । धार्पूताः । अस्वप्नजः । अनिमिषाः । अदब्धाः । उरुशंसाः । यजवे । मर्त्याय ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

श्री रोचना त्रीणि रोचनानि रोचमानाग्न्यादीनि तेजांसि दिव्या दिव्यानि दिविभवानि धारयंत । आदित्या अवास्थापयन् । किमर्थं । ऋजवे ऋजीकाय स्तोत्राणां मर्त्याय मनुष्याय भोगसिद्ध्यर्थमिति यावत् । कीदृशा आदित्याः । हिरण्ययाः । हिरण्मया हिरण्यालंकृतसर्वांगाः । यद्वा हितरमणीयवेषाः । शुचयो दीप्यमानाः । धारपूता उदकधारया क्षालिता इव निर्मलाः । अस्वप्न- जोऽसंजातस्वप्नाः ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति जसः सुः ॥ अपर आह । अस्वप्नजोऽस्वपंतो विगतनिद्राः ॥ स्वपितृषोर्नजिज्ञति नजिज् प्रत्यय इति तदेतत्पदकारस्यानभिमतं ॥ अनिमिषा निमेषरहिताः । अदब्धा असुरादिभिरहिंसिताः । उरुशंसा उरुभिर्बहुभिः शंसनीयाः स्तोतव्याः । एवंगुणविशिष्टा आधारयंतेत्यन्वयः ॥

śrī rocanā trīṇi rocanāni rocamānāgnyādīni tejāṃsi divyā divyāni divibhavāni dhārayaṃta | ādityā avāsthāpayan | kimarthaṃ | ṛjave ṛjīkāya stotrāṇāṃ martyāya manuṣyāya bhogasiddhyarthamiti yāvat | kīdṛśā ādityāḥ | hiraṇyayāḥ | hiraṇmayā hiraṇyālaṃkṛtasarvāṃgāḥ | yadvā hitaramaṇīyaveṣāḥ | śucayo dīpyamānāḥ | dhārapūtā udakadhārayā kṣālitā iva nirmalāḥ | asvapna- jo 'saṃjātasvapnāḥ ‖ supāṃ sulugiti jasaḥ suḥ ‖ apara āha | asvapnajo 'svapaṃto vigatanidrāḥ ‖ svapitṛṣornajijñati najij pratyaya iti tadetatpadakārasyānabhimataṃ ‖ animiṣā nimeṣarahitāḥ | adabdhā asurādibhirahiṃsitāḥ | uruśaṃsā urubhirbahubhiḥ śaṃsanīyāḥ stotavyāḥ | evaṃguṇaviśiṣṭā ādhārayaṃtetyanvayaḥ ‖

Gist: the Ādityas, golden-adorned, shining, sleepless and unharmed, uphold the three heavenly lights for the upright mortal.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

हिरण्ययाः (hiraṇyayāḥ) (hiraṇyayāḥ): those of golden form, or those of a beneficial and charming appearance; शुचयः (śucayaḥ): the shining; धारपूताः (dhārapūtāḥ): those pure as if washed by a stream of water; अस्वप्नजः (asvapnajaḥ): those without sleep; अनिमिषाः (animiṣāḥ): those who strike (close) the eyelid [sic, as supplied: the Kannada says "who do close the eyelid"; the Bhāvārtha has "who do not close"]; अदब्धाः (adabdhāḥ): unharmed by Asuras and others; उरुशंसाः (uruśaṃsāḥ): praised by many — the Ādityas. ऋजवे (ṛjave): of the upright-minded worshipper; मर्त्याय (martyāya): for the good of man; दिव्या (divyā): born in the world of the gods; त्री रोचना (trī rocanā): the three luminous orbs beginning with Agni; धारयंत (dhārayaṃta): have upheld.

p. 87

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Ādityas, of golden form, shining, pure as if washed by streams of water, sleepless, not closing the eyelids, unharmed by Asuras and others, praised by many, have upheld the three luminous orbs beginning with Agni, born in the world of the gods, for the good of the upright-minded worshipper, man.

Printed English translation

The Adityas, decorated with golden ornaments, brilliant, purified by showers, who never slumber, nor close their eyelids, who are unassailable, and praised by many, uphold the three bright heavenly regions for the sake of the upright man.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

श्री रोचना दिव्या धारयंत (śrī rocanā divyā dhārayaṃta): Sāyaṇa explains it as आदित्याः दिवि भवानि त्रीणि रोचमानानि अग्न्यादीनि तेजांसि अवस्थापर्य (ādityāḥ divi bhavāni trīṇi rocamānāni agnyādīni tejāṃsi avasthāparya) [as supplied]: it is described that the Ādityas have set firmly in place the three kinds of lights born in the sky, Agni, Sūrya and the rest, so as to bring happiness to those who praise them.

On the word हिरण्ययाः (hiraṇyayāḥ) he gives हिरण्यालंकृतसर्वांगाः (hiraṇyālaṃkṛtasarvāṃgāḥ) and हितरमणीयवेषाः (hitaramaṇīyaveṣāḥ): it is explained that the Ādityas have limbs adorned with golden ornaments, or have a dress and decoration that is beneficial and charming.

धारपूताः (dhārapūtāḥ): the Ādityas are pure, as if well washed by streams of water; अस्वप्नजः (asvapnajaḥ): without dreams or without sleep; उरुशंसाः (uruśaṃsāḥ): worthy of praise by many people. Thus the Ādityas' greatness, adornment, form and nature are described.

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वं विश्वे॑षां वरुणासि॒ राजा॒ ये च॑ दे॒वा अ॑सुर॒ ये च॒ मर्ताः॑ । श॒तं नो॑ रास्व श॒रदो॑ वि॒चक्षे॒ऽश्यामायूं॑षि॒ सुधि॑तानि॒ पूर्वा॑ ॥ १० ॥

tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ | śataṃ no rāsva śarado vicakṣe 'śyāmāyūṃṣi sudhitāni pūrvā ‖ 10 ‖

p. 88

॥ पदपाठः ॥

त्वं । विश्वेषां । वरुण । असि । राजा । ये । च । देवाः । असुर । ये । च । मर्ताः शतं । नः । रास्व । शरदः । विचक्षे । अश्याम । आयूंषि । सुधितानि । पूर्वा ॥ १० ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे असुर शत्रूणां क्षेपक वरुण त्वं विश्वेषां सर्वॆषां राजासि । केषां । ये च देवा देवजनाः ये च मर्ता मरणधर्माणो मनुष्याः । तेषामित्यर्थः। अतस्त्वं नोऽस्मभ्यं शतं शरदः शतसंख्याकान् संवत्सरान् विचक्षे विशेषेण दर्श- नाय रास्व ! प्रयच्छ ॥ रा दाने । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं ॥ वयं च पूर्वा पूर्वै- र्देवैः सुधितानि सुष्टु हितानि शतसंवत्सरलक्षणान्यायुंष्यश्याम । व्याप्नुयाम ॥ सुधितवसुधितनेमधितधिष्टधिषीय चेति निपात्यते । गतिरनंतर इति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । पूर्वा । सुपार सुलुगिति तृतीयाया डादेशः ॥

he asura śatrūṇāṃ kṣepaka varuṇa tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ sarvèṣāṃ rājāsi | keṣāṃ | ye ca devā devajanāḥ ye ca martā maraṇadharmāṇo manuṣyāḥ | teṣāmityarthaḥ| atastvaṃ no 'smabhyaṃ śataṃ śaradaḥ śatasaṃkhyākān saṃvatsarān vicakṣe viśeṣeṇa darśa- nāya rāsva ! prayaccha ‖ rā dāne | vyatyayenātmanepadaṃ ‖ vayaṃ ca pūrvā pūrvai- rdevaiḥ sudhitāni suṣṭu hitāni śatasaṃvatsaralakṣaṇānyāyuṃṣyaśyāma | vyāpnuyāma ‖ sudhitavasudhitanemadhitadhiṣṭadhiṣīya ceti nipātyate | gatiranaṃtara iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | pūrvā | supāra sulugiti tṛtīyāyā ḍādeśaḥ ‖

Gist: Varuṇa, lord of gods and mortals, is asked to grant a hundred years of sight, so that we may enjoy the lives enjoyed by the ancients; the tail gives the grammar of रास्व (rāsva), सुधितानि (sudhitāni) and पूर्वा (pūrvā).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

असुर (asura): O destroyer of enemies; वरुण (varuṇa): O Varuṇa; त्वं (tvaṃ): you; ये च देवाः (ye ca devāḥ): whatever gods there are; ये च मर्ताः (ye ca martāḥ): whatever men there are; विश्वेषां (viśveṣāṃ): of all of these; राजा असि (rājā asi): you are the lord; नः (naḥ): to us; शतं शरदः (śataṃ śaradaḥ): a hundred years; विचक्षे (vicakṣe): for seeing; रास्व (rāsva): give; (वयं च (vayaṃ ca): we also); पूर्वा (pūrvā): by the ancient sages; सुधितानि (sudhitāni): fully enjoyed; आयूंषि (āyūṃṣi): lifetimes; अश्याम (aśyāma): may we enjoy.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, destroyer of enemies, you are the lord of all the gods and all men. Let us see the full hundred years; as the former sages fully enjoyed a life of a hundred years, so may we also enjoy a full lifetime.

Printed English translation

Varuna, destroyer of foes, you are the sovereign over all, whether they be gods or mortals: grant to us to behold a hundred years, and that we may enjoy lives such as were enjoyed by ancient (sages).

p. 89

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

(Special Topics of Ṛk 10.) In this Ṛk Varuṇa is praised. The word असुर (asura) is explained as "destroyer of enemies"; it is described that Varuṇa is a destroyer of enemies and is the king of men and of gods; and the wish is expressed that this god may grant us, the sacrificers, to see a hundred years, that is, to live a hundred years. Further, पूर्वा सुधिता नि आयूंषि अश्याम: that we may live a hundred years, as was determined by the ancient gods; so the sacrificers pray for this god's favour, that such a lifespan may be granted to us.

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

न द॑क्षि॒णा वि चि॑किते॒ न स॒व्या न प्रा॒चीन॑मादित्या॒ नोत प॒श्चा । पा॒क्या॑ चिद्वसवो धी॒र्या॑ चिद्यु॒स्मानी॑तो॒ अभ॑यं॒ ज्योति॑रश्यां ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

न । दक्षिणा । वि । चिकिते । न । सव्या । न । प्राचीनं । आदित्याः । न । उत । पश्चा । पाक्या । चित् । वसवः । धीर्या । चित् । युष्मानीतः । अभयं । ज्योतिः । अश्यां ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अदित्यदेवताके पशौ न दक्षिणेत्येषा हविषो याज्या । तिस्रो भूमीर्धार- यन्त्रींरुत द्यून् न दक्षिणा वि चिकिते न सन्या । आ. ३. ८. । इति ॥ हे आदित्याः दक्षिणा दक्षिणो न भागोविचिकिते । मया न विज्ञायते । सव्या सव्योवामभागोऽपि न ज्ञायते ॥ उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगिति सोराजादेशः । तथा प्राचीनं पुरस्तादपि न ज्ञायते ॥ विभाषांचेरदिक्ष्मियामिति स्वार्थे खः ॥ उत अपि च पश्चा पश्चात् पृष्ठभागेऽपि न ज्ञायते । नैशेन तमसावृतत्वात् आंतरादज्ञा नाद्वा ॥ पश्च पश्चा च छंदसि । पा. ५. ३. ३३. । इति निपात्यते ॥ किं बहुना । पाक्या चित् । पाक्यः पक्तव्योऽपरिपक्वज्ञानोऽपि ॥ डुपचष् पाके । यहलोर्ण्यत् । तित्स्वरितं ॥ धीर्या चित् धीरे नेतव्यत्वेन भवो धीर्यः कातरः ॥ भवे छंदसीति

adityadevatāke paśau na dakṣiṇetyeṣā haviṣo yājyā | tisro bhūmīrdhāra- yantrīṃruta dyūn na dakṣiṇā vi cikite na sanyā | ā. 3. 8. | iti ‖ he ādityāḥ dakṣiṇā dakṣiṇo na bhāgovicikite | mayā na vijñāyate | savyā savyovāmabhāgo 'pi na jñāyate ‖ ubhayatra supāṃ sulugiti sorājādeśaḥ | tathā prācīnaṃ purastādapi na jñāyate ‖ vibhāṣāṃceradikṣmiyāmiti svārthe khaḥ ‖ uta api ca paścā paścāt pṛṣṭhabhāge 'pi na jñāyate | naiśena tamasāvṛtatvāt āṃtarādajñā nādvā ‖ paśca paścā ca chaṃdasi | pā. 5. 3. 33. | iti nipātyate ‖ kiṃ bahunā | pākyā cit | pākyaḥ paktavyo 'paripakvajñāno 'pi ‖ ḍupacaṣ pāke | yahalorṇyat | titsvaritaṃ ‖ dhīryā cit dhīre netavyatvena bhavo dhīryaḥ kātaraḥ ‖ bhave chaṃdasīti

p. 90

यत् ॥ कातरोऽपि ॥ उभयत्र सुपां सुलुगित्याकारः ॥ हे वसवो वासयितार आदित्या युष्मानीतो युष्माभिर्नितः शोभनेन मार्गेण प्रापितः सन् अभयं भयरहितं ज्योतिः सौरं तेज आंतरं वा ज्ञानात्मकमश्यां । प्राप्नुयां ॥

yat ‖ kātaro 'pi ‖ ubhayatra supāṃ sulugityākāraḥ ‖ he vasavo vāsayitāra ādityā yuṣmānīto yuṣmābhirnitaḥ śobhanena mārgeṇa prāpitaḥ san abhayaṃ bhayarahitaṃ jyotiḥ sauraṃ teja āṃtaraṃ vā jñānātmakamaśyāṃ | prāpnuyāṃ ‖

Gist: Addressed to the Ādityas: neither right, left, front nor behind is known to the speaker; may he, guided by them, reach fearless light; the tail gives the grammar of पाक्या (pākyā), धीर्या (dhīryā), पश्चा (paścā).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

आदित्याः (ādityāḥ): O Ādityas; दक्षिणा (dakṣiṇā): what lies on my right; न वि चिकिते (na vi cikite): is not known to me! सव्या (savyā): what lies on the left; न (na): is not known! प्राचीनं (prācīnaṃ): what lies in front; न (na): is not known. उत (uta): and; पश्चा (paścā): what lies at the back; न (na): is not known. पाक्या चित् (pākyā cit): though without mature knowledge; धीर्या चित् (dhīryā cit): though timid; वसवः (vasavaḥ): O Ādityas; युष्मानीतः (yuṣmānītaḥ): walking on the path laid down by you; अभयं (abhayaṃ): fearless; ज्योतिः (jyotiḥ): light; अश्यां (aśyāṃ): may I obtain.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, because of my ignorance and the darkness of night, I do not know what lies on my right, nor on my left, nor in front, nor behind. I am one without mature knowledge, and timid. Yet, walking on the path laid down by you, may I obtain the fearless light.

Printed English translation

Neither is the right hand known to us, Adityas, nor is the left : neither is that which is in front. nor that which is behind. (discerned by me): Givers of dwellings, may I, who am immature (in knowledge), and timid (in spirit), obtain, when guided by you, the light that is free from fear.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the sacrifice of an animal belonging to the Ādityas, this Ṛk, न दक्षिणा (na dakṣiṇā), is to be used as the yājyā mantra when the oblation is offered, as is set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra passage तिस्रो भूमीर्धारयन्श्रीरुत द्यून् न दक्षिणा वि चिकिते न सव्या (tisro bhūmīrdhārayanśrīruta dyūn na dakṣiṇā vi cikite na savyā). In this Ṛk a prayer made to the Ādityas is stated: that the ignorance, like pitch darkness, may be destroyed.

p. 91

(Special Topics of Ṛk 11, continued.) Addressing the Ādityas, with the words दक्षिणा (dakṣiṇā), सव्या (savyā), प्राचीनं पश्चा (prācīnaṃ paścā) it is described that the darkness of night, or the ignorance grown up in the mind, envelops me who knows nothing and makes the right and left, and the arrangement of the east and west directions, imperceptible; and with पाक्या चित् (pākyā cit), धीर्या चित् (dhīryā cit), युष्मानीतः अभयं ज्योतिरश्यां (yuṣmānītaḥ abhayaṃ jyotiraśyāṃ) a prayer is stated: that the sacrificer, though of small knowledge (slow-witted) or dull, being favoured by these Ādityas and having fear from no one, may obtain the light that destroys the darkness connected with the sun, or the knowledge that removes ignorance.

पाक्या (pākyā): पक्तव्यः अपरिपक्वज्ञानः (paktavyaḥ aparipakvajñānaḥ); Sāyaṇa explains it as one without complete knowledge. Yāska reads the word पाकः (pākaḥ) among the words for the praiseworthy (Ni. 3-13) and explains (Ni. 3-12): पाकः पक्तव्यो भवति विपक्वप्रज्ञ आदित्यः (pākaḥ paktavyo bhavati vipakvaprajña ādityaḥ). The explanation of the word पाक (pāka) was given earlier, in the Vāmana Sūkta.

धीर्या चित् (dhīryā cit): धीरे नेतव्यत्वेन भवः धीर्यः कातरः (dhīre netavyatvena bhavaḥ dhīryaḥ kātaraḥ): Sāyaṇa explains the meaning as one who is intelligent (is taught) and acts as instructed, that is, one who has not even a little knowledge. For the word चित् (cit) the sense of "and" (samuccaya) is stated.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यो राज॑भ्य ऋत॒निभ्यो॑ द॒दाश॒ यं व॒र्धय॑न्ति पु॒ष्टय॑श्च॒ नित्याः॑ । स रे॒वान्या॑ति प्रथ॒मो रथे॑न वसु॒दावा॑ वि॒दथे॑षु प्रश॒स्तः ॥ १२ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । राजभ्यः । ऋतनिभ्यः । ददाश । यं । वर्धयन्ति । पुष्टयः । च । नित्याः । ७ । रेवान् । याति । प्रथमः । रथेन । वस्तुदावा । विदथेषु । प्रशस्तः ॥ १२ ॥

yaḥ | rājabhyaḥ | ṛtanibhyaḥ | dadāśa | yaṃ | vardhayanti | puṣṭayaḥ | ca | nityāḥ | 7 | revān | yāti | prathamaḥ | rathena | vastudāvā | vidatheṣu | praśastaḥ ‖ 12 ‖

p. 92

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यो यजमानो राजभ्यो रुजमानेभ्य ऋतनिभ्य ऋतस्य सत्यस्य वा नेतृभ्य आदित्येभ्यो ददाश । चरुपुरोडाशादिकं ददाति। यं यजमानं पुष्टयः पोषका नित्याः शाश्वता आदित्याश्च वर्धयंति । स यजमानो देवान्थनवान् प्रथमः प्रथितः प्रख्यातः वसुदावा वसूनां धनानां दाता सन् प्रशस्तः सर्वैः प्रशस्यमानो विद- धेषु वेद्येषु लब्धव्येषु गृहेषु रथेन वाहनेन याति । गच्छति ॥

Gist: the sacrificer who offers cooked oblations to the Ādityas is made to prosper by them, and goes to the sacrifice in a chariot, wealthy, famed and praised.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yaḥ: the sacrificer who; rājabhyaḥ: to the shining ones; ṛtanibhyaḥ: to the Ādityas, who are leaders of the sacrifice; dadāśa: offers cooked offerings, cakes and the like (and); yaṃ: whom (which sacrificer); puṣṭayaḥ: the nourishing; nityāḥ: the eternal Ādityas; vardhayanti: cause to prosper; saḥ: that sacrificer; revān: as one wealthy; prathamaḥ: as one renowned; vasudāvā: as a giver of wealth; praśastaḥ: as one praised by all; vidatheṣu: in the sacrificial houses (to the sacrificial houses); rathena: seated in a chariot; yāti: goes.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who offers cooked offerings, cakes and the like to the shining Ādityas, the leaders of the sacrifice, and whom the nourishing and eternal Ādityas cause to prosper, that sacrificer, wealthy, renowned, a giver of wealth and praised by all, goes seated in a chariot to the sacrificial houses.

Printed English translation

He who presents offerings to the royal and true (Adityas); he whom their constant favours exalt ; he proceeds, wealthy. renowned, munificent and honoured, to sacrifices, in his chariot.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ऋतनिभ्यः ददाश (ऋतनिभ्यः ददाश (ṛtanibhyaḥ dadāśa)): he offers cooked offerings, cakes and the like to the Ādityas, the leaders of truth or of the sacrifice. Because the Ādityas stand in front and protect truth and the sacrifice, they are leaders; knowing this, the sacrificer offers them cooked offerings and cakes, the form of the oblation, and

p. 93

(continued) so pleases them. These Ādityas, पुष्टयः नित्याः (puṣṭayaḥ nityāḥ), nourish the whole world and are imperishable, and so they favour the sacrificer who offers them oblations, that he may prosper. The sacrificer who has won their favour, by the wealth obtained through that favour, is the chief of all, famous among all, and a giver of wealth to others; thus the greatness of the Ādityas' favour, as obtained by sacrificers, is described. And it is explained that the sacrificer, praised by others, seated in a chariot, goes towards the sacrificial house (प्र शस्तः विदथेषु रथेन याति (pra śastaḥ vidatheṣu rathena yāti)).

The word वसु (vasu) is given by Yāska among the names of rays (Ni. 2-13) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9, as printed). In यस्त्वा यंतं वसुना प्रातरित्वः (yastvā yaṃtaṃ vasunā prātaritvaḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-125--2) it is used in the sense of food (वसुना अन्नेन (vasunā annena)). Sāyaṇa says it is used here in the sense of wealth, and explains the word वसुदावा (vasudāvā) as one who gives wealth.

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

शुचि॑र॒सः सू॒यव॑सा॒ अद॑ब्ध॒ उप॑ क्षेति वृ॒द्धव॑याः सु॒वीरः॑ । निकि॒ष्टं घ्न॒न्त्यन्ति॑तो॒ न दू॒राद्य आ॑दि॒त्यानां॒ भव॑ति॒ प्रणी॑तौ ॥ १३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

शुचिः । अपः । सुयवसाः । अदब्धः । उप । क्षेति । वृद्धवयाः । सुवीरः । नकिः । तं । घ्न्ति । अन्तितः । न । दूरात् । यः । आदित्यानां । भवति । प्रनीशौ ॥ १३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स यजमानः शुचिर्दिप्यमानः शुद्धो वा अदब्धः सपत्नैरबाधितो वृद्ध- वयाः प्रभूतान्नः सुवीरः शोभनपुत्रश्च सन् सुयवसाः शोभनसस्यान्यपो वृष्टि- लक्षणान्युदकान्युपक्षेति । उपनिवसति । सर्वदा सुसस्यानामपां समीपे निवसती- त्यर्थः । तथा नकिर्न च तं घ्नंति हिंसंत्यंतितो न अंतिकात्समीपदेशाच्च दूराद्वि- प्रकृष्टाच्च देशादागता बाधकाः ॥ अंतिकस्य तसि कादिलोप इति लोपः ॥ यो यजमान आदित्यानामदितेः पुत्राणां मित्रादीनां प्रणीतौ प्रकृष्टे नयने प्रापणे भवति वर्तते स इति पूर्वत्र संबंधः ॥

Gist: the sacrificer is pure, unharmed, rich in food and sons, dwells near fertile waters, and no enemy near or far harms him who is under the Ādityas' guidance.

p. 94

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yaḥ: the sacrificer who; ādityānāṃ: of the Ādityas; praṇītau: in the excellent guidance; bhavati: is (that sacrificer); śuciḥ: as one pure; adabdhaḥ: not harmed by others; vṛddhavayāḥ: possessing abundant food; suvīraḥ: with excellent sons; being so, sūyavasāḥ: fit for growing good plants; apaḥ: of the waters; upa: near; kṣeti: dwells; taṃ: that sacrificer; nakiḥ: no one; ghnanti: harms; antitaḥ: whether near; dūrāt: or far; na: none can harm.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer who lives under the excellent guidance of the Ādityas is pure, unharmed by others, possessed of abundant food and excellent sons, and dwells near waters fit for growing good plants. No one harms that sacrificer, whether near or far.

Printed English translation

Pure unmolested, possessing (abundant) food and virtuous descendants, he dwells amidst fertilizing waters: no one, whether nigh or afar, harms him who is (safe) in the good guidance of the Adityas.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

शुचिः (शुचिः (śuciḥ)): shining or pure. The word शुचि (śuci) is explained by Yāska as शुक् शोचतेः, शुचि शोचतेः, ज्वलतिकर्मणः (śuk śocateḥ, śuci śocateḥ, jvalatikarmaṇaḥ) (Ni. 6-1). Sāyaṇa gives the meanings "shining with radiance" and "perfectly pure". So two meanings are stated: the sacrificer who worships the Ādityas is bright with lustre and also perfectly pure. Further, this sacrificer is not subject to the harm of enemies, possesses abundant food, has virtuous sons, and सुसस्यानां अपां समीपे सर्वदा निवसति (susasyānāṃ apāṃ samīpe sarvadā nivasati): he lives always in regions full of plants and rich in water, without difficulty in food and drink; thus the power of the Ādityas' favour that can reach the sacrificer is stated.

नकिः (नकिः (nakiḥ)): this word is stated by Yāska in the list of all words (Ni. 3-14) and is used here in the sense of "nearby" (as the Kannada puts it). The greatness of the Ādityas is described: enemies cannot harm the sacrificer who has gained their favour, whether from near or from far.

p. 95

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अदि॑ते॒ मित्र॒ वरु॑णो॒त मृ॑ळ॒ यद्वो॑ व॒यं च॑क्र॒मा कच्चि॒दागः॑ । उ॒र्व॑श्या॒मभ॑यं॒ ज्योति॑रिन्द्र॒ मा नो॑ दी॒र्घा अ॒भि न॑शं॒तमि॑स्राः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आदते [?] । मित्र । वरुण । उत । मृळ । यत् । वः । चक्रम । कत् । चित् । आगः । उरु । अश्यां । अभयं । ज्योतिः । इन्त्र । मा । नः । दीर्घाः । अभि । नशन् । शमिस्ताः [?] ॥ १४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥
