उत आपि च हे आदिते मित्र वरुण ॥ आमंत्रितं पूर्वमविद्यमानवदिति पूर्वपूर्वस्थ्यामंत्रितस्याद्यमानवद्भावात् सर्वेषां षाष्ठिकमामंत्रितस्येत्या- द्युदात्तत्वं ॥ यूयं प्रत्येकं मृळ । आस्माकमुपरि दयां कुरु । रक्षेत्यर्थः । यत् यद्यपि वयं वो युष्माकं कच्चित् किंचिदागोSपराधं चक्रम । अकुर्म । तथापि मृलेत्यर्थः । हे इंद्र परमैश्वर्योपेतादित्य उरु विस्तीणमभयं भय- रहितं ज्योतिस्तद्वीयं प्रकाशं ज्ञानात्मकं वाश्यां । अहं प्राप्नुयां । दीर्घा विस्त्रतास्तमिस्रास्तमसा युक्ता निशाः ॥ ज्योत्सातमिस्तातृंगिणा । पा. ५. २. ११४ । इति निपात्यते ॥ ता नोऽस्यान् माभिनशन् । माभिमुख्यन व्याप्पुवंतु ॥

Gist: the Ādityas are addressed: forgive whatever offence we have committed; may I obtain fearless wide light, and may long nights of darkness not overtake us.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

uta: and; adite: O Aditi; mitra: O Mitra; varuṇa: O Varuṇa; yat: if; vayaṃ: we; vaḥ: in regard to you; kaccit: any; āgaḥ: offence; cakrama: have committed; mṛḷa: show kindness to us and protect us; indra: O Āditya, endowed with excellent wealth; uru: wide; abhayaṃ: and fearless; jyotiḥ: light; aśyāṃ: may I obtain; dīrghāḥ: very long; tamisrāḥ: nights full of darkness; naḥ: us; mā abhi naśan: may they not encircle and pervade.

p. 96

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, even if we have committed some offence against you, show kindness to us and protect us. O Āditya, endowed with excellent wealth, may I obtain wide and fearless light. May the very long nights, full of darkness, not encircle and pervade us.

Printed English translation

Aditi, Mitra, Varuna, have pity upon us, even although we may have committed some offence against you: may I obtain, Indra, that great light which is free from peril; let not the protracted glooms (of night) envelop us.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

The meanings of the words Aditi, Mitra and Varuṇa have been explained earlier. Here these deities are addressed by these words, and protection is prayed for: that each of them should protect the sacrificer and the priests with kindness. Further, the prayer is described as asking them to pardon the offences committed by the sacrificer and the priests and to protect them.

Yāska has explained the meaning of the word Indra (Ni. 10-8); this explanation was given at length in the earlier volumes. Here the Ādityas are addressed by the word Indra; the meaning is explained as "those having unsurpassed wealth", and it is prayed that these Ādityas may grant the sacrificer their own abundant radiance or knowledge. It is also hoped that the Ādityas will so act that the nights, covered with pitch darkness and extending for a very long time, may pass happily for the sacrificer.

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उ॒भे अ॑स्मै पीपयतः समी॒ची दि॒वो वृ॒ष्टिं सु॒भगो॒नाम॒ पुष्य॑न् । उ॒भा क्षया॑वा॒जय॑न्याति पृ॒त्सूभावर्धौ॑ भवतः सा॒धू अ॑स्मै ॥ १५ ॥

ubhe asmai pīpayataḥ samīcī divo vṛṣṭiṃ subhagonāma puṣyan | ubhā kṣayāvājayanyāti pṛtsūbhāvardhau bhavataḥ sādhū asmai ‖ 15 ‖

p. 97

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उभे इति । आस्मै [?] पीपयतः । समीची इति संईची । दिवः । वृष्टिं । सुभगः । नाम । पुष्यन् । उभा । क्षयौ । आजयन् । याति । पृत्सु । उभौ अर्थौ [?] । भवतः । साधू इति । अस्मै ॥ १५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

य आदित्यानां भवति प्रणीताविति व्यवहितोऽप्यत्रेदंशेन परामृश्यते । अस्मै यजमानाय सविाची संगच्छमाने उभे द्यावापृथिव्यौ पीपयतः । प्राय- यतः । कामान्वर्धयतः ॥ प्यायि वृद्दौ । अस्माण्ण्यंताच्छांदसो लुज् । व्यत्ययेन तसस्तामादेशाभावो धातोः पीभावश्च ॥ स च सुभगः शोभनधनो दिवो द्युलो- कादागतां वृष्टिं पुष्यन् वर्धयन् भवति । नामेति प्रसिद्धिर्द्योत्यते । किंच पृत्सु पृतनासु संग्रामेष्वजयन् शत्रूनाभिमुख्येनाभिभवन् उभा क्षयावुभौ निवासौ ॥ क्षियंति निवसंत्यस्मिन्निति क्षयो निवासस्थानं । पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेणेत्यधिकरणे घः । क्षयो निवास इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ तौ परैरनाक्रांतं स्वकीयं निवासस्थानं आत्मनापहृतं परकीयं निवासस्थानं च याति । गच्छति । तथास्मै यजमानायोभा- वर्धौ जगतो भागौ चराचरात्मकौ मर्त्यामर्त्याकौ वा साधू साधकौ भवतः ॥

ya ādityānāṃ bhavati praṇītāviti vyavahito 'pyatredaṃśena parāmṛśyate | asmai yajamānāya saviācī saṃgacchamāne ubhe dyāvāpṛthivyau pīpayataḥ | prāya- yataḥ | kāmānvardhayataḥ ‖ pyāyi vṛddau | asmāṇṇyaṃtācchāṃdaso luj | vyatyayena tasastāmādeśābhāvo dhātoḥ pībhāvaśca ‖ sa ca subhagaḥ śobhanadhano divo dyulo- kādāgatāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ puṣyan vardhayan bhavati | nāmeti prasiddhirdyotyate | kiṃca pṛtsu pṛtanāsu saṃgrāmeṣvajayan śatrūnābhimukhyenābhibhavan ubhā kṣayāvubhau nivāsau ‖ kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃtyasminniti kṣayo nivāsasthānaṃ | puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥ prāyeṇetyadhikaraṇe ghaḥ | kṣayo nivāsa ityādyudāttatvaṃ ‖ tau parairanākrāṃtaṃ svakīyaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ ātmanāpahṛtaṃ parakīyaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ ca yāti | gacchati | tathāsmai yajamānāyobhā- vardhau jagato bhāgau carācarātmakau martyāmartyākau vā sādhū sādhakau bhavataḥ ‖

The printed text carries two footnotes, "1 ಜಯಗಣೇಶಾಯ ನಮಃ" (an invocation, "Victory to Gaṇeśa, salutation") and "1 ಪ್ರವರ್ತಕ" ("instigator"), whose points of attachment are not shown in the supplied text.

Gist: the sacrificer under the Ādityas' guidance is nourished by heaven and earth together, thrives with rain, and wins both his own and his enemies' dwellings; both halves of creation favour him.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

asmai: for this sacrificer (who is under the guidance of the Ādityas); ubhe: both heaven and earth; samīcī: coming together; pīpayataḥ: fulfil his desires; (he, being) subhagaḥ: possessed of excellent wealth; divaḥ: from the heavenly world; vṛṣṭiṃ: the rain (by the rain); puṣyan nāma: surely obtains growth; pṛtsu [?]: in battles; ājayan: defeating enemies; ubhā kṣayau: both kinds of dwelling-places, his own and those of his enemies; yāti: enters; asmai: for this sacrificer; ubhāvardhau: both kinds of creative works, moving and unmoving; sādhū: as favourable; bhavataḥ: become. (The Kannada text prints "dyāvāpṛthivī" as व्यावापृथिविगळिब्बरू (vyāvāpṛthivigaḷibbarū) [?] and "pṛtsu" as हृत्सु (hṛtsu) [?], apparently misreadings.)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

For the sacrificer who is under the guidance of the Ādityas, heaven and earth, coming together, fulfil his desires. Possessed of excellent wealth, he obtains growth through the rain that has come from the heavenly world.

p. 98

In battles, defeating his enemies, he enters both the dwelling-places that are his own and those of his enemies. To this sacrificer both kinds of creative works, moving and unmoving, become favourable.

Printed English translation

Both (heaven and earth) combined, cherish him (whom the Adityas protect); verily prosperous, he thrives, with the rain of heaven ; victorious in battles, (he defends) both his own dwelling (and assaults) that of his foe; to him both portions (of creation) are propitious.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

It is explained that for the sacrificer who has obtained the favour of the Ādityas and stands in the path they show, heaven and earth, ever together, bring about growth, favourably, so that his desires are fulfilled.

पृत्सु आजयन् उभौ क्षयौ याति (pṛtsu ājayan ubhau kṣayau yāti) — संग्रामेषु शत्रूनाभिमुख्येनाभिभवन्, परैरनाक्रांतं स्वकीयं निवासस्थानं आत्मनापहृतं परकीयं निवासस्थानं च गच्छति । (saṃgrāmeṣu śatrūnābhimukhyenābhibhavan, parairanākrāṃtaṃ svakīyaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ ātmanāpahṛtaṃ parakīyaṃ nivāsasthānaṃ ca gacchati |) The word pṛt is listed by Yāska (Ni. 3-9) among the names of battle. By the favour of the Ādityas the sacrificer overcomes his enemies in wars, and obtains his own dwelling (house) not assailed by others and also the houses of others which he has seized. That is, keeping his own dwelling in comfort and seizing the dwellings of his enemies as well, he lives happily by his own strength.

क्षयः क्षियंति निवसंत्यस्मिन्निति । (kṣayaḥ kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃtyasminniti |) The meaning of the word kṣaya is explained as places so arranged as to be convenient for dwelling and inhabited by people, that is, houses.

उभावर्धौ साधू—जगतः चराचरात्मकौ भागौ, मर्त्यामर्त्यात्मकौ वा । (ubhāvardhau sādhū—jagataḥ carācarātmakau bhāgau, martyāmartyātmakau vā |) The world is described as having two meanings: either it contains two kinds, the stationary (that does not move), in the form of trees, creepers and the like, and the moving, with beings able to move; or it contains two kinds of beings, those subject to death and those not subject to death, i.e. gods and mortals. All these are explained as becoming favourable and effective for the sacrificer.

p. 99

Ṛk 16

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

या वो॑ मा॒या अ॑भि॒द्रुहे॑ यजत्राः॒ पाशा॑ आदित्या रि॒पवे॒ विचृ॑त्ताः । अ॒श्वीव॒ ता अति॑ येषं॒ रथे॒नारि॑ष्टा उ॒रावा [?] शर्म॑न्ताम ॥ १६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

याः । वः । मायाः । अभिद्रुहे । यजत्राः । पाशाः । आदित्याः । रिपवे । विचृत्ताः । अश्वीऽइव [?] । तान् । अति । येषं । रथेन । अरिष्टाः । उरौ । आ । शर्मन् । स्याम ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे यजत्रा यष्टव्या आदित्या वो युष्माकं या माया अभिद्रुहेऽभि- द्रोहं कुर्वते राक्षसादये निर्मिताः ये च पाशा रिपवे शत्रवे विचृत्ताः ॥ चृती हिंसासंग्रंथनयोः । प्रसारिता इत्यर्थः । तान्पाशान् मायाश्च रथेनातियेषं । अतीत्य प्रयतेयं । अतितरेयमित्यर्थः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अश्वीव । यथा शोभ- नाश्वः कश्चित्पुरुषो दुस्तरान्मार्गान् शीघ्रमतिक्रामति तद्वत् ॥ येषृ प्रयत्ने भौवादिकोऽनुदात्तेत् । छांदसो लज् । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं ॥ तथा मयम- रिष्टाः शत्रुभिरहिंसिताः संत उर् विस्तीर्णे शर्मन् ॥ शर्मेति गृहनाम ॥ त्वया दत्ते सुखे गृहे ना आ समंतात् स्याम । वर्तमाना भवेम ॥

Gist: the Ādityas' illusions and snares, spread against fiends and foes, are to be crossed by the sacrificers as a horseman quickly crosses a hard road; may they dwell unharmed in a wide house.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

yajatrāḥ: worthy of sacrifice; ādityāḥ: O Ādityas; abhidruhe: for the binding of fiends and others who work harm; vaḥ: your; yāḥ māyāḥ: whatever powers of illusion there are; ripave: for the binding of enemies; pāśāḥ: whatever snares; vicchatāḥ [?]: are spread out (such); tān: those snares and illusions; aśvīva: as a man possessed of a horse crosses a hard road; rathena: by chariot; ati yeṣam: help us to cross; ariṣṭāḥ: we, unharmed by enemies; urau: in a wide; śarman: house; ā syāma: may we be happy.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, worthy of sacrifice, with whatever powers of illusion you have for binding the fiends and others who work harm, and whatever snares are spread for binding enemies, using those snares and illusions as well, help us also to cross by chariot, as a man with a horse crosses a hard road. Unharmed by enemies, may we be happy in a wide house.

p. 100

Printed English translation

Adorable Adityas, may I pass (safe) in your car from the illusions which (you devise) for the malignant, the snares which are spread for your foes, (in like manner) as a horseman (passes over a road); and thus may we abide secure in infinite felicity.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

yajatrāḥ ādityāḥ: the Ādityas are addressed as worthy of being worshipped by the sacrificers with sacrifice. Since they have spread illusions and snares for the restraint of the fiends who work harm in every way, and for the destruction of enemies bent on injury, the sacrificers pray that, like अश्वीव रथेन (aśvīva rathena) — a man with a good (swift) horse who quickly crosses roads hard to cross (the Sanskrit explanation is quoted in the bhāṣya, beginning शोभनाश्वः कश्चित् पुरुषः (śobhanāśvaḥ kaścit puruṣaḥ)) — they may cross, seated in the chariot by the favour of the Ādityas, using the illusions spread for the binding and restraint of enemies and fiends. This is explained by way of an illustration.

ariṣṭāḥ urau śarman ā syāma: the word śarma is listed among the names of house (Ni. 3-13; as printed in the supplied text, "ಸಿ. ೩-೧೩"). The sacrificers' wish is described: may we, unharmed by the injury of enemies, be happy in the large house granted by the Ādityas.

Ṛk 17

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

माहं म॒घोनो॑ वरुण प्रि॒यस्य॑ भूरि॒दान्न॒ आ वि॑दं॒ शून॑मा॒पेः । मा रा॒यो रा॑जन्स्य॒यमा॒दव॑ [?] स्थां बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥

māhaṃ maghono varuṇa priyasya bhūridānna ā vidaṃ śūnamāpeḥ | mā rāyo rājansyayamādava [?] sthāṃ bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖

p. 101

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मा । अहं मघोनः । वरुण । प्रियस्य । भूर्इदाव्यः [?] । आ । विदं । शूनं । आपेः । मा । रायः । राजन् । सुयमात् । आव । स्थां । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सु- वीराः ॥ १७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण मघोनो धनवतः प्रियस्यानुकूलस्य भूरिदाव्यो भूरेर्बहुलस्य दातुराढ्यस्याहं मा अविदं । मावेदयानि । आवेदनं विज्ञापनं मा करवाणि । किं तदनावेद्यं । आपेर्ज्ञातेः शूनं शून्यं दारिद्रं ॥ वर्णलोपश्चांदसः ॥ यद्वा शूनं गतं प्राप्तं दारिद्रं ॥ टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योः । श्विदितो निष्ठायामितीट् प्रति- षेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । ओदितश्चति नकारः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ एतदुक्तं भवति अस्मदीयाः पुत्रादयः क्षुधिता इति प्रभुप्रभुसमीपेभिधाय याचमानो मा भूवमिति । हेराजन् सुयमात् । सुष्टु नियम्यतेनेन पुरुषो गृह इति सुयमः ॥ ईषद्दुःसुष्टिति खलु ॥ ताद्बशाद्रायो धनान्मावस्थां । अवयुत्य स्थितो मा भूवं । वयं सुवीराः शोभनपुत्रा विदथे यज्ञॆ गृहे वर्तमानाः संतो बृहत् फ्रौढं स्तोत्रं वदेम । उच्चारयाम ॥

Gist: may I not, before a wealthy generous patron, plead my kinsmen's poverty and beg; may we, rich in sons, recite a great hymn at the sacrifice.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

varuṇa: O Varuṇa; maghonaḥ: of the wealthy one; priyasya: of the favourable one; bhūridānvaḥ: of the one who gives abundantly, before such a rich man; ahaṃ: I; āpeḥ: of my near kinsman; śūnaṃ: the poverty; mā ā vidaṃ: may I not have to declare; rājan: O lord Varuṇa; suyamāt: from the wealth gathered under restraint; rāyaḥ: by wealth; mā ava sthāṃ: may I not become empty; (vayaṃ: we); suvīrāḥ: together with excellent sons; vidathe: in the sacrificial house; bṛhat: a mature hymn; vadema: we recite.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, before a wealthy, favourable, abundantly giving rich man, may I not say that my sons and other near kinsmen suffer in poverty and so ask him for wealth. May I not be left empty of the wealth gathered under restraint. Together with excellent sons we recite a mature hymn in the sacrificial house.

p. 102

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 3 [as printed; should be 2], Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 27, p. 102.

Printed English translation

May I never (have to) represent, Varuna, the destitution of a (once) opulent, dear, and munificent kinsman : may I never, royal Varuna, be devoid of well-regulated riches : (and) may we, blessed with excellent descendants, worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

By the word वरुण (varuṇa) the Āditya is addressed here. It was explained earlier that Varuṇa too is one of the twelve Ādityas.

मघोनः—धनवतः (maghonaḥ—dhanavataḥ): the word मघ (magha) is read by Yāska (Ni. 3-9) among the names of wealth; the meaning "possessed of wealth" is given.

प्रियस्य भूरिदान्वः आपेः शुनं मा आ विदं (priyasya bhūridānvaḥ āpeḥ śunaṃ mā ā vidaṃ) (explained as): in the presence of a very generous, wealthy man, may I, the sacrificer, not become a petitioner by declaring poverty, saying that our sons and others are hungry. The prayer is explained thus: may we, the sacrificers, not have to go to a rich man who is beneficent and gives abundantly and ask for wealth, saying that our sons and the rest live in poverty.

शूनं—शून्यं, यद्वा शूनं गतं प्राप्तं दारिद्रं (śūnaṃ—śūnyaṃ, yadvā śūnaṃ gataṃ prāptaṃ dāridraṃ): the meaning of the word शून (śūna) is explained as the absence of any kind of thing, or the poverty (want) that leads to a state of emptiness.

राजन् सुयमात् रायः मा अवस्थाम् (rājan suyamāt rāyaḥ mā avasthām)—सुष्टु नियम्यते अनेन पुरुषो गृहे इति सुयमः (suṣṭu niyamyate anena puruṣo gṛhe iti suyamaḥ): Varuṇa is addressed by the word rājan, and it is prayed that by his favour the wealth gathered by us, the sacrificers, may never be destroyed.

The sacrificers say: बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ): at sacrifices, together with our excellent sons, we recite hymns; therefore bestow favour on us. This is the prayer.

p. 103

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 9, p. 103.

Sūkta 28 (Maṇḍala 2)

The twenty-eighth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

इदमित्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं । आत्रानुक्रम्यते' इदमेकादश वारुणमिति। पूर्वसूक्ते कूर्मो गार्त्समदो हि वेत्युक्तत्वादस्कोत्तरस्य च कूर्मो गृत्समदो वा ऋषिः । त्रिष्टुप् छंदः । वरुणो देवता । विनियोगो लैंगिकः । अत्र केचिदाहुः । इदमेकादशर्चं तु वारुणं भयपापनुत् । ऋणदारिद्र्यदुःस्वप्न- नाशनं चेति शुश्रुम । ऋग्विधा. १२५-१ । इति ॥

Gist: idam is the sixth sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of eleven ṛks, by Kūrma Gārtsamada or Gṛtsamada, in triṣṭubh metre, to Varuṇa; its application is by indication; the Ṛgvidhāna is quoted as saying it removes fear, sin, debt, poverty and bad dreams.

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta idaṃ kaverādityasya is the sixth sūkta of the third anuvāka; it has eleven ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said इदमेकादश वारुणं (idamekādaśa vāruṇaṃ) ("these eleven are to Varuṇa"). Since the previous sūkta states that the seer is कूर्मो गार्त्समदो हि वा (kūrmo gārtsamado hi vā), the seer of this sūkta and of the next is Kūrma, son of Gṛtsamada, or Gṛtsamada himself; the metre is triṣṭubh; the deity is Varuṇa; the application is laiṅgika. Concerning this sūkta, some say, from the verse इदमेकादशर्चं तु वारुणं भयपापनुत् । ऋणदारिद्र्यदुःस्वप्ननाशनं चेति शुश्रुम (idamekādaśarcaṃ tu vāruṇaṃ bhayapāpanut | ṛṇadāridryaduḥsvapnanāśanaṃ ceti śuśruma) (Ṛgvidhāna 2-21-1 as printed in the Anuvāda; the bhāṣya quotation prints the reference as 125-1), that for those who recite this eleven-ṛk hymn to Varuṇa, fear, sin, poverty and bad dreams are removed.

Sūkta—28

Maṇḍala 2 ‖ Anuvāka 3 ‖ Sūkta 5 [as printed; the sūkta is the sixth of the anuvāka] ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 7 ‖ Varga 9, 10 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 11 · Ṛṣi: Kūrma Gārtsamada, or Gṛtsamada · Devatā: Varuṇa · Chandas: triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

इ॒दं क॒वेरा॑दि॒त्यस्य॑ स्व॒राजो॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ सान्त्य॒भ्य॑स्तु [?] म॒ह्ना । अति॒यो म॒न्द्रो [?] य॒जथा॑य दे॒वः सु॑की॒र्तिं भि॑क्षे॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ भूरेः॑॥

idaṃ kaverādityasya svarājo viśvāni sāntyabhyastu [?] mahnā | atiyo mandro [?] yajathāya devaḥ sukīrtiṃ bhikṣe varuṇasya bhūreḥ‖

(The supplied text prints no Ṛk number after this verse. Possible slips flagged in the Kannada text: सान्त्यभ्यस्तु (sāntyabhyastu) (flagged in the Kannada text) where the Pada gives सन्ति (santi) and अभि (abhi) separately, and मन्द्रो (mandro) (flagged in the Kannada text) where the Pada gives मन्दः (mandaḥ).)

p. 104

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 104.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इदं । कवेः । आदित्यस्य । स्वराजः । विश्वानि । सन्ति । अभि । अस्तु । मह्ना । अति । यः । मन्दः । यजथाय । देवः । सुकीर्तिं । भिक्षे । वरुणस्य । भूरेः॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

कवेः क्रांतदर्शिन आदित्यास्यादितेः पुत्रस्य स्वराजः स्वयमेव राजमानस्येश्वरस्य वा वरुणस्येदं हविः स्तोत्रं वा यजमानः करोतीति शेषः । स च विश्वानि सर्वाणि संति द्वितीयभावनिकारभांजि [?] भूतजातानि मह्ना महिम्ना वरुणप्रासादाल्लभेना- भ्यस्तु । अभिभवतु । यो देवो द्योतमानो वरुणो यजथाय यष्टे पुरुषाय अति अतिशयेन मंद्रः स्तुत्यो हर्षयिता वा भवति तस्य भूरेः भर्तुर्वरु- णस्य सुकीर्तिं शोभनां स्तुतिं भिक्षे । प्रार्थये । यद्वा वरुणस्यॆति तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी । तेन वरुणेन दातव्यां शोभनां कीर्तिमहं याचे ॥

kaveḥ krāṃtadarśina ādityāsyāditeḥ putrasya svarājaḥ svayameva rājamānasyeśvarasya vā varuṇasyedaṃ haviḥ stotraṃ vā yajamānaḥ karotīti śeṣaḥ | sa ca viśvāni sarvāṇi saṃti dvitīyabhāvanikārabhāṃji [?] bhūtajātāni mahnā mahimnā varuṇaprāsādāllabhenā- bhyastu | abhibhavatu | yo devo dyotamāno varuṇo yajathāya yaṣṭe puruṣāya ati atiśayena maṃdraḥ stutyo harṣayitā vā bhavati tasya bhūreḥ bharturvaru- ṇasya sukīrtiṃ śobhanāṃ stutiṃ bhikṣe | prārthaye | yadvā varuṇasyèti tṛtīyārthe ṣaṣṭhī | tena varuṇena dātavyāṃ śobhanāṃ kīrtimahaṃ yāce ‖

Gist: This praise or oblation is offered to Varuṇa, son of Aditi, self-luminous and a lord; by his grace may the sacrificer overcome all beings; I ask of this delightful god the good fame he gives. (The word द्वितीयभावनिकारभांजि (dvitīyabhāvanikārabhāṃji) (flagged in the Kannada text) is unclear in the supplied text.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

kaveḥ: of the far-seeing one; ādityasya: of the son of Aditi; svarājaḥ: of the self-luminous one; varuṇasya: to Varuṇa; idaṃ: this oblation or hymn (is offered); (sa ca: the sacrificer who offers this oblation); viśvāni: all; santi: beings; mahnā: by (the greatness gained through Varuṇa's grace) majesty; abhyastu: may he bring under his control; devaḥ: shining; yaḥ: which Varuṇa; yajathāya: to the man who performs the sacrifice; ati: exceedingly; mandraḥ: is delighting; bhūreḥ: of such a Varuṇa, the supporter; sukīrtiṃ: the excellent praise; bhikṣe: I beg [or: bhūreḥ: from such a Varuṇa, the supporter; sukīrtiṃ: the auspicious fame; bhikṣe: I ask].

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer offers this oblation to Varuṇa, who is far-seeing, the son of Aditi, and self-luminous. Through his majesty gained by Varuṇa's favour may this sacrificer bring all beings under his control. From such a Varuṇa, the supporter, who is exceedingly delighting to the man who performs the sacrifice, I beg auspicious fame.

p. 105

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 9, p. 105.

Printed English translation

(The worshipper repeats) this praise of the sage, the self-radiant Aditya : may he preside over all beings by his power : I beg for fame of the sovereign Varuna, a diety [sic] who, when much pleased, (is propitious) to his adorer.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

कवेः (kaveḥ)—क्रांतदर्शिनः (krāṃtadarśinaḥ): Yāska has read the word kavi among the names of the intelligent (Ni. 12-13) and explained it: "the intelligent man is one who sees beyond (krānta-darśana), or from the root kavate" (Ni. 12-13). Varuṇa, the son of the goddess Aditi, is described as one who has seen the far shore of wisdom. स्वराजः (svarājaḥ)—स्वयमेव राजमानस्य ईश्वरस्य वा (svayameva rājamānasya īśvarasya vā): shining of himself, that is, brilliant without the help of other lights, and lord over all. The word इदं (idaṃ) is given the meaning oblation or hymn, and it is explained that the sacrificer offers the oblation or hymn to Varuṇa, who is self-luminous and sovereign over all.

विश्वानि संति (viśvāni saṃti)—सर्वाणि द्वितीयभाव विकारभांजि [?] भूतजातानि (sarvāṇi dvitīyabhāva vikārabhāṃji [?] bhūtajātāni) (the words द्वितीयभाव विकारभांजि (dvitīyabhāva vikārabhāṃji) are unclear in the supplied text): all created beings. It is explained that through the greatness arising from Varuṇa's favour the sacrificer may bring under his control all beings, moving and unmoving.

अतिमंद्रः (atimaṃdraḥ)—अतिशयेन स्तुत्यः हर्षयिता वा (atiśayena stutyaḥ harṣayitā vā): exceedingly praiseworthy, or a gladdener. The word mandra is read by Yāska among the names of speech (as printed: सि २-२३ (si 2-23), the reference letter being as supplied; the word before "names" is printed वाज्ञामगळल्लि (vājñāmagaḷalli)) and explained as "mandrā is delighting, or gladdening to the world" (as printed: सि. ११-३० (si. 11-30)). It is said that Varuṇa is praiseworthy to the sacrificer and the producer of joy.

सुकीर्तिं भिक्षे (sukīrtiṃ bhikṣe)—शोभनां स्तुतिं यद्वा वरुणेन दातव्यां शोभनां कीर्तिं (śobhanāṃ stutiṃ yadvā varuṇena dātavyāṃ śobhanāṃ kīrtiṃ): for the word bhūri, "of Varuṇa, the lord (bhartuḥ)": the sacrificer asks for the praise (the devout mind that performs it), or the excellent fame granted by the favour of Varuṇa.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तव॑ व्र॒ते सु॒भगा॑सः स्याम स्वा॒ध्यो॑ वरुण तुष्टु॒वांसः॑ । उ॒पाय॑न उ॒षसां॒ गोम॑तीनाम॒ग्नयो॒न जर॑माणा॒ अनु॒द्यून्॥

tava vrate subhagāsaḥ syāma svādhyo varuṇa tuṣṭuvāṃsaḥ | upāyana uṣasāṃ gomatīnāmagnayona jaramāṇā anudyūn‖

p. 106

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 106.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तव । व्रते । सुभगासः । स्याम । सुआध्यः । वरुण । तुस्तुवांसः । उपअयने । उषसां । गोमतीनां । अग्नयः । न । जरमाणाः । अनु । द्यून् ॥ २ ॥

tava | vrate | subhagāsaḥ | syāma | suādhyaḥ | varuṇa | tustuvāṃsaḥ | upaayane | uṣasāṃ | gomatīnāṃ | agnayaḥ | na | jaramāṇāḥ | anu | dyūn ‖ 2 ‖

(Differences between the Saṃhitā and Pada as supplied: तुष्टुवांसः (tuṣṭuvāṃsaḥ) in the Saṃhitā but तुस्तुवांसः (tustuvāṃsaḥ) in the Pada; उपायन (upāyana) in the Saṃhitā against उपअयने (upaayane) in the Pada. Both are as supplied; no correction made.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण स्वाध्यः शोभनाध्यानास्तुष्टुवांसः स्तुतवंतो वयं तव व्रते त्वदीये परिचरणाख्यॆ कर्मणि वर्तमानाः सुभगासः स्याम । शोभनधना भवेम । अपि च गोमतीनां रश्मिभिर्युक्तानामुषसामुपायन उपागमने सत्यग्नयो न यथाग्नयोऽग्निहोत्रादिकर्मार्थं समिध्यंते एवमनु द्यून् अनुदिनं जरमाणास्त्वां स्तुवंतो वयं दीप्यमाना भवेम ॥

Gist: O Varuṇa, may we, devout and praising you, engaged in your service, be rich; and as fires are kindled at dawn for the fire-offering, may we, praising you daily, shine.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Varuṇa: O Varuṇa; svādhyaḥ: we who are endowed with excellent meditation; tuṣṭuvāṃsaḥ: who praise (you); tava vrate: engaged in the work of worshipping you; subhagāsaḥ: possessed of excellent wealth; syāma: grant that we may become; gomatīnām: accompanied by rays; uṣasām: of the dawns; upāyane: at the time of rising; agnayo na: as the fires kindled for the fire-offering shine; anu dyūn: every day; jaramāṇāḥ: we who praise you; may we be shining.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, we who are endowed with excellent meditation and who praise you, engaged in the work of worshipping you, grant that we may become possessed of excellent wealth. As the fire kindled for the fire-offering shines at the rising of the dawns accompanied by rays, may we who praise you daily go on shining.

Printed English translation

May we, Varuna, deeply meditating on you earnestly praising you and (engaged) in your worship, be prosperous ; glorifying you daily, like the fires (that are kindled in your honour) at the coming of the luminous dawns.

p. 107

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 9, p. 107.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

व्रते (vrate)—त्वदीये परिचरणाख्यॆ कर्मणि वर्तमानाः (tvadīye paricaraṇākhyè karmaṇi vartamānāḥ): the word vrata is read by Yāska among the names of work (Ni. 3-2) and explained "vrata is a name of work, because it is chosen" (Ni. 2-13). Here Sāyaṇa gives the meaning: work consisting of service, relating to Varuṇa.

सुभगासः (subhagāsaḥ)—शोभनधनाः (śobhanadhanāḥ): here the prefix su is applied to the word bhaga. The word is used as an epithet of the sacrificers; the meaning wealth is given, and the sacrificers' prayer is stated, that they may be endowed with excellent wealth. Yāska explains भगो भजतेः (bhago bhajateḥ) (Ni. 1-7), reads it among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) with the meaning wealth, explains it as "dharma" in भगस्य भागधेयस्य (bhagasya bhāgadheyasya) (Ni. 9-21), and in प्रातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम (prātarjitaṃ bhagamugraṃ huvema) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-41-2) as one of the gods, a son of the goddess Aditi.

गोमतीनां उषसां उपायने अग्नयो न (gomatīnāṃ uṣasāṃ upāyane agnayo na): Yāska gives various meanings of the word go (Ni. 2-5). Here it is used in the sense of ray (raśmi). After giving this sense, the passage रश्मिभिर्युक्तानां उषसां उपागमे यथा अग्नयो अग्नि होत्रादिकर्मार्थं समिध्यंते एवं त्वां स्तुवंतो वयं दीप्यमाना भवेम (raśmibhiryuktānāṃ uṣasāṃ upāgame yathā agnayo agni hotrādikarmārthaṃ samidhyaṃte evaṃ tvāṃ stuvaṃto vayaṃ dīpyamānā bhavema) is given. The sacrificers' prayer is expressed thus: as at the rising of the dawns the fire is kindled for the performance of the fire-offering and other rites, so may we sacrificers who praise Varuṇa shine with splendour every day.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तव॑ स्याम पुरु॒वीर॑स्य॒ शर्म॑न्नुरु॒शंस॑स्य वरुण प्रणेतः । यू॒यं नः॑ पुत्रा अदितेरदब्धा अ॒भि क्ष॑मध्वं॒ युज्या॑य देवाः ॥

tava syāma puruvīrasya śarmannuruśaṃsasya varuṇa praṇetaḥ | yūyaṃ naḥ putrā aditeradabdhā abhi kṣamadhvaṃ yujyāya devāḥ ‖

(The supplied text prints no Ṛk number after this verse.)

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तव । स्याम । पुरुवीरस्य । शर्मन् । उरुशंसस्य । वरुण । प्रनेतरिति प्रनेतः । यूयं । नः । पुत्राः । आदितेः । आदब्धाः । अभि । क्षमध्वं । युज्याय । देवाः ॥

tava | syāma | puruvīrasya | śarman | uruśaṃsasya | varuṇa | pranetariti pranetaḥ | yūyaṃ | naḥ | putrāḥ | āditeḥ | ādabdhāḥ | abhi | kṣamadhvaṃ | yujyāya | devāḥ ‖

(The Pada: प्रनेतरिति प्रनेतः (pranetariti pranetaḥ) against Saṃhitā प्रणेतः (praṇetaḥ), and आदितेः (āditeḥ), आदब्धाः (ādabdhāḥ) against अदिते (adite), अदब्धा (adabdhā) in the Saṃhitā, are as supplied; the Pada here shows no Ṛk number. The Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of this Ṛk follows on the next page.)

p. 108

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 108.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे प्रणेतः सर्वस्य जगतः प्रकर्षेण नेतर्वरुण पुरुवीरस्य पुरुभिर्बहुभिः- र्वीर्रैरुपेतस्य यद्वा पुरूणां बहूनां शत्रोणां विशेषेण प्रेरकस्योरु- शंसस्योरुभिर्बहुभिः स्तूयमानस्य तव शर्मन् शर्मणि सुखे गृहे ना स्याम । अदितेः पुत्रा मित्रादयः ॥ परमपि छंदसीति परस्य षष्ठ्यंतस्य पूर्वामंत्रितांगव द्भावेनानुप्रवेशात् पदद्वयसमुदायस्याष्टमिकं सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥ अदब्बाः शत्रुभिरहिंसिताः । एवंभूता हे देवा यूयं नोऽस्मान् कृतापराधान् युज्याय सख्यायाभिक्षमध्वं । अस्माभिः कृतमपराधं सहध्वं ॥

Gist: Varuṇa, leader of all the world, may we dwell in your protection; sons of Aditi, unharmed by foes, forgive our offences and keep us in friendship.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Pranetaḥ (leader)—guide of the whole world; Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Puruvīrasya—of you who are endowed with many kinds of valour; Uruśaṃsasya—praised by many people; Tava—your; Śarman—in the pleasant house; Syāma—may we be; Aditeḥ putrāḥ—O sons of Aditi, Mitra and the other gods; Adabdhāḥ—unharmed by enemies; Devāḥ—divine in nature; Yūyaṃ—you; Naḥ—us (even though we have committed offences); Yujyāya—for friendship; Abhi kṣamadhvaṃ—forgive.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, guide of the whole world, may we dwell in your pleasant house, you who are endowed with many kinds of valour and are praised by many people. O sons of Aditi, Mitra and the other gods, unharmed by enemies and divine in nature, forgive our offences and preserve our friendship with you.

Printed English translation

Varuna, chief guide (of men), may we abide in the felicity of you who are endowed with great prowess, and are glorified by many: divine sons of Aditi, unharmed (by foes), have compassion upon us through your benevolence.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

प्रणीतः (praṇītaḥ) (as supplied; the Ṛk has praṇetaḥ)—सर्वस्य जगतः प्रकर्षेण नेतः (sarvasya jagataḥ prakarṣeṇa netaḥ): Varuṇa leads the whole world abundantly, that is, he regulates it greatly; this is the meaning explained.

p. 109

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 9, p. 109.

पुरुवीरस्य (puruvīrasya)—बहुभिर्वीरैरुपेतस्य यद्वा बहूनां शत्रूणां विशेषेण प्रेरकस्य (bahubhirvīrairupetasya yadvā bahūnāṃ śatrūṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa prerakasya). The word vīra is explained by Yāska as वीरो वीरयत्यमित्रान् । वेतेर्वा स्याद्दतिकर्मणः । वीरयतेर्वा (vīro vīrayatyamitrān | vetervā syāddatikarmaṇaḥ | vīrayatervā) (Ni. 1-7) [text as supplied]. Sāyaṇa gives two meanings, "endowed with strength" or "enemies", and so describes Varuṇa either as endowed with many heroes or as one who drives out enemies.

शर्मन् (śarman)—गृहे सुखे वा (gṛhe sukhe vā): the word śarma is read by Yāska (Ni. 3-13) among the names both of "house" and of "happiness"; therefore Sāyaṇa gives both meanings.

In the first half of this Ṛk Varuṇa is praised, in the second half the Ādityas, Mitra and the others, sons of Aditi. The sacrificers' dwelling in the happiness or house favoured by Varuṇa is prayed for, and the prayer is expressed that Mitra and the other Ādityas should forgive the sacrificers' offences.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

प्र सी॑मादि॒त्यो अ॑सृजद्विध॒र्ता ऋ॒तं सिंध॑वो॒ वरु॑णस्य यंति । न श्रा॑म्यंति॒ न वि मु॑चंत्ये॒ते वयो॒ न प॑प्तु रघु॒या परि॑ज्मन् ॥

pra sīmādityo asṛjadvidhartā ṛtaṃ siṃdhavo varuṇasya yaṃti | na śrāmyaṃti na vi mucaṃtyete vayo na paptu raghuyā parijman ‖

(The supplied text prints a stray "1," before the Saṃhitā label and no Ṛk number after the verse; the Saṃhitā reads पप्तु रघुया (paptu raghuyā) where the Pada has पप्तुः (paptuḥ). Both as supplied.)

॥ पदपाठः ॥

प्र । सीं । आदित्यः । असृजत् । विधर्ता । ऋतं । सिंधवः । वरुणस्य । यंति । न । श्राम्यंति । न । वि । मुचंति । एते । वयः । न । पप्तुः । रघुया । परिज्मन् ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

विधर्ता सेतुरिव जलस्य विधारयितादित्योऽदितेः पुत्रो वरुण्ययतं विधारण- हेतुभूतं सत्यं यद्वा नदीनामुपादानभूतमुदकं सीं सर्वतः प्रासृजत् । प्रकर्षेण सृष्टवान् ॥ अणोऽप्रगृह्यस्यानुनासिक इत्याकारः सानुनासिकः ॥ तेन वरुणस्यर्तेन सिंधवः स्यंदनशीला नद्यो यंति ! गच्छंति प्रवहंति । एते सिंधवो

vidhartā seturiva jalasya vidhārayitādityo 'diteḥ putro varuṇyayataṃ vidhāraṇa- hetubhūtaṃ satyaṃ yadvā nadīnāmupādānabhūtamudakaṃ sīṃ sarvataḥ prāsṛjat | prakarṣeṇa sṛṣṭavān ‖ aṇo 'pragṛhyasyānunāsika ityākāraḥ sānunāsikaḥ ‖ tena varuṇasyartena siṃdhavaḥ syaṃdanaśīlā nadyo yaṃti ! gacchaṃti pravahaṃti | ete siṃdhavo

p. 110

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 110.

न श्राम्यंति । श्रांतिं न प्राप्नुवंति । न विमुचंति । उपरता न भवंति । अनलसाः सर्वदैकरूप्येण प्रवहंतीत्यर्थः । एतदेवोच्यते । वयो न । वयः दक्षिण इव रघुया रघवः शीघ्रगामिनः परिज्मन् परिज्मनि भूम्यां पप्तुः । पतंति गच्छंति ॥ पत्लृ गतौ । लिट्युसि तनिपत्योश्चंदसीत्युपधालोपॆः । स्थानिवद्भावाद्विर्वचनादि । रघुया इत्यत्र सुपां सुलुगिति जसो याजादेशः ॥

Gist: Aditi's son Varuṇa, upholder like a dam, has sent forth the water (or truth); by his law the rivers flow untiringly and swiftly like birds. The grammatical tail explains the nasalised ā, the elision of the penultimate letter in the perfect paptuḥ (Pāṇini rules not numbered in the supplied text) and the substitution of yāc for jas in raghuyā.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Vidhartā—the holder of the water; Ādityaḥ—Varuṇa, son of Aditi; Ṛtaṃ—truth or water; Sīṃ—everywhere; Pra asṛjat—created; Varuṇasya—by Varuṇa's ordinance; Sindhavaḥ—the (flowing) rivers; Yanti—flow; Ete—these rivers; Na śrāmyanti—do not become weary; Na vi muñcanti—do not cease flowing; Vayo na—like birds; Raghuyā—swift; Parijman—on the earth; Paptuḥ—fall and glide.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Varuṇa, the holder of the water and son of Aditi, created water everywhere. By the power of Varuṇa's command the rivers flow. These rivers neither become weary nor stop their flow. Swift like birds, they fall on the earth and flow on.

Printed English translation

The Aditya, the upholder, has created all this water : the rivers flow by the power of Varuna: they never weary, they never stop; they have descended with swiftness, like birds upon the circumambient (earth).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ऋतं (ṛtaṃ)—विधारणहेतुभूतं सत्यं यद्वा नदीनामुपादानभूतमुदकं (vidhāraṇahetubhūtaṃ satyaṃ yadvā nadīnāmupādānabhūtamudakaṃ). The word ṛta is read by Yāska among the names of water, truth and sacrifice (Ni. 2-24, 4-19). Sāyaṇa gives two meanings: truth, the chief cause of upholding everything, or water, which is pre-eminent in the rivers.

विधर्ता (vidhartā)—सेतुरिव जलस्य विधारयिता (seturiva jalasya vidhārayitā): as a dam holds back water, so Varuṇa holds the rain-waters; the explanation compares him to a dam,

p. 111

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 9, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 111.

सिंधवः—स्यंदनशीलाः (siṃdhavaḥ—syaṃdanaśīlāḥ): "the flowing ones". The Nirukta authors have read this word among the names of rivers (Ni. 2-24), and they have also explained it, "Sindhu, from flowing" (Ni. 5-27). The comment says that Varuṇa created the waters, held them up for the benefit of the worlds, and made them flow over the earth in the form of rivers. These rivers never stop their flow; as swift-going birds, flying in the sky, also move about on the earth, so these rivers too, so that their waters are never in one place, flow in a single unvaried course (अनलसाः ऐकरूप्येण प्रवहंति (analasāḥ aikarūpyeṇa pravahaṃti)), giving no room for even the least sloth. The commentary explains that Varuṇa created the waters for the good of the world, held them, and made them flow ceaselessly over the earth. The Nirukta authors, too, have cited this same idea from the Ṛk beginning as follows (Ma. Saṃ. 8-69-12):

सुदेवो असि वरुण यस्य ते सप्त सिंधवः । अनुक्षरंति काकुदं सूम्यं सुषिरामिव ॥ (sudevo asi varuṇa yasya te sapta siṃdhavaḥ | anukṣaraṃti kākudaṃ sūmyaṃ suṣirāmiva ‖)

(The passage ends with "thus they have cited it from the Ṛk"; a software-generated line about a decorative symbol was removed from kn.md here. The reference is given as (Ma. Saṃ. 8-69-12) in kn.md.)

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वि मच्छ्र॑थाय रश॒नामि॒वाग॑ ऋ॒ध्याम॑ ते वरुण॒ खामृ॒तस्य॑ । मा तंतु॑श्छेदि॒ वय॑तो॒ धियं॑ मे॒ मा मात्रा॑ शार्य॒पसः॑ पु॒र॒ ऋतोः ॥ ५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

वि । मत् । श्रथय । रशनांइव । आगः । यध्याम । ते । वरुण । खां । ऋतस्य । मा । तंतुः । छेदि । वयतः । धियं । मे । मा । मात्रा । शारि । अपसः । पुरा । ऋतोः ॥ ५ ॥

vi | mat | śrathaya | raśanāṃiva | āgaḥ | yadhyāma | te | varuṇa | khāṃ | ṛtasya | mā | taṃtuḥ | chedi | vayataḥ | dhiyaṃ | me | mā | mātrā | śāri | apasaḥ | purā | ṛtoḥ ‖ 5 ‖

(Readings as supplied: Saṃhitā ऋध्याम (ṛdhyāma) against Pada यध्याम (yadhyāma), Saṃhitā मच्छ्रथाय (macchrathāya) and खामृतस्य (khāmṛtasya) against Pada मत् । श्रथय (mat | śrathaya) and खां । ऋतस्य (khāṃ | ṛtasya), Saṃhitā शार्यपसः (śāryapasaḥ) against Pada शारि । अपसः (śāri | apasaḥ); the bhāṣya below reads ऋध्याम. Not altered.)

p. 112

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 112.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण मत् मत्सकाशात् रशनामिव रज्जुमिवागो विहिताननुष्ठानजनितं पापं विश्रथय ! शिथिलीकुरु ! विमोचयेत्यर्थः । ते त्वत्संबंधिन ऋतस्योदकस्य पूर्णां खां नदीं ॥ खा इति नदीनाम ॥ तामृध्याम । लभेमहि । अपि च धियं कर्म वयतः संतन्वतो मे मम तंतुः कर्मसंततिर्मा छेदि। छिन्नो मा भूत् । नैरंतर्येणेत्यर्थः । कथा ऋतोः समाप्तिकालात्पुरा पूर्वमपसः कर्मणो मात्रा शरीरं प्राज्योदीच्यांगलक्षणं मा शारि ! शीर्णं विकलं मा भूत् ॥ कृ हिंसायां । कर्मणि लुज् ॥ पुर ऋतोरित्यत्र ऋत्यक इति प्रकृतिभावः ॥

he varuṇa mat matsakāśāt raśanāmiva rajjumivāgo vihitānanuṣṭhānajanitaṃ pāpaṃ viśrathaya ! śithilīkuru ! vimocayetyarthaḥ | te tvatsaṃbaṃdhina ṛtasyodakasya pūrṇāṃ khāṃ nadīṃ ‖ khā iti nadīnāma ‖ tāmṛdhyāma | labhemahi | api ca dhiyaṃ karma vayataḥ saṃtanvato me mama taṃtuḥ karmasaṃtatirmā chedi| chinno mā bhūt | nairaṃtaryeṇetyarthaḥ | kathā ṛtoḥ samāptikālātpurā pūrvamapasaḥ karmaṇo mātrā śarīraṃ prājyodīcyāṃgalakṣaṇaṃ mā śāri ! śīrṇaṃ vikalaṃ mā bhūt ‖ kṛ hiṃsāyāṃ | karmaṇi luj ‖ pura ṛtorityatra ṛtyaka iti prakṛtibhāvaḥ ‖

Gist: "O Varuṇa, loosen from me the sin born of omitted rites, like a rope; may we obtain the river full of water; let the thread of my rite not be cut, nor the body of the rite broken before its completion." The grammatical tail explains the aorist śāri (from कृ हिंसायां (kṛ hiṃsāyāṃ), luṅ in the passive) and the natural form (prakṛtibhāva) of पुर ऋतोः (pura ṛtoḥ).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Mat—from me; Raśanāmiva—binding like a rope; Āgaḥ—the sin consisting in the omission of the observance; Viśrathaya—destroy; Te—given by you; Ṛtasya—full of water; Khāṃ—the river; Ṛdhyāma—may we obtain; Dhiyaṃ—the rite; Vayataḥ—of one weaving; Me—my; Tantuḥ—the thread in the form of the rite; Mā chedi—may it not be cut; Ṛtoḥ—than the time of completion; Purā—before; Apasaḥ—of the rite; Mātrā—the body; Mā śāri—do not cause to be broken.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, remove from me the sin, consisting in the omission of the observance, that binds like a rope. May we obtain the river that is given by you and is full of water. May my thread of rite, while I weave the cloth of the rite, not be cut. Before the time of its completion, do not cause the body of my rite to be broken.

Printed English translation

Cast off from me sin, Varuna, as if it were a rope: may we obtain from you a channel (filled) with water : cut not the thread of me (engaged id [sic]) weaving pious works: blight not the elements of holy rites before the season (of their maturity).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रशनामिन आगः वि श्रथय (raśanāmina āgaḥ vi śrathaya)—The word आगः (āgaḥ) is explained by Yāska as "from the verb gam with the prefix ā" (Ni. 11 22, as printed). The word is formed by the prefix ā joined with the root gam. "It surely comes to the doer, the one who has performed the rite" (अवश्यमेवैतदागच्छति कर्तारं (avaśyamevaitadāgacchati kartāraṃ)): the meaning "that which comes to him" is thus settled.

p. 113

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 10, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 113.

Raśanā means a thing fit for tying, so that clothes and the like stand firm when worn; usually a rope (cord) and the like. Since here it destroys freedom, the raśanā is said to be binding. For the word agas Sāyaṇa gives the meaning विहिताननुष्ठानजनितं पापं (vihitānanuṣṭhānajanitaṃ pāpaṃ), the sin that may arise from abandoning an obligatory duty. This sin lies in the rite of the doer of the rite, so that even if the rite is performed it does not yield its proper fruit; it turns into a fault, the sin of not having performed the rite in the prescribed way, and binds. So the sacrificer's prayer is expressed that these sins, binding like a rope (cord), be destroyed for us by Varuṇa's grace.

धियं वयतः मे तंतुः मा छेदि (dhiyaṃ vayataḥ me taṃtuḥ mā chedi)—"May the continuity of my rite, while I carry the rite on, not be cut" (कर्म संतन्वतः मम कर्मसंततिः छिन्नो मा भूत् (karma saṃtanvataḥ mama karmasaṃtatiḥ chinno mā bhūt)). The word dhī is given among the names of rite (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of knowledge (Ni. 3-13); here it is used in the sense of rite. The word vayataḥ, formed from the root वेञ् (veñ) (tantusantāne, stretching threads), means weaving cloth. If the threads of one weaving cloth and the like break while he is at his work, his weaving does not come out right. In the same way the absence of interruption (nicchitti as supplied) in the sacrificers' rites is here prayed for. As a body is complete when joined with its limbs, so a rite is joined with its limbs (the rites to be performed in the middle). Whether the limb is lost, or the rite stops before completion, the rite is broken; the sacrificer's prayer is expressed that neither kind of breaking of the rite occur.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अपो॒ सु म्य॑क्ष वरुण भि॒यसं॒ मत्सम्रा॒ळ्कृता॒वोऽनु॑ मा गृभाय। दामे॑व व॒त्साद्वि मु॑मु॒ग्धंहो॑ न॒हि त्वदा॒रे नि॒मिष॑श्च॒नेशे॑ ॥ ६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अपो इति । सु । म्यक्ष । वरुण । भियसं । मत् । संराट् । यत्नवः । अनु । मा । गृभाय । दामिइव । वत्सात् । वि । मुमुग्नि । अंहः । नहि । त्वत् । आरे । निमिषः । चन । ईशे ॥

apo iti | su | myakṣa | varuṇa | bhiyasaṃ | mat | saṃrāṭ | yatnavaḥ | anu | mā | gṛbhāya | dāmiiva | vatsāt | vi | mumugni | aṃhaḥ | nahi | tvat | āre | nimiṣaḥ | cana | īśe ‖

(The Pada as supplied reads संराट् । यत्नवः (saṃrāṭ | yatnavaḥ) and मुमुग्नि (mumugni) against Saṃhitā मत्सम्राळ्कृतावोऽनु (matsamrāḷkṛtāvo 'nu) and वि मुमुग्धंहो (vi mumugdhaṃho), and अपो इति । सु (apo iti | su) against the Saṃhitā अपो सु (apo su); the Pada's closing Ṛk number is missing in the supplied text, which ends the page with a stray "8", removed. Not altered.) The remainder of Ṛk 6 follows on the next page.

p. 114

Running head: Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 28, Sāyaṇabhāṣya-sahitā, p. 114.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण भियसं भयं मत् मत्तः सु सुष्टु अपो म्यक्ष । अपगमयॆ । हे सम्राट् समग्राजमान हे ऋतावः सत्यवन् यज्ञवन्वा वरुण मा मामनुगृ- भाय । अनुगृहाण ॥ छंदसि शायजपीति त्वः शायजादेशः । हृगृहोर्भ इति भत्वं ॥ अपि च दामेव वत्सात् यथा दोग्धा वत्ससकाशाद्बंधनीं रज्जुं विमुंचति तथांहः पापं मत्सकाशाद्विमुमुग्नि । विमुंच ॥ छांदसः शपः श्लुः ॥ पृथक्कुरु । त्वदारे त्वत्तो दूरदेशे वर्तमानः । त्वदन्य इत्यर्थः । त्वत्तोऽन्यः कश्चित् निमिषश्चन निमेषस्यापि अक्षिपक्षचलनस्यापि नहीशे । नेष्टे । त्वमेवेश्वर इत्यर्थः ॥ लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेष्टिति तलोपः ॥

Gist: "O Varuṇa, drive fear away from me and favour me; as a milker looses the tether from a calf, loosen sin from me; no one apart from you is master even for the twinkling of an eye." The grammatical tail explains the Vedic forms (the substitution śāyaj and the change to bh in gṛbhāya; the śap-elision in mumugni; the loss of ta in īśe).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Bhiyasaṃ—fear; Mat—from me; Su—completely; Apo mṛkṣa [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā and Pada read म्यक्ष (myakṣa)]—remove; Samrāṭ—you who shine completely; Ṛtāvaḥ—you who are truthful, O Varuṇa; Mā—me; Anu gṛbhāya—favour; Vatsāt—from a calf (eager to drink milk), from its neck; Dāmeva—as one looses a rope; Aṃhaḥ—sin; Vi mumugni—release (from me); Tvadāre—whatever person is far from you; Nimiṣaścana—even for the time of a twinkling; Nahi īśe—it is not possible to be independent.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, remove fear from me. O Varuṇa, who shine completely and are truthful, favour me. As the rope is loosed from the neck of a calf eager to drink milk, release sin from me. No person who is far from you can be independent even for the time of a twinkling.

Printed English translation

Keep off all danger from me, Varuna : supreme monarch, endowed with truth, bestow your favour upon me: cast off (frem [sic] me) sin, like a tether from a calf: no one rules for the twinkling of an eye, apart fram [sic] you.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Varuṇa, भियसं मत् सु आपो म्यक्ष (bhiyasaṃ mat su āpo myakṣa): the sacrificers pray for Varuṇa's favour, which is the state in which fear is wholly removed, so that fear arises from nobody and in no way.

p. 115

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 10, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 115.

दामेव वत्सात् अंहः वि मुमुग्नि (dāmeva vatsāt aṃhaḥ vi mumugni)—as a milker looses the tether-rope from a calf, so loosen sin from me. The word aṃhas is explained by Yāska: "aṃhati, aṃhas and aṃhu are derived from the root han, with an irregular (nirūḍha) infix" (Ni. 4-25); that is, the words aṃhati, aṃhas, aṃhu are formed from the root han, and the meaning "sin" is understood from them. The prayer is expressed for Varuṇa's favour that the sacrificer be freed from sins, as one milking the cow looses the calf from the rope. This is stated here by way of a simile. In त्वदारे (tvadāre), the word āre is read among the names for "far" (Ni. 3-20). Sāyaṇa interprets त्वत्तो दूरदेशे वर्तमानस्त्वदन्यः (tvatto dūradeśe vartamānastvadanyaḥ) as: one who is in a place far from Varuṇa (that is, one who does not regard Varuṇa as protector; "other than Varuṇa" means one who is not a recipient of Varuṇa's favour). Such a person, whoever he may be, cannot be independent even for निमिषश्चन (nimiṣaścana), the subtle time in which the eyelid moves; and Varuṇa's power is declared, that he alone favours all so that they may be independent.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मा नो॑ व॒धैर्व॑रुण॒ ये त॑ इ॒ष्टावेनः॑ कृ॒ण्वंत॑मसुर भ्री॒णंति॑ । मा ज्योति॑षः प्रवस॒थानि॑ गन्म॒ वि षू मृधः॑ शिश्रथो जी॒वसे॑ नः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मा । नः । वधैः । वरुण । ये । ते । इष्टौ । एनः । कृण्वंतं । असुर । भ्रीणंति । मा । ज्योतिषः । प्रवसथानि । गन्म । वि । सु । मृधः । शिश्रथः । जीवसे । नः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण नोऽस्मान् वधैर्हननसाधनैरायुधैर्मा हिंसीरिति शेषः । हे असुर पापकृतां निरसितः ते त्वदीय इष्टौ यज्ञ एनो विहिताननुष्ठानेन जनितं पापं कृण्वंतं कुर्वंतं पुरुषं ये वधा भ्रीणंति हिंसंति शैरिति पूर्वत्र संबंधः ॥ भ्रीष् हिंसायां क्रैयादिकः ॥ अपि च ज्योतिषो गृहे वर्तमानादग्नेः

he varuṇa no 'smān vadhairhananasādhanairāyudhairmā hiṃsīriti śeṣaḥ | he asura pāpakṛtāṃ nirasitaḥ te tvadīya iṣṭau yajña eno vihitānanuṣṭhānena janitaṃ pāpaṃ kṛṇvaṃtaṃ kurvaṃtaṃ puruṣaṃ ye vadhā bhrīṇaṃti hiṃsaṃti śairiti pūrvatra saṃbaṃdhaḥ ‖ bhrīṣ hiṃsāyāṃ kraiyādikaḥ ‖ api ca jyotiṣo gṛhe vartamānādagneḥ

p. 116

Running head: Maṃ. 2, A. 3, Sū. 28, Sāyaṇabhāṣya-sahitā, p. 116.

सौरप्रकाशाद्वा प्रवसथानि प्रवासान्मा गन्म । मा गच्छाम । सर्वदा गृहे वर्तमानः सूर्यं पश्यंश्चिरकालं जीवेयमित्यर्थः ॥ गमेर्लुजि मंत्रे घसेति चेर्लुक् ॥ तथा नोऽस्माकं जीवसे जीवनाय मृधो हिंसकान् सुष्टु विशिश्रिथः । विश्लेषय । बाधस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

Gist: "O Varuṇa, do not harm us with the weapons that slay the sinner at your sacrifice; may we not go away from the sacrificial fire; scatter the harmful, that we may live long, seeing the sun in our own home." The tail gives luk forms of gam (gan-ma) in the Veda.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Asura—you who drive out the sinful; Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Te—directed to you; Iṣṭau—in the sacrifice; Enaḥ—sin (born of omission of the rite); Kṛṇvantaṃ—the man who commits; Ye—whichever weapons, instruments of slaying; Bhrīṇanti—injure (such); Vadhaiḥ—with weapons; Naḥ—us; Mā—do not injure; Jyotiṣaḥ—from the sacrificial fire; Pravasathāni—dwelling in another place; Mā ganma—may we not reach; Naḥ—our; Jīvase—for a (happy) life; Mṛdhaḥ—the harmful enemies; Vi śiśrathaḥ—destroy.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, who drive out the sinful, do not injure us with those weapons, instruments of slaying, which injure the man who, in the sacrifice directed to you, commits sin born of omission of the rite. May we not dwell in a place without the sacrificial fire. Destroy the harmful enemies so that we may obtain a happy life.

Printed English translation

Harm us not, Varuna, with those destructive (weapons), which, repeller (of foes), demolish him who does evil at your sacrifice : let us not depart (before our time) from the regions of light : scatter the malevolent, that we may live.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

असुर—पापकृतां निरसितः (asura—pāpakṛtāṃ nirasitaḥ). The word asura is stated among the names of cloud (Si. 2-22, as printed). It is explained: "asurāḥ: from the places (sthāna), or because they are asu-givers [as supplied]; 'from asu he created the asuras, hence the asura-ness of the asuras'" (Ni. 3-8). Sāyaṇa explains that Varuṇa is addressed by this word because he destroys sinners. And वधैः एनः कृण्वंतं ये भ्रीणंति नः मा (vadhaiḥ enaḥ kṛṇvaṃtaṃ ye bhrīṇaṃti naḥ mā)—"with weapons (instruments of slaying) which injure the man who commits sin born of omission of the prescribed observance, do not injure us" (as printed, with the misprint आयुध्यैः (āyudhyaiḥ) and आस्मान् (āsmān)): protection is prayed for, that Varuṇa not harm us, the sacrificers, with the weapons that destroy those who do harm and those who neglect duty in the sacrifices performed for Varuṇa.

p. 117

ज्योतिषः प्रवसथानि मा गन्म-गृहे वर्तमानादग्नेः सौरप्रकाशाद्वा प्रवासान् मा गच्छाम। सर्वदा गृहेवर्तमानः सूर्यं पश्यन् चिरकालं जीवेयं।

jyotiṣaḥ pravasathāni mā ganma-gṛhe vartamānādagneḥ sauraprakāśādvā pravāsān mā gacchāma| sarvadā gṛhevartamānaḥ sūryaṃ paśyan cirakālaṃ jīveyaṃ|

"...always, by the fire's light, from the sacrificial hall pervaded by it, or from a region joined with the sun's light, a state of no separate dwelling arises; that is, the sacrificer, seeing the fire kindled for the sacrifices and the sun, would dwell at home for a long time: such a state is the favour of Varuṇa that is prayed for here."

मृधः—हिंसकान् (mṛdhaḥ—hiṃsakān)—"the harmful ones." The word मृधः (mṛdhaḥ) is stated among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). And in the Ṛk

वि न इंद्र मृधो जहि नीचा यच्छ पृतन्यतः । यो अस्मा अभिदासत्यधरं गमया तमः ॥

vi na iṃdra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ | yo asmā abhidāsatyadharaṃ gamayā tamaḥ ‖

(Pu [sic] Saṃ. 10-152-4), the meaning is explained as मृधः-मृधकर्त्यन् शत्रून् (mṛdhaḥ-mṛdhakartyan śatrūn) (Si. 7-2) ("enemies, doers of harm" [as printed]).

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

नमः॑ पु॒रा ते॑ वरुणो॒त नू॒नमु॒ताप॒रं तु॑विजात ब्रवाम । त्वे हि कं॒ पर्व॑ते॒ न श्रि॒तान्यप्र॑च्युतानि दूळभ व्र॒तानि॑ ॥ ८ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

नमः । पुरा । ते । वरुण । उत । नूनं । उत । अपरं । तुविजात । ब्रवाम । त्वे इति । हि । कं । पर्वते । न । श्रितानि । अप्रच्युतानि । दुःसदभ । व्रतानि ॥ ८ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण पुरा पूर्वस्मिन्काले ते शुभ्यं नमो नमस्कारप्रतिपादकं नम इति शब्दमवादिस्म । उत अपि च नूनमद्यापि ब्रवाम । उत अपि च हे तुविजात बहुषु प्रदेशेषु प्रादुर्भूत वरुणापरमागामिन्यपि काले नमःशब्दं ब्रवाम । उच्चार- याम । कस्मादिति चेदुच्यते । दूळभ दुर्दभ दंभितुं हिंसितुमशक्य ॥ दुरो दाशनाशध्यादभेषु । पा. ६. ३. १०९. ५. । इति रेफस्योत्वमुत्तरपदादेः ष्टुत्वं च ।

he varuṇa purā pūrvasminkāle te śubhyaṃ namo namaskārapratipādakaṃ nama iti śabdamavādisma | uta api ca nūnamadyāpi bravāma | uta api ca he tuvijāta bahuṣu pradeśeṣu prādurbhūta varuṇāparamāgāminyapi kāle namaḥśabdaṃ bravāma | uccāra- yāma | kasmāditi ceducyate | dūḷabha durdabha daṃbhituṃ hiṃsitumaśakya ‖ duro dāśanāśadhyādabheṣu | pā. 6. 3. 109. 5. | iti rephasyotvamuttarapadādeḥ ṣṭutvaṃ ca |

p. 118

कमित्येतत्पादपूरणं ॥ हि यस्मात् त्वे त्वयि पर्वते न शिलोच्चय इवाप्रच्युता- न्यनैः प्रच्यावयितुमशक्यानि व्रतानि कर्माणि विधरणानि श्रितानि । आश्रितानि । तस्मादित्यर्थः ॥

kamityetatpādapūraṇaṃ ‖ hi yasmāt tve tvayi parvate na śiloccaya ivāpracyutā- nyanaiḥ pracyāvayitumaśakyāni vratāni karmāṇi vidharaṇāni śritāni | āśritāni | tasmādityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: Sāyaṇa says that, since Varuṇa's undertakings (vrata) rest in him unmoved like a rock, the worshippers bow to him; the tail of the bhāṣya gives the Vedic changes of dūḷabha (reference Pā. 6-3-109-5) and the filler kam.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Dūḷabha—O unobstructed one; Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Hi—because; Te—in you; Parvate na—as seen in mountains; Apracyutāni—not movable by others; Vratāni—powers of support; Śritāni—have taken refuge (therefore); Purā—in former time; Te—directed to you; Namaḥ—worship with obeisance was offered; Uta—and; Nūnaṃ—now also; Bravāma—we recite praise with obeisance; Uta—moreover; Tuvijāta—Varuṇa, born in many regions; Aparaṃ—in future times also (we shall offer you worship of this same kind).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O unobstructed Varuṇa, because powers of support, immovable by others as in mountains, have taken refuge in you, we have offered worship with obeisance to you in former time and now also. O Varuṇa, born in many regions, in the same way we shall recite praises with obeisance in the future also. (The printed text has "ಅಪ್ರತಿಹನಾದ" for "ಅಪ್ರತಿಹತನಾದ" in the first line, as supplied.)

Printed English translation

As we have offered adoration to you, Varuua [sic], of old, in like manner as we offer it now so may we offer it in future (to you), you are everywhere present: for in you, who are difficult of attainment, as in an (immoveable) mountain, all holy acts are assembled, and are not to be dissevered.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Varuṇa is addressed by the word तुविजात (tuvijāta). Since his authority extends over many regions, he is described as born in many regions accordingly, and as दूळभ (dūḷabha)—one who cannot be harmed by anyone. त्वे—पर्वते न अप्रच्युतानि व्रतानि श्रितानि (tve—parvate na apracyutāni vratāni śritāni)—त्वयि शिलोच्चय इव अन्यैः प्रच्यावयितुमशक्यानि आश्रितानि (tvayi śiloccaya iva anyaiḥ pracyāvayitumaśakyāni āśritāni): Varuṇa's power of support cannot be destroyed by anyone, like mountains, rocks, earth and trees; so his might is described. Then, addressing Varuṇa of such abundant might, the fixed practice of the obeisance-worship and the like, offered by sacrificers in the three times, past, present and future, and being offered, is stated.

p. 119

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

पर॑ ऋ॒णा सा॑वी॒रध॒ मत्कृ॑तानि॒ माहं रा॑जन्न॒न्यकृ॑तेन भोजं । अव्यु॑ष्टा॒ इन्नु भूय॑सीरु॒षास॒ आ नो॑ जी॒वान्व॑रुण॒ तासु॑ शाधि ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

परा । ऋणा । सावीः । अध । मत्कृतानि । मा । अहं । राजन् । अन्यकृतेन । भोजं । अविउष्टाः । इत् । नु । भूयसीः । उषसः । आ । नः । जीवान् । वरुण । तासु । शाधि ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण ऋणा ऋणानि पित्रादिभिः कृतान्यस्माभिर्देयानि परा सावीः । परा सुव । पराचीनं प्रेरय ॥ षू प्रेरणे । छांदसो लुज् ॥ अध आधुना मत्कृतानि मया निष्पादितानि ऋणानि परा सुव । अपि च हे राजन् स्वामिन् वरुण आहमन्य- कृतेनान्यैरर्जितेन धनेन मा भोजं । भोगं मा लभेयं । किं कारणमिति चेदुच्यते । भूयसीर्भूयस्यो बहुतरा उषसोऽव्युष्टा इन्नु॥ सत्यमव्युष्टा एव । अपररात्रेषूत्थाय ऋणानि चिंतयतो जाग्रतो मम व्युष्टा अप्यव्युष्टकल्पा आसन् । हे वरुण तासूषिसु नोऽस्मान् जीवान् जीवनवत आशाधि । आ समंताद- नुशिष्टान् कुरु । ऋणान्यपकृत्य भोगपर्याप्तं धनं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥

he varuṇa ṛṇā ṛṇāni pitrādibhiḥ kṛtānyasmābhirdeyāni parā sāvīḥ | parā suva | parācīnaṃ preraya ‖ ṣū preraṇe | chāṃdaso luj ‖ adha ādhunā matkṛtāni mayā niṣpāditāni ṛṇāni parā suva | api ca he rājan svāmin varuṇa āhamanya- kṛtenānyairarjitena dhanena mā bhojaṃ | bhogaṃ mā labheyaṃ | kiṃ kāraṇamiti ceducyate | bhūyasīrbhūyasyo bahutarā uṣaso 'vyuṣṭā innu‖ satyamavyuṣṭā eva | apararātreṣūtthāya ṛṇāni ciṃtayato jāgrato mama vyuṣṭā apyavyuṣṭakalpā āsan | he varuṇa tāsūṣisu no 'smān jīvān jīvanavata āśādhi | ā samaṃtāda- nuśiṣṭān kuru | ṛṇānyapakṛtya bhogaparyāptaṃ dhanaṃ prayacchetyarthaḥ ‖

Gist: Sāyaṇa takes the prayer to be that Varuṇa discharge the debts incurred by forefathers and by the speaker, so that he enjoy no wealth earned by others, and be given means of livelihood in the many dawns that have passed in sleeplessness over debts; the tail gives the root sū (to urge) with the Vedic luṅ form.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Ṛṇā—the debts incurred by our forefathers; Parā sāvīḥ—discharge; Adha—now; Matkṛtāni—discharge also the debts incurred by me; Rājan—O Varuṇa, the lord; Ahaṃ—I; Anyakṛtena—with wealth earned by others; Mā bhojaṃ—do not make me enjoy; Bhūyasīḥ—many times; Uṣasaḥ—the shining dawns; Avyuṣṭā innu—(because of the burden of debt) have become as if unrisen, like darkness; Tāsu—in such dawn-times; Naḥ—us; Jīvān—that we may have a peaceful life; Ā śādhi—make us free of debt.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, discharge the debts incurred by our forefathers and the debts now incurred by me. O Varuṇa, the lord, do not let me enjoy pleasure with wealth earned by others [the supplied text of the Bhāvārtha ends here, in mid-sentence, at the end of this window].

p. 120

(Continuation of the Bhāvārtha of Ṛk 9 from p. 119:) ... do not do so. Because I am under the pressure of debt, many shining dawns have, as it were, not dawned, and have become like darkness. In such dawn-times make us free of debt, so that we may have a peaceful life.

Printed English translation

Discharge, Varuna, the debts (contracted) by my progenitors, and those now (contracted) by me; and may I not royal Varuna be dependent (on the debts contacted [sic]) by another: many are the mornings that have as it were, indeed not dawned : make us, Varuna, alive in them.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the word ऋण (ṛṇa) (debt) and the verb परासावीः (parāsāvīḥ) are used only once. But since the words अध मत्कृतानि (adha matkṛtāni) are also used, Sāyaṇa repeats the object-word and the verb in explaining the sense: the debts incurred by the sacrificer's forefathers and the debts incurred by the sacrificer himself, both kinds, have to be paid by the sacrificer; hence the prayer is stated that Varuṇa grant that both kinds of debt be discharged.

On भूयसीः उषसः अव्युष्टा इन्नु (bhūyasīḥ uṣasaḥ avyuṣṭā innu): the word इत् (it) is given the sense of combination (samuccaya), and नु (nu) the sense of comparison. Sāyaṇa's words: भूयस्यः उषसः अपररात्रेषूत्ताय ऋणानि चिंतयतो जाग्रतो मम व्युष्टाअपि अव्युष्टकल्पाः आर्स (bhūyasyaḥ uṣasaḥ apararātreṣūttāya ṛṇāni ciṃtayato jāgrato mama vyuṣṭāapi avyuṣṭakalpāḥ ārsa) (as supplied; the last word, आर्स (ārsa), is doubtful [?]). That is: even when one is awake in the last watch of the night, thinking how to repay the debts, the dawns that have arrived and have passed one after another remain, as it were, as if they had not passed; thus the sacrificer's anxiety is shown to be abundant. And तासु नः जीवान् आशाधि (tāsu naḥ jīvān āśādhi): addressing Varuṇa, the prayer is made that, for the sacrificer who thinks much in those dawn-times, the debts be discharged (ऋणान्यपकृत्य (ṛṇānyapakṛtya)) and wealth sufficient for enjoyment be given (भोगपर्याप्तं धनं प्रयच्छ (bhogaparyāptaṃ dhanaṃ prayaccha)).

p. 121

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यो मे॑ राज॒न्यज्यो॑ वा॒ सखा॑ वा॒ स्वप्ने॑ भ॒यं भी॒रवे॒ मह्य॒-॑ माह । स्ते॒नो वा॒ यो दिप्स॑ति नो॒ वृको॑ वा॒ त्वं तस्मा॑द्वरुण पाह्य॒स्मान् ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । मे । राजन् । युज्यः । वा । सखा । वा । स्वप्ने । भयं । भीरवे । मह्यं । आह । स्तेनः । वा । यः । दिप्सति । नः । वृकः । वा । त्वं । तस्मात् । वरुण । पाहि । आस्मान्॥१०॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे राजन् वरुण मे मदीयो युज्यो योजनसमर्थः पित्रादिर्वा सखा समानख्यानोऽन्यो बांधवो वा स्वप्ने दृष्टं त्वद्विषयं भयं भीरवे भयशी- लाय मह्यं य आह ब्रूते । तथा स्तेनश्चौरो वा वृकोऽरण्यश्वा वा यो नोऽस्मान् दिप्सति । जिघांसति ॥ सनीवंतर्धोति विकल्पनादिडभावः । दंभ इच्छेतीत्वं ॥ हे वरुण त्वं तस्मात्सर्वस्मादस्मान्पाहि । रक्ष ॥

he rājan varuṇa me madīyo yujyo yojanasamarthaḥ pitrādirvā sakhā samānakhyāno 'nyo bāṃdhavo vā svapne dṛṣṭaṃ tvadviṣayaṃ bhayaṃ bhīrave bhayaśī- lāya mahyaṃ ya āha brūte | tathā stenaścauro vā vṛko 'raṇyaśvā vā yo no 'smān dipsati | jighāṃsati ‖ sanīvaṃtardhoti vikalpanādiḍabhāvaḥ | daṃbha icchetītvaṃ ‖ he varuṇa tvaṃ tasmātsarvasmādasmānpāhi | rakṣa ‖

Gist: Sāyaṇa takes the Ṛk to ask Varuṇa to protect from the fear that a relative or friend reports from a dream concerning him, and from a thief or wolf that wishes to harm; the tail explains the verb दिप्सति (dipsati) (from dambh, desiderative) with optional absence of the augment.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Rājan—O lord; Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Me—my; Yaḥ yujyaḥ—whichever father or other kinsman; Vā—or; Sakhā vā—whichever other relative; Svapne—in a dream (seen with reference to you); Bhayaṃ—the fear; Bhīrave—to the timid; Mahyaṃ—to me; Āha—explains and tells, from that too; Yaḥ stenaḥ vā—whichever thief; Vā—or; Vṛkaḥ—wolf; Naḥ—us; Dipsati [the supplied text has दिप्पति (dippati), as supplied]—harms; Tasmāt—from all that fear and that harm; Tvaṃ—you; Asmān—us; Pāhi—protect.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O lord Varuṇa, from whatever fear, seen in a dream with reference to you, that any father or other kinsman of mine, or any other relative, explains and tells to me, who am timid, or from whatever thief or wolf harms us, from all that fear and harm protect us completely.

Printed English translation

Protect us, Varuna, against every peril which a kinsman or a friend threatens me with alarmed in sleep; or from a thief or a wolf that attempts to destroy us.

p. 122

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the sacrificer prays for protection from Varuṇa, with removal of fear; the causes of fear are also stated. First, युज्यः—योजनसमर्थः पित्रादिः (yujyaḥ—yojanasamarthaḥ pitrādiḥ), a father or the like able to support; and सखा—समानख्यानः अन्योवा बांधवः (sakhā—samānakhyānaḥ anyovā bāṃdhavaḥ), a friend of like understanding with oneself, or a kinsman, indicates to the sacrificer a fear concerning the deity worshipped by the sacrificer; hence protection from this deity is sought.

Second, स्तेनः—चोरः, वृकः—अरण्यश्वा (stenaḥ—coraḥ, vṛkaḥ—araṇyaśvā): from creatures that cause harm, the thief and the wicked beasts that kill and eat in the forest (wolves), Varuṇa is prayed to protect.

Although the word स्तेन (stena) is not read by Yāska among the names of thieves, it is explained as स्तेनः कस्मात् संस्थानमस्मिन् पापकमिति नैरुक्ताः (stenaḥ kasmāt saṃsthānamasmin pāpakamiti nairuktāḥ) (Ni. 3-19) [the supplied text has पापकमिति (pāpakamiti), as supplied].

वृकः—अरण्यश्वा (vṛkaḥ—araṇyaśvā). The word वृक (vṛka) is read among the names of the thunderbolt (Ni. 3-11) and among the names of thieves (Ni. 3-19). It is also explained: वृकश्चंद्रमा भवति । विवृत ज्योतिष्को वा विकृतज्योतिष्टो वा, विक्रांतजोतिष्को वा (vṛkaścaṃdramā bhavati | vivṛta jyotiṣko vā vikṛtajyotiṣṭo vā, vikrāṃtajotiṣko vā) (Ni. 5-21); and वृको लांगलं भवति विकर्तनात् (vṛko lāṃgalaṃ bhavati vikartanāt) (Ni 6-26) — thus the meaning of the word वृक (vṛka) is explained. Sāyaṇa has explained the word as "wild dog (wolf)".

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

माहं म॒घोनो॑ वरुण प्रि॒यस्य॑ भूरि॒दान्न॒ आ वि॑दं॒ शून॑मा॒पेः । मा रा॒यो रा॑जन्सु॒ यमा॒दव॑ स्थां बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥

māhaṃ maghono varuṇa priyasya bhūridānna ā vidaṃ śūnamāpeḥ | mā rāyo rājansu yamādava sthāṃ bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ ‖

p. 123

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 8, p. 123.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मा । अहं । मघोनः । वरुण । प्रियस्य । भूर्इदान्वः । आ । विदं । शूनं । आपेः । मा । रायः । राजन् । सुयमात् । अव । स्थां । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सु- वीराः ॥ १७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे वरुण मघोनो धनवतः प्रियस्यानुकूलस्य भूरिदाव्यो भूरेर्बहुलस्य दातुराड्यस्याहं मा आविदं । मावेदयानि । आवेदनं विज्ञापनं मा करवाणि । किं तदनावेद्यं । आपेर्ज्ञातेः शूनं शून्यं दारिद्रं ॥ वर्णलोपश्रांदसः ॥ यद्वा शूनं गतं प्राप्तं दारिद्रं ॥ टुओश्वि गतिवृद्ध्योः । श्वीदितो निष्ठायामितीट् प्रति- षेधः । यजादित्वात्संप्रसारणं । ओदितश्चति नकारः । वृषादित्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ एतदुक्तं भवति । अस्मदीयाः पुत्रादयः क्षुधिता इति प्रभुप्रभुसमीपेभिधाय याचमानो मा भूवमिति । हे राजन् सुयमात् । सुष्टु नियम्यतेनेन पुरुषो गृह इति सुयमः ॥ ईषद्दुःसुष्टिति खलु ॥ तादृशाद्रायो धनान्मावस्थां । अवयुत्य स्थितो मा भूवं । वयं सुनीराः शोभनपुत्रा विदथे यज्ञे गृहे वर्तमानाः संतो बृहत् फौढं स्तोत्रं वदेम । उच्चारयाम ॥

he varuṇa maghono dhanavataḥ priyasyānukūlasya bhūridāvyo bhūrerbahulasya dāturāḍyasyāhaṃ mā āvidaṃ | māvedayāni | āvedanaṃ vijñāpanaṃ mā karavāṇi | kiṃ tadanāvedyaṃ | āperjñāteḥ śūnaṃ śūnyaṃ dāridraṃ ‖ varṇalopaśrāṃdasaḥ ‖ yadvā śūnaṃ gataṃ prāptaṃ dāridraṃ ‖ ṭuośvi gativṛddhyoḥ | śvīdito niṣṭhāyāmitīṭ prati- ṣedhaḥ | yajāditvātsaṃprasāraṇaṃ | oditaścati nakāraḥ | vṛṣāditvādādyudāttatvaṃ ‖ etaduktaṃ bhavati | asmadīyāḥ putrādayaḥ kṣudhitā iti prabhuprabhusamīpebhidhāya yācamāno mā bhūvamiti | he rājan suyamāt | suṣṭu niyamyatenena puruṣo gṛha iti suyamaḥ ‖ īṣadduḥsuṣṭiti khalu ‖ tādṛśādrāyo dhanānmāvasthāṃ | avayutya sthito mā bhūvaṃ | vayaṃ sunīrāḥ śobhanaputrā vidathe yajñe gṛhe vartamānāḥ saṃto bṛhat phauḍhaṃ stotraṃ vadema | uccārayāma ‖

Gist: Sāyaṇa takes the Ṛk as a prayer that the sacrificer may never have to go to a rich, kind and generous patron and plead his kinsman's poverty, nor be emptied of well-regulated wealth; the grammatical tail explains शूनम् (śūnam) from śvi (to go, to grow), with elision of a letter, and सुयमात् (suyamāt).

(Readings as supplied: the Pada reads भूर्इदान्वः for the Saṃhitā's भूरिदान्नः; the bhāṣya and Pratipadārtha have भूरिदाव्यः; the bhāṣya has सुनीराः where the Saṃhitā and Pada have सुवीराः; the bhāṣya tail has an odd sequence "ಟುಓಶ್ವಿ". All left as supplied.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Varuṇa—O Varuṇa; Maghonaḥ—of the wealthy; Priyasya—of the favourable one; Bhūridāvyaḥ—of him who gives abundantly, that is, of the rich man, in front of him; Ahaṃ—I; Āpeḥ—of my near kinsman; Śūnaṃ—the poverty; Mā ā vidaṃ—may I not (have to) tell it; Rājan—O lord Varuṇa; Suyamāt—from what is gathered under restraint (regulation); Rāyaḥ—from wealth; Mā ava sthāṃ—may I not become empty; (Vayaṃ—we); Suvīrāḥ—together with excellent sons; Vidathe—in the sacrificial house; Bṛhat—a mature hymn of praise; Vadema—we recite.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Varuṇa, may I never, before a rich, favourable and abundantly generous man, say that my sons and other near kinsmen are suffering in poverty, and so ask him for wealth. May I never be emptied of the wealth gathered under restraint. Together with excellent sons we shall recite a mature hymn of praise in the sacrificial house.

p. 124

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 3 [as printed; elsewhere 2], Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 28, p. 124.

Printed English translation

May I never (have to) represent, Varuna, the destitution of a (once) opulent, dear, and munificent kinsman : may I never, royal Varuna, be devoid of well-regulated riches : (and) may we, blessed with excellent descendants, worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

By the word वरुण (varuṇa) the Āditya is here addressed; it has been explained earlier that Varuṇa is one of the twelve Ādityas.

मघोनः—धनवतः (maghonaḥ—dhanavataḥ). The word मघ (magha) is read among the names of wealth by Yāska (Ni. 3-9); the meaning "possessed of wealth" is explained.

प्रियस्य भूरिदान्वः आपेः शुनं मा आ विदं (priyasya bhūridānvaḥ āpeḥ śunaṃ mā ā vidaṃ) [the supplied text has शुनं (śunaṃ) here, against शूनं (śūnaṃ) in the bhāṣya] — बहुलस्य दातुराड्यस्य समीपे अस्मदीयाः पुत्रादयः क्षुधिता इति दारिद्रमभिदाय याचमानो मा भूवं (bahulasya dāturāḍyasya samīpe asmadīyāḥ putrādayaḥ kṣudhitā iti dāridramabhidāya yācamāno mā bhūvaṃ): the prayer is explained thus: may we, the sacrificers, not have to go near a wealthy man who is kind and gives abundantly, state that our sons and the rest are in poverty, and beg wealth.

शूनं—शून्यं, यद्वा शूनं गतं प्राप्तं दारिद्रं (śūnaṃ—śūnyaṃ, yadvā śūnaṃ gataṃ prāptaṃ dāridraṃ): for the word शून (śūna) the meaning is explained as the state of having no kind of thing at all, or poverty (ownership) fit to bring about a state of emptiness.

राजन् सुयमात् रायः मा अवस्थाम्—सुष्टु नियम्यते अनेन पुरुषो गृहे इति सुयमः (rājan suyamāt rāyaḥ mā avasthām—suṣṭu niyamyate anena puruṣo gṛhe iti suyamaḥ): Varuṇa is addressed by the word राजन् (rājan), and it is prayed that by his favour the wealth gathered by us, the sacrificers, may never perish.

बृहद्वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (bṛhadvadema vidathe suvīrāḥ): it is prayed that we, the sacrificers, reciting hymns in the sacrifices together with our excellent sons, may be granted favour.

p. 125

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 11, p. 125.

Sūkta 29 (Maṇḍala 2)

The twenty-ninth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

धृतव्रता इति सप्तर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं गार्त्समदस्य कूर्मस्य गृत्समदस्य वार्षं त्रैष्टुभं वैश्वदेवं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । धृतव्रताः सप्त वैश्वदेवमिति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

Gist: dhṛtavratāḥ is the seventh sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of seven ṛks, by Kūrma Gārtsamada or Gṛtsamada, in triṣṭubh metre, to the Viśvedevas; the Anukramaṇī is quoted; the application is stated as already given.

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta dhṛtavratāḥ is the seventh sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has seven ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kūrma, son of Gṛtsamada, or Gṛtsamada himself; the deity is the Viśvedevas; the metre is triṣṭubh. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said धृतव्रताः सप्त वैश्वदेवं (dhṛtavratāḥ sapta vaiśvadevaṃ) (the seven dhṛtavratāḥ are for the Viśvedevas). The application is laiṅgika.

Sūkta—29

Maṇḍala 2 ‖ Anuvāka 3 ‖ Sūkta 29 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 7 ‖ Varga 11 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 7 · Ṛṣi: as supplied "ಕರ್ಮೋ ಗಾರ್ತಮದೋ ಗೃತ್ಸಮದೋ ವಾ" (Kūrma Gārtsamada, or Gṛtsamada; the first word and the second are garbled as supplied, left as they are) · Devatā: the Viśvedevas · Chandas: triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

धृत॑व्रता॒ आदि॑त्या॒ इषि॑रा आ॒रे मत्क॑र्त रह॒सूरि॒वागः॑ । शृ॒ण्व॒तो वो॒ वरु॑ण॒ मित्र॒ देवा॑ भ॒द्रस्य॑ वि॒द्वा अव॑से हुवे वः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

धृतव्रताः । आदित्याः । इषिराः । आरे । मत् । कर्त । रहसूः इव । आगः । शृण्वतः । वः । वरुण । मित्र । देवाः । भद्रस्य । विद्वान् । आवसे । हुवे । वः ॥ १ ॥

dhṛtavratāḥ | ādityāḥ | iṣirāḥ | āre | mat | karta | rahasūḥ iva | āgaḥ | śṛṇvataḥ | vaḥ | varuṇa | mitra | devāḥ | bhadrasya | vidvān | āvase | huve | vaḥ ‖ 1 ‖

p. 126

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 29, p. 126.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे धृतव्रता धृतकर्माण आदित्या आदितेः पुत्रा इषीरा गमनशीलाः सर्वैरभ्ये- षणीयाः प्रार्थनीया वा हे विश्वे देवा मदारे मत्तो दूरदेश आगो विहिता- ननुष्ठानादिजनितं पापं कर्त । कुरुत ॥ करोतेश्चांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । तप्तन- स्तनथनाश्लेति तबादेशः ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । रहसूरिव । रहस्यनैरज्ञाते प्रदेशे सूयत इति रहसूर्यभिचारिणी । सा यथा गर्भं पातयित्वा दूरदेशे परित्यजति तद्वत् । हे वरुण मित्र देवाश्च वो युष्मदीयस्य भद्रस्य युष्माभिः करणीयं श्रेयो विद्वान् जानन्नहं शृण्वतो मत्कृतानि स्तोत्राणि श्रोत्रेण जानतो वो युष्मान् अवसे रक्षणार्थं हुवे । आह्वयामि ॥

Gist: O Ādityas, sons of Aditi, upholders of rites, seekers of favour: cast my sin of faulty performance far away, as a secretly delivering woman casts away her child; knowing the good you bestow, I call you for protection.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

dhṛtavratāḥ—those who hold to their rites; iṣirāḥ—desired by all; ādityāḥ—O Ādityas; rahasūḥ iva—like a woman who has given birth in secret and throws the child far away so that no one sees it; āgaḥ—my sin, consisting of lapse in performance; mat—from me; āre—in a place very far away; karta—cast away and make it unseen; varuṇa—O Varuṇa; mitra—O Mitra; devāḥ—O Viśvedevas; vaḥ—to be obtained from you; bhadrasya—of the auspicious nature; vidvān—I who know; śṛṇvataḥ—you who hear my praise; vaḥ—you; avase—for protection; huve—I call.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Ādityas, who hold to your rites and are prayed to by all: as a woman who has given birth in secret throws the child far away where no one sees it, so throw my sin of lapse in performance far from me, out of sight. O Varuṇa, Mitra and Viśvedevas, I who know the auspicious good that comes from you call you, who hear my praise, for protection.

English translation (as printed)

Adityas, upholders of pious works, and who are to be sought by all, remove sin far from me, like, a woman delivered in secret: knowing, Mitra, Varuna, and (universal) gods, the good that follows from your hearing our prayers, I invoke you for (our) protection.

p. 127

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 11, p. 127.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

इषिराः—गमनशीलाः सर्वैरभ्येषणीयाः प्रार्थनीया वा (iṣirāḥ—gamanaśīlāḥ sarvairabhyeṣaṇīyāḥ prārthanīyā vā): Sāyaṇa explains the word as "of a moving nature; to be sought, or prayed to, by all", applying it as an epithet of the Ādityas: those of a roving nature, desired by all, worthy of being prayed to by all that their wishes be fulfilled. Yāska explains the word (Nirukta 4-7) as इषिरेण—ईषणेन ना एषणेन ना ऋषणेन ना (iṣireṇa—īṣaṇena nā eṣaṇena nā ṛṣaṇena nā). The Viśvedevas, sons of Aditi, are always of a moving nature; they are desired by all for the fulfilment of their tasks and wishes, and prayed to by all. Therefore may these Ādityas keep far away, that is, forgive or destroy, the offence in the form of a deficiency arising from variation in the performance of sacrifices and other rites by the sacrificer. Thus the Viśvedevas are addressed and taken to be sons of the goddess Aditi. The plural आदित्याः (ādityāḥ) is used in this ṛk; Sāyaṇa explains it as हे आदित्याः अदितिपुत्राः हे विश्वे देवाः (he ādityāḥ aditiputrāḥ he viśve devāḥ). Yāska explains विश्वे देवाः—सर्वॆ देवाः (viśve devāḥ—sarvè devāḥ) (Nirukta 12-40).

रहसूः इव—रहसि अन्यैरज्ञाते प्रदेशे सूयत इति रहसूः व्यभिचारिणी । सा यथा गर्भं पातयित्वा दूरदेशे परित्यजति तद्वत् (rahasūḥ iva—rahasi anyairajñāte pradeśe sūyata iti rahasūḥ vyabhicāriṇī | sā yathā garbhaṃ pātayitvā dūradeśe parityajati tadvat): since she gives birth in a place unknown to others and without human traffic, the unchaste woman is here designated by the word रहसूः (rahasūḥ).

As this woman throws far away the child she has borne, so may the offences of the sacrificer, the deficiencies consisting of non-performance of rites, be removed by the favour of these Ādityas or Viśvedevas; thus the prayer.

Addressing the sons of Aditi as Mitra, Varuṇa and Devāḥ, the poet says भद्रस्य विद्वान्—युष्माभिः करणीयं श्रेयः जानन् (bhadrasya vidvān—yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyaṃ śreyaḥ jānan): that he knows the greatness of the good which these gods bestow on the sacrificer; and शृण्वतः (śṛṇvataḥ): because these gods hear the hymns recited by the sacrificer, he will call them for his protection.

भद्रस्य (bhadrasya): in explaining this word Yāska says भद्रं भगेन व्याख्यातं (bhadraṃ bhagena vyākhyātaṃ) and then भजनीयं, भूतानां अभिद्रवणीयं, भवद्रमयतीति वा, भाजनवद्वा (bhajanīyaṃ, bhūtānāṃ abhidravaṇīyaṃ, bhavadramayatīti vā, bhājanavadvā) (Nirukta 4-9). Its meaning has been explained before.

p. 128

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 29, p. 128.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यू॒यं दे॑वाः॒ प्रम॑तियूर्यू॒यमोजो॑ यू॒यं द्वेषां॑सि॒॑ सनु॒तर्यु॑योत । अ॒भि॒क्ष॒त्तारो॑ अ॒भि च॒ क्षम॑ध्वम॒द्या च॑ नो मृ॒ळय॑ताप॒रं च॑ ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यूयं । देवाः । प्रमतिः । यूयं । ओजः । यूयं । द्वेषांसि । सनुतः । युयोत । अभिक्षत्तारः । अभि । च । क्षमध्वं । आद्य । च । नः । मृळयत । अपरं । च ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे देवाः प्रमतिः प्रकृष्टा मतिर्यस्य प्रित्रादेस्तादृशा अपि यूयमेव । तथौजो बलमपि यूयमेव । आपि च यूयं द्वेषांसि द्वेष्ट्यणि रक्षःपिशाचा- दीनि । सनुतरित्यव्ययं । अंतर्हितनामैतत् । अंतर्हिते प्रदेशे युयोत । पृथक्कुरुत ॥ यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । छांदसः शपः श्लुः । पूर्ववत्तस्य तबादेशः ॥ अभिक्षत्तारोऽभितः शत्रूणां हिंसितारो यूयमभि च क्षमध्वं । अभिभवत शत्रून् । अद्यास्मिन्निने नोऽस्मान्मृळयत । सुखयत । अपरं च अपरमपि कालं । आगामिन्यपि कालेऽस्मान् मृळयत ॥

Gist: O gods, you are wisdom and strength; drive our enemies, the demons and the like, to a hidden place; overcome our foes, and make us happy today and hereafter.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

devāḥ—O gods; pramatiḥ—excellent understanding; yūyam—you yourselves are; ojaḥ—strength; yūyam—you also; yūyam—you; dveṣāṃsi—the demons and others who hate us; sanutaḥ—to a hidden, distant place; yuyota—drive away; abhikṣattāraḥ—you who strike enemies on every side; abhi ca kṣamadhvam—defeat them completely; adya ca—today also; naḥ—us; mṛḷayata—make happy; aparaṃ ca—on another day also (make us happy).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, you yourselves are excellent understanding and strength. Drive the demons and others who hate us to a hidden, distant place. You who strike enemies on every side, defeat them completely. Make us happy today, and in the same way hereafter.

p. 129

Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 11, p. 129.

English Translation

You, gods, are intelligence, you are vigour: drive away the malevolent subduers (of enemies), overcome them entirely, and grant us felicity both now and in future.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

देवाः (devāḥ): Yāska explains the word deva as देवो दानाद्वा, दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा, द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा (devo dānādvā, dīpanādvā dyotanādvā, dyusthāno bhavatīti vā) (Nirukta 6-15; the text as supplied reads "ಸಿ." for "ನಿ.").

ओजः (ojaḥ): This word is read by Yāska among the names of water (Nirukta 2-24) and the names of strength (Nirukta 3-9), and explained as ओज ओजतेर्वा उज्जतेर्वा (oja ojatervā ujjatervā) (Nirukta 6-8). Sāyaṇa takes the meaning here to be "strength".

The gods are addressed. In regard to the sacrificer these gods are प्रमतिः—प्रकृष्टा मतिर्यस्य पित्रादेः (pramatiḥ—prakṛṣṭā matiryasya pitrādeḥ): protectors such as a father possessed of excellent understanding; and they are strength itself, able to carry out for the sacrificer the whole business of this world. The verse says that these gods should keep far away the demons, pisācas and the like who harm the sacrificer.

These gods are अभिक्षत्तारः—अभितः शत्रून् हिंसितारः (abhikṣattāraḥ—abhitaḥ śatrūn hiṃsitāraḥ), destroyers of enemies on every side; therefore, having destroyed the sacrificer's enemies, may they protect or make us happy अद्य अपरं च कालं मृळयत (adya aparaṃ ca kālaṃ mṛḷayata), both now and in the time to come. Thus the prayer is made.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

किमू॒ नु वः॑ कृणवा॒माप॑रेण॒ किं सने॑न वसव॒ आप्ये॑न । यू॒यं नो॑ मित्रावरुणादिते च स्व॒स्तिमिं॑द्रामरुतो दधात ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

किं । ऊं इति । नु । वः । कृणवाम । अपरेण । किं । सनेन । वसवः । अप्येन । यूयं । नः । मित्रावरुणा । अदिते । च । स्वस्तिं । इंद्रामरुतः । दधात ॥ ३ ॥

kiṃ | ūṃ iti | nu | vaḥ | kṛṇavāma | apareṇa | kiṃ | sanena | vasavaḥ | apyena | yūyaṃ | naḥ | mitrāvaruṇā | adite | ca | svastiṃ | iṃdrāmarutaḥ | dadhāta ‖ 3 ‖

p. 130

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 29, p. 130.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे देवा वो युष्माकं नु अद्येदानीं किमु कृणवाम । किं खलु कर्तु० शक्नवाम । न किमपीत्यर्थः । तथापरेणापरकालभाविना कर्मणा किं कर्तु० शक्ताः । तथा हे वसवो वासयितारो देवाः सनेन सनातनेनाप्येनाप्तव्येन कर्मणा युष्माकं किं कर्तु० शक्ताः । सर्वदापि युष्मदनुगुणं परिचरणं कर्तु० न शक्ता इत्यर्थः । हे मित्रावरुणौ हे अदिते हे इंद्रामरुतः ॥ देवताद्वंद्वे चेति पूर्वपदस्यानज् ॥ ते च सर्वॆ यूयं स्वस्तिमविनाशं नोऽस्मभ्यं दधात । धत्त । प्रयच्छत ॥ लोटि तस्य तबादेशे, जित्वा भावेनातोलोपाभावः ॥

Gist: What can we do for you, gods, now or later, or with an ancient, attainable rite? We cannot serve you adequately; grant us imperishable well-being. The grammatical tail (a rule on the dvandva of deity names, and the ending of the imperative) is not explained here.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

devāḥ—O gods; vaḥ—to you; nu—now; kimu kṛṇavāma—what can we do?
