Addressing the gods, the sacrificers pray that their chariots, travelling for food, may be swift and may go facing the people and the various regions.

Further, आशवः पद्याभिः रजः तित्रतः (āśavaḥ padyābhiḥ rajaḥ titrataḥ)—व्यापनशीलाः अश्वाः पादसाध्याभिर्ग- शिभिः रंजकं मार्गं तरंतः (vyāpanaśīlāḥ aśvāḥ pādasādhyābhirga- śibhiḥ raṃjakaṃ mārgaṃ taraṃtaḥ): swift horses cross the road, making dust rise with their paces; and पृथिव्याः सानौ पाणिभिः जंघनंत (pṛthivyāḥ sānau pāṇibhiḥ jaṃghanaṃta)—

(The Special Topics continue on p. 165.)

p. 165

भूमेः उच्छ्रिते प्रदेशे पाण्युपलक्षितैः पादैः अत्यर्थं गच्छति (bhūmeḥ ucchrite pradeśe pāṇyupalakṣitaiḥ pādaiḥ atyarthaṃ gacchati)—the horses go exceedingly on the elevated regions of the earth with their feet, which are like hands (so the passage is explained).

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उ॒त स्य न॒ इंद्रो॑ वि॒श्वच॑र्षणिर्दि॒वः शर्धे॑न॒ मारु॑तेन सु॒क्रतुः॑ । अनु॒ नु स्था॑त्यवृ॒काभि॑रू॒तिभी॒ रथं॑ म॒हे स॒नये॒ वाज॑सातये ॥ ३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत । स्यः । नः । इंद्रः । विश्वचर्षणिः । दिवः । शर्धेन । मारुतेन । सुक्रतुः । अनु । नु । स्थाति । अवृकाभिः । ऊतिभिः । रथं । महे । सनये । वाजसातये ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उत अपि च विश्वचर्षणिर्विश्वस्य सर्वस्य द्रष्टा यद्वा विश्वे चर्षणयो मनुष्या यस्य परिचारकाः । अथवा विश्वे सर्वॆ लोकाश्चर्षणयो द्रष्टव्या येन ॥ बहुप्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदांतोदात्तत्वं ॥ मारुतेन मरुत्समूह- रूपेण शर्धेन बलेन सह सुक्रतुः शोभनकर्मा शोभनप्रज्ञो वा स्य स इंद्रोऽवृकाभिर्हिंसकरहिताभिरूतिभी रक्षाभिः सहितः सन् दिवो द्युलोकादागत्य नु अद्य नोऽस्माकं रथमनुस्थाति । अनुगुण्येनाधितिष्ठतु ॥ छांदसः शपो लुक् ॥ किमर्थं । महे सनये महते धनाय । तथा वाजसातये वाजस्यान्नस्य सातये संभजनार्थं ॥

Gist: Indra, all-seeing and accompanied by the Maruts' might, is asked to come from heaven and mount our chariot for great wealth and food; the grammatical remarks concern accent and the dropped śap.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Uta—and; viśvacarṣaṇiḥ—able to see everything; mārutena—of the Maruts' collective; śardhena—with the might; sukratuḥ—doer of excellent deeds; syaḥ indraḥ—that well-known Indra; avṛkābhiḥ—harmless; ūtibhiḥ—with protections; divaḥ—coming from the heavenly world; nu—now; mahe sanaye—for the sake of great wealth; vājasātaye—for the gain of food and wealth (set out); naḥ—our; rathaṃ—chariot; anu sthāti—let him mount and sit.

p. 166

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Indra, all-knowing and all-powerful, famous, doing excellent deeds together with the might that takes the form of the host of the Maruts, come from heaven together with harmless protections, mount and sit in our chariot, which has set out for great gain of wealth and of food, and be our protector.

Printed English translation

Or, may that all-beholding Indra, the accomplisher of great deeds, qy [sic] the collective vigour of the Maruts, (coming) from heaven, protect our chariot with unassailable protection, (for the sake of securing to us) ample wealth and abundant food.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

विश्वचर्षणिः (viśvacarṣaṇiḥ) (viśvacarṣaṇiḥ)—the beholder of everything; or he whose attendants are all men; or he by whom all the worlds are to be looked upon. Yāska has read the word carṣaṇi (Ni. 3-13) among the verbs of seeing (paśyati). Sāyaṇa has explained the word in three ways: Indra is the one who sees everything; the one who has all men as attendants; the one who necessarily looks upon all the worlds. Having explained the meaning thus, the bhāṣya says that Indra, of such abundant greatness, is मारुतेन शर्धॆन सुक्रतुः (mārutena śardhèna sukratuḥ) as printed, that is, endowed with the strength in the form of the host of the Maruts and with excellent action or wisdom. Being so endowed, he comes from heaven; नः रथं अनुस्थाति-अस्माकं रथं अनुगुण्येन अधितिष्ठतु (naḥ rathaṃ anusthāti-asmākaṃ rathaṃ anuguṇyena adhitiṣṭhatu)—let him mount our chariot, ours who are the sacrificers, in such a way that there are no harmful fears; and महे सनाय (mahe sanāya) [sic, as printed; the Saṃhitā has sanaye]. For वाज (vāja) vāja-sātaye: that we may obtain abundant wealth and food, let him mount, sit in a manner suited to us, and protect. Thus the bhāṣya expresses the wish.

The word carṣaṇi is stated by Yāska among the names of men (Ni. 3-7), and is explained by Durgācārya (Ni. 5-25) as: चर्षणिः चायिता, (carṣaṇiḥ cāyitā,) established in the form of the presiding deity of the intellect, the beholder of all beings.

p. 167

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उ॒त स्य दे॒वो भुव॑नस्य स॒क्षणि॒स्त्वष्टा॒ ग्नाभिः॑ स॒जोषा॑ जूजुव॒द्रथं॑ । इळा॒ भगो॑ बृहद्दि॒वोत रोद॑सी पू॒षा पुरं॑धिर॒श्विना॒वधा॒ पती॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत । स्यः । देवः । भुवनस्य । सक्षणिः । त्वष्टा । ग्नाभिः । सजोषाः । जूजुवत् । रथं । इळा । भगः । बृहत्ऽदिवा । उत । रोदसी इति । पूषा । पुरंधिः । अश्विनौ । अध । पती इति ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उत अपि च स्यस देवो दानादिगुणयुक्तो भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य सक्षणिः सचनीयः सेव्यो ग्नाभिर्देवपत्नीभिः । छंदांसि वै ग्ना इति तैत्तिरीयकं । गाय- त्रादीनि छंदांसि च देवपत्न इत्युक्तं । सजोषाः समानप्रीतिः । एवंगुणविशिष्ट- स्वष्टास्मदीयं रथं जूजुवत् । प्रेरयतु ॥ जु इति सौत्रो धातुर्गत्यर्थः । अस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुजि रूपं ॥ तथेळा तिसृणां देवीनामाद्येडाख्या देवी च रथं प्रेरयतु । बृहद्दिवा बृहन्महद्दीव्यति द्योतत इति बृहद्दिवः ॥ इगुपधालक्षणः कः । सुपां सुलुगिति विभक्तेराकारः । तादृशो भगश्च प्रेरयतु । उत आपि च रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्यौ पुरंधिर्बहुधीः पूषा पोषको देवश्च ॥ अधशब्दश्चार्थे ॥ पती सूर्याया भर्तारावश्विनौ च एते सर्वॆSस्मदीयं [?] रथं प्रेरयंतित्यर्थः ॥

Gist: Tvaṣṭṛ with the wives of the gods, Iḷā, Bhaga, heaven and earth, Pūṣan, Purandhi and the Aśvins are asked to set our chariot in motion; ju is a root of motion, and jūjuvat is a causal form with the luṅ-type ending.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Uta—and; syaḥ—the well-known; devaḥ—endowed with generosity and other qualities; bhuvanasya—of all beings; sakṣaṇiḥ—to be served; gnābhiḥ—with the wives of the gods; sajoṣāḥ—having equal affection; tvaṣṭā—the god Tvaṣṭṛ; rathaṃ—our chariot; jūjuvat—let him set in motion (make it go easily); (so also) iḷā—Iḷā; bṛhaddivā—of great splendour; bhagaḥ—Bhaga; uta—and; rodasī—heaven and earth; purandhiḥ—of special wisdom; pūṣā—Pūṣan; patī—the two husbands of Sūryā; aśvinau—the Aśvin deities (let them make our chariot move comfortably).

p. 168

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the god Tvaṣṭṛ, famous, endowed with generosity and other qualities, served by all beings, and equally well pleased with the wives of the gods, urge on our chariot; likewise may Iḷā, the resplendent Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, Pūṣan of special wisdom, and the Aśvin deities, the husbands of Sūryā, urge on our chariot.

Printed English translation

Or, may the divine Twashtri, the defender of the world, together with the wives (of the gods), well pleased, urge on the chariot ; or may Ila, the resplendent Bhaga, Heaven and Earth, the sagacious Pushan, and the Ashwins, the two husbands (or Surya), urge on the chariot.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ग्नाभिः सजोषाः (gnābhiḥ sajoṣāḥ)—"equally fond of the wives of the gods." The word ग्नाः (gnāḥ) is stated by Yāska among the names of speech (Ni. 2-27), and is explained (Ni. 3-21) as "मेना ग्ना इति स्त्रीणां, ग्ना गच्छंत्येनाः (menā gnā iti strīṇāṃ, gnā gacchaṃtyenāḥ)" (menā and gnā are names of women; gnās are those to whom men go). Sāyaṇa takes the god (written in the supplied text तृषृ (tṛṣṛ) [?], i.e. Tvaṣṭṛ) to be one equally fond of the wives of the gods, explains that the word is used in the sense of "wives of the gods", cites the Taittirīya Saṃhitā sentence "छंदांसि वै ग्नाः (chaṃdāṃsi vai gnāḥ)" and states the meaning: the metres Gāyatrī and the rest are the wives of the gods. When the Nirukta discusses the meaning of the word त्वष्टा (tvaṣṭā) it cites the Ṛk

त्वष्टा दुहित्रे वहतुं कृणोतीदं विश्वं भुवनं समेति । यमस्य माता पर्युह्यमाना महो जाया विवस्वतो ननाश ॥ (tvaṣṭā duhitre vahatuṃ kṛṇotīdaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sameti | yamasya mātā paryuhyamānā maho jāyā vivasvato nanāśa ‖) (R.S. 10-17-1).

Durgācārya gives the meaning in the historical view as "त्वष्टा हि विश्वकर्मा (tvaṣṭā hi viśvakarmā)" and the etymological (Nairukta) view as "तृष्णा मध्यमः (tṛṣṇā madhyamaḥ)" (as supplied). Sāyaṇa has commented in accord with both views.

The god Tvaṣṭṛ has the qualities of giving gifts and so on; he is served by all beings in the world. The sacrificer's wish is stated: may this god of such greatness urge on our chariot.

p. 169

इळा (iḷā)—"Iḷā, the first of the three goddesses." The word इळा (iḷā) is stated among the names of the earth (Si. [?] 2-5), among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23), among the names of food (Si. [?] 3-9) and among the names of cows (Ni. 3-9), and is explained as derived from ईट्टेः स्तुतिकर्मणः (īṭṭeḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ) (the root īḍ, to praise).

Sāyaṇa explains the meaning thus: of the three goddesses Iḷā, Sarasvatī and Bhāratī, the goddess called Iḷā, the first, is to urge on the sacrificer's chariot.

बृहद्दिवा भगः (bṛhaddivā bhagaḥ)—"he who shines greatly, he who is resplendent, is बृहद्दिवः (bṛhaddivaḥ); such a one also let him urge on." May the god named Bhaga, who shines with abundant radiance, also urge on our chariot.

रोदसी पुरंधिः पूषा (rodasī puraṃdhiḥ pūṣā)—"Heaven and Earth, and the god who is of much wisdom and the nourisher." The words रोदसी (rodasī) and पुरंधी (puraṃdhī) are stated among the names of Heaven and Earth (Ni. 3-22). Yāska explains the word पुरंधि (puraṃdhi) as "पुरंधिर्बहुधीस्तत्क पुरंधिर्भगः (puraṃdhirbahudhīstatka puraṃdhirbhagaḥ)" (Ni. 6-13) [text as supplied, apparently incomplete], and also (of Indra and Varuṇa) "इंद्र इत्यपरं स बहुकर्मतमः, पुरां च दारयितृतमः वरुण इत्यपरं (iṃdra ityaparaṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ, purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ varuṇa ityaparaṃ)". Durgācārya describes the meaning as "पुरंधिः बहुधनस्य दाता (puraṃdhiḥ bahudhanasya dātā)" (Ni. 11-2); and the word is also explained (Ni. 12-30) as "पुरंध्या स्तुत्या (puraṃdhyā stutyā)". The word पूषा (pūṣā) is stated among the names of the earth (Ni. 2-5), and is explained (Ni. 12-17) as "अथ यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत् पूषा भवति (atha yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tat pūṣā bhavati)" (now, because he nourishes with the nourishment of rays, he is Pūṣan). As the meanings of these words have been explained at length in the earlier volumes, they are not explained here. The wish is expressed: may Heaven and Earth and the god Pūṣan, of abundant wisdom, urge on the chariots of us, the sacrificers.

पती अश्विनौ (patī aśvinau)—"the two husbands of Sūryā, and the Aśvins; let these urge on our chariot." The explanation of the word aśvinī was given earlier. The matter of the Aśvin deities marrying the goddess Sūryā has also been told earlier. The sacrificers pray: may the Aśvin deities, the husbands of the goddess Sūryā, urge on our chariot.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उ॒त तै दे॒वी सु॒भगे॑ मिथू॒दृशो॒षासा॒नक्ता॒ जग॑तामपी॒जुवा॑ । स्तु॒षे यद्वां॑ पृथिवि॒ नव्य॑सा॒ वचः॑ स्था॒तुश्च॒ वय॒स्त्रिव॑या उप॒स्थिरे॑ ॥

uta tai devī subhage mithūdṛśoṣāsānaktā jagatāmapījuvā | stuṣe yadvāṃ pṛthivi navyasā vacaḥ sthātuśca vayastrivayā upasthire ‖

p. 170

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत । त्ये इति । देवी इति । सुभगे इति सुभगे । मिथुऽदृशा । उषसानक्ता । जगतां। अपिजुवा । स्तुषे । यत् । वां । पृथिवि । नव्यसा । वचः । स्थातुः । च । वयः । त्रिवयाः । उपस्थिरे ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उत अपि च त्ये ते प्रसिद्धे देवी देव्यौ देवनशीले सुभगे शोभनधने मिथूदृशा मिथः परस्परं पश्यंत्यौ एवंभूते उषासानक्ता उषाश्च रात्रिश्च जगतां जंगमानामपीजुवा प्रेरयित्र्यौ भवतः । तस्मादस्मदीयमपि रथं प्रेरय तां । उत्तरोर्धर्चो द्यावापृथिव्यः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे पृथिवि वां युवां त्वां दिवं च नव्यसा नवीयसा नवतरेण प्रशस्येन वचो वचसा ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया लुक् ॥ यद्यदा स्तुषे स्तुवे ॥ उत्तमस्य व्यत्ययेन मध्यमः ॥ तदानीं स्थातुः स्थावरस्य व्रीह्यादेः संबंधि वयोऽन्नं चरुपुरोडाशादिलक्षणं त्रिवयाः । वय इत्यन्ननाम । ओषधिपशुसोमात्मकानि हविर्लक्षणान्यन्नानि यस्य तादृशोऽहमुप- स्तिरे । उपस्तृणामि । आज्येनोपस्तरणाभिघारणपूर्वकं प्रयच्छामीत्यर्थः ॥ स्तृज् आच्छादने । लट्युत्तमे छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् । अत्रत्यश्चशब्दश्चणिति निपातांतरं पादपूरणं । ऋत इद्दातोरितीत्वं । निपातैर्यद्यदिहंतेति निघात प्रतिषेधः ॥

Gist: The Dawn and Night, goddesses who look at each other, drive on the moving world, so let them urge on our chariot too; the Ṛk's second half addresses Heaven and Earth, with the sacrificer offering with ghee the three kinds of food (plants, animals, Soma); the grammar concerns stṛ, the dropped ending, ca as a particle and the suppression of the accent.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Uta—and; tye—the famous; devī—shining; subhage—possessing excellent wealth; mithūdṛśā—looking at each other; uṣāsānaktā—O Day-and-Night (you); jagatām—of the world consisting of moving things; apījuvā—are the impellers (therefore urge on our chariot too). Pṛthivi—O Heaven and Earth; vām—you two; navyasā—with new; vacaḥ—speech in the form of praise; yat—when; stuṣe—I praise (then); sthātuḥ—of the stationary rice and the like; vayaḥ—food; trivayāḥ—I who have prepared the threefold oblation (of plants, animals and Soma); upastire—I offer, spreading it with ghee.

p. 171

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Day and Night, renowned, shining, possessed of excellent wealth, looking at one another: as you are the quickeners of the whole moving world, urge on our chariot. O Heaven and Earth, whenever I, who hold the threefold oblation (plants, animals, Soma), praise you both with a new hymn, then I offer the food of the stationary rice and the like, spreading it with ghee.

Printed English translation

Or, may the two divine auspicious and mutually contemplating Day and Night, the animators of moving (creatures, urge it on): and, Earth Heaven [sic], whilst I praise you both with a new hymn, I offer you food of the standing (corn), although provided with the three (sorts of sacrificial) viands.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

उषासानक्ता (uṣāsānaktā)—Yāska explains the word उषासानक्ता (uṣāsānaktā) (uṣāsānaktā) as "Uṣas and Night; naktā is a name of night; it envelops beings, or with dew; indistinct in colour" (Ni. 8-11). A detailed description of this word was given earlier.

देवी सुभगे मिथूदृशा उषासानक्ता जगतां अपीजुवा (devī subhage mithūdṛśā uṣāsānaktā jagatāṃ apījuvā)—Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit: the two shining, richly endowed goddesses, looking at each other, Uṣas and Night, are impellers of the moving; therefore let them urge on our chariot. The explanation given: shining by nature with radiance, joined with abundant and pleasant wealth, looking at one another, the goddess Uṣas and Night, being impellers of all moving beings, are prayed by the sacrificers to urge on our chariots.

Addressing the Earth-goddess as "O Pṛthivī", युवां दिवं च (yuvāṃ divaṃ ca): Uṣas, Night and the sky; the sacrificer is described as praising with नव्यसा वचना (navyasā vacanā), new and praiseworthy hymns; and स्थातुः वयः त्रिवयाः उपस्तृणे (sthātuḥ vayaḥ trivayāḥ upastṛṇe): I, the sacrificer, possessing the food of the stationary (rice-related, in the form of caru, puroḍāśa and so on), offer the oblation-food, spreading it with ghee ritually.

p. 172

त्रिवयाः (trivayāḥ)—वय इत्यन्न नाम (vaya ityanna nāma): the word vayaḥ is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The foods offered to the deities as oblation are of three kinds: Soma-juice, animal and caru; the sacrificer possesses them.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उ॒त वः॒ शंस॑मु॒शिजा॑मिव श्म॒स्यहि॑र्बु॒ध्न्यो॒३॒॑३ज एक॑पादु॒त । त्रि॒त ऋ॑भु॒क्षाः स॑वि॒ता चनो॑ दधे॒ऽपां नपा॑दाशु॒हेमा॑ धि॒या॑ शमि ॥ ६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत । वः । शंसं । उशिजां इव । स्मसि । अहिः । बुध्न्यः । अजः । एकपात् । उत । त्रितः । ऋभुक्षाः । सविता । चनः । दधे । अपां । नपात् । आशुहेमा । धिया । शमि ॥६॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उत अपि च हे देवा उशिजामिव । इवेति संप्रत्यर्थियः । अस्मत्तः स्तुतिं कामयमानानां वो युष्माकं शंसं स्तुतिं संप्रति स्मसि । उश्मसि कामयामहे ॥ वश कांतौ । इदंतो मसिः । ग्रहिज्यादिना संप्रसारणं । छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥ उत अपि च अहिर्बुध्न्यः । बुध्ममंतरिक्षं । तत्र भवोऽहिनामा देवः । अज एकपात् । न जायत इत्यजः । एक एव पद्यते गच्छतीत्येकपात् । अज एकपात्संज्ञकः सूर्यः । त्रितस्तीर्णतम ऋभुक्षा उरुक्षय उरुनिवास ऋभूणां निवासयिता वेंद्रश्च सविता प्रसविता चनोऽन्नं दधे । विदधातु सर्वस्य । अस्मभ्यं करोतु । तथाशुहेमा शीघ्रगामि ॥ हि गतानित्यस्मादन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यंत इति मनिन् ॥ तादृशोऽपां नपात् अपां पौत्रीयस्थानीयोऽग्निः ॥ अद्भ्य ओषधिवनस्पतयो जायंते । ओषधिवनस्पतिभ्य- श्चायमग्निर्जायत इत्यग्नेरपां पौत्रत्वं । स च धिया स्तुत्या शमि । शमीति कर्म- नाम । यज्ञकर्मणि प्रीतो भवत्विति शेषः ॥

Gist: The sacrificers desire to praise the gods as the gods desire praise; may Ahirbudhnya, Aja Ekapād, Trita, Ṛbhukṣan and Savitṛ grant food, and may Agni, grandson of the waters, be pleased by the praise and the rite. The tail explains smasi (from vaś), the swift-going, and śami as a word for action.

p. 173

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Uta—and (O gods); उशिजामिव (uśijāmiva)—who desire our praises; vaḥ—for your satisfaction; śaṃsam—praise; smasi—we offer with devotion. Uta—and; ahirbudhnyaḥ—Ahirbudhnya; aja ekapāt—the god called Aja Ekapād; tritaḥ—Trita; यभुक्षाः (yabhukṣāḥ) [?]—Ṛbhukṣan (printed with य (ya) as supplied); savitā—Savitṛ; canaḥ—food; dadhe—may (they) provide (and likewise); āśuhemā—the swift-going; apāṃ napāt—Agni, the grandson of the waters; dhiyā—by our praises; śami—by our rites (may he be gratified).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods, for the satisfaction of you who desire our praises, we offer praise with devotion. And may Ahirbudhnya, the god called Aja Ekapād, Trita, Ṛbhukṣan and Savitṛ provide us with food. Likewise may the swift-going Agni, renowned by the name Apāṃ Napāt, be gratified by our rites.

Printed English translation

We desire, gods, to repeat the praise of you, who are propitiated by praise: may Ahirbudhnya, Ajaekapad, Trita, Ribhukshin, Savitri, bestow upon us food, and may the swift-moving grandson of the waters, (Agni, be gratified by) our praises and our worship.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

उशिजामिव शंसं स्मसि (uśijāmiva śaṃsaṃ smasi)—Sāyaṇa's Sanskrit says "we desire now your praise, you who desire praise from us". Here the word iva is given the meaning samprati, "now". The word उशिक् (uśik) is stated among the names of the wise (Ni. 3-19) and explained as उशिक् वष्टेः कांतिकर्मणः (uśik vaṣṭeḥ kāṃtikarmaṇaḥ) (Ni. 6-11). The sense is given as those who seek praise from the reciter. The meaning is explained: we sacrificers desire to recite the praises of you gods, who desire praise recited by sacrificers performing the rite.

अहिर्बुध्न्यः (ahirbudhnyaḥ)—बुद्धमंतरिक्षं तत्र भवः अहिनामा देवः (buddhamaṃtarikṣaṃ tatra bhavaḥ ahināmā devaḥ). The word ahirbudhnya is explained by Yāska as योऽहिः स बुद्ध्यो बुध्ममंतरिक्षं तन्निवासात् (yo 'hiḥ sa buddhyo budhmamaṃtarikṣaṃ tannivāsāt) (Si. [?] 10-46) [text as supplied]. The word budhna is given the meaning "atmosphere", and the god named Ahi, born in the atmosphere, is the sense explained.

p. 174

अज एकपात् (aja ekapāt)—Yāska explains: न जायत इत्यजः (na jāyata ityajaḥ) ("he is aja because he is not born"); he is ekapād because he goes (moves) by one foot alone; or he drinks (or protects) with one foot; or one foot belongs to him (Ni. 12-30). Durgācārya says that this is the Sun, ever moving, one foot (a quarter) of Brahman. It is known that Fire is a foot, Wind is a foot, the Sun is a foot, the Quarters are a foot. Entering the whole world with one portion he protects it; at the time of sleep, as fire, he digests the food of living beings; with one foot (portion) he drinks the water of the whole world; as the life-principle he has entered the whole world as one foot (Ni. 12-30). Thus the word is explained as the Sun: he is one foot of the formless Supreme Brahman of pure being-consciousness-bliss, always moving, protecting the whole world by one portion; and to this Sun, the one foot of the four-footed Brahman (Fire, Wind, Sun, Quarters), Durgācārya ascribes identity with the Supreme Self in the form of action. The explanation of this word was given earlier. Sāyaṇa explains the word as the Sun, the one who moves alone, the unborn.

त्रितः ऋभुक्षाः (tritaḥ ṛbhukṣāḥ)—Sāyaṇa: Trita is "the one who has crossed over most" (tīrṇatama), Ṛbhukṣāḥ is "of wide dwelling, he who settles the Ṛbhus", and both are Indra. Yāska explains त्रितस्तीर्णतमो मेधया बभूव (tritastīrṇatamo medhayā babhūva) ("Trita surpassed all by his intelligence"), or else a number may be intended: "from one, two, three; they became three" (Ni. 4-6); त्रितः त्रिस्थान इंद्रः (tritaḥ tristhāna iṃdraḥ) ("Trita is Indra of the three stations", Ni. 9-25). The word ऋभुक्षाः (ṛbhukṣāḥ) is stated among the names of the great (Ni. 3-13) and explained by Yāska as उरुक्षयणः ऋभूणां राजा (urukṣayaṇaḥ ṛbhūṇāṃ rājā) ("of wide dwelling, king of the Ṛbhus", Ni. 9-3). Sāyaṇa takes both words as epithets of Indra: one who surpasses all by the power of his intellect, who, pervading (abundantly) many places, is fit for his office, or who keeps the Ṛbhus in comfort.

सविता (savitā)—"the impeller of all." Yāska explains this word as सर्वस्य प्रसविता (sarvasya prasavitā) (Ni. 10-32). The sacrificer's prayer is thus stated: may the god named Ahi, the Sun renowned as Aja Ekapād, Indra and the god Savitṛ grant food to us the sacrificers.

p. 175

आशुहेमा अपान्नपात् (āśuhemā apānnapāt)—"the swift-going Agni, who stands in the place of the grandson of the waters." Yāska explains अपांनपात् तनूनप्रा व्याख्यातः (apāṃnapāt tanūnaprā vyākhyātaḥ) (Si. [?] 10-18).

धिया शमि (dhiyā śami)—Sāyaṇa: शमीति कर्मनाम (śamīti karmanāma), "śami is a name for rite": may he be gratified in the sacrificial rite; or, by our rite in the form of service, may there be happiness (śam) for that reason. Śamī is stated among the names of rites (Ni. 3-2). One sense is thus stated: from the waters herbs and trees are born, and from these Agni is born; therefore Agni, as the "grandson" (in the place of a grandson) of the waters, swiftly pervading, hearing our praises in the sacrificial rites of us the sacrificers, may be pleased. Or, since the locative singular of the word meaning "happiness" is śami, it is explained that Agni may be one who produces happiness for us by the services performed by us sacrificers.

धिया (dhiyā)—"by praise." The word dhī is read by Yāska among the names of rites (Ni. 3-2) and among the names of wisdom (Ni. 3-13). Here Sāyaṇa explains it as praise.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ए॒ता वो॑ व॒श्मुद्य॑ता यजत्रा॒ अत॑क्षन्ना॒यवो॒ नव्य॑से॒ सं । श्र॒व॒स्यवो॒ वाजं॑ चका॒नाः सप्ति॒र्न रथ्यो॒ अह॑ धी॒तिम॑श्याः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

एता । वः । वश्मि । उत्यता । यजत्राः । अतक्षन् । आयवः । नव्यसे । सं । श्रवस्यवः । वाजं । चकानाः । सप्तिः । न । रथ्यः । अह । धीतिं । अश्याः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे यजत्रा यजनीया विश्वे देवा वो युष्मदीयान्येतैतान्युद्यतोद्य- तानि वचांसि वश्मि। कामये । नव्यसे नवतराय स्तुत्यतमाय युष्मद्गणायायवो मत्पभृतयो मनुष्याः कामितानि स्तोत्राणि समतक्षन् । समस्कुर्वन् । किमिच्छंतः। श्रवस्यवः श्रवणीयं यशोऽन्नं वात्मन इच्छंतः । वाजं बलं चकानाः कामय-

he yajatrā yajanīyā viśve devā vo yuṣmadīyānyetaitānyudyatodya- tāni vacāṃsi vaśmi| kāmaye | navyase navatarāya stutyatamāya yuṣmadgaṇāyāyavo matpabhṛtayo manuṣyāḥ kāmitāni stotrāṇi samatakṣan | samaskurvan | kimicchaṃtaḥ| śravasyavaḥ śravaṇīyaṃ yaśo 'nnaṃ vātmana icchaṃtaḥ | vājaṃ balaṃ cakānāḥ kāmaya-

p. 176

मानाः ॥ कन दीप्ति कांतिगतिषु । लिटः क्‌नच् ॥ रथ्यो रथसंबंधी सप्तिर्न सर्पणशी- लोऽश्व इव युष्मद्गणो धीतिमस्मदीयं कर्माश्याः । प्राप्पोतु ॥ अशू व्याप्तौ । व्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदमध्यमौ । बहुलं छंदसीति विकरणस्य लुक् ॥

mānāḥ ‖ kana dīpti kāṃtigatiṣu | liṭaḥ knac ‖ rathyo rathasaṃbaṃdhī saptirna sarpaṇaśī- lo 'śva iva yuṣmadgaṇo dhītimasmadīyaṃ karmāśyāḥ | prāppotu ‖ aśū vyāptau | vyatyayena parasmaipadamadhyamau | bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti vikaraṇasya luk ‖

Gist: the sacrificer desires to recite these praises to the worshipful Viśve Devāḥ; men wishing for food and strength have fashioned hymns for them; may their host come like a chariot-horse to our rite.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Yajatrāḥ—O gods worthy of sacrifice. Vaḥ—addressed to you. Etā udyatā—these praise-words, to be recited with faith. Vaśmi—I wish to recite. Śravasyavaḥ—seekers of food. Vājam—strength. Cakānāḥ—those who desire. Āyavaḥ—men like me. Navyase—for the worship of you, the worshipful. Samatakṣan—(they) fashion (praises). Rathyaḥ—yoked to a chariot. Saptiḥ na—like a horse. Dhīśiṃ [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has dhītim]—towards our rite. Aśyāḥ—(may your host) come and arrive.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O gods worthy of sacrifice, I wish to recite these praise-words, addressed to you and to be recited with faith. Men like me, seeking food and desiring strength, fashion praises for the worship of you, the worshipful. Like a horse yoked to a chariot, may your host come to our rite.

Printed English translation

Adorable (gods), I desire that these (my) earnest praises (should please) you: men wishing for food, desirous of vigour, have constructed (hymns) for yours [sic] celebration; may you hasten like a (swift) chariot-horse to our (pious) rite.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यजत्रा (yajatrā)—यजनीयाः (yajanīyāḥ). Since the Viśve Devāḥ are worthy of sacrifice, they are addressed by this word. वः एता उद्यता वश्मि (vaḥ etā udyatā vaśmi)—युष्मदीयानि एतानि उद्यतानि वचांसि कामये (yuṣmadīyāni etāni udyatāni vacāṃsi kāmaye): it is described that the sacrificer wishes to recite praises addressed to these gods; and आयवः नव्यसे समतक्षन् (āyavaḥ navyase samatakṣan)—मत्पृतयोः मनुष्याः स्तुत्यतमाय युष्मद्गणाय स्तोत्राणि समस्कुर्वन् (matpṛtayoḥ manuṣyāḥ stutyatamāya yuṣmadgaṇāya stotrāṇi samaskurvan) (as supplied; the bhāṣya reads matprabhṛtayaḥ): the sacrificers and others, desiring fame, food and strength, have worshipped these gods with praises fit to be recited.

रथ्यः (rathyaḥ)—सप्तिर्न धीतिं अश्याः (saptirna dhītiṃ aśyāḥ)—रथसंबंधी सर्पणशीलो अश्व इव युष्मद्गणः अस्मदीयं कर्म प्राप्पोतु (rathasaṃbaṃdhī sarpaṇaśīlo aśva iva yuṣmadgaṇaḥ asmadīyaṃ karma prāppotu). Like a swift horse fit to be yoked to a chariot, (the text breaks off at the page end)

p. 177

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 177.

accepts the praise and the service of one who serves it, so may the Viśve devāḥ accept all the duties that concern them, namely the recitation of praises, the offering of oblations and so on, performed by us the sacrificers: thus the wish is expressed.

आयवः (āyavaḥ)—मनुष्याः (manuṣyāḥ). This word is stated among the names of men (Ni. 3-8). Here the sense is given as men such as those who perform the sacrifice.

सप्तिः (saptiḥ)—सर्पणशीलः अश्वः (sarpaṇaśīlaḥ aśvaḥ). The word sapti is read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27). The meaning is explained as a horse of a swiftly moving nature.

रथ्याः (rathyāḥ)—Yāska has described the plural form of the word rathya as रथस्य वोढारः (rathasya voḍhāraḥ) (Ni. 10-3). The word rathya, used as an epithet of sapti, is interpreted as "connected with a chariot".

Sūkta 32 (Maṇḍala 2)

The thirty-second sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

अस्य म इत्यष्टर्चं दशमं सूक्तं गृत्समदस्यार्षं षष्ठ्याद्यास्तिस्रोऽनु- ष्टुभः । शिष्टाः पंच जगत्यः । प्रथमा द्यावापृथिवीया ततॊ द्वे ऐंद्रौ त्वाष्टौ ना । ततो द्वे राकादेवत्ये द्वे सिनीवालीदेवत्ये अंत्या गुंग्वादिषड् देवताका । तथा चानुक्रांतं । अस्यमेऽष्टौ जागतं त्रैनुष्टुबंतं । द्यावापृथिव्येका द्वे ऐंद्रौ त्वाष्टौ ना द्वे द्वे राकासिनीवाल्ल्योरंत्या लिंगोक्तदेवतेति ॥ अभिप्लविके चतुर्थेऽहनि वैश्वदेवशस्त्र आद्यस्तृचो द्यावापृथिवीयनिविद्धानः । तथा च सूत्रितं । अस्य मे द्यावापृथिवी इति तिस्रस्ततं मे अप इति वैश्वदेवं । आ. ७-७ । इति ॥

Gist: the tenth sūkta of Anuvāka 3, of eight ṛks, of the Gṛtsamada seer; the last three ṛks are anuṣṭubh, the other five jagatī; deities as in the Anuvāda; the Anukramaṇī and the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (7-7) are quoted for the application.

Anuvāda (Kannada). This sūkta, अस्य मे (asya me), is the tenth sūkta in the third anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada; the last three ṛks, from the sixth to the eighth, are of anuṣṭubh metre; the remaining five ṛks are of jagatī metre. In this sūkta the first ṛk has Dyāvāpṛthivī (Heaven and Earth) as deity; the next two ṛks (ṛks 2-3) have Indra or Tvaṣṭṛ as deity; the next two ṛks (ṛks 4-5) have Rākā as deity; the next two ṛks (ṛks 6-7) have Sinīvālī as deity; the last ṛk (the 8th) has as deities six persons beginning with Gungū

p. 178

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 32, p. 178.

(Gungū and others). In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: अस्य मेऽष्टौ जागतं त्र्यनुष्टुबंतं द्यावापृथिव्यैका द्वे ऐंद्रौ त्वाष्टौ वा द्वे द्वे राकासिनीवाल्ल्योरंत्या लिंगोक्तदेवतेति (asya me 'ṣṭau jāgataṃ tryanuṣṭubaṃtaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyaikā dve aiṃdrau tvāṣṭau vā dve dve rākāsinīvāllyoraṃtyā liṃgoktadevateti). On the fourth day of the Abhiplava sacrifice, at the recitation of the Vaiśvadeva-śastra mantras, the first three ṛks of this sūkta are to be used as nivid-mantras relating to Dyāvāpṛthivī, as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra beginning अस्य मे द्यावापृथिवी (asya me dyāvāpṛthivī) and ending वैश्वदेवं (vaiśvadevaṃ) (Āś. 7-7).

Sūkta—32

Maṇḍala 2 ‖ Anuvāka 3 ‖ Sūkta 32 ‖ Aṣṭaka 2 ‖ Adhyāya 7 ‖ Varga 15 ‖ Number of ṛks in the Sūkta: 8 · Ṛṣi: Gṛtsamada · Devatā: 1. Dyāvāpṛthivī (printed द्यावाप्यथिवी (dyāvāpyathivī) [sic]); 2-3. Indra or Tvaṣṭṛ (printed स्वष्टा (svaṣṭā) [sic]); 4-5. Rākā; 6-7. Sinīvālī; 8. the deities named in the text (liṅgokta) · Chandas: 1-5 jagatī; 6-8 anuṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अ॒स्य मे॑ द्यावापृथिवी ऋताय॒तो भू॒तम॑वि॒त्री वच॑सः॒ सिषा॑सतः । ययो॒रायुः॑ प्रत॒रं ते इ॒दं पु॒र उप॑स्तुते वसू॒युर्वा०॒॑॑ महो दधे ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अस्य । मे । द्यावापृथिवी इति । ऋत्ययतः । भूतं । अवित्री इति । वचसः । सिसासतः । ययोः । आयुः । प्रतरं । ते इति । इदं । पुरः । उपस्तुते इत्युपस्तुते । वसुयुः । वां । महः । दधे ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

द्यावापृथिवी हे द्यावापृथिव्यौ ऋतायत ऋतं यज्ञमात्मन इच्छतः सिषासतो युवां संभक्तुमिच्छतोऽस्य वचसः ॥ वक्तीति वचाः स्तोता । असुन् ॥

dyāvāpṛthivī he dyāvāpṛthivyau ṛtāyata ṛtaṃ yajñamātmana icchataḥ siṣāsato yuvāṃ saṃbhaktumicchato 'sya vacasaḥ ‖ vaktīti vacāḥ stotā | asun ‖

p. 179

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 179.

स्तोतुरस्य मे ममावित्री अवित्यौ पालयित्र्य भूतं । भवतं । ययोर्द्यावा- पृथिव्योरायुरन्नं प्रतरं प्रकृष्टतरमुत्पद्यत इति शेषः । इदमिदानीं ते द्यावा- पृथिव्यावुपस्तुते तत्र तत्र स्थितैः स्तोतृभिः स्तुते वां युवां वसूयुर्धनका- मोSहं महो महतः ॥ विभक्तिव्यत्ययः ॥ महता स्तोत्रेण पुरो दधे । पुरस्करोमि ॥

Gist: O Heaven and Earth, protect me, who desire the sacrifice and wish to serve you; whose food is the best; I, wanting wealth, honour you with great praise.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

द्यावापृथिवी (dyāvāpṛthivī)—O Heaven and Earth. ऋतायतः (ṛtāyataḥ)—one who desires to perform the sacrifice, and सिषासतः (siṣāsataḥ)—who wishes to serve you, and वचसः (vacasaḥ)—a praiser: अस्य मे (asya me)—for this me, अवित्री (avitrī)—be protectresses; भूतं (bhūtaṃ)—be. ययोः (yayoḥ)—of which Heaven and Earth, आयुः (āyuḥ)—the food प्रतरं (prataraṃ)—is the most excellent; ते (te)—such, and उपस्तुते (upastute)—praised by all: नां (nāṃ) [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has vāṃ]—you two; इदं (idaṃ)—now; वसूयुः (vasūyuḥ)—desiring wealth; महः (mahaḥ)—with great praise; पुरः दधे (puraḥ dadhe)—I extol.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Heaven and Earth, be the protectresses of this me, who desire to perform the sacrifice, am eager to serve you, and am your praiser. You whose food is the most excellent and who are praised by all: you two I now extol with great praise, desiring wealth.

Printed English translation

Heaven and Earth, be the protectors of me your worshipper, anxious to propitiate you by worship and adoration, for of you two is abundant food : desiring riches, I glorify you both, and celebrate you with great (laudation).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this ṛk Heaven and Earth are praised. Addressing Heaven and Earth, the wish is expressed that they may be protectors of the sacrificer, who desires to serve them both by performing the sacrifice and by reciting praise, and who is reciting the praise.

वचसः (vacasaḥ)—वक्तीति वचाः स्तोता (vaktīti vacāḥ stotā). Since he recites praises, the word vacasaḥ is used in the sense of a reciter of praise.

p. 180

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 32, p. 180.

उपस्तुते (upastute)—तत्र तत्र स्थितैः स्तोतृभिः स्तुते । (tatra tatra sthitaiḥ stotṛbhiḥ stute |) It is explained that at the times of the sacrifices the Ṛtvijs and the sacrificers, each in his own place, praise (Heaven and Earth).

वसूयुः (vasūyuḥ)—धनकामः ! (dhanakāmaḥ !) Yāska explained the meaning as “वसूयवो वसुकामाः (vasūyavo vasukāmāḥ)” (Ni. 6-5) and also as “वसूयुः वसुमान् (vasūyuḥ vasumān)” (Ni. 6-32).

ययोः आयुः प्रतरं (yayoḥ āyuḥ prataraṃ)—It is described that the food obtained from these Heaven and Earth is abundant; and इदं ते उपस्तुते (idaṃ te upastute)—for this reason these Heaven and Earth are now praised by the respective Ṛtvijs in the sacrifices; and वसूयुः महः पुरः दधे (vasūyuḥ mahaḥ puraḥ dadhe)—the sacrificer, wishing to obtain wealth and the like, will gratify these Heaven and Earth by reciting laudable hymns.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मा नो॒ गुह्या॒ रिप॑ आ॒योरह॑न्दभ॒न्मा न॑ अ॒भ्योरी॑रधो दु॒च्चु-॑ ना॑भ्यः । मा नो॒ वि यौः॑ स॒ख्या वि॒द्धि तस्य॑ नः सुम्नाय॒ता मन॑सा॒ तत्त्वे॑- महे ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मा । नः । गुह्याः । रिपः । आयोः । अहन् । दभन् । मा । नः । अभ्यः । रीरधः । दुच्चुनाभ्यः । मा । नः । वि । यौः । सख्या । विद्दि । तस्य । नः । सुम्नयता । मनसा । तत् । त्वा । ईमहे ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे इंद्र त्वष्टर्वा आयोर्मनुष्यस्य शत्रुभूतस्य गुह्या गोप्या ज्ञातुम- शक्या रिपो हिंसारूपा माया नोऽस्मान् अहन् । उपलक्षणमेतत् । अदनि राष्टौ

he iṃdra tvaṣṭarvā āyormanuṣyasya śatrubhūtasya guhyā gopyā jñātuma- śakyā ripo hiṃsārūpā māyā no 'smān ahan | upalakṣaṇametat | adani rāṣṭau

p. 181

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 181.

च मा दभन् । मा हिंसिषुः । तथा नोऽस्मानाभ्यो दुच्चुनाभ्यः । शुनमिति सुख- नाम । दुःशुना दुच्चुनाः । दुःखकारिणीभ्यः शत्रुसेनाभ्यो मा रीरथः । वशं मा नैषीः । रध्यतिर्वशगमन इति यास्कः । रध हिंसासंराद्योः । अस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुजि चजि रूपं ॥ अपि च नोऽस्माकं सख्या सख्यानि सखित्वानि मा वि यौः । त्वया वियुक्तानि मा कार्षिः । अपि तु नोऽस्माकं तस्य तत् सखित्वं सुम्नायता सुखमस्माकमिच्छता मनसा विद्धि । जानीहि ॥ क्रियाग्रहणं कर्तव्यमिति कर्मणः संप्रदानत्वाच्चतुर्थ्यर्थे षष्ठी ॥ तत् त्वा त्वादृशं त्वामीमहे । अभिमतफलं याचामहे ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति तच्छब्दादुत्तरस्या विभक्तेर्लुक् ॥

Gist: O Indra (or Tvaṣṭṛ), may the hidden, harmful wiles of the hostile man not harm us; do not hand us to the enemy hosts, nor sever our friendship; know it with a mind wishing us well; we ask this of you.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

O Indra. आयोः (āyoḥ)—of the man who is an enemy. गुह्याः (guhyāḥ)—secret. रिपः (ripaḥ)—the wiles of a harmful kind! नः (naḥ)—us. अहन् (ahan)—whether by day or by night. मा दभन् (mā dabhan)—may they not harm. नः (naḥ)—us. आभ्यः दुच्चुनाभ्यः (ābhyaḥ duccunābhyaḥ)—to these hostile armies that cause suffering. मा रीरधः (mā rīradhaḥ)—do not make us subject. नः (naḥ)—with us. सख्या (sakhyā)—your friendship. मा वि यौः (mā vi yauḥ)—do not cause it to be broken. नः (naḥ)—with us. तस्य (tasya)—that friendship. सुम्नायता (sumnāyatā)—desiring happiness. मनसा (manasā)—with the mind. विद्भि (vidbhi)—know. तत् त्वा (tat tvā)—you, such a trusted friend. ई महे (ī mahe)—I ask for the desired fruit.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, may the secret and harmful wiles of the man who is our enemy not harm us, whether by day or by night. Do not make us subject to these hostile armies that cause suffering. Do not let your friendship with us be broken, but increase it so that it becomes a source of happiness. From you, such a trusted friend, I ask for the desired fruit.

Printed English translation

Let not the secret guile of man, (Indra), harm us by day (or night); leave us not subject to the malevolent, disunite us not from your friendship; regard us with the favourable thoughts that (spring) from it: we ask this (boon) of you.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk and in the next Ṛk both Indra and the deity called Tvaṣṭṛ (printed तृष्ट (tṛṣṭa), as supplied) are praised. The derivation of the word Indra and of the word Tvaṣṭṛ (printed तृष्ट (tṛṣṭa)) has been stated earlier.

p. 182

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 32, p. 182.

आयोः—गुह्याः रिषः नः अर्ह— शत्रुभूतस्य मनुष्यस्य ज्ञातुमशक्याः मायाः हिंसारूपाः अहनि रात्रौ च मा हिंसिषुः । (āyoḥ—guhyāḥ riṣaḥ naḥ arha— śatrubhūtasya manuṣyasya jñātumaśakyāḥ māyāḥ hiṃsārūpāḥ ahani rātrau ca mā hiṃsiṣuḥ |) (text as supplied; the words रिषः नः अर्ह (riṣaḥ naḥ arha) differ from the Saṃhitā.) The word आयुः (āyuḥ) is explained as the enemy, a man. It is a prayer to Indra and to Tvaṣṭṛ (printed तृष्ट (tṛṣṭa)) that the deeds practised by this enemy to harm us, the sacrificers, deeds that we are unable to know, may not harm us by day and night.

दुच्चुनाभ्यः (duccunābhyaḥ)—दुःशुनाः दुच्चुनाः दुःखकारिणीभ्यः शत्रुसेनाभ्यः । (duḥśunāḥ duccunāḥ duḥkhakāriṇībhyaḥ śatrusenābhyaḥ |) The word शुन (śuna) is stated by Yāska among the words for happiness (Ni. 3-13). When the prefix दुः (duḥ) with the meaning “producing suffering” joins the word शुन (śuna), which denotes happiness, the word दुच्चुन (duccuna) results. The sacrificers pray that Indra and the god Tvaṣṭṛ may not hand us over to the power of enemies who cause suffering.

नः सख्या मा वि यौ:—अस्माकं सखित्वानि त्वया वियुक्तानि मा कार्षिः । (naḥ sakhyā mā vi yau:—asmākaṃ sakhitvāni tvayā viyuktāni mā kārṣiḥ |) The sacrificers pray that their friendship with Indra may not be broken; and नः तस्य सुम्नायता मनसा विद्धि (naḥ tasya sumnāyatā manasā viddhi)—अस्माकं तत्सखित्वं सुखमस्माकमिच्छता मनसा जानीहि (asmākaṃ tatsakhitvaṃ sukhamasmākamicchatā manasā jānīhi)—that Indra should regard the friendship that has arisen between him and us with a mind that grants happiness to us sacrificers; this prayer of the sacrificers is stated.

सुम्मायता (summāyatā) (as supplied) - सुखमिच्छता । (sukhamicchatā |) Since the word सुम्म (summa) (as supplied) is stated among the words for happiness (Ni. 3-13), the meaning “desiring happiness” is given here for this word.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अहे॑ळता॒ मन॑सा श्रु॒ष्टिमा व॑ह॒ दुहा॑नां धे॒नुं पि॒प्युषी॑मस॒श्चतं॑ । पद्या॑भिरा॒शुं वच॑सा च वा॒जिनं॒ त्वां हि॑नोमि पुरुहूत वि॒श्वहा॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अहेळता । मनसा । श्रुष्टिं । आ । वह । दुहानां । धेनुं । पिप्युषीं । असश्चतं ॥ पद्याभिः । अशुं । वचसा । च । वाजिनं । त्वां । हिनोमि । पुरुहूत । विश्वहा ॥ ३ ॥

aheḷatā | manasā | śruṣṭiṃ | ā | vaha | duhānāṃ | dhenuṃ | pipyuṣīṃ | asaścataṃ ‖ padyābhiḥ | aśuṃ | vacasā | ca | vājinaṃ | tvāṃ | hinomi | puruhūta | viśvahā ‖ 3 ‖

p. 183

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 183.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे इंद्र त्वष्टर्वा अहेळता अक्रुध्यता मनसा श्रुष्टिं सुखकरीं दुहानां दोग्निं पिप्युषीं प्रवृद्धां पीनां ॥ प्याया वृद्धौ । लिटः क्वसुः । लिड्यजोश्चेति पीभावः । उगितश्चेति जीप् । संप्रसारणमिति संप्रसारणं । शासिवसिघसीनां चेति षत्वं ॥ असश्चतमसक्तावयनां एवंभूतां धेनुं गामावह। अभिमुख्येन प्रापय। अपि च हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूतेंद्र त्वष्टर्वा पद्याभिः पादगतिभिराशुं व्यापन- शीलं वचसा वाचा च वाजिनं वेगवंतं त्वां विश्वहा सर्वेष्वहःसु हिनोमि । स्तुतिभिः प्रेरयामि ॥ हि गतौ वृद्धौ च ॥

Gist: O Indra (or Tvaṣṭṛ), bring us the well-nourished, milk-yielding cow; I urge you, swift in your steps and in your words, with praises on all days.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O Indra) अहेळता (aheḷatā)—without anger. मनसा (manasā)—with the mind. श्रुष्टिं (śruṣṭiṃ)—that gives happiness. दुहानां (duhānāṃ)—that is to be milked. पिप्युषीं (pipyuṣīṃ)—well-fed. असश्चतं (asaścataṃ)—having limbs well fitted together. धेनुं (dhenuṃ)—the milch cow. आ वह (ā vaha)—bring and join to us, towards us. पुरुहूत (puruhūta)—O Indra, who are called by many. पद्याभिः (padyābhiḥ)—by the movements of the feet. आशुं (āśuṃ)—who pervade everything. वचसा (vacasā)—by speech. वाजिनं च (vājinaṃ ca)—and swift. त्वां (tvāṃ)—you. विश्वहा (viśvahā)—on all days. हिनोमि (hinomi)—I urge with praises.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, with a mind free from anger, bring and join to us, towards us, the cow that gives happiness, that is to be milked, that is well-fed and has limbs well fitted together. O Indra, who are called by many, you who pervade everything by the movements of your feet and are swift by speech, I urge on all days with praises.

Printed English translation

Bring to us, with benignant mind, the well-nourished and compactly-limbed milch cow, yielding milk, and conferring happiness : daily I glorify, you, who are adored by many, quick (your) steps, and rapid in (your) words.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Let Indra, or the god Tvaṣṭṛ, with a mind free from anger, that is अहेळता मनसा (aheḷatā manasā)—अक्रुध्यता मनसा (akrudhyatā manasā), that is, a mind filled with joy, towards us the sacrificers, grant us for our good a cow (milch cow) that gives happiness, that yields milk

p. 184

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 3, Sūkta 32, p. 184.

abundantly, whose body is well grown, and that is free from bad marks; thus the wish is expressed. Indra and the god Tvaṣṭṛ are addressed as पुरुहूत (puruhūta)—बहुभिराहूत (bahubhirāhūta), called in many sacrifices, with recitation of praises, by many priests and sacrificers. Then, पद्याभिः आशुं वचसा च वाजिनं त्वा विश्वहा हिनोमि (padyābhiḥ āśuṃ vacasā ca vājinaṃ tvā viśvahā hinomi)—the greatness of this god is described: he pervades everything by the movements of his own feet and is swift by his words; and it is said that, addressing this god who is endowed with such greatness, the sacrificer recites praises on all days. श्रुष्टिं (śruṣṭiṃ)—सुखकरीं (sukhakarīṃ). The word श्रुष्टी (śruṣṭī) is explained by Yāska as श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम (śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma) (Ni. 6-13). Durgācārya, giving the meaning श्रुष्टीवरीः सुखवतीः (śruṣṭīvarīḥ sukhavatīḥ), explains that the word is used in several senses. अहेळता (aheḷatā)—अक्रुध्यता (akrudhyatā). Yāska (Ni. 3-9) has read हेळतेः (heḷateḥ) among the words for the action of being angry. On this basis Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning here as "free from anger".

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

रा॒काम॒हं सु॒हवां॑ सुष्टु॒ती हु॑वे शृ॒णोतु॑ नः सु॒भगा॒ बोध॑तु॒॑ त्मना॑ । सीव्य॒त्वपः॑ सू॒च्याच्छि॑द्यमानया॒ ददा॑तु वी॒रं श॒तदा॑यमु॒क्त्यं॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

राकां अहं । सुहवां । सुस्तुती । हुवे । शृणोतु । नः । सुभगा । बोधतु । त्मना । सीव्यतु । अपः । सूच्या । अच्छैद्यमानया । ददातु । वीरं । शतदायं । उक्तं ॥

rākāṃ ahaṃ | suhavāṃ | sustutī | huve | śṛṇotu | naḥ | subhagā | bodhatu | tmanā | sīvyatu | apaḥ | sūcyā | acchaidyamānayā | dadātu | vīraṃ | śatadāyaṃ | uktaṃ ‖

p. 185

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 185.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पत्नीसंयाजेषु गृहपतेः प्राक् राकासिनीवाल्यौ यष्टव्ये । तत्र राकाया- गस्य राकामहमित्यादिके याज्यानुवाक्ये । सूत्रितं च । राकामहं सिनीवालि कुहू- महमिति द्वे द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये । आ. १-१० । इति ॥ तथाग्निमारुतेष्टेते धाय्कॆ । सूत्रितं च । राकामहमिति द्वे । आ. ५-२० । इति ॥ संपूर्णचंद्रा पौर्णमासी राका । तां देवीं सुहवां स्वाह्वानामाह्वान- प्रयोजनकारिणीं सुष्टती शोभनया स्तुत्याहं हुवे । आह्वयामि ॥ सुष्टुति- शब्दात्तृतीयैकवचनस्य सुपां सुलुगिति पूर्वसवर्ण ईकारः॥ सा च सुभगा शोभन- धना नोऽस्माकमाह्वानं शृणोतु । श्रुत्वा च त्मना आत्मना स्वयमेव बोधतु । अस्मदभिप्रायं बुध्यतां । बुद्ध्वा चापः कर्म पुत्रोत्पादनलक्षणं सूच्या सूची- स्थानीययाच्छिद्यमानयाविच्छन्नयानुग्रहबुद्ध्या सीव्यतु । संतनोतु । यथा वस्त्रादिकं सूच्या सूतं चिरं तिष्ठति एवमिदं करोतु । कृत्वा च वीरं विक्रांतं शतदायं बहुधनं बहुप्रदं वोक्ष्यं प्रशस्यं पुत्रं ददातु ॥

Gist: Rākā, the full-moon deity, is invoked with praise at the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings; may she hear, understand, and bestow a valiant, wealthy, praiseworthy son.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सुहवां (suhavāṃ)—worthy of an excellent invocation. राकां (rākāṃ)—the deity called Rākā. सुष्टुती (suṣṭutī)—with excellent praise. अहं (ahaṃ)—I. हुवे (huve)—call. सुभगा (subhagā)—that goddess who has excellent wealth. नः (naḥ)—our invocation. शृणोतु (śṛṇotu)—may she hear! त्मना (tmanā)—of her own accord. बोधतु (bodhatu)—may she understand our desire. अपः (apaḥ)—the work in the form of begetting a son. सूच्या (sūcyā)—like a needle. अच्छिद्यमानया (acchidyamānayā)—unbroken. With a mind of favour सीव्यतु (sīvyatu)—may she weave. वीरं (vīraṃ)—a valiant. शतदायं (śatadāyaṃ)—wealthy. उक्ष्यं (ukṣyaṃ) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has उक्त्यं (uktyaṃ))—praiseworthy son. ददातु (dadātu)—may she give.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I call the deity called "Rākā", who is worthy of an excellent invocation, with excellent praise. May that goddess, who has excellent wealth, hear our invocation. May she understand our desire of her own accord. May she weave the work in the form of begetting a son with a mind of favour that is like a needle and unbroken. May she give a son who is valiant, wealthy and praiseworthy.

Printed English translation

I invoke, with suitable praise, Raka, who is worthily invoked : may she, who is auspicious of good fortune, hear us, and spontaneously

p. 186

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 186.

understand (our purpose): may she sew her work with an infallible needle : may she grant us excellent and opulent descendants.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the sacrifice called Patnīsaṃyāja, before the offering to the Gṛhapati, offerings are to be made to the deities Rākā and Sinīvālī. Then, in the Rākā sacrifice, the first Ṛk of this sūkta, राकामहं (rākāmahaṃ), and the second Ṛk, यास्ते राके (yāste rāke), are used as the Yājyā and Puronuvākyā mantras, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra राकामहं सिनीवालि कुहू-महमिति द्वे द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये (rākāmahaṃ sinīvāli kuhū-mahamiti dve dve yājyānuvākye) (Ā. 1-10); and in the mantras having the Maruts as deity these Ṛks are to be used as Dhāyyā mantras, as expounded by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the sūtra राकामहमिति द्वे (rākāmahamiti dve) (Ā. 5-20). By this Ṛk and the next one the goddess Rākā is praised. Rākā: the full-moon night. The night that has the full moon is commonly called Pūrṇimā; this is what is called Rākā. सुहवां सुष्टुती अहं हुवे (suhavāṃ suṣṭutī ahaṃ huve): it is said that I call her who is well-called, i.e. who brings about the fulfilment of invocations, with excellent praise; as this goddess fulfils the wishes of those who call her, the sacrificer invokes her with excellent praise. The word सुभगा (subhagā) is taken to mean one who has excellent wealth: may this goddess who has excellent wealth hear the sacrificer's invocation, and having heard it, त्मना बोधतु (tmanā bodhatu), may she of herself understand the purpose for which the sacrificer has invoked her; and अपः सूच्या अच्छिद्यमानया सीव्यतु (apaḥ sūcyā acchidyamānayā sīvyatu), may she so favour us that the sacrificer's line is not broken. वीरं शतदायं उक्थं पुत्रं ददातु (vīraṃ śatadāyaṃ ukthaṃ putraṃ dadātu): the wish is expressed that she grant a son who is valiant, possessed of abundant wealth or giving abundantly, and praiseworthy. अपः सूच्या अच्छिद्यमानया सीव्यतु (apaḥ sūcyā acchidyamānayā sīvyatu)—the bhāṣya says: पुत्रोत्पादनलक्षणं कर्म सूचीस्थानीयया अविच्छन्नया अनुग्रहबुद्धा संतनोतु । यथावस्त्रादिकं सूच्यास्यतं चिरं तिष्ठति एवमिदं करोतु (putrotpādanalakṣaṇaṃ karma sūcīsthānīyayā avicchannayā anugrahabuddhā saṃtanotu | yathāvastrādikaṃ sūcyāsyataṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhati evamidaṃ karotu). The word अपः (apaḥ) has been read by Yāska among the names of action (Ni. 3-2). Here its meaning is explained as the action consisting of the begetting of sons. The meaning is explained thus: through the favour of the goddess Rākā, as a garment stitched with a needle remains firm for a long time, so may our line, by the birth of sons, remain firm for a long time.

p. 187

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 187.

The author of the Nirukta, in explaining the word राका (rākā), cites this very Ṛk (Ni. 11-32); gives the derivation राका—रातेर्दान कर्मणः (rākā—rāterdāna karmaṇaḥ), and then explains the Ṛk राकामहं सुह्वानां सुष्टुत्या-ह्वये शृणोतुनस्सुभगा बोधत्वात्मना सीव्यत्वपः प्रजननकर्म सूच्याच्छिद्यमानया। सूची सीव्यतेः ददातु वीरं शतप्रदमुक्थं व्यक्तव्यप्रशंसं (rākāmahaṃ suhvānāṃ suṣṭutyā-hvaye śṛṇotunassubhagā bodhatvātmanā sīvyatvapaḥ prajananakarma sūcyācchidyamānayā| sūcī sīvyateḥ dadātu vīraṃ śatapradamukthaṃ vyaktavyapraśaṃsaṃ) in the same way as the bhāṣyakāra has explained it.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यास्ते॑ राके सुम॒तयः॑ सु॒पेश॑सो॒ याभि॒र्ददा॑सि दा॒शुषे॒ वसू॑नि । ताभि॑र्नो अ॒द्य सु॒मना॑ उ॒पाग॑हि सहस्रपो॒षं सु॑भगे॒ ररा॑णा॥ ५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

याः । ते । राके । सुमतयः । सुपेशसः । याभिः । ददासि । दाशुषे । वसूनि । ताभिः । नः । अद्य । सुमनाः । उपआगहि । सहस्रपोषं । सुभगे । रराणा ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे राके देवि सुपेशसः शोभनरूपास्ते तव याः सुमतयः शोभनबु- द्धयः याभिर्मतिभिर्दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय वसूनि धनानि ददासि । प्रयच्छसि । अद्येदानीं ताभिर्मतिभिः सहिता त्वं सुमनाः शोभनमना भूत्वापा- गहि । उपागच्छ ॥ गमेश्चांदसः शपो लुक् । अनुदात्तोपदेशेत्यादिनानुनासिक- लोपः । असिद्धवदत्राभादित्यस्यासिद्धत्वाद्देर्लुगभावः ॥ किं कुर्वती । हे सुभगे शोभनधने सहस्रपोषं सहस्रसंख्याकस्य धनस्य पुष्टिं रराणा ददती ॥ रा दाने । व्यत्ययेन शानच् । छांदसः शपः श्लुः । अभ्यस्तानामादिरित्याद्युदात्तत्वं ॥

Gist: O goddess Rākā, with the good intentions with which you give wealth to the offerer, come to us today with good mind, bestowing a thousand-fold increase of wealth. The tail explains the verb forms upāgahi and rarāṇā.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सुभगे (subhage)—one with excellent wealth. राके (rāke)—O goddess Rākā. सुपेशसः (supeśasaḥ)—of excellent form. ते (te)—your. याः सुमतयः (yāḥ sumatayaḥ)—which auspicious intentions there are. याभिः (yābhiḥ)—by which very benevolent intentions. दाशुषे (dāśuṣe)—to the sacrificer who offers oblation.

p. 188

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 188.

वसूनि (vasūni)—wealth. ददासि (dadāsi)—you give. अद्य (adya)—now. नः (naḥ)—in our regard. ताभि (tābhi)—with those very intentions. सुमनाः (sumanāḥ)—having an auspicious mind. सहस्रपोषं (sahasrapoṣaṃ)—increase of wealth numbering a thousand. रराणा (rarāṇā)—giving. उपागहि (upāgahi)—be gracious (come).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Rākā, who have excellent wealth, with those auspicious intentions of yours, of excellent form, and with those very kindly intentions by which you give wealth to the sacrificer who offers oblation, now in our regard, with the same intentions, being of auspicious mind and giving an increase of wealth numbering a thousand, be gracious.

Printed English translation

Raka, with those your kind and gracious intentions, wherewith you grant riches to the donor (of oblations), approach us to-day; you who are auspicious of good fortune, favourably inclined, and bestowing a thousand blessings.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing this goddess by the words हे राके (he rāke), in याभिः दाशुषे यजमानाय वसूनि ददासि, अद्य ताभिः सुमनाः उपागहि—याभिः मतिभिः हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय धनानि प्रयच्छसि ताभिः मतिभिः सहिता त्वं शोभनमना भूत्वा उपागच्छ (yābhiḥ dāśuṣe yajamānāya vasūni dadāsi, adya tābhiḥ sumanāḥ upāgahi—yābhiḥ matibhiḥ havirdattavate yajamānāya dhanāni prayacchasi tābhiḥ matibhiḥ sahitā tvaṃ śobhanamanā bhūtvā upāgaccha) the prayer is made that, since this goddess is of a benevolent mind towards those who perform sacrifice addressed to her, she come to our sacrificial hall, accompanied by the kind intention that brings welfare to the sacrificers who offer oblations to her, in order to bestow wealth. And of सुभगे सहस्रपोषं रराणा—शोभनधने सहस्रसंखातस्य धनस्य पुष्टिं ददती (subhage sahasrapoṣaṃ rarāṇā—śobhanadhane sahasrasaṃkhātasya dhanasya puṣṭiṃ dadatī): since this goddess has abundant wealth she is addressed by the word सुभगे (subhage), and she will bestow on those who serve her the increase (abundance), the prosperity, of wealth numbering thousands; thus the generosity of this goddess is also described.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सिनी॑वालि॒ पृथु॑ष्टुके॒ या दे॒वाना॒मसि॒ स्वसा॑ । जु॒षस्व॑ ह॒व्यमाहु॑तं प्र॒जां दे॑वि दिदिड्डि नः ॥ ६ ॥

sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke yā devānāmasi svasā | juṣasva havyamāhutaṃ prajāṃ devi didiḍḍi naḥ ‖ 6 ‖

p. 189

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 189.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सिनीवालि । पृथुस्तुके । या । देवानां । असि । स्वसा । जुषस्व । हव्यं । आहुतं । प्रजां । देवि । दिदिड्डि । नः ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सिनिवाल्या यागे सिनीवालीत्यादिके द्वे याज्यानुवाक्ये । सूत्रं पूर्व- मुदाहृतं ॥ दृष्टचंद्रामावास्या सिनीवाली । हे सिनीवालि पृथुष्टुके पृथुजघने पृथु- संहते वा या त्वं देवानां स्वसासि स्वयंसंचारिणी भगिनी वा भवसि सा त्वमाहु- तमाभिमुख्येनाग्नौ प्रक्षिप्तं हव्यमस्मदीयं हविर्जुषस्व । सेवस्व । किंच हे देवि सिनीवालि नोऽस्माकं प्रजां पुत्रादिकां दिदिड्डि । उपचिनु अतिसर्जय वा । देही- त्यर्थः ॥ दिह उपचये । लोट छांदसः शपः श्लुः । दिश अतिसर्जन इत्यस्माद्वा ॥

sinivālyā yāge sinīvālītyādike dve yājyānuvākye | sūtraṃ pūrva- mudāhṛtaṃ ‖ dṛṣṭacaṃdrāmāvāsyā sinīvālī | he sinīvāli pṛthuṣṭuke pṛthujaghane pṛthu- saṃhate vā yā tvaṃ devānāṃ svasāsi svayaṃsaṃcāriṇī bhaginī vā bhavasi sā tvamāhu- tamābhimukhyenāgnau prakṣiptaṃ havyamasmadīyaṃ havirjuṣasva | sevasva | kiṃca he devi sinīvāli no 'smākaṃ prajāṃ putrādikāṃ didiḍḍi | upacinu atisarjaya vā | dehī- tyarthaḥ ‖ diha upacaye | loṭa chāṃdasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | diśa atisarjana ityasmādvā ‖

Gist: The Sinīvālī sacrifice uses this and the next Ṛk as yājyā and anuvākyā (the sūtra was cited earlier). Sinīvālī is the new-moon day on which the moon is seen as a thin sliver; O broad-hipped one, sister of the gods, enjoy our oblation and give us offspring. The tail explains didiḍḍi (from दिह (diha) or दिश (diśa)).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

पृथुष्टुके (pṛthuṣṭuke)—having broad hips. सिनीवालि (sinīvāli)—O goddess Sinīvālī. या (yā)—you who. देवानां (devānāṃ)—of the gods. स्वसा असि (svasā asi)—are the sister; such a you. आहुतं (āhutaṃ)—offered (into the fire). हव्यं (havyaṃ)—the oblation. जुषस्व (juṣasva)—partake of. देवि (devi)—O goddess. नः (naḥ)—to us. प्रजां (prajāṃ)—sons and the like. दिदिड्डि (didiḍḍi)—give. (The printed text has "ಎಲೆಲ ದೇವಿಯೇ" for "O goddess"; read as an evident slip for "ಎಲೈ", as printed.)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O goddess Sinīvālī, of broad hips, you who are the sister of the gods, such a you, partake of the oblation we have offered in the fire. O goddess, give us sons and the like.

Printed English translation

Wide-hipped Sinivali, who are the sister of the gods, accept the offered oblation, and grant us, goddess, progeny.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

It has been said earlier (Āśvalāyana-śrauta-sūtra, as printed "ಆ. ೫-೨೦") that in the Sinīvālī sacrifice this Ṛk beginning सिनीवालि (sinīvāli) and the next Ṛk beginning या सुबाहुः (yā subāhuḥ) are to be used as the yājyā and the purorucā/anuvākyā mantras.

p. 190

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 190.

The new-moon day (amāvāsyā) is of two kinds. Of these, the new-moon day on which the moon is seen as a mere sliver is known as Sinīvālī. This very sense is explained by the words "dṛṣṭacandrā amāvāsyā sinīvālī". The deity presiding over this new-moon day is addressed by the word हे सिनीवालि (he sinīvāli). She is described as पृथुष्टके (pṛthuṣṭake) [sic, as printed]—"pṛthujaghane pṛthusaṃhate vā", having a stout lower belly, or a strong bodily frame; and as देवानां स्वसा आसि (devānāṃ svasā āsi)—"svayaṃsaṃcāriṇī bhaginī vā bhavasi", one who moves about at her own will, or the sister of the gods. The Ṛk further wishes that she partake of the oblation offered into the fire ("āhutaṃ haviḥ juṣasva") by the sacrificers in her name; and it prays नः प्रजां दिदिड्डि (naḥ prajāṃ didiḍḍi) that this goddess increase or bestow sons and the like upon us sacrificers who offer shares of oblation in the sacrifices.

If on the day of new moon the moon is seen by itself as a mere sliver, that new-moon day is called by the name Sinīvālī; hence the explanation "dṛṣṭacandrā amāvāsyā sīnivālī" is given here. Yāska says: सिनीवाली कुहूरिति देव पत्न्याविति नैरुक्ताः । अमावास्या इति याज्ञिकाः । या पूर्वा अमावास्या सा सीनीवाली, या उत्तरा सा कुहूरिति विज्ञायते (sinīvālī kuhūriti deva patnyāviti nairuktāḥ | amāvāsyā iti yājñikāḥ | yā pūrvā amāvāsyā sā sīnīvālī, yā uttarā sā kuhūriti vijñāyate) (words as printed). That is: the Nairuktas hold that the two goddesses named Sīnīvālī and Kuhū are wives of gods; the ritualists hold that the time called amāvāsyā is of two kinds, Sīnīvālī and Kuhū (the earlier new-moon day is Sīnīvālī, the later is known as Kuhū). Having set out the two views, the commentator cites the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa passage that teaches this.

Further: सिनीवाली सिनमन्नं भवति सिनाति भूतानि वालं पर्व वृणोतेः तस्मिन्नन्नवती वालिनी वा, वालेनेवास्यामणुत्वाच्चंद्रमाः सेवितव्यो भवति इति वा (sinīvālī sinamannaṃ bhavati sināti bhūtāni vālaṃ parva vṛṇoteḥ tasminnannavatī vālinī vā, vālenevāsyāmaṇutvāccaṃdramāḥ sevitavyo bhavati iti vā) (Nirukta 11-32, as printed). Sina means food, which binds (nourishes) living beings and makes them possessed of food; since the gods desire oblations at the parva (junction) time, Sinīvālī is she who is filled with food—one kind of meaning. Secondly, the word vāla is used in the sense of bāla (a young boy): she is filled with oblations dear to the gods, or is served by the moon, which is minute in form, like a vāla (hair).

Also, citing this very mantra, he explains: सिनीवाली पृथुजघने, स्तुकः स्त्यायतेः संघातः । पृथुकेशस्तुते पृथुष्टुते वा । या त्वं देवानामसि स्वसा । स्वसा सु असा । स्नेषु सीदतीति वा । जुषस्व हव्यमदनं प्रजां च देवि दितुनः (sinīvālī pṛthujaghane, stukaḥ styāyateḥ saṃghātaḥ | pṛthukeśastute pṛthuṣṭute vā | yā tvaṃ devānāmasi svasā | svasā su asā | sneṣu sīdatīti vā | juṣasva havyamadanaṃ prajāṃ ca devi ditunaḥ) (Nirukta 11-34, as printed), and gives the meaning thus.

p. 191

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 191.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

या सु॑बा॒हुः स्वं॑गु॒रिः सु॒षूमा॑ बहु॒सूव॑री । तस्यै॑ वि॒श्वत्नै॑ ह॒विः सि॑नीवा॒लै जु॑होतन ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

या । सुबाहुः । सुअंगुरिः । सुसूमा । बहुसूवरी । तस्यै । विश्वत्स्थलि । हविः । सिनीवालैलि । जुहोतन ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

या सिनीवाली सुबाहुः शोभनबाहुः स्वंगुरिः शोभनांगुलिः सुषूमा सुष्टु प्रसवित्री ॥ षूज् प्राणिप्रसवे । अन्येभोऽपि दृश्यंत इति मनिन् । कृदुत्तर पदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ बहुसूवरी बह्नीनां प्रजानां सवित्री ॥ तेनैव सूत्रेण क्वनिप्स् वनो र चेति जीब्रेफौ । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ तस्यॆ सीनीवालै विश्वत्न्यै । विशां पालयित्र्यै ॥ विभाषा सपूर्वस्येति पत्युर्नकारांतादेशः । आयस्मयादित्वेन भत्वाद्विसो जश्वाभावः । परादिश्चंदसि बहुलमित्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं ॥ हे ऋत्विग्यजमाना हविर्जुहोतन । जुहुत ॥ तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चेति तनबादेशः ॥

Gist: Sinīvālī has beautiful arms and fingers, bears children well and is mother of many, and protects the people; priests and sacrificers, offer the oblation to her. The tail explains suṣūmā, bahusūvarī, viśvatnyai and juhotana.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

या (yā)—she who. सुबाहुः (subāhuḥ)—having excellent arms. स्वंगुरिः (svaṃguriḥ)—having excellent fingers. सुषूमा (suṣūmā)—having borne excellent sons. बहुसूवरी (bahusūvarī)—having many sons. तस्यै (tasyai)—to such a one. विश्वत्नै (viśvatnai)—the protectress of the people. सिनीवाल्यै (sinīvālyai)—to the goddess Sinīvālī. हविः (haviḥ)—oblation. जुहोतन (juhotana)—offer.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O sacrificers, to that goddess Sinīvālī who has excellent arms, excellent fingers, excellent sons and many sons, offer the oblation.

Printed English translation

Offer the oblation to that Sinivali, the protectress of mankind, who has beautiful fingers, who is the parent of many children, and who had numerous childrn [sic].

p. 192

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3, Sūkta 32, p. 192.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

या सुबाहुः स्वंगुरिः सुषूमा बहुसूवरी (yā subāhuḥ svaṃguriḥ suṣūmā bahusūvarī)—सिनीवाली शोभनबाहुः शोभनांगुलिः सुष्टु प्रसवित्रि, बह्नीनां प्रजानां सवित्रि (sinīvālī śobhanabāhuḥ śobhanāṃguliḥ suṣṭu prasavitri, bahnīnāṃ prajānāṃ savitri). This goddess called Sinīvālī has beautiful, excellent arms and fingers; she bears good sons and bears many children. Having thus described this goddess and her power, the commentator says तस्यॆ सिनीवाल्कॆ विश्वत्कृ हवि: जुहोतन (tasyè sinīvālkè viśvatkṛ havi: juhotana) (words as printed)—विशां पालयित्र्यै हवि: जुहुत (viśāṃ pālayitryai havi: juhuta): "Offer oblations to this Sinīvālī goddess, of such power, who protects the people" — the seer of the mantra's exhortation is thus described: priests and sacrificers are to offer oblations to her.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

या गुं॒गूर्या सि॑नीवा॒ली या रा॒का या सर॑स्वती । इं॒द्रा॒णीम॑ह्व ऊ॒तये॑ वरुणा॒नीं स्व॒स्तये॑ ॥ ९ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

या । गुंगूः । या । सिनीवाली । या । ताका [?] । या । सरस्वती . इंद्राणीं । अह्वे ऊतये । वरुणानीं । स्वस्तये ॥ ८ ॥

yā | guṃgūḥ | yā | sinīvālī | yā | tākā [?] | yā | sarasvatī . iṃdrāṇīṃ | ahve ūtaye | varuṇānīṃ | svastaye ‖ 8 ‖

(In the supplied text the Saṃhitā ends with the Ṛk number "९" and the Pada with "८"; the Pada's third word reads ताका (tākā) where the Saṃhitā has राका (rākā) [?]; both as supplied.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अत्र गुंगूशब्देन राकासिनीवाल्ल्योः साहचर्यात्कुहूरुच्यते । > या गुंगूः कुहूस्तामह्वे । आह्वयामि । एवमुत्तरत्रापि योज्यं । इंद्राणीमिंद्रस्य पत्निमूतये रक्षणार्थमह्वे : आह्वयामि । तथा वरुणानीं वरुणस्य पत्निं स्वस्तयेऽविनाशायाह्वयामि ॥ इंद्रवरुणेत्यादिना जीष् आनुगागमश्च ॥

Gist: here the word guṅgū, because of its association with Rākā and Sinīvālī, means Kuhū; the Ṛk invokes each of these goddesses, Indrāṇī for protection and Varuṇānī for welfare. The tail notes the feminine suffix īṣ and the ānuk augment in indrāṇī, varuṇānī.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

या (yā) (yā)—who; गुंगूः (guṃgūḥ)—the goddess Kuhū; या (yā)—who; सिनीवाली (sinīvālī)—Sinīvālī; या (yā)—who; राका (rākā)—Rākā; या (yā)—who; सरस्वती (sarasvatī)—Sarasvatī: she who is famed under these names. अह्वे (ahve)—I call. इंद्राणीं (iṃdrāṇīṃ)—Indra's wife; ऊतये (ūtaye)—I call her for protection. वरुणानीं (varuṇānīṃ)—Varuṇa's wife; स्वत्तये (svattaye) [sic, as printed]—I call her so that welfare may come about.

p. 193

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 15, p. 193.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

I call that goddess who is famed as Kuhū, as Sinīvālī, as Rākā and as Sarasvatī. I call Indrāṇī for protection and Varuṇānī for welfare.

Printed English translation

I invoke her who is Gangu, who is Sinivali, who is Raka, who is Saraswati : (I invoke) Indrani for protection, Varunani for welfare.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Here the goddess Kuhū is meant by the word गुंगूः (guṃgūḥ). Since Rākā and Sinīvālī were described in the preceding Ṛks, the commentator explains the word guṅgū here as Kuhū (that is, the new-moon day on which the moon is not seen). The Nirukta-writer says कूहूर्गूहतेः क्वा भूदिति वा क्व सती हूयत इति वा, क्वाहुतं जुहोतीति वा (kūhūrgūhateḥ kvā bhūditi vā kva satī hūyata iti vā, kvāhutaṃ juhotīti vā) (Nir. 11-34), and does not explain the word (guṅgū) formed from the root गुहू (guhū) (guhū), "to cover, to veil". The word kuhū itself is derived from the root gūh; and in three ways the form of the word kuhū is explained: "Where was she? Where is she invoked? Where does one offer the oblation?"—that is, "Where is this goddess? Where is she called? Where is the offering made?" The passage describes that the sacrificers invoke the goddess Kuhū, the goddess Sinīvālī, and the goddesses Rākā, Sarasvatī, Indrāṇī and Varuṇānī, for the sake of स्वस्तये अविनाशाय (svastaye avināśāya) (svastaye avināśāya), that welfare may come to themselves.

इंद्राणीं (iṃdrāṇīṃ)—इंद्रस्य पत्निं (iṃdrasya patniṃ). The Nirukta-writer has commented इंद्राणी इंद्रस्य पत्नि (iṃdrāṇī iṃdrasya patni) (Nir. 10-39). वरुणानीं (varuṇānīṃ)—वरुणस्य पत्निं (varuṇasya patniṃ). Yāska, in explaining the Ṛk उत ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्नीरिंद्राण्य १ ग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यंतु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनां (uta gnā vyaṃtu devapatnīriṃdrāṇya 1 gnāyyaśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyaṃtu devīrya ṛturjanīnāṃ) (Ma. Saṃ. 5-46-8, words as printed), says: इंद्राणींद्रस्य पत्नि, अग्नाया अग्नेःपत्नि, अश्विनी अश्वनोः पत्नि, रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि, वरुणानी वरुणस्य पत्नि (iṃdrāṇīṃdrasya patni, agnāyā agneḥpatni, aśvinī aśvanoḥ patni, rodasī rudrasya patni, varuṇānī varuṇasya patni) (Nir. 12-46): Indrāṇī is Indra's wife, Agnāyī Agni's wife, Aśvinī the Aśvins' wife, Rodasī Rudra's wife, Varuṇānī Varuṇa's wife.

p. 194

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 4, Sūkta 33, p. 194.

Sūkta 33 (Maṇḍala 2)

The thirty-third sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

चतुर्थेऽनुवाक एकादश सूक्तानि । तत्र ते पितरिति पंचदशर्चं प्रथमं

Gist: the first of the eleven sūktas of Anuvāka 4, of fifteen ṛks, of the Gṛtsamada seer, for Rudra, in triṣṭubh; the Anukramaṇī, the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra (4-8-23), the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (3-8) and Śaunaka are quoted for the application.

Anuvāda (Kannada). There are eleven sūktas in the fourth anuvāka of the second maṇḍala. Of them this sūkta beginning आ ते पितर्मरुतां (ā te pitarmarutāṃ) is the first. It has fifteen ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada; Rudra is the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. What is said in the Anukramaṇikā—आ ते पंचोना रौद्रमिति (ā te paṃconā raudramiti)—is explained: in the Rudra sacrifices beginning with the one named Śūlagava the western-quarter deity is to be worshipped with this sūkta, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra sūtra कद्रुद्रायेमा रुद्राया ते पितरिमा रुद्राय स्थिरधन्वन इति सर्वरुद्रयज्ञेषु दिशामुपस्थानं (kadrudrāyemā rudrāyā te pitarimā rudrāya sthiradhanvana iti sarvarudrayajñeṣu diśāmupasthānaṃ) (Gṛ. Sū. 4-8-23). In the animal sacrifice to Rudra, when the oblation is offered, the Ṛk आ ते पितः (ā te pitaḥ) is to be recited as the anuvākyā mantra, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra sūtra आ ते पितर्मरुतां सुम्मनेतु प्रबभ्रवे वृषभाय .श्वितीच इति तिस्रः (ā te pitarmarutāṃ summanetu prababhrave vṛṣabhāya .śvitīca iti tisraḥ) (Ā. 3-8). And on the application of this sūkta the sage Śaunaka says in the book Ṛgvidhāna: चतुर्दशीमुपोष्यकां कृष्णस्य जुहुयाच्चरुं । आतेसूक्तेन रौद्रेण प्रत्यृचं वाग्यतः शुचिः ॥ पूर्वमाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वाथोपस्थाय च शंकरं । हविःशेषेण वर्तेतैकांतरमतंद्रितः ॥ पूर्णमासे जयेन्मृत्युं रोगैश्च परिमुच्यते ॥ (caturdaśīmupoṣyakāṃ kṛṣṇasya juhuyāccaruṃ | ātesūktena raudreṇa pratyṛcaṃ vāgyataḥ śuciḥ ‖ pūrvamājyāhutīrhutvāthopasthāya ca śaṃkaraṃ | haviḥśeṣeṇa vartetaikāṃtaramataṃdritaḥ ‖ pūrṇamāse jayenmṛtyuṃ rogaiśca parimucyate ‖) (Ṛgvidhāna 1-30). That is: on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, fasting, self-controlled and pure, one is to recite each Ṛk of this Rudra sūkta, and having cooked the caru ... [the sentence continues on the next page].

p. 195

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 195.

[Continuing the Anuvāda from p. 194:] ... and having cooked the caru, one is to offer the oblation with ghee. After the oblation, the deity Rudra is to be approached (upasthāna). Then on that day only the remnant of the oblation is to be eaten, in solitude, without harbouring any anxiety; no other food is to be taken. If one observes this from the fourteenth day onwards for a month, one is said to be freed from untimely death and disease and to live happily.

Sūkta 33 — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 16, 17, 18. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deity: Rudra. Metre: triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

आ ते॑ पितर्मरुतां सु॒म्ममे॑तु॒ मा नः॒ सूर्य॑स्य सं॒दृशो॑- युयोथाः । अ॒भि नो॑ वी॒रो अर्व॑ति क्षमेत॒ प जा॑येमहि रुद्र प्र॒जाभिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आ । ते । पितः । मरुतां । सुम्मं । एतु । मानः । नः । सूर्यस्य । संदृशः । युयोथाः । अभि । नः । वीरः । अर्वति । क्षमेत । प्र । जायेमहि । रुद्र । प्रजाभिः ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतां पितः मरुत्संज्ञानां देवानामुत्पादक रुद्र ॥ परमपि छंदसीति षष्ठ्यंतस्य पूर्वामंत्रितांगवद्भावात्सर्वानुदात्तत्वं ॥ ते त्वदीयमस्मभ्यं दातव्यं सुम्मं सुखमैतु । आगच्छतु । रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वमिदं पित्रे मरुतामाख्या- यिकामुखेनावादिष्ट । ऋग्वे. १-११४-६. । तथा त्वं नोऽस्मान् सूर्यस्य संदृशः संदर्शनान्मा युयोथाः । मा पृथक्कार्षिः ॥ यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः । लङ्ग छांदसः शपः श्लुः । छंदस्युभयथेत्यार्थधातुकत्वेन जित्वाभावाद्गुणः ॥ अर्वति

he marutāṃ pitaḥ marutsaṃjñānāṃ devānāmutpādaka rudra ‖ paramapi chaṃdasīti ṣaṣṭhyaṃtasya pūrvāmaṃtritāṃgavadbhāvātsarvānudāttatvaṃ ‖ te tvadīyamasmabhyaṃ dātavyaṃ summaṃ sukhamaitu | āgacchatu | rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvamidaṃ pitre marutāmākhyā- yikāmukhenāvādiṣṭa | ṛgve. 1-114-6. | tathā tvaṃ no 'smān sūryasya saṃdṛśaḥ saṃdarśanānmā yuyothāḥ | mā pṛthakkārṣiḥ ‖ yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ | laṅga chāṃdasaḥ śapaḥ śluḥ | chaṃdasyubhayathetyārthadhātukatvena jitvābhāvādguṇaḥ ‖ arvati

p. 196

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 3 [sic, as printed; Anuvāka 4], Sūkta 33, p. 196.

शत्रु । भ्रातृव्यो वा अर्वेति श्रुतेः । नोऽस्माकं वीरो वीर्यवान् पुत्रादिरभिक्ष- मेत । अभिभवतु । यद्वा वीरस्यं नोऽस्मानभिक्षमेथाः । अस्मान् कृतापराधानभि- क्षमस्व । हे रुद्र प्रजाभिः पुत्रपौत्रादिभिः प्रजायेमहि । प्रभूताः स्याम ॥

Gist: O Rudra, father of the Maruts, may your happiness come to us; do not separate us from the sight of the sun; may our brave son overcome the enemy (or: do you forgive our offences); may we increase with progeny. The tail treats yuyothāḥ, arvati and abhikṣameta.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मारुतां पितः (mārutāṃ pitaḥ)—O Rudra, the father of the Maruts. ते (te)—from you to be obtained. सुम्मं (summaṃ)—happiness. आ एतु (ā etu)—may it come and reach us. नः (naḥ)—us. सूरस्य (sūrasya) [sic, as supplied]—of the sun. संदृशः (saṃdṛśaḥ)—from the sight. मा युयोथाः (mā yuyothāḥ)—do not separate (do not take his light away from us). अर्वति (arvati)—with the enemy (while fighting). नः (naḥ)—our. वीरः (vīraḥ)—brave son. अभिक्षमेत (abhikṣameta)—may he obtain the power to defeat him. रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra. प्रजाभिः (prajābhiḥ)—with sons, grandsons and so on. प्र जायेमहि (pra jāyemahi)—cause us to increase.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, father of the Maruts, may the happiness that is to be had from you come and reach us. Do not separate us from the sight of the sun and keep us in darkness. May our brave son, fighting the enemy, obtain the power to defeat him. O Rudra, cause our line to prosper through sons, grandsons and the rest.

Printed English translation

Father of the Maruts, may your felicity extend to us : exclude us not from the sight of the sun : (grant that) our valiant (descendants) may overcome (these) foes, and that we may be multiplied, Rudra, by (our) progeny.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुद्र (rudra)—Sāyaṇa has explained the word rudra in six ways. The word rudra is formed from the root रुद् (rud) with the causative suffix. Yāska: रुद्रो रौतीति सतः रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा रोदयतेर्वा (rudro rautīti sataḥ rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā rodayatervā). Rudra means रौति (rauti)—he who makes a sound, like the thunder of a cloud; रोरूयमाणो द्रवति (rorūyamāṇo dravati)—he who runs in the midst of the cloud making a noise; रोदयतेर्वा (rodayatervā)—he who defeats enemies and makes them weep: thus the meaning is explained. Further, following the history well known in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad [as printed], or following the Maitrāyaṇīya and third-śākhā text, यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रत्वं (yadarudat tadrudratvaṃ) ("because he wept, that is Rudra-hood": when his father Prajāpati was struck by arrows, he saw him, was distressed and wept) and यदरोदीत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वम् (yadarodīt tadrudrasya rudratvam)—because he wept, he is named Rudra (Ni. 10-7): thus the derivation of the word rudra is given.

p. 197

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 197.

Sāyaṇa's explanation of the word rudra is different from this. He is rudra either because at the time of dissolution he makes all weep; or because he destroys the sorrow called saṃsāra; or because he is taught by the Upaniṣads, which are of the nature of sound; or because he teaches self-knowledge to the worshippers of self-knowledge; or because he destroys ignorance, which covers knowledge as thick darkness covers light. Thus, by showing the differences of meaning arising from the sense of the root रुत् (rut), the meaning of the word rudra is explained. And in accordance with the history set out in the Aitihāsika view, the meaning of the word rudra, formed from the root रुदिल् अश्रुविमोचने (rudil aśruvimocane) ("to shed tears"), is explained by citing the Vedic text सोऽरोदिद्यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (so 'rodidyadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvaṃ) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-1). From this the greatness of Rudra and his compassion towards living beings become evident.

मरुतां पितः रुद्र ते सुम्नं आ एतु (marutāṃ pitaḥ rudra te sumnaṃ ā etu)—मरुत्संज्ञानां देवानामुत्पादक रुद्र त्वदीयमस्मभ्यं दातव्यं सुखं आगच्छतु (marutsaṃjñānāṃ devānāmutpādaka rudra tvadīyamasmabhyaṃ dātavyaṃ sukhaṃ āgacchatu) (Sāyaṇa's gloss: "O Rudra, begetter of the gods called Maruts, may your happiness, to be given to us, come"). Yāska has explained the word marutaḥ as मितराविणो वा, मितरोचिनो वा, महत् द्रवंतीति वा (mitarāviṇo vā, mitarocino vā, mahat dravaṃtīti vā) (Ni. 11-14) [as printed]; and having read the word rudra among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19) [as printed] and commented रुद्रो रौतीति सतः, रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति वा. रोदयतीर्वा (rudro rautīti sataḥ, rorūyamāṇo dravatīti vā. rodayatīrvā), he has cited the Kāṭhaka text यदरुदत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (yadarudat tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ) and the Maitrāyaṇīya-śākhā text यदरोदीत् तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं (yadarodīt tadrudrasya rudratvaṃ) (Ni. 10-7). Sāyaṇa, explaining that the Marut deities are Rudra's sons, says रुद्रस्य च मरुतां पितृत्वं “ इदं पित्रॆ मरुतां ” (ऋ. सं. १-११४-६) इत्यत्र आख्यायिकामुखीनावादिष्म (rudrasya ca marutāṃ pitṛtvaṃ “ idaṃ pitrè marutāṃ ” (ṛ. saṃ. 1-114-6) ityatra ākhyāyikāmukhīnāvādiṣma) [as supplied; the bhāṣya above reads -mukhenāvādiṣṭa]: in explaining the sūkta इदं पित्रॆ मरुतां (idaṃ pitrè marutāṃ) he has described, by way of a narrative, Rudra as the begetter of the Maruts. The wish is that the happiness granted by Rudra, begetter of the Marut deities, may come to us, the sacrificers.

नः सूर्यस्य संदृशः मा युयोथाः (naḥ sūryasya saṃdṛśaḥ mā yuyothāḥ)—अस्मान् सूर्यस्य संदर्शनात् मा पृथक्कार्षिः (asmān sūryasya saṃdarśanāt mā pṛthakkārṣiḥ). The wish is that the god Rudra may protect us, the sacrificers, so that the light of the sun is not lost to us; and, in नः वीरः अर्वति अभिक्षमेत (naḥ vīraḥ arvati abhikṣameta), that Rudra may grant our sons and others the strength to overcome the enemy; or, यद्वा वीरस्त्वं नो अस्मानभिक्षमेथाः अस्मान् कृतापराधानभि क्षमस्व (yadvā vīrastvaṃ no asmānabhikṣamethāḥ asmān kṛtāparādhānabhi kṣamasva), that the heroic Rudra may forgive us our offences; and, प्रजाभिः प्रजायेमहि (prajābhiḥ prajāyemahi), that we sacrificers may prosper through sons, grandsons and the rest.

p. 198

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 198.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वाद॑त्तेभी रुद्र॒ शंत॑मेभिः श॒तं हिमा॑ अतीय भेष॒जेभिः॑ । व्य१॒॑गस्मद्वेषो॑ वित॒रं व्यंहो॒ व्यमी॑वाश्चातयस्वा॒ विषू॑चीः ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

त्वादत्तेभिः । रुद्र । शंतमेभिः । शतं । हिमाः । अशीय । भेषजेभिः । वि । अस्मत् । द्वेषः । वितरं । वि । अंहः । वि । अमीवाः । चातयस्व । विषूचीः ॥ २॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे रुद्र त्वादत्तेभिस्त्वया दत्तैः शंतमेभिरतिशयेन सुखकरैर्भेषजेभिर्भे षजैरौषधैः शतं हिमाः शतं हेमंतान् शतं संवत्सरानशीय । व्याप्नुयां ॥ अश्नोतेर्लिजि छांदसो विकरणस्य लुक् ॥ अपि च अस्मदस्मत्तो द्वेषो द्वेष्टन् विचातयस्व । विनाशय । तथांहः पापं वितरमत्यंतं विचातयस्व । अमीना रोगा- न्विषूचीर्विषु नानांचंतीः कृत्स्नशरीरव्यापकान् रोगान्विचातयस्व । अस्मत्तः पृथक्कृत्य विनाशय ॥

Gist: O Rudra, may I live a hundred years through the soothing medicines given by you; drive away our haters, sin, and the diseases that spread through the whole body. The tail treats aśīya (loss of the vikaraṇa) and vi-cātayasva.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra. त्वादत्तेभिः (tvādattebhiḥ)—by those given by you, शंतमेभिः (śaṃtamebhiḥ)—and conducive to happiness, भेषजेभिः (bheṣajebhiḥ)—from the herbs. शतं हिमाः (śataṃ himāḥ)—a hundred years अशीय (aśīya)—may I attain in full. अस्मत् (asmat)—from us, द्वेषः (dveṣaḥ)—our enemies, वि चातयस्व (vi cātayasva)—destroy completely. अंहः (aṃhaḥ)—sin, वितरं वि (vitaraṃ vi)—(destroy) utterly. विषूचीः (viṣūcīḥ)—spreading through the body in many ways, अमीवाः वि (amīvāḥ vi)—the diseases (destroy).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, nourished by the use of the herbs given by you and conducive to happiness, may I live fully a hundred years. Destroy completely our enemies, sin, and the diseases that spread in many ways through the body.

p. 199

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā [as printed मग्वेदसंहिता (magvedasaṃhitā)], Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 199.

Printed English translation

Nourished by the sanatory vegetables which are bestowed by you, may I live a hundred winters: extirpate my enemies, my exceeding sin, and my manifold infirmities.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Rudra, the sacrificer expresses the wish that, by the medicines given by Rudra, शंतमेभिः भेषजेभिः (śaṃtamebhiḥ bheṣajebhiḥ), that is, abundantly happiness-giving, he may live शतं हिर्मा अशीय (śataṃ hirmā aśīya) [as supplied; hima], many years, happily; and, in अस्मत् द्वेषः विचातयस्व (asmat dveṣaḥ vicātayasva), that Rudra may destroy those who hate us, the sacrificers. And in अंहः वितर (aṃhaḥ vitara)—पापं अत्यंतं वि चातयस्व (pāpaṃ atyaṃtaṃ vi cātayasva)—he prays that Rudra may destroy our sins. विषूचीः (viṣūcīḥ)—विषु नाना अंचतीः कृत्स्नशरीरव्यापर्का (viṣu nānā aṃcatīḥ kṛtsnaśarīravyāparkā) [as supplied; -vyāpakān]: explaining the word विसूची (visūcī) [as supplied] as diseases that pervade the whole body in many ways, the sacrificers pray to the god Rudra that such diseases may be destroyed so that they do not befall the sacrificers.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

श्रेष्ठो॑ जा॒तस्य॑ रुद्र श्रि॒यासि॑ त॒वस्त॑मस्त॒वसां॑ वज्रबाहो । षर्षि॑ णः पा॒रमंह॑सः स्व॒स्ति विश्वा॑ अ॒भी॑ती॒ रप॑सो युयोधि ॥ ३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

श्रेष्ठः । जातस्य । रुद्र । श्रिया । असि । तवःतमः । तवसां । वज्रबाहो इति वज्रबाहो । पर्षि । नः । पारं । अ०हसः । स्वस्ति । विश्वाः । अभिइतीः । रपसः । युयोधि ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे रुद्र जातस्योत्पन्नस्य सर्वस्य जगतो मध्ये श्रियैश्वर्येण श्रेष्ठः प्रशस्यतमोऽसि । भवसि । तथा हे वज्रबाहो आयुधहस्त रुद्र तवसां प्रवृद्धानां

he rudra jātasyotpannasya sarvasya jagato madhye śriyaiśvaryeṇa śreṣṭhaḥ praśasyatamo 'si | bhavasi | tathā he vajrabāho āyudhahasta rudra tavasāṃ pravṛddhānāṃ

p. 200

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 200.

मध्ये तवस्तमोऽतिशयेन प्रवृद्दोऽसि । स त्वं नोऽस्मानंहसः पापस्य पारं तीरं स्वस्ति क्षेमेण पर्षि । पारय । तथा रपसः पापस्य विश्वाः सर्वा अभीतीरभिगमनानि युयोधि । पृथक्कुरु ॥ यौतेश्छांदसः शपः श्लुः । वा छंदसीत्यपित्त्वस्य विकल्पनात् जित्वाभावेऽजितश्चेति हेर्धिः ॥

Gist: O Rudra, you are the best of all born beings in glory and the mightiest of the mighty; carry us across the far shore of sin safely and keep off all approaches of sin. The tail treats yuyodhi.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra. जातस्य (jātasya)—of the whole created world, श्रिया (śriyā)—in splendour, श्रेष्ठः (śreṣṭhaḥ)—you are supreme. वज्रबाहो (vajrabāho)—O Rudra, holding the thunderbolt. तवसा (tavasā) [as supplied; Saṃhitā tavasām]—among the mighty तवस्तमः (tavastamaḥ)—you are the most powerful. नः (naḥ)—us, अंहसः (aṃhasaḥ)—of sin पारं (pāraṃ)—to the end (bring), स्वस्ति (svasti)—safely पर्षि (parṣi)—carry (us) across it. रपसः (rapasaḥ)—of sin, विश्वाः (viśvāḥ)—all अभीतीः (abhītīḥ)—blows, युयोधि (yuyodhi)—ward off.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, among all created beings you are supreme by your glory. O Rudra, holding the thunderbolt as weapon, among the mighty you are the mightiest. Bring us to the end of sin and carry us safely across it. Ward off the blows of every kind of sin.

Printed English translation

You, Rudra, are the chiefest of beings in glory : you, wielder of the thunderbolt, are the mightiest of the mighty : do you waft us in the safety over (the ocean) of sin : repel all the assaults of iniquity.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)
