Addressing Rudra, the commentary describes him, in जातस्य श्रिया श्रेष्ठः (jātasya śriyā śreṣṭhaḥ)—उत्पन्नस्य सर्वस्य जगतः मध्ये ऐश्वर्येण प्रशस्यतमः (utpannasya sarvasya jagataḥ madhye aiśvaryeṇa praśasyatamaḥ)—as the most praiseworthy of all, in the created world, by his power in the form of lordship over it.

वज्रबाहो तवसां तवस्तमः (vajrabāho tavasāṃ tavastamaḥ)—आयुधहस्त रुद्र प्रवृद्धानां मध्यॆ अतिशयेन प्रवृद्योसि (āyudhahasta rudra pravṛddhānāṃ madhyè atiśayena pravṛdyosi) [as supplied; -vṛddho 'si]. Explaining the word वज्र (vajra) as "weapon", it describes Rudra as bearing the weapon in his hand and as endowed with greatness exceeding that of all the great. The prayer is that this god may release the sacrificers from the sins each has committed and grant welfare; by the sentence अंधसः पारं स्वस्ति पर्षि (aṃdhasaḥ pāraṃ svasti parṣi) [as supplied; the ṛk has aṃhasaḥ] that he may remove sins committed earlier and bring about welfare; and, in रपसः विश्वाः अभीतीः युयोधि (rapasaḥ viśvāḥ abhītīḥ yuyodhi)—पापस्य (pāpasya) (continued on the next page)

p. 201

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16, p. 201.

(Continued:) सर्वाः अभिगमनानि पृथक्कुरु (sarvāḥ abhigamanāni pṛthakkuru)—that Rudra may keep us separate from contact with all the kinds of sin that may befall the sacrificers in future, that is, may destroy sins; thus the sacrificers' prayer is described.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मा त्वा॑ रुद्र चुक्रुधामा॒ नमो॑भि॒र्मा दुष्टु॑ती वृषभ॒ मा॑ सहू॑ती । उन्नो॑ वी॒रा अ॑र्पय भेष॒जेभि॑र्भि॒षक्त॑मं त्वा भि॒षजां॑ शृणोमि ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मा । त्वा । रुद्र । चुक्रुधाम । नमभिः । मा । दुःस्तुती । वृषभ । मा । सहूती । उत् । नः । वीरान् । अर्पय । भेषजेभिः । भिषक्तमं । त्वा । भिषजां । शृणोमि ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे रुद्र त्वा त्वां नमोभिरयथाक्रियमाणैर्नमस्कारैर्हविर्भिर्वा मा चुक्रुधाम । मा क्रोधयाम । क्रुद्धं मा कार्ष्म ॥ क्रुद्ध कोपे । अस्माण्ण्यंता- ल्लुजि चजि रूपं ॥ हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षितर्दुष्टुती दुःस्तुत्याशोभनया स्तुत्या मा चुक्रुधामेत्येव । तथा सहूती सहूत्या विसदृशैरन्यर्दॆवैः सहाह्वानेन मा क्रोधयाम । श्रेष्ठो हि स्वस्मान्न्यूनेन सहाह्वाने क्रुद्धो भवति । स त्वं नोऽस्माकं वीरान् पुत्रान्वेषजेभिस्त्वदीयैर्भेषजैरौषधैरुदर्पय । उत्कृष्टं संयोजय । हे रुद्र त्वा त्वां भिषजां चिकित्साभिज्ञानां मध्यॆ भिषक्तममतिशयेन भैषज्यस्य कर्तारं शृणोमि । प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक् । वा. सं. १६-५. । इति च मंत्रांतरेpप्युक्तं ॥

Gist: O Rudra, may we not anger you by faulty homage, bad praise, or by invoking other gods along with you; make our sons thrive with your medicines; I hear you are the best of physicians.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra. त्वा (tvā)—you, नमोभिः (namobhiḥ)—with (defective) acts of worship, मा चुक्रुधाम (mā cukrudhāma)—we shall not make angry. वृषभ (vṛṣabha)—O Rudra, who showers desired objects. दुष्टुती (duṣṭutī)—with inauspicious praises, मा (mā)—we shall not make (you) angry.

p. 202

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 202.

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 4 continued:) सहूती (sahūtī)—by invoking, along with you, other deities unlike you, and worshipping them. मा (mā)—(we shall) not (cause) you anger. नः (naḥ)—our. वीरान् (vīrān)—heroic sons. भेषजेभिः (bheṣajebhiḥ)—with your medicines. उत् अर्पय (ut arpaya)—cause (them) to be united (with them). त्वा (tvā)—you. भिषजां (bhiṣajāṃ)—among physicians [as supplied: "ವೈದ್ಯರಲ್ಲಿಲ್ಲಾ"; the Bhāvārtha has "ವೈದ್ಯರೆಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಾ", among all physicians]. भिषक्तमं (bhiṣaktamaṃ)—as the most excellent physician. शृणोमि (śṛṇomi)—I have heard and know.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, giver of what is desired, may we not provoke you to anger by worship that is deficient, by inauspicious praises, or by calling and worshipping other, unlike deities together with you. We could not do so. Make our heroic sons united with your medicines. I have heard and know you to be the most excellent physician among all physicians.

Printed English translation

Let us not provoke you, Rudra, to wrath by our (imperfect) adorations; nor, showerer (of benifits) [sic], by our unworthy praise, nor by our invocation (of other deities); invigorate our sons by your medicinal plants, for I hear that you are a chief physician amongst physicians.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the verb चुक्रुदाम (cukrudāma) is repeated three times and added as the verb to each of the three sentences, and the sense is explained accordingly.

In the first sentence: नमोभिः (namobhiḥ) — आयथाक्रियमाणैः नमस्कारैः हविर्भिर्वा (āyathākriyamāṇaiḥ namaskāraiḥ havirbhirvā): it is said that the sacrificers do not make this god Rudra angry by acts of homage performed without following the order laid down in the śāstra, or by offerings of oblation.

दुष्टतौ—दुःस्तुत्या अशोभनया स्तुत्या (duṣṭatau—duḥstutyā aśobhanayā stutyā) [as supplied; the Ṛk has दुष्टुती (duṣṭutī)]—"not proper", that is: by reciting praises whose sense makes one understand either the might or the qualities of this god otherwise than they are, and thereby preventing this god from giving the sacrificer his wishes as desired, the sacrificers do not act so as to make this god angry; so the sense is described.

सुहूती--सुहूत्या विसदृशैः अन्यैः देवैः सह आह्वानेन मा क्रोधयाम । श्रेष्ठो हि स्वस्मत् न्यूनेन सहाह्वाने न क्रुद्धो भवति । (suhūtī--suhūtyā visadṛśaiḥ anyaiḥ devaiḥ saha āhvānena mā krodhayāma | śreṣṭho hi svasmat nyūnena sahāhvāne na kruddho bhavati |) [as supplied; the Ṛk has सहूती (sahūtī)]. When this god is invoked at the sacrifices, he is not made angry with the sacrificers by being invoked together with other minor deities. If one who is superior in might and qualities is joined with one lower than himself, the impression arises that he has been slighted. Since that would amount to an offence, the sacrificers, knowing the might of this god, act accordingly; so it is described.

p. 203

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 16; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 203.

(Continued:) Since in other mantras this god is declared "प्रथमो दैव्यो भिषक् (prathamo daivyo bhiṣak)" (Tai. Saṃ. 4-1-5-2), "the first divine physician", the sacrificers know him as त्वा भिषजां-चिकित्साभिज्ञानां मध्यॆ अतिशयेन भैषज्यस्य कर्तारं शृणोमि (tvā bhiṣajāṃ-cikitsābhijñānāṃ madhyè atiśayena bhaiṣajyasya kartāraṃ śṛṇomi)—the foremost among the physicians who treat and destroy diseases, whether of the mind or of the body. And for this reason also: नः वीर्रान् भेषजेभिः उत् अर्पय—अस्माकं पुत्रान् त्वदीयैः औषध्यैः उत्कृष्टं संयोजय (naḥ vīrrān bheṣajebhiḥ ut arpaya—asmākaṃ putrān tvadīyaiḥ auṣadhyaiḥ utkṛṣṭaṃ saṃyojaya) [as supplied: वीर्रान् (vīrrān)]. The wish is expressed that this god give proper medicines to the children of us sacrificers and make them excel all others.

Since the performers of sacrifice first invoke all the gods, satisfy them with oblations and the like, and only afterwards invoke this Rudra separately, it is described in this way here that they should not incur this god's wrath.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

हवी॑मभि॒र्हव॑ते॒ यो ह॒विर्भि॒रव॒ स्तोमे॑भी रु॒द्रं दि॑षीय । ऋ॒दू॒दरः॑ सु॒हवो॒ मा नो॑ अ॒स्यै ब॒भ्रुः सु॒शिप्रो॑ रीरधन्म॒नाय्कॆ ॥॑

॥ पदपाठः ॥

हवीमभिः । हवते । यः । हविभिः । अव । स्तोमेभिः । रुद्रं । दिषीय । यदूवरः । सुहवः । मा । नः । अस्यै । बभ्रुः । सुशिप्रः । रीरधत् । मनाय्कॆ ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यो रुद्रो हविर्भिश्चरुपुरोडाशादिभिः सहितैर्हवीमभिराह्वानैः स्तुतिलक्ष- णैर्हवते । आह्वयते स्तूयते ॥ व्यत्ययेन कर्मणि कर्तृप्रत्ययः । बहुलं छंदसीति ह्वयतेः संप्रसारणं ॥ तं रुद्रं स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरवदिषीय ।

yo rudro havirbhiścarupuroḍāśādibhiḥ sahitairhavīmabhirāhvānaiḥ stutilakṣa- ṇairhavate | āhvayate stūyate ‖ vyatyayena karmaṇi kartṛpratyayaḥ | bahulaṃ chaṃdasīti hvayateḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ ‖ taṃ rudraṃ stomebhiḥ stotrairavadiṣīya |

p. 204

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 33, p. 204.

अवखंडयामि । पृथक्करोमि । अपगतक्रोधं करोमीति यावत् ॥ दो अवखं- दने । व्यत्ययेनात्मनेपदं । बहुलं छंदसीतीत्वं ॥ युदूदरः । युदूदरो मृदूदर इति यास्कः । नि. ६ ४. । सुहवः शोभनाह्वानो बभ्रुर्भर्ता सर्वस्य बभ्रुवर्णो वा । सुशिप्रः । शिप्रे हनू नासिके वा । शोभनशिप्रः । एवंगुणविशिष्टः स रुद्रोस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ । हन्मीति मन्यमानाबुद्धिर्मना । तस्यै नोऽस्मान्मा रीरधत् । मा वशं नैषीत् ॥ रथ हिंसासंराद्योः । अस्माण्ण्यंताल्लुज चजु रूपं । रध्यति- र्वशगमन इति यास्कः ॥

Gist: The Rudra who is invoked with oblations and praises I will appease with hymns; may he, soft-bellied, bountiful, tawny and fair-jawed, not give us over to this hostile intent.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यः (yaḥ)—the Rudra who. हविर्भिः (havirbhiḥ)—accompanied by cooked offerings, cakes and the like. हवीमभिः (havīmabhiḥ)—with invocations that are in the form of praise. हवते (havate)—is praised. रुद्रं (rudraṃ)—such a Rudra. स्तोमेभिः (stomebhiḥ)—with hymns. अव दिषीय (ava diṣīya)—I make (him) free from anger and calm of mind. ऋतूदरः (ṛtūdaraḥ) [as supplied; Saṃhitā ऋदूदरः (ṛdūdaraḥ), bhāṣya युदूदरः (yudūdaraḥ)]—one with a soft belly. सुहवः (suhavaḥ)—one with an excellent invocation. बभ्रुः (babhruḥ)—one of tawny colour. सुशिप्रः (suśipraḥ)—one with fine cheeks or nose, that Rudra. अस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ (asyè manāykè)—to this evil mind that wishes us harm. नः (naḥ)—us. मा रीरधत् (mā rīradhat)—may he not bring (us) under its sway.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Rudra who is praised with invocations that are in the form of praise and accompanied by cooked offerings, cakes and the like, such a Rudra I make free from anger and calm of mind by praising him with hymns. May Rudra, who has a soft belly, an excellent invocation, a form of tawny colour and a fine nose, not bring us under the sway of this evil mind that wishes us harm.

Printed English translation

May I pacify by my praises that Rudra, who is worshipped with invocations and oblations; and never may he who is soft-bellied. of a tawny hue, and handsome chin ; who is reverently invoked ; subject us not to that malevolent disposition (that purposes our destruction).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

This Rudra is ऋदूदरः सुहवः बभ्रुः सुशिप्रः (ṛdūdaraḥ suhavaḥ babhruḥ suśipraḥ) — शोभनाह्वानः भर्ता सर्वस्य बभ्रुवर्णो वा शिप्रे हनूनासिके वा सुशिप्रः (śobhanāhvānaḥ bhartā sarvasya babhruvarṇo vā śipre hanūnāsike vā suśipraḥ) — "soft-bellied", that is, of fierce [text breaks off here] (continued on the next page)

p. 205

dress, ornaments and the like, yet he has an intention that produces welfare. Because the invocation of this god is beneficial, he is one of good invocation, the lord of all; or one whose body has a golden-brown lustre; one who has handsome cheeks or a nose; or, describing this god, the sacrificers (say): हविर्भिः हवीमभिः हवते स्तोमेभिः अवदिषीय (havirbhiḥ havīmabhiḥ havate stomebhiḥ avadiṣīya), चरुपुरोडाशादिभिः सहितैः आह्वानैः स्तुतिलक्षणै, स्त्युयते स्तोत्रैः अवखंडयामि—पृथक्करोमि (carupuroḍāśādibhiḥ sahitaiḥ āhvānaiḥ stutilakṣaṇai, styuyate stotraiḥ avakhaṃḍayāmi—pṛthakkaromi) (as supplied): by the offerings of oblations such as cooked offerings and cakes, and by invocations in the form of praise, having praised and gratified (him), we so act that no anger arises in this god; and अस्यॆ मनाय्कॆ नः मा रीरधत् (asyè manāykè naḥ mā rīradhat), हन्मीति मन्यमाना बुद्धिमना तस्यॆ अस्मान् मा वशं नैषीत् (hanmīti manyamānā buddhimanā tasyè asmān mā vaśaṃ naiṣīt)—it is prayed that the intention of destroying others, which exists (in him), may not arise towards the sacrificers.

ऋदूदरः (ṛdūdaraḥ): Yāska explains ऋदूदरः सोमो मृदूदरो मृदुरुदरेष्टिति वा (ṛdūdaraḥ somo mṛdūdaro mṛdurudareṣṭiti vā) (Si. 6-4 [as supplied]) as "one with a soft middle part", or "soft in the middle (inside)", and as the Soma (creeper); and he has explained the word शिप्र (śipra) as the cheeks or the nose.

सुशिप्रः (suśipraḥ): Yāska: सुशिप्रमेतेन व्याख्यातं । हनू नासिके वा, हनुः हंतेः । नासिका नसतेः (suśiprametena vyākhyātaṃ | hanū nāsike vā, hanuḥ haṃteḥ | nāsikā nasateḥ) (Ni. 6-17); he has explained the meaning of the word शिप्र as the cheeks or the nose.

बभ्रुः (babhruḥ): In explaining the meaning of the word बभ्रु (babhru), Yāska cites the Ṛk या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा । मन्यॆ नु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च ॥ (yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyastriyugaṃ purā | manyè nu babhrūṇāmahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-1) and explains बभ्रूणां बभ्रुवर्णानां (babhrūṇāṃ babhruvarṇānāṃ) (Ni. 9-29). Durgācārya gives the meaning: ओषधयः स्वभावतः पच्यमानाः सर्वा एव बभ्रुवर्णाः कपिलाः संपद्यंते (oṣadhayaḥ svabhāvataḥ pacyamānāḥ sarvā eva babhruvarṇāḥ kapilāḥ saṃpadyaṃte); that is, the herbs take on a golden-brown colour at the time they generally ripen.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उन्मा॑ ममंद वृष॒भो म॒रुत्वा॒न्त्वक्षी॑यसा॒ वय॑सा॒ नाध॑मानं । घृणी॑व च्छा॒याम॑र॒पा अ॑ती॒या वि॑वासेयं रु॒द्रस्य॑ सु॒म्मं ॥ ६ ॥

unmā mamaṃda vṛṣabho marutvāntvakṣīyasā vayasā nādhamānaṃ | ghṛṇīva cchāyāmarapā atīyā vivāseyaṃ rudrasya summaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

p. 206

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत् । मा । ममंद । वृषभः । मरुत्वान् । त्वक्षीयसा । वयसा । नाधमानं । घृणि इव । छायां। अरपाः । अतीय । आ । विवासेयं । रुद्रस्य । सुम्नं ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

वृषभः कामानां वर्षिता मरुत्वान् मरुद्भिः पुत्रैर्युक्तो रुद्रो नाध मानं याचमानं मामां त्वक्षीयसा दीप्तेन वयसान्नेनोन मंद । उत्कर्षेण तर्पयतु । अपि जाहं फृणीव छायां यथा सूर्यकिरणसंतप्तश्चायां प्रविशति एवं रुद्रस्य सुम्मं सुखमरपा आपापः सन् अशीय । व्याप्प्नुयां । तदर्थं तं रुद्रमाविवासेयं । परिचरेयं ॥ विवासतिः परिचरणकर्मा ॥

Gist: May Rudra, showerer of desires and accompanied by the Maruts, gratify me, a suppliant, with bright food; free from sin I would attain his happiness as one scorched by the sun's rays enters shade. The tail explains vivāsati as a verb of serving.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—the one who showers the desired object; मरुत्वान् (marutvān)—accompanied by the Marut deities; that Rudra; नाधमानं (nādhamānaṃ)—who begs in humility; मा (mā)—me; त्वक्षीयसा (tvakṣīyasā)—with bright; वयसा (vayasā)—with food; उत् ममन्द (ut mamanda)—may he gratify exceedingly; (and may I also) घृणीव (ghṛṇīva)—like one scorched by the heat of the sun; छायां (chāyāṃ)—takes refuge in the shade; रुद्रस्य (rudrasya)—obtainable from Rudra; सुम्मं (summaṃ)—happiness; अरपाः (arapāḥ)—being free from sin; अशीय (aśīya)—may I obtain fully.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Rudra, who showers the desired object and is accompanied by the Marut deities, gratify me, who beg in humility, exceedingly with bright food. May I also, being free from sin, fully obtain the happiness obtainable from Rudra, as one scorched by the heat of the sun takes refuge in the shade.

Printed English translation

May the showerer of benifits [sic], the lord of Maruts, gratify me his suppliant with invigorating food : may I, free from sin, so propitiate Rudra, that I may attain to his felicity, as a man, distressed by heat, (finds relief) in the shade.

p. 207

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वृषभः (vṛṣabhaḥ)—कामानां वर्षिता (kāmānāṃ varṣitā): the quality of the god Rudra is described thus, that he gives desired things to those who take refuge in him. May this Rudra, मरुत्वान् (marutvān), accompanied by his sons the Marut deities, fulfil the prayer of the sacrificers by granting bright food and so produce satisfaction; and फृणीव छायां रुद्रस्य सुम्नं अरसा आशीय—यथा सूर्यकिरणसंतप्तः छायां प्रविशति एवं रुद्रस्य सुखं अपापः व्यापु यां (phṛṇīva chāyāṃ rudrasya sumnaṃ arasā āśīya—yathā sūryakiraṇasaṃtaptaḥ chāyāṃ praviśati evaṃ rudrasya sukhaṃ apāpaḥ vyāpu yāṃ) (as supplied): as one scorched by the sharp heat of the sun takes refuge in the shade, so the sacrificer, free from sins, will obtain the happiness granted by Rudra—thus the sacrificer's blessing is described.

अरपाः (arapāḥ)—अपापः (apāpaḥ): रपोरिप्रमिति पापनामनी भवतः (raporipramiti pāpanāmanī bhavataḥ) (Ni. 4-21): Yāska explains that the two words रपः and रिप्र (rapaḥ, ripra) both denote sin. Here the word अरपाः is explained as one without sin.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

क्व१॒ं॑ स्य ते॑ रुद्र मृळ॒याकु॒र्हस्तो॒ यो अस्ति॑ भेष॒जो जला॑षः । अ॒प॒भ॒र्तान् रप॑सो॒ दैव्य॑सा॒भी नु मा॑ वृषभ चक्षमीथाः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

क्व । स्यः । ते । रुद्र । मृळयाकुः । हस्तः । यः । अस्ति । भेषजः । जलाषः । अपभर्ता । रहसः । दैव्यस्य । अभि । नु । मा । वृषभ । चक्षमीथाः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे रुद्र ते तव मृळयाकुः सुखयिता स्यः स हस्तः क्व कुत्र वर्तते । यो हस्तो भेषजो भैषज्यकृत् जलाषः सर्वेषां सुखकरोऽस्ति । भवति । स हस्तो विद्यत एव । तेन हस्तेन मां रक्षेति भावः । अपि च हे वृषभ कामानां वर्षितः दैव्यस्य देवकृतस्य रपसः पापस्यापभर्तापहर्ता विनाशयिता भूत्वा कृतापराधं मां नु क्षिप्रमभिचक्षमीथाः । अभिक्षमस्व । क्षमूष् सहने । लजि छांदसः शपः श्लुः । बहुलं छंदसीतीडागमः ॥

Gist: Where is that gracious, healing hand of yours, Rudra? With it protect me; showerer of desires, remove the sin caused by the gods and forgive me quickly. The tail explains abhicakṣamīthāḥ.

p. 208

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra. यः (yaḥ)—which hand. भेषजः (bheṣajaḥ)—that destroys disease. जलाषः (jalāṣaḥ)—that gives joy. अस्ति (asti)—is. ते (te)—your. मृळयाकुः (mṛḷayākuḥ)—the comforting. स्यः (syaḥ)—the well-known. हस्तः (hastaḥ)—hand. क्व (kva)—where? वृषभ (vṛṣabha)—O Rudra, showerer of desires. दैव्यस्य (daivyasya)—caused by the gods. रपसः (rapasaḥ)—also the sin. अपभर्ता (apabhartā)—you who have the power to destroy it. मा (mā)—me, the offender. नु (nu)—quickly. अभि चक्षमीथाः (abhi cakṣamīthāḥ)—forgive completely.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, where is that hand of yours, comforting and well known, which destroys disease and gives joy? O Rudra, showerer of desires, you who have the power to destroy even the sin done by the gods and to forgive: forgive me, the offender, quickly and completely.

Printed English translation

Where, Rudra, is your joy-dispensing hand, which is the healer and delighter (of all) : showerer (of benifits) [sic], you are the dispeller of the sins of the gods, quickly have compassion upon me.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुद्र ते मृळयाकुः हस्तः क्व (rudra te mṛḷayākuḥ hastaḥ kva)—Asking where the comforting hand is, the text states the extraordinary quality of the hand: that this hand destroys the disease of all and is comforting to all; and it expresses the wish that Rudra protect the sacrificers with that hand (भेषजः जलाषः भैषज्यकृत् सर्वेषां सुखकरः (bheṣajaḥ jalāṣaḥ bhaiṣajyakṛt sarveṣāṃ sukhakaraḥ); तेन हस्तेन मां रक्ष (tena hastena māṃ rakṣa)).

दैव्यस्य रपसः अपभर्ता मा अभिचक्षमीथाः (daivyasya rapasaḥ apabhartā mā abhicakṣamīthāḥ)—देवकृतस्य पापस्य विनाशयिता भूत्वा कृतापराधं मां अभिक्षमस्व (devakṛtasya pāpasya vināśayitā bhūtvā kṛtāparādhaṃ māṃ abhikṣamasva). It is explained thus: may Rudra destroy the sins that have come upon the sacrificer through contrary conduct towards the gods, and pardon me, the sacrificer who has committed the offence.

जलाषः—सर्वेषां सुखकरः (jalāṣaḥ—sarveṣāṃ sukhakaraḥ). The word जलाष (jalāṣa) is stated by Yāska (Ni. 2-24) among the names of water; here the meaning "comforting" is given.

p. 209

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

प्र ब॒भ्रवे॑ वृष॒भाय॑ श्वि ती॒चे म॒हो म॒हीं सु॑ष्टु॒तिमा॑रयामि । न॒म॒स्या क॑ल्मली॒किनं॒ नमो॑भिर्गृणी॒मसि॑ त्वे॒षं रु॒द्रस्य॒ नाम॑ ॥ ८ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

प्र । बभ्रवे । वृषभाय । श्वितीचे । महः । महीं । सुस्तुतिं । ईरयामि । नमस्य । कल्मलीकिनं । नमःभिः । गृणीमसि । त्वेषं । रुद्रस्य । नाम ॥ ८ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

रुद्रदेवत्ये पशौ वपापुरोडाशहविषां क्रमेण प्र बभ्रव इत्याद्यास्ति स्रो याज्याः । प्र बभ्रवे वृषभाय श्वितीच इति तिस्र आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तात् । आ. ३-८. । इति ॥ बभ्रवे विश्वस्य भर्त्रॆ बभ्रुवर्णाय वा वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रे तद्वत् प्रसह्यकारिणे वा श्चितीचे श्वैत्यमंचते ॥ श्चिता वर्णॆ । औणादिक इन्मत्तयः । श्ति- मंचतीत्यंचतेर्यत्विगित्यादिना क्विन् । चतुर्थैकवचनेच इत्यकारलोपे चाविति दीर्घत्वं । उदात्तनिवृत्तिस्वरेण विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं ॥ एवंगुणविशिष्टाय रुद्राय महो महीं महतोऽपि महतीं सुष्टुतिं शोभनस्तुतिं प्रेरयामि । प्रकर्षे- णोच्चारयामि । हे स्तोतः कल्मलीकिनं । ज्वलतो नामधेयमेतत्। नैघं. १-१७। ज्वलंतं । कलयत्यपगमयति मलमिति कल्मलीकं तेजः । तद्वंतं रुद्रं नमोभि- र्नमस्कारैर्हविर्भिर्वा नमस्य । पूजय । वयं च रुद्रस्य महादेवस्य त्वेषं दीप्तं नाम गृणीमसि ! गृणीमः संकीर्तयामः ॥ गृ शब्दे । क्रैयादिकः । इदंतो मसिः । प्वादीनां ह्रस्वः ॥

Gist: In the animal sacrifice to Rudra, this Ṛk and the next two are the yājyā verses for the vapā, puroḍāśa and oblations in order (Āśv. 3-8). Rudra is called babhru, vṛṣabha, śvitīca; the poet offers him a great praise and bids the worshipper adore the blazing Rudra. The tail treats śvitīca, gṛṇīmasi.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

बभ्रवे (babhrave)—to the one of brown colour; वृषभाय (vṛṣabhāya)—the showerer of desires; श्वितीचे (śvitīce)—the one of white form, to Rudra. महो महीं (maho mahīṃ)—greater than the excellent. सुष्टुतिं (suṣṭutiṃ)—excellent praise. प्र ईरयामि (pra īrayāmi)—I offer with devotion. कल्मलीकिनं (kalmalīkinaṃ)—Rudra, who has the radiance that destroys impurity. नमोभिः (namobhiḥ)—with salutations or with oblations. नमस्य (namasya)—worship! (we also) रुद्रस्य (rudrasya)—of Rudra. त्वेषं (tveṣaṃ)—the radiant power. गृणीमसि नाम (gṛṇīmasi nāma)—we surely praise.

p. 210

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

To Rudra, who is of brown colour, the showerer of desires, and of white form, I offer praise greater than the excellent. Worship with oblations Rudra, who has the radiance that destroys impurity. We also praise the radiant power of Rudra.

Printed English translation

I address infinite and earnest praise to the showerer (of benifits) [sic], the cherisher (of all), the white-complexioned : adore the consumer (of sin), with prostrations: we gloriaify [sic] the illustrious name of Rudra.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In the animal sacrifice related to Rudra, when the vapā, puroḍāśa and oblations are offered, the Ṛk प्र बभ्रवे (pra babhrave) of this sūkta and the two following Ṛks are to be used in order as yājyā mantras; this is stated by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra, प्र बभ्रवे वृषभाय श्वितीच इति तिस्र आ पश्चातान्नासत्या पुरस्तात् (pra babhrave vṛṣabhāya śvitīca iti tisra ā paścātānnāsatyā purastāt) (Āś. 3-8).

बभ्रवे-विश्वस्य भर्त्रे बभ्रुवर्णाय वा (babhrave-viśvasya bhartre babhruvarṇāya vā): Rudra is the lord of the whole world, or he is of brown colour. वृषभाय कामानां वर्षित्रॆ तद्वत्पसह्यकारिणे वा (vṛṣabhāya kāmānāṃ varṣitrè tadvatpasahyakāriṇe vā): he fulfils the wishes of those who serve him, or, like a bull, does his work by force. श्वितीचे—शैत्यमंचते (śvitīce—śaityamaṃcate): he has a pure radiance. Having so described Rudra, the Ṛṣi, seer of the mantra, says that for Rudra possessed of these qualities, महो महीं सुष्टुतिं ईरयामि (maho mahīṃ suṣṭutiṃ īrayāmi), "I shall utter abundantly praise full of greatness."

कल्मलीकिनं रुद्रं नमोभिः नमस्य—ज्वलंतं रुद्रं नमस्कारैः हविर्भिर्वा पूजय (kalmalīkinaṃ rudraṃ namobhiḥ namasya—jvalaṃtaṃ rudraṃ namaskāraiḥ havirbhirvā pūjaya): addressing the sacrificer and the priest who are the praisers, it is said: worship Rudra, who shines with radiance, with oblations and with salutations.

रुद्रस्य तेषं नाम गृणीमसि—महादेवस्य दीप्तं नाम संकीर्तयामः (rudrasya teṣaṃ nāma gṛṇīmasi—mahādevasya dīptaṃ nāma saṃkīrtayāmaḥ): it is explained that we, the seers of the mantra, recite the name, shining with brilliance, of this Mahādeva who is full of greatness beyond all the gods.

कल्मलीकिनं—कलयति अपगमयति मलमिति कल्मलीकं तेजः तद्वंतं (kalmalīkinaṃ—kalayati apagamayati malamiti kalmalīkaṃ tejaḥ tadvaṃtaṃ). Yāska, कल्मलीकिनं (kalmalīkinaṃ) the word, ज्वलतो नामधेयानि (jvalato nāmadheyāni) among the names of ज्वलतः (jvalataḥ) (blazing)

p. 211

Running head: [A. 2 A. 7 V. 17.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 211 (as supplied). The window begins inside the Special Topics of Ṛk 8.

(Ni. 2-28) he has read. Sāyaṇa explains मलं (malaṃ) as "that which destroys sin", explains the word कल्मलीक (kalmalīka) as radiance, and describes कल्मलीकुं (kalmalīkuṃ) as one possessed of radiance.

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स्थि॒रेभि॒रंगैः॑ पुरु॒रूप॑ उ॒ग्रो ब॒भ्रुः शु॒क्रेभिः॑ पिपिशे॒ हिर॑ण्यैः । ईशा॑नाद॒स्य भुव॑नस्य॒ भूरे॒न्वा उ॑ योषद्रु॒दाद॑सु॒र्यं॑ ॥ ९ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

स्थिरेभिः । अंगैः । पुरुरूपः । उग्रः । बभ्रुः । शुक्रेभिः । पिपिशे । हिरण्यैः । ईशानात् । अस्य । भुवनस्य । भूरेः । न । वै । ऊं इति । योषत् । रुद्रात् । असुर्यं ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स्थिरेभिः स्थिरैर्दृढैरंगैरवयवय्यर्युक्तः पुरुरूपोऽष्टमूर्त्यात्मकैर्ब- हुभी रूपैरुपेत उग्र उद्धूर्णस्तेजस्वी बभ्रुर्भर्ता बभ्रुवर्णो वा रुद्रः शुक्रेभिर्दिप्तैर्हिरण्यैहिरण्मय्कॆर्हितरमणीय्कॆर्वालंकारैः पिपिशे ! दीप्यते ॥ पित अवयवे । कर्मणि लिट् ॥ ईशानादीश्वरादस्य भुवनस्य भूतजातस्य भूरेर्भर्तू रुद्रादसुर्यं ॥ असु क्षेपणे । असेरुरन् । आसरः क्षेप्ता । तत्र साधुः ॥ असुर्यं बलं न वा उ योषत् । नैव पृथग्भवति ॥ यौतेर्लॆट्व्यडागमः । सिब्बहुलं लेटीति सिप् ॥

Gist: Rudra, with firm limbs and many (eightfold) forms, fierce and brown, shines with bright golden ornaments; from the lord and sustainer of this world strength is never separate. The tail treats piśe and asuryam.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

स्थिरेभिः (sthirebhiḥ)—firm; अंगैः (aṃgaiḥ)—endowed with limbs; पुरुरूपः (pururūpaḥ)—endowed with many forms; उग्रः (ugraḥ)—possessed of manifest brilliance; बभ्रुः (babhruḥ)—of brown colour: Rudra; शुक्रेभिः (śukrebhiḥ)—resplendent; हिरण्यैः (hiraṇyaiḥ)—golden; with such ornaments; पिपिशे (pipiśe)—he shines; ईशानात् (īśānāt)—from the lord; अस्य भुवनस्य (asya bhuvanasya)—for this whole world; भूरेः (bhūreḥ)—the sustainer; रुद्रात् (rudrāt)—from Rudra; असुरं (asuraṃ) [sic: the Saṃhitā has असुर्यं (asuryaṃ)]—universal power; न वा उ योषत् (na vā u yoṣat)—is not separated at all.

p. 212

Running head: [212 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2 A. 4 Sū. 33] (as supplied).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Rudra, who has firm limbs, is endowed with many forms, has manifest brilliance and is of brown colour, shines with resplendent golden ornaments. From Rudra, the lord, who sustains this whole world, universal power is never separated.

Printed English translation

(Firm) with strong limbs, assuming many forms, fierce, and tawny-coloured, he shines with brilliant golden ornaments : vigour is inseparable from Rudra, the supreme ruler and lord of this world.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Rudra is स्थिरेभिरंगैः (sthirebhiraṃgaiḥ) (दृढैरवयवैर्युक्तः (dṛḍhairavayavairyuktaḥ)): endowed with limbs that are joined with strength and brilliance and are powerful. पुरुरूपः (pururūpaḥ) (अष्टमूर्त्यात्मकैः बहुभिः रूपैः उपेतः (aṣṭamūrtyātmakaiḥ bahubhiḥ rūpaiḥ upetaḥ)): he shines with the eight forms, namely earth, water, sun, moon, fire, wind, space and the yajamāna who performs the sacrifice; and उग्रः (ugraḥ) (उद्गूर्णः तेजस्वी (udgūrṇaḥ tejasvī)): he is filled with strength and brilliance; and बभ्रुः (babhruḥ) (भर्ता बभ्रुवर्णो वा (bhartā babhruvarṇo vā)): he is the overlord of the world, or he is of golden-brown colour. Having so described him, (Sāyaṇa) explains that Rudra शुक्रेभिः हिरण्यैः पिपिशे (śukrebhiḥ hiraṇyaiḥ pipiśe) (दीपैः हितरमणीयैः हिरण्मय्यरलंकारैर्वा दीप्यते (dīpaiḥ hitaramaṇīyaiḥ hiraṇmayyaralaṃkārairvā dīpyate)): adorns himself with golden ornaments that are very bright, beneficial and charming.

ईश्वरात् रुद्रात् असुर्यं न वा उ योषत् (īśvarāt rudrāt asuryaṃ na vā u yoṣat)—अस्य भूतजातस्य भर्तुः (asya bhūtajātasya bhartuḥ) ईश्वरात् असुर्यं बलं नैव पृथक् भवति (īśvarāt asuryaṃ balaṃ naiva pṛthak bhavati): it is said that no other thing is mightier than this Rudra, the lord of all beings and master of everything.

असुर्यं (asuryaṃ)—the suffix उरन् (uran) is added to the root असु क्षेपणे (asu kṣepaṇe) and the word असुर (asura) results; by असुरः क्षेप्ता (asuraḥ kṣeptā) the word असुर (asura) means "one who throws". By the sūtra तत्र साधुः (tatra sādhuḥ) the suffix य (ya) is added, giving असुर्य (asurya). Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as "strength".

p. 213

Running head: [A. 2 A. 7 V. 17.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, p. 213 (as supplied).

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अर्ह॑न्बिभर्षि॒ साय॑कानि॒ धन्वाह॑न्नि॒ष्कं य॑ज॒तं वि॒श्वरू॑पं । अर्प॑न्नि॒दं द॑यसे॒ विश्व॒मभ्वं॒ न वा ओजी॑यो रुद्र॒ त्वद॑स्ति ॥ १० ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अर्हन् । बिभर्षि । सायकानि । धन्व । अर्हन् । निष्कं । यजतं । विश्वरूपं । अर्हन् । इदं । दयसे । विश्वं । अभ्वं । न । वै । ओजीयः । रुद्र । त्वत् । अस्ति ॥ १० ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे रुद्र त्वमर्हन् अर्हो योग्य एव सन् सायकानि शरान् धन्व धनुश्च बिभर्षि । धारयसि । तथार्हन्नेव यजतं यजनीयं पूजनीयं विश्वरूपं बहुविधरूपयुक्तं निष्कं हारं बभर्षि । तथार्हन्नेवेदं विश्वं सर्वमभ्वं । महन्नामृतत् । अतिविस्तृतं जगद्दयसे । रक्षिसि । देज् रक्षणे । हे रुद्र त्वत् त्वत्तोऽन्यत् किंचिदोजीय ओजस्वितरं बलवत्तरं न वा अस्ति । न खलु विद्यते । अतस्त्वमेवोक्तव्यापारेषु योज्य इत्यर्थः ॥ ओजःशब्दान्मत्वर्तियो विनिः । ततः अतिशायनिक इष्टन् । विन्मत्तोर्लुक् । टेरिति टिलोपः ॥

Gist: O Rudra, though worthy of worship you bear arrows, bow and a many-formed necklace, and protect this vast universe; nothing is mightier than you. The tail treats ojīyaḥ.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra; अर्हन् (arhan)—you who are worthy of worship; सायकानि (sāyakāni)—arrows; धन्व (dhanva)—and bow; बिभर्षि (bibharṣi)—you bear; अर्हन् (arhan)—being worthy of worship; यजतं (yajataṃ)—worthy of worship; विश्वरूपं (viśvarūpaṃ)—of many forms; निष्कं (niṣkaṃ)—a necklace (you wear); अर्हन् (arhan)—being worthy of praise; इदं विश्वं (idaṃ viśvaṃ)—this whole; अभ्वं (abhvaṃ)—and great world; दयसे (dayase)—you protect; रुद्र (rudra)—O Rudra; ओजीयः (ojīyaḥ)—one with greater inner strength than you; त्वत् (tvat)—other than you, anyone; न वै अस्ति (na vai asti)—there is none at all.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, you who are worthy of worship bear arrows and bow. Being worthy of worship, you wear a necklace that is worthy of worship and of many forms. Being worthy of praise, you protect this whole and great world. O Rudra, there is none at all other than you who has greater strength than you.

p. 214

Running head: [214 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṃ. 2. A. 4. Sū. 33.] (as supplied).

Printed English translation

Worthy ( of reverence ), you bear arrows and a bow : worthy (of praise), you wear an adorable and omniform necklace; worthy (of adoration), you preserve all this vast universe: there is no one more powerful than you.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Rudra as "O Rudra", the text says that this Rudra, being himself worthy of worship, bears bow and arrows; that he wears यजनीयं पूजनीयं विश्वरूपं निष्कं हारं बिभर्षि (yajanīyaṃ pūjanīyaṃ viśvarūpaṃ niṣkaṃ hāraṃ bibharṣi), necklaces that are worthy of worship and of manifold forms; and that अर्हन्नेव इदं विश्वं अभ्वं दयसे (arhanneva idaṃ viśvaṃ abhvaṃ dayase), he protects all this vast world. Thus the power, the adornment and the wondrous work of this Rudra are described. And ओजेयः न वै अस्ति (ojeyaḥ na vai asti) [as supplied; the Ṛk has ओजीयः] — त्वत्तः अन्यत् किंचित् बलवत्तरं न खलु विद्यते (tvattaḥ anyat kiṃcit balavattaraṃ na khalu vidyate): since nothing other than this Rudra, nothing greater in strength, exists, त्वमेव उक्तव्यापारेषु योज्यः (tvameva uktavyāpāreṣu yojyaḥ) — it is said that Rudra alone is capable of performing the work of protecting this world.

अभ्वं (abhvaṃ)—अतिविस्तृतं (ativistṛtaṃ). Yāska has read the word अभ्व (abhva) among the names of "great" (Ni. 3-13). Sāyaṇa takes this word as an adjective of विश्वं (viśvaṃ) and explains the meaning as "very vast".

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स्तु॒हि श्रु॒तं ग॑र्त॒सदं॒ युवा॑नं मृ॒गं न भी॒ममु॑पह॒त्तु मु॒ग्रं । मृ॒ळा ज॑रि॒त्रे रु॑द्र॒ स्तवा॑नो॒ऽन्यं ते॑ अ॒स्मन्नि व॑पंतु॒ सेनाः॑ ॥ ११ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

स्तुहि । श्रुतं । गर्तसदं । युवानं । मृगं । न । भीमं । उपहत्नुं । उग्रं । मृळ । जरित्रे । रुद्र । स्तवानः । अन्यं । ते । अस्मत् । नि । वपंतु । सेनाः ॥ ११ ॥

stuhi | śrutaṃ | gartasadaṃ | yuvānaṃ | mṛgaṃ | na | bhīmaṃ | upahatnuṃ | ugraṃ | mṛḷa | jaritre | rudra | stavānaḥ | anyaṃ | te | asmat | ni | vapaṃtu | senāḥ ‖ 11 ‖

p. 215

Running head: [A. 2. A. 7. V. 18.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 215 (as supplied).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

प्रयाणे मृगस्यामनोज्ञवचः श्रुत्वा स्तुहि श्रुतमित्येतां जपेत् । सूत्रितं च । स्तुहि श्रुतं गर्तसदं युवानमिति मृगस्य । गृ. ३-१०-१०. । इति ॥ हे स्तोतः श्रुतं विश्रुतं प्रख्यातं रुद्रं स्तुहि । कीदृशं । गर्तसदं । गर्तो रथः । तत्र सीदंतं युवानं नित्यतरुणं मृगं न भीमं मृगं सिंहमिव भयंकरं । उपहत्नुमुपहंतारं शत्रूणां मुग्रमुद्गूर्णं । हे रुद्र त्वं स्तवानोSस्माभिः स्तूयमानः सन् जरित्रॆ स्तोत्रे मह्यं मृळ । सुखय । ते त्वदीयाः सेना अस्मदन्यमस्मद्व्यतिरिक्तं पुरुषं निवपंतु । निघ्नंतु ॥

prayāṇe mṛgasyāmanojñavacaḥ śrutvā stuhi śrutamityetāṃ japet | sūtritaṃ ca | stuhi śrutaṃ gartasadaṃ yuvānamiti mṛgasya | gṛ. 3-10-10. | iti ‖ he stotaḥ śrutaṃ viśrutaṃ prakhyātaṃ rudraṃ stuhi | kīdṛśaṃ | gartasadaṃ | garto rathaḥ | tatra sīdaṃtaṃ yuvānaṃ nityataruṇaṃ mṛgaṃ na bhīmaṃ mṛgaṃ siṃhamiva bhayaṃkaraṃ | upahatnumupahaṃtāraṃ śatrūṇāṃ mugramudgūrṇaṃ | he rudra tvaṃ stavānoSsmābhiḥ stūyamānaḥ san jaritrè stotre mahyaṃ mṛḷa | sukhaya | te tvadīyāḥ senā asmadanyamasmadvyatiriktaṃ puruṣaṃ nivapaṃtu | nighnaṃtu ‖

Gist: On hearing the harsh cry of a wild animal on a journey one should recite this Ṛk (Gṛhya sūtra cited). Praise the renowned Rudra, seated in his car, ever young, terrible as a lion; the hosts are asked to destroy our other enemies.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O praiser); [praise] Rudra, who sits in the chariot, ever youthful, terrible like a lion, the destroyer of enemies, possessed of manifest strength, and renowned. Rudra, being praised by us, bring happiness to me, the praiser. Let your hosts destroy the enemy other than ourselves.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O praiser, praise and pray to Rudra, who sits in the chariot, ever youthful, terrible as a lion, destroyer of enemies, possessed of manifest strength and renowned. O Rudra, being praised by us, bring happiness to me, the praiser. May your hosts destroy the enemy other than ourselves.

Printed English translation

Glorify the renowned Rudra, riding in his car, ever youthful, destructive, fierce like a formidable wild beast: Rudra, propitiated by praise, grant happiness to him who praises (you), and let your hosts destroy him who is our adversary.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

That this Ṛk स्तुहि श्रुतं (stuhi śrutaṃ) is to be recited when, on a journey, one hears the harsh cry of wild animals, is set out by the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya Sūtra, स्तुहि श्रुतं गर्तसदं युवानमिति मृगस्य (stuhi śrutaṃ gartasadaṃ yuvānamiti mṛgasya) (Ā. Gṛ. 3-10-10).

In the first half of this Ṛk the Ṛṣi, seer of the mantra, addresses the priest who praises at the sacrifice. हे स्तोतः (he stotaḥ), O praising priest —

p. 216

Running head: [216 Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā [Maṃ. 2. A. 4. Sū. 33.] (as supplied).

श्रुतं गर्तसदॆं (śrutaṃ gartasadèṃ) [sic, as supplied] युवानं मृगं न भीमं उपहत्तुं उग्रं रुद्रं स्तुहि (yuvānaṃ mṛgaṃ na bhīmaṃ upahattuṃ ugraṃ rudraṃ stuhi) — प्रख्यातं, रथे सीदंतं (prakhyātaṃ, rathe sīdaṃtaṃ) ... "praise Rudra, the renowned, seated in the chariot, ever young, terrible like a lion, the destroyer of enemies, the uplifted (fierce one)." Rudra is famous because he is full of greatness; he is seated in a chariot; like a lion he is terrible to all; he is mighty. The command is expressed: praise Rudra of such majesty. In the second half the prayer of the sacrificer is stated, addressing Rudra: हे रुद्र स्तवानः त्वं जरित्रॆ मह्यं मृळ (he rudra stavānaḥ tvaṃ jaritrè mahyaṃ mṛḷa) — "O Rudra, praised by us, give happiness to me, the praiser"; so it is prayed that Rudra, praised by us the sacrificers, be gracious to us who have recited the praise; and ते सेनाः अस्मत् अन्यं नि वपंतु (te senāḥ asmat anyaṃ ni vapaṃtu) — "let your hosts destroy the person other than ourselves": let Rudra's hosts leave us who praise and destroy another man.

गर्तसदं (gartasadaṃ)—रथे सीदंतं (rathe sīdaṃtaṃ). Yāska has read the word गर्त (garta) among the names of the house (Ni. 3-13). And citing the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-7)

ಅಭ್ರಾತೇವ ಪುಂಸ ಏತಿ ಪ್ರತೀಚೀ ಗರ್ತಾ ರುಗಿವ ಸನಯೇ ಧನಾನಾಂ । ಜಾಯೇವ ಪತ್ಯ ಉಶತೀ ಸುವಾಸಾ ಉಷಾ ಹಸ್ರೇವ ನಿ ರಿಣೀತೇ ಅಪ್ಸಃ ॥

he describes the meaning of the word गर्त (garta) as गर्तः सभा स्थाणुः (gartaḥ sabhā sthāṇuḥ) (Ni. 3-5). And: श्मशानसंचयोपि गर्त उच्यते (śmaśānasaṃcayopi garta ucyate), and गुरतेरपगूर्णॆ भवति (guraterapagūrṇè bhavati); and in the Ṛk (cited as "Mi. Saṃ. 5-62-8", as printed)

ಹಿರಣ್ಯರೂಪಮುಷಸೋ ವ್ಯುಷ್ಟಾವಯಃಸ್ಥೂಣಮುದಿತಾ ಸೂರ್ಯಸ್ಯ । ಆ ರೋಹಥೋ ವರುಣ ಮಿತ್ರ ಗರ್ತಮತಶ್ಚಕ್ಷಾಥೇ ಅದಿತಿಂ ದಿತಿಂ ಚ ।

the word गर्त (garta) also: रथोपि गर्त उच्यते । गृणातेः स्तुतिकर्मणः । स्तुततमं यानं (rathopi garta ucyate | gṛṇāteḥ stutikarmaṇaḥ | stutatamaṃ yānaṃ) (Ni. 3-5). Thus four meanings are given: the house (in the gambling place) where the dice-pieces are placed, a house, the pit in a cemetery, and the chariot (the text says "house, house", as supplied). Here Sāyaṇa says it is used in the sense of chariot.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

कु॒मा॒रश्चि॑त्पि॒तरं॒ वंद॑मानं॒ प्रति॑ नानाम रुद्रोप॒यंतं॑ । भूरे॑र्दा॒तारं॒ सत्प॑तिं गृणीषे स्तु॒तस्त्वं भे॑ष॒जा रा॑स्य॒स्मे ॥ १२ ॥

kumāraścitpitaraṃ vaṃdamānaṃ prati nānāma rudropayaṃtaṃ | bhūrerdātāraṃ satpatiṃ gṛṇīṣe stutastvaṃ bheṣajā rāsyasme ‖ 12 ‖

p. 217

॥ पदपाठः ॥

कुमारः । चित् । पितरं वंदमानं प्रति । ननाम रुद्र । उपयंतं । धूरेः । दातारं । सत्पतिं । गृणीषे । स्तुतः । त्वं । भेषजा । रासि । अस्मे इति ॥ १२ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

वंदमानं आयुष्मान् भव सौम्यति स्तुवंतं पितरं कुमारश्चित् यथा कुमारः ॥ चिदित्येतदुपमार्थे ॥ हे रुद्र उपयंतमस्मत्समीपे गच्छंतं त्वां प्रतिननाम । प्रतिनतोऽस्मि । अपि च भूरेर्बहुनो धनस्य दातारं सत्पतिं सशां पालयितारं ॥ पत्यावैश्वर्य इति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ हे रुद्र एवंभूतं त्वां गृणीषे । सौमि ॥ मिपस्तिजां शिजो भवंतीति से आदेशः । स्तुतश्च त्वमस्मे अस्मभ्यं भेषजा भेषजानि रासि । देहि ॥

vaṃdamānaṃ āyuṣmān bhava saumyati stuvaṃtaṃ pitaraṃ kumāraścit yathā kumāraḥ ‖ cidityetadupamārthe ‖ he rudra upayaṃtamasmatsamīpe gacchaṃtaṃ tvāṃ pratinanāma | pratinato 'smi | api ca bhūrerbahuno dhanasya dātāraṃ satpatiṃ saśāṃ pālayitāraṃ ‖ patyāvaiśvarya iti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ‖ he rudra evaṃbhūtaṃ tvāṃ gṛṇīṣe | saumi ‖ mipastijāṃ śijo bhavaṃtīti se ādeśaḥ | stutaśca tvamasme asmabhyaṃ bheṣajā bheṣajāni rāsi | dehi ‖

Gist: Rudra, I bow to you as a son to a father who blesses him; you are the giver of much wealth and protector of the good; being praised, give us healing herbs.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Rudra—O Rudra; vandamānam—(the father) who speaks the blessing "be long-lived"; pitaram—the father; kumāraś cit—as a son bows and salutes; upayantam—to you who come towards us; prati nanāma—coming face to face I bow; bhūreḥ—of abundant wealth; dātāram—the giver; satpatim—the protector of the good; gṛṇīṣe—I praise; stutaḥ tvam—you praised by us; asme—to us; bheṣajā—medicines; rāsi—give.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, as a son bows to the father who pronounces the blessing "be long-lived", and salutes him, so I come face to face with you, who approach towards us, and bow. I praise you, the giver of abundant wealth and protector of the good. Being praised by us, give us medicines.

Printed English translation

I bow, Rudra, to you, approaching (our rite), as a boy to his father when pronouncing a blessing upon him : I glorify you, the giver of much (wealth), the protector of the virtuous ; thus glorified, bestow healing herbs upon me.

p. 218

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

हे रुद्र—उपयंतं वंदमानं पितरं कुमारश्चित् प्रति ननाम (he rudra—upayaṃtaṃ vaṃdamānaṃ pitaraṃ kumāraścit prati nanāma) — addressing Rudra: O Rudra, while you move near us the sacrificers, as a son performs obeisance to a father who blesses him with "be long-lived", so we the sacrificers perform obeisances to you. And भूरेः दातारं सत्पतिं गृणीषे (bhūreḥ dātāraṃ satpatiṃ gṛṇīṣe) — we praise you, the giver of abundant wealth and protector of the good, by reciting hymns. It is thus explained. And स्तुतः त्वं आस्मे भेषजा रासि (stutaḥ tvaṃ āsme bheṣajā rāsi) — you, praised by us, grant us medicines so that diseases and the like do not come. This is the explanation.

In कुमारश्चित् (kumāraścit) the word चित् (cit) is used in the sense of comparison. Yāska explains, with examples, that the word चित् (cit) has several uses: चिदित्येषो अनेककर्मा, आचार्यश्चिदिदं ब्रूयादिति पूजायां, दधि चिदित्युपमार्थे, कुल्माषांश्चिदित्यवकुत्सिते (cidityeṣo anekakarmā, ācāryaścididaṃ brūyāditi pūjāyāṃ, dadhi cidityupamārthe, kulmāṣāṃścidityavakutsite) — that is, the word conveys the senses of honour, comparison and disparagement.

The particle अस्मे (asme) is used in all seven case-relations (Ni. 6-7), Yāska says, and he gives examples of all of them. Here Sāyaṇa has explained the meaning as used in the dative.

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

या वो॑ भेष॒जा म॑रुतः॒ शुची॑नि॒ या शंत॑मा वृषणो॒ या॒॑ म॑यो॒भु । यानि॒ मनु॒रवृ॑णीता पि॒ता न॒स्ता शं च॒ योश्च॑ रु॒द्रस्य॑ वत्मि ॥ १३ ॥

yā vo bheṣajā marutaḥ śucīni yā śaṃtamā vṛṣaṇo yā mayobhu | yāni manuravṛṇītā pitā nastā śaṃ ca yośca rudrasya vatmi ‖ 13 ‖

p. 219

॥ पदपाठः ॥

या । वः । भेषजा । मरुतः । शुचीनि । या । शंतमा । वृषणः । या । मयःभु । यानि । मनुः । अवृणीत । पिता । नः । ता । शं । च । योः । च । रुद्रस्य । वश्मि ॥ १३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतो रुद्रपुत्रा वो युष्माकं या यानि भेषजा भेषजान्यस्मदा- रोग्य हेतुभूतान्षधानि शुचीनि शुद्धानि निर्मलानि संति । हे वृषणः कामानां वर्षितारो मरुतो या यानि च युष्मदीयानि भेषजानि शंतमा अतिशयेन सुखकराणि ! या यानि च भेषजानि मयोभु मयोभूनि मयसः सुखस्य भावयि- त्यणि नोऽस्मत्पिता मनुर्यानि भेषजानि युष्मदीयान्यवृणीत वृतवान् ता तानि भेषजानि रुद्रस्य महादेवस्य संबंधि शं च योश्च यच्छमनीयानां रोगाणा- मुपशमनं यावनीयानां भयानां यद्यावनमस्मत्तः पृथक्करणं तदुभयं च वश्मि ! कामये ॥ वश कांत् ! आदादिकः ॥

he maruto rudraputrā vo yuṣmākaṃ yā yāni bheṣajā bheṣajānyasmadā- rogya hetubhūtānṣadhāni śucīni śuddhāni nirmalāni saṃti | he vṛṣaṇaḥ kāmānāṃ varṣitāro maruto yā yāni ca yuṣmadīyāni bheṣajāni śaṃtamā atiśayena sukhakarāṇi ! yā yāni ca bheṣajāni mayobhu mayobhūni mayasaḥ sukhasya bhāvayi- tyaṇi no 'smatpitā manuryāni bheṣajāni yuṣmadīyānyavṛṇīta vṛtavān tā tāni bheṣajāni rudrasya mahādevasya saṃbaṃdhi śaṃ ca yośca yacchamanīyānāṃ rogāṇā- mupaśamanaṃ yāvanīyānāṃ bhayānāṃ yadyāvanamasmattaḥ pṛthakkaraṇaṃ tadubhayaṃ ca vaśmi ! kāmaye ‖ vaśa kāṃt ! ādādikaḥ ‖

Gist: the Maruts' medicines are pure, most comforting and beneficial; those chosen by Manu, and Rudra's two (curing diseases, removing fears), I desire.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Marutaḥ—O Maruts, sons of Rudra; vaḥ—your; yā—which; bheṣajā—medicines; śucīni—are pure; vṛṣaṇaḥ—O Maruts who shower desires; yā—which of your medicines; śantamā—are comforting; yā—which medicines; mayobhu—establish happiness; yāni—which medicines; naḥ pitā—our father; manuḥ—Manu; avṛṇīta—chose; tā—those medicines; ca—and; rudrasya—belonging to Rudra; śam—the disease-destroying; yoḥ ca—and that which produces freedom from fear (these two kinds of medicines); vaśmi—I wish to obtain.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, sons of Rudra and showerers of desires, whichever of your medicines are pure, whichever are comforting, whichever our father Manu chose, those, and also the two kinds of medicines belonging to Rudra, the disease-destroying and the fear-removing, I wish to obtain.

p. 220

Printed English translation

Maruts, I solicit of you those medicaments which are pure ; those, showerers (of benifits) [sic] which give great pleasure; those which confer felicity ; those which (our) sire, Manu, selected; and those (medicaments) of Rudra which are the alleviation (of disease), and defence (against danger).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

The Maruts, the sons of Rudra, are praised in this Ṛk as हे मरुतः—रुद्रपुत्राः (he marutaḥ—rudraputrāḥ). These Maruts are वृषणः—कामानां वर्षितारः (vṛṣaṇaḥ—kāmānāṃ varṣitāraḥ), that is, they fulfil all the desires of the sacrificers; therefore the sacrificers pray to the Maruts for bodily health, so as to pass their lives happily; the prayer is made for the medicines obtainable through their favour and also for the favour of Rudra.

वः यानि भेषजा शुचीनि शंतमा मयोभु नः पिता अवृणीत । भेषजानि अस्मदारोग्यहेतुभूतानि, शुद्धानि निर्मलानि, अतिशयेन सुखकराणि, मयस्य सुखस्य भावयित्यणि, अस्मत्पिता मनु? युष्मदीयानि भेषजानि अवृणीत । (vaḥ yāni bheṣajā śucīni śaṃtamā mayobhu naḥ pitā avṛṇīta | bheṣajāni asmadārogyahetubhūtāni, śuddhāni nirmalāni, atiśayena sukhakarāṇi, mayasya sukhasya bhāvayityaṇi, asmatpitā manu? yuṣmadīyāni bheṣajāni avṛṇīta |) The medicines connected with the Maruts are the means of producing health in us, the sacrificers; they are pure, they bring abundant happiness, and they also produce happiness; therefore our father Manu has chosen these medicines: thus the greatness of the medicines is stated. (The quoted Sanskrit is given as supplied, including "ಮಯಸ್ಯ", "ಭಾವಯಿತ್ಯಣಿ" and "ಮನು?".) And तानि भेषजानि रुद्रस्य शंयोश्च वश्मि महादेवसंबंधि शमनीयानां रोगाणामुपशमनं यावनीयानां भयानामस्मत्तः पृथक्करणं तदुभयं च प्रार्थये (tāni bheṣajāni rudrasya śaṃyośca vaśmi mahādevasaṃbaṃdhi śamanīyānāṃ rogāṇāmupaśamanaṃ yāvanīyānāṃ bhayānāmasmattaḥ pṛthakkaraṇaṃ tadubhayaṃ ca prārthaye)—the sacrificers have prayed for the favour that is connected with Mahādeva, that destroys (allays) diseases and removes fears in situations where fear arises, and for the medicines connected with the Maruts [sic: as printed] (these two).

शंयुः (śaṃyuḥ)—Yāska explains this word as सुखंयुः (sukhaṃyuḥ) (Ni. 4-21). Durgācārya takes शं युः (śaṃ yuḥ) as two words, explaining शं (śaṃ) as रोगाणां उपशमनं (rogāṇāṃ upaśamanaṃ), the destruction of diseases, and युः (yuḥ) as भयानां यावनं (bhayānāṃ yāvanaṃ), the state in which fears do not arise.

p. 221

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

परि॑ णो हे॒ती रु॒द्रस्य॑ वृज्याः॒ परि॑ त्वे॒षस्य॑ दुर्म॒तिर्म॒ही गा॑त् । अव॑ स्थि॒रा म॒घव॑द्भ्यस्तनुष्व॒ मीढ्व॑स्तो॒काय॒ तन॑याय मृळ ॥ १४ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

परि । नः । हेतिः । रुद्रस्य । वृज्याः । परि । त्वेषस्य । दुःमतिः । मही । गात् । अव । स्थिरा । मघवत्ऽभ्यः । तनुष्प । माढ्वः । तोकाय । तनयाय । मृळ ॥ १४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

रुद्रस्य महादेवस्य हेतिरायुधं नोऽस्मान्परिवृज्याः । परिवर्जयतु । यथा त्वेषस्य दीप्तस्य रुद्रस्य मही महती दुर्मतिर्दुःखकारिणी बुद्धिश्च परिगात् । अस्मान्वर्जयित्वान्यत्र गच्छतु ॥ अपपरी वर्जने । पा. १-४-८८. ॥ हे मीढ्वः सेचन- समर्थ रुद्र स्थिरा स्थिराणि त्वदीयानि धनूंषि मघवद्भो हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेभ्यो यजमानेभ्योvवतनुष्ट । अवततज्यानि कुरु । तथा तोकायास्मत्पुत्राय तनयाय तत्पुत्राय च मृळ । सुखं कुरु ॥

rudrasya mahādevasya hetirāyudhaṃ no 'smānparivṛjyāḥ | parivarjayatu | yathā tveṣasya dīptasya rudrasya mahī mahatī durmatirduḥkhakāriṇī buddhiśca parigāt | asmānvarjayitvānyatra gacchatu ‖ apaparī varjane | pā. 1-4-88. ‖ he mīḍhvaḥ secana- samartha rudra sthirā sthirāṇi tvadīyāni dhanūṃṣi maghavadbho havirlakṣaṇadhanayuktebhyo yajamānebhyovvatanuṣṭa | avatatajyāni kuru | tathā tokāyāsmatputrāya tanayāya tatputrāya ca mṛḷa | sukhaṃ kuru ‖

Gist: may Rudra's weapon and wrathful mind pass us by; may he turn his bows from the sacrificers and make our sons and grandsons happy. Grammar tail: the sūtra cited is as printed (Pā. 1-4-88).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Rudrasya—of Rudra; hetiḥ—the weapon; naḥ—us; pari vṛjyāḥ—may it leave, not making us its target; tveṣasya—of the radiant Rudra; mahī—the great; durmatiḥ—the painful, wrath-like mind; pari gāt—may it turn its aim elsewhere than at us; mīḍhvaḥ—O Rudra, showerer of desires; sthirā—your strong bows; maghavadbhyaḥ—from the sacrificers who possess wealth in the form of oblations; ava tanuṣva—turn away to another quarter; tokāya—to our sons; tanayāya—to our grandsons; mṛḷa—bring happiness.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May we not become targets of Rudra's weapon. May the great, painful, wrath-like mind of the radiant Rudra turn its aim elsewhere than at us. O Rudra, showerer of desires, turn your strong bows away from the sacrificers who possess wealth in the form of oblations. Bring happiness to our sons and our grandsons.

p. 222

Printed English translation

May the javelin of Rudra avoid us : may the great displeasure of the radiant deity pass away (from us) : showerer of benefits, turn away your strong (bow) from the wealthy (offerers of oblations), and bestow happiness upon (our) sons and grandsons.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुद्रस्य हेतिः नः परि वृज्याः (rudrasya hetiḥ naḥ pari vṛjyāḥ)—the prayer is that the weapon of Mahādeva, which uproots enemies, may be kept far from us, the sacrificers; and श्वेषस्य दुर्मतिः परिगात् (śveṣasya durmatiḥ parigāt) (as printed; the Saṃhitā has त्वेषस्य (tveṣasya))—that the evil mind of this fiery Rudra, which causes sorrow to enemies, may not be directed at us, the sacrificers, but may rest on others. The word माढ्वः (māḍhvaḥ) (as printed; the Saṃhitā has मीढ्वः (mīḍhvaḥ)) is explained as सेचनसमर्थः (secanasamarthaḥ), able to grant rain, Rudra being thus addressed; and स्थिरा मघवद्भ्यः अवतनुष्प—स्थिराणि त्वदीयानि धनूंषि हविर्लक्षणधनयुक्तेभ्यः यजमानेभ्यः अवततज्यानि :कुरु (sthirā maghavadbhyaḥ avatanuṣpa—sthirāṇi tvadīyāni dhanūṃṣi havirlakṣaṇadhanayuktebhyaḥ yajamānebhyaḥ avatatajyāni :kuru)—the prayer is that Rudra's bow be turned away from the sacrificers who possess wealth in the form of oblations and directed at other people; and शोकाय तनयाय मृळ (śokāya tanayāya mṛḷa) (as printed; the Saṃhitā has तोकाय (tokāya))—that the sacrificers' sons and grandsons be kept in happiness.

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ए॒वा ब॑भ्रो वृषभ चेकितान॒ यथा॑ देव॒ न हृ॑णी॒षे न हंसि॑ । ह॒व॒न॒श्रुन्नो॑ रुद्रे॒ह बो॑धि बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ १५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

एव । बभ्रो इति । वृषभ । चेकितान । यथा । देव । हृणीषे । न । हंसि । हवनश्रुत् । नः । रुद्र । इह । बोधि । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुवीराः ॥ १५ ॥

eva | babhro iti | vṛṣabha | cekitāna | yathā | deva | hṛṇīṣe | na | haṃsi | havanaśrut | naḥ | rudra | iha | bodhi | bṛhat | vadema | vidathe | suvīrāḥ ‖ 15 ‖

p. 223

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 18, p. 223.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे बभ्रो जगतो भर्तर्बभ्रुवर्ण वा वृषभ कामानां वर्षितः चेकितान सर्वं जानन् हे देव द्योतमान रुद्र यथा येन प्रकारेण न हृणीषे न क्रुध्यसि न च हंसि ॥ हृणीज् लज्जायां अयं क्रुध्यतिकर्मा च ॥ एवं हवनश्रुत् अस्मदीय- माह्वानं शृण्वन् नोऽस्मान् हे रुद्र इहास्मिन्देशे बोधि । बुध्यस्व । विदथे यज्ञे गृहे वा सुवीराः शोभनपुत्राः संतो बृहत् प्रौढं त्वदीयं स्तोत्रं वदेम । उच्चारयाम ॥

he babhro jagato bhartarbabhruvarṇa vā vṛṣabha kāmānāṃ varṣitaḥ cekitāna sarvaṃ jānan he deva dyotamāna rudra yathā yena prakāreṇa na hṛṇīṣe na krudhyasi na ca haṃsi ‖ hṛṇīj lajjāyāṃ ayaṃ krudhyatikarmā ca ‖ evaṃ havanaśrut asmadīya- māhvānaṃ śṛṇvan no 'smān he rudra ihāsmindeśe bodhi | budhyasva | vidathe yajñe gṛhe vā suvīrāḥ śobhanaputrāḥ saṃto bṛhat prauḍhaṃ tvadīyaṃ stotraṃ vadema | uccārayāma ‖

Gist: Rudra, bearer of the world, showerer and all-knowing, is asked to hear the invocation, not to be angry or slay, and to know the sacrificers who will praise him with fine sons; the grammatical remark is on the root hṛṇīj (shame; here "be angry").

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Babhro—O bearer of the whole world; vṛṣabha—showerer of desires; cekitāna—all-knowing; deva—radiant; rudra—O Rudra; yathā—in whatever way; na hṛṇīṣe—you are not angry (with us); na ca haṃsi—and do not slay us in wrath (in that way); havanaśrut—as hearer of our invocation; naḥ—us; iha—in this sacrificial place; bodhi—know; vidathe—in the sacrificial house; suvīrāḥ—we, accompanied by excellent heroic sons; bṛhat—your mature praise; vadema—we recite.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Rudra, bearer of the whole world, showerer of desires, all-knowing and radiant: in the way in which you are not angry with us and do not slay us in wrath, hear our invocation and know us in this sacrificial place. In the sacrificial house, accompanied by heroic sons, we recite your mature praise.

Printed English translation

Cherisher of the world, showerer (of benefits), omniscient and divine (Rudra), hearer of our invocation, so consider us on this occasion, that you may not be irate, nor slay us, but that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing Rudra with the words बभ्रो (babhro), वृषभ (vṛṣabha), चेकितान (cekitāna) and देव (deva), the commentary describes his greatness: he rules the whole world as its lord; he fulfils the desires of those who serve him; he knows everything and is all-knowing; he shines with lustre or brilliance [the supplied text reads "ನರ್ಣಿಸಿ" for "describing"; I take it as varṇisi, as supplied]. As to the sacrificers, यथा न हृणीषे न च हंसि (yathā na hṛṇīṣe na ca haṃsi)—the god is not angry and does not cause destruction; नः हवनश्रुत् बोधि (naḥ havanaśrut bodhi)—we sacrificers pray that, hearing the invocation we make in the sacrifices, he may know us rightly; and विदथे सुवीराः बृहत् वदेम (vidathe suvīrāḥ bṛhat vadema)—in sacrifices and in houses, with our sons of good qualities, we shall recite the mature praises of this god. So it is explained.

p. 224

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 224.

Sūkta 34 (Maṇḍala 2)

The thirty-fourth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

धारावरा इति पंचदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं मारुतं । अंत्या त्रिष्टुप् शिष्टा जगत्यः । तथा चानुक्रांतं । धारावरा मारुतं त्रिष्टुबंतमिति ॥ पृष्याभिप्लवषडहयोस्तृतीयेऽहन्याग्नि मारुतशस्त्रस्येदं मारुतनिविद्वानं । सूत्रि- तं च । वैश्वानराय धिषषां धारावरा मरुतस्त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अंगिरा इत्याग्नि- मारुतं । आ. ७-७. । इति ॥

Gist: the second sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of fifteen ṛks, of the Gārtsamada seer, for the Maruts; the last ṛk in triṣṭubh, the rest in jagatī; the Anukramaṇī is quoted, and the use at the third day of the Pṛṣṭhya and Abhiplava ṣaḍahas, in the Āgnimāruta recitation, is cited from the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (7-7).

Anuvāda (Kannada). This sūkta beginning धारावरा (dhārāvarā) is the second sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has fifteen ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta; the Maruts are the deity; the last ṛk is in triṣṭubh metre, the remaining ṛks in jagatī metre. What the Anukramaṇikā says—धारावरा मारुतं त्रिष्टुबंतमिति (dhārāvarā mārutaṃ triṣṭubaṃtamiti)—is explained: on the third day of the sacrifices called Pṛṣṭhya [as supplied: "ಸೃಷ್ಟ್ಯ"] and Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, at the beginning of the recitation of the Āgnimāruta-śastra mantras, this sūkta is to be used for the nivid mantras, as set out by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra sūtra वैश्वानराय धिषणां धारावरा (vaiśvānarāya dhiṣaṇāṃ dhārāvarā) मरुतस्त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अंगिरा इत्याग्निमारुतं (marutastvamagne prathamo aṃgirā ityāgnimārutaṃ) (Ā. 7-7).

Sūkta 34 — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 19, 20, 21. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deity: the Maruts. Metre: Ṛks 1–14 jagatī; Ṛk 15 triṣṭubh.

p. 225

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 225.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

धा॒रा॒व॒रा म॒रुतो॑ धृ॒ष्ट्वो॑ जसो मृ॒गा न भी॒मास्तवि॑षीभिर॒र्चिनः॑। अ॒ग्नयो॒ न शु॑शुचा॒ना ऋ॑जी॒षिणो॒ भृमिं॒ धमं॑तो॒ अप॒ गा॑ अवृण्वत ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

धारावराः । मरुतः । धृष्णुओजसः । मृगाः । न । भीमाः । तविषीभिः । अर्चिनः । अग्नयः । न । शुशुचानाः । ऋजीषिणः । भृमिं । धमंतः । अप । गाः । अवृण्वत ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

धारावरा उदकधारयांतरिक्षमावृण्वंतः । यद्वा धाराणां धृतानां स्थिराणां वृक्षादीनां निवारयितारश्चालायितारः । धृष्ट्वोऽजसः परेषां धर्षकेण बलेन युक्ताः । आत एव मृगा न भीमाः । सिंहा इव भयंकराः । तविषीभिरात्मीय्यै- र्बलैर्वृष्टिप्रदानादिनार्चिनः सर्वं जगत्पूजयंतः । अग्नयो न शुशुचाना दीप्ता वह्नय इव दीप्यमानाः ॥ शुच दीप्तौ । लिटः कानच् ॥ ऋजीषिणः । ऋजीषमुदकं तद्वंतः । यद्वा ऋजीषोऽपगतसारः सोमः । तेन युक्ताः । तृतीयसवने ह्याग्निमारुते मरुतः स्तूयंते । तत्र च सवनद्वयेऽभिसुतं गतसारं सोममभि- षुण्वंति । अतस्तेषां तद्युक्तत्वं । एवंभूता मरुतो भृमिं भ्राम्यंतं मेघं धमंतो वर्षणार्थमितस्ततः प्रेरयंतो गास्तदंतर्गता वर्ष्या अपोऽपावृण्वत । अपावृताः कुर्वंति यथा सर्वैदृश्यंते तथा प्रवर्षंतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा भृम्याख्यो वीणाविशेषः । तं धमंतो वादयंतो गा वलनाम्मा सुरेणापिहिता अपावृण्वत । अपगतावरणा अकुर्वन् ॥

dhārāvarā udakadhārayāṃtarikṣamāvṛṇvaṃtaḥ | yadvā dhārāṇāṃ dhṛtānāṃ sthirāṇāṃ vṛkṣādīnāṃ nivārayitāraścālāyitāraḥ | dhṛṣṭvo 'jasaḥ pareṣāṃ dharṣakeṇa balena yuktāḥ | āta eva mṛgā na bhīmāḥ | siṃhā iva bhayaṃkarāḥ | taviṣībhirātmīyyai- rbalairvṛṣṭipradānādinārcinaḥ sarvaṃ jagatpūjayaṃtaḥ | agnayo na śuśucānā dīptā vahnaya iva dīpyamānāḥ ‖ śuca dīptau | liṭaḥ kānac ‖ ṛjīṣiṇaḥ | ṛjīṣamudakaṃ tadvaṃtaḥ | yadvā ṛjīṣo 'pagatasāraḥ somaḥ | tena yuktāḥ | tṛtīyasavane hyāgnimārute marutaḥ stūyaṃte | tatra ca savanadvaye 'bhisutaṃ gatasāraṃ somamabhi- ṣuṇvaṃti | atasteṣāṃ tadyuktatvaṃ | evaṃbhūtā maruto bhṛmiṃ bhrāmyaṃtaṃ meghaṃ dhamaṃto varṣaṇārthamitastataḥ prerayaṃto gāstadaṃtargatā varṣyā apo 'pāvṛṇvata | apāvṛtāḥ kurvaṃti yathā sarvaidṛśyaṃte tathā pravarṣaṃtītyarthaḥ | yadvā bhṛmyākhyo vīṇāviśeṣaḥ | taṃ dhamaṃto vādayaṃto gā valanāmmā sureṇāpihitā apāvṛṇvata | apagatāvaraṇā akurvan ‖

Gist: the Maruts are explained as water-streamed encirclers of the sky, or movers of firm trees; mighty like lions; filled with rain-water or with soma; they blow the wandering cloud and release its rain; alternatively they play the bhṛmi lute and release the cows hidden by the Asura.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Dhārāvarāḥ—those who envelop the sky with streams of water, or who make firmly standing trees and the like move; dhṛṣṇvojasaḥ [as supplied: धृष्णोऽजसः (dhṛṣṇo 'jasaḥ)]—those with strength that crushes enemies; mṛgā na—like lions; bhīmāḥ—of fearful form; taviṣībhiḥ—by their own powers; arcinaḥ—who honour the world; agnayo na—like blazing fires; śuśucānāḥ—shining; [rjīṣiṇaḥ—possessing water (the supplied text reads यजीषिणः (yajīṣiṇaḥ) here, while the Saṃhitā and Pada have ऋजीषिणः (ṛjīṣiṇaḥ))]; marutaḥ—the Maruts; bhṛmiṃ—the wandering clouds;

p. 226

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 226.

dhamantaḥ—urging on for rain; gāḥ—the waters contained in them; apa avṛṇata [as supplied; the Saṃhitā has अवृण्वत (avṛṇvata)]—cause to pour down in the form of rain.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who make firmly standing trees and the like move, who have strength that crushes enemies, who are fearful in form like lions, who honour the world by their own powers, who shine like blazing fires and who possess water, urge the wandering clouds on for rain and cause the waters within them to pour down as rain.

Printed English translation

The Maruts, shedders of showers, endowed with resistless might, like formidable lions, reverencing (the world) by their energies, resplendent as fires, laden with water, and blowing about the wandering cloud, give vent to its (collected) rain.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

धारावराः (dhārāvarāḥ)—the commentary explains the word in three ways, citing उदकधारया अंतरिक्षमावृण्वंतः (udakadhārayā aṃtarikṣamāvṛṇvaṃtaḥ) and the alternatives. The Maruts pervade the sky with streams of rain-water (drops falling without interval in one even manner); or they make firmly standing trees and the like move; or they, by their own power, protect and bear the whole world.

धृष्ट्वोऽजसः मृगा न भीमाः (dhṛṣṭvo 'jasaḥ mṛgā na bhīmāḥ)—endowed with a force that overcomes enemies, and therefore fearful like lions; the might of the Maruts is compared with the might of the lion.

तविषीभिः अर्चिनः (taviṣībhiḥ arcinaḥ)—by their own strength, through the rain-waters they bestow, they make the whole world worthy of worship (of praise). अग्नयो न शुशुचानाः (agnayo na śuśucānāḥ)—shining abundantly with splendour, like blazing fires. So it is described.

p. 227

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 227.

ऋजीषिणः (ऋजीषिणि (ṛjīṣiṇi))—the commentary says: ऋजीषिमुदकं तद्वंतः (ṛjīṣimudakaṃ tadvaṃtaḥ) ("those possessing ṛjīṣa, water"), and alternatively ऋजीषो अपगतसारः सोमः (ṛjīṣo apagatasāraḥ somaḥ) ("ṛjīṣa is soma whose essence has gone"), "joined with that". Sāyaṇa gives the word ṛjīṣa the meaning udaka (water) and explains in one way that, since the Marut deities pour down rain-water, they are "possessing water". In the second meaning it denotes soma plants from which the sap (essence) has been pressed. When the sacrificial rite is performed, the hymn to the Agni-Maruts is recited at the third pressing; then, from the husks left over from the earlier pressings, sap is pressed out again and offered to these deities. Because soma plants pressed at the two times, the morning and midday pressings, are pressed again at the evening pressing, the sapless husk is called ṛjīṣa. Having such soma as their oblation-share, the Maruts are here called ṛjīṣiṇaḥ, so the meaning is explained.

Yāska, explaining the word ṛjīṣī, cites the ṛk

आपांतमन्युस्तृपलप्रभर्मा धुनिश्विमीवाञ्चरुमा ऋजीषी । सोमो विश्वान्यतसा वनानि नार्वागिंद्रं प्रतिमानानि देभुः ॥

āpāṃtamanyustṛpalaprabharmā dhuniśvimīvāñcarumā ṛjīṣī | somo viśvānyatasā vanāni nārvāgiṃdraṃ pratimānāni debhuḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-89-5)

and explains the meaning: ऋजीषी सोमः यत् सोमस्य पूयमानस्य अतिरिच्यते तदृजीषमपार्जितं भवति तेनर्जिषी सोमः (ṛjīṣī somaḥ yat somasya pūyamānasya atiricyate tadṛjīṣamapārjitaṃ bhavati tenarjiṣī somaḥ) (Ni. 5-12) ("ṛjīṣī is soma: what remains over of the soma being purified is ṛjīṣa, what is wiped off; hence ṛjīṣī soma"), and says अथाप्यैंद्रो निगमो भवति (athāpyaiṃdro nigamo bhavati) ("further, there is an Indra passage"). Durgācārya cites the ṛk

ऋजीषी वज्री वृषभस्तुराषाट्भुष्मी राजा वृत्रहा सोमपाना । युक्त्वा हरिभ्यामुप यासदर्नाज् माध्यंदिने सवने मत्सदिंद्रः ॥

ṛjīṣī vajrī vṛṣabhasturāṣāṭbhuṣmī rājā vṛtrahā somapānā | yuktvā haribhyāmupa yāsadarnāj mādhyaṃdine savane matsadiṃdraḥ ‖

(as printed "ಪು. ಸಂ ೫-೪೦-೪", i.e. 5-40-4; the abbreviation is the supplied text's)

and says that ṛjīṣī is Indra: ऋजीषी इंद्रः (ṛjīṣī iṃdraḥ).

भृमिं धमंतः गाः अप अवृण्वत (भृमिं धमंतः गाः अप अवृण्वत (bhṛmiṃ dhamaṃtaḥ gāḥ apa avṛṇvata))—the commentary says: भ्राम्यंतं मेघं वर्षणार्थमितस्ततः प्रेरयंतः (bhrāmyaṃtaṃ meghaṃ varṣaṇārthamitastataḥ prerayaṃtaḥ) ("urging hither and thither, for the sake of rain, the wandering cloud") तदंतर्गताः अपः अपावृताः कुर्वंति (tadaṃtargatāḥ apaḥ apāvṛtāḥ kurvaṃti) ("they uncover the waters contained in it"); or, भृम्याख्यः वीणाविशेषः तं धमंतो वादयंतः (bhṛmyākhyaḥ vīṇāviśeṣaḥ taṃ dhamaṃto vādayaṃtaḥ) ("a particular lute called bhṛmi; blowing it, that is, playing it"), बलनाम्मा असुरेणापिहिता गाः अपगतावरणा अकुर्वन् (balanāmmā asureṇāpihitā gāḥ apagatāvaraṇā akurvan) ("they freed from covering the cows hidden by the Asura named Bala" [as supplied; elsewhere the supplied text has vala]). In the first sense, the Maruts urge the clouds that roam the sky, filled with water, hither and thither to rain, so that the waters hidden in the clouds come out in the form of rain. In the second sense the word bhṛmi is taken to mean a lute: when the Asura Vala had stolen the cows of the gods and hidden them, the Maruts played the lute, discovered the place where the cows were, and caused the cows to come out. This legend has been described before.

p. 228

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 228.

Yāska comments भृमिः भ्राम्यतेः (bhṛmiḥ bhrāmyateḥ) (Ni. 6-21) ("bhṛmi from the root bhram") and cites the ṛk

इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् । आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानां ॥

imāmagne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imamadhvānaṃ yamagāma dūrāt | āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhṛmirasyṛṣikṛnmartyānāṃ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-16, as printed "ಪು. ಸಂ.")

and explains that by the word bhṛmi Agni is denoted.
