Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

द्यावो॒ न सृभि॑श्चितयंत खा॒दिनो॒ व्य१॒ं॑भ्रिया॒ न द्यु॑तयंत॒॑ वृ॒ष्टयः॑ । रु॒द्रो यद्वो॑ मरुतो रुक्मवक्षसो॒ वृषाज॑नि॒ पृश्न्याः॑ शु॒क्र॑ ऊधनि ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

(the label is garbled in the supplied text, पवनाति (pavanāti); replaced by the standard label. As supplied, the Pada reads स्त्रृभिः (strṛbhiḥ), रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (rukṣmavakṣasaḥ), पृश्नाः (pṛśnāḥ) and शुक्रॆ (śukrè), which differ from the Saṃhitā सृभिः (sṛbhiḥ), रुक्मवक्षसो (rukmavakṣaso), पृश्न्याः (pṛśnyāḥ), शुक्र (śukra) and the bhāṣya स्त्वभिः (stvabhiḥ), रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (rukṣmavakṣasaḥ).)

द्यावः । न । स्त्रृभिः । चितयंत । खादिनः । वि । अभ्रियाः । न । द्युतयंत । वृष्टयः। रुद्रः । यत् । वः । मरुतः । रुक्ष्मवक्षसः । वृषा । अजनि । पृश्नाः । शुक्रॆ । ऊधनि ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स्त्वभिः । नक्षत्रनामैतत् । यदाह यास्कः । ऋक्षाः स्त्वभिरिति नक्षत्राणां । नि. ३-२० । इति । नक्षत्रैर्द्यावो न यथा द्युलोकाश्चितयंत चेतयंति स्वात्मानं ज्ञापयंति ॥ चिती संज्ञाने । प्रकाशंत इत्यर्थः । तथा खादिनः शत्रूणां खादका मरुतः स्वकीयैराभरणैर्ज्ञायंते । यद्वा खादः कटकं । तद्युक्ताः संतः प्रकाशंते । तथा वृष्टयो वर्षका मरुतोऽभ्रिया न । अभ्रेषु भवा विद्युत् इव

stvabhiḥ | nakṣatranāmaitat | yadāha yāskaḥ | ṛkṣāḥ stvabhiriti nakṣatrāṇāṃ | ni. 3-20 | iti | nakṣatrairdyāvo na yathā dyulokāścitayaṃta cetayaṃti svātmānaṃ jñāpayaṃti ‖ citī saṃjñāne | prakāśaṃta ityarthaḥ | tathā khādinaḥ śatrūṇāṃ khādakā marutaḥ svakīyairābharaṇairjñāyaṃte | yadvā khādaḥ kaṭakaṃ | tadyuktāḥ saṃtaḥ prakāśaṃte | tathā vṛṣṭayo varṣakā maruto 'bhriyā na | abhreṣu bhavā vidyut iva

p. 229

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 229.

विद्युतयंत । सर्वं जगद्विद्योतयंति । प्रकाशयंति ॥ अभ्रशब्दाद्भवार्थे समुद्रा- भ्राद्ध इति घ-प्रत्ययः । शेषः प्रत्यक्षकृतः रुक्ष्मवक्षसः रुक्ष्मं रोचमाणाभरणं वक्षस्युरसि येषां तादृशा हे मरुतो यद्यदा वो युष्मान् वृषा सेचनसमर्थो रुद्रो महादेवः पृश्न्याः । पृश्चिर्माध्यमिका वाक् । तस्याः संबंधिनि शुक्रे निर्मल ऊधन्युद्धते प्रदेशेऽजनि । अजनयत् । तदानीमिति पूर्वत्र संबंधः । यद्वा पृश्निर्नानावर्णेयं भूमिः पुरा गोरूपधरासीत् तस्यां महेशो वृषो भूत्वा मरुत उत्पादयामासेत्याचक्षते । तदत्तोच्यते । हे मरुतो यद्यस्माद्वो युष्मान् वृषा वृषरूपो रुद्रः पृश्न्या गोः शुक्रे निर्मल ऊधन्यूधसि पयस उत्पत्ति स्थानेऽजनि । अजीजनत् । तस्माद्यूयमेवं महानुभावा जाता इत्यर्थः । तथा च तैत्तरीयकं । पृश्नियै वै पयसो मरुतो जाताः । तै. सं. २.२-११४ । इति ॥

vidyutayaṃta | sarvaṃ jagadvidyotayaṃti | prakāśayaṃti ‖ abhraśabdādbhavārthe samudrā- bhrāddha iti gha-pratyayaḥ | śeṣaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ rukṣmavakṣasaḥ rukṣmaṃ rocamāṇābharaṇaṃ vakṣasyurasi yeṣāṃ tādṛśā he maruto yadyadā vo yuṣmān vṛṣā secanasamartho rudro mahādevaḥ pṛśnyāḥ | pṛścirmādhyamikā vāk | tasyāḥ saṃbaṃdhini śukre nirmala ūdhanyuddhate pradeśe 'jani | ajanayat | tadānīmiti pūrvatra saṃbaṃdhaḥ | yadvā pṛśnirnānāvarṇeyaṃ bhūmiḥ purā gorūpadharāsīt tasyāṃ maheśo vṛṣo bhūtvā maruta utpādayāmāsetyācakṣate | tadattocyate | he maruto yadyasmādvo yuṣmān vṛṣā vṛṣarūpo rudraḥ pṛśnyā goḥ śukre nirmala ūdhanyūdhasi payasa utpatti sthāne 'jani | ajījanat | tasmādyūyamevaṃ mahānubhāvā jātā ityarthaḥ | tathā ca taittarīyakaṃ | pṛśniyai vai payaso maruto jātāḥ | tai. saṃ. 2.2-114 | iti ‖

Gist: stṛbhiḥ means stars (Yāska, Nir. 3-20); the Maruts shine with their ornaments as the heavens with stars and like cloud-born lightning; Rudra, the bull, begot them in the pure udder of Pṛśni (Taittirīya citation).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (rukṣmavakṣasaḥ)—wearing a golden-coloured ornament on the breast; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; यत् (yat)—when; वः (vaḥ)—you; वृषा (vṛṣā)—capable of sprinkling (shedding); रुद्रः (rudraḥ)—Rudra; पृश्न्याः (pṛśnyāḥ)—of Pṛśni; शुक्रे (śukre)—in the pure one, ऊधनि (ūdhani)—and swollen (uplifted) one, the womb [as supplied: "ಉದರ"]; अजनि (ajani)—created (then); स्तृभिः (stṛbhiḥ)—by the stars; द्यावो न (dyāvo na)—as the sky [as supplied "ಆಂತರಿಕ್ಷ"] makes itself shine; खादिनः (khādinaḥ)—you who wear bracelets (by your ornaments); चितयंत (citayaṃta)—make yourselves shine; वृष्टयः (vṛṣṭayaḥ)—you, causers of rain; अभ्रिया न (abhriyā na)—like lightnings born of clouds; विद्युतयंत (vidyutayaṃta)—cause the world to shine.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, who wear a golden-coloured ornament on the breast, when Rudra, capable of shedding (rain), caused you to be born in the pure heart [as supplied: "ಹೃದಯದಲ್ಲಿ"; the Pratipadārtha has "womb", उदर (udara), and the printed English "womb"] of Pṛśni, then, as the sky makes itself shine with stars, you, wearers of bracelets, make yourselves shine [as supplied: "ಪ್ರಕಾಶಪಶಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತೀರಿ", evidently a misprint] by your ornaments. You, causers of rain, make the world shine like lightnings born of clouds.

Printed English translation

Since, golden-breasted Maruts, the vigorous (Rudra) begot you of the pure womb of Prishni, therefore they, the devourers (of their enemies), are conspicuous (by their ornaments), as the heavens are by the constellatoins [sic] ; and, senders of rain, they are brilliant as the cloud-born (lightning).

p. 230

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 230.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

स्त्वभिः द्यावो न चितयंत (stvabhiḥ dyāvo na citayaṃta)—"As the heavens make themselves known by the stars": just as the luminous worlds make themselves shine, so the Maruts, खादिनः (khādinaḥ) (devourers of their enemies), are known by their own ornaments. Or खादः (khādaḥ) is a bracelet (कटकं (kaṭakaṃ)), and, possessed of it, they shine. Yāska (नि. ३-२० (ni. 3-20)) has read स्त्वभिः (stvabhiḥ) among the twenty-six names beginning with the two-word group उत्तराणि नामानि (uttarāṇi nāmāni), and explains: ऋक्षाः स्त्वभिरिति नक्षत्राणां (ṛkṣāḥ stvabhiriti nakṣatrāṇāṃ) (these are names of the stars) and स्त्वभिस्तीर्णानीव ख्यायंते (stvabhistīrṇānīva khyāyaṃte) (they appear as if strewn). Sāyaṇa has thus given two kinds of meaning: as the worlds, beginning with the atmosphere, that shine with light reveal their own form by the stars, so the Maruts, the destroyers of enemies, are known by their ornaments; or खाद (khāda) means the ornament called a bracelet worn on the hand, and the Maruts shine with the bracelets they wear on their hands.

वृष्टयः अभ्रिया न विद्योतयंत (vṛṣṭayaḥ abhriyā na vidyotayaṃta)—The rain-giving Maruts light up the whole world like the lightning born in the clouds. The Marut deities who pour down rain-water make all the worlds full of light, as the lightnings born in the clouds illuminate the world. In both these sentences न (na) is used as a particle of comparison.

वृषा रुद्रः पृश्नाः शुक्रे ऊधनि वः अजनयत् (vṛṣā rudraḥ pṛśnāḥ śukre ūdhani vaḥ ajanayat)—Mahādeva, capable of sprinkling (seed), begot (you) in the pure, raised region (उद्धतप्रदेशे (uddhatapradeśe)) of Pṛśni, the Mādhyamikā Vāk (the speech of the middle region). Yāska has read the word पृश्निः (pṛśniḥ) among the common names (सि. २-१३ (si. 2-13) as supplied). One kind of meaning has been set forth thus: Mahādeva, who is able to sprinkle, placed his seed in the pure womb of the goddess Pṛśni, who has the form of the Mādhyamikā Vāk, and so produced the Marut deities. Secondly, यदा पृश्निर्नानावर्णेयं भूमिः पुरा गोरूपधरा आसीत् । तस्यां महेशः वृषो भूत्वा मरुतः उत्पादयामासेत्याचक्षते । तदत्रोच्यते (yadā pṛśnirnānāvarṇeyaṃ bhūmiḥ purā gorūpadharā āsīt | tasyāṃ maheśaḥ vṛṣo bhūtvā marutaḥ utpādayāmāsetyācakṣate | tadatrocyate): this earth of many colours, in former times, when she had taken the form of a cow, Maheśvara took the form of a bull and produced the Maruts; so they say, and this legend is told by this sentence. Sāyaṇa explains this view, and, because the origin of the Maruts is of this kind, describes the Maruts as रुक्ष्मवक्षसः (rukṣmavakṣasaḥ) (रुक्मं रोचमानाभरणं येषां ते (rukmaṃ rocamānābharaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ te): those who have a shining ornament), adorned with shining ornaments; as stars make the atmosphere shine, so they make the whole world shine with their ornaments; and, being born of Mahādeva, they are possessed of abundant greatness.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

p. 231

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 231.

उ॒क्षंते॒ अश्वा॒ अत्या॑ इवा॒ जिषु॑ न॒दस्य॒ कर्णै॑स्तुरयंत आ॒शुभिः॑ । हिर॑ण्यशिप्रा मरुतो॒ दवि॑ध्वतः पृ॒क्षं या॑थ॒ पृष॑तीभिः समन्यवः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उक्षंते अश्वान् । अत्यान् इव । आजिषु । नदस्य । कर्णैः । तुरयंते । आशुभिः । हिरण्यशिप्राः । मरुतः । दविध्वतः । पृक्षं । याथ । पृषतीभिः । समन्यवः ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

मरुतोऽश्वान् व्याप्तान् लोकानुक्षंते । सिंचंति । अशू व्याप्त् । औणादिकः क्वन्त्रत्रयः । आजिसु संग्रामेष्वत्यानिव सततगामिनस्तुरगान् यथा स्वेदापनोदा- योदकैः सिंचंति तद्वत् । अपि च ते मरुत आशुभिः शीघ्रगमनैरश्वर्नदस्य शब्दवतो मेघस्य कर्णैः कृतैर्मध्यप्रदेशैस्तुरयंते । वर्षाणार्थं वृष्टुत्पादनाय त्वरितं गच्छंति ॥ तुर त्वरणे ॥ शेषः प्रत्यक्षकृतः । हे हिरण्यशिप्राः । शिप्रं शिरस्त्राणं । सुवर्णमयशिरस्त्राणाः समन्यवः समानमनस्काः समानक्रोधा वा हे मरुतो दविध्वतो महीरुहादिकं कंपयंतो यूयं ॥ धूञ् कंपन इत्यस्माद्वाध- र्त्यादावेतद्रूपं निपात्यते ॥ पृषतीभिर्युष्मद्रथे योजिताभिः श्वेतबिंद्वंकिताभि- र्मृगीभिर्वडवाभिर्वा वृक्षं । अन्ननामैतत् । हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतं यजमानं ॥ अर्श आदित्वादच् ॥ याथ । गच्छत ॥

maruto 'śvān vyāptān lokānukṣaṃte | siṃcaṃti | aśū vyāpt | auṇādikaḥ kvantratrayaḥ | ājisu saṃgrāmeṣvatyāniva satatagāminasturagān yathā svedāpanodā- yodakaiḥ siṃcaṃti tadvat | api ca te maruta āśubhiḥ śīghragamanairaśvarnadasya śabdavato meghasya karṇaiḥ kṛtairmadhyapradeśaisturayaṃte | varṣāṇārthaṃ vṛṣṭutpādanāya tvaritaṃ gacchaṃti ‖ tura tvaraṇe ‖ śeṣaḥ pratyakṣakṛtaḥ | he hiraṇyaśiprāḥ | śipraṃ śirastrāṇaṃ | suvarṇamayaśirastrāṇāḥ samanyavaḥ samānamanaskāḥ samānakrodhā vā he maruto davidhvato mahīruhādikaṃ kaṃpayaṃto yūyaṃ ‖ dhūñ kaṃpana ityasmādvādha- rtyādāvetadrūpaṃ nipātyate ‖ pṛṣatībhiryuṣmadrathe yojitābhiḥ śvetabiṃdvaṃkitābhi- rmṛgībhirvaḍavābhirvā vṛkṣaṃ | annanāmaitat | havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaṃ yajamānaṃ ‖ arśa āditvādac ‖ yātha | gacchata ‖

Gist: the Maruts sprinkle the pervaded worlds as men sprinkle horses in battle; they rush in the middle regions of the sounding cloud; golden-helmeted and like-minded, they shake the trees and come with their spotted mares to the sacrificer's food.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

आजिषु (ājiṣu)—in battles; अत्यानिव (atyāniva)—as (to remove fatigue) water is poured over horses; (मरुतः (marutaḥ)—the Maruts) अश्वान् (aśvān)—all the pervaded worlds; उक्षंते (ukṣaṃte)—drench with water; (the same Maruts) आशुभिः (āśubhiḥ)—with swift horses; नदस्य (nadasya)—of the sounding clouds; कर्णैः (karṇaiḥ)—through the paths made (in the middle regions); तुरयंते (turayaṃte)—rush swiftly (to produce rain); हिरणशिप्राः (hiraṇaśiprāḥ) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has हिरण्यशिप्रा (hiraṇyaśiprā))—O you who have helmets made of gold; समन्यवः (samanyavaḥ)—and of equal mind; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; दविध्वतः (davidhvataḥ)—you who make trees and the like tremble; पृषतीभिः (pṛṣatībhiḥ)—with horses coloured with spots;

p. 232

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 232.

प्रक्षं (prakṣaṃ) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has पृक्षं (pṛkṣaṃ))—towards the sacrificer who is provided with food in the form of the oblation; याथ (yātha)—come.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As water is poured over horses in battles to remove their fatigue, the Maruts drench all the worlds with water. The same Maruts, with swift horses, make paths in the middle region of the sounding clouds and rush swiftly to produce rain. O Maruts, with helmets made of gold and of equal mind, you who make trees and the like tremble, come with your horses coloured with spots towards the sacrificer who is provided with food in the form of the oblation.

Printed English translation

They sprinkle the wide-extended (lands) with water, as (men sprinkle) horses (when heated) in battles; and they rush along with swift (horses) on the skirts of the sounding (cloud): Maruts, golden-helmed, and of one mind, agitating (the trees), come with your spotted deer to (receive the sacrificial) food.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अश्वान् अजिषु अत्यानिव सिंचंति (aśvān ajiṣu atyāniva siṃcaṃti) (as supplied)—The Maruts sprinkle the pervaded worlds in battles, as horses that move constantly are sprinkled with water to remove their sweat. Yāska has read the two words अश्व (aśva) and अत्य (atya) among the names of the horse (नि. २-२७ (ni. 2-27)). Sāyaṇa gives अश्व (aśva) the meaning "that which pervades", and explains that the Marut deities sprinkle the pervaded worlds with rain-water, the illustration being stated as: as horses that move constantly in battles are sprinkled with water to remove their sweat, and so relieved of fatigue.

आशुभिः नदस्य कर्णैः तुरयंते (āśubhiḥ nadasya karṇaiḥ turayaṃte)—Those Maruts, with swift-going horses, go quickly through the middle regions of the sounding cloud to produce rain. It is explained thus: in the middle of the clouds that are filled with water and sound, the Maruts, making the middle regions of the clouds into swiftly moving horses, move rapidly so that the waters in the cloud may pour down on the earth as rain.

हिरण्यशिप्रा: (hiraṇyaśiprā:)—सुवर्णमयशिरस्त्राणाः । शिप्रं शिरस्त्राणं (suvarṇamayaśirastrāṇāḥ | śipraṃ śirastrāṇaṃ): the Marut deities wear a head-ornament (helmet) made of gold; समन्यवः (samanyavaḥ)—समासमनस्काः समानक्षोडवा (samāsamanaskāḥ samānakṣoḍavā) (as supplied; the text of this window breaks off here, the sentence continues in the next window)

p. 233

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 233.

(Since they are renowned as the seven Maruts) they are of one kind of mind, or of one kind of anger, and they make trees and the like tremble; thus the Marut deities are described. And पृषतीभिः वृक्षं यात—युष्मद्रथे योजिताभिः श्वेतबिंद्वंकिताभिः मृगीभिः वडवाभिर्वा हविर्लक्षणान्नवंतं यजमानं गच्छथ । (pṛṣatībhiḥ vṛkṣaṃ yāta—yuṣmadrathe yojitābhiḥ śvetabiṃdvaṃkitābhiḥ mṛgībhiḥ vaḍavābhirvā havirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaṃ yajamānaṃ gacchatha |): O Maruts, come to the sacrificer who is provided with food in the form of the oblation, seated in your chariots yoked with deer marked with white spots, or with mares, and offering the oblation-food, so the meaning is described.

Yāska has stated the vehicles of the several deities: हरी इंद्रस्य । रोहितो अग्नेः । हरित आदित्यस्य । रासभावश्विनोः । अजाः पूष्णः । पृषत्यो मरुतां । अरुज्यो गाव उषसः। श्यावाः सवितुः। विश्वरूपा बृहस्पतेः । नियुतो वायोः । इति दशादिष्टोपयोजनानि (harī iṃdrasya | rohito agneḥ | harita ādityasya | rāsabhāvaśvinoḥ | ajāḥ pūṣṇaḥ | pṛṣatyo marutāṃ | arujyo gāva uṣasaḥ| śyāvāḥ savituḥ| viśvarūpā bṛhaspateḥ | niyuto vāyoḥ | iti daśādiṣṭopayojanāni) (नि.२-२८ (ni.2-28)) (the two bays of Indra; the red horse of Agni; the green horses of Āditya; the two asses of the Aśvins; the goats of Pūṣan; the spotted does of the Maruts; the ruddy cows of Uṣas; the dark-brown horses of Savitṛ; the many-formed ones of Bṛhaspati; the Niyut team of Vāyu; these are the ten as the harnessings specified). Here the Maruts are said to have पृषतः (pṛṣataḥ) (spotted does). A fuller explanation of this has been given in the earlier volumes.

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

पृ॒क्षे ता विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना ववक्षिरे मि॒त्राय॑ वा॒ सद॒मा जी॒रदा॑नवः । पृष॑दश्वासो अनव॒भ्ररा॑धस ऋजि॒प्यासो॒ न व॒युने॑षु धू॒र्षदः॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

पृक्षे । ता । विश्वा । भुवना । ववक्षिरे । मित्राय । वा । सदं । आ । जीरदानवः । पृषत्अश्वासः । अनवभ्रराधसः । ऋजिप्यासः । नः । वयुनेषु । धूःसदः ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

पृक्षे पृक्षवते हविर्लक्षणान्नयुक्ताय यजमानाय ता तानि विश्वा सर्वाणि भुवनान्युदकानि मित्राय । वाशब्द उपमार्थः । मित्रायेव सदं सदा आ ववक्षिरे । मरुत अवहंति । यद्वा वाशब्दोऽवधारणे । मित्रभूताय यजमानाय्कॆव पृक्षेऽन्ने निमित्तभूते सति वृष्ट्युदकान्यावहंति । कीदृशा मरुतः । जीरदानवः ।

pṛkṣe pṛkṣavate havirlakṣaṇānnayuktāya yajamānāya tā tāni viśvā sarvāṇi bhuvanānyudakāni mitrāya | vāśabda upamārthaḥ | mitrāyeva sadaṃ sadā ā vavakṣire | maruta avahaṃti | yadvā vāśabdo 'vadhāraṇe | mitrabhūtāya yajamānāykèva pṛkṣe 'nne nimittabhūte sati vṛṣṭyudakānyāvahaṃti | kīdṛśā marutaḥ | jīradānavaḥ |

p. 234

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 34, p. 234.

क्षिप्रदानाः । पृषदश्वासः पृषद्भिः श्वेतबिंदुभिर्युक्ता अश्वा येषां ते तथोक्ताः । अनवभ्रराधसः ॥ भृशु भ्रंशु अधःपतने । अवभ्रंशनमवभ्रः । डोऽन्यत्रापि दृश्यते । सा. ६-२-४८-४ । इति दप्रत्ययः । नास्त्ववभ्रो यस्येति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तर- पदांतोदात्तत्वं । अनवभ्रं भ्रंशनरहितं राधो धनं येषां ते । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ऋजिप्यासोन । ऋजु अकुटिलं प्राप्नुवंतो गच्छंतोऽश्वा इव वयुनेषु गंतृषु मध्यॆ धूर्षदो धुरि मेघस्य वहने सीदंतो निषण्णा इत्यर्थः ॥

kṣipradānāḥ | pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ pṛṣadbhiḥ śvetabiṃdubhiryuktā aśvā yeṣāṃ te tathoktāḥ | anavabhrarādhasaḥ ‖ bhṛśu bhraṃśu adhaḥpatane | avabhraṃśanamavabhraḥ | ḍo 'nyatrāpi dṛśyate | sā. 6-2-48-4 | iti dapratyayaḥ | nāstvavabhro yasyeti bahuvrīhau nañsubhyāmityuttara- padāṃtodāttatvaṃ | anavabhraṃ bhraṃśanarahitaṃ rādho dhanaṃ yeṣāṃ te | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ ‖ ṛjipyāsona | ṛju akuṭilaṃ prāpnuvaṃto gacchaṃto 'śvā iva vayuneṣu gaṃtṛṣu madhyè dhūrṣado dhuri meghasya vahane sīdaṃto niṣaṇṇā ityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: the Maruts always bring all the waters to the sacrificer provided with food, as to a friend, or bring the rain-waters for him alone when food is the occasion; their steeds are spotted, their wealth undiminishing, and they sit at the yoke of the cloud.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

जीरदानवः (jīradānavaḥ)—those who give without delay; अनवभ्रराधसः (anavabhrarādhasaḥ)—those who have wealth free from destruction; पृषदश्वासः (pṛṣadaśvāsaḥ)—those who have horses of a colour in the form of spots; ऋजिप्यासो न (ṛjipyāso na)—like horses running straight; वयुनेषु (vayuneṣu)—in the paths to be traversed; धूर्षदः (dhūrṣadaḥ)—those who sit in the chariot in the form of the cloud, being the Maruts; पृक्षे (pṛkṣe)—to the sacrificer who is provided with food in the form of the oblation; ता विश्वा भुवना (tā viśvā bhuvanā)—all the water; मित्राय वा (mitrāya vā)—as one gives respectfully to a friend; सदं (sadaṃ)—always; आ ववक्षिरे (ā vavakṣire)—bring.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, who give without delay, who have wealth free from destruction, who have horses of a colour in the form of spots, and who sit in the chariot in the form of the cloud like horses running straight along the paths, always bring all the water to the sacrificer who is provided with food in the form of the oblation, as one gives respectfully to a friend.

Printed English translation

The prompt-giving Maruts ever confer upon the (offerer of sacrificial) food, as upon a friend, all these (world-supporting) waters: they who have spotted deer for steeds, who are possessed of inexhaustible riches, aud [sic] who, seated in their chariots, (proceed) amongst the moving (clouds), like horses going straight (to the goal).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पृक्षे विश्वा भुवना मित्राय वा आववक्षिरे (pṛkṣe viśvā bhuvanā mitrāya vā āvavakṣire)—हनिर्लक्षणान्नयुक्ताय यजमानाय सर्वाणि उदकानि मित्रायेव मरुतः सदा आवहंति । यदा वा शब्दो अवधारणे मित्रभूताय यजमानाय्कॆव पृक्षे अन्ने निमित्तभूते सति वृष्ट्युदकान्यावहंति । (hanirlakṣaṇānnayuktāya yajamānāya sarvāṇi udakāni mitrāyeva marutaḥ sadā āvahaṃti | yadā vā śabdo avadhāraṇe mitrabhūtāya yajamānāykèva pṛkṣe anne nimittabhūte sati vṛṣṭyudakānyāvahaṃti |) (as supplied, हनिर्लक्षण (hanirlakṣaṇa); compare हविर्लक्षण (havirlakṣaṇa) in the bhāṣya): the Maruts always bring all the waters to the sacrificer provided with food in the form of the oblation, as to a friend; or else, the word वा (vā) being for emphasis, they bring the rain-waters to the sacrificer who is like a friend, when food is the occasion. Here two kinds of meaning have been given for the particle वा (vā), that of comparison and that of emphasis. From this two

p. 235

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 19, p. 237 (as supplied; the page is p. 235 in the sequence of this window).

Note: the text of this page begins with a fresh Special Topics label and with entries that do not follow the sentence broken off at the end of p. 234 ("From this two …"); the page is reproduced as supplied, and the order of the supplied pages may need checking by the user.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

समन्यवः—समानमनस्काः, समानक्रोधाः समानतेजसो वा । (samanyavaḥ—samānamanaskāḥ, samānakrodhāḥ samānatejaso vā |) The author of the Nirukta has read the word मन्यु (manyu) among the names of anger (नि. ३-९ (ni. 3-9)) and has explained: मन्युर्मन्यतेर्दिप्तिकर्मणः क्रोधकर्मणो वधकर्मणो वा (manyurmanyaterdiptikarmaṇaḥ krodhakarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā) (नि. १०-३१ (ni. 10-31)). It is said that the Marut deities are of one kind of mind, of one kind of anger and splendour, and भ्राजदृष्टयः—दीप्यमानायुधाः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ—dīpyamānāyudhāḥ), having weapons that shine, and so they are described as coming to the sacrificial hall.

धेनुभिः रष्यदूधभिः अध्वस्मभिः पथिभिः हंसासो न स्वसराणि—प्रीणयितृभिः महोधस्कैः यद्वा शब्दायमानोच्छ्रितप्रदेशैः मेघैस्सह मार्गैरेव वा यथा हंसाः स्वकीयानि निवासस्थानानि प्राप्नुवंति तद्वत् । (dhenubhiḥ raṣyadūdhabhiḥ adhvasmabhiḥ pathibhiḥ haṃsāso na svasarāṇi—prīṇayitṛbhiḥ mahodhaskaiḥ yadvā śabdāyamānocchritapradeśaiḥ meghaissaha mārgaireva vā yathā haṃsāḥ svakīyāni nivāsasthānāni prāpnuvaṃti tadvat |) The way and the order in which the Maruts come to the sacrifices for the drinking of Soma are stated. It is explained that they come to the sacrificial hall, as swans reach their own dwelling places, either with the clouds that gladden the whole world and are provided with abundant (thick) streams of water, or that sound and stand in lofty regions, or by the paths.

रष्यदूधभिः—विरष्यीति महन्नाम । ऊधांसि जलस्रोतो मार्गः । महोधस्कैः । यद्वा शब्दायमानोच्छ्रितप्रदेशाः । (raṣyadūdhabhiḥ—viraṣyīti mahannāma | ūdhāṃsi jalasroto mārgaḥ | mahodhaskaiḥ | yadvā śabdāyamānocchritapradeśāḥ |) विरष्यी (viraṣyī) is stated among the names of the great (नि. ३-१३ (ni. 3-13)). The path along which water pours down in a stream is called ऊधन् (ūdhan). Sāyaṇa has explained it as "having drops (streams) of thick water", or as "lofty regions that make a strong sound".

पथिभिः—पतंति गच्छंतीति पंथानो मेघाः । (pathibhiḥ—pataṃti gacchaṃtīti paṃthāno meghāḥ |) Because they are of a moving nature, the clouds are spoken of by the word पंथानः (paṃthānaḥ).

मधोर्मदाय-सोमस्य मदार्थं । (madhormadāya-somasya madārthaṃ |) The word मधु (madhu) is stated among the names of water (नि. २-२४ (ni. 2-24)). And—

मरुत्ता इंद्र वृषभो रणाय पिबा सोममनुष्वधं मदाय । आ सिंचस्व जठरे मध्व ऊर्मिं त्वं राजासि प्रदिवः सुतानां ॥

maruttā iṃdra vṛṣabho raṇāya pibā somamanuṣvadhaṃ madāya | ā siṃcasva jaṭhare madhva ūrmiṃ tvaṃ rājāsi pradivaḥ sutānāṃ ‖

(म. सं. ३-४७-१ (ma. saṃ. 3-47-1))

In this Ṛk: मधु न ऊर्मि० । मधु सोमं इत्यौपमिकं माद्यतेः । इदमपीतर-न्मध्वेतस्मादेव । (नि. ४-८) (madhu na ūrmi0 | madhu somaṃ ityaupamikaṃ mādyateḥ | idamapītara-nmadhvetasmādeva | (ni. 4-8)) (as supplied). Because it produces intoxication, Soma is described as the meaning of the word मधु (madhu).

p. 236

Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 34 (as supplied). The page begins with the Pada-pāṭha of Ṛk 5; its Saṃhitā-pāṭha was not on this page.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

इंधन्वभिः । धेनुभिः । रप्यदूधभिः । अध्वस्मभिः । पथिभिः । भ्राजत् ऽयष्टयः । आ । हंसासः । न । स्वसराणि । गंतन । मधोः । मदाय । मरुतः । समन्यवः ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

समन्यवः समानमनस्काः समानक्रोधाः समानतेजसो ना हे मरुतो भ्राजदृष्टयो दीप्यमानायुधा यूयमिंधन्वभिः समिंधनवद्भिः ॥ इंधन- शब्दाच्छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्त्वर्थीयो वनिप् । छांदसो वर्णलोपः ॥ धेनुभिः प्रीणयितृभिश्च रष्यदूधभिः । विरप्यीति महन्नाम । महोधस्मैः । ऊधांसि जलस्रोतोमार्गः । यद्वा रप लप व्यक्तायां वाचि । शब्दायमानोच्चृत- प्रदेशैरध्वस्मभिर्ध्वंसनरहितैः पथिभिः । पतंति गच्छंतीति पंथानो मेघाः । एवं- भूतैर्मेघैः सह मार्गैरेव नागंतन । किमर्थं । मधोर्मदाय । सोमस्य मदार्थं । तत्र दृष्टांतः । हंसासो न । यथा हंसाः स्वसराणि स्वकीयानि निवासस्थानानि प्राप्नुवंति तद्वत् ॥

samanyavaḥ samānamanaskāḥ samānakrodhāḥ samānatejaso nā he maruto bhrājadṛṣṭayo dīpyamānāyudhā yūyamiṃdhanvabhiḥ samiṃdhanavadbhiḥ ‖ iṃdhana- śabdācchaṃdasīvanipāviti mattvarthīyo vanip | chāṃdaso varṇalopaḥ ‖ dhenubhiḥ prīṇayitṛbhiśca raṣyadūdhabhiḥ | virapyīti mahannāma | mahodhasmaiḥ | ūdhāṃsi jalasrotomārgaḥ | yadvā rapa lapa vyaktāyāṃ vāci | śabdāyamānoccṛta- pradeśairadhvasmabhirdhvaṃsanarahitaiḥ pathibhiḥ | pataṃti gacchaṃtīti paṃthāno meghāḥ | evaṃ- bhūtairmeghaiḥ saha mārgaireva nāgaṃtana | kimarthaṃ | madhormadāya | somasya madārthaṃ | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | haṃsāso na | yathā haṃsāḥ svasarāṇi svakīyāni nivāsasthānāni prāpnuvaṃti tadvat ‖

Gist: O Maruts of one mind, with shining weapons, come by the unobstructed paths of the clouds, with their full-uddered streams, for the joy of the Soma, as swans reach their own dwellings.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

समन्यवः (samanyavaḥ)—those of equal minds; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; भ्राजदृष्टयः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ)—you who have shining weapons; इंधन्वभिः (iṃdhanvabhiḥ)—lustrous; धेनुभिः (dhenubhiḥ)—satisfying; रष्यदूधभिः (raṣyadūdhabhiḥ)—having great streams of water; अध्वस्मभिः (adhvasmabhiḥ)—indestructible; पथिभिः (pathibhiḥ)—by the paths of the clouds; मधोः (madhoḥ)—obtained by drinking the Soma juice; मदाय (madāya)—for joy [the supplied text has ಹಷಾರ್ಥವಾಗಿ, as printed]; स्वसराणि (svasarāṇi)—going to and reaching their own dwelling places; हंसासो न (haṃsāso na)—like swans, with a stately gait; आ गंतन (ā gaṃtana)—come.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts of equal minds, you who have shining weapons, come, with the lustrous cows (clouds) and by the indestructible paths of the clouds that have great streams of water, for the joy to be obtained from drinking the Soma juice, like swans with a stately gait going to and reaching their own dwellings.

Printed English translation

Maruts, who are of one mind, and are armed with shining lances, come with the bright, full-uddered cows, by unobstructed paths, to partake of the exhilaration of the (soma) juice, as swans (fly) to their nests.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

समन्यवः—समानमनस्काः, समानक्रोधाः समानतेजसो वा । (samanyavaḥ—samānamanaskāḥ, samānakrodhāḥ samānatejaso vā |) The author of the Nirukta has read the word मन्यु (manyu) among the names of anger (नि. (ni.) 3-9) and has explained: मन्युर्मन्यतेर्दिप्तिकर्मणः क्रोधकर्मणो वधकर्मणो वा (manyurmanyaterdiptikarmaṇaḥ krodhakarmaṇo vadhakarmaṇo vā) (नि. (ni.) 10-31). It is described that the Marut deities have one and the same kind of mind, one and the same kind of anger and splendour, and are भ्राजदृष्टयः—दीप्यमानायुधाः (bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ—dīpyamānāyudhāḥ), having shining weapons; they are described as coming to the sacrificial hall.

धेनुभिः रष्यदूधभिः अध्वस्मभिः पथिभिः हंसासो न स्वसराणि—प्रीणयितृभिः महोधस्कैः यद्वा शब्दायमानोच्छ्रितप्रदेशैः मेघैसह् मार्गैरेव वा यथा हंसाः स्वकीयानि निवासस्थानानि प्राप्नुवंति तद्वत् । (dhenubhiḥ raṣyadūdhabhiḥ adhvasmabhiḥ pathibhiḥ haṃsāso na svasarāṇi—prīṇayitṛbhiḥ mahodhaskaiḥ yadvā śabdāyamānocchritapradeśaiḥ meghaisah mārgaireva vā yathā haṃsāḥ svakīyāni nivāsasthānāni prāpnuvaṃti tadvat |) The way and the order in which the Maruts come to the sacrifices for the drinking of Soma are stated. It is explained that they come to the sacrificial hall, either with the clouds that gladden the whole world and have abundant (thick) streams of water, or that sound and stand in lofty regions, or by the paths, as swans reach their own dwelling places.

रष्यदूधभिः—विरष्यीति महन्नाम । ऊधांसि जलस्रोतोमार्गः । महोधस्कैः । यद्वा शब्दायमानोच्छ्रितप्रदेशाः । (raṣyadūdhabhiḥ—viraṣyīti mahannāma | ūdhāṃsi jalasrotomārgaḥ | mahodhaskaiḥ | yadvā śabdāyamānocchritapradeśāḥ |) विरष्यी (viraṣyī) is stated among the names of the great (नि. (ni.) 3-13). The path along which water pours down in a stream is called ऊधन् (ūdhan). Sāyaṇa has explained it as "having drops (streams) of thick water", or as "lofty regions that make a strong sound".

पथिभिः—पतंति गच्छंतीति पंथानो मेघाः । (pathibhiḥ—pataṃti gacchaṃtīti paṃthāno meghāḥ |) Because they are of a moving nature, the clouds are spoken of by the word पंथानः (paṃthānaḥ).

मधोर्मदाय—सोमस्य मदार्थं । (madhormadāya—somasya madārthaṃ |) The word मधु (madhu) is stated among the names of water (नि. (ni.) 2-24). And—

समन्यवः समानमनसः समानक्रोधा वा हे मरुतो नोऽस्माकं ब्रह्माणि ॥ अन्ननामैतत् ॥ अन्नानि सवनान्यभिषुतसोमलक्षणानि हवींष्यागंतन । आगच्छत ॥ गमेर्लोटि छांदसः शपो लुक् । तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति तस्य तनबादेशः । आत एव जित्वाभावादनुनासिकलोपाभावः ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । नरां न शंसः । नरामस्माकं शंसः शंसनीयं स्तोत्रं यथागच्छथ तद्वत् ॥ नरशब्दात् षष्ठीबहुवचनस्यानित्य- मागमशासनमिति नुडभावः । शंसः कर्मणि घञंत आद्युदात्तः । सुपां सुलुगित्यमः सुआदेशः ॥ आगत्य च धेनुमुदकदानेन प्रीणयितारमश्वामिवोधनि पिप्यत । यथाश्वाः पीनावयवा भवंति तद्वन्मेघं वर्षणसमर्थमाप्यायितं कुरुतेत्यर्थः । अपि च जरित्रॆ स्तोत्रे वाजपेशसं वाजैरन्नॆराश्लिष्टं ॥ पिश अवयवे ॥ धियं कर्म कर्त । कुरुत ॥ करोतेश्छांदसः शपो लुक् । पूर्ववत्तशब्दस्य तबादेशः ॥

samanyavaḥ samānamanasaḥ samānakrodhā vā he maruto no 'smākaṃ brahmāṇi ‖ annanāmaitat ‖ annāni savanānyabhiṣutasomalakṣaṇāni havīṃṣyāgaṃtana | āgacchata ‖ gamerloṭi chāṃdasaḥ śapo luk | taptanaptanathanāścati tasya tanabādeśaḥ | āta eva jitvābhāvādanunāsikalopābhāvaḥ ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | narāṃ na śaṃsaḥ | narāmasmākaṃ śaṃsaḥ śaṃsanīyaṃ stotraṃ yathāgacchatha tadvat ‖ naraśabdāt ṣaṣṭhībahuvacanasyānitya- māgamaśāsanamiti nuḍabhāvaḥ | śaṃsaḥ karmaṇi ghañaṃta ādyudāttaḥ | supāṃ sulugityamaḥ suādeśaḥ ‖ āgatya ca dhenumudakadānena prīṇayitāramaśvāmivodhani pipyata | yathāśvāḥ pīnāvayavā bhavaṃti tadvanmeghaṃ varṣaṇasamarthamāpyāyitaṃ kurutetyarthaḥ | api ca jaritrè stotre vājapeśasaṃ vājairannèrāśliṣṭaṃ ‖ piśa avayave ‖ dhiyaṃ karma karta | kuruta ‖ karoteśchāṃdasaḥ śapo luk | pūrvavattaśabdasya tabādeśaḥ ‖

(मि. सं. (mi. saṃ.) 3-47-1, as supplied)

In this Ṛk: मधु न ऊर्मि० । मधु सोमं इत्यौपमिकं माद्यतेः । इदमपीतरन्मध्वेतस्मादेव । (madhu na ūrmi0 | madhu somaṃ ityaupamikaṃ mādyateḥ | idamapītaranmadhvetasmādeva |) (नि. (ni.) 4-8). Because it produces intoxication, Soma is described as the meaning of the word मधु (madhu).

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

म॒रुत्वा॑ इंद्र वृष॒भो रणा॑य॒ पिबा॒ सोम॑मनुष्व॒धं मदा॑य । आ सिं॑चस्व ज॒ठरे॒ मध्व॑ ऊ॒र्मिं त्वं राजा॑सि प्र॒दिवः॑ सु॒तानां॑ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आ नो ब्रह्माणि मरुतः समन्यवो नरां न शंसः सवनानि गंतन । अश्वामिव पिप्यत धेनुमूधनि कर्ता धियं जरिते वाजपेशसं ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

आ । नः । ब्रह्माणि । मरुतः । समन्यवः । नरां । न । शंसः । सवनानि । गंतन । अश्वां इव । पिप्यत । धेनुं । ऊधनि । कर्त । धियं । जरित्रे । वाजपेशसं ॥ ६ ॥

ā | naḥ | brahmāṇi | marutaḥ | samanyavaḥ | narāṃ | na | śaṃsaḥ | savanāni | gaṃtana | aśvāṃ iva | pipyata | dhenuṃ | ūdhani | karta | dhiyaṃ | jaritre | vājapeśasaṃ ‖ 6 ‖

Gist: O Maruts of one mind, come to our food-offerings and Soma-libations as to the praise of men, make the cloud swell like a mare's udder, and fashion a rite that brings food to the singer.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

समन्यवः (samanyavaḥ)—those of equal minds; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; नः (naḥ)—to be offered by us; ब्रह्माणि (brahmāṇi)—the food; सवनानि (savanāni)—the Soma juice that has been pressed [as supplied: हिंदल्पट्ट (hiṃdalpaṭṭa)], desiring it; नरां (narāṃ)—of men (like us); शंसः न (śaṃsaḥ na)—as you come desiring praises; आ गंतन (ā gaṃtana)—come; (then) धेनुं (dhenuṃ)—the cloud that satisfies by giving water; अश्वामिव ऊधनि (aśvāmiva ūdhani)—as one makes the limbs of mares robust by giving them water to drink; पिप्यत (pipyata)—make it swell so as to be rain-producing; जरित्रे (jaritre)—for the singer; वाजपेशसं (vājapeśasaṃ)—so as to provide food; धियं (dhiyaṃ)—the rite; कर्त (karta)—perform. (The supplied text of this page ends here, at माडिरि (māḍiri), without Bhāvārtha or printed English.)

p. 239

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts of one mind, come desiring the food offered by us and the pressed Soma juice, just as you come desiring the praises of men like us. Then make the cloud, which gratifies by giving water, swell so as to produce rain, as one makes the limbs of mares robust by giving them water to drink. Perform the rite so that food is provided to the singer.

Printed English translation

Maruts, who are of one mind, come to the food that is offered a1 (our) sacrifices, as (you come) to the praises of men : nourish the milch cow. (the cloud), so that it may be like a mare with a full udder, and render the pious rite productive of abundant food to the worshipper. [sic: "a1" as supplied; line break after "cow." as supplied]

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

On the first part (नः ब्रह्माणि सवनानि नरां न शंसः आ गंतन (naḥ brahmāṇi savanāni narāṃ na śaṃsaḥ ā gaṃtana)) the bhāṣya says: as our food, that is, oblations in the form of pressed Soma, come to us like praise that is worthy of being praised. The Kannada explanation adds: addressing the Maruts, the sacrificers say that, just as the Maruts come to hear the hymns we recite, they should come to accept the carefully pressed Soma juice and the food in the form of oblation that we offer.

On धेनुं अश्वामिव ऊधनि पिप्यत (dhenuṃ aśvāmiva ūdhani pipyata) the bhāṣya says: as mares become plump-limbed through giving them water, so make the cloud capable of raining and swollen. The explanation adds: the Maruts, coming to the sacrificial hall and accepting the oblations we offer, should delight the whole world by pouring rain; as well-fed horses are robust, the cloud, filled with waters and capable of producing rain, should be made to swell so as to give us joy; this is the wish expressed.

On जरित्रे वाजपेशसं धियं कर्त (jaritre vājapeśasaṃ dhiyaṃ karta) the bhāṣya says: perform for the singer a rite embraced by food. The explanation adds: the Maruts should perform the duties so that food increases for us, who recite praises at the sacrifices as priests or sacrificers; thus it is described.

ब्रह्माणि (brahmāṇi) means foods. The word ब्रह्म (brahma) is said to occur among the names of food (Ni. 3-9) and among the names of wealth (Ni. 3-9) [both references as supplied].

p. 240

The Special Topics continue; the Ṛk cited for ब्रह्माणि (brahmāṇi) is:

यामधर्वा मनुष्यता दध्यङ्छयमत्नत । तस्मिन् ब्रह्माणि पूर्वथेंद्र उक्ता समग्मतार्चन्ननु स्वराज्यं ॥

yāmadharvā manuṣyatā dadhyaṅchayamatnata | tasmin brahmāṇi pūrvatheṃdra uktā samagmatārcannanu svarājyaṃ ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 1-80-16)

In that verse ब्रह्माणि (brahmāṇi) is explained as "works" (कर्माणि (karmāṇi)). Here the meaning "food" is given.

The word धेनु (dhenu) is said to occur among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23). Here धेनुं (dhenuṃ) is used in the sense of "the one who gratifies" (प्रीणयितारं (prīṇayitāraṃ)), the one who delights.

जरित्रे (jaritre) means स्तोत्रे (stotre), "for the singer". The word जरिता (jaritā) is said to occur among the names of singers (Ni. 3-19). The meaning is explained as the priests who recite praises.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तं नो॑ दात मरुतो वा॒जिनं॒ रथ॑ आपा॒नं ब्रह्म॑ चि॒तय॑द्दि॒वेदि॑वे । इषं॑ स्तो॒तृभ्यो॑ वृ॒जने॑षु का॒रवे॑ स॒निं मे॒धामरि॑ष्टं दु॒ष्करं॒॑ सहः ॥ ७ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तं । नः । दात । मरुतः । वाजिनं । रथे । आपानं । ब्रह्म । चितयत् । दिवेदिवे । इषं । स्तोतृभ्यः । वृजनेषु । कारवे । सनिं । मेधां । अरिष्टं । दुस्तरं । सहः ॥७॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतः तं पुत्रं नोऽस्मभ्यं दात । दत्त प्रयच्छत ॥ छांदसः शपो लुक् ॥ कीदृशं । वाजिनमन्नवंतं बलवंतं वा । रथे रंहणे युष्मदीय आगमने निमित्तभूते सति दिवेदिवे प्रतिदिवसं चितयत् प्रज्ञापयत् युष्मद्गुणप्रख्यापकं । ब्रह्म स्तोत्रमापानमाप्नुवंतं । अपि च इषमन्नं स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं दात । प्रयच्छत । तथा वृजनेषु संग्रामेषु कारवे स्तोत्रे ॥ वचनव्यत्ययः ॥ मेधां युद्ध प्रज्ञानं सनिं धनदातृत्वं चारिष्टं शत्रुभिरहिंसितं दुस्तरं शत्रुभिस्तरीतुमशक्यं सहो बलं च प्रयच्छत ॥

he marutaḥ taṃ putraṃ no 'smabhyaṃ dāta | datta prayacchata ‖ chāṃdasaḥ śapo luk ‖ kīdṛśaṃ | vājinamannavaṃtaṃ balavaṃtaṃ vā | rathe raṃhaṇe yuṣmadīya āgamane nimittabhūte sati divedive pratidivasaṃ citayat prajñāpayat yuṣmadguṇaprakhyāpakaṃ | brahma stotramāpānamāpnuvaṃtaṃ | api ca iṣamannaṃ stotṛbhyo 'smabhyaṃ dāta | prayacchata | tathā vṛjaneṣu saṃgrāmeṣu kārave stotre ‖ vacanavyatyayaḥ ‖ medhāṃ yuddha prajñānaṃ saniṃ dhanadātṛtvaṃ cāriṣṭaṃ śatrubhirahiṃsitaṃ dustaraṃ śatrubhistarītumaśakyaṃ saho balaṃ ca prayacchata ‖

Gist: O Maruts, give us that son, rich in food and strength, who daily proclaims your praise; also give food, battle-wisdom, liberality, and unharmed, unconquerable strength.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मरुतः (marutaḥ) (Marutaḥ)—O Maruts; वाजिनं (vājinaṃ)—him who has food; रथे (rathe)—on account of your coming; दिवेदिवे (divedive)—every day; चितयत् (citayat)—describing and making known your qualities; ब्रह्म (brahma)—the hymn;

p. 241

आपानं (āpānaṃ)—him who composes and recites; तं (taṃ)—that son; नः (naḥ)—to us; दात (dāta)—give; इषं (iṣaṃ)—food; स्तोतृभ्यः (stotṛbhyaḥ)—to us, the singers (give); वृजनेषु (vṛjaneṣu)—in battles; कारवे (kārave)—to the singer; मेधां (medhāṃ)—intelligence endowed with skill in battle; सनिं (saniṃ)—liberality in giving wealth; अरिष्टं (ariṣṭaṃ)—freedom from harm by enemies; दुस्तरं (dustaraṃ)—unrepelled by enemies; सहः (sahaḥ)—strength (give).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, give us, the singers, the son who is rich in food and who, on account of your coming, daily composes and recites the hymn that describes and makes known your qualities, and give food. In battles, give to the singer the skill needed to fight, freedom from harm by enemies, and unrepelled strength.

Printed English translation

Bestow upon us, Maruts, that (son) who shall enjoy abundance, and who shall be repeating your appropriate praises day by day to (induce) your coming: give food to those who praise you ; to him who glorifies you in battles: (grant him) liberality. intelligence, and unimpaired unsurp assable vigour.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing the Maruts as हे मरुतः (he marutaḥ), the sacrificers pray नः तं पुत्रं दात (naḥ taṃ putraṃ dāta): "may the Maruts grant us a son." The son they pray for is, in the bhāṣya's words, one who has food or strength and who, on account of the Maruts' coming, daily attains a hymn proclaiming their qualities. The explanation adds: the son granted to the sacrificers should be possessed of food and strength, and should daily recite their praises at the time of the Maruts' coming to the sacrifice; thus it is wished. And the sacrificers wish: स्तोतृभ्यः इषं, वृजिनेषु कारवे मेधां, सनिं, अरिष्टं, दुस्तरं महः प्रयच्छत (stotṛbhyaḥ iṣaṃ, vṛjineṣu kārave medhāṃ, saniṃ, ariṣṭaṃ, dustaraṃ mahaḥ prayacchata) (as supplied: वृजिनेषु (vṛjineṣu) and महः (mahaḥ) here, against वृजनेषु (vṛjaneṣu) and सहः (sahaḥ) in the Saṃhitā). May the Maruts grant food to the priests who recite praises; to him who recites the praise at the time of battle, intelligence that wins in battle; the generosity of giving wealth; and strength that cannot be despised by enemies.

The word कारु (kāru) is said to occur among the names of singers (Ni. 3-19).

p. 242

Sūkta 34, Ṛk 7, Special Topics (continued from p. 241): Sāyaṇa explains सनिं (saniṃ) as धनदातृत्वं (dhanadātṛtvaṃ) ("liberality in giving wealth"). Yāska has explained the meaning in this verse:

हिनोता नो अध्वरं देवयाज्या हिनोत ब्रह्म सनये धनानां । ऋतस्य योगे वि प्यध्वमूढः श्रुष्टिवरीर्भूतनास्मभ्यमापः ॥

hinotā no adhvaraṃ devayājyā hinota brahma sanaye dhanānāṃ | ṛtasya yoge vi pyadhvamūḍhaḥ śruṣṭivarīrbhūtanāsmabhyamāpaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-30-11)

Here he explains that सनये (sanaye) means लब्धये (labdhaye), "for the obtaining of wealth" (Ni. 6-22).

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यद्युं॒जते॑ म॒रुतो॑ रु॒क्मव॑क्ष॒सोऽश्वा॒न्रथे॑षु॒ भग॒ आ सु॒दान॑वः । धे॒नुर्न शिश्वे॒ स्वस॑रेषु पिन्नते॒ जना॑य रा॒तह॑विषे म॒हीमिषं॑ ॥ ८ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यत् । युंजते । मरुतः । रुक्ष्मवक्षसः । अश्वान् । रथेषु । भगे । आ । सुदानवः । धेनुः । न । शिश्वे । स्वसरेषु । पिन्नते । जनाय । रातहविषे । महीं । इषं ॥ ८ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

रुक्ष्मवक्षसो रोचमानाभरणोरस्काः सुदानवः शोभनदाना मरुतो यद्यदा रथेषु भगे भजनीये स्थाने । धुरीत्यर्थः । अश्वानायुंजते । अभिमु- ख्येन युक्तान्कुर्वंति । तदानीमेव रातहविषे दत्तहविष्काय यजमानाय महीं महतीमिषमन्नं तत्कारणभूतमुदकं वा स्वसरेषु स्वकीयेषु गृहेषु पिन्नते । सिंचंति किरंति ॥ पिवि सेचने ॥ तत्र दृष्टांतः । धेनुर्न शिश्वे । यथा धेनुः प्रसुत- स्तनी सती स्वकीयाय वत्साय क्षीरं प्रयच्छति तद्वत् ॥

rukṣmavakṣaso rocamānābharaṇoraskāḥ sudānavaḥ śobhanadānā maruto yadyadā ratheṣu bhage bhajanīye sthāne | dhurītyarthaḥ | aśvānāyuṃjate | abhimu- khyena yuktānkurvaṃti | tadānīmeva rātahaviṣe dattahaviṣkāya yajamānāya mahīṃ mahatīmiṣamannaṃ tatkāraṇabhūtamudakaṃ vā svasareṣu svakīyeṣu gṛheṣu pinnate | siṃcaṃti kiraṃti ‖ pivi secane ‖ tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | dhenurna śiśve | yathā dhenuḥ prasuta- stanī satī svakīyāya vatsāya kṣīraṃ prayacchati tadvat ‖

Gist: When the Maruts, with gleaming ornaments on their breasts, yoke their horses to the chariot-poles, they pour abundant food or water into the houses of the sacrificer, as a cow gives milk to her calf.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुक्मवक्षसः (rukmavakṣasaḥ)—those whose breasts bear golden ornaments; सुदानवः (sudānavaḥ)—those who give excellent gifts; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—the Maruts; यत् (yat)—when; रथेषु भगे (ratheṣu bhage)—in the yoke-regions of the chariots; अश्वान् (aśvān)—horses; आ युंजते (ā yuṃjate)—they yoke facing forward

p. 243

(at that very moment); रातहविषे (rātahaviṣe)—to him who has offered the oblation; जनाय (janāya)—to the sacrificer; महीं (mahīṃ)—great; इषं (iṣaṃ)—food; स्वसरेषु (svasareṣu)—in their own houses; शिश्वे (śiśve)—to her calf; धेनुर्न (dhenurna)—as a cow gives milk abundantly; पिन्वते (pinvate) [sic: printed पिन्नते (pinnate) in the Saṃhitā and Pada]—they pour out.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, whose breasts are adorned with golden ornaments and who give excellent gifts, the moment they yoke horses to their chariots, pour great food into the houses of the sacrificers who have offered oblations, as a cow gives abundant milk to her calf.

Printed English translation

When the golden-breasted munificent Maruts yoke their horses to their chariots on an auspicious (occasion), they shed in their peculiar (directions) abundant food upon him who offers them oblations, as a milch cow (gives milk) to her calf.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुक्मवक्षसः सुदानवः मरुतः (rukmavakṣasaḥ sudānavaḥ marutaḥ)—the Maruts, who wear golden ornaments (necklaces) on their breasts and give abundant gifts, sit in their chariots to receive the oblation at the sacrifice, and to the sacrificers who offer shares of the oblation, महीं इषं (mahīṃ iṣaṃ) (explained as great food, or the water that causes it), that is, abundant food, or the rain-waters that cause the growth of the plants and the like from which food arises, they grant. So it is described.

स्वसरेषु धेनुर्न शिश्वे (svasareṣu dhenurna śiśve)—the Sanskrit explanation given is स्वकीयेषु गृहेषु यथा धेनुः प्रस्तुतस्तनीयाय (svakīyeṣu gṛheṣu yathā dhenuḥ prastutastanīyāya) followed by वत्साय क्षीरं प्रयच्छति तद्वत् (vatsāya kṣīraṃ prayacchati tadvat) (as a cow gives milk to her calf). As cows in their own dwelling give milk for their calves, so the Maruts of their own accord bestow food and waters on the sacrificers who offer them oblations; thus their generosity is described.

The word स्वसर (svasara) is listed among the names of houses (Ni. 3-13) and among the names of days (Ni. 2-21), and Yāska has explained it in Ni. 5-4 (स्वसराण्य- (svasarāṇya-) ... स्वयं सारीण्यपिवा (svayaṃ sārīṇyapivā), the passage as supplied). Here it is used in the sense of "house".

p. 244

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यो नो॑ मरुतो वृ॒कता॑ति॒ मर्त्यो॑ रि॒पुर्द॒धे व॑सवो॒ रक्ष॑ता॒ रि॒षः । व॒र्तय॑त॒ तपु॑षा च॒क्रिया॒भि तमन॑ रुद्रा अ॒शसो॑ हंतना॒ वधः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यः । नः । मरुतः । वृकताति । मर्त्यः । रिपुः । दधे । वसवः । रक्षत । रिषः । वर्तयत । तपुषा । चक्रिया । अभि । तं । अव । रुद्राः । अशसः । हंतन । वधरिति ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतः यो मर्त्यो मनुष्यो वृकताति आदाताः वृकः ॥ वृक आदाने । वृकज्येष्ठाभ्यां तिल्तातिलौ च छंदसि । पा. ५-४-४१. । इति स्वार्थिकस्तातिल्पत्ययः ॥ तादृशः सन् नोऽस्माकं रिपुर्दधे । रिपुतयात्मानं धारयति । हे वसवो वासयि- तारो मरुतो रिषो हिंसकादस्मान्रक्षत । पालयत । आस्माकं शत्रुभूतं मर्त्य० तपुषा तापयित्रा चक्रिया ऋष्टाख्यया शक्त्याभिवर्तयत । अभितो निवर्तयत । हे रुद्रा रुद्रपुत्राः । यद्वा रोरूयमाणा द्रवंतः अशसो भक्षकस्य ॥ अश भोजन इत्यस्मादौणादिकोऽसिप्रत्ययः ॥ तादृशस्य राक्षसादेवधर्हनन- साधनमायुधमवहंतन । अवयुत्यास्मत्तः पृथक्कृत्य नाशयत ॥ हंतेर्लोटि तप्तनप्तनथनाश्चति तनप् ॥

he marutaḥ yo martyo manuṣyo vṛkatāti ādātāḥ vṛkaḥ ‖ vṛka ādāne | vṛkajyeṣṭhābhyāṃ tiltātilau ca chaṃdasi | pā. 5-4-41. | iti svārthikastātilpatyayaḥ ‖ tādṛśaḥ san no 'smākaṃ ripurdadhe | riputayātmānaṃ dhārayati | he vasavo vāsayi- tāro maruto riṣo hiṃsakādasmānrakṣata | pālayata | āsmākaṃ śatrubhūtaṃ martya0 tapuṣā tāpayitrā cakriyā ṛṣṭākhyayā śaktyābhivartayata | abhito nivartayata | he rudrā rudraputrāḥ | yadvā rorūyamāṇā dravaṃtaḥ aśaso bhakṣakasya ‖ aśa bhojana ityasmādauṇādiko 'sipratyayaḥ ‖ tādṛśasya rākṣasādevadharhanana- sādhanamāyudhamavahaṃtana | avayutyāsmattaḥ pṛthakkṛtya nāśayata ‖ haṃterloṭi taptanaptanathanāścati tanap ‖

The bhāṣya cites a Pāṇini sūtra (Pā. 5-4-41) for the affix तातिल् (tātil) in वृकताति (vṛkatāti), and an Uṇādi affix असि (asi) for अशसः (aśasaḥ). Gist: O Maruts, protect us from the mortal who, wolf-like, makes himself our enemy; turn him back with your burning weapon, and destroy the weapon of that devouring foe.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वसवः (vasavaḥ)—O you who provide dwelling-places; मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; यः मर्त्यः (yaḥ martyaḥ)—whatever mortal; वृकताति (vṛkatāti)—like a cruel wolf; नः (naḥ)—towards us; रिपुः (ripuḥ)—enmity; दधे (dadhe)—fosters; रिषः (riṣaḥ)—from that harmful enemy; रक्षत (rakṣata)—protect (us); तं (taṃ)—that enemy; तपुषा (tapuṣā)—with the burning; चक्रिया (cakriyā)—weapon called ṛṣṭi; अभि वर्तयत (abhi vartayata)—make him turn away from us; रुद्राः (rudrāḥ)—O Maruts, sons of Rudra; अशसः (aśasaḥ)—of such a devouring asura; वधः (vadhaḥ)—the weapon that kills; अव हंतन (ava haṃtana)—destroy.

p. 245

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, who provide dwelling-places, protect us from that harmful enemy, the man who fosters wolf-like enmity towards us as a cruel wolf would. With your burning weapon make that enemy turn away from us. O Maruts, sons of Rudra, destroy the weapon, the instrument of killing, of such a devouring asura.

Printed English translation

Maruts, grant ers [sic] of dwellings, protect us from the malignity of the man who cherishes wolf-like enmity against us : encompass him with your burning diseases ; ward off the murderous (weapon) of the devourer.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वसवः (vasavaḥ)—वासयितारः (vāsayitāraḥ) (those who make [the sacrificers] dwell happily): thus the Marut deities are addressed. यः मर्त्यः वृकताति रिपुर्दधे रिषः रक्षत (yaḥ martyaḥ vṛkatāti ripurdadhe riṣaḥ rakṣata)—the Sanskrit explanation is यः मनुष्यः आदाता वृकः सन् रिपुतया आत्मानं धारयति हिंसकादस्मान् पालयत (yaḥ manuṣyaḥ ādātā vṛkaḥ san riputayā ātmānaṃ dhārayati hiṃsakādasmān pālayata). The prayer is: the man who behaves like a wolf towards the sacrificers and practises enmity against them is harmful to us; protect us from him. And: अस्माकं शत्रुभूतं मर्त्यं तपुषा चक्रिया अभिवर्तयत (asmākaṃ śatrubhūtaṃ martyaṃ tapuṣā cakriyā abhivartayata) is explained as तापयित्रा ऋष्ट्या शक्त्या निवर्तयत (tāpayitrā ṛṣṭyā śaktyā nivartayata); that is, turn him back with your all-consuming power known as ṛṣṭi, so that no harm may come to us sacrificers from one who is our enemy.

For the word रुद्राः (rudrāḥ) the explanation is रुद्रपुत्राः रोरूयमाणाद्रवंतः (rudraputrāḥ rorūyamāṇādravaṃtaḥ): the Marut deities are addressed as sons of Rudra and as those who rush swiftly with a roaring sound. अशसः वधः अवहंतन (aśasaḥ vadhaḥ avahaṃtana)—भक्षकस्य राक्षसादेः हननसाधनमायुधं अस्मत्तः पृथक्कृत्य नाशयत (bhakṣakasya rākṣasādeḥ hananasādhanamāyudhaṃ asmattaḥ pṛthakkṛtya nāśayata): turn away from us the weapon that Rākṣasas and others, wishing to destroy us, employ to kill us, and destroy those Rākṣasas and the rest; thus protection is prayed for.

p. 246

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

चि॒त्रं तद्वो॑ मरुतो॒ याम॑ चेकिते॒ पृश्न्या॒ यदूध॒रप्या॒पयो॒॑ दु॒हुः । यद्वा॑न्॒दे नव॑मानस्य रुद्रियास्त्रि॒तं जरा॑य जुर॒ताम॑दाभ्याः ॥१०॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

चित्रं । तत् । वः । मरुतः । याम । चेकिते । पृश्न्याः । यत् । ऊधः । अपि । अपयः । दुहुः । यत् । वा । निदे । नवमानस्य । रुद्रियाः । त्रितं । जराय । जुरतां । अदाभ्याः ॥१०॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतो वो युष्माकं चित्रं चायनीयं याम प्रापणं चेकिते । सर्वैर्ज्ञायते । इदानीं परोक्षवदाह । अपिशब्दः प्रसिद्धौ । यद्यदा खलु पृश्ना माध्यमिकाया वाचः संबंधिनमूधरुद्धतं मेघमापयः प्रापयितारो मरुतो दुहुः । दुहंति ॥ दुहेश्छांदसो लिट् । छंदसि चेति वक्तव्यमिति द्विर्वचनाभावः ॥ यद्वा यदा च नवमानस्य स्तुवतस्तितस्य निदे निंदकाय शत्रवे हिंसां कृतवंत इति शेषः ॥ निदि कुत्सायां । क्विप् चेति क्विप् । तदानीं हे अदाभ्या अहिंस्या रुद्रिया रुद्रस्य पुत्रा मरुतस्त्रितमृषिं जुरतां हिंसतां शत्रूणां जराय जरणाय विनाशाय अभूतेति शेषः ॥

he maruto vo yuṣmākaṃ citraṃ cāyanīyaṃ yāma prāpaṇaṃ cekite | sarvairjñāyate | idānīṃ parokṣavadāha | apiśabdaḥ prasiddhau | yadyadā khalu pṛśnā mādhyamikāyā vācaḥ saṃbaṃdhinamūdharuddhataṃ meghamāpayaḥ prāpayitāro maruto duhuḥ | duhaṃti ‖ duheśchāṃdaso liṭ | chaṃdasi ceti vaktavyamiti dvirvacanābhāvaḥ ‖ yadvā yadā ca navamānasya stuvatastitasya nide niṃdakāya śatrave hiṃsāṃ kṛtavaṃta iti śeṣaḥ ‖ nidi kutsāyāṃ | kvip ceti kvip | tadānīṃ he adābhyā ahiṃsyā rudriyā rudrasya putrā marutastritamṛṣiṃ juratāṃ hiṃsatāṃ śatrūṇāṃ jarāya jaraṇāya vināśāya abhūteti śeṣaḥ ‖

Gist: The coming of the Maruts is known to all, when they approach the lofty cloud and milk it for rain, and when they destroy the reviler of Trita, who praises them.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; वः (vaḥ)—your; चित्रं (citraṃ)—wonderful; तत् याम (tat yāma)—coming; चेकिते (cekite)—is known by all; यत् (yat)—when; पृश्न्या? (pṛśnyā?)—related to Pṛśni; ऊधः (ūdhaḥ)—the cloud on high; अपयः (apayaḥ)—the Maruts who approach; दुहुः (duhuḥ)—call forth for the sake of rain; यद्वा (yadvā)—when indeed; नवमानस्य (navamānasya)—of Trita who praises (the line break splits the word); निदे (nide)—to the reviling asura they cause harm (then); अदाभ्याः (adābhyāḥ)—the unharmed ones; रुद्रियाः (rudriyāḥ)—the sons of Rudra, the Maruts; त्रितं (tritaṃ)—the sage called Trita; जुरतां (juratāṃ)—to the harming enemies; जराय (jarāya)—become destroyers.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, your wonderful coming is known to all. When the Maruts approach the lofty cloud that belongs to Pṛśni and call it forth for the sake of rain, when they cause harm to the reviling asura of Trita who praises them, then, unharmed and sons of Rudra, the Maruts become destroyers of the enemies who harm the sage Trita.

p. 247

Printed English translation

Maruts, your moryeallous [sic] energy is well known, whereby, seizing the udder of heaven, you milked it (of the rain), destroyed the reviler of your worshipper, and (came), irresistible sons of Rudra, to Trita for the destruction of his enemies.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यत् पृश्न्याः ऊदः आपयः दुहुः (yat pṛśnyāḥ ūdaḥ āpayaḥ duhuḥ)—यदा खलु माध्यमिकाया वाचः संबंधिनं उद्धतं मेघं प्रापयितारो मरुतः दुहंति (yadā khalu mādhyamikāyā vācaḥ saṃbaṃdhinaṃ uddhataṃ meghaṃ prāpayitāro marutaḥ duhaṃti): at the time when the Marut deities envelop the cloud, full of waters belonging to the middle-region speech, and pour down rain-waters, वः चित्रं याम चेकिते (vaḥ citraṃ yāma cekite)—युष्माकं चायनीयं प्रापणं सर्वैः ज्ञायते (yuṣmākaṃ cāyanīyaṃ prāpaṇaṃ sarvaiḥ jñāyate): the desirable coming of the Maruts is known to all. And: यद्वा नवमानस्य निदे अदाभ्याः रुद्रियाः त्रितं जुरतां जराय (yadvā navamānasya nide adābhyāḥ rudriyāḥ tritaṃ juratāṃ jarāya), explained as यदा च स्तुवतः त्रितस्य निंदकाय हिंसां कृतवंतः अहिंस्याः रुद्रस्य पुत्राः मरुतः त्रितं ऋषिं हिंसतां शत्रूणां विनाशाय अभूत (yadā ca stuvataḥ tritasya niṃdakāya hiṃsāṃ kṛtavaṃtaḥ ahiṃsyāḥ rudrasya putrāḥ marutaḥ tritaṃ ṛṣiṃ hiṃsatāṃ śatrūṇāṃ vināśāya abhūta): when the Marut deities, who are not subject to the harm done by others and are sons of Rudra, destroy those who harm the sage Trita, who has fallen into calamity and is praising them, they are the cause of the destruction of the enemies of the sage Trita; thus it is described, and also that the coming of the Maruts is known to all. The meaning of the word त्रित (trita) (Trita) has been explained earlier.

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

तान्नो॑ म॒हो म॒रुत॑ एव॒यान्नो॒ विष्णो॑रे॒षस्य॑ प्रभृ॒थे॑ ह॑वामहे हिर॑ण्यवर्णान्नकु॒हान्य॒तस्रु॑चो ब्रह्म॒ण्यंतः॒ शंस्यं॒ राध॑ ईमहे ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तान् । वः । महः । मरुतः । एव्‌याव्नः । विष्णोः । एषस्य । प्रभृथे । हवामहे । हिरण्यवर्णान् । ककुहान् । यतस्रुचः । ब्रह्मण्यंतः । शंस्यं । राधः । ईमहे ॥

tān | vaḥ | mahaḥ | marutaḥ | evyāvnaḥ | viṣṇoḥ | eṣasya | prabhṛthe | havāmahe | hiraṇyavarṇān | kakuhān | yatasrucaḥ | brahmaṇyaṃtaḥ | śaṃsyaṃ | rādhaḥ | īmahe ‖

p. 248

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुत एवयान्न एवं गंतव्यं स्तोत्रं यज्ञं वा गंत्र्यन् महो महतो महानुभावांस्तान्वो युष्मान्विष्टोर्व्यापकस्य ग्रहचमसादिषु सर्वत्र व्याप्य वर्तमानस्यैषस्यॆषणीयस्य प्रार्थनीयस्य सोमस्य प्रभृथे प्रभरणेऽभिष- वादिभिः प्रकर्षेण संपादने सति हवामहे । आह्वयामहे । आहूय च हिरण्य- वर्णान् हितरमणीयवर्णान्वा ककुहान् श्रेष्ठान् स्तुत्यान्वा एवंभूतांस्तान् यतस्रुचो यागायोद्यतस्रुचो ब्रह्मण्यंतः । ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं । तदिच्छंतो वयं शंस्यं प्रशंसनीयं राधो धनमीमहे । याचामहे ॥

he maruta evayānna evaṃ gaṃtavyaṃ stotraṃ yajñaṃ vā gaṃtryan maho mahato mahānubhāvāṃstānvo yuṣmānviṣṭorvyāpakasya grahacamasādiṣu sarvatra vyāpya vartamānasyaiṣasyèṣaṇīyasya prārthanīyasya somasya prabhṛthe prabharaṇe 'bhiṣa- vādibhiḥ prakarṣeṇa saṃpādane sati havāmahe | āhvayāmahe | āhūya ca hiraṇya- varṇān hitaramaṇīyavarṇānvā kakuhān śreṣṭhān stutyānvā evaṃbhūtāṃstān yatasruco yāgāyodyatasruco brahmaṇyaṃtaḥ | brahma stotraṃ | tadicchaṃto vayaṃ śaṃsyaṃ praśaṃsanīyaṃ rādho dhanamīmahe | yācāmahe ‖

Gist: We call the Maruts to the preparation of Soma in the cups; holding up our ladles and wishing to praise, we ask for praiseworthy wealth.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

मरुतः (marutaḥ)—O Maruts; एवयाव्यः (evayāvyaḥ)—who come toward our sacrifice; महः (mahaḥ)—of great majesty; तान् वः (tān vaḥ)—you; विष्णोः (viṣṇoḥ)—that pervades the cups and the rest; एषस्य (eṣasya)—desirable (Soma); प्रभृथे (prabhṛthe)—for the sake of its preparation; हवामहे (havāmahe)—we call; and हिरण्यवर्णान् (hiraṇyavarṇān)—golden-hued; ककुहान् (kakuhān)—excellent, those Soma vessels; यतस्रुचः (yatasrucaḥ)—we who hold up the ladles for the sacrifice; ब्रह्मण्यंतः (brahmaṇyaṃtaḥ)—and are possessed of praise; शंस्य (śaṃsya)—praiseworthy; राधः (rādhaḥ)—wealth; ईमहे (īmahe)—we ask.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, you who come toward our sacrifice and are of great majesty, we call for the sake of the preparation of the desirable Soma that fills the cups and the rest. And we, who hold up the ladles for the sacrifice toward those golden-hued, excellent Soma vessels and are possessed of praise, ask for praiseworthy wealth.

Printed English translation

We invoke you, mighty Maruts, who frequent such sacrifices (as this, to be present) at the offering of the diffusive and desirable (libation): lifting up our ladles, and reciting their praise, we solicit the golden-hued and lofty Maruts for excellent wealth.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Addressing the Marut deities with हे मरुतः (he marutaḥ), the passage एवयाव्यः महः वः विष्णोः ऐषस्य प्रभृथे हवामहे (evayāvyaḥ mahaḥ vaḥ viṣṇoḥ aiṣasya prabhṛthe havāmahe) is explained: एवं गंतव्यं स्तोत्रं यज्ञं वा गन्तान् महानुभावान् (evaṃ gaṃtavyaṃ stotraṃ yajñaṃ vā gantān mahānubhāvān)

p. 249

युष्मान् ग्रहचमसादिषु सर्वत्र व्याप्य वर्तमानस्य प्रार्थनीयस्य सोमस्य अभिषवादिभिः प्रकर्षण संपादने सति आह्वयामहे (yuṣmān grahacamasādiṣu sarvatra vyāpya vartamānasya prārthanīyasya somasya abhiṣavādibhiḥ prakarṣaṇa saṃpādane sati āhvayāmahe). It is described thus: the sacrificers invite the Marut deities, of abundant majesty, who come on hearing the praise recited under a particular discipline, or who come to sacrifices performed in the prescribed manner, after the Soma has been prepared by pressing and the other rites, filling the vessels called graha or camasa, in which oblations are offered in the fire, and Soma being worthy of praise.

ककुर्हा (kakurhā) [sic]—श्रेष्ठा स्तुत्यान् वा (śreṣṭhā stutyān vā): the word कुकुह (kukuha) [sic] is read by Yāska among the words for "great" (Nirukta 3-13). The Maruts are described as superior to all by their majesty (excellent), or as worthy of praise. And हिरण्यवर्णान् (hiraṇyavarṇān)—हितरमणीयवर्णान् (hitaramaṇīyavarṇān): of a colour pleasing to all, or of a charming radiance; having the bodily lustre of gold: so the Maruts are described.

ब्रह्मण्यंतः यतस्रुचः (brahmaṇyaṃtaḥ yatasrucaḥ)—ब्रह्म स्तोत्रं तदिच्छंतः उद्यतस्रुचः (brahma stotraṃ tadicchaṃtaḥ udyatasrucaḥ): it is described that at the time of the sacrifice the priests recite the praises and hold up in their hands the vessels with which the oblation full of offerings is poured.

शंस्यं राधः ईमहे (śaṃsyaṃ rādhaḥ īmahe)—प्रशंसनीयं धनं प्रार्थयामहे (praśaṃsanīyaṃ dhanaṃ prārthayāmahe): it is explained that in the sacrifices the sacrificers and priests invite the Maruts, fill the vessels used for the oblation with the offering-material and make them ready, stand ready to pour the oblation in the fire, offer the oblation to the Maruts, and then pray that excellent wealth be given.

Ṛk 12

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ते दश॑ग्वाः प्रथ॒मा य॒ज्ञमू॑हिरे॒ ते नो॑ हिन्वंतू॒षसो॒ व्यु॑ष्टिषु । उ॒षा न रा॒मीर॑रु॒णैरपो॑र्णुते म॒हो ज्योति॑षा शुच॒ता॑ गोअर्णसा ॥ १२ ॥

te daśagvāḥ prathamā yajñamūhire te no hinvaṃtūṣaso vyuṣṭiṣu | uṣā na rāmīraruṇairaporṇute maho jyotiṣā śucatā goarṇasā ‖ 12 ‖

p. 250

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ते । दशग्वाः । प्रथमाः । यज्ञं । ऊहिरे । ते । नः । हिन्वंतु । उषसः । विउष्टिषु । उषाः । न । रामीः । अरुणैः । अप । ऊर्णुते । महः । ज्योतिषा । शुचता । गोऽर्णसा ॥ १२ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतो दशग्वाः । ये दशभिर्मासैः सिद्धिं गता अंगिरसस्तद्रूपा भूता प्रथमा आदित्येभ्यः प्रथमभाविनः संतो यज्ञमूहिरे । अवहन् । आदित्यानामंगि- रसां च स्वर्गगमनं प्रति स्पर्धमानानां मध्यॆ पूर्वमेवांगिरसो यागाननु- ष्ठाय स्वर्गं प्राप्ताः । तथा च श्रूयते । आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नंगिरसश्च तेऽग्रेऽग्नि- नाग्निमयजंतेति । तादृशास्त्र उषसो व्युष्टिषु विवासेषु प्रभातेषु सत्सु नोऽस्मान् हिन्वंतु । प्रेरयंतु ॥ हि गतौ वृदौ च ॥ रामीः कृष्णवर्णा रात्रिरुषा न यथोषा अरुणैरारोचमानैः स्वतेजोभिरपोर्णुते । अपवृणोत्यपसारयति। तथा महो महता शुचता दीप्यमानेन गोअर्णसा गच्छदुदकेन ; ज्योतिषा सूर्याख्येन तमो निवारयंति । सूर्यमंडलमावृण्वतो वृत्रादीन् हत्वा सर्वं जगत्पकाशयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

he maruto daśagvāḥ | ye daśabhirmāsaiḥ siddhiṃ gatā aṃgirasastadrūpā bhūtā prathamā ādityebhyaḥ prathamabhāvinaḥ saṃto yajñamūhire | avahan | ādityānāmaṃgi- rasāṃ ca svargagamanaṃ prati spardhamānānāṃ madhyè pūrvamevāṃgiraso yāgānanu- ṣṭhāya svargaṃ prāptāḥ | tathā ca śrūyate | ādityāścaivehāsannaṃgirasaśca te 'gre 'gni- nāgnimayajaṃteti | tādṛśāstra uṣaso vyuṣṭiṣu vivāseṣu prabhāteṣu satsu no 'smān hinvaṃtu | prerayaṃtu ‖ hi gatau vṛdau ca ‖ rāmīḥ kṛṣṇavarṇā rātriruṣā na yathoṣā aruṇairārocamānaiḥ svatejobhiraporṇute | apavṛṇotyapasārayati| tathā maho mahatā śucatā dīpyamānena goarṇasā gacchadudakena ; jyotiṣā sūryākhyena tamo nivārayaṃti | sūryamaṃḍalamāvṛṇvato vṛtrādīn hatvā sarvaṃ jagatpakāśayaṃtītyarthaḥ ‖

Gist: The Maruts, in the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, performed the sacrifice before the Ādityas; may they urge us at dawn, as Uṣas drives away the dark nights with her ruddy lights.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

ते (te)—those same Maruts; दशग्वाः (daśagvāḥ)—having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months; प्रथमाः (prathamāḥ)—ready before the Ādityas; यज्ञमूहिरे (yajñamūhire)—carried out the sacrifice; ते (te)—those same Maruts; उषसः (uṣasaḥ)—of Uṣas; व्युष्टिषु (vyuṣṭiṣu)—at the time of her manifestation; नः (naḥ)—us; हिन्वंतु (hinvaṃtu)—may they urge on; रामिाः (rāmiāḥ) [as printed]—the dark-coloured nights; उषाः (uṣāḥ)—Uṣas; अरुणैः (aruṇaiḥ)—with attractive lights; अपोर्णुते न (aporṇute na)—as she drives away and destroys (so also the Maruts); महः (mahaḥ)—great; शुचता (śucatā)—shining; गोअर्णसा (goarṇasā)—drawing up the water in the form of mist; ज्योतिषा (jyotiṣā)—with the light called the Sun (they destroy the darkness).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Those same Maruts, having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, were ready before the Ādityas and carried out the sacrifice. May those same Maruts urge us at the time of the manifestation of Uṣas. Uṣas drives away the dark-coloured nights with her attractive

p. 251

lights, pushing them far away and destroying them, so the Maruts too destroy the darkness with their own radiance called the Sun, which is great, shining and drinks up the water in the form of mist.

English Translation (as printed)

May they, who, the first celebrators of the tenmonths' [sic] rite, accomplished this sacrifice, reanimate us at the rising dawn ; for as the dawn with purple rays drives away the night, so (do they scatter the darkness) with great, and pure. and [sic] mist-dispelling radiance.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

ते दशग्वाः प्रथमाः यज्ञमूहिरे - मरुतः ये दशभिः मासैः सिद्धिंगताः अंगिरसः तद्रूपा भूत्वा आदित्येभ्यः प्रथमभाविनः संतः यज्ञमवहन् । आदित्यानां अंगिरसां च स्वर्गगमनं प्रति स्पर्धमानानां मध्यॆ पूर्वमेवांगिरसो यागा- ननुष्ठाय स्वर्गं प्राप्ताः ।

te daśagvāḥ prathamāḥ yajñamūhire - marutaḥ ye daśabhiḥ māsaiḥ siddhiṃgatāḥ aṃgirasaḥ tadrūpā bhūtvā ādityebhyaḥ prathamabhāvinaḥ saṃtaḥ yajñamavahan | ādityānāṃ aṃgirasāṃ ca svargagamanaṃ prati spardhamānānāṃ madhyè pūrvamevāṃgiraso yāgā- nanuṣṭhāya svargaṃ prāptāḥ |

It is explained: the Maruts, having taken the form of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months only, were present before the Ādityas and carried out the sacrifice. A contest arose between the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, at one time, as to who should reach heaven first; the Aṅgirases performed the sacrifice first and attained heaven before the Ādityas. This story is told in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 1-16): “आदित्याश्चैवेहासन्नंगिरसश्च तेऽग्रॆग्निनाग्निमयजंत” (“ādityāścaivehāsannaṃgirasaśca te 'grègnināgnimayajaṃta”). Sāyaṇa describes the Maruts as having the identity of the Aṅgirases who attained success in ten months, as born and established before the Ādityas, and as performing sacrifices. The inquiry into this identity of the Aṅgirases and the Maruts has been explained in the earlier volumes.

ते उषसः व्युष्टिषु नः हिन्वंतु तादृशाः ते मरुतः प्रभातेषु सत्सु अस्मान् प्रेरयॆंतु ।

te uṣasaḥ vyuṣṭiṣu naḥ hinvaṃtu tādṛśāḥ te marutaḥ prabhāteṣu satsu asmān prerayèṃtu |

It is said: those same Maruts, when the dawns have broken, may urge us on; that is, may the Maruts, of abundant power, urge us, the sacrificers, to our necessary duties after the time of dawn has passed, that is, in the morning.

रामाः उषाः न अरुणैः अपोर्णुते महः शुचता गोअर्णसा ज्योतिषा— कृष्णवर्णाः राश्रीः उषाः यथा आरोचमानैः स्वतेजोभिः अपसारयति कथा महता दीप्यमानेन गच्छदुदकेन सूर्याख्येन तमः निवारयंति । सूर्यमंडल- मावृण्वतो वृत्रादीन् हत्वा सर्वं जगत् प्रकाशयंति ।

rāmāḥ uṣāḥ na aruṇaiḥ aporṇute mahaḥ śucatā goarṇasā jyotiṣā— kṛṣṇavarṇāḥ rāśrīḥ uṣāḥ yathā ārocamānaiḥ svatejobhiḥ apasārayati kathā mahatā dīpyamānena gacchadudakena sūryākhyena tamaḥ nivārayaṃti | sūryamaṃḍala- māvṛṇvato vṛtrādīn hatvā sarvaṃ jagat prakāśayaṃti |

(The first word of this gloss is printed रामाः (rāmāḥ) in the supplied text, where रामीः (rāmīḥ) would be expected from the Saṃhitā; given as supplied.) It is described: as Uṣas drives away the night, black with darkness, with her well-shining lights, so the Maruts, filled with water, cover the sun, kill Vṛtra and the others who make darkness, break up the cloud that prevents the sun's light

p. 252

from reaching the world, and make light for the world. So it is described.

Ṛk 13

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ते क्षो॒णीभि॑ररु॒णेभि॒र्नांजिभी॑ रु॒द्रा ऋ॒तस्य॒ सद॑नेषु वावृधुः । नि॒मेघ॑माना॒ अत्ये॑न॒ पाज॑सा सुश्चं॒द्रं वर्ण०॑ दधिरे सु॒पेश॑सं ॥१३॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ते । क्षोणीभिः । अरुणेभिः । न । अंजिभिः । रुद्राः । ऋतस्य । सदनेषु । ववृधुः । निमेघमानाः । अत्येन । पाजसा । सुचंद्रं । वर्णं । दधिरे । सुपेशसं ॥ १३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

रुद्रा रुद्रपुत्रास्ते मरुतः क्षोणीभिः शब्दकारिभिर्विर्णाख्यैर्विणाविशेषैर- रुणेभिर्नांजभिः ॥ नशब्दः समुच्चये ॥ आरोचमानैररुणवर्णैर्वा रूपाभिव्यंज- कैरलंकारैश्च समन्विताः संत ऋतस्योदकस्य सदनेषु निवासभूतेषु मेघेषु वावृधुः । वर्धंते । अपि च अत्येन सततगामिना शीघ्रं व्याप्नुवता पाजसात्मीयेन बलेन निमेघमाना नितरां मेघादुदकं चिंतयंतस्ते सुचंद्रं शोभनाह्लादनं सुपेशसं ॥ पेश इति रूपनाम ॥ शोभनरूपं वर्णं दधिरे । कांतिं धारयंति ॥

rudrā rudraputrāste marutaḥ kṣoṇībhiḥ śabdakāribhirvirṇākhyairviṇāviśeṣaira- ruṇebhirnāṃjabhiḥ ‖ naśabdaḥ samuccaye ‖ ārocamānairaruṇavarṇairvā rūpābhivyaṃja- kairalaṃkāraiśca samanvitāḥ saṃta ṛtasyodakasya sadaneṣu nivāsabhūteṣu megheṣu vāvṛdhuḥ | vardhaṃte | api ca atyena satatagāminā śīghraṃ vyāpnuvatā pājasātmīyena balena nimeghamānā nitarāṃ meghādudakaṃ ciṃtayaṃtaste sucaṃdraṃ śobhanāhlādanaṃ supeśasaṃ ‖ peśa iti rūpanāma ‖ śobhanarūpaṃ varṇaṃ dadhire | kāṃtiṃ dhārayaṃti ‖

Gist: The Maruts, sons of Rudra, equipped with sounding lutes and red ornaments, grow in the clouds, the abodes of water, and take on a fair, lovely colour.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

रुद्राः (rudrāḥ)—the Maruts, sons of Rudra; ते (te)—they; क्षोणीभिः (kṣoṇībhiḥ)—provided with lutes having charming sounds; अरुणेभिर्न (aruṇebhirna)—like the red colour; अंजिभिः (aṃjibhiḥ)—adorned with ornaments; ऋतस्य (ṛtasya)—of water; सदनेषु (sadaneṣu)—in the clouds that are its abodes; वावृधुः (vāvṛdhuḥ)—they grow; अत्येन (atyena)—swift-going; पाजसा (pājasā)—with their own strength; निमेघमानाः (nimeghamānāḥ)—squeezing the water out of the cloud; सुश्चंद्रं (suścaṃdraṃ)—delightful; सुपेशसं (supeśasaṃ)—showing an attractive form; वर्णं (varṇaṃ)—the lustre; दधिरे (dadhire)—they obtain.

p. 253

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Maruts, sons of Rudra, provided with lutes of charming sounds and adorned with ornaments like the red colour, grow in the clouds, the abodes of water. Squeezing the water of the cloud by their swift strength, they possess a lustre that is delightful and shows an attractive form.

English Translation (as printed)

They, the Rudras (equipped) with melodious (lutes), and decorated with purple ornaments, exalt in the dwellings of the waters ; and scattering the clouds with rapid vigour, they are endowed with delightful and beautiful forms.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

रुद्राः—रुद्रपुत्राः

rudrāḥ—rudraputrāḥ

The word रुद्र (rudra) is explained as "children of Rudra"; the Maruts, sons of Rudra,

क्षोणीभिः—शब्दकारीभिः विणाख्यैः वीणावीशेषैः ।

kṣoṇībhiḥ—śabdakārībhiḥ viṇākhyaiḥ vīṇāvīśeṣaiḥ |

are provided with sounding lutes called वाणि (vāṇi) (Sāyaṇa's gloss has विणाख्यैः (viṇākhyaiḥ), as supplied). And

अरुणेभिः नांजिभिः—अरुण वर्णैः ना रूपाभिव्यंजकैरलंकारैश्च समन्विताः ।

aruṇebhiḥ nāṃjibhiḥ—aruṇa varṇaiḥ nā rūpābhivyaṃjakairalaṃkāraiśca samanvitāḥ |

they are endowed with a red colour of great brightness, or with ornaments that bring out (make beautiful) the form (shape), and so they grow in the middle of the clouds. Again,

अत्येन पाजसा निमेघमानाः सुश्चंद्रं सुपेशसं वर्ण० दधिरे—शीघ्रं व्याप्नुवता आत्मीयेन बलेन मेघादुदकं नितरां चितयंतः शोभनाह्लादनं शोभनरूपं कांतिं धार यंति ।

atyena pājasā nimeghamānāḥ suścaṃdraṃ supeśasaṃ varṇa0 dadhire—śīghraṃ vyāpnuvatā ātmīyena balena meghādudakaṃ nitarāṃ citayaṃtaḥ śobhanāhlādanaṃ śobhanarūpaṃ kāṃtiṃ dhāra yaṃti |

the Maruts, with their (powerful) strength that quickly spreads, make the rain-water pour from the clouds without remaining at all (completely); they are very delightful and bear a form of beautiful shape. So it is explained.

सुपेशसं— पेश इति रूपनाम ।

supeśasaṃ— peśa iti rūpanāma |

The word पेशसं (peśasaṃ) is given among the names of form (Ni. 3-13) and among the names of gold, and is explained: पेश इति रूपनाम पिंशतेर्विपिशितं भवति (peśa iti rūpanāma piṃśatervipiśitaṃ bhavati) (Ni. 8-12).

p. 254

Ṛk 14

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ता इ॑या॒नो महि॒ वरू॑थमू॒तय॒ उप॒ फेदे॒ना नम॑सा गृणीमसि । त्रि॒तो न यान्पंच॒ होत्था॑न॒भिष्ट॑य आव॒नवर्त॒दव॑राञ्च॒क्रियाव॑से ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

तान् । इयानः । महि । वरूथं । ऊतये । उप । घ । इत् । एना । नमसा । गृणेमसि । त्रितः । न । यान् । पंच । होत्यन् । अभिष्टये । आववर्तत् । अवरान् । चक्रिया । अवसे ॥ १४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

तान् मरुतो महि महद्वरूथं वरणीयं प्रशस्तं धनं तन्मरुत ऊतये रक्षणार्थमियान इयाना याचमाना वयं ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति जसः सुः ॥ एनानेन नमसा नमस्कारेण स्तोत्रेण वोपेत् उपेत्य गृणीमसि । स्तुमः ॥ घेति पादपू- रणः । एनेत्यत्र सुपां सुलुगिति तृतीयाया आजादेशः । नशब्दः समुच्चये ॥ त्रित ऋषिश्च यानेतान् मरुतः पंच होत्थन् अध्यात्मप्राणापानादिपंचवृत्तात्मना वर्तमानान् अत एव होमनिष्पादकान् अवरान् मुख्यानभिष्टयेऽभिलषितसिद्ध्यर्थं चक्रिया नाभिचक्रेणावसेऽवितुं संगंतुमाववर्तत् । स्वस्मान्निर्जिगमिषून्प्राणान् स्वात्माभिमुखमावर्तयत् । यद्वा चक्रिया ऋष्टाख्येनायुधेन युक्तान् अवसे स्तुत्यादिभिस्तर्पयितुमावर्तयत् । तान् स्तुम इति संबंधः ॥ ववर्तदिति वृतेर्ण्यं- ताल्लुजि चङि रूपं ॥

tān maruto mahi mahadvarūthaṃ varaṇīyaṃ praśastaṃ dhanaṃ tanmaruta ūtaye rakṣaṇārthamiyāna iyānā yācamānā vayaṃ ‖ supāṃ sulugiti jasaḥ suḥ ‖ enānena namasā namaskāreṇa stotreṇa vopet upetya gṛṇīmasi | stumaḥ ‖ gheti pādapū- raṇaḥ | enetyatra supāṃ sulugiti tṛtīyāyā ājādeśaḥ | naśabdaḥ samuccaye ‖ trita ṛṣiśca yānetān marutaḥ paṃca hotthan adhyātmaprāṇāpānādipaṃcavṛttātmanā vartamānān ata eva homaniṣpādakān avarān mukhyānabhiṣṭaye 'bhilaṣitasiddhyarthaṃ cakriyā nābhicakreṇāvase 'vituṃ saṃgaṃtumāvavartat | svasmānnirjigamiṣūnprāṇān svātmābhimukhamāvartayat | yadvā cakriyā ṛṣṭākhyenāyudhena yuktān avase stutyādibhistarpayitumāvartayat | tān stuma iti saṃbaṃdhaḥ ‖ vavartaditi vṛterṇyaṃ- tālluji caṅi rūpaṃ ‖

Gist: We, imploring the Maruts for ample, choice wealth for protection, approach and praise them with this homage; Trita turned the five Maruts towards himself.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

न (na)—and; पंच (paṃca)—five in number, as prāṇa, apāna and the rest; यान् (yān)—which Maruts; अवरान् (avarān)—very chief; होत्यन् (hotyan)—as priests (for the sacrifice); अभिष्टये (abhiṣṭaye)—for the accomplishment of his desired end; चक्रिया (cakriyā)—with their weapons; अवसे (avase)—for protecting himself;

p. 255

त्रितः (tritaḥ)—Trita; अववर्तत् (avavartat)—whom he prayed not to go out and held back in himself; तान् (tān)—those Maruts; मही (mahi)—great; वरूथं (varūthaṃ)—and praiseworthy wealth; ऊतये (ūtaye)—for protection; इयानः (iyānaḥ)—we who pray; एना नमसा (enā namasā)—with this praise accompanied by homage; उप इत् (upa it)—approaching; गृणीमसि (gṛṇīmasi)—we praise.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We who pray for great and praiseworthy wealth for protection approach with this praise accompanied by homage, and praise those Maruts — the five, prāṇa, apāna and the rest, whom Trita, for the accomplishment of his desired end, as very chief priests of the sacrifice, and for protecting himself with their weapons, prayed not to go out and held back within himself.

English Translation (as printed)

Imploring them for ample wealth, and (having recourse to him) for protection, we glorify them with this praise ; like the five chief priests whom Trita detained for the (performance of) the sacrifice, and to protect it with their weapons.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

त्रितः यान् पंच होत्यन् अपर्रा अभिष्टये चक्रिया अवसे आववर्तत्-त्रित ऋषिः एतान् मरुतः अध्यात्मप्राणापानादिपंचवृत्तात्मना वर्तमानान् आत एव होमनिष्पादकान् मुख्यान् अभिलषितसिद्ध्यर्थं, नाभिचक्रेण अनितुं संगंतुं स्वस्मा न्निर्जिगमिषून् प्राणान् स्वात्माभिमुखमावर्तयत् । यद्वा चक्रिया ऋष्टाख्येना युधेन युक्तान् स्तुत्यादिभिः तर्पयितुं आवर्तयत् !

tritaḥ yān paṃca hotyan aparrā abhiṣṭaye cakriyā avase āvavartat-trita ṛṣiḥ etān marutaḥ adhyātmaprāṇāpānādipaṃcavṛttātmanā vartamānān āta eva homaniṣpādakān mukhyān abhilaṣitasiddhyarthaṃ, nābhicakreṇa anituṃ saṃgaṃtuṃ svasmā nnirjigamiṣūn prāṇān svātmābhimukhamāvartayat | yadvā cakriyā ṛṣṭākhyenā yudhena yuktān stutyādibhiḥ tarpayituṃ āvartayat !

Here the word पंचहोत्यन् (paṃcahotyan) is used in the sense that in this body the Maruts (the winds), bearing the names prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna and samāna, dwell doing their respective functions in keeping with the body, as the maintainers of the state of the self. By this it is indicated that they are the chief means by which the worship of the bodily Vaiśvānara fire is accomplished. Since their seat is in the heart as prāṇa, in the anal region as apāna, and in the navel as samāna, the sage Trita held these Maruts, who were eager to go out of the body, in the Svādhiṣṭhāna wheel in the navel, and made them face himself; and it is said that by this Trita's protection came about, and that these Maruts are chief in bringing about all desired ends and the meditation that takes the form of worship of the self; and also that in the sacrifices performed in the world by the sacrificers, the Marut deities, receiving the oblations, are chief in accomplishing the sacrificers' desires.

p. 256

The Marut deities' accomplishing of the oblation is described in two ways, and their chief place in fulfilment of desires in three ways. In the second sense, the Maruts bear a spear-weapon named ṛṣṭi; and for protecting the sacrificers, or those who praise them, the sage Trita turned them back so that they should be in his navel-wheel, in order to please the Maruts with praise and the like. So it is explained.

तान् महि वरूथं ऊतये इयानः उप इत् गृणीमसि—मरुतः महत् प्रशस्तं धनं तत्! मरुतः रक्षणार्थं यजमानाः वयं अनेन नमस्कारेण स्तोत्रेण वा उपेत्य स्तुमः

tān mahi varūthaṃ ūtaye iyānaḥ upa it gṛṇīmasi—marutaḥ mahat praśastaṃ dhanaṃ tat! marutaḥ rakṣaṇārthaṃ yajamānāḥ vayaṃ anena namaskāreṇa stotreṇa vā upetya stumaḥ

Thus it is described: we sacrificers, praying to the Marut deities for obtaining the wealth that can necessarily be had for our protection, and for protecting us, will worship them with homage or with praises.

The word वरूथ (varūtha) is mentioned by Yāska among the names of houses (Ni. 3 13). Here Sāyaṇa gives the sense "choice" and explains it as praiseworthy wealth. In त्रितः न (tritaḥ na) he states that the word न is used in the sense of conjunction (नशब्दः समुच्चये (naśabdaḥ samuccaye)).

Ṛk 15

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यया॑ र॒ध्रं पा॒रय॒थात्यंहो॒ यया॑ नि॒दो मुं॒चथ॒॑॑ वंदितारं । अ॒र्वाची॒ सा म॑रुतो॒ या व॑ ऊ॒तिरो षु वा॒श्रेव॑ सुम॒तिर्जि॑- गातु ॥ १५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यया । रध्रं । पारयथ । अति । अंहः । यया । निदः । मुंचथ । वंदितारं । अर्वाची । सा । मरुतः । या । वः । ऊतिः । ओ इति । सु । वाश्राइव । सुमतिः । जिगातु ॥ १५ ॥

yayā | radhraṃ | pārayatha | ati | aṃhaḥ | yayā | nidaḥ | muṃcatha | vaṃditāraṃ | arvācī | sā | marutaḥ | yā | vaḥ | ūtiḥ | o iti | su | vāśrāiva | sumatiḥ | jigātu ‖ 15 ‖

p. 257

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 21, p. 257.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे मरुतो ययोत्या रध्रमाराधकं यजमानमंहः पापमति पारयथ। अतिक्रमयथ । ययोत्या वंदितारं स्तोतारं निदो निंदितुः शत्रोः सकाशान्मुं- चथ । मोचयथ । हे मरुतो वो युष्मदीया योतिः सर्वाच्यस्मदभिमुखा भवतु । तथा सुमतिर्युष्मदीया शोभना मतिरनुग्रहात्मिका बुद्धिश्च वाश्रेव हंभारवं कुर्वती धेनुरिव वत्सं सुष्टु ओ जिगातु । एवं गच्छतु । आस्मान् प्रति सर्वथागच्छत्व्यर्थः ॥

he maruto yayotyā radhramārādhakaṃ yajamānamaṃhaḥ pāpamati pārayatha| atikramayatha | yayotyā vaṃditāraṃ stotāraṃ nido niṃdituḥ śatroḥ sakāśānmuṃ- catha | mocayatha | he maruto vo yuṣmadīyā yotiḥ sarvācyasmadabhimukhā bhavatu | tathā sumatiryuṣmadīyā śobhanā matiranugrahātmikā buddhiśca vāśreva haṃbhāravaṃ kurvatī dhenuriva vatsaṃ suṣṭu o jigātu | evaṃ gacchatu | āsmān prati sarvathāgacchatvyarthaḥ ‖

Gist: O Maruts, may the protection by which you carry the worshipper over sin and free the praiser from the reviler, and your gracious thought, like a cow lowing to her calf, come towards us.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Marutaḥ—O Maruts; yayā—by which protection; radhram—the worshipping sacrificer; aṃhaḥ—from sin; ati pārayatha—you carried over; yayā—by which protection; vaṃditāram—the devotee who praises you; nidaḥ—from the reviling enemy; muṃcatha—you released; vaḥ—your; yā ūtiḥ—that well-known protection which is yours; sā—that; arvācī—may it be turned towards us; vāśreva—as a cow, making her sound of affection, goes to and joins her calf; sumatiḥ—your gracious thought also; su—exceedingly; o jigātu—may it come towards us.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Maruts, by whatever protection you carried the worshipping sacrificer across sin, and by whatever protection you freed the devotee who praises you from the reviling enemy, may that same protection be turned towards us also. As a cow, making her sound of affection, goes to her calf, may your gracious thought also spread exceedingly towards us.

English Translation (as printed)

Maruts, may that protection wherewith you convey the worshipper beyond sin, wherewith you rescue thc [sic] reciter of your praise from the scoffer, be present with us: may your benign disposition tend towards us, like a loving (cow towards her calf).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यया ऊत्या रध्रं अंहतः अति पारयथ, वंदितारं निदः मुंचथ वः सा आर्वाची—अराधकं यजमानं पापमतिक्रमयथ स्तोतारं निंदितुः शत्पोः सकाशात् मोचयथ युष्मदीया सा ऊतिः अस्मदभिमुखा भवतु ।

yayā ūtyā radhraṃ aṃhataḥ ati pārayatha, vaṃditāraṃ nidaḥ muṃcatha vaḥ sā ārvācī—arādhakaṃ yajamānaṃ pāpamatikramayatha stotāraṃ niṃdituḥ śatpoḥ sakāśāt mocayatha yuṣmadīyā sā ūtiḥ asmadabhimukhā bhavatu |

Explained thus: the Maruts carry the worshipping sacrificer across sins; they free the praiser from the reviling enemy; may that protection of yours be turned towards us. The Marut deities are said to possess a manner of protection that carries across sins the sacrificer who serves them, and

p. 258

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35, p. 258.

that destroys the enemies who revile and injure those who praise them, and protects the latter. So the power of protection belonging to the Maruts is to be turned towards the sacrificers; thus the sacrificers' prayer is described.

सुमतिः वाश्रेव सुष्टु ओजिगातु - युष्मदीया शोभना मतिः अनुग्रहात्मिका बुद्धिश्च हंभारवं कुर्वती धेनुरिव वत्समिव गच्छतु

sumatiḥ vāśreva suṣṭu ojigātu - yuṣmadīyā śobhanā matiḥ anugrahātmikā buddhiśca haṃbhāravaṃ kurvatī dhenuriva vatsamiva gacchatu

The thought of the Marut deities, which protects others or bestows favour, is to be well disposed towards us sacrificers, as a milch cow approaches her calf with a lowing sound. So it is prayed.

The varga-end mark that follows (a number between tildes) is garbled in the supplied text and is not read.

Sūkta 35 (Maṇḍala 2)

The thirty-fifth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

उपेमिति पंचदशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभमपांनपाद्दे- वताकं । > तथा चानुक्रांतं । उपेमपोनप्रीयमिति ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः ॥

Gist: the third sūkta of the fourth anuvāka, of fifteen ṛks, of the Gārtsamada seer, in triṣṭubh, for Apāṃ Napāt; the Anukramaṇī is quoted; the use of the sūkta is by the Liṅga (indication).

Anuvāda (Kannada). This sūkta beginning उपेमसृक्षि (upemasṛkṣi) [as supplied] is the third sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has fifteen ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer; Apāṃ Napāt is the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: उपेमपोनप्रीयमिति (upemaponaprīyamiti) [as supplied]. The use (viniyoga) is laiṅgika (by indication).

Sūkta 35 — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 35; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Vargas 22, 23, 24. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 15. Seer: Gṛtsamada (the label is printed as "यमः" for ऋषिः). Deity: Apāṃ Napāt (printed "अपांसपात्" [sic]). Metre: triṣṭubh.

p. 259

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 7, Varga 22, p. 259.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उपे॑मसृक्षि वाज॒युर्व॑च॒स्यां चनो॑ दधीत ना॒द्यो गिरो॑ मे । अ॒पां नपा॑दाशु॒हेमा॑ कु॒वित्स सु॒पेश॑सस्करति॒ जोषि॑ष॒द्धि ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उप । ईं । अस्पृक्षि । वाजयुः । वचस्यां । चनः । दधीत । नाद्यः । गिरिः । मे । अपां । नपात् । आशुहेमा । कुवित् । सः । सुपेशसः । करति । जोषिषत् । हि ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥
