Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

यमु॒ पूर्व॒महु॑वे॒ तमि॒दं हु॑वे॒ सेदु॒ हव्यो॑ द॒दिर्यो नाम॒॑ पत्यते । अ॒ध्व॒र्युभिः॒ प्रस्थि॑तं सो॒म्यं मधु॑ प्रो॒त्रात्सोमं॑ द्रविणोदः॒॒॑॑ पिब ऋतुभिः ॥ २ ॥

yamu pūrvamahuve tamidaṃ huve sedu havyo dadiryo nāma patyate | adhvaryubhiḥ prasthitaṃ somyaṃ madhu protrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba ṛtubhiḥ ‖ 2 ‖

(Note: the supplied Saṃhitā text of this Ṛk reads प्रोत्रात्सोमं (protrātsomaṃ) where Ṛk 1 and the bhāṣya have होत्रात् (hotrāt); also पत्यते (patyate), सोम्यं (somyaṃ); kept as supplied, not corrected.)

p. 320

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यं । ऊं इति । पूर्वं । अहुवे । तं । इदं । हुवे । सः । इत् । ऊं इति । हव्यः । ददिः । यः । नाम । पत्यते । अध्वर्युभिः । प्रस्थितं । सोम्यं । मधु । प्रोत्रात् । सोमं । द्रविणःदः । पिब । ऋतुभिः ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे द्रविणोदो यमु यं त्वामेव पूर्वं होतृकर्तृके सोमया- गेऽहुवे । आहूतवानस्मि इदं संप्रति तं तमेव पोतृकर्तृके सोमयागे हुवे। अह्वयामि । सेत् स एव द्रविणोदा हव्यो ह्वातव्यः ॥ उ इति पूरणे ॥ ददिरभीष्ट- फलस्य दाता यो नाम यः खलु पत्यते देवतात्वेनेष्टे तस्मै द्रविणोदसे सोम्यं सोमात्मकं मध्वध्वर्युभिः प्रस्थितं प्रणीतमासीत् । हे द्रविणोदः पोत्रात् पोतुर्यागादृतुभिरूर्जसंज्ञकैः सह सोमं पिब ॥

Gist: O Draviṇodas, you whom I called in the Hotṛ's Soma sacrifice I now call in the Potṛ's; the Soma is ready; drink it from the Potṛ's sacrifice with the Ṛtus called Ūrja.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Draviṇodaḥ — O Draviṇodas). Yamu — you whom. Pūrvaṃ — formerly (in the Soma sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ). Ahuve — I invoked with prayer. Idaṃ — now (in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ as well). Taṃ — that same you. Huve — I call. Set — that same you, renowned as Draviṇodas. Havyaḥ — are worthy of invocation. Yo nāma — which god. Dadiḥ — as the giver of desired ends. Patyate — is renowned. (For that Draviṇodas) Somyaṃ — consisting of Soma. Madhu — intoxicating oblation. Adhvaryubhiḥ — by the Adhvaryus. Prasthitaṃ — has been brought. Draviṇodaḥ — O Draviṇodas. Potrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ. Ṛtubhiḥ — together with the deities called Ūrja. Somaṃ — the Soma. Piba — drink.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Draviṇodas, you whom I formerly invoked with prayer in the Soma sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, that same you I now call in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ as well. You, renowned as Draviṇodas, are worthy of invocation. For that god who is renowned as the giver of desired ends, an oblation consisting of Soma and intoxicating has been brought by the Adhvaryus. O Draviṇodas, in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ, drink the Soma together with the deities called Ūrja.

p. 321

Printed English translation

He, whom I formerly invoked, and whom I now invoke, is verily worthy of invocation, for he is renowned as a benefactor: the Soma libation has been brought by thc [sic] priests : drink, Dravinodas, along with the Ritus, the Soma, the offering of the Potri.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

यं उ पूर्वं अहुवे इदं तं हुवे (yaṃ u pūrvaṃ ahuve idaṃ taṃ huve) — हे द्रविणोदः यं त्वां होतृकर्तृके सोमयागे आहूतवानस्मि संप्रति तमेव पोतृकर्तृके सोमयागे आह्वयामि । (he draviṇodaḥ yaṃ tvāṃ hotṛkartṛke somayāge āhūtavānasmi saṃprati tameva potṛkartṛke somayāge āhvayāmi |) The sacrificer addresses the deity Draviṇodas again: O Draviṇodas, earlier (in the previous Ṛk) I invited you to drink Soma together with the Ṛtus in the Hotṛ's sacrifice. Now in the Soma sacrifice performed by the priest called Potṛ also, I invite you to come to the sacrificial ground with the deities presiding over the month called Ūrja (Kārttika) and drink the Soma juice.

सः इत् हव्यः उ (saḥ it havyaḥ u) — That Draviṇodas is worthy to be invited for drinking Soma. This fact is well known.

यो नाम ददिः पत्यते सोम्यं मधु अध्वर्युभिः प्रस्थितं (yo nāma dadiḥ patyate somyaṃ madhu adhvaryubhiḥ prasthitaṃ) — For that Draviṇodas who is renowned as the giver of desired ends to sacrificers and others, the tasty Soma juice has been brought, prepared and placed by the priests called Adhvaryus.

द्रविणोदः पोत्रात् ऋतुभिः सोमं पिब (draviṇodaḥ potrāt ṛtubhiḥ somaṃ piba) — हे द्रविणोदः पोतुर्यागात् ऊर्जसंज्ञकैः ऋतुभिः सह सोमं पिब । (he draviṇodaḥ poturyāgāt ūrjasaṃjñakaiḥ ṛtubhiḥ saha somaṃ piba |) O Draviṇodas, drink this Soma juice, which the Adhvaryus have prepared for you and placed on the sacrificial altar, together with the deities presiding over the month Ūrja (Kārttika): such is the sacrificer's prayer stated here.

The particles इत् (it) and उ (u) are used to fill out the pāda. Yāska has said अथापि पदपूरण इदमु तदु (athāpi padapūraṇa idamu tadu) (Ni. 1-5) [reference as printed], and Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, also says उकारः पडपूरणः (ukāraḥ paḍapūraṇaḥ) [sic, as supplied].

(Note: a stray line "21" at the end of the page in the supplied text, probably a footnote or page-signature number; kept in kn.md, not explained.)

p. 322

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

मेद्यं॑तु ते॒ वह्न॑यो॒ येभि॒रीय॒सेऽरि॑षण्यन्वीळयस्वा वनस्पते । आ॒यूया॑ धृष्णो अभि॒गूर्या॒ त्वं ने॒ष्टात्सोमं॑ द्रविणोदः॒॒॑॑ पिब ऋतुभिः ॥ ३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

मेद्यंतु । ते । वह्नयः । येभिः । ईयसे । अरिषण्यन् । वीळयस्व । वनस्पते । आयोय । धृष्टो इति । अभिगूर्य । त्वं । नेष्ट्रात् । सोमं । द्रविणःदः । पिब । ऋतुभिः ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे द्रविणोदो येभिर्यैर्वाहैरीयसे प्राप्नोषि ॥ ते तव वह्नयो वोढार इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् । नि. ८-३ ॥ ते मेद्यंतु । तृप्यंतु । हे वनस्पते वनानां पते अरिषण्यन् अहिंसन् वीळयस्व । दृढीभव । हे धृष्टो धर्षक त्वमा- यूयागत्य अभिगूर्योद्यम्य नेष्त्रात् नेष्टुर्यागादृतुभिः सहःसंज्ञकैः सह सोमं पिब ॥

Gist: O Draviṇodas, may your bearers be satisfied; strengthen yourself, harming none; come, and drink Soma with the Ṛtus from the Neṣṭṛ's sacrifice.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Draviṇodaḥ — O Draviṇodas. Yobhiḥ [as supplied] — by which bearers. Īyase — you are brought. Te vahnayaḥ — those bearers of yours. Medyantu — may they be satisfied. Vanaspate — lord of the forests. Ariṣaṇyan — not being harmful. Vīḷeyasva [as supplied] — become one of firm body. Dhṛṣṭo — O subduer of enemies. Tvaṃ — you. Āyūya [as supplied] — having come. Abhigūrya — approving our sacrifice. Neṣvāt [as supplied] — in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ. Ṛtubhiḥ — with the deities called Sahas [as supplied]. Somaṃ — the Soma juice. Piba — drink.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Draviṇodas, may those bearers by which you are brought be satisfied. O Lord of the forest, become one of firm body, but do not be harmful. O subduer of enemies, O

p. 323

Draviṇodas, come, approve our sacrifice, and in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ drink the Soma together with the deities called Sahas [as supplied].

Printed English translation

May these your bearers, by whom you are borne along, be satisfied ; lord of the forest, be firm, doing no injury, steadfast of resolve ; come, and being gracious, drink, Dravinodas, along with the Ritus, the Soma, the offering the Neshtri [sic].

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

द्रविणोदः येभिः ईयसे ते वह्नयः मेद्यंतु (draviṇodaḥ yebhiḥ īyase te vahnayaḥ medyaṃtu) — the supplied text then adds a Sanskrit explanation (the words of Sāyaṇa's gloss, not repeated here). Kannada explanation: O Draviṇodas, the officiating priests who bring you, born in the fire-sticks (araṇis), to the sacrificial altar: may they be satisfied; thus the prayer is made.

Yāska has given an etymology for this passage (Ni. 8-3): वेद्यंतु ते वह्नयो वोढारो (vedyaṃtu te vahnayo voḍhāro) [as supplied; the quotation continues over several lines through वनस्पत इत्येन (vanaspata ityena) ... पिबर्तुभिः (pibartubhiḥ) and is not retyped here; its words as supplied are in the Kannada file].

According to this etymology the word medyantu is derived from the root इम्मिदा (immidā) [as supplied], "to be affectionate"; मेद्यंतु (medyaṃtu) is the third person plural imperative: "let them rejoice, let them be satisfied". Vahnayaḥ means "bearers" (the supplied text has प्रोढारः (proḍhāraḥ)): the word vahni is formed from the root vah, meaning "to carry, to bear, to reach", so vahnayaḥ means those who carry. The word can also mean a horse that bears a burden; here it is used in the sense of the priests who carry Agni (Draviṇodas). Ariṣaṇyat means "not harming, not being harmed", an epithet of Agni. Dhṛṣṇu is generally "one who destroys enemies".

Dhiṣṇya, dhiṣaṇya: dhiṣaṇā means speech (vāk). Because the Hotṛ sits near the deity and praises him in verses of praise, dhiṣṇya means "one who is praised". Or, according to धीसादिनीति वा धीसानिनीति वा (dhīsādinīti vā dhīsāninīti vā): dhīḥ means understanding or ritual work (sacrificial work), and since he is reached by understanding or ritual work he is dhiṣṇya; or since understanding or ritual work resides in him, or he gives them to those who worship him, the word dhiṣṇya may be so derived. Dhiṣṇya may also mean sacrificial work or the sacrificial ground. Here the prayer is that Soma be drunk in the sacrifice performed by the priest called Neṣṭṛ.

p. 324

Vanaspate is a vocative addressed to Agni. How is Agni called by the name vanaspati? Yāska says (as supplied): एष हि वनानां पाता ना पालयिता वा (eṣa hi vanānāṃ pātā nā pālayitā vā) [sic, as supplied; nā for vā?] — the passage goes on to say that, although Agni is within the forest trees and able to burn them, he does not burn them, and so is their protector. The word vana is derived from a root meaning "to be, to dwell". Here vanaspati means the lord or protector of trees: Agni, though dwelling within trees, does not burn them but guards them, and is therefore called vanaspati, protector of trees.

ऋतुभिः—कालैः (ṛtubhiḥ—kālaiḥ): ṛtus are definite periods of time. If a year is divided into six equal parts, each part, containing two months, indicates a fixed period of time; such a period is described by the word ṛtu.

[Software-generated line in the supplied text, removed from the Kannada text: "This image contains no text. It shows a decorative squiggly line or border." Noted, not translated.]

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अपा॑द्दो॒त्रादु॒त पो॒त्राद॑मत्तो॒त ने॒ष्ट्राद॑जुषत॒ प्रयो॑ हि॒तं । तु॒रीयं॒ पात्र॒ममृ॑क्त॒मम॑र्त्यं द्रविणो॒दाः पि॑बतु द्राविणो-॒ दसः ॥ ४ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अपात् । होत्रात् । उत । पोत्रात् । अमत्त । उत । नेष्ट्रात् । अजुषत । प्रयः । हितं । तुरीयं । पात्रं । अमृक्तं । अमर्त्यं । द्रविणःदाः । पिबतु । द्राविणःदसः ॥ ४ ॥

apāt | hotrāt | uta | potrāt | amatta | uta | neṣṭrāt | ajuṣata | prayaḥ | hitaṃ | turīyaṃ | pātraṃ | amṛktaṃ | amartyaṃ | draviṇaḥdāḥ | pibatu | drāviṇaḥdasaḥ ‖ 4 ‖

p. 325

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अच्छावाकस्येयं । यो द्रविणोदा होत्राद्दोतुर्यागात् सोममपात् पीतवान् उत किंच पोत्रात्पोतुर्यागादमत्त सोमं पीत्वामाद्यत् । उत आपि च नेष्ट्रात् नेष्टुर्यागाद्धितं दत्तं प्रयो देवानामन्न रूपं सोममजुषत । आसेविष्ट । स द्राविणोदसो हवीरूपद्रविणस्य प्रदातृभ्य ऋत्विग्यो हितः ॥ ऋत्वि- जोऽत्र द्रविणोदस उच्यंते हविषो दातारस्ते चैनं जनयंति । नि. ८-२ । इति यास्केनोक्तत्वात् ॥ तादृशो द्रविणोदा अमृतं दशापवित्रॆणामृष्टममर्त्यम- मरणसाधनं तुरीयं पात्रं चतुर्थपात्रस्थं सोमं पिबतु ॥

Gist: This verse belongs to the Acchāvāka. Draviṇodas, who drank Soma at the Hotṛ's, Potṛ's and Neṣṭṛ's sacrifices, is asked to drink the unstrained, immortal Soma in the fourth cup.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Yaḥ — which Draviṇodas. Hotrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ. Apāt — drank the Soma. Uta — and. Potrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ. Amatta — was satisfied with drinking Soma. Uta — and. Neṣṭrāt — in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ. Hitaṃ — offered. Prayaḥ — food-like for the gods, the Soma. Ajuṣata — enjoyed. (Saḥ — that Draviṇodas.) Draviṇodasaḥ — is for the priests who offer wealth in the form of oblations. Draviṇodāḥ — the same god. Amṛktaṃ — unhurt. Amartyaṃ — free of death. Turīyaṃ pātraṃ — contained in the fourth cup, the Soma. Pibatu — let him drink. (Spellings ಆಪಾತ್, ಆಮತ್ತ, ತುರಿಯಂ, ನೇಷ್ಟೃಕರ್ತಕವಾದ, ಅನ್ನ ಪ್ರಾಯದುದೂ kept as supplied.)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Draviṇodas who drank Soma in the sacrifice performed by the Hotṛ, was satisfied by drinking Soma in the sacrifice performed by the Potṛ, and enjoyed the Soma offered in the sacrifice performed by the Neṣṭṛ, which is like food for the gods, is there for the priests who offer wealth in the form of oblations. Let that same god drink the Soma that is unhurt, free of death and contained in the fourth cup.

Printed English translation

Whether he has drink [sic] the Soma from the offering of the Hotri ; whether he has been exhilarated by the offering of the Potri ; whether he has been pleased with the (sacrificial) food presented as the act of the Neshtri ; still let Dravinodas quaff the unstrained amborsial [sic] cup the forrth [sic] offered by the priest.

p. 326

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the priest called Maitrāvaruṇa speaks, addressing the priest called Acchāvāka. In the three preceding Ṛks Draviṇodas has been asked to drink the Soma offered in the sacrifices performed by the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ. The first half of this Ṛk states the same matter again. Now he is asked to drink the Soma that is in the fourth cup, offered by the priests.

तुरीयं पात्रं (turīyaṃ pātraṃ) — the Soma juice in the fourth cup. What has been said up to now is, in order, the Soma juice in the three cups of the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ; it is explained that the Soma juice offered by these priests is in the fourth cup.

अमृक्तं (amṛktaṃ) — > अमृष्टं, अशुद्धं, अपूर्णमित्यर्थः ।

amṛṣṭaṃ, aśuddhaṃ, apūrṇamityarthaḥ | O Draviṇodas, the Soma offered up to now by the priests Hotṛ, Potṛ and Neṣṭṛ is incomplete; that is, you have not been fully satisfied by drinking the Soma they offered. Therefore the intended sense is: drink the Soma juice in the fourth cup now offered by the priests and be satisfied.

अमर्त्यं (amartyaṃ) — > अमरणसाधनं । यत् पीत्वा न म्रियते । अमनुष्ययोग्यं ।

amaraṇasādhanaṃ | yat pītvā na mriyate | amanuṣyayogyaṃ | "Preventing death", that is, one who drinks this Soma does not die. Therefore this divine Soma is not fit for human beings; it is fit for the gods and is like nectar (amṛta).

द्रविणोदसः (draviṇodasaḥ) — > हवीरूपद्रविणस्य प्रदातारः ।

havīrūpadraviṇasya pradātāraḥ | The commentator explains it as the priests who offer oblations. Yāska also says: एतदग्निं द्रविणोदसमाहेत्यृत्विजोSत्र द्रविणोदस उच्यंते हविषो दातारस्ते चैनं जनयंति ॥

etadagniṃ draviṇodasamāhetyṛtvijoStra draviṇodasa ucyaṃte haviṣo dātāraste cainaṃ janayaṃti ‖ (Si. 8-2) [as supplied; the bhāṣya quotes this passage as Ni. 8-2] Thus he gives the etymology: Agni too is named Draviṇodas; because the priests offer oblations to that Agni, the priests also are called Draviṇodas.

p. 327

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अ॒र्वांच॑म॒द्य य॒य्यं॑ नृ॒वाह॑णं॒ रथं॑ युंजाथामि॒ह वां॒॑॑ विमोचनं । पृं॒क्तं ह॒वींषि॒ मधु॒ना हि कं॑ ग॒तमथा॒ सोमं॑ पिबतं वाजिनी- वसू ॥ ५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अर्वांचं । अद्य । यय्यं । नृवाहनं । रथं । युंजाथां । इह । वां । विमोचनं । पृंक्तं । हवींषि । मधुना । आ । हि । कं । गतं । अथ । सोमं । पिबतं । वाजिनी- वसू इति वाजिनीवसू ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विनौ अद्यास्मिन्नहनि यय्यं ययिं गंतारं नृवाहणं नेत्रोर्युव- योर्वोढारमिह यज्ञे वां युवयोर्विमोचनं विमोचयितारं रथमर्वां- चं यथार्वाग्भवति तथा युंजाथां । किंच मधुना स्वादुरसेन हवींषि पृंकतं । संयोजयतं । अथ चा गतं । अगच्छतं ॥ हि कमिति पूरणे ॥ अथानंतरं हे वाजिनीवसू। वाज एव वाजिनी । अन्नेन वासयितारौ बलवर्धनौ वा सोमं पिबतं॥

Gist: The Aśvins are asked to yoke their car, facing us, for this sacrifice; to mix the oblations with sweet juice; to come and drink the Soma.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau — O Aśvin gods.) Adya — at this time of the sacrifice. Yayyaṃ — that which moves about [as supplied]. Nṛvāhaṇaṃ — that which carries you, the leaders. Iha — in this sacrifice of ours. Vāṃ — you. Vimocanaṃ — that which sets down (brings and unloads). Rathaṃ — the car. Arvāṃcaṃ — so that it comes facing us. Yuṃjāthāṃ — yoke and make ready. Madhunā — with sweet juice. Havīṃṣi — the oblations. Pṛṃkaṃ [as supplied; the Saṃhitā and Pada read pṛṃktaṃ] — mix. Ā gataṃ hi — please come. Atha — afterwards. Vājinīvasū — O Aśvin gods, who give food and dwelling. Somaṃ — the Soma juice. Pibataṃ — drink.

p. 328

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, yoke and make ready, facing us, the car that moves about at this time of the sacrifice, that carries you the leaders, and that sets you down in this sacrifice of ours. Mix the oblations with sweet juice. After you have come here, O Aśvins, who give food and dwelling, drink the Soma juice.

Printed English translation

Yoke to-day, Ashwins, your rolling car, conveying (you), the leaders (of the rite) ; and setting you down before us : mix the oblations with the sweet juice : come, you are affluent with (abundant) food, and the Soma.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the Aśvin gods are asked to come to the sacrificial ground and drink the Soma offered by the sacrificer and others.

अद्य (adya) — > अस्मिन्नहनि यज्ञे वा !

asminnahani yajñe vā ! "On this day, or in the sacrifice we are now performing", is the meaning.

नृवाहणं (nṛvāhaṇaṃ) — > नेत्रोर्युवयोर्वोढारं ।

netroryuvayorvoḍhāraṃ | The meaning is: that which carries you two, the Aśvin gods, the leaders of men, to our sacrificial ground. This word is an epithet of the word rathaṃ.

इह नां विमोचनं रथं अर्वांचं युंजाथां (iha nāṃ vimocanaṃ rathaṃ arvāṃcaṃ yuṃjāthāṃ) [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā reads वां (vāṃ) for नां (nāṃ)] — > इह यज्ञे युवयोः > विमोचयितारं रथं यथा अर्वाक् भवति तथा युंजाथां ।

iha yajñe yuvayoḥ vimocayitāraṃ rathaṃ yathā arvāk bhavati tathā yuṃjāthāṃ | O Aśvin gods, make ready, so that you come facing the sacrifice we are now performing and so that your car is brought and stopped before us and the horses unyoked; that is, turn your car towards the sacrifice so that it is convenient for it to come to our sacrificial ground, and yoke horses to your car so that this happens. This is the intended sense.

वाजिनीवसू (vājinīvasū) — the word वाजः (vājaḥ) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). > अन्नेन > वासयितारौ बलवर्धनौ वा ।

annena vāsayitārau balavardhanau vā | "Those who nourish by giving food and the like to those who serve them", or "those who increase strength or power", is the meaning.

O Aśvin gods, turn your car to face us and yoke the horses, so as to come to our sacrificial ground. Then come to our sacrificial ground and drink the sweet or tasty Soma juice. You are givers of food, or of strength, to those who worship you; such as you, drink Soma in our sacrifice. This is the main intention of this Ṛk.

p. 329

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

जोष्य॑ग्ने स॒मिधं॒ जोष्याहु॑तिं॒ जोषि॒ ब्रह्म॒ जन्मं॒ जोषि॒॑ सुष्टु॒तिं । विश्वे॑भि॒र्विश्वा॑ ऋ॒तुना॑ वसो म॒ह उ॒शन्दे॒वा उ॑श॒तः पा॑यया॒ हविः ॥ ६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

जोषि । अग्ने । संइधं । जोषि । आहुतिं । जोषि । ब्रह्म । जन्यं । जोषि । सुस्तुतिं । विश्वेभिः । विश्वान् । ऋतुना । वसो इति । महः । उशन् । देवान् । उशतः । पायय । हविः ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अग्ने समिधं जोषि । जुषस्व । आहुतिं जोषि । जुषस्व । ब्रह्म शस्त्रं जन्यं जनेभ्यो हितं जोषि । जुषस्व । सुष्टुतिं शोभनस्तोत्रं जोषि । जुषस्व । किंचॆ वसो सर्वेषामावासभूत हे अग्ने उशतः कामयमानान् महो महतो विश्वान् सर्वानेवान् उशन् कामयमानस्त्वमृतुना तपस्यसंज्ञकेन सह तथा विश्वेभिः सर्वैर्देवैः सह हविर्हवीरूपं सोमं पायय ॥

Gist: O Agni, enjoy the fuel, the oblation, the prayer and the praise; desiring the great gods, drink the Soma together with the Ṛtu and all the gods.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

Agni — O Agni. Samidham — the fuel. Joṣi — enjoy it and be satisfied. Āhutim — the oblation. Joṣi — enjoy. Brahma — the prayer in the form of a śastra. Janyam — as good for men. Joṣi — enjoy. Suṣṭutim — the excellent praise. Joṣi — enjoy. Vaso — O Agni, the abode of all. Uśataḥ — those who desire the oblation. Mahaḥ — and are endowed with great qualities. Viśvān devān — all the gods. Uśan — you who desire them. Ṛtunā — together with the deity named Tapasya. Viśvebhiḥ — together with all the gods. Haviḥ — the Soma in the form of the oblation. Pāyaya — drink.

p. 330

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 3 (as printed; the Maṇḍala is 2), Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 37, p. 330.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Agni, enjoy the fuel, the oblation, the prayer in the form of a śastra, and the excellent praise, and be satisfied. Thereby make it good for men. O Agni, abode of all, you who desire all the gods, who wish for the oblation and are endowed with great qualities, drink the Soma in the form of the oblation together with the Ṛtu deity named Tapasya and with all the other gods.

Printed English translation

Be pleased, Agni, with the fuel ; be pleased with the oblation ; be pleased with the sacred prayer that is good for men ; be pleased with holy praise, asylum of all : Agni, willing (to accept oblations), render all the great gods desirous (of the same), and with them all, and with the Ritu drink the oblation.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk Agni is prayed to drink Soma. O Agni, enjoy the fuel sticks (pieces of wood) that we offer in the fire; enjoy the oblation (the offering) that we make; hear and be pleased with the śastra mantras that we recite; and listen with favour to the excellent praise that we utter to please you. Thus pleased, come with all the gods to the sacrificial ground and drink the Soma juice prepared for you, together with the deity presiding over the month Tapasya. This is the main purport of the Ṛk.

समिधं (samidhaṃ) — well-dried pieces of wood used for offering in the fire. These pieces should be about four fingers' breadth in length, with their tips, and should come from certain prescribed trees such as the Aśvattha and the Palāśa.

ब्रह्म (brahma) — the word brahma is read both among the names of food and among the names of praise. Here the commentators explain it as a śastra-mantra that praises Agni. (The printed text of the page ends here, without a full stop; the passage may continue on the next page.)

p. 331

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ:"), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 331.

Sūkta 38 (Maṇḍala 2)

The thirty-eighth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

उदु ष्य इत्येकादशर्चं षष्ठं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभं सवितृदेवताकं । अत्रानुक्रमणिका । उदु ष्य एकादश सावित्रमिति ॥ व्यूढे दशरात्रे षष्ठेऽहनि वैश्वदे- वशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं सावित्रनिविद्वानीयं । व्यूळ्हश्चेदिति खंडे सूत्रितं । षष्ठस्योदु ष्य देव इति गार्त्समदं । आ. ८-८ । इति ॥

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta beginning Udu ṣya is the sixth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eleven ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta; Savitṛ is the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: "Udu ṣya, eleven, addressed to Savitṛ." In the Daśarātra sacrifice called Vyūḍha, on the sixth day, while reciting the Vaiśvadeva śastra mantras, this sūkta is applied for the nivid mantras addressed to Savitṛ, as explained by the sūtra "ṣaṣṭhasyodu ṣya deva iti gārtsamadam" in the section beginning "vyūḍhaś cet" of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (as printed, Ā. 8-8).

Sūkta 38 — Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 38; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, 3 (as printed). Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 11. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deity: Savitṛ. Metre: Triṣṭubh.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

उदु॒ ष्य दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता स॒वाय॑ शश्वत्त॒मं तद॑सा॒ वह्नि॑रस्थात् । नू॒नं दे॒वेभ्यो॒ वि हि धाति॒ रत्न॒मथाभ॑जद्वी॒तिहो॑त्रं स्व॒स्तौ ॥ १ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

उत् । ऊं इति । स्यः । देवः । सविता । सवाय । शश्वत्तमं । तत्त्वापसाः । वह्निः । अस्थात् । नूनं । देवेभ्यः । वि । हि । धाति । रत्नं । अथ । आ । अभजत् । वीतिहोत्रं । स्वस्तौ ॥ १ ॥

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 332.

Ṛk 1 (continued from p. 331)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

स्यः स देवो द्योतमानः सविता सवाय लोकानां प्रसवायानुज्ञायै शश्व- त्तमं प्रतिदिनमुदस्थात् । उत्तिष्ठति । कीदृशः सविता । तदपाः तत्पसवकर्मा ॥ अपः अप्प इति कर्मनामसु पाठात् ॥ वह्निर्वोढा जगतां । किंच नूनं संप्रति देवेभ्यः स्तोतृ- भ्यो रत्नं धनं वि हि धाति । प्रयच्छति ॥ हीति पूरणे ॥ अथ अपि च वीतिहोत्रं कांतयज्ञं यजमानं स्वस्तावविनाशे क्षेमेऽभजत् । भागिनं करोतु । यद्यपि स्वस्तिशब्दो विभक्त्यंतनिर्दिष्टशब्दपरस्तथाप्यपर्यवसानादर्थपरो भवति ॥

syaḥ sa devo dyotamānaḥ savitā savāya lokānāṃ prasavāyānujñāyai śaśva- ttamaṃ pratidinamudasthāt | uttiṣṭhati | kīdṛśaḥ savitā | tadapāḥ tatpasavakarmā ‖ apaḥ appa iti karmanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ vahnirvoḍhā jagatāṃ | kiṃca nūnaṃ saṃprati devebhyaḥ stotṛ- bhyo ratnaṃ dhanaṃ vi hi dhāti | prayacchati ‖ hīti pūraṇe ‖ atha api ca vītihotraṃ kāṃtayajñaṃ yajamānaṃ svastāvavināśe kṣeme 'bhajat | bhāginaṃ karotu | yadyapi svastiśabdo vibhaktyaṃtanirdiṣṭaśabdaparastathāpyaparyavasānādarthaparo bhavati ‖

Gist: Savitṛ, the doer of the world's work and its bearer, rises daily for the world's generation, grants wealth to the praisers, and is asked to make the sacrificer share in lasting well-being.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

tadapāḥ — he who has the work of the creation of the world. vahniḥ — he who bears the burden of the world. syaḥ — the well-known. devaḥ — the shining. savitā — Savitṛ. savāya — for the generation of the world. śaśvattamaṃ — every day. ut asthāt — rises up, having dawned. nūnaṃ — certainly. devebhyaḥ — to the praisers. ratnaṃ — wealth. vi hi dhāti — he gives. atha — and. vītihotraṃ — the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice. svasau [?] — to well-being (the printed text reads स्वसौ (svasau); the Saṃhitā has svastau; the text after it, "ಆ" before abhajat, is garbled as supplied). abhajat — may he make a sharer.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Savitṛ, who has the work of the creation of the world, who bears the burden of the world, the well-known, the shining, rises up daily, having dawned, for the generation of the world, and is the giver of wealth to the praisers. In the same way, may he bring well-being to the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice.

Printed English translation

In truth, the divine Savitri, the bearer (of the world), has perpetually been present for the generation (of mankind), for such is his office: verily he grants wealth to the pious (worshippers): may he. therefore, bestow upon the offerer of the oblation (sufficient) for his well-being.

(The Kannada text prints the heading "English Translation-" before the above; it stands inside the Bhāvārtha lines as supplied.)

Note: the Pada reading given on p. 331 ends tattvāpasāḥ, while the Pratipadārtha and the bhāṣya here have tadapāḥ* / तदपाः (tadapāḥ); reported as supplied.*

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

devaḥ savitā — On the deity Savitṛ Yāska says: सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता । आदित्योSपि सवितोच्यते (savitā sarvasya prasavitā | ādityoSpi savitocyate) (Nirukta 10-31, 32, 33). That is: he who brings forth the whole world, the cause of the origin of all the world; the Āditya (the sun too) is also called Savitṛ. Thus he has given the etymology.

p. 333

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 333.

Eleven sūktas of the Ṛgveda, and parts of some other sūktas, praise the deity Savitṛ. The opinion of the commentators is that the sun just at the moment of rising is the deity Savitṛ, and afterwards it is the sun. Savitṛ is, for the most part, a deity of gold. His eye (Ṛ. S. 1-35-8), his hands (1-35-9, 10), his tongue (6-71-3) and all his other limbs are described as golden. His chariot too is golden (1-35-2, 5).

The radiance of the god Savitṛ is immense. His golden light spreads over and illumines the whole world. He raises his golden arms and wakes all the living beings that were sleeping in the night (2-38-2; 4-53-3, 4; 6-71-1, 5; 7-45-2). Seated in his golden chariot he goes along looking over all creatures (1-35-2, 3). Shining with the sun's rays, Savitṛ of yellow-brown hair sends forth his light constantly from the eastern quarter (10-139-1). He goes round three times the three upper regions that light up the atmosphere and the sky (4-53-5); he is the one who gives the gods immortality and men long life (4-54-2). Just as the sun is prayed to, so Savitṛ is prayed to for the removal of bad dreams (5-82-4) and for release from sin (4-54-3). Water and wind are subject to his rule (2-38-2). The other deities follow his lead (5-81-3). Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, Rudra and others cannot resist his determination or his independence (2-38-7, 9; 5-83-2). The Vasus, Aditi, Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman praise his fame (7-38-3, 4). Like Pūṣan and Sūrya, Savitṛ is the lord of things moving and unmoving (4-53-6). All things desired by everyone are under his control. He himself, being in heaven, earth and sky, brings about what is auspicious (1-24-3; 2-28-11); like the other deities he too is the support of the sky (4-53-2; 10-149-4), the support of the whole world (4-54-4); he has bound the earth with bonds and set it to stand firm, and he has made the sky stand in the intervening space that has no beams or supports (10-149-1).

Because Savitṛ is the maker of rain, and because his path lies in the atmosphere, he is spoken of as a deity of the middle region. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Ś. Brā. 12-3-5-1) the view is expressed that Savitṛ and Prajāpati are one and the same deity. In the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa (1-6-4-1) it is said that Prajāpati himself, as Savitṛ, created the creatures (the printed text reads प्रजाप्रतिये (prajāpratiye) [?], presumably for prajāpati; the opening bracket of the reference is missing in the print). In the Ṛk 3-62-10 it is said that, having meditated on the vigour and greatness of Savitṛ, his vigour may impel all. This very mantra is known in the Vedas as the Gāyatrī, and has gained pre-eminence among all the Vedic mantras. As a rule the word deva is used together with the word savitṛ.

p. 334

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 334.

(The sentence begun on p. 333 ends at the top of this page: "…the custom is that the word deva is used.") The name Savitṛ is given to a special power of the sun that produces life in the world and gives the power of motion to creatures. According to some, the sun is this gross disc, a mass of light seen in the sky, and Savitṛ is the divine power, embodied, of that sun.

Many matters concerning the deity Savitṛ we shall explain in detail when we give the explanation of the Ṛk Ṛ. S. 3-62-10 (Gāyatrī).

सवाय—लोकानां प्रसवाय । (savāya—lokānāṃ prasavāya |) The meaning is: in order that the activities of the creatures in the world, such as their birth and continuance, may go on. If the sun (Savitṛ) does not rise, neither the birth of creatures nor activities such as movement go on. The idea is that Savitṛ is the cause of all the activities of the world.

तदपाः— (tadapāḥ—) The word apaḥ is read among the names of works (Nirukta 3-2). Here tadapāḥ means one who is endowed with those works, that is, the cause of the works of creation, continuance and so on.

वह्निः— (vahniḥ—) The word vahni, formed from the root वह प्रापणे (vaha prāpaṇe), means one who bears, that is, one who sustains the world. That is, all the activities of the world go on through this god Savitṛ. The idea is that he is both the sustainer and the nourisher of the world.

देवेभ्यः—स्तोतृभ्यः । (devebhyaḥ—stotṛbhyaḥ |) On the word deva Yāska has given the etymology: देवो दानाद्वा दीपनाद्वा द्योतनाद्वा द्युस्थानो भवतीति वा । (devo dānādvā dīpanādvā dyotanādvā dyusthāno bhavatīti vā |) That is, the word deva may mean "giver"; or, he is called deva because he illumines, or because his qualities are described and praised, or because he dwells in heaven. In the present Ṛk, taking the meaning of dīpana or dyotana as describing the qualities of the god Savitṛ and making them shine, the sense is explained as the priests who describe the qualities of the deity, that is, who praise him.

रत्नं-रमणीयं धनं । (ratnaṃ-ramaṇīyaṃ dhanaṃ |) It means pleasing wealth, that is, wealth attractive to people.

नीतिहोत्रं [?]—कांतयज्ञं यजमानं । (nītihotraṃ [?]—kāṃtayajñaṃ yajamānaṃ |) (The headword is printed nītihotram [?]; the Saṃhitā and Pada have vītihotram.) The idea is: to the sacrificer who desires a sacrifice, that is, who desires to perform a sacrifice addressed to the deities.

स्वस्तौ—अविनाशे क्षेमे । (svastau—avināśe kṣeme |) Yāska's etymology is स्वस्तित्यविनाशि नाम (svastityavināśi nāma) (Nirukta 3-21): well-being that does not perish, or wealth and other prosperity.

p. 335

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 335.

(Continuation of the Special Topics on Ṛk 1; the page opens in the middle of a sentence, and the first letters are printed as supplied, तपदाः (tapadāḥ) for what should be तदपाः (tadapāḥ) [?].) तपदाः वह्निः स्यः देवः सविता सवाय शश्वत्तमं उत् अस्थात् (tapadāḥ vahniḥ syaḥ devaḥ savitā savāya śaśvattamaṃ ut asthāt)—this god Savitṛ is the cause of the world's activities and the one who nourishes the world. This well-known Savitṛ rises every day so that all the activities of the creatures of the world, such as creation and continuance, may go on.

नूनं देवेभ्यः रत्नं वि हि धाति (nūnaṃ devebhyaḥ ratnaṃ vi hi dhāti)—this god will now give delightful wealth and the like to the priests and sacrificers who are praising him.

अथ वीतिहोत्रं स्वस्तौ आ अभजत् (atha vītihotraṃ svastau ā abhajat)—here the word अथ (atha) is said to have the sense of "and" (samuccaya). And may this god become a sharer in the matter of producing well-being for the sacrificer who desires to perform a sacrifice addressed to him or is performing it; that is, the meaning is that he should produce well-being for the sacrificer.

हि (hi)—the word हि (hi) is used here merely to fill out the foot (pādapūraṇa).

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

विश्वस्य । हि । श्रुष्टये । देवः । ऊर्ध्वः । प्र । बाहवा । पृथुपाणिः । सिसर्ति । आपः । चित् । अस्य । व्रते । आ । निमृग्राः । आयं । चित् । वातः । रमते । परिङ्मन् ॥

Note: the supplied text reads ऊर्ध्वर्न् (ūrdhvarn) and निम्मग्रा (nimmagrā) in the Saṃhitā against ऊर्ध्वः (ūrdhvaḥ) and निमृग्राः (nimṛgrāḥ) in the Pada, and अयं (ayaṃ) in the Saṃhitā against आयं (āyaṃ) in the Pada; reported as supplied. The bhāṣya has अयं चिद्वातः (ayaṃ cidvātaḥ).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

देवो द्योतमानः सविता पृथुपाणिर्महत्करो विश्वस्य श्रुष्टये जगतः सुखायोर्ध्व उद्दतः सन् बाहवा बाहू प्रसिसर्ति । प्रसारयति । आपश्चित् आपोS- प्यस्य व्रते प्रसवाख्यॆ कर्मणि सति ॥ व्रतं कर्वरमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ आ स्यंदंत इति शेषः। ताश्च निमृग्रा नितरां शोधयित्यो गंगादिरूपेण जगत्पावयंतीत्यर्थः। अयं चिद्वातोऽयमपि वायः परिज्मन् परितो गते व्याप्ते०तरिक्षे रमते ॥

devo dyotamānaḥ savitā pṛthupāṇirmahatkaro viśvasya śruṣṭaye jagataḥ sukhāyordhva uddataḥ san bāhavā bāhū prasisarti | prasārayati | āpaścit āpoS- pyasya vrate prasavākhyè karmaṇi sati ‖ vrataṃ karvaramiti tannāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ ā syaṃdaṃta iti śeṣaḥ| tāśca nimṛgrā nitarāṃ śodhayityo gaṃgādirūpeṇa jagatpāvayaṃtītyarthaḥ| ayaṃ cidvāto 'yamapi vāyaḥ parijman parito gate vyāpte0tarikṣe ramate ‖

Gist: Savitṛ, large-handed, rising for the good of the world, stretches out his arms; the waters flow in his work, purifying as Gaṅgā and the rest; the wind too moves in the all-pervading atmosphere.

p. 336

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2, Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 336.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

devaḥ — the shining Savitṛ. pṛthupāṇiḥ — having extended hands (rays). viśvasya — of the world. śruṣṭaye hi — for the happiness indeed. ūrdhvaḥ — rising up, having dawned. bāhavā — his arms. pra sisarti — spreads out. nimṛgrāḥ — those that purify the world in the forms of Gaṅgā and so on. āpaścit — the waters also. asya vrate — on account of the work (of the nature of creation) of this Savitṛ. ā (syandante) — flow, running on. ayaṃ cidvātaḥ — this wind also. parijman — in this all-pervading atmosphere. ramate — sports.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The shining Savitṛ, with extended rays, rises up for the happiness of the world and spreads out his arms. The waters too, which purify the world in the forms of Gaṅgā and the rest, flow on account of this work of Savitṛ, which is of the nature of creation. This wind also sports in this all-pervading atmosphere.

Printed English translation

The divine, vast-handed (Savitri), having risen, stretches forth his arms for the delight of all : the purifying waters (flow) for (the fulfilment of) his rites, and this circumambient air sports (in the firmament).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

viśvasya śruṣṭaye — विश्वस्य श्रुष्टये—जगतः सुखाय (viśvasya śruṣṭaye—jagataḥ sukhāya). Śruṣṭi means happiness; the meaning is "for the happiness of the whole world". Yāska has read the word śruṣṭi among the names for "quick" (kṣipra): having said in the etymology श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम—आशु अष्टीति (śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma—āśu aṣṭīti) (Ni. 6-13), and elsewhere श्रुष्टीवरीः-सुखवत्यः (śruṣṭīvarīḥ-sukhavatyaḥ) (Ni. 6-22) ("happy ones"), the commentator has accepted the meaning "happiness" for the word śruṣṭi in the present Ṛk and explained it so.

vrate — the word व्रतं (vrataṃ) is listed among the names of work (Ni. 3-1). Explaining this word in detail, Yāska says—

व्रतमित कर्मनाम वृणोतीति सतः । इदमपीतरत् व्रतमेतस्मादेव निवृत्तिकर्म वारयतीति सतः । अन्नमपि व्रतमुच्यते यदाव्रणोति शरीरं ।

vratamita karmanāma vṛṇotīti sataḥ | idamapītarat vratametasmādeva nivṛttikarma vārayatīti sataḥ | annamapi vratamucyate yadāvraṇoti śarīraṃ |

(Reference printed (सि. २-१३) ((si. 2-13)), i.e. "Si. 2-13" as supplied; probably Nirukta, but the print has Si..)

p. 337

Running head: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 337.

Thus he has given three meanings of the word vrata. That is: because the good or bad work done by a man pervades him, work is called vrata; or this work may also be a work of restraint, that is, because it holds back, i.e. prevents, work that he does not want or that is forbidden by the śāstra, it is called vrata; and because it pervades the body, food too is called vrata; so he has explained.

    1. The word vrata is used in the sense of preventing, checking, protecting—

याः पार्थिवासो या अपामपि व्रते ता नो देवीः सुहवाः शर्म यच्छत ।

yāḥ pārthivāso yā apāmapi vrate tā no devīḥ suhavāḥ śarma yacchata |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-7.) In the word vrate of this Ṛk the meaning is vṛjina, that is, protection (as printed, in English: "protection") made by averting evil. The prayer is: may the goddesses who are on the earth and the goddesses who are in the water release us from distress and bring us protection and happiness. Here vrate means the protection that rescues from distress.

तासां नि चिक्क्युः कवयो निवानं परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ।

tāsāṃ ni cikkyuḥ kavayo nivānaṃ pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-114-2.) The poets (sages) discovered what was hidden in caves where no one could see it; here vrateṣu is used as an adjective of guhyeṣu, with the meaning "hidden".

ददृश्र एषामवमा सदांसि परेषु या गुह्येषु व्रतेषु ।

dadṛśra eṣāmavamā sadāṃsi pareṣu yā guhyeṣu vrateṣu |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-54-5.)

असि यमो अस्यादित्यो अर्वन्नसि त्रितो गुह्येन व्रतेन ।

asi yamo asyādityo arvannasi trito guhyena vratena |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-163-3.) Here too the word vratena is used in the sense "hidden".

  1. Vrata indicates a prohibitory rule, "such a work shall not be done", or a rule of dharma, "just such a work must be done" (law or ordinance)—

यच्चिद्दि ते विशो यथा प्र देव वरुण व्रतं । मिनीमसि द्यविद्यवि ॥

yacciddi te viśo yathā pra deva varuṇa vrataṃ | minīmasi dyavidyavi ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-1, printed "ಋಂ. ಸಂ."; the Kannada print has no closing mark before the reference.) O Varuṇa, since we are mere men, whichever of your ordinances we transgress (do not take note of it, and complete the work).

य उ श्रिया दमेष्टा दोषोषासि प्रशस्यते । यस्य व्रतं न मायते ।

ya u śriyā dameṣṭā doṣoṣāsi praśasyate | yasya vrataṃ na māyate |

The (Agni) whose ordinance is not transgressed...................................

22 (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-8-3) (the stray "22" before the reference is as supplied).

p. 338

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2 (printed "ಮಂ. ೨."), Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 338.

इंद्रस्य कर्म सुकृता पुरूणि व्रतानि देवा न मिनंति विश्वे ।

iṃdrasya karma sukṛtā purūṇi vratāni devā na minaṃti viśve |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3 32-8, as printed, with a space where a hyphen is expected.) Indra's deeds of valour are many and well done. The gods do not break (do not transgress) Indra's rules and ordinances.

विश्वं सत्यं मघवाना युवोरिदापश्चन प्र मिनंति व्रतं वां ।

viśvaṃ satyaṃ maghavānā yuvoridāpaścana pra minaṃti vrataṃ vāṃ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-24-12.) O mighty gods, all that is yours is true. Even the waters do not transgress your rules and ordinances. (The printed translation has a stray colon before "your".)

वनानि विभ्यो नकिरस्य तानि व्रता देवस्य सवितुर्मिनंति ।

vanāni vibhyo nakirasya tāni vratā devasya saviturminaṃti |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-7, the "." after "Saṃ" missing in print.) No one transgresses these rules of the god Savitṛ.

Garbled duplicate line as supplied (kept, not deleted): the verse of Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-12 appears twice in the supplied text, first with जेति (jeti) for चेति (ceti) and then again below; the first copy is kept here as an italic note in kn.md.

अमिनती दैव्यानि व्रतानि सूर्यस्य चेति रश्मिभिर्दृशाना ।

aminatī daivyāni vratāni sūryasya ceti raśmibhirdṛśānā |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-92-12.)

अमिनती द्यैव्यानि व्रतानि प्रमिनती मनुष्या युगानि ।

aminatī dyaivyāni vratāni praminatī manuṣyā yugāni |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-124-12.) This goddess Uṣas does not transgress the rules and ordinances of the gods.

किं स्विन्नो राजा जगृहे कदस्याति व्रतं चकृमा को वि वेद ।

kiṃ svinno rājā jagṛhe kadasyāti vrataṃ cakṛmā ko vi veda |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-12-5.) Which rule (of this Agni) shall we transgress?

अयमेक इत्था पुरूरु चष्टे वि विश्वतिः । तस्य व्रतान्यनु वश्चरामसि ।

ayameka itthā purūru caṣṭe vi viśvatiḥ | tasya vratānyanu vaścarāmasi |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-25-16.) We shall follow (observe) his rules. In these and other Ṛks, and also in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-33-9; 7-5-4; 7-87-7, the word व्रत (vrata) indicates the sense of rules and ordinances.

And the word अनुव्रतं (anuvrataṃ) occurring in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-3; 2-38-6; 8-40-8; 1-136-5; 3-61-1; 4-13-2; 5-69-1 and others indicates the sense "in accordance with the rules and ordinances".

  1. In some contexts, when the rules of the gods are explained in the sense of sacrifice or sacrificial acts, the word व्रत (vrata) is used. It is said that by performing sacrifices and the like one does not neglect the wish or the ordinance of the gods

p. 339

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 339 (Ṛgvedasaṃhitā).

(The sentence of p. 338 continues:) the wish or ordinance of the gods is not neglected, it is said—

यो अग्नीषोमा हविषा सपर्याद्देवद्रीचा मनसा यो धृतेन । तस्य व्रतं रक्षतं पातमहंसो विशे जनाय महि शर्म यच्छतं ।

yo agnīṣomā haviṣā saparyāddevadrīcā manasā yo dhṛtena | tasya vrataṃ rakṣataṃ pātamahaṃso viśe janāya mahi śarma yacchataṃ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-8.) O Agni and Soma, the man (the sacrificer) who worships Agni and Soma with oblations and other substances, wholeheartedly — protect his sacrifice, guard him so that no harm befalls him.

त्वमग्ने प्रथमो अंगिरस्तमः कविर्देवानां परि भूषसि व्रतं ।

tvamagne prathamo aṃgirastamaḥ kavirdevānāṃ pari bhūṣasi vrataṃ |

(printed "ಮ ಸಂ. ೧-೩೧-೨", the Ṛ missing in print; as supplied.) O Agni, you are the foremost among the Aṅgiras sages, the first, and a poet. Perform the sacrifice of the gods.

तस्य व्रतानि भूरिपोषिणो वयमुप भूषेम दम आ सुवृक्तिभिः ।

tasya vratāni bhūripoṣiṇo vayamupa bhūṣema dama ā suvṛktibhiḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3-9.) We, endowed with wealth and other riches, shall perform in our house Agni's sacrificial acts with hymns of praise and so on — in these and other Ṛks, and also in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-6-5; 8-42-1; 6-14-3; 1-24-15; 6-54-9; 10-36-13; 5-18-5, the word व्रत (vrata) is used in one of the senses "sacrifice", "sacrificial act" or "act". When the words of the various mantras are explained so that the meaning fits, whichever of the three kinds of meaning given by Yāska for the word व्रत (vrata) fits properly according to the context is to be given. This is the principal meaning and the usage of the word व्रत (vrata).

The Nirukta explains the words of this Ṛk thus:

देवः पृथुपाणिः विश्वस्य श्रुष्टये हि ऊर्ध्वः बाहवा प्रसिसर्ति

devaḥ pṛthupāṇiḥ viśvasya śruṣṭaye hi ūrdhvaḥ bāhavā prasisarti

— "For the happiness of the whole world this god Savitṛ rises up and stretches out his arms." Here "arms" means rays. The Sun (Savitṛ), having risen, makes his rays spread in all directions and gives happiness to the creatures of the world.

निम्मग्राः आपः चित् अस्य व्रते आ (स्यंदंति)

nimmagrāḥ āpaḥ cit asya vrate ā (syaṃdaṃti)

— "By the rule of this god, that is, by his work called creation, the waters produced flow in the forms of Gaṅgā and other rivers, purifying the people of the world." In this sentence the verb स्यंदंति (syaṃdaṃti) is to be supplied. (The first word is printed निम्मग्राः (nimmagrāḥ) in the supplied text, as supplied; compare the Pratipadārtha on p. 336.) By the rays of the sun the waters in the sea and other reservoirs are heated, gather in the atmosphere in the form of vapour, remain some time in the form of clouds, and then he makes those waters fall on the earth in the form of rain. The rain-waters gather together and flow in the form of rivers. By the water of those rivers

p. 340

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2 (printed "ಮಂ. ೨."), Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 340.

people are not only purified but also obtain food and other nourishment through the growth of plants and so on, and live happily. It is indicated here that for all this the व्रत (vrata) of the god Savitṛ, that is, his work (his rule), is the cause.

"This wind also sports in the all-pervading atmosphere" — that is, the wind around us moves about playfully in the atmosphere which is spread everywhere. The meaning is: that the wind blows in the wide atmosphere for the good of men is also the rule of that god Savitṛ.

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

आ॒शुभि॑श्चि॒द्यान्वि मु॑चाति नू॒नमरी॑रम॒दत॑मानं चि॒देतोः॑ । अ॒ह्यर्षू॑णां चि॒न्न्य॑या अवि॒ष्यामनु॑ व्र॒तं स॑वि॒तुर्मोक्यागा॑त् ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

आशुभिः । चित् । यान् । वि । मुचाति । नूनं । अरीरमत् । आतमानं । चित् । एतोः। अह्यर्षूणां । चित् । नि । अयान् । अविष्यां । अनु । व्रतं । सवितुः । मोकी । आ । अगात् ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यान् गच्छन् सविताशुभिश्चिच्छीघ्रगामिभिरपि रश्मिभिर्विमुचाति । विमुच्यते । नूनमिति पूरणः । अतमानं चित्सततं गच्छंतमपि जनमेतोर्गमनादरीरमत् । उपरमयति । किंच अह्यर्षणां । अहिमाहंतारं शत्रुमर्षंत्यभिगच्छंतीत्यह्य- र्षवः । तेषामप्यविष्यां गमनेच्छां न्ययान् । नियच्छति। सवितुः प्रेरकस्य सूर्यस्य व्रतं कर्मानु पश्चान्मोकी रात्रिः । मोकी शोकीति रात्रिनामसु पाठात् ॥ आगात्! आगच्छति । सवितुश्चॆष्टोपरतौ रात्रिरागच्छतीति यावत् ॥

yān gacchan savitāśubhiścicchīghragāmibhirapi raśmibhirvimucāti | vimucyate | nūnamiti pūraṇaḥ | atamānaṃ citsatataṃ gacchaṃtamapi janametorgamanādarīramat | uparamayati | kiṃca ahyarṣaṇāṃ | ahimāhaṃtāraṃ śatrumarṣaṃtyabhigacchaṃtītyahya- rṣavaḥ | teṣāmapyaviṣyāṃ gamanecchāṃ nyayān | niyacchati| savituḥ prerakasya sūryasya vrataṃ karmānu paścānmokī rātriḥ | mokī śokīti rātrināmasu pāṭhāt ‖ āgāt! āgacchati | savituścèṣṭoparatau rātrirāgacchatīti yāvat ‖

Gist: Savitṛ, going, releases (the horses) with swift rays; he stops even the constantly moving; he restrains the wish of the warriors to go; after his work the night comes.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यान् (yān) — Savitṛ who moves. आशुभिश्चित् (āśubhiścit) — by the swift-going rays. वि मुचाति (vi mucāti) — becomes released. अतमानं चित् (atamānaṃ cit) — even people who move constantly. एतोः (etoḥ) — from their moving. अरीरमत् (arīramat) — he stops. अह्यर्षणां (ahyarṣaṇāṃ) — of the warriors, the assailants of enemies (the Pratipadārtha continues on the next page).

p. 341

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 341 (Ṛgvedasaṃhitā).

(The Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 3 continues:) अविष्यां (aviṣyāṃ) — also the wish to go forward towards battle. न्ययान् (nyayān) — he checks and stops. सवितुः (savituḥ) — of the Sun. व्रतं अनु (vrataṃ anu) — after the work consisting of his movement. मोकी (mokī) — the night. आगात् (āgāt) — appears.

Stray line as supplied (kept, not deleted; in kn.md as an italic note): "। ಭಾನುವಾರ ।" (a Kannada word meaning "Sunday", between the Pratipadārtha and the Bhāvārtha).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Savitṛ, whose work is movement, is released from his swift-going rays. He makes even the people who move constantly stop their moving. He also checks and stops the wish of the warriors, the assailants of enemies, to go forward towards battle. After the work consisting of his movement, the night appears.

Printed English translation

The moving (Sun) is liberated by his rapid rays: verily he has stopped the traveller from his journey : he restrains the desire of warriors for combat, for night follows (the cessation of) the function of Savitri.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

Having said so far that by the rule (vrata, the ordinance) of the god Savitṛ the activities of the world go on, and that Savitṛ rises for the happiness of the people, the sage now describes in this Ṛk that after Savitṛ has set, all the activities of the world stop and night appears.

आशुभिः (āśubhiḥ) — शीघ्रगामिभिः रश्मिभिः (śīghragāmibhiḥ raśmibhiḥ): it means "by rays that spread swiftly". The word आशु (āśu) is read among the names for horse (Nighaṇṭu 2-27, printed "ಸಿ. ೨-೨೭") and among the names for "swift" (3-9, printed "ಸಿ. ೩-೯"). And the derivation is given: आश इति च शु इति च क्षिप्रनामनी भवतः (āśa iti ca śu iti ca kṣipranāmanī bhavataḥ) (6-1, printed "ಸಿ. ೬-೧") and आशवः क्षिप्रकारिणः (āśavaḥ kṣiprakāriṇaḥ) (9-9, printed "ಸಿ. ೯-೯"). Because the rays spread everywhere very quickly, the word आशु (āśu) is here explained as "rays".

नूनं (nūnaṃ) — of this word Yāska says:

नूनमिति विचिकित्सार्थीयो भाषायामुभयमन्वध्यायं विचिकित्सार्थीयश्च पदपूरणश्च ॥

nūnamiti vicikitsārthīyo bhāṣāyāmubhayamanvadhyāyaṃ vicikitsārthīyaśca padapūraṇaśca ‖

(Nirukta 1-5, printed "ನಿ. ೧-೫".) He explains that the word नूनं (nūnaṃ) is used in the sense of doubt (vicikitsā), that is, to convey a conclusion reached after deliberate examination, or also for filling out a pada (verse-quarter). He describes that in the Chandas (the Veda) the word नूनं (nūnaṃ) is used both in the sense of vicikitsā and in the sense of filling out the pada, while elsewhere it is used in the sense of vicikitsā. Durgācārya, the commentator on the Nirukta, says: विचिकित्सा नाम विवेकपूर्वको अवधारणाभिप्रायः (vicikitsā nāma vivekapūrvako avadhāraṇābhiprāyaḥ) — in circumstances where doubt arises, deciding by deliberation is called vicikitsā.

p. 342

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṇḍala 2 (printed "ಮಂ. ೨."), Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 342.

The commentator (Sāyaṇa) says that in the present Ṛk it is used for filling out the pada.

अतमानं (atamānaṃ) — this word, formed from the root अत सातत्यगमने (ata sātatyagamane) (printed with "!" after it), means people who move at all times (or who are engaged in some work or other).

अह्यर्षणां अविष्यां (ahyarṣaṇāṃ aviṣyāṃ) —

अह्यर्षणां अविष्यां—अहिमाहंतारं शत्रुमर्षंत्यभिगच्छंतीत्यह्यर्षवः तेषामपि गमनेच्छां ।

ahyarṣaṇāṃ aviṣyāṃ—ahimāhaṃtāraṃ śatrumarṣaṃtyabhigacchaṃtītyahyarṣavaḥ teṣāmapi gamanecchāṃ |

अहि (ahi) means people who wish to kill, that is, enemies. The warriors who rush forward to meet those enemies are called अह्यर्षवः (ahyarṣavaḥ). Their गमनेच्छॆ (gamanecchè) (wish to go) means their eagerness to fight, is the sense.

यान् आशुभिश्चित् वि मुचाति आतमानं चित् एतोः आरीरमत् (yān āśubhiścit vi mucāti ātamānaṃ cit etoḥ ārīramat) (as printed: ಆತಮಾನಂ in the explanation, ಅತಮಾನಂ in the Ṛk) —

यान् आशुभिश्चित् वि मुचाति आतमानं चित् एतोः आरीरमत्—गच्छन् सविता शीघ्रगामिभिरपि रश्मिभिः विमुच्यते नूनं सततं गच्छंतमपि जनं गमनात् उपरमयति ।

yān āśubhiścit vi mucāti ātamānaṃ cit etoḥ ārīramat—gacchan savitā śīghragāmibhirapi raśmibhiḥ vimucyate nūnaṃ satataṃ gacchaṃtamapi janaṃ gamanāt uparamayati |

Savitṛ (the Sun), who moves from morning to evening, after he has withdrawn from his rays, that is, after he has set, makes even the people who are by nature moving about, or who are busy with their tasks and works, stop their respective activities. In the daytime, while Savitṛ (the Sun) shines, all people are engaged in moving about and in other activities. After the sun has set, since darkness comes, people cannot do any work and have to keep quiet — this is the meaning.

अह्यर्षणां अविष्यां नि अयान् (ahyarṣaṇāṃ aviṣyāṃ ni ayān) — when the sun has set, not only do the movement and other activities of the people stop, but even warriors who are eager for battle stop the battle they are fighting. That is, since Savitṛ has set and darkness comes, the work of battle stops — this is the meaning.

सवितुः व्रतं अनु मोकी आगात् (savituḥ vrataṃ anu mokī āgāt) — the word मोकी (mokī) is read among the names for night (Nirukta 2-18, printed "ನಿ. ೨-೧೮"). After Savitṛ (the Sun) has stopped his work of movement, that is, after he has set, the night comes — this is the meaning.

Ṛk 4

Note: in the Saṃhitā of Ṛk 4 the second line is garbled as supplied (ಉತ್ಸಂಹಾಯಾಸ್ಥಾದ್ವ ೦ ತೂರದರ್ಧರರಮತಿಃ, with a stray ೦), while the Pada reads ವಿ ಋತೂನ್ ಅದರ್ಧಃ ಅರಮತಿಃ [?]. Also ವಿತತಂ in the Saṃhitā against ವಿತ್ತತಂ in the Pada, and ಶಕ್ಕ in the Saṃhitā against ಶಕ್ಮ in the Pada and bhāṣya; all as supplied. The Pada begins with ಪುನರಿತಿ as supplied.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

पुनः॒ सम॑व्य॒द्वित॑तं॒ वयं॑ती म॒ध्या कर्तो॒न्य॑धा॒च्छक्क॒ धीरः॑ । उत्सं॒हाया॑स्था॒द्व ० १॒॑तूर॑दर्धर॒रम॑तिः सवि॒ता दे॒व आगा॑त् ॥ ४ ॥

punaḥ samavyadvitataṃ vayaṃtī madhyā kartonyadhācchakka dhīraḥ | utsaṃhāyāsthādva 0 tūradardhararamatiḥ savitā deva āgāt ‖ 4 ‖

p. 343

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2 (printed "ಅ."), Adhyāya 8, Varga 2, p. 343 (Ṛgvedasaṃhitā).

॥ पदपाठः ॥

पुनरिति । सं । अव्यत् । वित्ततं । वयंती । मध्या । कर्तोः । नि । अधात् । शक्म । धीरः। उत् । संहाय । अस्थात् । वि । ऋतून् । अदर्धः । अरमतिः । सविता । देवः । आ । आगात् ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

वयंती वस्त्रं वयंती नारीव रात्रिर्विततमालोकं पुनः समव्यत् । संवे- ष्टयते । पुनःशब्दः पूर्वेद्युरप्येवमकार्षिदिति द्योतयति । धीरः प्रज्ञोSपि सर्वो लोकः कर्तोः क्रियमाणं कर्म ॥ कर्तोः कर्तवा इति तन्नामसु पाठात्॥ शक्म कर्तु० शक्यमपि मध्या मध्य उपक्रांतं कर्मापरिसमास्येत्यर्थः । न्यधात् । निहितवान् । सवितर्युपरत इति शेषः । सर्वो लोकः संहायॆ शय्यां विहायो- दस्थात् । अवशिष्टं कर्म कर्तु० पुनरुत्तिष्ठति ॥ संपूर्वो जहातिः शय्यापरित्यागे वर्तते । तथा च श्रूयते । कलिः शयानो भवति संजिहानस्तु द्वापरः । ऐ. ब्रा. ७-१५। इति । सविता सर्वस्य प्रसविता सूर्योSरमतिरनुपरतिर्देवो द्योतमान आगात् । आगच्छति । उदेतीति यावत् । ऋतून् कालविशेषांश्च व्यदर्दः । विदारयति ॥

vayaṃtī vastraṃ vayaṃtī nārīva rātrirvitatamālokaṃ punaḥ samavyat | saṃve- ṣṭayate | punaḥśabdaḥ pūrvedyurapyevamakārṣiditi dyotayati | dhīraḥ prajñoSpi sarvo lokaḥ kartoḥ kriyamāṇaṃ karma ‖ kartoḥ kartavā iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt‖ śakma kartu0 śakyamapi madhyā madhya upakrāṃtaṃ karmāparisamāsyetyarthaḥ | nyadhāt | nihitavān | savitaryuparata iti śeṣaḥ | sarvo lokaḥ saṃhāyè śayyāṃ vihāyo- dasthāt | avaśiṣṭaṃ karma kartu0 punaruttiṣṭhati ‖ saṃpūrvo jahātiḥ śayyāparityāge vartate | tathā ca śrūyate | kaliḥ śayāno bhavati saṃjihānastu dvāparaḥ | ai. brā. 7-15| iti | savitā sarvasya prasavitā sūryoSramatiranuparatirdevo dyotamāna āgāt | āgacchati | udetīti yāvat | ṛtūn kālaviśeṣāṃśca vyadardaḥ | vidārayati ‖

Gist: Night, like a woman weaving cloth, again wraps the spread-out world; the wise man stops his work half-done; Savitṛ rises and the night is cut into seasons.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वयंती (vayaṃtī) — like a woman weaving cloth. विततं (vitataṃ) — the spread-out world. पुनः (punaḥ) — again. समव्यत् (samavyat) — (the night) covers. धीरः (dhīraḥ) — the wise man (the world). कर्तोः (kartoḥ) — from the work to be done. शक्त्य (śaktya) (printed so; the Pada and bhāṣya read ಶಕ್ಮ) — even though he has the strength to do the work. मध्या (madhyā) — in the middle of the work. न्यधात् (nyadhāt) — stops (and again after the rising of Savitṛ). संहाय (saṃhāya) — leaving the bed. उत् अस्थात् (ut asthāt) — rises up. सविता (savitā) — the Sun, the begetter (prasavitṛ) of the world. अरमतिः (aramatiḥ) — without any pause. देवः (devaḥ) — shining. अगात् (agāt) — appears again. ऋतून् (ṛtūn) — the divisions of time. वि आदर्धः (vi ādardhaḥ) (as printed) — he splits up and divides.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like a woman weaving cloth, the night again covers the spread-out world. The wise man, even though he has the strength to do the work, stops the work half-done after the night has arrived. Again, after the rising of Savitṛ, he leaves his bed and rises. The Sun, the begetter of the world, appears again shining, without any pause. He splits up and divides the divisions of time.

(The printed English translation and the Special Topics of Ṛk 4 follow on the next page, p. 344.)

p. 344

Running head: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ, Maṇḍala 2 (printed "ಮ. ೨."), Aṣṭaka 4 (as printed), Sūkta 38, p. 344.

Printed English translation

She, (Night) enwarps the extended (world) like (a woman) weaving (a garment): the prudent man lays aside the work he is able (to execute) iu [sic] the midst (of his labour); but all spring up (from repose) when the divine, unwearied Sun, who has divided the seasons, again appears.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk also it is said that as soon as night arrives, all the business and activities of the people stop half-done, and that they go on again after the rising of the Sun.

वयंती विततं पुनः समव्यत् (vayaṃtī vitataṃ punaḥ samavyat) — वस्त्रं वयंती नारीव रात्रिः आलोकं पुनः संवेष्टयते (vastraṃ vayaṃtī nārīva rātriḥ ālokaṃ punaḥ saṃveṣṭayate) — as a woman who is weaving cloth covers everything with the cloth, so the night again, that is, as on the previous day so also on this day, covers the whole world with darkness. After the sun has set, darkness spreads everywhere and it becomes night; in the time of night, which is full of such darkness, people cannot see and therefore cannot do any work. Whatever work has been done up to the coming of darkness, they have to stop at that.

धीरः कर्तोः शक्त्य मध्या न्यधात् संहाय उत् अस्थात् (dhīraḥ kartoḥ śaktya madhyā nyadhāt saṃhāya ut asthāt) — सवितर्युपरते सति प्रज्ञोSपि सर्वो लोकः क्रियमाणं कर्म० कर्तु० शक्यमपि मध्यॆ उपक्रांतं कर्मापरिसमाप्य निहितवान् । ततः सवितुरदयानंतरं सर्वो लोकः शय्यां विहाय अवशिष्टं कर्म कर्तु० पुनरुत्तिष्ठति । (savitaryuparate sati prajñoSpi sarvo lokaḥ kriyamāṇaṃ karma0 kartu0 śakyamapi madhyè upakrāṃtaṃ karmāparisamāpya nihitavān | tataḥ savituradayānaṃtaraṃ sarvo lokaḥ śayyāṃ vihāya avaśiṣṭaṃ karma kartu0 punaruttiṣṭhati |) (as supplied: ಕರ್ಮ೦, ಕರ್ತು೦, ಸವಿತುರದಯಾನಂತರಂ) When the god Savitṛ has set, darkness spreads; so a working man, however intelligent, cannot work in the dark and stops half-way the work that is half finished. Again, after the sun has risen, he gets up from his bed and begins to complete the work that had been left unfinished. That is, the people in the world, after sunset, stop in the middle the works they were doing, being unable to do them in the dark, and after sunrise, in the light of day, continue and complete the works they had stopped before — this is the meaning.

सविता अरमतिः देवः आगात् (savitā aramatiḥ devaḥ āgāt) — सर्वस्य प्रसविता सूर्यः अनुपरतिः द्योतमान आगच्छति । (sarvasya prasavitā sūryaḥ anuparatiḥ dyotamāna āgacchati |) The god Savitṛ, the source of the whole world, shining, without ever taking rest, comes again and again, that is, every day; that is, he rises. People in the world, if they work every day, want rest from time to time; but the god Savitṛ

p. 345

Running head: "ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೮. ವ. ೨." (as printed, Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 2), Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 345.

(The sentence continues:) although he travels every day without fail, there is no rest for him. As he rose on the former days, so he will rise without fail in the future also — this is the main sense.

ऋतून् वि अदर्धः (ṛtūn vi adardhaḥ) — कालविशेषांश्च विदारयति । (kālaviśeṣāṃśca vidārayati |) It has been said before that ऋतु (ṛtu) means a particular division of time. Since the god Savitṛ rises without fail every day, the divisions of the year, such as season (ṛtu), month, fortnight and day, can be known by his rising and setting. Therefore it is said here that Savitṛ makes the divisions of time.
