Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

नानौकां॑सि॒ दुर्यो॒ विश्व॒मायु॒र्वि ति॑ष्ठते प्रभ॒वः शोको॑ अ॒ग्नेः । ज्येष्ठं॑ मा॒ता सू॒नवे॑ भा॒गमाधा॒दन्व॑स्य॒ केत॑मिषि॒तं स॑वि॒त्रा ॥ ५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

नाना । ओकांसि । दुर्यः । विश्वं । आयुः । वि । तिष्ठते । प्रभवः । शोकः । अग्नेः । ज्येष्ठं । माता । सूनवे । भागं । आ । आधात् । अनु । अस्य । केतं । इषितं । सवित्रा ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

प्रभवः प्रभूतोऽग्नेः शोकस्तेजो दुर्यो गृह्यो गृहे भवो नानौ- कांसि यजमानानां पृथग्भूतान्नगृहान्वितिष्ठते । अधितिष्ठति । विश्वमायुः सर्वमन्नं चाधितिष्ठति ॥ आयुः सूनृतेत्यन्न नामसु पाठात् ॥ मातोषाः सवित्रान्विषितं प्रेषि- तमस्य केतं प्रज्ञापकमग्निर्ज्येष्ठं प्रथममग्निहोत्राख्यं भागं सूनवेऽग्निय आधात् । आदधाति ॥

prabhavaḥ prabhūto 'gneḥ śokastejo duryo gṛhyo gṛhe bhavo nānau- kāṃsi yajamānānāṃ pṛthagbhūtānnagṛhānvitiṣṭhate | adhitiṣṭhati | viśvamāyuḥ sarvamannaṃ cādhitiṣṭhati ‖ āyuḥ sūnṛtetyanna nāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ mātoṣāḥ savitrānviṣitaṃ preṣi- tamasya ketaṃ prajñāpakamagnirjyeṣṭhaṃ prathamamagnihotrākhyaṃ bhāgaṃ sūnave 'gniya ādhāt | ādadhāti ‖

Gist: The bright power of Agni, born in the houses, spreads over the sacrificers' houses and all food; Uṣas, his mother, appoints for her son the first share, the Agnihotra.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

दुर्यः (duryaḥ) — connected with the house. अग्नेः शोकः (agneḥ śokaḥ) — the radiance of Agni. प्रभवः (prabhavaḥ) — abundantly. नाना ओकांसि (nānā okāṃsi) — in many sacrificial houses. वि तिष्ठते (vi tiṣṭhate) — spreads out and occupies. विश्वं आयुः (viśvaṃ āyuḥ) — (becomes the lord) of all food; माता (mātā) — the mother, Uṣas. सवित्रा (savitrā) — by Savitṛ. अनु ईषितं (anu īṣitaṃ) — sent. अस्य केतं (asya ketaṃ) — the indicator of this Agni. ज्येष्ठं (jyeṣṭhaṃ) — and the first, called Agnihotra. भागं (bhāgaṃ) — the share. सूनवे (sūnave) — to the son, Agni. आधात् (ādhāt) — she has appointed.

p. 346

Running head: ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ, "ಮಂ. ೩." (as printed; the Maṇḍala is 2), Aṣṭaka 4, Sūkta 38, p. 346.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiance of Agni, connected with the house, abundantly spreads over and occupies many sacrificial houses. It becomes the lord of all food. The mother Uṣas has appointed, for her son Agni, the first share, called Agnihotra, which is sent by Savitṛ and is the indicator of this Agni.

Printed English translation

The engendered domestic radiance of Agni spreads through various dewellings [sic], and presides over all (sorts of sacrificial) food : the mother, (Dawn). has assigned to her son, (Agni), the best portion (at sacrifices), which is the manifestation of him imparted by Savitri [sic].

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the description of the early morning, when the night has passed and Savitṛ is rising, is set out.

ओकांसि (okāṃsi) — यजमानानां पृथग्भूतान् गृहान् । (yajamānānāṃ pṛthagbhūtān gṛhān |) The separate houses of many sacrificers; Yāska says ओक इति निवासनामोच्यते (oka iti nivāsanāmocyate) (Ni. 3-3): the explanation is that ओक (oka) is a name for a dwelling house. Since many sacrificers perform sacrifice at the same time, that is, in the early morning, in their separate houses, the plural is used in नाना ओकांसि (nānā okāṃsi), "many houses".

दुर्यः (duryaḥ) — the word दुर्य (durya) is read among the names of houses (Ni.-13, as printed with no first number). गृह्यो गृहे भवः (gṛhyo gṛhe bhavaḥ) — Agni who is established in the house of the sacrificer is described here by the word दुर्य (durya).

आयुः (āyuḥ) — the word आयुः (āyuḥ) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). आयु (āyu) may also mean the span of life.

शोकः (śokaḥ) — this word, formed from the root शुच दीप्तौ (śuca dīptau), means light, radiance.

ज्येष्ठं (jyeṣṭhaṃ) — प्रथममग्निहोत्राख्यं । (prathamamagnihotrākhyaṃ |) The rite called Agnihotra, which is performed in the early morning before all other rites — this is the commentator's explanation.

माता सूनवे भागं (mātā sūnave bhāgaṃ) — here the goddess Uṣas is called the mother of Agni. Since after the time of dawn the fire is established and the homa and other rites are performed, Uṣas is described as the mother of Agni.

p. 347

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 347.

(Special Topics of Ṛk 5, continued) दुर्यः अग्नेः शोकः प्रभवः नाना ओकांसि वि तिष्ठते (duryaḥ agneḥ śokaḥ prabhavaḥ nānā okāṃsi vi tiṣṭhate)—गृहसंबंधि अग्नेस्तेजः यजमानानां पृथग्भूतान् गृहान् अधितिष्ठति । (gṛhasaṃbaṃdhi agnestejaḥ yajamānānāṃ pṛthagbhūtān gṛhān adhitiṣṭhati |) Many sacrificers who perform sacrifice in the early morning install fire in their own separate houses and perform the Agnihotra and other rites. Since the sacrificers are many, their houses too are many. Agni is installed at the same moment in all these houses and shines with his radiance. That he thus shines at one and the same time in many houses is described here as Agni's greatness.

विश्वं आयुः (viśvaṃ āyuḥ)—सर्वमन्नं चाधितिष्ठति । (sarvamannaṃ cādhitiṣṭhati |) Since Agni is the giver of food to the sacrificers, to the priests and to those who praise him, he is described as the lord of all food and other things to be eaten.

माता सवित्रा अनु ईषितं अस्य केतं ज्येष्ठं भागं सूनवे आधात् (mātā savitrā anu īṣitaṃ asya ketaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bhāgaṃ sūnave ādhāt)—उषाः सवित्रा प्रेषितं प्रज्ञापकमग्नेः प्रथममग्निहोत्राख्यं भागं सूनवेऽग्नये आदधाति । (uṣāḥ savitrā preṣitaṃ prajñāpakamagneḥ prathamamagnihotrākhyaṃ bhāgaṃ sūnave 'gnaye ādadhāti |) By the command of the god Savitṛ, the mother of Agni, that is, the goddess Uṣas, who rises before Agni, has arranged that the first share in the Agnihotra and other rites that the sacrificers perform in the morning be offered to her son Agni. The sacrificers install the fire in the morning that arrives after the appearance of Uṣas. Since the time of dawn therefore arrives before the installation of the fire, Uṣas is said to be the mother of Agni. It is natural for a mother to wish her son well; accordingly Uṣas has arranged that the first oblation be offered to Agni in the Agnihotra and other rites that the sacrificers perform as soon as it is morning. Thus the greatness of Savitṛ is described here: this arrangement made by Uṣas is prompted by the god Savitṛ.

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

स॒माव॑वर्ति॒ विष्ठि॑तो जिगी॒षुर्विश्वे॑षां॒ काम॒श्चर॑ताम॒माभू॑त् । शश्वा॒ अपो॒ विकृ॑तं हि॒त्वा गा॒दनु॑ व्र॒तं स॑वि॒तुद्वैव्य॑स्य ॥ ६ ॥

samāvavarti viṣṭhito jigīṣurviśveṣāṃ kāmaścaratāmamābhūt | śaśvā apo vikṛtaṃ hitvā gādanu vrataṃ savitudvaivyasya ‖ 6 ‖

p. 348

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38, p. 348.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

संआववर्ति । विस्थितः । जिगीषुः । विश्वेषां । कामः । चरतां । अमा । अभूत् । शश्वान् । अपः । विकृतं । हित्वी । आ । अगात् । अनु । व्रतं । सवितुः । दैव्यस्य ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

जिगीषुर्विजयेच्छुर्योद्धा विष्ठितो युद्धार्थं प्रस्थितः समाववर्ति । समावर्तयति । विश्वेषां सर्वेषां चरतां जंगमानाममा । अमा दम इति गृह- नामसु पाठात् । गृहं प्रति कामोऽभूत् । भवति । शश्वान् नित्यं कर्मरतोऽपः कर्म विकृतमर्धकृतं हित्वी हित्वागात् । गृहमागच्छति । एतत्सर्वं दैव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य सवितुः प्रेरकस्य सूर्यस्य व्रतमस्तमयाख्यं कर्मानु जायत इत्यर्थः ॥

jigīṣurvijayecchuryoddhā viṣṭhito yuddhārthaṃ prasthitaḥ samāvavarti | samāvartayati | viśveṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ caratāṃ jaṃgamānāmamā | amā dama iti gṛha- nāmasu pāṭhāt | gṛhaṃ prati kāmo 'bhūt | bhavati | śaśvān nityaṃ karmarato 'paḥ karma vikṛtamardhakṛtaṃ hitvī hitvāgāt | gṛhamāgacchati | etatsarvaṃ daivyasya divi bhavasya savituḥ prerakasya sūryasya vratamastamayākhyaṃ karmānu jāyata ityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: The warrior setting out to fight turns back; home is the wish of all moving beings; the toiler leaves his work half done and returns home, following the sunset rite of Savitṛ.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

जिगीषुः (jigīṣuḥ) — desirous of obtaining victory. विष्ठितः (viṣṭhitaḥ) — the warrior who has set out for battle. समाववर्ति (samāvavarti) — turns back. विश्वेषां (viśveṣāṃ) — of all; चरतां (caratāṃ) — of beings that are moving; to such creatures. अमा (amā) — the house. कामः (kāmaḥ) — as the desired place. अभूत् (abhūt) — it is. दैव्यस्य (daivyasya) — of the one born in the heaven-world. सवितुः (savituḥ) — of the Sun. व्रतं (vrataṃ) — the rite called the setting. अनु (anu) — when it is known. शश्वान् (śaśvān) — even one who is constantly intent on work. अपः (apaḥ) — his own task. विकृतं (vikṛtaṃ) — though half done. हित्वी (hitvī) — stopping it there. आगात् (āgāt) — comes home.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The warrior who is eager for victory and has set out for battle returns home. For all creatures the house is the desired place. When the rite of the Sun, born in the heaven-world, called the setting, is known, even one who is constantly intent on work leaves his task there, though half done, and comes home.

Printed English translation

The warrior, eager for victory, who has gone forth (to battle), turns back; (for) home is the desire of all moving beings: abandoning his half-wrought toil, the labourer returns (home) when the function of the divine Savitri (is suspended).

p. 349

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 349.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

(The printed label is garbled in the supplied text; it reads as Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu.) In this Ṛk it is described that after Savitṛ (the Sun) has set, people stop what they are doing, however much of it is done, and turn back towards their homes.

जिगीषुः विष्ठितः समाववर्ति (jigīṣuḥ viṣṭhitaḥ samāvavarti)—विजयेच्छुः योद्धा युद्धार्थं प्रस्थितः समावर्तयति । (vijayecchuḥ yoddhā yuddhārthaṃ prasthitaḥ samāvartayati |) The warrior who has set out to fight his enemies and conquer them stops the fighting as soon as evening comes and returns home. For after the sun has set it is dark and nothing can be seen, so no work can be done. Therefore he stops the battle and other tasks he has begun and turns towards home.

विश्वेषां चरतां अमा कामः अभूत् (viśveṣāṃ caratāṃ amā kāmaḥ abhūt)—सर्वेषां जंगमानां प्राणिनां गृहं प्रति कामो भवति । (sarveṣāṃ jaṃgamānāṃ prāṇināṃ gṛhaṃ prati kāmo bhavati |) Because the word अमा (amā) is read among the names of the house (Ni. 3-13), it means "house". After sunset all creatures whose nature is to move about wish to go to their own houses or dwelling places. By day animals and men too leave their houses and move about in various places, to gain food and other things or to do other duties. In the evening, when it is dark and no work can be done, they wish to go to their own dwellings for rest; this is the meaning.

देव्यस्य सवितुः व्रतं अनु शश्वान् अपः विकृतं हित्वा आगात् (devyasya savituḥ vrataṃ anu śaśvān apaḥ vikṛtaṃ hitvā āgāt)—दिवि भवस्य सवितुः प्रेरकस्य सूरस्य अस्तमयाख्यं कर्म अनु अर्थकृतं कर्म हित्वा गृहमागच्छति । (divi bhavasya savituḥ prerakasya sūrasya astamayākhyaṃ karma anu arthakṛtaṃ karma hitvā gṛhamāgacchati |) After sunset the man who is at work stops the work he is doing half way, turns back and comes home. That he thus leaves work unfinished and comes away half way is the greatness of the rule (law) of the god Savitṛ called the setting; this is the main idea. (The supplied text prints देव्यस्य (devyasya), सूरस्य (sūrasya) and अर्थकृतं (arthakṛtaṃ) here, where the Saṃhitā/bhāṣya above have दैव्यस्य (daivyasya), सूर्यस्य (sūryasya) and अर्धकृतं (ardhakṛtaṃ); noted, not altered.)

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

त्वया॑ हि॒तमप्य॑म॒प्सु भा॒गं धन्वान्वा मृ॑ग॒यसो॒ वि त॑स्थुः । वना॑नि॒ विभो॒ नकि॑रस्य॒ तानि॑ व्र॒ता दे॒वस्य॑ सवि॒तुर्मि॑नंति ॥ ७ ॥

tvayā hitamapyamapsu bhāgaṃ dhanvānvā mṛgayaso vi tasthuḥ | vanāni vibho nakirasya tāni vratā devasya saviturminaṃti ‖ 7 ‖

p. 350

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38, p. 350.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

त्वया । हितं । अप्यं । अप्सु । भागं । धन्व । अनु । आ । मृगयसः । वि । तस्थुः । वनानि । विभ्यः । नकिः । अस्य । तानि । व्रता । देवस्य । सवितुः । मिनंति ॥ ७ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे सवितस्त्वयाप्संतरिक्षे ॥ आपः पृथिवीत्यंतरिक्षनामसु पाठात् ॥ जलाधारे वा हितं निहितमप्यमपां संबंधिनं भागं धन्वानु निर्जलप्रदेशेश्वरणेषु मृग- यसो मृगयमाणा मृगा आ समंताद्वितस्थुः । अधितिष्ठंति । किंच वनानि वृक्षा विभ्यः पक्षिभ्य आवासादिरूपेण त्वया भागो दत्तः । अस्य देवस्य सवितुस्तानि तादृशानि व्रता व्रतानि कर्माणि नकिर्मिनंति । केऽपि न हिंसंति ॥

Gist: Savitṛ, you have placed the share belonging to the waters in the firmament; animals search for it in waterless regions; you have made the trees dwellings for birds; no one can obstruct this god's works.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(सवितः (savitaḥ) — O Savitṛ). त्वया (tvayā) — by you. अप्पु (appu) (as supplied) — in the firmament. हितं (hitaṃ) — what has been placed. अप्यं (apyaṃ) — what belongs to the waters (the Kannada says "to the belly", उदरसंबंधवादुदू (udarasaṃbaṃdhavādudū), as supplied). भागं (bhāgaṃ) — the share. धन्वानु (dhanvānu) — in waterless forest regions. मृगयसः (mṛgayasaḥ) — the animals that search. आ (ā) — all around. वि तस्थुः (vi tasthuḥ) — stand pressing in. वनानि (vanāni) — the forest trees. विभ्यः (vibhyaḥ) — to the birds (you have arranged them as dwellings). अस्य देवस्य सवितुः (asya devasya savituḥ) — of this Savitṛ, who is divine in nature. तानि व्रता (tāni vratā) — such extraordinary works. नकिः मिनंति (nakiḥ minaṃti) — no one can obstruct.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Savitṛ, the animals that search in the waterless forest regions press in all around the share connected with water (or "the belly" as supplied) that you have placed in the firmament. You have arranged the forest trees to be dwellings for the birds. No one can obstruct the extraordinary works of this Savitṛ, who is divine in nature.

Printed English translation

The animals search in dry places for the watery element which has been collected in the firmament by you : the woods are assigned (by you) to the birds : no one obstructs these functions of the divine Savitri.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अप्यं (apyaṃ)—अपां संबंधिनं भागं (apāṃ saṃbaṃdhinaṃ bhāgaṃ) — the share that belongs to water, that is, the region of water.

p. 351

Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, p. 351.

अप्पु (appu)—अंतरिक्षे (aṃtarikṣe) । Because the words आपः (āpaḥ) and पृथिवी (pṛthivī) are read among the names of the firmament (Ni. 2-10), अप्पु (appu) means "in the firmament".

धन्व (dhanva)—The word धन्व (dhanva) is read among the names of the firmament (Ni. 2-10), and there is also the explanation धन्वांतरिक्षं धन्वंत्सस्मादापः (dhanvāṃtarikṣaṃ dhanvaṃtsasmādāpaḥ) (as supplied, the second part looks garbled) (Ni. 5-5). The Bhāṣyakāra explains it with निर्जलप्रदेशेश्वरणेषु (nirjalapradeśeśvaraṇeṣu) (as supplied): a waterless forest region.

नकिः (nakiḥ)—The particle नकिः (nakiḥ) is read among the nine groups of pronominal words beginning हिकं नुकं (hikaṃ nukaṃ) (as supplied) (3-12). It means "not at all".

त्वया अप्पु हितं अप्यं भागं धन्व अनु मृगयसः आ वि तस्थुः (tvayā appu hitaṃ apyaṃ bhāgaṃ dhanva anu mṛgayasaḥ ā vi tasthuḥ)—हे सवितः त्वया अंतरिक्षे निहितं अपां संबंधिनं भागं निर्जलप्रदेशेश्वरणेषु मृगयमाणा मृगाः आसमंतात् अधितिष्ठंति (he savitaḥ tvayā aṃtarikṣe nihitaṃ apāṃ saṃbaṃdhinaṃ bhāgaṃ nirjalapradeśeśvaraṇeṣu mṛgayamāṇā mṛgāḥ āsamaṃtāt adhitiṣṭhaṃti) । O god Savitṛ, in order that rain may fall you have established water in the firmament in the form of clouds. Since there has been no rain, there is no water anywhere on the earth. Therefore the animals of the forest, searching for the water that sustains life, roam in the waterless forest regions.

वनानि विभ्यः (vanāni vibhyaḥ)—वृक्षा आवासादिरूपेण त्वया भागो दत्तः (vṛkṣā āvāsādirūpeṇa tvayā bhāgo dattaḥ) । Trees and the like have been arranged by you as dwelling places for birds.

अस्य देवस्य सवितुः तानि व्रता नकिः मिनंति (asya devasya savituḥ tāni vratā nakiḥ minaṃti)—तादृशानि सवितुः कर्माणि केऽपि न हिंसंति (tādṛśāni savituḥ karmāṇi ke 'pi na hiṃsaṃti) । These rules of Savitṛ, that is, the works mentioned above, the wandering of animals in the forest for water and the nesting and dwelling of birds in trees, go on according to Savitṛ's command. No one is able to obstruct them; this is the meaning.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

या॒द्रा॒ध्यं१॒॑ वरु॑णो॒ योनि॒मप्य॒मनि॑शितं नि॒मिषि॒ जर्भु॑राणः । विश्वो॑ मार्तां॒डो व्र॒जमा प॒शुर्गा॑त्स्थ॒शो जन्मा॑नि सवि॒ता व्याकः॑ ॥

yādrādhyaṃ varuṇo yonimapyamaniśitaṃ nimiṣi jarbhurāṇaḥ | viśvo mārtāṃḍo vrajamā paśurgātsthaśo janmāni savitā vyākaḥ ‖

p. 352

Running head: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38, p. 352.

॥ पदपाठः ॥

यार्त्स्राध्यं । वरुणः । योनिं । अप्यं । अनिशितं । निमिषि । जर्भुराणः । विश्वः । मार्तांडः । व्रजं । आ । पशुः । गात् । स्थतः । जन्मानि । सविता । वि । आ । अकरित्यकः ॥ ८ ॥

yārtsrādhyaṃ | varuṇaḥ | yoniṃ | apyaṃ | aniśitaṃ | nimiṣi | jarbhurāṇaḥ | viśvaḥ | mārtāṃḍaḥ | vrajaṃ | ā | paśuḥ | gāt | sthataḥ | janmāni | savitā | vi | ā | akarityakaḥ ‖ 8 ‖

Note: the Pada as supplied reads यार्त्स्राध्यं (yārtsrādhyaṃ), स्थतः (sthataḥ) and अकरित्यकः (akarityakaḥ) where the Saṃhitā has याद्राध्यं (yādrādhyaṃ), स्थशो (sthaśo) and व्याकः (vyākaḥ); noted, not altered.

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

वरुणो याद्राध्यं यातां गच्छतां राध्यं राधनीयमप्यमाप्तुं योग्य- मनिशितमतीक्ष्णं । सुखकरमिति यावत् । योनिं स्थानं निमिषि निमेषे सवितुरस्त- मये सति विश्रमार्थं प्राणिभ्यः प्रयच्छति । वरुणस्य रात्रेनिर्वाहकत्वात् । जर्भुराणो भृशं गच्छन् विश्वः सर्वो मार्तांडो मृताद्भिन्नादंडादुत्पद्यमानः पक्ष्यागात् । आगच्छति । विश्वः पशुरपि व्रजं गोष्ठमागात् । सविता प्रेरकः स्थशः स्थाने स्थाने जन्मानि जातानि भूतानि व्याकः । पृथगकार्षित् ॥

Gist: at sunset Varuna grants moving beings a pleasant resting place; birds and cattle return to nests and pens; Savitṛ distributes creatures to their several places.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वरुणः (varuṇaḥ) — Varuṇa. याद्राध्यं (yādrādhyaṃ) — what is worthy of worship by moving living beings. अप्यं (apyaṃ) — what is fit to enter. अनिशितं (aniśitaṃ) — agreeable. योनिं (yoniṃ) — dwelling place. निमिषे (nimiṣe) — after sunset (he arranges it for the rest of living beings). जर्भुराणः (jarbhurāṇaḥ) — those that fly in haste. विश्वः (viśvaḥ) — all. मार्तांडः (mārtāṃḍaḥ) — birds. आ गात् (ā gāt) — come and gather (in their nests). पशुः (paśuḥ) — cattle also. व्रजं (vrajaṃ) — come and gather in the pen. सविता (savitā) — Savitṛ, the impeller. स्थशः (sthaśaḥ) — in the several directions. जन्मानि (janmāni) — living beings. व्याकः (vyākaḥ) — separated them one from another.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

After sunset Varuṇa arranges, for the rest of living beings, dwelling places that are worthy of worship by moving creatures, fit to enter and agreeable. All the birds, flying in haste, come and gather in their nests. Cattle also gather in their pens. Savitṛ, the impeller, has separated living beings one from another in all directions.

Printed English translation

The ever-going Varuna grants a cool, accessible, and agreeable place (of rest), to all moving (creachers) [sic], on the closing of eyes (of Savitri);

(The printed translation of this Ṛk breaks off here in the supplied text at the end of p. 352; it continues on p. 353.)

p. 353

and every bird and every beast repairs to its lair when Savitri has dispersed (all) beings in various directions.

(Stray line "23" at the foot of p. 353 in the supplied text, a signature mark, kept in kn.md and not translated.)

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

याद्राध्यं (yādrādhyaṃ)—यातां गच्छतां संराधनीयं (yātāṃ gacchatāṃ saṃrādhanīyaṃ) । Worthy of worship, that is, desirable, for creatures whose nature is to move about. Creatures and men who have wandered all day for food and the like and are tired out look forward eagerly to night, the time of their rest. The sense is therefore that night is welcomed by all.

योनिं (yoniṃ)—A place, or a dwelling-place. The word yoni is read among the names of house (Ni. 3-13).

वरुणः (varuṇaḥ)—The god Varuṇa. वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ) (Ni. 10-3) स हि वियत् वृणोति मेघजालेन (sa hi viyat vṛṇoti meghajālena) । Because he covers the sky, pervading it with masses of clouds, he is called Varuṇa; this is Yāska's explanation. The subject of the god Varuṇa is treated in the next Ṛk. That Varuṇa is the presiding deity of night is stated in the Yajurveda: मैत्रं वा अहर्वारुणी रात्रिः (maitraṃ vā aharvāruṇī rātriḥ) (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4).

अप्यं (apyaṃ)—आप्तुं योग्यं (āptuṃ yogyaṃ) । Fit to be attained, which all desire.

अनिशितं (aniśitaṃ)—अतीक्ष्णं सुखकरमिति यावत् (atīkṣṇaṃ sukhakaramiti yāvat) । Nishita means sharp; anishita means not sharp, pleasant. The sense is that night, the time of rest, is pleasant to all.

मार्तांडः (mārtāṃḍaḥ)—मृताद्भिन्नात् अंडादुत्पद्यमानः पक्षी (mṛtādbhinnāt aṃḍādutpadyamānaḥ pakṣī) । A bird is born from an egg; since that egg (anḍa) is not dead but alive, the bird born from it is called mārtāṇḍa. So the commentator explains the meaning.

स्थशः (sthaśaḥ)—स्थाने स्थाने (sthāne sthāne) । In many different places, or in many directions.

वरुणः याद्राध्यं अप्यं अनिशितं योनिं निमिषे वरुणो रात्र्यभिमानी देवः गच्छतां संराधनीयं प्राप्तुं योग्यं सुखकरं स्थानं सवितुरस्तमये विश्रमार्थं प्रयच्छति (varuṇaḥ yādrādhyaṃ apyaṃ aniśitaṃ yoniṃ nimiṣe varuṇo rātryabhimānī devaḥ gacchatāṃ saṃrādhanīyaṃ prāptuṃ yogyaṃ sukhakaraṃ sthānaṃ saviturastamaye viśramārthaṃ prayacchati) । The god Varuṇa is the presiding deity of night. Therefore, for the creatures that have toiled and wandered all day for food and are tired, after sunset he provides the pleasant dwelling-place they desire for rest. How? This is made clear in the following sentences.

जर्भुराणः विश्वः मार्तांडः आ गात् (jarbhurāṇaḥ viśvaḥ mārtāṃḍaḥ ā gāt)—भृशं गच्छन् अंडादुत्पद्यमानः सर्वः पक्षी आ गच्छति (bhṛśaṃ gacchan aṃḍādutpadyamānaḥ sarvaḥ pakṣī ā gacchati) । All the birds born of eggs, having moved about much during the day, come after sunset to their several dwelling-places, the nests. Here the word mārtāṇḍa, denoting a bird, should be taken as a collective singular and given a plural sense.

p. 354

पशुः व्रजं आगात् (paśuḥ vrajaṃ āgāt)—विश्वः पशुः गोष्ठमागात् (viśvaḥ paśuḥ goṣṭhamāgāt) । Here too the word paśu is used as a collective singular. All animals, cows and the rest, go to their respective pens.

सविता स्थशः जन्मानि व्याकः (savitā sthaśaḥ janmāni vyākaḥ)—आसौ प्रेरकः सविता स्थाने स्थाने जातानि भूतानि पृथगकार्षीत् (āsau prerakaḥ savitā sthāne sthāne jātāni bhūtāni pṛthagakārṣīt) । This god Savitṛ, who impels all things, causes all the creatures born on the earth to go to their several separate dwelling-places. That is, all creatures do not gather at one spot at night. Birds go to their nests in the trees; cows and other cattle go to the pens assigned to them; men go to their houses. In this way the greatness of Savitṛ is described, who has provided different resting places for creatures.

Ṛk 9

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

न यस्येंद्रो॒ वरु॑णो॒ न मि॒त्रो व्र॒तम॑र्य॒मा न मि॒नंति॑ रु॒द्रः । नारा॑तय॒स्तमि॒दं स्व॒स्ति हु॒वे दे॒वं स॑वि॒तारं॒ नमो॑भिः ॥ ९ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

न । यस्य । इंद्रः । वरुणः । न । मित्रः । व्रतं । अर्यमा । न । मिनंति । रुद्रः । न । अरातयः । तं । इदं । स्वस्ति । हुवे । देवं । सवितारं । नमःभिः ॥ ९ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

यस्य सवितुर्देवस्य व्रतं प्रसवाख्यं कर्मेंद्रो न मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । वरुणश्च न मिनाति मित्रश्चार्यमा च न मिनाति रुद्रश्च न मिनाति । अरातयोऽसुराश्च न मिनंति ॥ मिनातीति श्रुतमाख्यातं यथायोगं विपरिणामेन प्रत्येकमभिसंब- ध्यते । तं सवितारं सर्वस्य प्रेरकं देवं द्योतमानविदमिदानीं नमोभिरन्नरू- पैर्हविर्भिः सह ॥ नम आयुरित्यन्ननामसु पाठात् ॥ स्वस्ति क्षेमाय हुवे । स्तौमि ॥

Gist: neither Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Rudra nor enemies impede Savitṛ's act of impelling; he is invoked with food-offerings for welfare.

p. 355

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

यस्य (yasya)—of which Savitṛ. व्रतं (vrataṃ)—the unique work. इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra. न (na) (मिनाति (mināti))—cannot obstruct. वरुणः (varuṇaḥ)—Varuṇa. न (na)—cannot obstruct. मित्रः (mitraḥ)—Mitra. अर्यमा (aryamā)—Aryaman. न (na)—cannot obstruct. रुद्रः (rudraḥ)—Rudra. न (na)—cannot obstruct. अरातयः (arātayaḥ)—even enemies. न मिनंति (na minaṃti)—cannot injure. तं (taṃ)—such. देवं (devaṃ)—resplendent. सवितारं (savitāraṃ)—Savitṛ. इदं (idaṃ)—now. नमोभिः (namobhiḥ)—with offerings in the form of food. स्वस्ति (svasti)—for well-being. हुवे (huve)—I invoke and praise.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

That Savitṛ, whose unique work neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra or Aryaman, nor Rudra can obstruct, and whom enemies cannot injure, that resplendent Savitṛ I now invoke and praise, for well-being, with food-offerings.

Printed English translation

I invite to this place, with reverential salutations, for my good, that divine Savitri, whose functions neither Indaa [sic], nor Varuna, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman, nor Rudra, nor the enemies (of the gods), impede.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

The unique work (ordinance) of the god Savitṛ cannot be obstructed or violated by any gods such as Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman and Rudra. No enemies can injure this god. The chief purport of this Ṛk is: "I praise such a greatly glorious Savitṛ by offering him food-offerings."

इंद्र (iṃdra)—We have written about Indra at length before.

मित्रः (mitraḥ), वरुणः (varuṇaḥ), अर्यमा (aryamā)—Although these three deities are regarded as separate gods, here they seem to be explained as the partial deities of those names among the many forms of the Sun, that is, among the twelve Ādityas. Moreover, in some places these three deities are said to be different forms of Agni.

त्वमग्ने वरुणो जायसे यत्त्वं मित्रो भवसि यत्समिद्धः (tvamagne varuṇo jāyase yattvaṃ mitro bhavasi yatsamiddhaḥ) । (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1)

त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि (tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi) । (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-2)

p. 356

[Running head, p. 356: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

In these Ṛks it is said that Agni, when born, is called Varuṇa; when well kindled and blazing brightly, Mitra; and in the marriage-related homas and the like, Aryaman: that Agni has these three names. Moreover, in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

मित्रोऽसि वरुणोऽसीत्याह । मैत्रं ना अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः । अहोरात्राभ्यामेवैनमुपावहरति ॥

mitro 'si varuṇo 'sītyāha | maitraṃ nā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ | ahorātrābhyāmevainamupāvaharati ‖

(Tai. Brā. 1-7-10-1)

It is said that Mitra is the lord of the day and Varuṇa the lord of the night. Therefore it should be noted that these three deities are said in some places to be partial deities of the Sun and in some places to be different names of Agni.

In the Purāṇas and the like, Mitra is one of the twelve Ādityas. In the Ṛgveda, although Mitra is another name of the Sun, Mitra has a distinct individuality, that is, a personal prominence. In the Ṛgveda Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are said to be the sons of Aditi. Therefore they are called Ādityas in many places. That the Ādityas, that is, the sons of Aditi, are six in number:

इमा गिर आदित्येभ्यो धृतस्नूः सनाद्राजभ्यो जुह्वा जुहोमि । शृणोतु मित्रो अर्यमा भगो नस्तुविजातो वरुणो दक्षो अंशः ॥

imā gira ādityebhyo dhṛtasnūḥ sanādrājabhyo juhvā juhomi | śṛṇotu mitro aryamā bhago nastuvijāto varuṇo dakṣo aṃśaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1)

[Garbled duplicate reference line as supplied, kept: (Ma. Saṃ. 2-27-1).]

means that only six names are given: Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa.

देवा आदित्या ये सप्त तेभिः सोमाभि रक्ष न इंद्रायेंदो परि स्रव ।

devā ādityā ye sapta tebhiḥ somābhi rakṣa na iṃdrāyeṃdo pari srava |

(Ma. Saṃ. 9-114-3) [as supplied; the initial is printed म (ma) here, as in the garbled line above]

In this [Ṛk] the sons of Aditi are said to be seven. [The text has मक्किनल्लि (makkinalli) for ऋक्किनल्लि (ṛkkinalli): apparent slip of the supplied text, kept as supplied.]

अष्टौ पुत्रासो आदितेर्यॆ जातास्तन्व १ स्परि । देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः परा मार्तंडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिरुप प्रैत्तूर्व्यं युगं । प्रजायै मृत्यवे त्वत्पुनर्मार्तंडमाभरत् ॥

aṣṭau putrāso āditeryè jātāstanva 1 spari | devā upapraitsaptabhiḥ parā mārtaṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditirupa praittūrvyaṃ yugaṃ | prajāyai mṛtyave tvatpunarmārtaṃḍamābharat ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8, 9)

[Note on the supplied text: the first line has a stray numeral १ (1) after तन्व (tanva) and स्परि (spari); kept as supplied, no reading is claimed.]

In these Ṛks it is said that Aditi had first seven sons and then Mārtaṇḍa, eight sons in all. Moreover, in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:

अष्टा पुत्रासो आदितेः । ये जातास्तन्वः हरि । देवा उपप्रैत्सप्तभिः । परामार्तांडमास्यत् । सप्तभिः पुत्रैरदितिः । उपप्रैत्पूर्व्यं युगं ।

aṣṭā putrāso āditeḥ | ye jātāstanvaḥ hari | devā upapraitsaptabhiḥ | parāmārtāṃḍamāsyat | saptabhiḥ putrairaditiḥ | upapraitpūrvyaṃ yugaṃ |

p. 357

[Running head, p. 357: A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā. The block begun on p. 356 continues here.]

प्रजायै मृत्यवे तत् । परामार्तांडमाभरदिति । ताननुक्रमिष्यामः मित्रश्च वरुणश्च । धाता चार्यमा च । अगंशश्च भगश्च । इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्श्चेत्येते ॥

prajāyai mṛtyave tat | parāmārtāṃḍamābharaditi | tānanukramiṣyāmaḥ mitraśca varuṇaśca | dhātā cāryamā ca | agaṃśaśca bhagaśca | iṃdraśca vivasvāgścetyete ‖

(Tai. A. 1-13-3)

The names of the eight sons of Aditi are also given: Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātā, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra, Vivasvān are those eight. [In the quotation on p. 356 the text has हरि (hari) where the Ṛk has परि (pari); kept as supplied.] The same matter is stated in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa:

अदितिः पुत्रकामा । साध्येभ्यो देवेभ्यो ब्रह्मौदनमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै धाता चार्यमा जाजायेतां । सा द्वितीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोधत्त । तस्यै मित्रश्च ।वरुणश्चाजायेतां । सा तृतीयमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या अगंंशश्च भगश्चाजायेतां । सा चतुर्थमपचत् । तस्या उच्छेषणमददुः । तत्पाश्नात् । सा रेतोऽधत्त । तस्या इंद्रश्च विवस्वाग्ंश्चाजायेतां ॥

aditiḥ putrakāmā | sādhyebhyo devebhyo brahmaudanamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai dhātā cāryamā jājāyetāṃ | sā dvitīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā retodhatta | tasyai mitraśca |varuṇaścājāyetāṃ | sā tṛtīyamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā agaṃṃśaśca bhagaścājāyetāṃ | sā caturthamapacat | tasyā uccheṣaṇamadaduḥ | tatpāśnāt | sā reto 'dhatta | tasyā iṃdraśca vivasvāgṃścājāyetāṃ ‖

(Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1, 2, 3)

It is stated [thus]. The fact that Aditi bore eight sons is clearly set out here. Among these eight, the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, are the specially famous ones in the Ṛgveda. In the Ṛgveda, sūkta 2-7 [as printed], there is an extensive description of the beneficent heroic deeds of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman.

Mitra (मित्रः (mitraḥ))—Yāska has given the derivation of the word Mitra in his Nirukta as follows:

मित्रः प्रमीतेस्त्रायते । संमिन्वानो द्रवतीति ना । मेदयतेर्वा ।

mitraḥ pramītestrāyate | saṃminvāno dravatīti nā | medayatervā |

(Si. 10-21) [as supplied; the abbreviation is not the usual one for the Nirukta, and no correction is made]

What is the meaning of the word Mitra? It is: मित्रः कस्मात् । स हि प्रमितेः त्रायते । प्रमितिः मरणं । ततः सर्वलोकं त्रायते वर्षद्वारेण । (mitraḥ kasmāt | sa hi pramiteḥ trāyate | pramitiḥ maraṇaṃ | tataḥ sarvalokaṃ trāyate varṣadvāreṇa |) "Prāmiti" means death. Because he causes rain in the world, thereby provides food and other nourishment to people, averts and protects them from the fear of death by hunger, this deity is called Mitra.

समंततो मिन्वानः उदकेन द्रवति अंतरिक्षलोके । (samaṃtato minvānaḥ udakena dravati aṃtarikṣaloke |) This deity, being lord of water, dwelling in the atmosphere, through the clouds makes all around, that is, the whole region, be soaked, that is, wet with water; therefore this deity is called Mitra.

Or: स्नेहनार्थस्य सर्वं ह्यसावुदकेन स्नेहयति । (snehanārthasya sarvaṃ hyasāvudakena snehayati |) This deity makes everything cling together by water, that is, unite into one; therefore this deity is called Mitra. Having given these three kinds of derivation, to support it [he cites]:

p. 358

[Running head, p. 358: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

मित्रो जनान् यातयति ब्रुवाणो मित्रो दाधार पृथवीमुत द्यां । मित्रः कृष्णीरनिमिषाभि चष्टे मित्राय हव्यं धृतवज्जु होत ॥

mitro janān yātayati bruvāṇo mitro dādhāra pṛthavīmuta dyāṃ | mitraḥ kṛṣṇīranimiṣābhi caṣṭe mitrāya havyaṃ dhṛtavajju hota ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59-1) [printed with a stray space: "3-59 -1"]

This Ṛk is given as an example. In this Ṛk it is described very well how Mitra, helping the works such as agriculture, pouring rain and the like, and providing food and other nourishment to people, sustains, that is, nourishes, both the people of the earth and the dwellers in heaven. "O men, offer to such a Mitra the oblations and the like mixed with ghee": thus Mitra's unique qualities and his beneficence to the world are described. The only sūkta in the Ṛgveda devoted to Mitra is this one of 9 Ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59); elsewhere Mitra is praised together with other deities such as Varuṇa. Because the association of Mitra and Varuṇa is very frequent, there is, as said before, only one sūkta in the Ṛgveda having Mitra alone as deity (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59); even there the praise of that deity is indistinct. But only in the first Ṛk is Mitra's distinctive character well stated. In the fifth Ṛk of the same sūkta:

महा आदित्यो नमसोपसद्यो यातयज्जनो गृणते सुशेवः ।

mahā ādityo namasopasadyo yātayajjano gṛṇate suśevaḥ |

(Ma. Saṃ. 3-59-5) [as supplied: म. (ma.) for ऋ. (ṛ.)]

this Mitra is called the great Āditya who unites all men together. The word यातयज्जन (yātayajjana) that gives this sense is used of Mitra and Varuṇa in

व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातॆयज्जना ।

vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātèyajjanā |

(Ma. Saṃ. 5-72-2) [as supplied; the text has मिक्किनल्लि (mikkinalli) for ऋक्किनल्लि (ṛkkinalli) in the next sentence, kept]

this Ṛk, and of the three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, in

मित्रस्तयोर्वरुणो यातयज्ज नोऽर्यमा यातयज्जनः ।

mitrastayorvaruṇo yātayajja no 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ |

(Ma. Saṃ. 1-136-3)

this Ṛk. According to the sūkta Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-59 mentioned above, Mitra is the support of heaven and earth. The five tribes of men (pañcajanāḥ) are obedient to him; he is the sustenance of life for all the other deities: thus Mitra's qualities are described. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-81-4 Savitṛ and Mitra are said to be one; in the Vājasaneyisaṃhitā (Vā. Saṃ. 4-3) that Viṣṇu took his three steps following Mitra's ordinances; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-8-4 that Agni, established before the dawn, himself generates Mitra for himself; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-5-4 that the blazing Agni is himself Mitra; in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-3-1 that when Agni is born he is Mitra, and

p. 359

[Running head, p. 359: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3.]

मित्रो अग्निर्भवति यत्समिद्भो मित्रो होता वरुणो जातवेदाः । मित्रो अध्वर्युरिषिरो दमूना मित्रः सिंधूनामुत पर्वतानां ॥

mitro agnirbhavati yatsamidbho mitro hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ | mitro adhvaryuriṣiro damūnā mitraḥ siṃdhūnāmuta parvatānāṃ ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 3-5-4) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

In this Ṛk, Agni well kindled is called Mitra; this Mitra is said to be the Hotṛ priest at the sacrifice, the Adhvaryu, Varuṇa, and the Agni called Jātavedas; and he is the friend (benefactor) of the rivers and of the mountains: thus Mitra's qualities are described.

Varuṇa: "Varuṇa is so called because he covers (vṛṇoti)" (Nirukta 10-2), says Yāska's derivation: this deity is called Varuṇa because he is covered (āvṛta) by masses of cloud. The words quoted are वरुणो वृणोतीति सतः (varuṇo vṛṇotīti sataḥ) [as supplied].

Varuṇa is a most exalted deity, equal to Indra in power and the like. The number of mantras addressed to Varuṇa alone is very small. There are twelve sūktas in the Ṛgveda with Varuṇa as deity; but the sūktas that praise Mitra and Varuṇa together number twenty-four. [Printed ಮಿತ್ರಾವರಣನ್ನು (mitrāvaraṇannu), sic for mitrāvaruṇa-.]

Varuṇa has a human body and human activities. But rather than his physical body and activities, the description of his moral activities and deeds is what is chiefly indicated. He has a face, eyes, arms, hands and feet; he drives a chariot, sits, eats, drinks: such descriptions of his bodily activities are there. That the Sun is the eye of Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa is stated plainly in the Ṛks

चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः ।

citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1)

उदु त्यच्चक्षुर्महि मित्रयोरा एति प्रियं वरुणयोरदब्धं ।

udu tyaccakṣurmahi mitrayorā eti priyaṃ varuṇayoradabdhaṃ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-51-1)

उद्वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान् ।

udvāṃ cakṣurvaruṇa supratīkaṃ devayoreti sūryastatanvān |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-61-1)

चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक् तमांसि ।

cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasya devaścarmeva yaḥ samavivyak tamāṃsi |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-63-1) [printed "ಋ ಸಂ." without the full stop]

नमो मित्रस्य वरुणस्य चक्षसे महो देवाय तदृतं सपर्यत ।

namo mitrasya varuṇasya cakṣase maho devāya tadṛtaṃ saparyata |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-37-1)

Since the point that the Sun is, as it were, their eye occurs in the very first Ṛk of the sūktas addressed to Mitra and Varuṇa, it seems that this is the aspect that first strikes one whenever Mitra and Varuṇa are mentioned. And in Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-66-10

p. 360

[Running head, p. 360: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

Aryaman, Mitra and Varuṇa are said to have the Sun as their eye. That Varuṇa is far-seeing (urucakṣasam) is said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-5; 1-25-16 and other Ṛks.

आ नो बर्हि रिशादसो वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । सीदंतु मनुषो यथा ॥

ā no barhi riśādaso varuṇo mitro aryamā | sīdaṃtu manuṣo yathā ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 1-26-4) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

व्रतेन स्थो ध्रुवक्षेमा धर्मणा यातॆयज्जना । नि बर्हिषि सदतं सोमपीतये ॥

vratena stho dhruvakṣemā dharmaṇā yātèyajjanā | ni barhiṣi sadataṃ somapītaye ‖

(Mi. Saṃ. 5-72-2) [as supplied: ಮಿ. (Mi.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.); the text has यातॆयज्जना (yātèyajjanā) here]

In these and other Ṛks Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman are prayed to come and sit on the darbha grass spread on the sacrificial altar, for drinking Soma. [Printed ವರಣ (varaṇa), sic for varuṇa.]

यदी सखाया सख्याय सोमैः सुतेभिः सुप्रयसा मादय्यैते ।

yadī sakhāyā sakhyāya somaiḥ sutebhiḥ suprayasā mādayyaite |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-41-3)

In these and other Ṛks it is said that Varuṇa drinks Soma along with Indra and other deities.

बिभ्रद्दापिं हिरण्ययं वरुणो वस्त निर्णिजं । परि स्पशो नि षेदिरे ।

bibhraddāpiṃ hiraṇyayaṃ varuṇo vasta nirṇijaṃ | pari spaśo ni ṣedire |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-25-13)

In this Ṛk there is a description that Varuṇa wears a golden mantle or robe and a shining garment. Varuṇa's chariot is golden, bright like the Sun, and has whips that urge on the horses. Mitra and Varuṇa mount their chariot in a very lofty region of the sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-1); such descriptions occur. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is golden and is in the upper world. And Varuṇa, sitting in his palace—

नि षसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्या ३ स्वा । साम्राज्याय सुकृतुः । अतो विश्वान्यद्भुता चिकित्त्वा अभि पश्यति । कृतानि या च कर्त्वा ॥

ni ṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastyā 3 svā | sāmrājyāya sukṛtuḥ | ato viśvānyadbhutā cikittvā abhi paśyati | kṛtāni yā ca kartvā ‖

(Pu. Saṃ. 1-25-10, 11) [as supplied: ಪು. (Pu.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.); the text has पस्त्या ३ स्वा (pastyā 3 svā) with a stray numeral ೩]

sees everything that goes on in the world. The dwelling of Mitra and Varuṇa is very large, very lofty, firm, resting on a thousand pillars; and their house has a thousand doors (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-88-5). The all-seeing Sun, setting out from his own dwelling, goes to the house of Mitra and Varuṇa to report men's deeds, and enters their dear house: such descriptions also occur.

p. 361

[Running head, p. 361: Ṛgvedasaṃhitā, A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3.]

Varuṇa, alone or together with Mitra, is called king in many places, like other deities.

अबुद्धे राजा वरुणो वनस्योर्ध्वं स्तूपं ददते पूतदक्षः ।

abuddhe rājā varuṇo vanasyordhvaṃ stūpaṃ dadate pūtadakṣaḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-7)

त्वं विश्वेषां वरुणासि राजा ये च देवा असुर ये च मर्ताः ।

tvaṃ viśveṣāṃ varuṇāsi rājā ye ca devā asura ye ca martāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-10)

तेन विश्वस्य भुवनस्य राजा यवं न वृष्टिव्युर्नत्ति भूम ।

tena viśvasya bhuvanasya rājā yavaṃ na vṛṣṭivyurnatti bhūma |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3)

In these and other Ṛks Varuṇa is said to be king not only of men but of the gods and of all the worlds. Besides Varuṇa, deities such as Indra, Yama and Soma also have the honorific name of king.

There are many stories connected with Indra; but with Varuṇa it is quite the opposite: there is not a single story. Varuṇa is much praised as the regulator of the physical and moral ordinances (varuṇasya vratāni). The divine power of Mitra and Varuṇa is described by the word māyā. Applied to the gods, it means the hidden power they have to do good; in the context of the rākṣasas, the same word means the crooked power they have to do evil. In the good sense this word suits Mitra and Varuṇa; in the bad sense it applies to the rākṣasas. Like the word asura, the word māyā is used in both senses.

By this māyā power hidden in himself, Varuṇa, standing in the atmosphere, measures the earth by means of the Sun as with a measuring rod. He makes the Sun cross the intermediate space and causes him to be dimmed by rain-clouds; then honey-mixed (sweet) drops fall (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-4). He makes the sky rain. Therefore this word māyā is said chiefly of Varuṇa among the gods in all the Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-14; 7-28-4; 10-99-10; 10-147-5. [In the supplied text a colon stands between ೧೦-೯೯-೧೦ and ೧೦-೧೪೭-೫; changed to a semicolon in kn.md for the reference check, numbers untouched.]

Varuṇa is the one who lays down the laws of nature. It is he who established earth and heaven. And

आसीदद्विश्वा भुवनानि संराड्विश्वेत्तानि वरुणस्य व्रतानि ।

āsīdadviśvā bhuvanāni saṃrāḍviśvettāni varuṇasya vratāni |

(Ma. Saṃ. 8-42-1) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

in this Ṛk it is said that Varuṇa dwells in all the worlds, and that his ordinances and the like are observed everywhere there,

p. 362

[Running head, p. 362: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

तिस्रो द्यावो निहिता अंतरस्मिन् तिस्रो भूमिरुपराः षड्विधानाः ।

tisro dyāvo nihitā aṃtarasmin tisro bhūmiruparāḥ ṣaḍvidhānāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-87-5)

in this it is said that the three upper worlds and the three earthly (lower) worlds are in his power. Varuṇa and Mitra rule the whole universe (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63-7). They are the protectors of the whole world (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-4). Varuṇa is the support of heaven, earth and sky (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-69-1, 4). He has placed fire in the water, the Sun in the sky, and Soma upon the stone. He has made a broad path for the Sun. Varuṇa, Mitra and Aryaman clear the way for the Sun (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-60-4). In many such Ṛks there is a description of Varuṇa's authority.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-8-4) it says मित्रोऽहरजनयद्वरुणो रात्रिं (mitro 'harajanayadvaruṇo rātriṃ), that is, Mitra created the day and Varuṇa the night. Therefore, मैत्रं वा अहः । वारुणी रात्रिः (maitraṃ vā ahaḥ | vāruṇī rātriḥ): it is said in many places that Mitra is lord of the day and Varuṇa lord of the night (Tai. Saṃ. 2-1-7-4). In one place it is said that Varuṇa divided the seasons.

वेद मासो धृवव्रतो द्वादश प्रजावतः । वेदा य उपजायते ।

veda māso dhṛvavrato dvādaśa prajāvataḥ | vedā ya upajāyate |

(Ma. Saṃ. 1-25-8) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

In this Ṛk it is said that the twelve months are known to Varuṇa, and

वि ये दधुः करदं मासमादहर्यज्ञ मक्तुं चादृचं । अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा क्षत्रं राजान आशत ॥

vi ye dadhuḥ karadaṃ māsamādaharyajña maktuṃ cādṛcaṃ | anāpyaṃ varuṇo mitro aryamā kṣatraṃ rājāna āśata ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 7-66-11) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

in this Ṛk it is said that Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman divided the autumn, the month, the day and the night.

It is said in many places that he is also the one who regulates the waters. He is the one who made the rivers flow; at his command they flow on continuously (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-28-4). That the rivers, though they rush and pour water into the sea, do not fill it is due to his hidden power (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-6). Varuṇa and Mitra are lords of the rivers. That Varuṇa is lord of the oceans is an established point, yet it occurs in the Ṛgveda very rarely; perhaps its being unimportant may be the reason. In the Purāṇas and the like Varuṇa is famous as lord of the waters; and that Varuṇa, as one of the eight guardians of the quarters, is lord of the western quarter is a statement made in the Purāṇas and the like. In the Ṛgveda there is no support for it. In general, all that concerns Varuṇa relates to the water that is together with the atmosphere. Among the deities prayed to for rain

p. 363

[Running head, p. 363: A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā.]

Varuṇa and Mitra are the foremost. When all the mountains are covered with clouds, Varuṇa pours water, from an overturned vessel (a cloud), on heaven, earth and sky and wets the whole earth; this is said in Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-85-3 and 4. One whole sūkta (that is, Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-63) also indicates their rain-pouring power. In the Yajurveda Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 5-5-4-1) आपो वरुणस्य पत्नय आसन् (āpo varuṇasya patnaya āsan): the waters were the wives of Varuṇa; and (Tai. Saṃ. 6-4-3-2) मित्रावरुणौ ना अपां नेतार् (mitrāvaruṇau nā apāṃ netār): Mitra and Varuṇa are the leaders of the waters. [The printed ನಾ (nā) is kept as supplied.]

It is repeatedly said that the ordinances of Varuṇa are firmly established. For this very reason he is called Dhṛtavrata ("of firm ordinances"). This epithet is applied to both Mitra and Varuṇa.

परि धामानि मर्मृशद्वरुणस्य पुरो गये विश्वे देवा अनु व्रतं नभंतामन्यके समे ॥

pari dhāmāni marmṛśadvaruṇasya puro gaye viśve devā anu vrataṃ nabhaṃtāmanyake same ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 8-41-7) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

न वां देवा अमृता आ मिनंति व्रतानि मित्रावरुणा ध्रुवाणि ।

na vāṃ devā amṛtā ā minaṃti vratāni mitrāvaruṇā dhruvāṇi |

(Ma. Saṃ. 5-69-4) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

In these and other Ṛks it is said that the gods themselves obey the commands of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, and that even the primeval gods cannot transgress their firm ordinances. Mitra and Varuṇa are the regulators of law (ṛta) and of light. It is by the strength of these ordinances that they are able to support the laws. This quality is found especially in these two, sometimes in the Ādityas, or in other ordinary deities as well. The epithet "promoters of truth (ṛta) and justice" (ṛtasya gopāḥ), that is, those who keep the laws (or make others keep them), is seen to be applied often to Mitra and Varuṇa.

Varuṇa's power is immeasurable. Neither flying birds nor flowing rivers can reach the boundary of his realm; they cannot withstand his power; they cannot check his wrath. The sky and the rivers too have not reached the limit of the territory of Mitra and Varuṇa. Everything is contained in Varuṇa. The dwellings of all creatures, the three heavens and the three earths are all placed in him. Varuṇa is omniscient. The flight of birds in the sky, the passage of ships on the sea, the course of the far-travelling wind, all these are known to him. He sees all things that are past or yet to come. He is the witness of men's true and false deeds. The deeds, thoughts and devices of every man are all known to Varuṇa. Heaven

p. 364

[Running head, p. 364: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

and the earthly worlds, and all that lies beyond them, he can comprehend. However far beyond the sky one may run, no one can leave the range of Varuṇa's sight.

Being the regulator of morality, Varuṇa grows very angry at sin. Sin makes him very angry, and so does transgression of his ordinances; for both these he imposes a very severe punishment. Varuṇa's noose, which binds sinners, is mentioned in Ṛks such as Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-24-15; 1-25-11; 6-74-4; 10-85-24. [In the supplied text a colon stands between 1-25-11 and 6-74-4; changed to a semicolon in kn.md for the reference check, numbers untouched.] That noose binds the speaker of untruth and releases the speaker of truth.

युवो राष्ट्रं बृहदिन्वति द्यौर्यौ सेतृभिररज्जुभिः सिनीथः । परि नो हेळो वरुणस्य वृज्या उरुं न इंद्रः कृणवदु लोकं ॥

yuvo rāṣṭraṃ bṛhadinvati dyauryau setṛbhirarajjubhiḥ sinīthaḥ | pari no heḷo varuṇasya vṛjyā uruṃ na iṃdraḥ kṛṇavadu lokaṃ ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 7-84-2) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

In this Ṛk it is said that Varuṇa, accompanied by Indra, binds with bonds that are not ropes. This word "noose" (pāśa) occurs in the whole Ṛgveda in only one place, in a mantra addressed to Agni, and that too in the context of praying to loosen the noose that binds his devotees. Therefore it may be said that these acts of noose-binding and release (loosening the noose) belong to Varuṇa alone. Varuṇa, together with Mitra, is the driver away, the hater and the punisher of untruth. Mitra and Varuṇa punish those who are negligent in their worship. But Varuṇa forgives those who repent; he unties them like a rope; and he effects the removal of sin. He releases a man not only from the sin committed by himself but also from the sin committed by his forefathers. Even those who daily transgress the very rules laid down by him and afterwards repent he saves. And he shows compassion to those who have transgressed his commands through forgetfulness. In Varuṇa there are hundreds and thousands of medicines. He drives death away and removes sin. He can take away life, and can also grant life. He is very skilful in protecting immortality (nityatva). Thus the description of Varuṇa's qualities is found in many Ṛks. Here we have described it very briefly; at a suitable occasion we shall describe it at length.

In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā—फल्गुनीनक्षत्रमर्यमा देवता .... .... .... .... अनूराधा नक्षत्रं मित्रो देवता (phalgunīnakṣatramaryamā devatā .... .... .... .... anūrādhā nakṣatraṃ mitro devatā) (Tai. Saṃ. 4--4-9-2 [as printed: two hyphens]), that is, it is said that Aryaman is lord of the (earlier) Phalgunī constellation and Mitra of the Anurādhā constellation.

Aryaman—In the sūktas addressed to the Ādityas, in general the Ādityas meant are Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman. As we have said before, in the Ṛgveda (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-27-1) Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga,

p. 365

[Running head, p. 365: A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā.]

Varuṇa, Dakṣa, Aṃśa: only the names of these six persons are there. In Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-114-3 the number of the Ādityas is given as seven, and in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-8 it is said that Aditi first presented seven sons to the gods and afterwards obtained the eighth, Mārtaṇḍa. In Atharvaveda 8-9-21 and in Tai. Brā. 1-1-9-1 also it is said that Aditi had eight sons: Mitra, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Dhātṛ, Indra and Vivasvān. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 6-1-2-8; 11-6-3-8) the Ādityas are said to be twelve, one for each month. In the Purāṇas and the like too the Ādityas are twelve in number.

Although the name of the deity Aryaman occurs in the Ṛgveda in about a hundred places, since he has no complete personality Yāska, in his Nirukta (Nighaṇṭu), when explaining the derivation of the names of the deities, has left out the name of this deity Aryaman. Except in two mantras, everywhere else he is mentioned only together with other deities, and that mostly together with Mitra and Varuṇa. Addressing Agni, in the context of wooing maidens, it is said:

त्वमर्यमा भवसि यत्कनीनां नाम स्वधावन् गुह्यं बिभर्षि ।

tvamaryamā bhavasi yatkanīnāṃ nāma svadhāvan guhyaṃ bibharṣi |

(Ma. Saṃ. 5-3-2) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

that is, "you are Aryaman."

भगो अर्यमा सविता पुरंधिर्मह्यं त्वादुर्गार्हपत्याय देवाः ।

bhago aryamā savitā puraṃdhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-85-36)

In this Ṛk the bridegroom says: "O gods, Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ and Purandhi gave this bride to me, to help me in the householder's stage of life."

न तमंहो न दुरितं देवासो अष्ट मर्त्यं । सजोषसो यमर्यमा मित्रो नयंति वरुणो अति द्विषः ॥

na tamaṃho na duritaṃ devāso aṣṭa martyaṃ | sajoṣaso yamaryamā mitro nayaṃti varuṇo ati dviṣaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126-1)

शुनमस्मभ्यमूतये वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा । शर्म यच्छंतु सप्रथ आदित्यासो यदीमहे अति द्विषः ॥

śunamasmabhyamūtaye varuṇo mitro aryamā | śarma yacchaṃtu sapratha ādityāso yadīmahe ati dviṣaḥ ‖

(Ma. Saṃ. 10-126-7) [as supplied: ಮ. (Ma.) for ಋ. (Ṛ.)]

Although the deities of Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-126 are called Viśvedevas, it is chiefly the Ādityas who are praised here in the Ṛks cited above. Moreover, the words देवासः अष्ट (devāsaḥ aṣṭa) in the first Ṛk refer to the eight Ādityas (nowhere in the Veda is the number of the Ādityas said to be more than eight). Again, the word आदित्यासः (ādityāsaḥ) in the 7th Ṛk shows the same clearly. In every Ṛk of this sūkta (except the last Ṛk) the refrain वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा (varuṇo mitro aryamā)

p. 366

[Running head, p. 366: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

("Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman"), the names of Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, is repeated again and again like a refrain, which indicates that among the Ādityas these three, Mitra, Varuṇa and Aryaman, hold the chief place. Since the subject of Aryaman is not much described in the Ṛgveda, a detailed account is not possible.

Rudra—The explanation of the word Rudra by the Nirukta-writer is as follows:

रुद्रो रौतीति सतः रोरूयमाणो द्रवतीति ना रोदयतेर्वा । यदरुदत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं इति काठकं । यदरोदीत्तद्रुद्रस्य रुद्रत्वं इति हारिद्रविकं ॥

rudro rautīti sataḥ rorūyamāṇo dravatīti nā rodayatervā | yadarudattadrudrasya rudratvaṃ iti kāṭhakaṃ | yadarodīttadrudrasya rudratvaṃ iti hāridravikaṃ ‖

(Ni. 10-5)

रुद्रनॆंदरॆ रौति-स्तनयित्नुशब्दं करोति (rudranèṃdarè rauti-stanayitnuśabdaṃ karoti): Rudra is one who makes a sound like the thunder of a cloud; or रोरूयमाणो द्रवति (rorūyamāṇo dravati): one who moves swiftly while roaring; or रोदयतेः (rodayateḥ): one who makes enemies weep; and so on. In the Ṛgveda Rudra is not an influential deity, but in the Yajurveda, the Purāṇas and the like Rudra is regarded as a very important deity.

[Kannada text note: the supplied text prints the two lines of the Nirukta quotation with a hyphenated line break (ಯದರು- / ದತ್ತ…); joined in kn.md as one block. The prose Sanskrit quotations of this page and the previous one were made > blocks with the reference on its own line.]

Ṛk 10

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

भगं॒ धियं॑ वा॒जयं॑तः॒ पुरं॑धिं॒ नरा॒शंसो॒ ग्नास्पति॑र्नो अव्याः । आ॒ये वा॒मस्य॑ संग॒थे र॑यी॒णां प्रि॒या दे॒वस्य॑ सवि॒तुः स्या॑म ॥ १० ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

भगं । धियं । वाजयंतः । पुरंधिं । नराशंसः । ग्नापतिः । नः । अव्याः । आअये । वामस्य । संगथे । रयाणां । प्रियाः । देवस्य । सविशुः । स्याम ॥ ११॥

bhagaṃ | dhiyaṃ | vājayaṃtaḥ | puraṃdhiṃ | narāśaṃsaḥ | gnāpatiḥ | naḥ | avyāḥ | āaye | vāmasya | saṃgathe | rayāṇāṃ | priyāḥ | devasya | saviśuḥ | syāma ‖ 11‖

[Note: the supplied text prints the number 11 after the Pada, against 10 after the Saṃhitā, and reads ग्नापतिः (gnāpatiḥ) in the Pada against ग्नास्पतिः (gnāspatiḥ) in the Saṃhitā, रयाणां (rayāṇāṃ) against रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ) and सविशुः (saviśuḥ) against सवितुः (savituḥ); all kept as supplied, to be settled by the user.]

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

भगं भजनीयं धियं ध्यातव्यं पुरंधिं पुरस्य धारयितारं बहुप्रज्ञं वा सवितारं ॥ पुरंधिर्बहुधिरिति यास्कः ॥ वाजयंतो वाजिनं बलिनं कुर्वतः ॥ विभक्ति व्यत्ययः ॥ नः स्तुवतोऽस्मान् नराशंसो नरैः शंसनीयो ग्नास्पतिर्देवपत्नीनां पतिश्चंदसां पतिर्वा ॥ तथा च श्रूयते छंदांसि वै ग्ना इति उत ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्नीः । ऋग्वे. ५-४६-८ । इति च ॥ सविताव्याः । अव्यात् । किंच वामस्य धनस्य

bhagaṃ bhajanīyaṃ dhiyaṃ dhyātavyaṃ puraṃdhiṃ purasya dhārayitāraṃ bahuprajñaṃ vā savitāraṃ ‖ puraṃdhirbahudhiriti yāskaḥ ‖ vājayaṃto vājinaṃ balinaṃ kurvataḥ ‖ vibhakti vyatyayaḥ ‖ naḥ stuvato 'smān narāśaṃso naraiḥ śaṃsanīyo gnāspatirdevapatnīnāṃ patiścaṃdasāṃ patirvā ‖ tathā ca śrūyate chaṃdāṃsi vai gnā iti uta gnā vyaṃtu devapatnīḥ | ṛgve. 5-46-8 | iti ca ‖ savitāvyāḥ | avyāt | kiṃca vāmasya dhanasya

p. 367

[Running head, p. 367: A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā.]

रयीणां पशूनां च ॥ तथा च श्रूयते पशवो वै रयिरिति ॥ आय आगमने संगथे संगमने च निमित्ते देवस्य द्योतमानस्य सवितुः प्रेरकस्य वयं प्रियाः स्याम । भवेम ॥

Gist: Savitṛ, worthy of worship and of meditation, very wise, praised by men and guardian of the gods' wives, is to protect us; may we be dear to him for gaining wealth and cattle.

[Note: a label सायणभाष्यं (sāyaṇabhāṣyaṃ) was inserted in kn.md before the bhāṣya, the bhāṣya block was split from the Pada block, and a hyphenated line break (ದೇವ- / ಪತ್ನೀಃ) was joined; the bhāṣya, split by the page break, is placed as two blocks.]

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

भगं (bhagaṃ)—the worshipful; धियं (dhiyaṃ)—worthy of meditation; पुरंधिं (puraṃdhiṃ)—and all-wise Savitṛ; वाजयंतः (vājayaṃtaḥ)—worshipping (him); नः (naḥ)—us; नराशंसः (narāśaṃsaḥ)—the one praised by men; ग्नास्पतिः (gnāspatiḥ)—the protector of the gods' wives, Savitṛ; अव्याः (avyāḥ)—may he protect. वामस्य (vāmasya)—of wealth (and); रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ)—of cattle; आये (āye)—for the gain; संगथे (saṃgathe)—for the accumulation; देवस्य (devasya)—of the divine; सवितुः (savituḥ)—to Savitṛ; प्रियाः (priyāḥ)—(we) as beloved ones; स्याम (syāma)—may we be.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Savitṛ, who is praised by men and is the protector of the gods' wives, protect us who worship the worshipful, meditation-worthy, all-knowing Savitṛ. May we be beloved of the divine Savitṛ, for the gain and the accumulation of wealth and cattle.

Printed English translation

May he, who is adored by men, the protector of the wives (of the gods), preserve us; when worshipping him, who is auspicious, the object of meditation, and the all-wise : may we be the beloved of the divinc [sic] Savitri, that we may (thence be successful) in accumulation of wealth and the acquisition of cattle.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पुरंधिं— पुरस्य धारयितारं बहुप्रज्ञं वा (puraṃdhiṃ— purasya dhārayitāraṃ bahuprajñaṃ vā) ।—One who holds and nourishes our cities (puras). Or, since the word धी (dhī) also means wisdom, Purandhi is also understood as one possessed of much wisdom. Yāska has given the explanation of the word Purandhi as पुरंधिर्बहुधीः (puraṃdhirbahudhīḥ) (Ni. 6-13). The meaning is one of abundant intelligence, a discerning person.

नराशंसः—नरैः शंसनीयः (narāśaṃsaḥ—naraiḥ śaṃsanīyaḥ) ।—One praised by men. There is also a separate deity Narāśaṃsa. This deity is said to be a transformation of Agni. A detailed account of this deity we have given in the Āprī-sūktas (see Ṛ. Saṃ. part 8, page 546).

p. 368

[Running head, p. 368: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

ग्नास्पतिः (gnāspatiḥ)—The word ग्नाः (gnāḥ) is read among the names of speech (Ni. 2-23) and among the names of women (Ni. 3-21). Yāska's explanation is also अपि च ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्न्यः (api ca gnā vyaṃtu devapatnyaḥ) (Ni. 24-46) [as printed]. The commentator also cites the Vedic sentence छंदांसि वै ग्नाः (chaṃdāṃsi vai gnāḥ), that is, the metres too are called ग्ना (gnā). Therefore ग्नास्पतिः (gnāspatiḥ) may be taken as "the lord of the metres" or as "the husband of the gods' wives, that is, of the divine women". Yāska, citing the Ṛk

उत ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्नीरिंद्राण्य १ ग्नाय्यश्विनी राट् । आ रोदसी वरुणानी शृणोतु व्यंतु देवीर्य ऋतुर्जनीनां ॥

uta gnā vyaṃtu devapatnīriṃdrāṇya 1 gnāyyaśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyaṃtu devīrya ṛturjanīnāṃ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-46-8)

has stated the names of the gods' wives in his explanation:

अपि च ग्ना व्यंतु देवपत्न्यः । इंद्राणींद्रस्य पत्न्यग्नाय्यग्नेः पत्न्यश्विन्यश्विनोः पत्नि राट् राजते । रोदसी रुद्रस्य पत्नि । वरुणानी च वरुणस्य पत्नि ॥

api ca gnā vyaṃtu devapatnyaḥ | iṃdrāṇīṃdrasya patnyagnāyyagneḥ patnyaśvinyaśvinoḥ patni rāṭ rājate | rodasī rudrasya patni | varuṇānī ca varuṇasya patni ‖

(Si. 12-46) [as printed]

That is: Indra's wife is called Indrāṇī, Agni's wife Agnāyī, the wife of the Aśvin gods Aśvinī, Rudra's wife Rodasī, and Varuṇa's wife Varuṇānī.

[Note: in kn.md the two Sanskrit quotations above, printed as prose in the supplied text, were made > blocks with their references on their own lines; a line break with hyphen inside the second (पत्न्यश्विन्य- / श्विनोः (patnyaśvinya- / śvinoḥ)) was joined; the readings इंद्राण्य १ ग्नाय्यश्विनी (iṃdrāṇya 1 gnāyyaśvinī) in the first and the reference letter सि. (si.) (for the Nirukta) are kept as supplied.]

The main purport: this god Savitṛ is worshipful and worthy of meditation, praised by men, the guardian of the gods' wives or the lord of the metres. May Savitṛ protect us who worship such a god. The meaning stated is that we, by worshipping this Savitṛ for the gain of wealth and the obtaining of cattle, may become the objects of his love.

Ṛk 11

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ तद्दि॒वो अ॒द्भ्यः पृ॑थि॒व्यास्त्वया॑ द॒त्तं काम्यं॒ राध॒ आ गा॑त् । शं यत्सो॒तृभ्य॑ आ॒पये॒ भवा॑त्युरु॒शंसा॑य सवितर्जरि॒त्रॆ ॥ ११ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

अस्मभ्यं । तत् । दिवः । आर्‍भ्यः । पृथिव्याः । त्वया । दत्तं । काम्यं । राधः । आ । गात् । शं । यत् । स्तोतृभ्यः । अपये । भवाति । उरुशंसाय । सवितः । जरित्रे ॥ ११ ॥

asmabhyaṃ | tat | divaḥ | ārbhyaḥ | pṛthivyāḥ | tvayā | dattaṃ | kāmyaṃ | rādhaḥ | ā | gāt | śaṃ | yat | stotṛbhyaḥ | apaye | bhavāti | uruśaṃsāya | savitaḥ | jaritre ‖ 11 ‖

[Note: the Pada as supplied reads आर्‍भ्यः (ārbhyaḥ) after दिवः (divaḥ), where the Saṃhitā and the Pratipadārtha have अद्भ्यः (adbhyaḥ) and अदृश्यः (adṛśyaḥ); kept as supplied, for the user to settle. The Pada's आ । गात् (ā | gāt) is split over two lines in the supplied text.]

p. 369

[Running head, p. 369: A. 2, A. 8, Va. 3, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā (the first abbreviation printed अ. (a.) for Aṣṭaka, as supplied).]

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे सवितः अस्मभ्यं त्वया दत्तं तत् प्रसिद्धं काम्यं कमनीयं राधो धनं दिवो द्युलोकात् अद्भो०तरिक्षलोकात् पृथिव्या भूमेश्चा गात् । आगच्छतु । किंच स्तोतृभ्यः स्तोतृणामापये बंधवे तद्वंशजाय यद्धनं शं सुखकरं भवाति भवेत् उरुशंसाय बहुस्तुतये जरित्रे स्तोत्रे मह्यं ॥ जरिता कारुरिति स्तोतृनामसु पाठात् ॥ हे सवितः तत्पयच्छ ॥

Gist: Savitṛ, may the coveted wealth you give come to us from heaven, atmosphere and earth; may the wealth that brings happiness to the praisers' kin be mine, the praiser.

[Note: the bhāṣya as supplied reads अद्भो०तरिक्षलोकात् (adbho0tarikṣalokāt); kept as supplied.]

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सवितः (savitaḥ)—O Savitṛ; अस्मभ्यं (asmabhyaṃ)—to us; त्वया (tvayā)—by you; दत्तं (dattaṃ)—that which is given; तत् (tat)—the well-known; काम्यं (kāmyaṃ)—the attractive; राधः (rādhaḥ)—wealth; दिवः (divaḥ)—from the heavenly world; अदृश्यः (adṛśyaḥ) [as supplied; evidently meant for अद्भ्यः (adbhyaḥ)]—from the atmosphere; पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)—from the earth; आ गात् (ā gāt)—may it come and join; स्तोतृभ्यः (stotṛbhyaḥ)—of those who praise you; आपये (āpaye)—to the kinsfolk; यत् (yat)—which wealth; शं (śaṃ)—as happiness-bringing; भवाति (bhavāti)—becomes; (तत् (tat)—that); उरुशंसाय (uruśaṃsāya)—to me who praises you greatly; जरित्रे (jaritre)—a devotee, the praiser (may it be obtained).

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Savitṛ, may the wealth given by you, well known and attractive, come and join me from the heavenly world, from the atmosphere and from the earth. The very wealth that becomes a source of happiness to the kinsfolk of those who praise you, may it be obtained also by me, who worship you and am your praiser.

Printed English translation

May that desirable wealth which is granted to us, Savitri, by you proceed from the sky, from the waters, from the earth; and may the happiness (which belongs) to the race of those who eulogise you, devolve upon me, repeating diligently you [sic] praises.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अद्भ्यः—अंतरिक्षलोकात् (adbhyaḥ—aṃtarikṣalokāt)—Since the word अप् (ap) is read among the names of the atmosphere (Ni. 2-10), अद्भ्यः (adbhyaḥ) means "from the atmospheric world".

राधः (rādhaḥ)—Since the word राधः (rādhaḥ) is read among the names of wealth (Ni 3-9) [as printed, without the full stop], राधः (rādhaḥ) means wealth.

[Printed at the foot of p. 369: the stray figure "24" (a signature number), kept as an italic note.]

p. 370

[Running head, p. 370: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 38.]

आपॆये—बंधवे तद्वंशजाय (āpèye—baṃdhave tadvaṃśajāya)—[The Kannada text spells the headword आपॆये (āpèye), as supplied.] To the kinsfolk, and also to those born in their line.

उरुशंसाय—बहुस्तुतये (uruśaṃsāya—bahustutaye)—The word उरु (uru) is read among the names of "much" (Ni. 3-13). The meaning is: to one who praises you in many ways.

जरित्रे—स्तोत्रे मह्यं (jaritre—stotre mahyaṃ)—To me who am praising; the word जरिता (jaritā) is read among the names of praisers (Ni. 3-19).

The main purport: O god Savitṛ, whatever wealth you give to other praisers, obtainable from earth, atmosphere and heaven, give such wealth to me, who praise you in many ways, and to my kinsfolk. May happiness come to me through that attractive wealth that you give.

The thirty-ninth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

ग्रावेणेवेत्यष्टर्चं सप्तमं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभमाश्विनं ग्रावाणेनाष्टावाश्विनमित्यनुक्रांतत्वात् ॥ प्रवर्ग्येऽभिष्टवे पूर्वे पटलेऽस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । ग्रावाणेवेळे द्यावापृथिवी । आ. ४-६ । इति ॥ प्रातरनुवाकाश्विनशस्त्रयोरपीदं सूक्तं । सूत्रितं च । ग्रावाणेव नासत्याभ्यामिति त्रीणि । आ. ४-१५ । इति ॥

grāveṇevetyaṣṭarcaṃ saptamaṃ sūktaṃ gārtsamadaṃ traiṣṭubhamāśvinaṃ grāvāṇenāṣṭāvāśvinamityanukrāṃtatvāt ‖ pravargye 'bhiṣṭave pūrve paṭale 'sya viniyogaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | grāvāṇeveḷe dyāvāpṛthivī | ā. 4-6 | iti ‖ prātaranuvākāśvinaśastrayorapīdaṃ sūktaṃ | sūtritaṃ ca | grāvāṇeva nāsatyābhyāmiti trīṇi | ā. 4-15 | iti ‖

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta beginning Grāṇeva [as supplied; the Sanskrit above has ग्रावेणेव (grāveṇeva)] is the seventh sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has eight ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta; the Aśvin gods are the deity; the metre is triṣṭubh. The Anukramaṇikā says: ग्राणेवाष्टावाश्विनं (grāṇevāṣṭāvāśvinaṃ) ("Grāṇeva, eight, addressed to the Aśvins" [the supplied text has ग्राणे (grāṇe) here]). Its application is in the Pravargya sacrifice, in the Abhiṣṭava in the earlier paṭala, as explained by the sūtra ग्राणेवेळे द्यावापृथिवी (grāṇeveḷe dyāvāpṛthivī) (Ā. 4-6) of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra [as supplied]; and its application in the Prātaranuvāka and in the recitation of the Āśvina śastra is explained by the sūtra ग्राणेव नासत्याभ्यामिति त्रीणि (grāṇeva nāsatyābhyāmiti trīṇi) (Ā. 4-15).

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विन् ग्रावाणेव अरातिं प्रति प्रेषितौ पाषाणाविव तदर्थ० ॥ अर्तॆर्धातोरर्थशब्दः । अर्थोऽर्तेरिति यास्कः । नि. १-१८ ॥ तमरातिमित्यर्थः । इदिति पूरणः । जरेथे । जरयेथे । अरातिं बाधेथां । यद्वा यथा गुरू ग्रावाणौ क्षिप्तौ तदानीमेव शीघ्रं गच्छतस्तथा तत् तमर्थ० गंतारं जरेथे । शीघ्रं गत्वा स्तुतमित्यर्थः ॥ जरतिः स्तुतिकर्मा ॥ किंच गृध्रेव गृध्राविव पक्षिणाविव वृक्षं फलितं वृक्षं निधिमंतं धनवंतं यजमानमच्छ । आगच्छतमिति शेषः । विदथे यज्ञे ॥ विदथः सवनमिति यज्ञनामसु पाठात् ॥ उक्तशासोकश्चशंसितार् ब्रह्माणेव ब्राह्मणाविव । जन्या जनपदेषु दूतेव राज्ञा प्रेषितौ दूताविव पुरुत्रा बहुभिः पुरुषैर्हव्या ह्वातव्यौ युवां । अत्रोपमेयद्वित्वानुसारेणोपमानद्वित्वं ॥

he aśvin grāvāṇeva arātiṃ prati preṣitau pāṣāṇāviva tadartha0 ‖ artèrdhātorarthaśabdaḥ | artho 'rteriti yāskaḥ | ni. 1-18 ‖ tamarātimityarthaḥ | iditi pūraṇaḥ | jarethe | jarayethe | arātiṃ bādhethāṃ | yadvā yathā gurū grāvāṇau kṣiptau tadānīmeva śīghraṃ gacchatastathā tat tamartha0 gaṃtāraṃ jarethe | śīghraṃ gatvā stutamityarthaḥ ‖ jaratiḥ stutikarmā ‖ kiṃca gṛdhreva gṛdhrāviva pakṣiṇāviva vṛkṣaṃ phalitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ nidhimaṃtaṃ dhanavaṃtaṃ yajamānamaccha | āgacchatamiti śeṣaḥ | vidathe yajñe ‖ vidathaḥ savanamiti yajñanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ uktaśāsokaścaśaṃsitār brahmāṇeva brāhmaṇāviva | janyā janapadeṣu dūteva rājñā preṣitau dūtāviva purutrā bahubhiḥ puruṣairhavyā hvātavyau yuvāṃ | atropameyadvitvānusāreṇopamānadvitvaṃ ‖

Gist: Like two stones hurled at the foe, the Aśvins crush the foe; like two vultures to a fruit-laden tree they come to the wealthy sacrificer; like two priests and two royal messengers they are invoked by many.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods). Grāvāṇeva—like stones thrown at an enemy. Tat artham—that enemy. Jarethe—destroy (him). Vṛkṣam—to the tree; Gṛdhreva—like a vulture going towards it. Vidathe—in the sacrificial house. Uktaśāsā—reciting the ukta. Brahmāṇeva—like Brāhmaṇas. Janyā—in the land. Dūteva—like royal messengers. Purutrā—by many sacrificers. Havyā—you who are to be invoked. Nidhimantam—to the wealthy sacrificer. Accha—come to him.

[Running head, p. 372: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 3 [sic, as supplied; elsewhere Maṃ. 2], A. 4, Sū. 39.]

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

[Note: the label was garbled in the supplied text (೧ ಭಾನಾರ್ಥ ೧) and was replaced by the standard label.]

O Aśvin gods, like stones thrown at the enemy, descend swiftly and destroy the foes. Like a vulture going towards a tree, like Brāhmaṇas reciting the ukta in the sacrificial house, like royal messengers in the land, you who are invoked by many sacrificers, come towards the wealthy sacrificer.

English Translation (as printed)

Descend, Ashwins, like falling stones, for the purpose (of destroying our foes); hasten to the presence of the wealth-possessing (worshippers), like, vultures to a tree: like two Brahmanas repeating hymns, (be present) at the sacrifice, and come like (royal) messengers in the land, welcomed by many people.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this sūkta the Aśvin gods are praised. In seven of its eight ṛks, all except the last, various similes (illustrations) are used in praying to the Aśvins; the use of many similes is the special feature of this sūkta. In many instances the simile does not fit exactly or is not apt to the occasion.

ग्रावाणेव तत् अर्थं इत् जरेथे—ग्रावाणेव अरातिं प्रति प्रेषितौ साषा-णाविव तमरातिं बाधेथां । (grāvāṇeva tat arthaṃ it jarethe—grāvāṇeva arātiṃ prati preṣitau sāṣā-ṇāviva tamarātiṃ bādhethāṃ |) [Line break inside the quotation, as supplied; the hyphen joins साषाणाविव (sāṣāṇāviva), while the bhāṣya above reads पाषाणाविव (pāṣāṇāviva).] Here the commentator explains the word अर्थं (arthaṃ) as arāti, an enemy. For the word artha, formed from the root ऋ गतौ (ṛ gatau), the meaning is "the enemy who rushes forward (in battle)". Yāska states the etymology अर्थोSर्तॆः (arthoSrtèḥ) [as supplied, with a Latin S]; that is, according to the Kannada, the word artha is formed from the root आर्ति (ārti) (ārti), which indicates going; this is the sense of the etymology. O Aśvin gods, as stones thrown at enemies cause them pain, so you afflict them: such is the intention.

वृक्षं गृध्रेव निधिमंतं अच्छ—पक्षिणाविव फलितं वृक्षं । (vṛkṣaṃ gṛdhreva nidhimaṃtaṃ accha—pakṣiṇāviva phalitaṃ vṛkṣaṃ |) As birds quickly approach trees laden with fruit, so come towards our wealthy sacrificer.

विदथे उक्तशासा ब्रह्माणेव-यज्ञे उक्तशंसितारौ ब्राह्मणाविव । (vidathe uktaśāsā brahmāṇeva-yajñe uktaśaṃsitārau brāhmaṇāviva |) The word vidatha is read among the names of sacrifice (Ni. 3-19). As Brāhmaṇas who recite the ukta and other mantras come to a sacrifice, so come to our sacrificial ground.

p. 373

[Running head, p. 373: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 4; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 373 (printed ಮುಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ, as supplied). The supplied text had merged this page into the previous one; the page marker and this heading were inserted by hand and p. 373 appended to pages.json.]

जन्या दूतेव—जनपदेषु राज्ञा प्रेषितौ दूताविव । (janyā dūteva—janapadeṣu rājñā preṣitau dūtāviva |) As a king sends his messengers into his realm and the messengers receive honour from the people, so you come to our sacrificial ground and be honoured with worship and the like: such is the intention.

पुरुत्रा हव्या—बहुभिः पुरुषैः ह्वातव्यौ । (purutrā havyā—bahubhiḥ puruṣaiḥ hvātavyau |) Those who are called by many men performing sacrifices to come to the sacrificial ground. It is desired that you, endowed with such greatness, come to our sacrificial ground also.

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

प्रा॒त्॒रर्यावा॑णा र॒थ्ये॑व वी॒राजेव॑ य॒मा वर॒मा स॑चेथे । मेने॑इव त॒न्वा॒३॒॑शुंभ॑माने॒ दंप॑तीव क्रतु॒विदा॒ जने॑षु ॥ २ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

प्रातःयावाना । रथ्याइव । वीरा । अजाइव । यमा । वरं । आ । सचेथेइति । मेने इवेति मेनेइव । तन्वा । शुंभमाने इति । दंपती इवेति दंपतीइव । क्रतुविदा । जनेषु ॥ २ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विन् प्रातर्यावाणा प्रातरेव यज्ञार्थं गंतारौ रथ्येव रथिनाविव वीर् स्वकर्मणि शूरौ । अजेवाजाविव भागाविव यमा यमलौ । मेने इव नार्याविव तन्ना शरीरेण शुंभमाने शोभमान् । दंपतीव जायापती इव संगतौ जनेषु विषयेषु क्रतुविदा कर्मविदौ युवां वरं संभक्तारमासचेथे । आगच्छत ॥

[Note: a hyphenated line break in the bhāṣya was joined in kn.md.]

Gist: The Aśvins go at dawn to the sacrifice, like two charioteer heroes, like a pair of twins, shining in body like two beautiful women, like husband and wife, skilled in rites among men; they come to the worshipper.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods). Rathyeva vīrā—like two heroes seated in a chariot. Prātaryāvāṇā—going to the sacrifice at dawn itself. Ajīva [sic, as supplied; the Saṃhitā has अजाइव (ajāiva)]—like a pair of goats. Yamā—twins. Tanvā—by charming bodies. Śumbhamāne—shining.

p. 374

[Running head, p. 374: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 39.]

Mene iva—like two beautiful women. Dampatīva—like a husband and wife joined together. Janeṣu—among the people who perform sacrifice. Kratuvidā—you who know the nature of the rite being performed. Varam—to the sacrificer who worships in the best manner. Ā sacethe—come, both of you, together.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, going at dawn itself to the sacrifice like two heroes seated in a chariot, twins like a pair of goats, like two beautiful women shining with charming bodies, like husband and wife, knowing the nature of the rites performed among the people who sacrifice, come, both of you together, to the sacrificer who worships in the best manner.

English Translation (as printed)

Moving at dawn like two heroes in a car ; like a pair of goats; like two women lovely in form ; or like husband and wife ; come together, knowing (how sacred) rites (are to be celebrated) amongst men, (to bestow) happiness (on the worshipper)

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this ṛk the Aśvins are described by several similes. प्रातर्यावाणा—प्रातरेव यज्ञार्थं गंतारौ । (prātaryāvāṇā—prātareva yajñārthaṃ gaṃtārau |) Those who go towards the sacrifice at dawn itself. Ordinarily the Aśvins, Uṣas and Savitṛ are invoked at dawn; so these are gods who go to the sacrifice at dawn. The Aśvins appear like two heroes seated in a chariot; like two goats of one form, that is, of like shape — the form of the two Aśvins is exactly the same, no difference is seen between them, so they are described as of like form, like twins; they are also like two beautiful women shining with charming bodies, and shine like a husband and wife endowed with beauty and youth. "Knowing the rites performed by people" means: knowing who in the land performs a sacrifice and at what times, they go there at their invitation. It is stated that such Aśvins should come together, both, to our sacrificial ground.

p. 375

[Running head, p. 375: A. 2 Ad. 8 Va. 4, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 375.]

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

शृंगे॑व नः प्रथ॒मा गं॑तम॒र्वाक्छ॒फावि॑न॒ जर्भु॑राणा॒ तरो॑भिः । च॒क्र॒वा॒केव॒ प्रति॒ वस्तो॑रुस्रा॒र्वांचा॑ यातं र॒थ्ये॑व शक्रा ॥ ३ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

शृंगा इव । नः । प्रथमा । गंतं । अर्वाक् । शफौ इव । जर्भुराणा । तरभिः । चक्रवाका इव । प्रति । वस्तोः । उस्रा । अर्वांचा । यातं । रथ्या इव । शक्रा ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विन् शृंगेव पशोः शृंगे इव प्रथमा देवानां प्रथमौ शफाविवाश्वादेः खुराविव तरोभिर्वेगैर्जर्भुराणा भृशं गच्छंतौ युवां नोऽस्मान्प्रत्यर्नागभिमुखमागंतं। आगच्छतं । किंच हे अश्विन् वस्तोः प्रति अहः प्रति चक्रवाकेव चक्रवाकाविव हे उस्रा शत्रूणामुत्सारकौ गमनशीलौ वा रथ्येव रथिनाविव हे शक्रा स्वकर्मणि शक्तावर्वांचास्मदभिमुखौ यातं । गच्छतं ॥

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods.) शृंगेव (śṛṃgeva)—you who are like the horns of an animal. प्रथमा (prathamā)—chief among the gods. शफाविव (śaphāviva)—you who are like the hooves of horses. तरोभिः (tarobhiḥ)—with swift motions. जर्भुराणा (jarbhurāṇā)—you who travel swiftly. नः अर्वाक् (naḥ arvāk)—toward us. गंतं (gaṃtaṃ)—come. वस्तोः प्रति (vastoḥ prati)—awaiting the day. चक्रवाकेव (cakravākeva)—you who are like cakravāka birds. उस्रा (usrā)—you Aśvin gods, who overthrow enemies. रथ्येव (rathyeva)—like heroes riding in chariots. शक्रा (śakrā)—you who are able in your deeds. अर्वांचा (arvāṃcā)—toward us. यातं (yātaṃ)—come.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, you who are like the horns of an animal, chief among the gods, like the hooves of horses, travelling swiftly with rapid motions, come toward us. You who are like cakravāka birds awaiting the day, overthrowers of enemies, O Aśvin gods, like heroes riding in chariots, able in your deeds, come toward us.

p. 376

[Running head, p. 376: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 39.]

English Translation (as printed)

Come to us, the first (before other gods), like a pair of horns or like two hoofs, travelling with rapid (steps); like a pair of Chakravakas, awaiting day; overthrowers of foes, like warriors in cars, able (to perform all things), come to our presence.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

O Aśvin gods, you are lofty like the two horns of an animal; the foremost among the gods, or those who come to the sacrificial ground before all the other gods; swift in going like the hooves of horses, that is, travelling quickly. Such as you are, come toward us as the cakravāka bird awaits the day itself; and you who are like heroes seated in a chariot, who destroy enemies and are able in your deeds, come toward us, to the sacrificial ground — this is the main sense.
