Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ना॒वेव॑ नः पारयतं यु॒गेव॒ नभ्ये॑व न उप॒धीव॑ प्र॒धीव॑ । श्वाने॑व नो॒ अरि॑षण्या त॒नूनां॒ खृग॑लेव वि॒स्रसः॑ पातम॒स्मान् ॥ ४ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

[Line-end hyphen of the Pada joined by hand in kn.md; the supplied text reads उपधीS (upadhīS) with a Latin S for the avagraha.]

नावाइव । नः । पारयतं । युगाइव । नभ्याइव । नः । उपधी इवेत्युपधीSइव । प्रधी इवेति प्रधीSइव । श्वानाइव । नः । अरिषण्या । तनूनां । खृगलाइव । विस्स्रसः । पातं । अस्मान् ॥ ४ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विनौ नावेव नावाविव सिंधून् नोऽस्मान् दुर्गाणि पारयतं । युगेव यथा रथस्य युगे नभ्येव यथा च रथचक्रनाभिफलके । उपधी इव यथा तत्पार्श्वस्थे फलके प्रधी इव यथा वा चक्रबाह्यवलयौ रथं पारयतः तथा

he aśvinau nāveva nāvāviva siṃdhūn no 'smān durgāṇi pārayataṃ | yugeva yathā rathasya yuge nabhyeva yathā ca rathacakranābhiphalake | upadhī iva yathā tatpārśvasthe phalake pradhī iva yathā vā cakrabāhyavalayau rathaṃ pārayataḥ tathā

p. 377

[Running head, p. 377: A. 2 Ad. 8 Va. 4, Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 377. The bhāṣya block is split by the page break: the first part ends on p. 376, the rest follows here as a second block; line-end hyphens joined by hand.]

नोऽस्मान्दुर्गाणि पारयतं । किंच श्वानेव श्वानाविव यथा श्वान् बाधकेभ्यो रज्ञंतौ तनोर्हिंसामपनयतः तथा नोऽस्माकं तनूनामंगानामरिषण्यावहिंकौ भवतं । खृगलेव यथा तनु त्राणे तनु हिंसाया रक्षतः तथा विस्रसो जराया अस्मान्युवां पातं ॥

(Gist: like boats carry across rivers, like the yoke, nave, spokes and rim carry a chariot across rough places, carry us over difficulties; like two dogs or two coats of mail, be harmless to our bodies and protect us from old age.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods.) नावेव (nāveva)—as boats carry across a river. नः (naḥ)—us. पारयतं (pārayataṃ)—carry across from sorrow and protect. युगेव (yugeva)—like the "rogas" [sic, as supplied; the Bhāvārtha has "nogas", i.e. yokes] of a chariot, नभ्येव (nabhyeva)—like the naves, उपधीव (upadhīva)—like the spokes (as supplied, इरचि (iraci)), प्रधी इव (pradhī iva)—like the outer rims (as all these carry across a chariot with a pair of wheels), नः (naḥ)—us (carry across from sorrow). श्वानेव (śvāneva)—as dogs protect from those who do harm. नः (naḥ)—our. तनूनां (tanūnāṃ)—of the bodies. अरिषण्या (ariṣaṇyā)—be harmless. खृगलेव (khṛgaleva)—as coats of mail protect from the harm of enemies. विस्रसः (visrasaḥ)—from old age. आस्मान् (āsmān) [sic, as supplied for अस्मान् (asmān)]—us. पातं (pātaṃ)—protect.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, as boats carry across a river, carry us across from sorrow and protect us. As the yokes, naves, spokes and outer rims of a chariot with two wheels carry it across rough places, so carry us across from sorrow. Like dogs and like coats of mail, protect us from the harm of enemies. Protect us from old age.

English Translation (as printed)

Bear us across (the sea of life), like two vessels, or (over difficult places), like the poles of a cas [sic], the axles, the spokes, the fellies (of two wheels): Be like two dogs, warding off injury to our persons, and, like two coats of mail, defend us from decay.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this ṛk the Aśvin gods are prayed, by many illustrations, to carry us, who offer praise, out of our troubles.

नावेव नः पारयतं—हे अश्विनौ नावाविव सिंधून् दुर्गाणि पारयतं । (nāveva naḥ pārayataṃ—he aśvinau nāvāviva siṃdhūn durgāṇi pārayataṃ |) O Aśvin gods, as a boat or ferry carries across rivers, remove our difficulties and carry us across our troubles. As rivers are crossed easily by a boat, so by your grace make us escape from our troubles — this is the sense.

p. 378

[Running head, p. 378: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 39. Line-end hyphens in the Sanskrit quotation joined by hand in the Kannada text. The Special Topics of Ṛk 4 continue from p. 377.]

युगेव नभ्येव उपधीव प्रधीव नः (पारयतं) (yugeva nabhyeva upadhīva pradhīva naḥ (pārayataṃ))—The yokes of a chariot, its axle, its spokes (iraci, as supplied) and its outer rims carry the chariot over (so that it travels easily); in the same way carry us out of sorrow.

श्वानेव नः तनूनां अरिषण्या—यथा श्वानौ बाधकेभ्यो रक्षंतौ तनोर्हिंसामपनयतः तथा अस्माकं अंगानां अहिंसकौ भवतं । (śvāneva naḥ tanūnāṃ ariṣaṇyā—yathā śvānau bādhakebhyo rakṣaṃtau tanorhiṃsāmapanayataḥ tathā asmākaṃ aṃgānāṃ ahiṃsakau bhavataṃ |) As the dogs we keep near us protect us from enemies who would do us harm, so protect us that no harm comes to our bodies.

खृगलेव विस्रसः अस्मान् पातं—यथा तनुत्राणे तनुहिंसाया रक्षतः तथा युवां जरायाः अस्मान् पातं । (khṛgaleva visrasaḥ asmān pātaṃ—yathā tanutrāṇe tanuhiṃsāyā rakṣataḥ tathā yuvāṃ jarāyāḥ asmān pātaṃ |) As the protective armour (iron coats of mail, "Armour" as printed in English) that we wear in battle and the like guards our body from the weapons of enemies, so protect us from the affliction of old age — this is the main purport.

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

वाते॑वाजु॒र्या न॒द्ये॑व री॒तिर॒क्षी इ॑व॒ चक्षु॒षा या॑तम॒र्वाक् । हस्ता॑विव त॒न्ने॒३॒॑ ३ शंभ॑विष्ठा॒ पादे॑व नो नयतं॒ वस्यो॒ अच्छ॑ ॥ ५ ॥

वाताइव । अजुर्या । नद्याइव । रीतिः । अक्षी इवेत्यक्षी इव । चक्षुषा । आ । यातं । अर्वाक् । हस्तौ इव । तन्वे । शंभविष्ठा । पादाइव । नः । नयतं । वस्यः । अच्छ ॥ ५ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विनौ वातेव वाताविवाजुर्या जरितुमशक्य नद्येव नद्याविव रीतिः ॥ व्यत्ययेनैकवचनं ॥ शीघ्रं गंतार् युवां । अक्षी इव आक्षिणी इव चक्षुषा दर्शनेनार्वागस्मदभिमुखमायातं । आगच्छतं । किंच हस्तेव हस्ताविव पादेव पादाविव तन्वे शरीराय शंभविष्ठा सुखस्य भावयितृतमौ युवां नोऽस्मान् वस्को वसीयः श्रेष्ठं धनमच्छ प्रति नयतं । प्रापयतं ॥

he aśvinau vāteva vātāvivājuryā jaritumaśakya nadyeva nadyāviva rītiḥ ‖ vyatyayenaikavacanaṃ ‖ śīghraṃ gaṃtār yuvāṃ | akṣī iva ākṣiṇī iva cakṣuṣā darśanenārvāgasmadabhimukhamāyātaṃ | āgacchataṃ | kiṃca hasteva hastāviva pādeva pādāviva tanve śarīrāya śaṃbhaviṣṭhā sukhasya bhāvayitṛtamau yuvāṃ no 'smān vasko vasīyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ dhanamaccha prati nayataṃ | prāpayataṃ ‖

(Gist: like winds, like rivers, like two eyes come toward us; like hands and feet, bringers of comfort to the body, lead us to the best wealth. The bhāṣya has a Saṃhitā-form हस्तेव (hasteva) for the Saṃhitā's हस्ताविव (hastāviva) in places, and गंतार् (gaṃtār) and वस्को (vasko) as supplied; not corrected. The Saṃhitā's तन्ने (tanne) is as supplied; the Pada has तन्वे (tanve).)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods.) अजुर्या (ajuryā) (ajuryā)—of unobstructed power. वातेव (vāteva) (vāteva)—like the storm winds. रीतिः (rītiḥ) (rītiḥ)—swiftly flowing. नद्येव (nadyeva) (nadyeva)—like rivers. चक्षुषा (cakṣuṣā) (cakṣuṣā)—having power of sight. अक्षीव (akṣīva) (akṣīva)—like eyes. अर्वाक् (arvāk) (arvāk)—toward us. आ यातं (ā yātaṃ) (ā yātaṃ)—come. हस्तौ इव (hastau iva) (hastau iva)—like two hands. पादा इव (pādā iva) (pādā iva)—like two feet. तन्वे (tanve) (tanve)—to the body. शंभविष्ठा (śaṃbhaviṣṭhā) (śaṃbhaviṣṭhā)—you who bring comfort. नः (naḥ) (naḥ)—us. वस्यः अच्छ (vasyaḥ accha) (vasyaḥ accha)—toward the best wealth. नयतं (nayataṃ) (nayataṃ)—lead.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, come toward us like the storm winds of unobstructed power, like swiftly flowing rivers, like eyes that have the power of sight. You who bring comfort to the body like two hands and two feet, lead us toward the best wealth.

English Translation (as printed)

Irresistible as two winds, rapid as two rivers, and quick of sight, come like two eyes before ns [sic]; like two hands; like two feet; subservient to the well-being of our bodies, conduct us to (the acquirement) of excellent (wealth).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

अजुर्या वातेव, रीतिः नद्येव, चक्षुषा अक्षी इव अर्वाक् आ यातं । (ajuryā vāteva, rītiḥ nadyeva, cakṣuṣā akṣī iva arvāk ā yātaṃ |) The ṛṣi prays by illustrations that the Aśvin gods come quickly to us. Nothing can check the speed of a storm wind; it uproots the trees and the like in front of it. Often huts and houses cannot bear its force and are flung to a distant place. At sea it sinks ships. Therefore the force of the storm is unobstructed; nothing stands against it. In the same way a swiftly flowing river sweeps away everything in its path, and no one can stop a river's flow. For well-seeing eyes nothing is hidden; they can see what is near and what is far; their power of sight is vast. Therefore, O Aśvin gods, come toward us with unobstructed motion like the force of the storm, like a swiftly flowing river, like eyes that see everything. No one has the power to stop your coming toward us.

p. 380

[Running head, p. 380: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 39. The Special Topics of Ṛk 5 continue from p. 379.]

हस्ताविव पादेव तन्ने शंभविष्ठा नः वस्य अच्छ नयतं—यथा हस्तौ पादौ शरीराय सुखस्य भावयित्यृतमौ तथा युवां आस्मान् श्रेष्ठं धनं प्रति प्रापयतं । (hastāviva pādeva tanne śaṃbhaviṣṭhā naḥ vasya accha nayataṃ—yathā hastau pādau śarīrāya sukhasya bhāvayityṛtamau tathā yuvāṃ āsmān śreṣṭhaṃ dhanaṃ prati prāpayataṃ |) As the legs and hands in the body, wishing only the welfare of the body, work to give the body comfort, so, for our comfort, provide us, both of you, with the best wealth we need — this is the purport. (Quotation as supplied: तन्ने (tanne), भावयित्यृतमौ (bhāvayityṛtamau), आस्मान् (āsmān) not corrected.)

Ṛk 6

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ओष्ठा॑विन॒ मध्वा॒स्ने वदं॑ता॒ स्तना॑विन पिप्यतं जी॒वसे॑ नः । नासे॑व नस्त॒न्वो॑ रक्षि॒तारा॒ कर्णा॑विन सु॒श्रुता॑ भूतम॒स्मे ॥ ६ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

ओष्ठौ इव । मधु । आस्ने । वदंता । स्तन्सौ इव । पिप्यतं । जीवसे । नः । नासा इव । नः । तन्वः । रक्षितारा । कर्णौ इव । सुश्रुता । भूतं । आस्मे इति ॥ ६ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विनौ ओष्ठाविवास्न आस्याय मधुररसवद्वचनं वदंतौ स्तनाविव नोऽस्मान् जीवसे जीवनाय पिप्यतं । प्याययतं । किंच नासेव नासिके इव नोऽस्माकं तन्वस्तनो रक्षितारा रक्षितारौ भूतं । भवतं । अपि च कर्णाविवास्मे आस्माकं सुश्रुता सुश्रवणे युवां भूतं । भवतं ॥

he aśvinau oṣṭhāvivāsna āsyāya madhurarasavadvacanaṃ vadaṃtau stanāviva no 'smān jīvase jīvanāya pipyataṃ | pyāyayataṃ | kiṃca nāseva nāsike iva no 'smākaṃ tanvastano rakṣitārā rakṣitārau bhūtaṃ | bhavataṃ | api ca karṇāvivāsme āsmākaṃ suśrutā suśravaṇe yuvāṃ bhūtaṃ | bhavataṃ ‖

(Gist: like lips speaking sweetly to the mouth, like breasts nourish us for life; like the nose guard our bodies; like ears be good listeners for us. Spellings in the Saṃhitā and Pada (ओष्ठाविन (oṣṭhāvina), स्तनाविन (stanāvina), स्तन्सौ (stansau), आस्मे (āsme)) are as supplied, not corrected.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Aśvinau—O Aśvin gods!) आस्ने (āsne) (āsne)—in the mouth. ओष्ठाविन (oṣṭhāvina) (oṣṭhāvina) [as supplied]—like the lips. मधु (madhu) (madhu)—sweetly. वदंता (vadaṃtā) (vadaṃtā)—speaking, and. स्तनाविव (stanāviva) (stanāviva)—like breasts (the Kannada gloss is printed स्तगळंतॆ (stagaḷaṃtè), a syllable missing). नः (naḥ) (naḥ)—us. जीवसे (jīvase) (jīvase)—for life. पिप्यतं (pipyataṃ) (pipyataṃ)—be nourishers. नासेव (nāseva) (nāseva)—like the nose. नः (naḥ) (naḥ)—our. तन्वः (tanvaḥ) (tanvaḥ)—of the body. रक्षितारा (rakṣitārā) (rakṣitārā)—be protectors. कर्णाविव (karṇāviva) (karṇāviva)—like ears. सुश्रिता (suśritā) (suśritā) [as supplied; the Saṃhitā has सुश्रुता (suśrutā)]—hearing excellent praises and the like. अस्मे (asme) (asme)—on our behalf. भूतं (bhūtaṃ) (bhūtaṃ)—be.

p. 381

[Running head, p. 381, as supplied: "ಅ. ೨. ಆ. ೮. ವ. ೫. ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 381". The Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 6 was complete on p. 380.]

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, be to us like lips in the mouth, speaking sweetly; be like breasts, nourishing us for our living; and be like the nose, protectors of our body. Be to our share like ears, hearing excellent praises and the like.

English Translation (as printed)

Like two lips uttering sweet words; like two breasts yielding nourishment for our existence; be to us like two noses, preserving our persons, and like two ears for the hearing of agreeable (sounds).

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

आस्ने ओष्ठाविव मधु वदंता—हे अश्विनौ ओष्ठाविव आस्याय मधुररसवद्वचनं वदंतौ ।

āsne oṣṭhāviva madhu vadaṃtā—he aśvinau oṣṭhāviva āsyāya madhurarasavadvacanaṃ vadaṃtau |

O Aśvin gods, just as the two lips in our mouth give us joy when they speak pleasant words, sweet like honey-juice, so do good to us.

स्तनाविव नः जीवसे पिप्यतं (stanāviva naḥ jīvase pipyataṃ)—As the breasts of the mother, when we were infants, gave us milk and made us grow, so nourish us by giving us food and the like.

नासेव नः तन्न रक्षितारा (nāseva naḥ tanna rakṣitārā) (as supplied; the Pratipadārtha has ತನ್ವಃ)—As our nose, by giving warning, keeps us from going to foul-smelling places, so protect us from any harm by enemies and from other kinds of danger.

कर्णाविव सुश्रिता अस्मे भूतं (karṇāviva suśritā asme bhūtaṃ) (as supplied)—As our ears feel joy on hearing pleasing words, so hear the excellent praises we recite and take delight.

अस्मे (asme)—This word is used in the sense of all seven case-endings. Example—

अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥

asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖

अस्मे इत्येतत्पदं सर्वविभक्त्यंतं । तस्मादनेकार्थं । एकमेव हैतच्छब्धरूपं सप्तस्वपि विभक्त्यर्थेषु वर्तते । प्रकरणादिवशात् तस्य नियमो भवति । तद्यथा— प्रथमायास्तावत्—अस्मे ते बंधुः । वयमित्यर्थः ॥

asme ityetatpadaṃ sarvavibhaktyaṃtaṃ | tasmādanekārthaṃ | ekameva haitacchabdharūpaṃ saptasvapi vibhaktyartheṣu vartate | prakaraṇādivaśāt tasya niyamo bhavati | tadyathā— prathamāyāstāvat—asme te baṃdhuḥ | vayamityarthaḥ ‖

That is, the word अस्मे (asme) is used in the sense of the seven case-endings according to context; that is, according to the passage, any one of the seven case meanings can be given to this word. For example, in the sentence अस्मे (asme) (continued on the next page)

p. 382

[Running head, p. 382: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 39. A stray "1." printed before items (2) and, on p. 383, (6) in the supplied text was removed.]

ते बंधुः (te baṃdhuḥ), the word अस्मे (asme) means वयं (vayaṃ)—"we". This is an example of the sense of the nominative.

अस्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । आस्मानित्यर्थः ॥

asme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | āsmānityarthaḥ ‖

द्वितीयायास्तावत् (dvitīyāyāstāvat)—for the word अस्मे (asme) the meaning is the accusative अस्मान् (asmān)—"us". As an example of this meaning:

आ श्येन्यस्य जवसा नूतनेनास्मे यातं नासत्या सजोषाः । हवे हि वामश्विना रातहव्यः शश्वत्तमाया उषसो व्युष्टौ ॥

ā śyenyasya javasā nūtanenāsme yātaṃ nāsatyā sajoṣāḥ | have hi vāmaśvinā rātahavyaḥ śaśvattamāyā uṣaso vyuṣṭau ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-111 as printed)

They have given this Ṛk. In it the word अस्मे (asme) means अस्मान् (asmān)—"us".

अस्मे समानेभिवृषभ पौंस्येभिः । अस्माभिरित्यर्थः ।

asme samānebhivṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | asmābhirityarthaḥ |

तृतीयायास्तावत् (tṛtīyāyāstāvat)—here अस्मे (asme) means अस्माभिः (asmābhiḥ)—"by us", the sense of the instrumental. On this point—

भूरि चकर्थ युज्येभिरस्मे समानेभिवृषभ पौंस्येभिः । भूरीणि हि कृणवामा शविष्ठेंद्र क्रत्वा मरुतो यद्वशाम ॥

bhūri cakartha yujyebhirasme samānebhivṛṣabha pauṃsyebhiḥ | bhūrīṇi hi kṛṇavāmā śaviṣṭheṃdra kratvā maruto yadvaśāma ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-165-7)

They have given this Ṛk as the example. Here अस्मे (asme) means अस्माभिः (asmābhiḥ)—"by us".

अस्मे प्रयंधि मघवन्नजीषिन् । अस्मभ्यमित्यर्थः ॥

asme prayaṃdhi maghavannajīṣin | asmabhyamityarthaḥ ‖

चतुर्थ्यास्तावत् (caturthyāstāvat)—here अस्मे (asme) means अस्मभ्यं (asmabhyaṃ)—"for us", the sense of the dative. Example—

अस्मे प्रयंधि मघवन्नजीषिन्निंद रायो विश्ववारस्य भूरेः । अस्मे शतं शरदो जीवसे धा अस्मे वीराञ्छत इंद्र शिप्रिन् ॥

asme prayaṃdhi maghavannajīṣinniṃda rāyo viśvavārasya bhūreḥ | asme śataṃ śarado jīvase dhā asme vīrāñchata iṃdra śiprin ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-36-10)

In this Ṛk the words अस्मे (asme) mean अस्मभ्यं (asmabhyaṃ)—"for us", the sense of the dative.

अस्मे आराच्चिद्वेषः सनुतर्ययोतु । अस्मदित्यर्थः ।

asme ārāccidveṣaḥ sanutaryayotu | asmadityarthaḥ |

पंचम्यास्तावत् (paṃcamyāstāvat) here अस्मे (asme) means अस्मत् (asmat)—"from our side" (the Kannada text has ದೆಶೆಯಿಂದ, as supplied). Example—

तस्य वयं सुमता यज्ञियस्यापि भद्रे सौमनसे स्याम । स सुत्रामा स्ववा इंद्रो अस्मे आराचिद्वेषः सनुतर्ययोतु ॥

tasya vayaṃ sumatā yajñiyasyāpi bhadre saumanase syāma | sa sutrāmā svavā iṃdro asme ārācidveṣaḥ sanutaryayotu ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-47-13)

p. 383

[Running head, p. 383, as supplied: "ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೮. ವ. ೫ ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 383".]

In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (asme) means अस्मत् (asmat)—"from our side"; this is the sense of the ablative (the Kannada text prints ಸಂಚಮೀ, as supplied).

ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे । अस्माकमित्यर्थः ।

ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme | asmākamityarthaḥ |

षष्ठ्यास्तावत् (ṣaṣṭhyāstāvat)—here अस्मे (asme) means अस्माकं (asmākaṃ)—"to us" (as supplied; "our"). To explain this meaning—

आ नो भर भगमिंद्र द्युमंतं नि ते देष्णस्य धीमहि प्ररेके । ऊर्व इव पप्रथे कामो अस्मे तमा पृण वसुपते वसूनां ॥

ā no bhara bhagamiṃdra dyumaṃtaṃ ni te deṣṇasya dhīmahi prareke | ūrva iva paprathe kāmo asme tamā pṛṇa vasupate vasūnāṃ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-30-19)

They have cited this Ṛk. In it the word अस्मे (asme) means अस्माकं (asmākaṃ)—"our, to us", the sense of the genitive.

अस्मे धत्त वसवो वसूनि । अस्मास्वित्यर्थः ॥

asme dhatta vasavo vasūni | asmāsvityarthaḥ ‖

सप्तम्यास्तावत् (saptamyāstāvat)—here अस्मे (asme) means "in us". For example—

अग्ने वाजस्य गोमत ईशानः सहसो यहो । अस्मे धेहि जातवेदो महि श्रवः ॥

agne vājasya gomata īśānaḥ sahaso yaho | asme dhehi jātavedo mahi śravaḥ ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-29-4)

In this Ṛk the word अस्मे (asme) means अस्मासु (asmāsu)—"in us", the sense of the locative.

Ṛk 7

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

हस्ते॑व श॒क्तिम॒भि सं॑द॒दी नः॒ क्षामे॑व नः॒ सम॑जतं॒ रजां॑सि । इ॒मा गिरो॑ अश्विना युष्म॒यंतीः॒ क्षोणेत्रे॑णेव॒ स्वधि॑तिं॒ सं शि॑शीतं॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

हस्ता इव । शक्तिं । अभि । संददी इति संसददी । नः । क्षामइव । नः । सं । अजतं । रजांसि । इमाः । गिरः । अश्विना । युष्मयंतीः । क्षोत्रेण इव । स्वधितिं । सं । शिशीतं ॥७॥

hastā iva | śaktiṃ | abhi | saṃdadī iti saṃsadadī | naḥ | kṣāmaiva | naḥ | saṃ | ajataṃ | rajāṃsi | imāḥ | giraḥ | aśvinā | yuṣmayaṃtīḥ | kṣotreṇa iva | svadhitiṃ | saṃ | śiśītaṃ ‖7‖

(Note: the Saṃhitā ends without the Ṛk number, the Pada ends with ॥೭॥. The Pada's ಸಂದದೀ ಇತಿ ಸಂಸದದೀ, ಕ್ಷಾಮಇವ and ಕ್ಷೋತ್ರೇಣ ಇವ differ from the Saṃhitā's ಸಂದದೀ, ಕ್ಷಾಮೇವ and ಕ್ಷೋಣೇತ್ರೇಣೇವ; all as supplied, not corrected. The Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 7 follows on the next page.)

p. 384

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे अश्विनौ हस्तेव हस्ताविव शक्तिं सामर्थ्यं नोऽस्माकमभिसंददी अभिमुख्येन सम्यक् प्रयच्छंतौ भवतं । किंच क्षामेव रोदसी इव रजांसि स्थानान्युदकानि वा ॥ उदकं रज उच्यत इति यास्कः ॥ नोऽस्माकं समजतं । प्रेरयतं । आपिच अश्विना हे अश्विनौ इमा गिरोऽस्माभिः कृताः स्तुतीर्युष्मयंतीर्युवामिच्छंतीः स्वधितिमसिं क्ष्णोत्रेणेव तेजनशाणवत् संशिशीतं । सम्सक् तीक्ष्मीकुरुतं ॥

Gist: the Aśvins are asked to give strength like two hands, to bestow waters or abodes like heaven and earth, and to sharpen the praises like a blade on a whetstone.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अश्विनौ (aśvinau)—O Aśvin deities; हस्तेव (hasteva)—like two hands; शक्तिं (śaktiṃ)—strength; नः (naḥ)—to us; अभि संददी (abhi saṃdadī)—be givers (printed कोडुववरागिरि (koḍuvavarāgiri)); क्षामेव (kṣāmeva)—like heaven and earth; रजांसि (rajāṃsi)—waters (or places); नः (naḥ)—to us; समजतं (samajataṃ)—impel; स्वधितिं (svadhitiṃ)—a sword; क्षोत्रेणेव (kṣotreṇeva)—as one rubs it on a whetstone and makes it sharp; इमा गिरः (imā giraḥ)—our words of praise; युष्मयंतीः (yuṣmayaṃtīḥ)—approaching you and pleasing you; सं शिशीतं (saṃ śiśītaṃ)—make sharp.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin deities, be givers of strength to us, like two hands. Like heaven and earth, impel (give) waters to us. As a sword is rubbed on a whetstone and made sharp, make these our words of praise so sharp that they approach you and give you satisfaction.

Printed English translation

Like two hands, Ashwins, be ever investing us with vigour ; like heaven and earth, bestow upon us rain : give sharpness to the praises that are addressed to you, as they whet an axe upon a grindstone.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

क्षामा—रोदसी इव (kṣāmā—rodasī iva). Although the word क्ष्या (kṣyā) or क्षामा (kṣāmā) is listed among the names of the earth, here it is a dual-ending word and is used to denote heaven and earth. Since all the qualifying words describing the Aśvin deities in this sūkta are in the dual, the word क्षामा (kṣāmā) too must be taken as dual, and the sense "the two worlds" or "heaven and earth" given to it.

p. 385

रजांसि (rajāṃsi)—

रजो रजतेर्जोर्यती रज उच्यते । उदकं रज उच्यते । लोका रजांस्युच्यंते

rajo rajaterjoryatī raja ucyate | udakaṃ raja ucyate | lokā rajāṃsyucyaṃte

(Nir. 4-19)

Since Yāska gives this etymology, in the present context both meanings, water and worlds, can be given.

क्षोत्रेणेव—तेजनशाणवत् (kṣotreṇeva—tejanaśāṇavat). A whetstone or another kind of stone used for rubbing and sharpening weapons such as swords and knives.

स्वधितिं (svadhitiṃ)—The word स्वधिति (svadhiti) is read among the names of the thunderbolt (Nir. 3-11). It is also customary to call sharp swords and other weapons स्वधिति (svadhiti); in the scriptural sentence ओषधे त्रायस्यैनं स्वधिते मैनग्ं हिग्ंसीः (oṣadhe trāyasyainaṃ svadhite mainagṃ higṃsīḥ) too the word स्वधिति (svadhiti) is used in the sense of a knife (a razor).

शिशीतं—सम्यक् तीक्ष्णीकुरुतं (śiśītaṃ—samyak tīkṣṇīkurutaṃ): make well sharp. For the word शिशीते (śiśīte) Yāska gives the etymology—

शिशीते । शिशीते शृंगे रक्षसे विनिक्षे । निश्यति शृंगे रक्षसो विनिक्षणनाय । रक्षो रक्षितव्यमस्मात् । रहसि क्षणोतीति ना । रात्रौ नक्षत इति वा ॥

śiśīte | śiśīte śṛṃge rakṣase vinikṣe | niśyati śṛṃge rakṣaso vinikṣaṇanāya | rakṣo rakṣitavyamasmāt | rahasi kṣaṇotīti nā | rātrau nakṣata iti vā ‖

(Nir. 4-18)

Quoting the mantra शिशीते शृंगे रक्षसे विनिक्षे (śiśīte śṛṃge rakṣase vinikṣe), he explains the meaning of the word शिशीते (śiśīte): a bull (or an animal) rubs and sharpens its horn in order to kill enemies or to protect itself.

अश्विना हस्तेव शक्तिं नः अभि संददी (aśvinā hasteva śaktiṃ naḥ abhi saṃdadī)—

हे अश्विनौ हस्ताविव सामर्थ्यं अस्माकमाभिमुख्येन प्रयच्छंतौ भवतं ।

he aśvinau hastāviva sāmarthyaṃ asmākamābhimukhyena prayacchaṃtau bhavataṃ |

No work can be done without the help of the hands; hence the hands are well known to have the power of working. Therefore, O Aśvin deities, as our hands give us strength in all our tasks and carry the work through, so you two, like two hands, produce in us strength and capacity in all matters: this is the purport.

क्षामेव रजांसि नः समजतं (kṣāmeva rajāṃsi naḥ samajataṃ)—

रोदसी इव नः स्थानान्युदकानि वा प्रयच्छतं ।

rodasī iva naḥ sthānānyudakāni vā prayacchataṃ |

As heaven and earth provide us dwelling places to live in, and give the rain-waters that sustain life, and protect us, so you too provide us with dwelling places and rain, and protect us.

स्वधितिं क्ष्णोत्रेणेव इमा गिरः युष्मयंतीः सं शिशीतं (svadhitiṃ kṣṇotreṇeva imā giraḥ yuṣmayaṃtīḥ saṃ śiśītaṃ)—

अपि च हे आश्विनौ आस्माभिः कृताः स्तुतीः युवामिच्छंतीः आसिं तेजनशाणवत् समक्तीक्ष्णि-

(Note: the Sanskrit line breaks off with a hyphen at the foot of p. 385; the printed sheet-mark "25" that follows on this page was removed from kn.md. The Sanskrit is continued on the next page.)

p. 386

कुरुतं ।

kurutaṃ |

And, O Aśvin deities, as a sword is rubbed on a whetstone and made sharp, make sharp the words of praise we make for you; that is, listen to our praises with regard: this is the purport.

Ṛk 8

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

ए॒तानि॑ वामश्विना॒ वर्ध॑नानि॒ ब्रह्म॒ स्तोमं॑ गृत्सम॒दासो॑ अक्रन् । तानि॑ नरा जुजुषा॒णोप॑ यातं बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

एतानि । वां । अश्विना । वर्धनानि । ब्रह्म । स्तोमं । गृत्समदासः । अक्रन् । तानि । नरा । जुजुषाणा । उप । यातं । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुवीराः ॥ ८ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अश्विना हे अश्विन् वां युवयोरेतानि वर्धनानि वृद्धिसाधनानि ब्रह्म ब्रह्माणि मंत्रान् स्तोमं स्तोत्रं च गृत्समदासो गृत्समदा अक्रन् । अकुर्वन् । तानि ब्रह्माणि नरा नेतारौ जुजुषाणा भृशं प्रीयमाणौ युवामुपयातं । उपगच्छतं । किंच सुवीराः शोभनपुत्रा वयं विदथे यज्ञे युवां बृहद्वदेम । प्रभूतं स्तुमः ॥

Gist: the Gṛtsamadas made these growth-giving mantras and praise for the Aśvins; they are asked to come, pleased, and the we, with good sons, will praise them at the sacrifice.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

अश्विना (aśvinā)—O Aśvin deities; वां (vāṃ)—of you two; वर्धनानि (vardhanāni)—means of growth (satisfaction); एतानि ब्रह्म (etāni brahma)—these mantras in the form of praise; स्तोमं (stomaṃ)—praise in the form of a stoma; गृत्समदासः (gṛtsamadāsaḥ)—the Gṛtsamada sages; अक्रन् (akran)—have made; तानि (tāni)—those praises; नरा (narā)—you leaders; जुजुषाणा (jujuṣāṇā)—enjoying them with regard; उपयातं (upayātaṃ)—come to us; सुवीराः (suvīrāḥ)—we, endowed with excellent heroic sons; विदथे (vidathe)—in the sacrificial house; बृहत् (bṛhat)—abundant praise; वदेम (vadema)—we recite.

p. 387

[Running head, p. 387: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 5; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 387.]

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Aśvin gods, the Gṛtsamada seers have composed these mantras in the form of praise, and this praise in the form of a stoma, which are the means of satisfying you both. O leaders, come to us, enjoying those praises with regard. We, endowed with excellent heroic sons, recite abundant praise in the sacrificial house.

Printed English

The Gritsmadas have composed this prayer, these praises, Ashwins, for your exaltation : be propitiated by them leaders of ceremonies, and come hither ; that, blessed with excellent descendants, we may worthily glorify you at this sacrifice.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

वर्धनानि—वृद्धिसाधनानि । (vardhanāni—vṛddhisādhanāni |) (vardhanāni, means of growth). There is a custom of saying that when the gods' qualities are sung with mantras, their power and capacity increase. Therefore here the praises called brahma and stomaṃ are said to be means of growth. On this point many Śruti sentences can be cited, such as इमा वर्धंतु वां गिरः । (imā vardhaṃtu vāṃ giraḥ |), वर्धंतु त्वा सुष्टुतयः । (vardhaṃtu tvā suṣṭutayaḥ |), गीर्भिर्वर्धयामो वचोभिः । (gīrbhirvardhayāmo vacobhiḥ |) and others.

ब्रह्म—ब्रह्माणि स्तोत्राणि । (brahma—brahmāṇi stotrāṇi |) The word brahma is read both among the names of food and among the names of praise. Here it is used in the sense of praise. Since in this Ṛk the word stoma, also meaning praise, occurs as well, there is a difference between these two in meaning and in explanation. What a stoma is, its nature, its divisions and subdivisions and similar matters we have explained at length in Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 2, pp. 137 to 150.

गृत्समदासः (gṛtsamadāsaḥ)—Since the plural of the word gṛtsamada is used here, it should be understood that the plural is used to refer to the seer Gṛtsamada, his descendants, other relatives and so on.

जुजुषाणा—भृशं प्रीयमाण् । (jujuṣāṇā—bhṛśaṃ prīyamāṇ |) जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । (juṣī prītisevanayoḥ |) For this word, formed from this root, the meaning is "being very pleased". O Aśvin gods, may these praises composed by us, descendants of the seer Gṛtsamada, increase your power and give you joy. Being very pleased with us because of our praises, come to our sacrificial ground. At this sacrifice we, together with sons and grandsons, recite abundant praise for you: this is the main purport.

[The Kannada text prints ಸೋತ್ರ for ಸ್ತೋತ್ರ in the last sentence, as supplied.]

p. 388

[Running head, p. 388: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 40.]

The fortieth sūkta.

Sāyaṇa's introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed; see the Anuvāda below for the sense):

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सोमापूषणेति षडृचमष्टमं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभं सोमापूषदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रांतं । सोमापूषणा षट् सोमापौष्णमंत्योSर्धर्चोSप्यदितेरिति । अवतु देव्यदितिरित्यस्यांत्यार्थर्चस्यादितिर्देवता ॥ सोमापौष्टे पशौ, वपापुरोडाशहविषामाद्यास्ति स्रः क्रमेणानुवाक्या उत्तरास्तिस्रो याज्याः । अग्नीषोमाविति खंडे सूत्रितं । सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां । आ. ३-८ । इति ॥

[Note: in kn.md the Sanskrit introduction was made a > block with an inserted label, and two hyphenated line breaks were joined.]

Anuvāda (Kannada). The sūkta beginning सोमापूषणा (somāpūṣaṇā) is the eighth sūkta in the fourth anuvāka. It has six ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta; the metre is triṣṭubh; the two deities Soma and Pūṣan are the deity of the sūkta. The Anukramaṇikā says: सोमापूषणा षट् सोमापौष्णमंत्योSर्धर्चोSप्यदितेः (somāpūṣaṇā ṣaṭ somāpauṣṇamaṃtyoSrdharcoSpyaditeḥ) ("Soma and Pūṣan, six; the last half-verse is addressed to Aditi as well"). The deity of the latter half of the last Ṛk, "Avatu devy aditiḥ", is Aditi. In the animal sacrifice performed for Soma and Pūṣan, when the offerings of omentum and cake are made, the first three Ṛks of this sūkta are to be used as anuvākyā mantras and the last three as yājyā mantras, as explained by the sūtra beginning सोमापूषणा जनना याणां (somāpūṣaṇā jananā yāṇāṃ) in the section "Agnīṣomau" of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra (Ā. 3-8). [The sūtra is printed रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ) in the Sanskrit block above and याणां (yāṇāṃ) here, as supplied. The sūtra's anuvākya/yājyā sense is stated by the Kannada.]

Sūkta 40 (Maṇḍala 2)

[The heading lines of the supplied text, kept as a note: ಸೂಕ್ತ—೪೦; Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 4, Sūkta 40; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6; number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6; seer: Gṛtsamada; deity: Ṛks 1 to 5 and the first half of Ṛk 6: Soma and Pūṣan; the latter half of 6: आदितिः (āditiḥ) (as supplied, for Aditi); metre: Triṣṭubh.]

Pīṭhike (Introduction)

The deities of this sūkta are Soma and Pūṣan. In the Ṛgveda it is seen specially that two deities are joined together and invoked and praised together.

p. 389

[Running head, p. 389: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 389.]

Mantras that address two deities of this kind (pairs of deities) are called saṃstavika mantras. The principal deities among them are fourteen: Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, Brahmaṇaspati, Parvata, Kutsa, Viṣṇu, Vāyu, Mitra, Rudra, Vāta, Parjanya. [Fourteen as stated in the supplied text; the list given has fourteen names.] Thus:

Indrāgnī (Indra + Agni)—

इंद्राग्नी रोचना दिवः

iṃdrāgnī rocanā divaḥ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-12-9).

Indrāsomā (Indra + Soma)—

इंद्रासोमा समघशंसं

iṃdrāsomā samaghaśaṃsaṃ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-2).

Indrāvaruṇā (Indra + Varuṇa)—

इंद्रावरुणा युवमध्वराय नः

iṃdrāvaruṇā yuvamadhvarāya naḥ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-82-1).

Indrāpūṣaṇā (Indra + Pūṣan)—

इंद्रापूषणा वयं

iṃdrāpūṣaṇā vayaṃ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-57-1).

Indrābṛhaspatī (Indra + Bṛhaspati)—

इदं वामास्यॆ हविः प्रियमिंद्राबृहस्पती

idaṃ vāmāsyè haviḥ priyamiṃdrābṛhaspatī

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-49-1).

Indrābrahmaṇaspatī (Indra + Brahmaṇaspati)—

अच्छेंद्राब्रह्मणस्पती हविर्नः

accheṃdrābrahmaṇaspatī havirnaḥ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-24-12).

Indrāparvatā (Indra + Parvata)—

इंद्रापर्वता बृहता रथेन

iṃdrāparvatā bṛhatā rathena

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-53-1).

Indrākutsā (Indra + Kutsa)—

इंद्राकुत्सा वहमाना रथेन

iṃdrākutsā vahamānā rathena

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-31-9).

Indrāviṣṇū (Indra + Viṣṇu)—

इंद्राविष्णू दृंहिताः शंबरस्य

iṃdrāviṣṇū dṛṃhitāḥ śaṃbarasya

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-99-5).

Indravāyū (Indra + Vāyu)—

इंद्रवायू इमे सुताः

iṃdravāyū ime sutāḥ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-2-4).

Mitrāvaruṇā (Mitra + Varuṇa)—

आ नो मित्रावरुणा

ā no mitrāvaruṇā

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-62-16).

Somāpūṣaṇā (Soma + Pūṣan)—

सोमापूषणा जनना रयाणां

somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayāṇāṃ

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-40-1).

[Note: in kn.md the twelve quotations of this page were made > blocks with the reference left on its own line. The last quotation is printed रयाणां (rayāṇāṃ) here as supplied (the bhāṣya on p. 388 has रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ)).]

p. 390

[Running head, p. 390: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 40.]

Somārudrā (Soma + Rudra)—

[Note: the heading is printed in the supplied text but no quotation follows it; none is supplied.]

Vātāparjanyā (Vāta + Parjanya)—

धर्कारो दिव ऋभवः सुहस्ता वातापर्जन्या महिषस्य तन्यतोः [?]

dharkāro diva ṛbhavaḥ suhastā vātāparjanyā mahiṣasya tanyatoḥ [?]

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-66-10).

[Note: the first word of the quotation is धर्कारो (dharkāro) as supplied; marked [?]. In kn.md the quotations of this page were made > blocks with the reference left on its own line.]

Agnīṣomau (Agni + Soma)—

अग्नीषोमाविमं सु मे

agnīṣomāvimaṃ su me

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-93-1).

Agnīsarjanyā (Agni + Sarjanya) [sic: the heading reads सर्जन्य (sarjanya) where the quotation has पर्जन्य (parjanya)]—

अग्नीपर्जन्याववतं धियं मे

agnīparjanyāvavataṃ dhiyaṃ me

(Ya. Saṃ. 6-52-16) [reference printed with the abbreviation य. सं. (ya. saṃ.) as supplied].

Agnāviṣṇū (Agni + Viṣṇu)—

अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसा

agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā

(Tai. Saṃ. 4-7-1).

There are many such saṃstava mantras in the Ṛgveda. There are also many Ṛks which, when indicating a pair of deities, do not use the dual number but use the singular separately for each. For example—

अग्न इंद्रश्च दाशुषे दुरोणे

agna iṃdraśca dāśuṣe duroṇe

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-25-4).

त्वं नो अग्ने वरुणस्य विद्वान्

tvaṃ no agne varuṇasya vidvān

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-1-4).

मरुतः पिबत ऋतुना

marutaḥ pibata ṛtunā

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-15-2).

and so on. In these Ṛks, although the pairs of deities Agni + Indra, Agni + Varuṇa, Marut + Ṛtu are indicated, the dual number has not been used. The deities are indicated separately, each in the singular.

Soma. We have given explanations about the Soma plant many times. But everywhere there it was said that soma is the juice drawn from a kind of creeper called soma, that it gives enthusiasm and joy to those who drink it, and that, when the deities are invoked, they should come to the sacrificial ground and drink the soma juice; many such descriptions have been given. Apart from the ninth Maṇḍala, sūktas praising Soma as a deity are very rare in the other Maṇḍalas. All the sūktas of the ninth Maṇḍala praise only the deity Soma. On that occasion a detailed account of Soma is necessary, but a brief account here cannot be out of place.

[End of the page text; the note "..", a doubled full stop after स्तुतिसुवुदागिदॆ (stutisuvudāgidè), is printed as supplied.]

p. 391

[Running head, p. 391: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 391.]

Since Soma sacrifices are the most important among the rites of the Ṛgveda, it is natural that the deity Soma too is one of the principal deities. The 114 sūktas of the ninth Maṇḍala and 6 other sūktas, 120 sūktas in all, praise the deity Soma. Parts of 4–5 sūktas, and 5–7 sūktas jointly with Indra, Agni, Pūṣan or Rudra, also praise the deity Soma. The name Soma occurs, alone or as part of a compound, about 120 times. In terms of number, the deity Soma stands third. Anthropomorphism is very sparing. Since the Soma plant and its juices are mentioned again and again, it is impossible to forget them entirely; hence references to the form, limbs or movements of that deity are also rare. Whatever deeds of prowess are mentioned are similar to those of other deities, and are colourless or subordinate. Like other deities, under the name Indu or Soma he too is invited to come to the sacrifice, sit on the darbha seat and accept the offerings. Throughout the ninth Maṇḍala the matter in hand is the Soma juice: pressing out the juice with stones, filtering it through a woollen sieve into wooden vessels, offering it to the deities as a drink through Agni (1-94-14; 5-51-1; 8-43-11 etc.), or its being drunk by the priests, and so on.

The Soma juice is mixed in three ways (trāśiraḥ, 5-27-5): mixed with milk (gavāśir), mixed with curds (dadhyāśir) and mixed with barley (yavāśir). This mixing is called "putting on a garment" (vastra, vāsaḥ, atka); "nirṇik" (shining garment, 9-14-5) is also said. This word is also used of the sieve (9-70-7). For this reason Soma is described as beautiful (9-34-4; etc.) and as abundantly adorned with ornaments (9-81-2). Rarely a mixing with ghee (9-82-2) or with water is also mentioned; but the word āśir is not used for these.

In the sacrifices āpyāyana (soaking again in water the half-pressed soma plants) is a rite (Mai. Saṃ. 4-5-5). In the Ṛgveda this root (āpyā) is used in connection with Soma, but here it is used to indicate that Soma is equal to the moon. Only in one place (9-31-4) might this sacrificial rite be indicated. It is said that the Soma juice swells like a river or the sea (9-64-8, 9-107-12).

Soma is pressed three times a day. The Ṛbhu deities are invoked to the evening pressing (4-33-11 etc.), Indra alone (4-36-7) to the midday pressing (3-21-1 and 2; 8-37-1), and Indra, to drink first, to the morning pressing (10-112-1).

[Note: in kn.md two colons between references (after "3-21-1 and 2" on p. 391 and after "9-77-1" on p. 392) were changed to semicolons so that the check does not read them as one reference.]

p. 392

[Running head, p. 392: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 40.]

The Soma juice has an inexpressible power which ordinary food or drink does not have. By this power it invigorates men, or whoever drinks it, and makes them accomplish even deeds that are impossible for men. For that reason it is a divine drink, equal to nectar, and gives occasion to the idea that it is nectar itself. It would not be an exaggeration to say that those who drink it become immortal. It is the intoxicating drink dear to the deities (9-85-2) and the bestower of immortality (1-84-4); this juice, pressed by men and mixed with milk, is drunk by all the deities (9-109-15); by it they are quickly exhilarated (8-2-18) and, having drunk, become glad (8-58-11). Soma is eternal (1-43-9; 8-88-12; 9-3-1 etc.); the deities drank it to obtain immortality (9-106-8). He (the deity Soma) bestows immortality on the deities (1-91-6; 9-108-3) and on men (1-91-1; 8-48-3). In the imperishable world, the seat of everlasting radiance and glory, the dwelling-place of Vaivasvata, he makes his worshipper immortal and places him there (9-113-7 and 8).

By drinking the Soma juice a man's enthusiasm increases. But the Soma juice is chiefly offered to the deities; therefore the joy and enthusiasm arising from Soma arise in the deities. The effect of the intoxication arising from Soma falls mostly on Indra. It helps Indra to subdue the hostile powers in the atmosphere. It is said many times that the special power and ability needed to fight Vṛtra came from the Soma juice (8-81-17 etc.). In the intoxication produced by the Soma juice Indra defeats all enemies (9-1-10), and no one can face in battle Indra who has drunk Soma (6-47-1). Soma is the very self of Indra (9-85-3); the auspicious Mitra (10-25-9) increases Indra's might (9-76-2) and helps in the slaying of Vṛtra (9-61-22). Accompanied by Soma, Indra made the waters flow for men and slew the serpent (4-28-1). Hence sometimes Soma itself is called Indra's thunderbolt (9-72-7; 9-77-1; 9-111-3). This Soma juice, belonging to Indra, becomes the thunderbolt that wins a thousand victories (9-47-3). The intoxicant that can destroy hundreds of strongholds is the Soma juice (9-48-2), and it is the plant that slays Vṛtra and intoxicates (6-17-11). In this way the deity Soma himself, like Indra, is called the slayer of Vṛtra and the breaker of strongholds (9-88-4). Indra's own epithet "Vṛtrahā" is applied to Soma five or six times.

Because it is the most important plant, the Soma plant is called the lord of all plants (9-114-2), the king (9-97-18 and 19), the lord of the forest (vanaspati, 1-91-6; 9-12-7) and of all plants

[The text of p. 392 breaks off here, in mid-sentence, as supplied; it continues on p. 393.]

p. 393

[Running head, p. 393: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 393.]

and it is also said to be the fundamental (root) one (1-91-22). In the Brāhmaṇas all trees are named saumya (सौम्य (saumya), connected with Soma, Śa. Brā. 12-1-1-2). Moreover, like other principal deities, Soma too has the name "king". He is the king of the rivers (9-89-2) and of the whole world (9-97-58); the king or father of the deities (9-86-10; 9-87-2; 9-109-4); the king of the divine men (9-97-24) and of the Brāhmaṇas (Vā. Saṃ. 9-40; Tai. Saṃ. 1-8-10; Mai. Saṃ. 2-6-9). That he is a deity has been said many times; only in one place (9-3-6 and 7) is he described as a deity who is suta (pressed out, squeezed) for the deities.

In later literature "Soma" is the name of the moon. When the deities have drunk him and he has waned, the sun makes him full again. In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (5-10-1) it is said that the moon is Soma, that he is the food of the deities, and that they drink him up. In the Brāhmaṇas themselves the identity of moon and Soma is a common matter: King Soma is the food of the deities and he is the moon (Śa. Brā. 1-6-4-5). That plant useful in yoga, or its juice, indicates the moon-deity (Kau. Brā. 7-10; 4-4). The opinion of the Brāhmaṇas is that the moon wanes day by day because the Pitṛs and the deities consume him, who is of the nature of nectar. In the Yajurveda it is said that the daughters of Prajāpati are the wives of the moon and that they are the cluster of stars. In the Atharvaveda (Ā. Va. 7-81-3 and 4; 11-6-7 etc.) wherever "Soma" occurs the meaning is generally the moon. Among the passages that state the identity of moon and Soma, the 85th sūkta of the tenth Maṇḍala (10-85), describing the marriage of Soma and Sūryā [printed "Sūraiya", sic], is the chief. Here Soma is in the lap of the stars. It is said that no one eats the Soma known to the priests, and that there is a difference between this Soma and that which they have to press. The secret of this is known only to the Brāhmaṇas. There are descriptions of Soma as heavenly, radiant, dispelling darkness and so on; moreover it has the name "Indu" (इंदु (iṃdu)) (6-44-21). It is compared to the moon reflected in the water in vessels (8-71-8; compare 1-105-1). The Soma described as drapsa (द्रप्प (drappa), a drop, a bead) and going to the sea (10-123-8) must also be the moon.

In the opinion of some, Soma means the moon and nothing but the moon, not another deity. The whole ninth Maṇḍala praises this moon [as printed]; wherever this word occurs in the Ṛgveda it indicates either the Soma creeper or the moon, these two only. They argue that the juice that comes from that creeper is nectar, that the moon is the support of that nectar, that the moon is a more important deity than the sun, and that after him comes Indra. Others, again, say that the above opinion has insufficient support in the Ṛgveda [printed "Ṛgvada", sic] or none at all. However much support the identity of moon and Soma may find in later works, in the Ṛgveda [printed "Ṛgvada", sic], among the hundreds of ṛks addressed to the deity Soma, it is only rarely, here and there, that it is hinted at, and nowhere is it stated clearly.

p. 394

[Running head, p. 394: Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā, Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 40.]

Besides, none of the commentators has said that there is any basis for this point in the Veda.

Pūṣā-Pūṣan. Of the deity called Pūṣan too we shall give a detailed account here. Since this deity is famous as one who searches for lost things and brings them back, in many ṛks there is a description of this kind. For this word (पूषा (pūṣā)) Yāska has given the etymology—

Quotation from the Nirukta, in Sanskrit:

पूषा । अथ यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत्पूषा भवति ॥

pūṣā | atha yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tatpūṣā bhavati ‖

(Ni. 12-16)

That is, because he nourishes with rays or beams, this deity has the name Pūṣā. From this etymology of the word, when this deity is described, epithets such as "endowed with brilliance", "luminous", "radiant" are used. From this very description they say that Pūṣan is one of the twelve Ādityas and a special form of the sun.

Quotation from the Bṛhaddevatā, in Sanskrit:

पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः । तेनैनमस्तौत्पूषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पंचभिः ॥

puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ | tenainamastautpūṣeti bharadvājastu paṃcabhiḥ ‖

(Bṛ. De. 2-63)

That is: since he destroys the darkness and nourishes the earth so that it grows, the name Pūṣan suits this deity. The seer Bharadvāja praised this deity with five sūktas, so it is stated in the work called Bṛhaddevatā.

Pūṣan sees all living beings clearly, at one time (3-62-9). Like the sun he too is the lord of all things that move and do not move (1-115-1; 7-60-2). All living beings are known to him and he looks upon all living beings. Pūṣan was born on the way of far heaven and earth. His vehicle is the ram (aja); because he knows the paths, they call him the protector of the ways. He is the protector of every road (6-49-8). He is prayed to remove the trouble that may come on the road (6-54-9) and to make the road auspicious (10-59-7). On the highway and in the forest he is the one who shows the way. Therefore it is said that everyone setting out on a journey should travel invoking Pūṣan, the lord of the roads, and reciting the 53rd sūkta of the sixth Maṇḍala (6-53). It is said that all who have lost their way should take refuge in Pūṣan alone (Ā. Gṛ. 3-6-8; Sāṃ. Śrau. 3-4-9). It is his work to follow the cattle and protect them (6-54-5, 6, 10 and 6-58-2), to guard them so that they do not fall into a pit and get hurt, and to drive them home so that no harm befalls

p. 395

[Running head, p. 395: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6; Ṛgvedasaṃhitā 395.]

them, and to bring back the cattle that have strayed (6-54-7, 10), and so on.

Pūṣan is used in the dual number with Soma (2-40) and Indra (6-57), the two; once (6-55-5) he is called Indra's brother. Apart from these two, he is most often addressed together with Bhaga (1-90-4; 4-30-24; 5-41-4; 5-46-2; 10-125-2; compare Śa. Brā. 11-4-3-3; Kā. Śrau. Sū. 5-13-1), and with Viṣṇu (1-90-5; 5-46-3; 6-21-9; 7-44-1; 10-66.5, as printed). In all these mantras Pūṣan and another deity are spoken of as exactly equal. With other deities too there is a use here and there.

From the passages quoted so far it does not appear that Pūṣan is an element of nature. But many passages show that he is connected with the sun. Yāska too (Ni. 7-9) calls him the Āditya who protects all things. His chief functions are: setting the paths in order and bringing the dead to the place where the righteous are. By the first quality he is a guide and the protector of animals; that is, one may say that he is the one who improves the condition of the people.

This word Pūṣan is formed from the root पुष् (puṣ) (to produce nourishment). This quality is clear both from his epithets (विश्ववेदाः (viśvavedāḥ) अनष्टवेदाः (anaṣṭavedāḥ), पुरूवसु (purūvasu), पुष्टिंभर (puṣṭiṃbhara)) and from the prayers for wealth (6-48-15; etc.). He is the lord of immense wealth, of a stream and a heap of riches (6-55-2 and 3). But the wealth obtained from Pūṣan is not connected with rain, as is the wealth obtained from Indra, Parjanya, the Maruts and others; it is connected with radiance [light]. In this world he is a fearless refuge for men and cattle; in the other world he shows the way to blissful regions. By these the condition of the people improves and the people become happy. That is, Pūṣan may be called the part of the sun which is beneficent to the people.

Ṛk 1

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सोमा॑पूषणा॒ जन॑ना रयी॒णां जन॑ना दि॒वो जन॑ना पृथि॒व्याः । जा॒त् विश्व॑स्य॒ भुव॑नस्य गो॒पौ दे॒वा अ॑कृण्वन्न॒मृत॑स्य॒ नाभिं॑ ॥ १ ॥

The page 393 text continues the sentence ending "and of all plants" of p. 392. No other changes.]

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सोमापूषणा । जनना । रयाणां । जनना । दिवः । जनना । पृथिव्याः । जात् । विश्वस्य । भुवनस्य । गोपौ । देवाः । अकृण्वन् । अमृतस्य । नाभिं ॥ १ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

सोमापूषणा हे सोमापूषणौ युवां रयीणां धनानां जनना जनयितारौ दिवो द्युलोकस्यापि जनना जनयितारौ पृथिव्याः प्रथितायाश्च जनयितारौ भवथः । किंच जात् जातमात्रावेव युवां विश्वस्य भुवनस्य कृत्सस्य जगतो गोपौ गोप्तारौ देवा अमृतस्यामरणस्य नाभिं हेतुमकृण्वन् । अकार्षुः ॥

Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya: Soma and Pūṣan are the begetters of wealth, of heaven and of earth; as soon as born they are the guardians of the whole world, and the gods made them the source of immortality.

(Note: in kn.md the line break hyphen in the bhāṣya (ಜನ-/ಯಿತಾರೌ) was joined inside the block. No other change.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

सोमापूषणा (somāpūṣaṇā)—O Soma and Pūṣan deities (both of you together). रयीणां (rayīṇāṃ)—of wealth. जनना (jananā)—you are the producers. दिवः (divaḥ)—of the heavenly world. जनना (jananā)—you are the makers. पृथिव्याः (pṛthivyāḥ)—of the earth. जनना (jananā)—you are the creators. जात् (jāt)—as soon as born. विश्वस्य भुवनस्य (viśvasya bhuvanasya)—of the whole world. गोपौ (gopau)—you, the protectors. देवाः (devāḥ)—the gods. अमृतस्य (amṛtasya)—of immortality. नाभिं (nābhiṃ)—as the cause. अकृण्वन् (akṛṇvan)—made.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma and Pūṣan deities, you two are the makers of wealth, of the heavenly world and of the earth. As soon as you were born you became the protectors of the whole world, and the gods made you the cause of immortality.

Printed English translation

Soma and Pushan, you two are the generators of riches, the generators of heaven, the generators of earth ; as soon as born you are the guardians of the whole world : the gods have made you the source of immortality.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

The meaning of this Ṛk is clear. O deities Soma and Pūṣan, you two are the lords of wealth, that is, you produce wealth (wealth in cattle). The heavenly world, that is, heaven, and the earth you yourselves have produced; heaven and earth came into being from you.

p. 397

Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 8, Varga 6] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 397 (as supplied).

Moreover, as soon as you were born, that is, from birth, you are the protectors of the entire world. Therefore the gods made you the chief cause of the deathless state, or made you yourselves the cause of the deathless state; that is, it is through you that all attained the state of immortality (freedom from death): this is the chief meaning.

अमृतस्य (amṛtasya)—mṛta means dying; amṛta is the state of not having that, long life. There is a tradition that the gods do not undergo death and live for ever. Amṛta has many meanings: the Soma juice, water, the best food of the gods.

Ṛk 2

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

(Note: kn.md had a stray line "1 ಸಂಹಿತಾಶಾಲೆ", a garbled label for the Saṃhitā, replaced by the standard label, the stray "1" is kept as an italic note in kn.md; the Saṃhitā lines, supplied as prose, were made a > block.)

इ॒मौ दे॒वौ जाय॑मानौ जुषंते॒मौ तमां॑सि गूहता॒मजु॑ष्टा । आ॒भ्यामिंद्रः॑ प॒क्वमा॒मास्वं॒तः सो॑मापू॒षभ्यां॑ जनदु॒स्रिया॑सु ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

(Note: the supplied label "೧ ಜಪಮಾಲೆ ೧" is garbled (stray numerals); replaced by the standard label, kept as an italic note in kn.md. The Pada's ಇಮ್, ದೇವ್, ಜಾಯಮಾನ್, ಇಮ್ differ from the Saṃhitā's ಇಮೌ, ದೇವೌ, ಜಾಯಮಾನೌ, ಇಮೌ, as supplied, not corrected.)

इम् । देव् । जायमान् । जुषंत । इम् । तमांसि । गूहतां । अजुष्टा । अभ्यां । इंद्रः । पक्वं । आमासु । अंतरिति । सोमापूषभ्यां । जनत् । उस्रियासु ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

(Note: the supplied label "॥ ರಾಮಚಂದ್ರಾಯನಂ ॥" is garbled; replaced by the standard label and kept as an italic note in kn.md. Hyphenated line breaks joined inside the block.)

इमौ सोमापूषण् देवौ द्योतमानौ जायमानावुत्पन्नमात्रावेव जुषंत । सर्वे देवा अजुषंत । सेवितवंत इति यावत् । किंच इमौ सोमापूषणावजुष्टासेव्यानि तमांसि सर्वस्य गूहतां । नाशयतः । किंच अभ्यामेताभ्यां सोमापूषभ्यां सहेंद्र आमासु तरुणीषूस्रियासु गोष्टंतर्मध्य ऊधःप्रदेशे पक्वं परिपक्वं पयो जनत् । जनयति ॥

Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya: These two deities, as soon as born, are served by all the gods; they destroy the unwelcome darkness; with them Indra produces ripe milk in the udders of young cows.

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(Note: the supplied label "॥ ಪ್ರತಿದರ್ಥ ॥" is garbled; replaced by the standard label and kept as an italic note in kn.md.)

इमौ देवौ (imau devau)—these two divine beings Soma and Pūṣan. जायमानौ (jāyamānau)—as soon as born. जुषंत (juṣaṃta)—(all the gods) worship. इमौ (imau)—these two. अजुष्टा (ajuṣṭā)—not fit to be served, तमांसि (tamāṃsi)—the darknesses. गूहतां (gūhatāṃ)—they destroy. अभ्यां (abhyāṃ) (its gloss follows on p. 398)

p. 398

Running head: [398] Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [Maṃ. 2, A. 4, Sū. 40] (as supplied).

अभ्यां सोमापूषभ्यां (abhyāṃ somāpūṣabhyāṃ)—with the help of these Soma and Pūṣan. इंद्रः (iṃdraḥ)—Indra. आमासु (āmāsu)—in those in youth. उस्रियासु (usriyāsu)—of the cows. अंतः (aṃtaḥ)—in the udder regions. पक्वं (pakvaṃ)—ripe milk. जनत् (janat)—produced.

(Note: the Pratipadārtha entry अभ्यां सोमापूषभ्यां (abhyāṃ somāpūṣabhyāṃ) is split by the page break; the words are joined here.)

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These two divine beings Soma and Pūṣan: as soon as they are born all the gods worship them. They destroy the darknesses not fit to be served (that is, wanted by nobody). With the help of these Soma and Pūṣan deities Indra produced ripe milk in the udders of cows in their youth.

Printed English translation

(The gods) propitiate these two divinities at the moment of their birth, for they drive away the disagreeable glooms : with these two, Soma and Pushan, Indra generates the mature (milk) in the immature heifers.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पक्वं (pakvaṃ)—परिपक्वं पयः । (paripakvaṃ payaḥ |) Milk that is ready so as to be fit for taking. Yāska explains the word pakva as पक्वमौषधं (pakvamauṣadhaṃ) (Ni. 5-28), and

पक्वं-उदकदानं मेघं । बहूनां मेघानां मध्यॆ यः पक्वो मेघः उदकदाने समर्थः तं

pakvaṃ-udakadānaṃ meghaṃ | bahūnāṃ meghānāṃ madhyè yaḥ pakvo meghaḥ udakadāne samarthaḥ taṃ

(Ni. 6-34)

as its explanation. That is, fruits or herbs in trees such as vanaspati, filled with juices and ready for use; or, if taken as referring to the cloud, the cloud that has gathered water in itself and is able to shower rain. In whatever context the word pakva is used, its meaning may be said to be: a thing fit and ready for use. Since in the present Ṛk the words उस्रियासु अंतः (usriyāsu aṃtaḥ) are used, the thing filled in the udders of cows and ready for use is payas, milk: this is the sense.

अमासु (amāsu)—अपक्वासु । (apakvāsu |) Not yet fully matured, that is, not aged, in the youthful state, having newly calved: this is the meaning.

उस्रियासु (usriyāsu)—The word usriyā is read among the names of the cow (Ni. 3-9), and there is also an explanation

उस्रियायाः । उस्रियेति गोनाम ! उस्राविणोऽस्यां भोगाः । उस्रेति च

usriyāyāḥ | usriyeti gonāma ! usrāviṇo 'syāṃ bhogāḥ | usreti ca

(Ni. 4-19)

That is, because in her (the cow) the juice (milk), the means of enjoyment, flows (is milked), the cow is called usriyā or usrā. Among those, a cow in youth, that is, fit to give milk, is meant.

p. 399

(Editorial note: in the supplied text the Sanskrit quotations on this page ran on as prose; they have been set as > blocks in the Kannada file, with the references on their own lines, and a hyphenated line break inside the bhāṣya quotation has been joined.)

आभ्यां सोमापूषभ्यां इंद्रः आमासु उस्रियासु अंतः पक्वं जनत्—एताभ्यां सोमापूषभ्यां सह इंद्रः तरुणेषु गोषु मध्यॆ ऊधः प्रदेशे परिपक्वं जनयति ।

ābhyāṃ somāpūṣabhyāṃ iṃdraḥ āmāsu usriyāsu aṃtaḥ pakvaṃ janat—etābhyāṃ somāpūṣabhyāṃ saha iṃdraḥ taruṇeṣu goṣu madhyè ūdhaḥ pradeśe paripakvaṃ janayati |

Along with these deities Soma and Pūṣan, Indra fills the udders of cows in their youth with ripe milk, that is, milk fit for use. This act of Indra is described in the Ṛks

आमासु पक्वमैरय आ सूर्यं रोहयो दिवि ।

āmāsu pakvamairaya ā sūryaṃ rohayo divi |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-89-7)

आमासु चिद्दधिषे पक्वमंतः पयः कृष्णासु रुशद्रोहिणेषु ।

āmāsu ciddadhiṣe pakvamaṃtaḥ payaḥ kṛṣṇāsu ruśadrohiṇeṣu |

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-62-9)

In the second example quoted above it is described that Indra fills even black or red cows with white milk: whatever the colour of the cow, its milk is white only; this is described as arising from Indra's surpassing power. About the phrase आ सूर्यं रोहयो दिवि (ā sūryaṃ rohayo divi) in the first example, the commentator gives an ancient story:

पूर्वं पणयो नामासुरा अंगिरसां गा आपहृत्यांधकारावृते कस्मिंश्चित्पर्वते ताः स्थापितवंतः । ततोऽज्जिरस इंद्रं स्तुत्वा गाः पुनरस्मभ्यमाहरेति तैरुक्त इंद्रो गवां स्थानं तमसावृतं दृष्ट्वा तत्र गोदर्शनाय द्युलोके सर्वप्रकाशकं सूर्यमारोहितवान् स्थापितवान् ॥

pūrvaṃ paṇayo nāmāsurā aṃgirasāṃ gā āpahṛtyāṃdhakārāvṛte kasmiṃścitparvate tāḥ sthāpitavaṃtaḥ | tato 'jjirasa iṃdraṃ stutvā gāḥ punarasmabhyamāhareti tairukta iṃdro gavāṃ sthānaṃ tamasāvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra godarśanāya dyuloke sarvaprakāśakaṃ sūryamārohitavān sthāpitavān ‖

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-89-7, Sā. Bhā.)

In former times the asuras called Paṇis stole the cows of the Aṅgirases and kept them in a cave full of dense darkness in a certain mountain. The Aṅgiras sages then praised and pleased Indra and prayed that he bring back their cows. Indra, seeing that the place of the cows was very dark and that searching was impossible, and knowing that light was necessary to find the cows, set in the sky the sun that illumines everything with its radiance. By the light of that sun it became possible to search out and bring the cows: this is the ancient story. In the present Ṛk also, the statement इमौ तमांसि गूहतामजुष्टॆ (imau tamāṃsi gūhatāmajuṣṭè) (the darkness that had spread here was destroyed by Soma and Pūṣan), although it concerns Soma and Pūṣan, may be supposed to support that same matter of Indra's setting the sun in the sky to find the cows.

p. 400

Ṛk 3

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

सोमा॑पूषणा॒ रज॑सो वि॒मानं॑ स॒प्तच॑क्रं॒ रथ॒मवि॑श्वमिन्वं । वि॒षू॒वृतं॒ मन॑सा यु॒ज्यमा॑नं॒ तं जि॑न्वथो वृषणा॒ पंच॑रश्मिं ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

सोमापूषणा । रजसः । विमानं । सप्तचक्रं । रथं । अविश्वमिन्वं । विषुवृतं । मनसा । युज्यमानं । तं । जिन्वथः । वृषणा । पंचरश्मिं ॥ ३ ॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

वृषणा वृषणौ कामानां वर्षितारौ सोमपूषणा हे सोमपोषणा रजसो लोकस्य । लोका रजांस्युच्यंत इति यास्कः । विमानं परिच्छेदकं । सर्वमानमित्यर्थः । सप्तचक्रं सप्तर्तुचक्रं । त्रयोदशो मासः सप्तम ऋतुः । अस्ति त्रयोदशो मास इति श्रुतेः । अविश्वमिन्वं विश्वस्यापरिच्छेद्यं विषुवृतं विश्वक् सर्वत्र परिवर्तमानं पंचरश्मिं पंचर्तुरश्मिं । हेमंतशिशिरयोः समासेनर्तवः पंच । तथा च श्रूयते । द्वादश मासाः पंचर्तवो हेमंतशिशिरयोः समासेन । ऐ. ब्रा. १-१ । इति । मनसा युज्यमानं मनोमात्रेण युज्यमानं । तं प्रसिद्धं रथं जिन्वथः । आस्मान्प्रति प्रेरयथः ॥

Gist: Soma and Pūṣan, showerers of desires, are asked to send to us the seven-wheeled (seven-season) chariot that measures the world and is yoked by the mind; Sāyaṇa takes the seven as the seasons including the thirteenth month and the five reins as five seasons (Hemanta and Śiśira counted together), citing the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (as printed, 1-1).

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

वृषणा (vṛṣaṇā)—showerers of desires. सोमापूषणा (somāpūṣaṇā)—O Soma and Pūṣan deities. रजसः (rajasaḥ)—of the world. विमानं (vimānaṃ)—that which divides and measures. सप्तचक्रं (saptacakraṃ)—having seven wheels in the form of seasons. अविश्वमिन्वं (aviśvaminvaṃ)—not distinct from the universe. विषुवृतं (viṣuvṛtaṃ)—pervading everywhere. पंचरश्मिं (paṃcaraśmiṃ)—having five reins (the Kannada print reads कडिवाणगुळुळ्ळदू (kaḍivāṇaguḷuḷḷadū) for "having reins", apparently a misprint). मनसा (manasā)—by the mind alone. युज्यमानं (yujyamānaṃ)—to be yoked and made ready. तं (taṃ)—that well-known. रथं (rathaṃ)—chariot. जिन्वधः (jinvadhaḥ) (as printed; the bhāṣya and Pada read जिन्वथः (jinvathaḥ))—urge towards us.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma and Pūṣan, showerers of desires: the chariot that divides and measures the world, has seven wheels in the form of seasons, has no state distinct from the universe, is pervading everywhere, has five reins, is to be yoked and made ready by the mind alone, and is well known: urge it towards us.

p. 401

Printed English translation

Soma and Pushan, showeres [sic] (of benifits [sic]), direct towards us the seven-wheeled car, the measure of the spheres, undistinguishable from the universe, everywhere existing, (guided) by five reins, and to be harnessed by the mind.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

In this Ṛk the sage prays to Soma and Pūṣan: send towards us the chariot that has seven wheels, has the reins of five (horses), is able to travel everywhere, and is to be yoked and made ready by mere resolve of the mind. The chariot here is the year (saṃvatsara). The six seasons of the year together with the intercalary thirteenth month make seven seasons, the seven wheels. The five seasons: since there is a custom of calling the last two of the six seasons together by the name हेमंतशिशिरौ (hemaṃtaśiśirau), the total is stated here as five seasons. Those five seasons are the reins of the five horses. Such a chariot, the year, is all-pervading, that is, time contains everything; there is nothing distinct from it. The prayer is uttered here: come to us with such a chariot. It is said in the introduction to this sūkta that the deity Pūṣan is of the nature of Āditya (the sun). Since the divisions of time, year, seasons, months, days and so on, arise from the course of the sun, this is described here as the chariot of Soma and Pūṣan and is invoked.

वृषणा सोमापूषणा रजसः विमानं (vṛṣaṇā somāpūṣaṇā rajasaḥ vimānaṃ)—O Soma and Pūṣan, who pour out desired things, your (chariot) divides and measures the world. Here रजसः (rajasaḥ) means लोकस्य (lokasya); according to Yāska's explanation लोकाः रजांस्युच्यंते (lokāḥ rajāṃsyucyaṃte) (Ni. 4-19), the word rajas means world. To divide and measure the world means: as a stretch of land is measured by the going of a chariot, so by the chariot of time the extent of the worlds, or the extent of time, is divided. The sense is that by the course of Soma and Pūṣan, or of Āditya (the going of the chariot), the divisions of year, season, month, fortnight and day come about. This is what is described here by the words लोकस्य विमानं (lokasya vimānaṃ).

सप्तचक्रं रथं अविश्वमिन्वं विषूवृतं (saptacakraṃ rathaṃ aviśvaminvaṃ viṣūvṛtaṃ)—Here the seven wheels are the seven seasons. Ordinarily there are six seasons in a year, one season to every two months. When an intercalary month occurs there are thirteen months in the year. That thirteenth month alone, as one (text breaks off at the end of this page)

Stray line kept from the supplied text (a lone number at the end of the window, not part of the sense): 26

p. 402

taken as a season, there are seven seasons in all. On the matter of there being thirteen months in a year, the commentator has also cited the Śruti text अस्ति त्रयोदशो मास इत्याहुः (asti trayodaśo māsa ityāhuḥ) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-3-4). These seasons proceed one after another in a cyclic order. When all seven seasons have come once and ended, the first season comes again. Therefore these seven seasons are compared to the seven wheels of a chariot that is always revolving. For the word अविश्वमिन्वं (aviśvaminvaṃ) the meaning is विश्वस्यापरिच्छेद्यं (viśvasyāparicchedyaṃ), that is, not distinct from the universe. The sense is: since everything, that is, all places and times, is contained in the universe, there is no thing distinct from (different from) the universe; following this doctrine the chariot called time is described here as non-different from the universe [the print reads विश्वदिंब (viśvadiṃba) for "from the universe", apparently a misprint]. And for the word विषूवृतं (viṣūvṛtaṃ) — विश्वक् सर्वत्र परिवर्तमानं (viśvak sarvatra parivartamānaṃ) — following the same doctrine, it is described here that, because time pervades everything and there is nothing outside time and place, the chariot called time is pervading everywhere.

पंचरश्मिं (paṃcaraśmiṃ)—पंचर्तुरश्मिं । हेमंतशिशिरयोः समासेन ऋतवः पंच । (paṃcarturaśmiṃ | hemaṃtaśiśirayoḥ samāsena ṛtavaḥ paṃca |) Although there are six seasons in the year, one season to every two months, it is the custom to take the last two seasons, that is, Hemanta and Śiśira, as one season and to speak of them by the single word हेमंतशिशिरौ (hemaṃtaśiśirau); therefore it is also the custom to speak of five seasons. This matter is stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa sentence द्वादशमासाः पंचर्तवो हेमंतशिशिरयोः समासेन (dvādaśamāsāḥ paṃcartavo hemaṃtaśiśirayoḥ samāsena) (Ai. Brā. 1-1), and the commentator has cited this Śruti proof. These five seasons are the five rays (ropes), that is, the five reins (bridles) of the horses, as explained here.

मनसा युज्यमानं तं रथं जिन्वथः (manasā yujyamānaṃ taṃ rathaṃ jinvathaḥ)—मनोमात्रेण युज्यमानं प्रसिद्धं रथं प्रेरयथः । (manomātreṇa yujyamānaṃ prasiddhaṃ rathaṃ prerayathaḥ |) For yoking this chariot the help of hands and other limbs is not needed; by the mere resolve of the mind the chariot is yoked and made ready. The sage prays to Soma and Pūṣan: "Impel towards us such a chariot."

Ṛk 4

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

दि॒व्य१॒ं॑न्यः सद॑नं च॒क्र उ॒च्चा पृ॑थि॒व्याम॒न्यो अध्यं॒तरि॑क्षे । ताव॒स्मभ्यं॑ पुरु॒वारं॑ पुरु॒क्षुं रा॒यस्पोषं॒ वि ष्य॑तां॒ नाभि॑म॒स्मे॥

divyaṃnyaḥ sadanaṃ cakra uccā pṛthivyāmanyo adhyaṃtarikṣe | tāvasmabhyaṃ puruvāraṃ purukṣuṃ rāyaspoṣaṃ vi ṣyatāṃ nābhimasme‖

p. 403

॥ पदपाठः ॥

दिवि । अन्यः । सदनं । चक्रे । उच्चा । पृथिव्यां । अन्यः । अधि । अंतरिक्षे । ता । अस्मभ्यं । पुरुऽवारं । पुरुऽक्षुं । रायः । पोषं । वि । स्यतां । नाभिं । अस्मे-इति ॥ ४ ॥

divi | anyaḥ | sadanaṃ | cakre | uccā | pṛthivyāṃ | anyaḥ | adhi | aṃtarikṣe | tā | asmabhyaṃ | puru 'vāraṃ | puru 'kṣuṃ | rāyaḥ | poṣaṃ | vi | syatāṃ | nābhiṃ | asme-iti ‖ 4 ‖

(The Saṃhitā reads वि ष्यतां (vi ṣyatāṃ) where the Pada reads वि । स्यतां (vi | syatāṃ), as printed.)

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

अन्यस्तयोरेकः पूषोच्चा उच्चैरुच्छ्रिते दिवि द्युलोके सदनं स्थानं चक्रे । चकार । अन्नोऽपरः सोमः पृथिव्यामोषधिरूपेण अध्यंतरिक्षेऽंतरिक्षे च चंद्ररूपेण सदनं चक्रे। तौ सोमापूषणौ युवां पुरुवारं बहुभिर्वर्णीयं पुरुक्षुं बहुकीर्तिं रायस्पोषं धनस्य पुष्टिं । पश्वात्मकं धनमित्यर्थः । तथा च ब्राह्मणं पशवो वै रायस्पोष इति । अस्मे अस्माकं नाभिं विश्वस्य भोगस्य हेतुभूतमस्मभ्यं भविष्यतां । विमुंचतां । प्रयच्छतामित्यर्थः ॥

anyastayorekaḥ pūṣoccā uccairucchrite divi dyuloke sadanaṃ sthānaṃ cakre | cakāra | anno 'paraḥ somaḥ pṛthivyāmoṣadhirūpeṇa adhyaṃtarikṣe 'ṃtarikṣe ca caṃdrarūpeṇa sadanaṃ cakre| tau somāpūṣaṇau yuvāṃ puruvāraṃ bahubhirvarṇīyaṃ purukṣuṃ bahukīrtiṃ rāyaspoṣaṃ dhanasya puṣṭiṃ | paśvātmakaṃ dhanamityarthaḥ | tathā ca brāhmaṇaṃ paśavo vai rāyaspoṣa iti | asme asmākaṃ nābhiṃ viśvasya bhogasya hetubhūtamasmabhyaṃ bhaviṣyatāṃ | vimuṃcatāṃ | prayacchatāmityarthaḥ ‖

Gist: Of the two, Pūṣan has made his seat in high heaven; Soma, as the plant on earth and as the moon in the sky; may they give us wealth of cattle, the source of all enjoyment. (The print reads अन्नोऽपरः (anno 'paraḥ) in the bhāṣya; kept as supplied.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

ಅನ್ಯಃ—(of Soma and Pūṣan) the one, the deity Pūṣan. ಉಚ್ಚಾ—very lofty. ದಿವಿ—in the heavenly world. ಸದನಂ—abode. ಚಕ್ರೇ—has made. ಅನ್ಯಃ—the other, Soma. ಪೃಥಿವ್ಯಾಂ—on the earth (in the form of the plant). ಅಧ್ಯಂತರಿಕ್ಷೇ—and in the atmosphere (in the form of the moon) has made an abode. ತೌ—those two, Soma and Pūṣan. ಅಸ್ಮೇ—our. ನಾಭಿಂ—that which is the cause (of all enjoyments). ಪುರುವಾರಂ—desired by many. ಪುರುಕ್ಷುಂ—possessing much fame. ರಾಯಸ್ಪೋಷಂ—the increase of wealth, which consists of cattle. ಅಸ್ಮಭ್ಯಂ—to us. ವಿ ಷ್ಯತಾಂ—may they provide.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Of Soma and Pūṣan, the one, the deity Pūṣan, has made his abode in the very lofty heavenly world. The other, Soma, has made his abode on the earth in the form of the plant and in the atmosphere in the form of the moon. May those two, Soma and Pūṣan, provide us with the increase of wealth, which consists of cattle, which is the cause of all our enjoyments, desired by many and possessing much fame.

Printed English translation

One of them, (Pushan) has made his dwelling above in heaven ; the other, (soma), upon earth, and in the firmament : may they both grant

p. 404

us much-desired and much-commended abundant wealth of cattle, the source to us (of enjoyments.)

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

पुरुवारं (puruvāraṃ)— बहुभिर्वर्णीयं । (bahubhirvarṇīyaṃ |) Desired by many; needed by everyone.

पुरुक्षुं (purukṣuṃ)—बहुकीर्तिं (bahukīrtiṃ)—much fame. Since the word क्षु (kṣu) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9), the meaning "much food" can also be given.

धनस्य पुष्टिं । पश्वात्मकं धनमित्यर्थः । (dhanasya puṣṭiṃ | paśvātmakaṃ dhanamityarthaḥ |) (on रायस्पोषं (rāyaspoṣaṃ)): the increase of wealth, that is, abundance of wealth. Indicating that it may also be said to mean wealth in cattle, wealth in the form of cattle, the commentator cites in support the Śruti sentence पशवो वै रायस्पोषः (paśavo vai rāyaspoṣaḥ) (Tai. Saṃ. 5-4-6-2). Since in the present Ṛk रायः पोषः (rāyaḥ poṣaḥ) are two separate words, the two words may be explained separately: रायः (rāyaḥ)—wealth, पोषः (poṣaḥ)—increase.

दिव्यः अन्यः उच्चा सदनं चक्रे (divyaḥ anyaḥ uccā sadanaṃ cakre)—तयोरेकः पूषा उच्छ्रिते द्युलोके स्थानं चकार । (tayorekaḥ pūṣā ucchrite dyuloke sthānaṃ cakāra |) Of the two called Soma and Pūṣan, Pūṣan has set up his place of residence in the heavenly world, the very lofty region.

अन्यः पृथिव्यां अधि अंतरिक्षे (anyaḥ pṛthivyāṃ adhi aṃtarikṣe)—अपरः सोमः पृथिव्यां ओषधिरूपेण अंतरिक्षे च चंद्ररूपेण सदनं चक्रे । (aparaḥ somaḥ pṛthivyāṃ oṣadhirūpeṇa aṃtarikṣe ca caṃdrarūpeṇa sadanaṃ cakre |) The other, the deity Soma, has set up his place of residence on the earth and in the atmosphere; the sense is that he is on the earth in the form of the plant, that is, of the soma creeper, and in the atmosphere in the form of the moon.

Here a point calls for consideration. That the deity Soma dwells in the atmosphere in the form of the moon gives room for difference of opinion. The word soma is nowhere in the Ṛgveda used in the sense of the moon. The word is used only in the senses of the soma creeper, the soma juice, or the deity who is the presiding spirit of the soma creeper. In the Yajurveda and in the Purāṇas and similar works it is customary to give the word soma, besides the meaning of soma juice, the meaning of the moon, and of Īśvara or Rudra (उमया सहितः सोमः (umayā sahitaḥ somaḥ)). For the Śruti sentence सोम ओषधीनामधिपतिः (soma oṣadhīnāmadhipatiḥ) it is proper to explain that the soma creeper is the lord or king of the plants and trees. In the Purāṇas and similar works the meaning that the moon is the lord of them is explained. In the Yajurveda:

सोमाभूयो भरेत्याहापरिमितानेव पशूवनरुंधे चंद्रमसि मम भोगाय भवेत्याह ।

somābhūyo bharetyāhāparimitāneva paśūvanaruṃdhe caṃdramasi mama bhogāya bhavetyāha |

(Kṛ. Saṃ. 6-1-4-8)

Note on the kn.md edits: the Yajurveda quotation at the end of p. 404 was moved into a > block with its reference on its own line; the hyphen line-breaks inside the Pada and bhāṣya blocks were joined (the Pada's अस्मे-इति (asme-iti) keeps the printed hyphen). The print's page 404 text breaks off here at the quotation; the translation of the sentence follows on the next page.

p. 405

In this sentence Soma is addressed as being in the form of the moon. In the sense of Rudra, too, for the word soma—

नमः सोमाय च रुद्राय च । (namaḥ somāya ca rudrāya ca |) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-5-8-1)

[The same line is repeated in the supplied text:] नमः सोमाय च रुद्राय च । (namaḥ somāya ca rudrāya ca |) (Tai. Saṃ. 4-5-8-1)

—many such sentences can be cited from the Yajurveda and the other Vedas. But in the Ṛgveda alone the word soma means the soma creeper or Soma, the deity presiding over it. In Ṛks such as या ओषधी सोमराज्ञीः (yā oṣadhī somarājñīḥ) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-97-18, 19) and ओषधयः सं वदंते सोमेन सह राज्ञा । (oṣadhayaḥ saṃ vadaṃte somena saha rājñā |) (10-98-22) too, it is stated quite clearly that the soma creeper, or Soma its presiding deity, is the king or lord of the plants and trees. Therefore to explain the word soma here as the moon, as is said in the Purāṇas and similar works, is not quite appropriate.

Besides this, the sentence दिव्यः अन्यः सदनं चक्रे उच्चा (divyaḥ anyaḥ sadanaṃ cakre uccā) can also be explained in another way. The commentator has said that the word अन्यः (anyaḥ) here means the deity Pūṣan, one of Soma and Pūṣan. But the word अन्यः (anyaḥ) can also be explained as the deity Soma, one of Soma and Pūṣan. In that case the sense can be stated that Soma, one of Soma and Pūṣan, has made his abode in the extremely lofty heavenly world. In support of this there are many Śruti sentences, such as तृतीयास्यामितो दिवि सोम आसीत् (tṛtīyāsyāmito divi soma āsīt) (Tai. Brā. 3-2-1-1) and तृतीयस्यामितो दिवि सोमस्तमाहर (tṛtīyasyāmito divi somastamāhara) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-1-6-1).

Next, the second sentence, पृथिव्यां अन्यः अधि अंतरिक्षे (pṛthivyāṃ anyaḥ adhi aṃtarikṣe), can be explained with reference to Pūṣan. This Pūṣan, being on the earth in the form of the deity Pūṣan, helps people by recovering lost things for them and by being a guide to those who have lost their way. Since Pūṣan is a portion of Āditya, that is the Sun, or is one of the twelve Ādityas, it is natural that this deity dwells in the atmosphere (in the Sun's place). Therefore this sentence can be explained as meaning that this deity Pūṣan has provided for himself a place both on the earth and in the atmosphere.

तौ अस्मे नाभिं पुरुवारं पुरुक्षुं रायः पोषं अस्मभ्यं वि ष्यतां (tau asme nābhiṃ puruvāraṃ purukṣuṃ rāyaḥ poṣaṃ asmabhyaṃ vi ṣyatāṃ)—हे सोमापूषणौ युवां बहुभिर्वर्णीयं बहुकीर्तिं धनस्य पुष्टिं विश्वस्य भोगस्य नाभिं हेतुभूतं अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छतां ॥ (he somāpūṣaṇau yuvāṃ bahubhirvarṇīyaṃ bahukīrtiṃ dhanasya puṣṭiṃ viśvasya bhogasya nābhiṃ hetubhūtaṃ asmabhyaṃ prayacchatāṃ ‖) Here the prayer is stated: O Soma and Pūṣan, may you two give us what is desired by many, great fame (or food), and the increase of wealth that is the means of enjoyment, that is, abundance of wealth and wealth in cattle.

p. 406

Ṛk 5

॥ संहितापाठः ॥

विश्वा॑न्य॒न्नो भुव॑ना ज॒जान॒ विश्व॑म॒न्यो अ॑भि॒चक्षा॑ण एति । सोमा॑पूषणा॒वव॑तं॒ धियं॑ मे यु॒वाभ्यां॒ विश्वाः॒ पृत॑ना जयेम ॥ ५ ॥

॥ पदपाठः ॥

विश्वानि । अन्यः । भुवना । जजान । विश्वं । अन्यः । अभिचक्षणाः । एति । सोमापूषणौ । अवतं । धियं । मे । युवाभ्यां । विश्वाः । पृतनाः । जयेम ॥५॥

॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥

हे सोमापूषणौ अन्नो युवयोरेकः सोमो विश्वानि भुवना भुवनानि भूतजातानि जजान । अजनयत् । तथा च मंत्रः । सोमः पवते जनिता मतीनां । ऋग्वे. ९-९६-५ । इति । अन्नोऽपरः पूषादित्यो विश्वमभिचक्षाणोऽभिपश्यन्नेति । गच्छति । तौ युवां सोमापूषणौ मे धियं कर्म ॥ धीः शचीति कर्मनामसु पाठात् ॥ अवतं । रक्षतं । किंच वयं युवाभ्यां हेतुभ्यां विश्वाः पृतनाः सर्वाः शत्रुसेना जयेम । अभिभवेम ॥

he somāpūṣaṇau anno yuvayorekaḥ somo viśvāni bhuvanā bhuvanāni bhūtajātāni jajāna | ajanayat | tathā ca maṃtraḥ | somaḥ pavate janitā matīnāṃ | ṛgve. 9-96-5 | iti | anno 'paraḥ pūṣādityo viśvamabhicakṣāṇo 'bhipaśyanneti | gacchati | tau yuvāṃ somāpūṣaṇau me dhiyaṃ karma ‖ dhīḥ śacīti karmanāmasu pāṭhāt ‖ avataṃ | rakṣataṃ | kiṃca vayaṃ yuvābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ sarvāḥ śatrusenā jayema | abhibhavema ‖

(Gist: Soma, one of the two, produced all beings; the other, Pūṣan (Āditya), goes about beholding the universe; protect my rite; through you may we conquer all hostile hosts. Hand-fixes to kn.md: the doubled label Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya was reduced to one; the Pratipadārtha, which the supplied text had inside the bhāṣya block under a garbled label "1 ಪ್ರತಿಪದಾರ್ಥ 1", was set out as its own section and un-quoted. The bhāṣya cites the Ṛk reference as ऋग्वे. ९-९६-५ (ṛgve. 9-96-5) and the Special Topics as 9-96-2, as supplied.)

प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

(O Soma and Pūṣan deities) One of you, Soma, created all beings. The other, Pūṣan (the Āditya), goes about looking upon the whole world. O Soma and Pūṣan, protect my rite (धियं (dhiyaṃ)). Through your help may we conquer all the hostile armies.

भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma and Pūṣan, one of you, Soma, has created all beings; the other, Pūṣan, moves about looking upon the whole world. O Soma and Pūṣan, protect my rite. With your help may we conquer all the hostile armies.

p. 407

Printed English translation

One of you, (Soma), has generated all beings ; the other proceeds looking upon the universe : Soma and Pushan, protect my (pious) rite : through you, may we overcome all the hosts of our enemies.

विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)

सोमापूषण् अन्यः विश्वानि भुवनानि जजान (somāpūṣaṇ anyaḥ viśvāni bhuvanāni jajāna)—हे सोमापूषण् युवयोरेकः विश्वानि भुवनानि भूतानि अजनयत् । (he somāpūṣaṇ yuvayorekaḥ viśvāni bhuvanāni bhūtāni ajanayat |) O deities Soma and Pūṣan, one of you, the deity Soma, created all the worlds or all beings (living creatures). In this matter, in the Ṛk

सोमः पवते जनिता मतीनां जनिता दिवो जनिता पृथिव्याः । जनिताग्नेर्जनिता सूर्यस्य जनितेंद्रस्य जनितोत विष्णोः ॥ (somaḥ pavate janitā matīnāṃ janitā divo janitā pṛthivyāḥ | janitāgnerjanitā sūryasya janiteṃdrasya janitota viṣṇoḥ ‖) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-2)

it is said that the deity Soma purifies everything; that he is the one who impels the minds of all of us, or the author of the mantras; that he created the heavenly world (heaven) and the earth; and that he produced the deities Agni, Sūrya, Indra and Viṣṇu.

विश्वं अन्यः अभिचक्षाणः एति (viśvaṃ anyaḥ abhicakṣāṇaḥ eti)—अपरः पूषा आदित्यः विश्वं अभिपश्यन् गच्छति । (aparaḥ pūṣā ādityaḥ viśvaṃ abhipaśyan gacchati |) The other of you, called Pūṣan, in the form of Āditya, goes about constantly looking upon the whole universe. As in the sentence आ देवो याति भुवनानि पश्यन् (ā devo yāti bhuvanāni paśyan) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-35-2), Āditya, in the form of Savitṛ, goes about constantly looking upon all beings and all worlds; there is nothing that does not fall within his sight. This too is said.

मे धियं अवतं (me dhiyaṃ avataṃ)—मे कर्म अवतं । (me karma avataṃ |) Since the word धीः (dhīḥ) is read among the names of action, धियं (dhiyaṃ) means "action" (Ni. 3-1). O Soma and Pūṣan, protect my action, that is, the sacrificial rite I am now performing, so that it is completed in full; this is the sense.

युवभ्यां विश्वाः पृतनाः जयेम (yuvabhyāṃ viśvāḥ pṛtanāḥ jayema) (as supplied; the Saṃhitā has युवाभ्यां (yuvābhyāṃ))—the word पृतनाः (pṛtanāḥ) is read among the names of battle (Ni. 3-9). O deities Soma and Pūṣan, by your favour, that is, with your help, may we conquer in battle all the hostile armies; so the prayer is made.
